translation: O you who believe, eat from the wholesome things We have provided for you, and give thanks to Allah, if it is Him you worship.
interpretation: True worship includes recognizing Allah as the source of one’s provision, receiving it with gratitude, and using what is wholesome in a way that reflects devotion to Him.

translation: He has forbidden you only carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, and that over which a name other than Allah’s has been invoked. But whoever is compelled, without seeking it or exceeding the bounds, bears no sin. Surely Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: The verse establishes these prohibitions while making clear that preserving life takes precedence in genuine necessity. The allowance is limited to what necessity requires, and Allah’s forgiveness and mercy mean that a person compelled to take it is not blameworthy.

translation: Indeed, those who conceal what Allah has sent down of the Book and trade it for a small price consume nothing but fire into their bellies. Allah will not speak to them on the Day of Resurrection, nor purify them, and they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns that knowingly suppressing divine guidance for worldly advantage is not a harmless bargain: it corrupts the person inwardly and places them beyond the honor and purification granted by Allah in the Hereafter.

translation: Those are the ones who have traded guidance for misguidance, and forgiveness for punishment. How astonishingly they endure the Fire!
interpretation: The closing words express astonishment and reproach, not praise: by knowingly choosing misguidance over guidance and punishment over forgiveness, they have brought themselves to face the Fire with extraordinary resolve.

translation: That is because Allah sent down the Book in truth, and indeed those who differ concerning the Book are in deep discord.
interpretation: The verse teaches that rejecting or distorting the revelation is not a harmless disagreement: it places people in serious opposition to the truth Allah revealed.

translation: Righteousness is not that you turn your faces toward the east or the west. Rather, the righteous are those who believe in God, the Last Day, the angels, the Scripture, and the prophets; who give wealth, despite their love for it, to relatives, orphans, the needy, the traveler, those who ask, and for freeing people from bondage; who establish prayer and give alms; who keep their covenants when they make them; and who are steadfast in hardship, suffering, and times of conflict. These are the ones who are true, and these are the God-conscious.
interpretation: The verse teaches that outward religious observance finds its integrity in a life shaped by faith, generosity, worship, fidelity, and steadfastness. Turning toward a sacred direction has its place, but it cannot substitute for honoring God through care for others and faithfulness under pressure; the truly God-conscious unite conviction with conduct.

translation: O you who believe, just retribution is prescribed for you in cases of those killed: a free person for a free person, an enslaved person for an enslaved person, and a woman for a woman. But if something is pardoned to someone by his brother, then the matter should be pursued honorably, and payment should be made to him graciously. This is a mitigation from your Lord and a mercy. Whoever transgresses after that will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse places retaliation under a principle of measured justice, restraining cycles of vengeance and forbidding punishment beyond what is due. It also makes room for pardon and a fair settlement, presenting mercy as a divinely granted alternative to retaliation. The reference to the victim’s kin as a “brother” encourages humane treatment even amid a grave dispute, while the warning at the end forbids abusing either the right to seek justice or the opportunity to forgive.

translation: And in just retribution there is life for you, O people of understanding, so that you may be mindful.
interpretation: The verse teaches that proportionate justice can protect life: when people know that murder will be answered by lawful accountability, it deters violence and restrains cycles of private revenge. Addressing people of understanding, it calls them to recognize the wisdom of justice and to act with awareness of God.

translation: It is prescribed for you, when death approaches one of you and they leave behind wealth, to make a fair bequest for parents and close relatives—a duty upon the God-conscious.
interpretation: The verse presents care for one’s family as part of piety: a person facing death should ensure that their wealth is distributed with fairness and consideration for close relatives, in keeping with the limits and inheritance rules established in Islamic law.

translation: Whoever changes it after hearing it—the sin is only upon those who change it. Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: The verse places responsibility on those who knowingly alter a bequest after it has been made known, assuring that Allah hears what is said and knows what is done, even if the alteration is hidden from people.

translation: But whoever fears that a testator has acted unjustly or wrongfully, and brings about a reconciliation between the parties, bears no sin. Indeed, God is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse permits someone who sees that a will may cause injustice or wrongdoing to intervene to set matters right and reconcile those affected. Such intervention is not blameworthy when its purpose is fairness; it is met with God’s forgiveness and mercy.

translation: O you who believe, fasting has been prescribed for you, as it was prescribed for those before you, so that you may become mindful of God.
interpretation: Fasting is a means of cultivating taqwa: by willingly restraining lawful desires for God’s sake, believers strengthen their self-discipline and become more conscious of their duties to Him.

translation: For a limited number of days. Whoever among you is ill or traveling should make up the same number of days later. Those who are able to fast only with great difficulty may compensate by feeding a needy person. Whoever gives more willingly, it is better for him; and fasting is better for you, if you only knew.
interpretation: The verse presents fasting as a manageable obligation with concessions: the ill and traveler make up missed days later, while those for whom fasting is enduringly burdensome may give food to someone in need instead. Its emphasis on voluntary generosity and on fasting’s greater benefit encourages believers to choose the form of worship they are able to sustain faithfully.

translation: The month of Ramadan is the one in which the Qur’an was sent down as guidance for humanity, with clear proofs of guidance and the criterion of right and wrong. So whoever among you is present for the month, let them fast it; and whoever is ill or traveling, then an equal number of days later. God desires ease for you, not hardship, so that you may complete the prescribed number of days, glorify God for having guided you, and perhaps be grateful.
interpretation: The verse presents fasting as an act of devotion shaped by both discipline and mercy: the obligation is tied to Ramadan, the month of the Qur’an’s guidance, while illness and travel bring a clear concession rather than undue hardship. Completing the missed days preserves the observance, and glorifying God and giving thanks recognize that both the guidance and the means to follow it are gifts from Him.

translation: When My servants ask you about Me, surely I am near. I answer the call of the one who calls upon Me when they call upon Me. So let them respond to Me and believe in Me, so that they may be rightly guided.
interpretation: God’s nearness here conveys that prayer is addressed directly to Him, without distance or intermediary. His answering is paired with the servant’s response: turning to Him in trust and living by His guidance. The verse thus presents supplication not as a demand that God act on human terms, but as a relationship of reliance and faithful responsiveness through which a person is guided.

translation: It has been made lawful for you, on the nights of fasting, to be intimate with your wives. They are a garment for you, and you are a garment for them. Allah knew that you had been betraying yourselves, so He turned to you in mercy and pardoned you. So now be intimate with them and seek what Allah has ordained for you. Eat and drink until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct to you from the black thread; then complete the fast until nightfall. But do not be intimate with them while you are observing retreat in the mosques. These are the limits set by Allah, so do not approach them. Thus Allah makes His signs clear to people so that they may be mindful of Him.
interpretation: The verse presents the rules of fasting as both merciful and purposeful: Allah permits marital intimacy during the nights of fasting, acknowledging human needs and pardoning earlier lapses, while setting clear limits for the fast and for devotional retreat. Its image of spouses as garments conveys mutual closeness, protection, and comfort. The command not to approach Allah’s limits urges believers to observe these boundaries carefully, cultivating mindfulness through disciplined worship.

translation: Do not consume one another’s wealth unjustly, nor use it to influence the authorities so that you may wrongfully consume a portion of other people’s wealth, while you know.
interpretation: The verse warns that wealth does not become lawful merely because it is obtained through a favorable ruling or official influence. Bribery and manipulation of legal processes to take what belongs to others remain deliberate wrongdoing, especially when a person knows the claim is unjust.

translation: They ask you about the new moons. Say, “They are time markers for people and for the pilgrimage.” Righteousness is not that you enter houses from their backs; rather, righteousness is in one who is mindful of God. Enter houses through their doors, and be mindful of God so that you may succeed.
interpretation: The verse directs attention from speculation about the changing shape of the moon to its practical purpose as a measure of time, while correcting a mistaken custom treated as religious virtue. It teaches that devotion is not established by unusual outward practices, but by God-consciousness, expressed through following sound guidance rather than inventing burdensome rituals.

translation: Fight in the way of Allah those who fight you, but do not transgress. Indeed, Allah does not love transgressors.
interpretation: The verse permits fighting against those who wage war, while placing it under a strict moral limit: believers must not exceed what is justified or turn defense into aggression. The closing warning makes restraint part of obedience to God.

translation: Kill them wherever you encounter them, and drive them out from where they drove you out; persecution is worse than killing. Do not fight them at the Sacred Mosque unless they fight you there. If they fight you, then fight them: such is the recompense of those who reject faith.
interpretation: This passage addresses Muslims facing an ongoing conflict in which they had been attacked and expelled. Its permission to fight is tied to that conflict: it calls for resistance to those driving them out, while forbidding them to initiate fighting at the Sacred Mosque. It is therefore not a general command to harm people for their beliefs, but a directive framed by aggression, persecution, and limits on warfare.

translation: But if they cease, then Allah is truly All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: If those opposing the believers stop their aggression, they should no longer be treated as enemies; God’s forgiveness and mercy encompass those who turn away from wrongdoing.

translation: Fight them until persecution is no more and worship is devoted to Allah. If they desist, then there is no hostility except against the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse sets a limit on fighting: its aim is to end persecution that prevents people from practicing their faith, not to compel belief. When the opponents desist, hostilities must cease; only those who continue wrongdoing remain subject to opposition.

translation: The sacred month is for the sacred month, and violations are subject to fair retribution. So whoever attacks you, respond in proportion to the attack against you. Be mindful of God, and know that God is with the mindful.
interpretation: The verse establishes that defending oneself against wrongdoing is permissible, but justice must remain proportionate: an injury does not license excess or revenge beyond what was done. Awareness of God is what keeps the pursuit of justice within those limits.

translation: Spend in the way of God, and do not let your own hands cast you into ruin. Do what is excellent; indeed, God loves those who do what is excellent.
interpretation: The verse calls believers to give in support of what is right and not, through neglect or harmful choices, bring ruin upon themselves or their community. It urges them to act with care and generosity, knowing that God loves excellence in conduct.

translation: Complete the Hajj and the Umrah for Allah. If you are prevented from doing so, then offer whatever sacrificial offering is available. Do not shave your heads until the offering has reached its place of sacrifice. If any of you is ill or has an ailment of the head, then the ransom is fasting, charity, or a sacrifice. When you are secure, whoever combines Umrah with Hajj must offer whatever sacrifice is available. If someone cannot afford it, then they must fast three days during the Hajj and seven when they return—ten in all. This applies to those whose families do not reside near the Sacred Mosque. Be mindful of Allah, and know that Allah is severe in punishment.
interpretation: The rites of pilgrimage are to be carried out sincerely for Allah, while the prescribed alternatives make allowance for obstruction, illness, and inability to afford an offering. These concessions do not make the worship casual: they preserve its obligations in another form and place the pilgrim’s conduct within a larger demand for devotion and obedience. The closing warning underscores that the rules are part of a serious covenant with Allah, so worshippers should observe them with care and reverence.

translation: The pilgrimage is during well-known months. So whoever undertakes the pilgrimage in them must refrain from sexual relations, disobedience, and arguing during the pilgrimage. Whatever good you do, Allah knows it. And take provisions, for the best provision is mindfulness of Allah. And be mindful of Me, O people of understanding.
interpretation: By placing the pilgrimage within a time of restraint and devotion, the verse teaches that its outward rites should be matched by inner discipline: pilgrims are to guard their conduct and avoid conflict, while remembering that every good deed is known to Allah. Material provisions matter, but reverence for Allah is the truest provision for the journey and for life beyond it.

translation: There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord. When you depart from ʿArafāt, remember Allah at al-Mashʿar al-Ḥarām, and remember Him as He has guided you, though before that you were surely among those who had gone astray.
interpretation: The verse teaches that devotion during pilgrimage does not require abandoning lawful livelihood: seeking provision is permitted, while the rites themselves call pilgrims to remember Allah with gratitude. At the sacred gathering after ʿArafāt, they are to recall that their guidance and knowledge of worship are gifts from Allah, for without His guidance they would have remained lost.

translation: Then proceed from where the people proceed, and ask Allah for forgiveness. Surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse directs the pilgrims to join the rest of the people in carrying out the pilgrimage rites, rather than claiming a special exemption, and to seek forgiveness for their shortcomings. It teaches humility and equality in worship, while assuring them of Allah’s mercy.

translation: When you have completed your rites, remember Allah as you remember your fathers—or with even greater remembrance. Among the people are those who say, “Our Lord, grant us in this world,” and they will have no share in the Hereafter.
interpretation: The verse calls believers to let remembrance of God surpass even their deepest customary attachments, and warns against treating faith merely as a means to worldly gain. A person who asks only for this world neglects the lasting good of the Hereafter.

translation: And among them are those who say, “Our Lord, grant us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.”
interpretation: This prayer expresses a balanced hope: to seek what is truly good in worldly life without losing sight of lasting good in the Hereafter, while asking God for protection from the ultimate consequence of wrongdoing.

translation: Those will have a share of what they have earned, and Allah is swift in reckoning.
interpretation: The verse assures that each person will receive the due consequence of their deeds; nothing is overlooked, and Allah’s judgment is not hindered by time or circumstance.

translation: And remember Allah during the appointed days. Whoever hastens to leave after two days, there is no blame upon him; and whoever stays longer, there is no blame upon him—provided that he is mindful of Allah. Be mindful of Allah, and know that you will be gathered unto Him.
interpretation: The verse teaches that pilgrims may either leave Mina after two days or remain for an additional day; neither choice is blameworthy when made with mindfulness of Allah. The essential matter is sincere remembrance and obedience, with awareness that everyone will ultimately return to Allah for judgment.

translation: Among people is one whose speech about the life of this world impresses you, and who calls God to witness what is in his heart, though he is the fiercest of opponents.
interpretation: The verse warns against mistaking eloquence and pious assurances for sincerity: a person may invoke God while concealing a hostile disposition, but outward words cannot hide the heart’s truth from God.

translation: And when he turns away, he strives throughout the land to spread corruption there and destroy crops and offspring. And Allah does not love corruption.
interpretation: The verse warns that persuasive words and claims of good intent do not establish a person’s righteousness; their character is revealed by whether their actions protect or damage the foundations of communal life. Corruption that brings such harm is abhorrent to God.

translation: When he is told, “Be mindful of Allah,” pride in sin takes hold of him. Hell is sufficient for him—and what a miserable resting place.
interpretation: The verse portrays a person whose arrogance turns sincere moral counsel into an affront, so he persists in wrongdoing rather than submit to what is right. It warns that such defiance has a grave consequence: a final abode of punishment.

translation: Among people is one who gives himself up in pursuit of Allah’s pleasure; and Allah is Compassionate toward His servants.
interpretation: The verse portrays sincere devotion as being willing to sacrifice one’s own interests for what pleases God. Such dedication is not overlooked: God’s compassion encompasses those who seek His pleasure.

translation: O you who believe, enter fully into submission to God, and do not follow Satan’s footsteps. Indeed, he is a clear enemy to you.
interpretation: The verse calls believers to embrace faith wholeheartedly rather than choosing only the parts that suit them, and to be alert to how wrongdoing can begin with small compromises that gradually lead them away from God’s guidance.

translation: But if you slip after clear proofs have come to you, then know that Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.
interpretation: Once the truth has been made clear, turning away from it is a grave choice: Allah’s might means no one can escape His judgment, while His wisdom means that His judgment is never unjust or without purpose.

translation: Are they waiting for anything but that God should come to them in canopies of clouds, with the angels, and the matter be decided? To God all affairs return.
interpretation: The verse warns those who resist the truth that they should not wait until the final judgment, when God’s decisive judgment is made manifest and the matter is settled. The imagery conveys the awe of that event without specifying how it occurs.

translation: Ask the Children of Israel how many clear signs We gave them. Whoever changes Allah’s favor after it has come to him—Allah is severe in punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns that receiving clear guidance is a responsibility: to reject it or distort its meaning after it has been made known is to turn away from Allah’s favor, and such ingratitude carries serious consequences.

translation: The worldly life has been made alluring to those who disbelieve, and they mock those who believe. But those who are mindful of God will be above them on the Day of Resurrection. And God provides for whom He wills without measure.
interpretation: Worldly success and the scorn it can invite are not measures of a person’s true standing. God’s judgment overturns such appearances: honor belongs to those who remain mindful of Him, while His provision is not limited by human expectations or calculations.

translation: Humanity was once one community, then Allah sent the prophets as bearers of glad tidings and warnings, and sent down with them the Book in truth to judge between people concerning what they differed over. None differed over it except those who had been given it, after clear proofs had come to them, out of rivalry among themselves. Then Allah, by His permission, guided those who believed to the truth concerning what they had differed over. Allah guides whomever He wills to a straight path.
interpretation: The verse teaches that disagreement about divine guidance can persist even after the truth has been made clear, when rivalry and self-interest distort people’s response. True guidance comes from Allah: He enables believers, by His permission, to recognize the truth and follow a straight path.

translation: Or did you suppose that you would enter Paradise without facing what those who passed away before you faced? They were touched by hardship and adversity and were shaken until the Messenger and those who believed with him said, “When will Allah’s help come?” Surely, Allah’s help is near.
interpretation: The verse teaches that faith does not guarantee a life free from trial; steadfastness through hardship is part of the path to Paradise. Even profound distress does not mean that divine help is absent or far away.

translation: They ask you what they should spend. Say, “Whatever good you spend should be for parents, close relatives, orphans, the needy, and the traveler.” Whatever good you do, Allah surely knows it.
interpretation: The verse teaches that sincere generosity is expressed through care for those with a particular claim on one’s support, beginning with family and extending to vulnerable people in the wider community. No such good deed is overlooked by Allah.

translation: Fighting has been prescribed for you, though it is hateful to you. Perhaps you dislike something while it is good for you, and perhaps you love something while it is harmful to you. God knows, and you do not know.
interpretation: The verse teaches that human judgment is limited: what feels painful or unwanted may serve a greater good, while what seems desirable may bring harm. In the context of the duty to fight, it calls believers to trust God’s knowledge and wisdom even when obedience is difficult, rather than treating their immediate feelings as the measure of what is ultimately good.

translation: They ask you about fighting in the sacred month. Say, “Fighting in it is a grave matter. But barring people from God’s way, disbelieving in Him, preventing access to the Sacred Mosque, and driving its people out of it are graver in God’s sight. Persecution is worse than killing.” They will not cease fighting you until they turn you back from your religion, if they can. Whoever among you turns back from his religion and dies as a disbeliever—their deeds will come to nothing in this world and the Hereafter. They are the companions of the Fire, where they will remain forever.
interpretation: The verse teaches that moral judgment must consider the full pattern of wrongdoing, not isolate one act from its context: fighting during a sacred month is serious, yet persecution, expulsion, and obstruction of worship are graver. It also warns believers that pressure to abandon faith may persist, while making clear that the stated judgment concerns those who die in disbelief.

translation: Indeed, those who believe, those who emigrate, and those who strive in the way of God— they hope for God’s mercy. And God is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse teaches that hope in God’s mercy is joined to sincere faith and willing effort for His sake. Such effort does not make a person entitled to mercy; rather, God’s forgiveness and compassion remain the source of hope.

translation: They ask you about wine and gambling. Say, “In both is great sin, though they have some benefits for people; but their sin is greater than their benefit.” And they ask you what they should spend. Say, “What is surplus to your needs.” Thus God makes the revelations clear to you so that you may reflect.
interpretation: The verse teaches a discerning moral outlook: a practice is not made acceptable simply because it offers some advantage when its harms are greater. It also presents giving as an act of balance and generosity, encouraging people to share what they can spare rather than neglect their own needs.

translation: In this world and the Hereafter. They ask you about orphans. Say, “Putting things right for them is best. If you share your lives with them, they are your brothers. God knows who causes harm and who sets things right. Had He willed, He could have burdened you. Indeed, God is Almighty, Wise.”
interpretation: The verse allows those caring for orphans to share their households and affairs with them, provided their intention is to protect the children’s interests rather than exploit them. Its reassurance is that sincere care, not rigid separation, is the aim—and God knows the difference between genuine reform and wrongdoing.

translation: Do not marry women who associate others with God until they believe. A believing enslaved woman is better than a woman who associates others with God, even if she pleases you. And do not give believing women in marriage to men who associate others with God until they believe. A believing enslaved man is better than a man who associates others with God, even if he pleases you. Such people call toward the Fire, while God, by His permission, calls toward Paradise and forgiveness. He makes His signs clear to people so that they may take heed.
interpretation: The verse teaches that shared faith should outweigh attraction or social standing in marriage, because a person’s deepest commitments shape the direction of life. It cautions believers against bonds that draw them away from God, while pointing to God’s guidance as an invitation to forgiveness and Paradise.

translation: They ask you about menstruation. Say, “It is a state of harm, so refrain from sexual relations with women during menstruation, and do not have intercourse with them until they are pure. Once they have purified themselves, approach them as God has commanded you. Surely God loves those who turn to Him in repentance and those who purify themselves.”
interpretation: The instruction concerns sexual intercourse during menstruation, not excluding women from ordinary companionship. Intimacy is to resume only after menstruation has ended and purification has taken place, within the limits God has set. The closing verse links physical cleanliness with the broader virtues of repentance and purity.

translation: Your wives are a place of cultivation for you, so approach your place of cultivation as you wish. And send good deeds ahead for yourselves; be mindful of God, and know that you will meet Him. And give glad tidings to the believers.
interpretation: The metaphor of cultivation presents marital intimacy as part of a relationship with responsibilities and lawful boundaries. The verse also directs believers to prepare for their meeting with God through good deeds and mindfulness of Him, while offering them hope in His promise.

translation: Do not make God the target of your oaths, using them as an excuse to refrain from doing good, being mindful of God, or making peace among people. God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: A person should not let an oath become an obstacle to a righteous act. If an oath would prevent them from doing good, guarding against wrongdoing, or reconciling people, they should not use it to justify withholding that good.

translation: Allah will not call you to account for thoughtless oaths, but He will call you to account for what your hearts have earned. Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Forbearing.
interpretation: The verse distinguishes words spoken without deliberate intent from oaths chosen knowingly and sincerely. It teaches that accountability rests on what a person intends and earns inwardly, while affirming that God is forgiving and does not hasten to punish.

translation: For those who swear to abstain from their wives, there is a waiting period of four months. If they return to them, then surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: This ruling gives a spouse who has been abandoned through such an oath a defined limit to the uncertainty: the husband must either resume marital relations or, after the allotted period, resolve the marriage according to its obligations. Returning is met with Allah’s forgiveness and mercy.

translation: And if they resolve to divorce, then surely Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: A decision about divorce is known to Allah in both its spoken form and its underlying intentions, so it should be made with honesty and awareness of His judgment.

translation: Divorced women shall wait by themselves for three qurūʾ. It is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs, if they believe in God and the Last Day. Their husbands have the stronger claim to take them back during that period, if they truly seek reconciliation. Women have rights corresponding to the obligations upon them, according to what is fair; and men have a degree of responsibility over them. God is Almighty, All-Wise.
interpretation: The verse frames divorce as a period in which honesty, fairness, and the possibility of reconciliation must be respected. A woman must not conceal a pregnancy or other relevant matter, and a husband’s right to resume the marriage is tied to a sincere wish to make things right—not to harm or control her. The mutual rights and duties are grounded in what is fair, while the “degree” assigned to men is understood as an additional responsibility within the marital arrangement, not permission to disregard women’s rights. The closing names God’s might and wisdom as a reminder that these rules are bounded by justice and wise purpose.

translation: Divorce is twice; then either retain [her] honorably or release [her] graciously. It is not lawful for you to take back anything of what you have given them, unless both fear that they cannot uphold the limits set by God. If you fear that they cannot uphold God’s limits, then neither of them is blameworthy for whatever she gives to secure her release. These are the limits set by God, so do not transgress them; whoever transgresses God’s limits—those are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse sets a moral boundary around marital separation: after either of the first two divorces, a husband must choose between continuing the marriage with fairness and care or ending it with kindness, rather than keeping his wife in hardship or using divorce to take back what he gave her. If the spouses fear they cannot fulfill their obligations to one another, the wife may seek release by offering compensation, without either being blamed for that arrangement. The ruling emphasizes that both marriage and its dissolution must remain within God’s limits of justice and good conduct.

translation: Then if he divorces her [for the third time], she is not lawful to him afterward until she marries another husband. Then if that husband divorces her, there is no blame upon the two of them if they return to one another, provided they think they can uphold Allah’s limits. These are Allah’s limits, which He makes clear to people who know.
interpretation: The verse sets a firm boundary after a third divorce: the former spouses cannot simply resume their marriage. Reconciliation becomes possible only after she has married another husband and that marriage has ended, and only if both believe they can live together within the limits Allah has set.

translation: When you divorce women and they reach the end of their waiting period, then either retain them honorably or release them honorably. Do not retain them to harm them and transgress; whoever does that wrongs himself. Do not take God’s signs as a jest. Remember God’s favor upon you and what He has sent down to you of the Book and wisdom, with which He admonishes you. Be mindful of God, and know that God has knowledge of all things.
interpretation: The verse insists that divorce must not be used as a means of control or injury: a husband should either resume the marriage with sincere, honorable intent or let the woman go with dignity. Treating God’s guidance lightly in this matter is itself a wrong, so believers are called to remember the guidance they have received and act with awareness that God knows their intentions and deeds.

translation: When you divorce women and they reach the end of their waiting period, do not prevent them from marrying their former husbands if they mutually agree in a proper manner. This is an admonition for whoever among you believes in God and the Last Day. That is purer and more wholesome for you. God knows, and you do not know.
interpretation: The verse forbids guardians or others from obstructing a woman’s lawful choice to remarry her former husband once her waiting period has ended, provided both agree and the marriage is conducted properly. It teaches that respecting this mutual consent is a matter of faith and is better, even when people cannot see all the wisdom behind it.

translation: Mothers shall breastfeed their children for two complete years, for whoever wishes to complete the nursing period. The child’s father must provide for their food and clothing in a fair manner. No soul is burdened beyond its capacity. Neither a mother should be harmed on account of her child, nor a father on account of his child; and the heir has the same obligation. If the two parents wish to wean the child by mutual consent and consultation, there is no blame upon them. And if you wish to have your children nursed by another woman, there is no blame upon you, provided you pay what you have agreed upon in a fair manner. Be mindful of God, and know that God sees all that you do.
interpretation: The verse presents care for a child as a shared responsibility governed by fairness, capacity, and the child’s welfare—not as a means for either parent to pressure or injure the other. Decisions such as early weaning or arranging another nurse are therefore to be made through genuine consultation and mutual agreement, with compensation handled justly. Its closing reminder that God sees what people do underscores that these duties remain accountable even when no one else is watching.

translation: Those of you who die and leave wives behind—their wives shall wait by themselves for four months and ten days. When they have reached the end of that term, there is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves in a proper manner. And God is fully aware of what you do.
interpretation: The waiting period gives a widow a defined time of mourning and ensures that matters surrounding her marriage are clear. Once it has ended, she may make lawful decisions about her future, including remarriage, in a manner consistent with what is recognized as proper; the verse also cautions those around her that God knows how they treat her and respond to her choices.

translation: There is no blame upon you for hinting at a proposal to women, or for keeping such an intention within yourselves. God knows that you will think of them, but do not make secret promises to them; speak only in an honorable manner. Do not resolve to marry until the prescribed waiting period has reached its end. Know that God knows what is within you, so be mindful of Him. And know that God is forgiving and forbearing.
interpretation: The verse permits a restrained, indirect expression of interest in a woman observing a waiting period, while forbidding secret commitments or a marriage contract before that period ends. Its guidance protects her dignity and the legal boundaries of the waiting period, requiring honorable speech and self-restraint even when private intentions are known to God. The closing assurance that God is forgiving and forbearing pairs accountability with mercy.

translation: There is no blame upon you if you divorce women before you have touched them or set a bridal gift for them. Provide for them: the well-to-do according to his means and the one of limited means according to his means—a fair provision, as is incumbent upon those who do good.
interpretation: The verse places humane conduct at the heart of a separation: even when no bridal gift was agreed and the marriage was not consummated, a woman’s dignity should not be disregarded. What is given should be fair and proportionate to the husband’s means, so that the ending of the relationship is marked by generosity rather than injury.

translation: If you divorce them before you have consummated the marriage, but you have already stipulated a bridal gift for them, then they are entitled to half of what you stipulated—unless they waive their claim, or the one who holds the marriage bond waives his right. To waive it is closer to righteousness. Do not forget graciousness between you; surely God sees all that you do.
interpretation: The verse teaches that even when a marriage ends before it is consummated, its financial rights should be honored; beyond what is legally due, either spouse may choose generosity. It presents such graciousness not as an obligation, but as a sign of righteousness, and reminds both parties that God knows how they treat one another.

translation: Maintain the prayers, especially the middle prayer, and stand before God in devout obedience.
interpretation: The verse presents prayer as a trust requiring constant care, not something to be set aside amid life’s demands. By giving special emphasis to the middle prayer, it calls for vigilance at a point especially vulnerable to neglect, while “standing before God” conveys humility and wholehearted devotion.

translation: If you are in fear, then pray on foot or riding. But when you are secure, remember God as He has taught you what you did not know.
interpretation: The verse shows that devotion to God is not abandoned in hardship: its outward form may be adapted to danger, while safety calls for worship according to the guidance God has taught. This guidance itself is a gift, directing people toward forms of worship they could not have known on their own.

translation: As for those among you who die and leave wives behind, they should make a bequest for their wives: provision for a year, without turning them out. But if they leave, then you bear no blame for what they do with themselves in a proper manner. Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.
interpretation: The verse instructs that a widow be provided for and not forced from her home after her husband’s death. If she chooses to leave, she may make lawful choices for herself without blame being placed on those responsible for her provision.

translation: And divorced women are entitled to a provision according to what is reasonable—a duty upon the God-conscious.
interpretation: The verse calls for divorce to be handled with dignity and fairness: a woman should not be left without reasonable support when the marriage ends. It presents this care as a mark of God-consciousness, guided by what is just and customary.

translation: Thus Allah makes His signs clear to you, so that you may reason.
interpretation: Allah’s explanations are meant to be reflected upon: by using their understanding, people can recognize the guidance in His signs and respond to it wisely.

translation: Have you not considered those who left their homes in their thousands, fearing death? Allah said to them, “Die,” then brought them back to life. Indeed, Allah is gracious to people, but most people are not grateful.
interpretation: Their story shows that life and death are ultimately in Allah’s hands: fleeing cannot escape His decree, and being given life is a favor that calls for trust in Him and gratitude.

translation: Fight in the way of Allah, and know that Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: The verse calls believers to strive for Allah’s cause with awareness that He hears what they say and knows their intentions and actions, so their struggle should be sincere and accountable to Him.

translation: Who is it that will lend Allah a good loan, so He may multiply it for them many times over? Allah withholds and grants abundantly, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: Calling a gift to those in need or a contribution for God’s cause a “loan” honors the giver and assures them that nothing offered sincerely is lost: God will reward it many times over. Since He alone determines when provision is restricted or enlarged, generosity is an act of trust in Him, and all people ultimately return to Him.

translation: Have you not considered the chiefs of the Children of Israel after Moses, when they said to one of their prophets, “Appoint for us a king, and we will fight in the way of God”? He said, “Might it be that, if fighting is prescribed for you, you will not fight?” They said, “Why should we not fight in the way of God, when we have been driven from our homes and separated from our children?” But when fighting was prescribed for them, they turned away, except for a few of them. And God knows the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse warns that sincere commitment is proved when a demand becomes real, not merely declared in response to hardship. The people’s stated resolve gave way when the duty was imposed, exposing the gap between their words and their conduct; God knows who acts unjustly by abandoning what they have pledged to uphold.

translation: Their prophet said to them, “Indeed, God has appointed Talut as king over you.” They said, “How can he have kingship over us when we are more entitled to kingship than he is, and he has not been granted abundant wealth?” He said, “God has chosen him over you and increased him in knowledge and stature. God grants His authority to whomever He wills. God is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing.”
interpretation: The people measure a leader’s worth by lineage, entitlement, and wealth, but the verse redirects them to God’s judgment: leadership is not secured by worldly privilege. Talut’s knowledge and strength are named as qualities suited to his responsibility, while God’s encompassing knowledge and will remain the source of authority.

translation: Their prophet said to them, “The sign of his kingship is that the Ark will come to you, containing reassurance from your Lord and remnants of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left behind, carried by the angels. Surely in that is a sign for you, if you are believers.”
interpretation: The return of the Ark, bearing sacred reminders of Moses and Aaron and brought by the angels, was a miraculous confirmation that God had appointed Talut as king. Its reassurance invited the people to trust God’s guidance and recognize the sign through faith.

translation: When Talut set out with the armies, he said, “Allah is testing you with a river. Whoever drinks from it is not of me; but whoever does not taste it is of me—except one who takes a handful in his hand.” Yet they drank from it, apart from a few of them. When he and those who believed with him had crossed it, they said, “We have no strength today against Jalut and his armies.” Those who were certain they would meet Allah said, “How often has a small company overcome a larger company by Allah’s permission! Allah is with the steadfast.”
interpretation: The river tests whether the people will restrain themselves and trust their leader’s command when faced with temptation. Their strength is not measured by their numbers: those who remain steadfast and trust in Allah can face overwhelming odds, because victory comes by His permission.

translation: When they advanced to face Goliath and his troops, they said, “Our Lord, pour patience upon us, make our feet firm, and grant us victory over the disbelieving people.”
interpretation: Their prayer shows that steadfastness begins by turning to God: they ask not only for victory, but for the patience and firmness needed to face fear and remain faithful in the struggle.

translation: So they defeated them by Allah’s permission, and David killed Goliath. Allah gave him kingship and wisdom and taught him what He willed. Were it not for Allah’s restraining some people by means of others, the earth would have been corrupted; but Allah is gracious to all the worlds.
interpretation: The verse presents victory and authority as gifts from Allah, not merely the outcome of human strength: David’s kingship, wisdom, and knowledge all came from Him. It also teaches that Allah protects the earth from corruption by enabling people to check one another’s power, a form of divine favor extending to all creation.

translation: These are the signs of Allah that We recite to you in truth, and surely you are among the messengers.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the revelation is conveyed truthfully and that the Prophet Muhammad is truly a messenger of God, giving authority to the message being recited.

translation: Those messengers: We favored some of them over others. Among them were those to whom Allah spoke, and He raised some of them in rank. We gave Jesus, son of Mary, clear signs and strengthened him with the Holy Spirit. Had Allah willed, those who came after them would not have fought one another after clear signs had come to them. But they differed: some believed and some disbelieved. Had Allah willed, they would not have fought; but Allah does what He wills.
interpretation: The verse teaches that receiving divine guidance and clear signs does not make people agree or compel them to believe: people may respond differently and even descend into conflict. Their disagreements unfold within Allah’s will, while the messengers themselves are not all alike in rank or bestowed gifts.

translation: O you who believe, spend from what We have provided for you before a Day comes when there will be no bargaining, no friendship, and no intercession. And it is the disbelievers who are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: Believers are urged to give from their provision while they still have the opportunity, for on the Day of Judgment wealth cannot be offered as a ransom, worldly ties cannot secure rescue, and no one can intercede independently of God. To reject faith is therefore to wrong oneself by turning away from the guidance and opportunity God has given.

translation: Allah—there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all. Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on earth. Who can intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what lies before them and what lies behind them, and they encompass nothing of His knowledge except what He wills. His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth, and preserving them does not weary Him. He is the Most High, the Most Great.
interpretation: The verse presents God as utterly unlike creation: His life and sustaining power are constant, His knowledge encompasses all, and nothing exists or acts independently of Him. Even intercession depends on His permission, while human knowledge reaches only what He chooses to disclose. The vastness of the heavens and earth does not burden Him, affirming that all creation remains under His effortless care and supreme authority.

translation: There is no compulsion in religion. The right way has become distinct from error. Whoever rejects false gods and believes in God has grasped the firmest handhold, which will never break. God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: Faith is not genuine when forced: guidance is made clear, and each person must freely turn from false powers toward God. The image of an unbreakable handhold conveys the security of placing one’s trust in God, who knows and hears the choices people make.

translation: Allah is the Guardian of those who believe; He brings them out of darkness into light. As for those who disbelieve, their guardians are false powers; they bring them out of light into darkness. Those are the inhabitants of the Fire, where they will remain forever.
interpretation: Allah’s guardianship is guidance that leads believers from confusion and falsehood to the truth. By contrast, those who turn to false powers are led away from that guidance, with the lasting consequence described in the verse.

translation: Have you not considered the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord because God had granted him kingship? Abraham said, “My Lord is the One who gives life and causes death.” He said, “I give life and cause death.” Abraham said, “God brings the sun from the east, so bring it from the west.” Then the one who disbelieved was confounded. God does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: The verse shows that worldly authority can foster the illusion of control, but it cannot rival God’s power. When the king’s claim rested on a misleading use of words, Abraham turned to the sun’s regular course as a clear sign of divine sovereignty; faced with what he could not answer, the king was confounded. Persistent wrongdoing and pride can therefore keep a person from recognizing the truth even when it is made plain.

translation: Or [consider] the one who passed by a town fallen into ruin. He said, “How will Allah bring this back to life after its death?” So Allah caused him to die for a hundred years, then raised him. He said, “How long have you remained?” He replied, “A day, or part of a day.” He said, “Rather, you have remained a hundred years. Look at your food and drink: they have not spoiled. And look at your donkey. We will make you a sign for the people. And look at the bones, how We raise them and then clothe them with flesh.” When it became clear to him, he said, “I know that Allah is capable of all things.”
interpretation: The encounter answers a question about resurrection through a sign made directly visible: the man is restored after a century, while his food remains unchanged and the renewal of his donkey’s bones is shown to him. His experience teaches that Allah’s power over life and death is not limited by time, decay, or what people consider impossible, and that what is witnessed in one instance points to the certainty of resurrection.

translation: And [mention] when Abraham said, “My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead.” He said, “Have you not believed?” Abraham replied, “Yes, but so that my heart may be reassured.” He said, “Then take four birds and cut them into pieces; then place a portion of them on each hill, and call them—they will come to you swiftly. And know that Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.”
interpretation: Abraham’s request was not a denial of resurrection; he already believed, but sought the added reassurance of witnessing how Allah brings the dead to life. The birds’ swift return by Allah’s command demonstrates that resurrection is entirely within His power, while His wisdom governs how He makes it known.

translation: The example of those who spend their wealth in the way of God is like a grain that grows seven ears, with a hundred grains in each ear. God multiplies the reward for whom He wills, and God is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: The verse teaches that sincere giving for God’s sake is never diminished: God can make its reward vastly exceed the amount given, according to His wisdom and knowledge of each person’s intention and deed.

translation: Those who spend their wealth in the way of God and then do not follow what they have spent with reminders of their generosity or hurtful words will have their reward with their Lord. No fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve.
interpretation: True charity preserves the dignity of the person receiving it. Giving is not a favor to be used later for self-praise or to wound someone; its goodness lies in sincere generosity that seeks God’s approval and leaves the recipient unharmed.

translation: Kind words and forgiveness are better than charity followed by hurt. And Allah is Self-Sufficient, Forbearing.
interpretation: The worth of giving lies not merely in what is handed over, but in the care and humility with which it is given. A kind word—or forgiving someone rather than humiliating them—can better honor a person’s dignity than a gift later used to wound them. Since Allah needs no one’s charity and is Forbearing toward human failings, people should give without arrogance or reproach.

translation: O you who believe, do not render your charitable gifts worthless by reminding others of your generosity or hurting them, like someone who spends his wealth to be seen by people and does not believe in God and the Last Day. His likeness is that of a smooth rock covered with soil: a heavy rain strikes it and leaves it bare. They gain nothing from what they have earned. God does not guide the disbelieving people.
interpretation: Charity has spiritual worth when it is given sincerely and with respect for the recipient. Using a gift to claim credit, shame someone, or win public admiration strips it of that worth, like rain washing all the soil from a bare stone; outward generosity cannot compensate for a heart lacking sincere faith.

translation: The likeness of those who spend their wealth seeking Allah’s pleasure and to strengthen their own souls is that of a garden on elevated ground: when heavy rain falls upon it, it yields twice its usual produce; and if no heavy rain falls upon it, a light shower is enough. Allah sees all that you do.
interpretation: Sincere giving, rooted in conviction rather than display, is like a fertile garden: it bears abundant good whether circumstances are generous or modest. Allah knows the intention behind every act and its true worth.

translation: Would any of you wish to have a garden of date palms and grapevines, with rivers flowing beneath it and every kind of fruit, then—having grown old and with helpless children—have it struck by a fiery whirlwind and burned away? In this way Allah makes the signs clear to you, so that you may reflect.
interpretation: The image warns how devastating it is to have one’s good deeds lost just when one most needs their reward. Like a person whose garden is destroyed in old age while dependants rely on it, someone who corrupts their charity through showing off or hurtful reminders may be left with nothing at the moment of greatest need.

translation: O you who believe, spend from the good things you have earned and from what We have brought forth for you from the earth. Do not deliberately choose what is bad to give away, when you yourselves would not accept it except by overlooking its faults. And know that Allah is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy.
interpretation: Giving should reflect sincere respect for others: a believer does not offer charity what they themselves would reject as defective or worthless. The verse calls for generosity from wholesome provision, while reminding us that God has no need of our gifts; their worth lies in the sincerity and care with which they are given.

translation: Satan threatens you with poverty and urges you to indecency, while Allah promises you forgiveness from Him and bounty. Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: In the context of giving, the verse contrasts fear-driven miserliness with trust in Allah: Satan uses anxiety about losing wealth to discourage generosity and lead toward wrongdoing, whereas Allah invites people to hope in His forgiveness and bounty. His knowledge encompasses both their intentions and their circumstances.

translation: He grants wisdom to whom He wills; whoever is granted wisdom has indeed been granted abundant good. Yet none take heed except people of understanding.
interpretation: True wisdom is a gift from God: the ability to recognize what is right and live by it. Its worth surpasses material gain, and those who reflect with sound understanding are the ones who recognize its value.

translation: Whatever you spend, or whatever vow you make, Allah knows it. And the wrongdoers will have no helpers.
interpretation: No act of giving or vow is hidden from Allah; He knows its purpose and will judge it accordingly. Those who wrongfully turn away from His guidance should not expect anyone to protect or rescue them from His judgment.

translation: If you give charity openly, that is good; but if you conceal it and give it to the poor, that is better for you, and He will erase some of your misdeeds. Allah is fully aware of what you do.
interpretation: Concealing charity can safeguard sincerity and protect the recipient’s dignity, while giving openly may also be beneficial when it encourages others. The verse teaches that the worth of giving is known to God, who rewards sincere deeds and may make them a means of expiation.

translation: You are not responsible for guiding them; rather, Allah guides whom He wills. Whatever good you spend is for your own benefit, and you should spend only seeking the pleasure of Allah. Whatever good you spend will be repaid to you in full, and you will not be wronged.
interpretation: Guidance belongs to Allah, so believers are not to make their generosity conditional on someone accepting their faith. They should give sincerely for Allah’s sake, trusting that every good deed will be fully rewarded and that no one will lose anything of what they have done.

translation: [Give] to the poor who are constrained in the cause of Allah and cannot travel through the land. Someone unaware of their circumstances may think them well-off because they refrain from asking. You can recognize them by their appearance; they do not plead with people persistently. Whatever good you spend, Allah knows it.
interpretation: The verse calls for attentiveness to people whose hardship is hidden by their dignity and self-restraint. Their reluctance to ask should not make them overlooked; rather, believers should seek them out and give generously, trusting that Allah knows every act of charity and the need it answers.

translation: Those who spend their wealth by night and by day, privately and publicly, will have their reward with their Lord. They will have no fear, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: The verse teaches that sincere generosity is not limited by time or circumstance, and may be practiced privately or openly when appropriate. Its reassurance is that those who give for God’s sake can trust in His reward and mercy rather than be consumed by fear of what lies ahead or sorrow over what has passed.

translation: Those who consume usury will not rise except as one rises who is driven to madness by Satan’s touch. That is because they say, “Trade is just like usury.” But God has permitted trade and forbidden usury. Whoever receives an admonition from their Lord and desists may keep what has already passed, and their affair rests with God. But whoever returns to it—those are the people of the Fire; they will remain there forever.
interpretation: The verse rejects the claim that usury is merely another form of trade: lawful exchange and exploitative gain are not morally equivalent. Its image of a person rising in confusion conveys the spiritual disorder associated with this false reasoning. At the same time, the verse leaves the door open to repentance: one who heeds the warning and stops is not held to account for what came before, while knowingly returning to usury after the admonition carries grave consequences.

translation: Allah diminishes usury and makes charity grow. And Allah does not love anyone who is persistently ungrateful and sinful.
interpretation: The verse teaches that wealth gained through usury is deprived of blessing and ultimately brought to ruin, while charity is made fruitful through blessing and reward. It warns that knowingly persisting in this wrongdoing reflects a rejection of God’s guidance.

translation: Indeed, those who believe, do righteous deeds, establish prayer, and give zakah will have their reward with their Lord. They will have no fear, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: True faith is shown not only in belief, but also in worship and care for others. The verse offers reassurance that those who live by this faith are in God’s care, free from fear about what lies ahead and grief over what has passed.

translation: O you who believe, be mindful of Allah and give up whatever remains of usury, if you are truly believers.
interpretation: The verse calls believers to show the sincerity of their faith through obedience to God: they must abandon any unpaid usurious gains, trusting that devotion to God takes precedence over financial profit.

translation: If you do not, then be warned of a war from Allah and His Messenger. But if you repent, you may have your principal sums: you will neither wrong others nor be wronged.
interpretation: The verse gives a grave warning against persisting in usury and directs those who repent to claim only the original amount they lent. In this way, neither lender nor borrower is subjected to injustice.

translation: If someone is in hardship, then grant them respite until they are able to repay. But if you remit the debt as charity, that is better for you, if only you knew.
interpretation: The verse teaches that financial hardship should be met with compassion rather than pressure: a creditor should allow a struggling debtor time to recover, and forgiving the debt is an even greater act of generosity and spiritual good.

translation: Be mindful of a Day when you will be returned to Allah; then every soul will be fully repaid for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse calls people to live with awareness of their ultimate return to God: every person will face the full consequences of their choices, with neither their deeds overlooked nor their due withheld. That certainty makes justice and sincere obedience urgent in this life.

translation: O you who believe, when you contract a debt for a specified term, write it down. Let a scribe write it between you with fairness, and let no scribe refuse to write as Allah has taught him; so let him write. Let the one who owes the debt dictate, and let him be mindful of Allah, his Lord, and not diminish anything from it. If the one who owes the debt is incapable, weak, or unable to dictate himself, then let his guardian dictate fairly. Call upon two witnesses from among your men; and if two men are not available, then one man and two women from among those you accept as witnesses, so that if one of the two women errs, the other may remind her. Let witnesses not refuse when they are called. Do not tire of writing down the debt, whether small or large, together with its due term. That is more just in the sight of Allah, more reliable as testimony, and more likely to prevent doubt between you. But if it is an immediate trade that you conduct among yourselves, there is no blame upon you if you do not write it down. And have witnesses when you make a sale. Let neither scribe nor witness be harmed; if you do so, it is wrongdoing on your part. Be mindful of Allah, and Allah teaches you; and Allah has knowledge of all things.
interpretation: The verse presents careful record-keeping as an expression of faith and justice, not as a sign of mistrust. By requiring fairness and protecting the rights of both parties, it seeks to prevent memory, power, or circumstance from becoming a means of denying what is owed. Its closing reminder that Allah teaches and knows all things places these practical safeguards within a wider moral responsibility: people should act transparently because their dealings are ultimately accountable to God.

translation: If you are traveling and cannot find someone to write it down, then take a pledge in hand. But if one of you entrusts the other, let the one who was entrusted fulfill that trust and be mindful of God, his Lord. Do not conceal testimony; whoever conceals it has a sinful heart. And God knows all that you do.
interpretation: The verse presents written records and pledged security as safeguards when a debt is made, especially during travel, but places honest trust at the heart of every agreement. Whoever receives that trust must honor it before God, and anyone who conceals relevant testimony bears moral responsibility even if the truth is hidden from others.

translation: To Allah belongs all that is in the heavens and all that is on the earth. Whether you disclose what is within yourselves or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, and Allah has power over all things.
interpretation: The verse teaches that faithfulness is not merely outward: inward intentions and commitments also lie within God’s knowledge and judgment. Yet the final reckoning belongs to Him alone, whose power encompasses both justice and forgiveness.

translation: The Messenger has believed in what was sent down to him from his Lord, and so have the believers. Each believes in God, His angels, His scriptures, and His messengers. “We make no distinction between any of His messengers.” They say, “We hear and obey. Your forgiveness, our Lord; to You is the final return.”
interpretation: The verse presents faith as wholehearted trust in God’s guidance rather than selective acceptance: honoring every messenger is joined to a willingness to obey, while asking forgiveness acknowledges human fallibility and the ultimate accountability of returning to God.

translation: Allah does not burden any soul beyond its capacity. It will have the good it has earned, and it will bear the evil it has earned. Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or make a mistake. Our Lord, do not lay upon us a burden as You laid upon those before us. Our Lord, do not burden us with what we cannot bear. Pardon us, forgive us, and have mercy on us. You are our Protector, so grant us victory over the disbelieving people.
interpretation: The verse teaches that divine accountability is just and within a person’s capacity, while also guiding believers to approach God with humility: asking that human forgetfulness and mistakes not lead to punishment, that unbearable burdens be lifted, and that pardon, forgiveness, and mercy be granted. Its closing appeal places their hope for strength and victory in God, their Protector.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Alif, Lam, Mim.
interpretation: The opening calls the reader to begin in Allah’s name, while Alif, Lam, Mim are among the Qur’an’s disjointed letters whose intended meaning is known to Allah.

translation: Allah—there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all.
interpretation: This affirms that ultimate divinity belongs to Allah alone: He possesses perfect, everlasting life and sustains all existence, while all else depends on Him.

translation: He has sent down to you the Book in truth, confirming what came before it; and He sent down the Torah and the Gospel.
interpretation: The verse presents the Qur’an as a revelation from God that continues the guidance given through earlier scriptures, affirming their divine origin and the shared truth at the heart of God’s message.

translation: Before, as guidance for mankind, and He sent down the Criterion. Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah’s signs will have a severe punishment; and Allah is Almighty, Possessor of retribution.
interpretation: The earlier revelations were sent as guidance, and the Criterion makes clear the distinction between truth and falsehood. Rejecting God’s signs is therefore a grave matter, while His might ensures that no rejection or wrongdoing escapes His just recompense.

translation: Indeed, nothing in the earth or in the heaven is hidden from Allah.
interpretation: The verse affirms that Allah’s knowledge is complete: no person’s actions, intentions, or circumstances escape Him, whether concealed or apparent. This calls people to sincerity and accountability, while assuring them that nothing they endure is unknown to Him.

translation: He is the One who shapes you in the wombs as He wills. There is no deity except Him, the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: Human beings do not determine the form in which they come into existence; their creation unfolds according to God’s will. His power over that creation is joined with wisdom, and therefore worship and ultimate trust belong to Him alone.

translation: It is He who sent down the Book to you. Some of its verses are clear and foundational, while others are ambiguous. Those whose hearts are inclined to deviation follow what is ambiguous in it, seeking discord and seeking its interpretation. None knows its ultimate interpretation except God. Those firmly grounded in knowledge say, “We believe in it; all of it is from our Lord.” Yet none take heed except people of understanding.
interpretation: The verse teaches that ambiguity in revelation calls for humility, not manipulation: people grounded in knowledge affirm the whole Book as coming from God, while those bent toward error exploit its less clear passages to provoke discord.

translation: Our Lord, do not let our hearts turn away after You have guided us, and grant us mercy from Yourself. Indeed, You are the Bestower.
interpretation: This is a prayer for steadfastness: even after receiving guidance, believers ask God to protect their hearts from straying and to sustain them through His mercy. Its wording reflects humility, recognizing that guidance and the strength to remain firm are gifts from God, who gives generously.

translation: Our Lord, surely You will gather all people for a Day about which there is no doubt. Indeed, Allah never fails in His promise.
interpretation: This prayer affirms complete trust in God’s promise of the Day of Resurrection: the certainty of that gathering gives believers confidence that every deed will be brought to account and every divine promise fulfilled.

translation: Those who disbelieve—their wealth and children will not avail them at all against God. They are the fuel of the Fire.
interpretation: The verse warns that worldly wealth and family cannot shield a person from God’s judgment; ultimate security comes not from such possessions but from faith and obedience to God.

translation: Like the way of Pharaoh’s people and those before them: they denied Our signs, so Allah seized them for their sins. And Allah is severe in punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns that rejecting God’s signs has consequences: as with earlier peoples, worldly power cannot shield a community from accountability when it persists in wrongdoing.

translation: Say to those who disbelieve: “You will be defeated and gathered into Hell—and what a wretched resting place!”
interpretation: The verse warns that rejecting the truth brings both humiliation and loss, and that worldly power cannot shield its rejecters from accountability before God.

translation: You already had a sign in the two forces that met: one fighting in the cause of God and the other unbelieving. They saw them with their own eyes as twice their number. God supports with His victory whoever He wills. Surely in this is a lesson for those who have insight.
interpretation: The encounter shows that victory is not secured by numbers alone: God can sustain those who strive in His cause against a seemingly stronger force. Those who look beyond outward appearances recognize in this a sign of God’s power and a reason to trust His support.

translation: Made alluring to people is the love of desirable things: women, children, heaps of gold and silver, fine horses, livestock, and cultivated land. These are the enjoyments of worldly life, while with God is the finest return.
interpretation: The verse recognizes the powerful appeal of worldly possessions and desires without declaring them evil in themselves. It cautions that their attraction is temporary and should not become life’s ultimate aim, for lasting fulfillment lies in turning toward God and the final return to Him.

translation: Say, “Shall I tell you of something better than all that? For those who are mindful of God, with their Lord are gardens beneath which rivers flow, where they will remain forever, and purified spouses, and God’s pleasure.” God sees His servants well.
interpretation: The verse teaches that lasting fulfillment is not found in worldly attractions but in a life lived with awareness of God and the enduring nearness and approval of God. His all-seeing knowledge assures that sincere devotion is never overlooked.

translation: Those who say, “Our Lord, we have indeed believed, so forgive us our sins and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.”
interpretation: True faith is joined with humility: believers acknowledge their need for God’s forgiveness and seek His protection from the consequences of sin.

translation: The patient, the truthful, the devoutly obedient, those who spend, and those who seek forgiveness in the hours before dawn.
interpretation: These are qualities of sincere devotion: steadfastness in hardship, truthfulness, humble obedience to God, generosity toward others, and seeking God’s forgiveness in the quiet hours before dawn.

translation: Allah bears witness that there is no deity except Him, as do the angels and those endowed with knowledge—upholding justice. There is no deity except Him, the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: The verse presents the oneness of God as a truth affirmed by God Himself and recognized by the angels and people of knowledge. His justice is inseparable from His rule, while His might and wisdom show that His authority is both absolute and perfectly ordered.

translation: Indeed, the religion with God is Islam. Those who were given the Scripture differed only after knowledge had come to them, out of mutual resentment. Whoever rejects God’s signs—God is swift in reckoning.
interpretation: The verse presents wholehearted submission to God as the heart of true religion, and warns that religious disagreement can arise not from a lack of guidance but from people’s own rivalries and desires. Knowledge therefore brings responsibility: rejecting clear signs is not without consequence.

translation: So if they argue with you, say, “I have submitted myself to God, and so have those who follow me.” And say to those who were given the Scripture and to the unlettered, “Have you submitted yourselves?” If they submit, they are rightly guided; but if they turn away, your duty is only to convey the message. And God sees His servants.
interpretation: The verse presents sincere submission to God as the heart of the Prophet’s call, shared by those who follow him. He is to invite all people to that submission, while leaving their response to them: his responsibility is to convey the message, and God fully sees and knows each person’s response.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah’s signs, kill the prophets unjustly, and kill those among the people who command justice—give them news of a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse condemns not only rejecting divine guidance but also using violence to silence those who uphold justice; the phrase “give them news” is a stark, ironic warning of the punishment their actions bring.

translation: Those are the ones whose deeds have come to nothing in this world and the Hereafter, and they will have no helpers.
interpretation: The verse teaches that deeds cannot ultimately benefit their doers when they are rejected by God; neither worldly support nor anyone’s intercession can then rescue them from the consequences.

translation: Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture? They are called to the Book of God so that it may judge between them, yet a group of them turns away, refusing to accept it.
interpretation: The verse criticizes those who claim a connection to divine revelation but resist its judgment when it conflicts with their preferences. Their turning away shows that possessing scripture is not enough; sincere faith requires accepting God’s guidance even when it challenges one’s desires.

translation: That is because they say, “The Fire will touch us only for a number of days,” and what they used to fabricate has deluded them about their religion.
interpretation: They had persuaded themselves that any punishment would be brief, relying on claims they had invented rather than sincere faith and accountability. The verse warns that religious self-deception can make people complacent about the consequences of their choices.

translation: How will it be when We gather them for a Day about which there is no doubt, and every soul is paid in full for what it has earned, and they are not wronged?
interpretation: The verse confronts those who presume they are secure from divine judgment: the gathering and reckoning are certain, and God’s justice means that no one’s deeds will be overlooked or recompense withheld.

translation: Say, “O Allah, Owner of all sovereignty, You grant sovereignty to whom You will and take it away from whom You will. You honor whom You will and humble whom You will. All good is in Your hand. Indeed, You have power over all things.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that power, honor, and their loss are not ultimately controlled by people; they remain subject to God’s will and wisdom. It therefore calls the believer to place trust in God rather than treating worldly status as permanent or self-earned.

translation: You cause the night to enter the day, and You cause the day to enter the night; You bring the living out of the dead, and the dead out of the living; and You provide for whom You will without measure.
