interpretation: The verse points to God’s complete sovereignty over the changing order of creation and the transformations within it. Since these realities unfold by His power, His giving is not confined by human expectations or calculation; provision comes according to His wisdom and will.

translation: Let not the believers take the disbelievers as allies in preference to the believers. Whoever does so has no bond with God—unless you are guarding yourselves against them as a precaution. God warns you to beware of Him, and to God is the return.
interpretation: The verse warns believers against giving those hostile to their faith the loyalty and allegiance owed to their fellow believers. It allows cautious, protective conduct when there is a real threat, without making that a license for betrayal or sincere allegiance to hostility. The closing warning reminds people that their choices are ultimately accountable to God.

translation: Say, “Whether you conceal what is in your hearts or reveal it, Allah knows it. He knows whatever is in the heavens and the earth, and Allah has power over all things.”
interpretation: The verse calls believers to sincerity: no hidden intention is beyond Allah’s knowledge, so faith and conduct should be made upright inwardly as well as outwardly. His complete knowledge and power also reassure believers that nothing lies beyond His awareness or ability.

translation: On the Day every soul will find whatever good it has done present before it, and whatever evil it has done, it will wish there were a great distance between itself and that evil. Allah warns you to beware of Him; yet Allah is Most Compassionate toward His servants.
interpretation: The verse teaches that no deed is lost: a person will face the reality of their actions and may deeply regret the wrong they chose. Allah’s warning calls people to turn away from sin before that day, while His compassion leaves the door to repentance and righteous action open.

translation: Say, “If you love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you and forgive you your sins. And Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.”
interpretation: The verse presents following the Prophet as the practical proof of sincere love for Allah: love is not merely claimed but shown through obedience. Such devotion brings Allah’s love and forgiveness, grounded in His mercy.

translation: Say, “Obey Allah and the Messenger.” But if they turn away, then indeed Allah does not love the disbelievers.
interpretation: Obedience to Allah and His Messenger is presented as the mark of sincere submission; knowingly turning away from that guidance is a rejection of faith and places a person among those whom Allah does not love.

translation: Indeed, God chose Adam, Noah, the family of Abraham, and the family of ʿImrān above all people.
interpretation: The verse presents prophethood and guidance as gifts granted by God’s choice. By naming these individuals and families, it points to the honored lineages through whom God conveyed revelation and called people to faith.

translation: Descendants, one from another. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: Their succession was joined not only by lineage but by shared faith and devotion; Allah hears what they say and knows the sincerity and goodness within them.

translation: When the wife of ʿImrān said, “My Lord, I have vowed to You what is in my womb, dedicated to Your service, so accept it from me. Surely You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.”
interpretation: Her vow expresses wholehearted devotion: she entrusts the child she carries to God’s service and asks God to accept that offering, knowing that He hears her prayer and knows the sincerity behind it.

translation: When she gave birth to her, she said, “My Lord, I have given birth to a female”—and God knew best what she had given birth to. “A male is not like a female. I have named her Mary, and I place her and her descendants in Your protection from Satan, the accursed.”
interpretation: The mother had expected a son for the service to which she had dedicated her child, and she recognizes that her daughter is not what she had anticipated. Yet God knows the greatness and purpose of the child she has been given. By naming Mary and asking God to protect her and her descendants, she entrusts their future to God, whose wisdom and care exceed her own expectations.

translation: So her Lord accepted her graciously, caused her to grow in a beautiful way, and placed her under the care of Zechariah. Whenever Zechariah entered the sanctuary to see her, he found provision with her. He said, “Mary, where did this come from?” She replied, “It is from God. Indeed, God provides for whom He wills without measure.”
interpretation: The verse portrays Mary’s life as a sign of God’s special care: He nurtures her, provides for her in ways beyond ordinary expectation, and teaches those who witness it that provision ultimately comes from Him, unconstrained by human calculations.

translation: Thereupon Zachariah called upon his Lord, saying, “My Lord, grant me from Yourself good offspring. Surely You hear every supplication.”
interpretation: Zachariah’s prayer expresses trust that God can grant what lies beyond ordinary means, and that He hears the sincere longing of His servants. By asking for “good” offspring, he seeks not merely a child, but one blessed with righteousness.

translation: Then the angels called to him while he was standing in prayer in the sanctuary: “God gives you good news of John, who will confirm a word from God, and will be noble, chaste, and a prophet among the righteous.”
interpretation: The verse presents Yahya’s mission as closely connected to the divine message he would affirm—commonly understood as a reference to Jesus—and portrays prophetic honor as moral as well as spiritual: “noble” suggests excellence and leadership in virtue, while “chaste” points to disciplined restraint. The setting of Zakariya’s prayer also emphasizes that this glad tidings comes as a response to devoted supplication.

translation: He said, “My Lord, how can I have a son when old age has overtaken me and my wife is barren?” He said, “Thus does Allah do whatever He wills.”
interpretation: Zachariah’s question expresses astonishment at the promise, given his age and his wife’s barrenness, rather than denial of God’s power. The reply teaches that God’s will is not confined by ordinary causes or human expectations.

translation: He said, “My Lord, appoint a sign for me.” He said, “Your sign is that you will not speak to people for three days except by gesture. And remember your Lord often, and glorify Him in the evening and at dawn.”
interpretation: His inability to speak was a divinely given sign confirming the promise he had received, not a barrier to worship. While he communicated through gestures, he was to devote himself especially to remembering and glorifying God.

translation: And when the angels said, “O Mary, indeed God has chosen you, purified you, and chosen you above the women of all worlds.”
interpretation: Mary’s distinction is presented as a gift of divine favor: her purity and honored rank prepare her for a singular role in God’s plan. The verse invites recognition that true honor lies in God’s choice and in a life made worthy through devotion.

translation: O Mary, be devoutly obedient to your Lord, prostrate yourself, and bow with those who bow.
interpretation: Mary is called to devote herself wholly to God through humble worship, while joining the community of worshippers rather than standing apart from them.

translation: That is part of the news of the unseen which We reveal to you. You were not with them when they cast their pens to determine which of them would care for Mary, nor were you with them when they disputed.
interpretation: The verse presents this account as knowledge granted to the Prophet through revelation, not something he witnessed or learned from those involved. It therefore points to revelation as the source of his knowledge of these hidden events and affirms the divine origin of his message.

translation: When the angels said, “O Mary, God gives you good news of a word from Him: his name will be the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, honored in this world and the Hereafter, and among those brought near.”
interpretation: Calling Jesus “a word from Him” emphasizes that his existence comes about through God’s creative command, while the honor and nearness he receives are gifts from God. The verse thus presents his extraordinary origin and exalted rank without making him independent of his Creator.

translation: He will speak to people in the cradle and in maturity, and he will be among the righteous.
interpretation: Jesus’s speech in infancy is a sign of God’s extraordinary favor, while his maturity among the righteous points to a life marked by steadfast devotion and virtue.

translation: She said, “My Lord, how can I have a child when no man has touched me?” He said, “Thus Allah creates whatever He wills. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, ‘Be,’ and it is.”
interpretation: The response teaches that Allah’s creative power is not bound by the usual causes of human birth. Mary’s child will come about by His will and command, even without a father.

translation: And He will teach him the Book and wisdom, and the Torah and the Gospel.
interpretation: God’s teaching of Jesus encompasses divine revelation and wisdom, affirming that his mission is rooted in the same tradition of guidance conveyed through the Torah and the Gospel.

translation: And [He made him] a messenger to the Children of Israel, [who said], “I have come to you with a sign from your Lord: I fashion for you from clay something in the shape of a bird, then breathe into it, and it becomes a bird by Allah’s permission. I heal those born blind and the lepers, and bring the dead to life by Allah’s permission. And I tell you what you eat and what you store in your homes. Surely in this is a sign for you, if you are believers.”
interpretation: The repeated phrase “by Allah’s permission” makes clear that these extraordinary signs are not powers independent of God; they are granted through the messenger as evidence of his mission and an invitation to believe.

translation: And [I have come] confirming what was before me of the Torah, and to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you. I have come to you with a sign from your Lord, so be mindful of Allah and obey me.
interpretation: Jesus presents his mission as continuous with the revelation given to Moses, while explaining that the easing of certain prohibitions is by God’s authority, not his own. The sign from God confirms this authority; therefore, true reverence for God entails following the messenger He has sent.

translation: Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is the straight path.
interpretation: True guidance rests on recognizing Allah as the Lord of all and directing worship to Him alone; this devotion is the sound, upright way.

translation: When Jesus sensed disbelief from them, he said, “Who will be my helpers in the cause of Allah?” The disciples replied, “We are Allah’s helpers. We believe in Allah, and bear witness that we submit to Him.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the disciples’ response as a declaration of loyal support for Jesus’ mission because it serves Allah, grounded in faith and wholehearted submission to Him.

translation: Our Lord, we believe in what You have revealed and follow the Messenger, so include us among the witnesses.
interpretation: The disciples affirm that their faith is grounded in God’s revelation and shown through following His Messenger. They ask God to count them among those who bear witness to the truth with sincere belief and steadfast commitment.

translation: They plotted, and Allah planned; and Allah is the best of planners.
interpretation: Those who opposed Jesus devised a scheme against him, but God brought their plans to nothing and fulfilled His own purpose. God’s “planning” here means His wise and just response that overcomes wrongdoing, not deceit.

translation: When God said, “O Jesus, I will take you and raise you to Myself, and purify you from those who disbelieve. I will make those who follow you prevail over those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection. Then to Me you will all return, and I will judge between you concerning what you used to differ about.”
interpretation: The verse reassures Jesus that human opposition cannot thwart God’s purpose: God will vindicate and protect him, while the lasting resolution of disputes about him belongs to God, who alone will judge with complete knowledge and justice.

translation: As for those who disbelieve, I will punish them severely in this world and the Hereafter, and they will have no helpers.
interpretation: The verse warns that rejecting faith has consequences in both worldly life and the Hereafter, and that no ally can ultimately shield those who face God’s judgment.

translation: As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, He will grant them their rewards in full. And Allah does not love the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse reassures believers that their faith and good deeds will not go unrewarded, while affirming that injustice is contrary to what Allah loves.

translation: This is what We recite to you of the signs and the wise reminder.
interpretation: The account just given is presented as divine revelation: its truth and guidance come from God, and its wisdom calls people to reflect and be rightly guided.

translation: Indeed, the likeness of Jesus in the sight of Allah is like that of Adam: He created him from dust, then said to him, “Be,” and he was.
interpretation: The verse teaches that Jesus’ miraculous creation does not make him divine: Adam was created without either parent, while Jesus was created without a father. Both came into being by Allah’s command, demonstrating His power to create as He wills.

translation: The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among those who doubt.
interpretation: This affirms that what God has revealed is true and calls the Prophet—and, through him, the believers—to remain steadfast in that certainty rather than be shaken by doubt.

translation: Whoever disputes with you about him after the knowledge that has come to you, say: “Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, and ourselves and yourselves; then let us pray earnestly and invoke God’s curse upon the liars.”
interpretation: The verse presents the challenge of mutual prayer as a solemn appeal to God when dispute persists despite clear knowledge: each side is to come with those nearest to them and ask God to expose falsehood. It teaches that speaking about divine matters carries serious accountability, and that truth should be sought with humility before God rather than defended through empty argument.

translation: Indeed, this is the true account, and there is no god except Allah. Surely Allah is the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the account just given is grounded in truth, not speculation, and that its central implication is the exclusive divinity of Allah. His might means no rival can share His authority, while His wisdom points to the purpose and perfect judgment behind His decree.

translation: But if they turn away, then surely Allah knows those who spread corruption.
interpretation: Turning away from the truth does not obscure a person’s motives or conduct; Allah knows fully who is committed to corruption.

translation: Say, “O People of the Scripture, come to a common word between us and you: that we worship none but God, associate nothing with Him, and do not take one another as lords besides God.” But if they turn away, say, “Bear witness that we are submitting to God.”
interpretation: The verse calls people of different scriptural communities to a shared principle: ultimate worship and devotion belong to God alone. No person or religious authority should be given a status that competes with God’s, and the invitation is made through clear, common ground rather than coercion. If others decline, believers are to remain steadfast in their own submission to God.

translation: O People of the Book, why do you argue about Abraham when the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed until after him? Will you not reason?
interpretation: The verse challenges the People of the Book to set aside claims shaped by later religious identities: Abraham lived before either scripture was revealed, so such claims cannot be justified by them. It calls them to reason fairly about his faith rather than argue from anachronistic labels.

translation: Here you are, arguing about matters of which you have knowledge; why, then, do you argue about matters of which you have no knowledge? Allah knows, while you do not know.
interpretation: The verse warns against making confident claims about religious matters without sound knowledge. Human understanding is limited, so disputes should be guided by evidence and humility before Allah, whose knowledge is complete.

translation: Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian; rather, he was upright, devoted in submission to God, and was not one of the polytheists.
interpretation: The verse presents Abraham’s faith as sincere devotion to the one God, not as belonging to religious identities that arose later. His example is one of turning away from every form of associating partners with God and submitting wholly to Him.

translation: Indeed, the people most entitled to Abraham are those who followed him, this Prophet, and those who believe. And Allah is the protector of the believers.
interpretation: True closeness to Abraham is not established by ancestry, but by following his devotion to God. The Prophet and the believers are therefore most entitled to his legacy, and Allah supports and cares for those who believe.

translation: A group among the People of the Book wished to lead you astray, but they lead none astray except themselves, though they do not realize it.
interpretation: Their attempts to turn believers away from the truth ultimately bring harm upon their own souls, while they remain unaware of the consequence.

translation: O People of the Book, why do you disbelieve in the signs of Allah when you yourselves bear witness?
interpretation: The verse reproaches those who reject God’s signs despite recognizing their truth, calling them to act consistently with the knowledge they already possess.

translation: O People of the Scripture, why do you mingle truth with falsehood and conceal the truth while you know?
interpretation: The verse rebukes those who knowingly blur the distinction between truth and falsehood and hide what they recognize as true. Their knowledge makes this concealment a deliberate betrayal of truth, not an innocent mistake.

translation: A group among the People of the Book said, “Believe in what was sent down to those who believe at the beginning of the day, and reject it at its end, so that they may turn back.”
interpretation: This describes a deliberate attempt to shake the believers’ confidence: by outwardly embracing the revelation and then publicly rejecting it, the group hoped to make others doubt its truth and abandon their faith.

translation: “Do not trust anyone except those who follow your religion.” Say, “True guidance is Allah’s guidance.” [They say this] lest anyone else be granted the like of what you were given, or contend with you before your Lord. Say, “All bounty is in Allah’s hand; He grants it to whomever He wills. Allah is all-encompassing, all-knowing.”
interpretation: The verse challenges the attempt to claim exclusive ownership of divine guidance and favor. Allah’s gifts are not restricted by people’s religious boundaries or fears of being challenged; He grants them according to His wisdom, and His knowledge and bounty encompass all.

translation: He singles out for His mercy whom He wills, and Allah is the Possessor of great bounty.
interpretation: Allah’s mercy is a gift bestowed according to His wisdom, not something people can claim as their due or restrict to those they choose; His generosity is abundant beyond measure.

translation: Among the People of the Book is one who, if you entrust him with a treasure, will return it to you; and among them is one who, if you entrust him with a single gold coin, will not return it to you unless you keep pressing him. That is because they say, “We are not accountable regarding the unlettered people.” And they knowingly attribute a lie to God.
interpretation: The verse condemns those who use religious or communal distinction as an excuse to betray the trust of people outside their own group. It also makes clear that such conduct is not shared by everyone among the People of the Book, but is a deliberate wrong for which its perpetrators are accountable.

translation: Indeed, whoever fulfills their covenant and is mindful of God—God loves those who are mindful of Him.
interpretation: True righteousness is shown by honoring one’s commitments and remaining conscious of God; such integrity is beloved by God.

translation: Indeed, those who trade God’s covenant and their oaths for a small price will have no share in the Hereafter. God will neither speak to them nor look upon them on the Day of Resurrection, nor purify them; and they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns against knowingly betraying a solemn commitment to God and using oaths to gain worldly benefit. Its severe language portrays the ultimate consequence of such deceit: exclusion from God’s favor and purification, followed by painful punishment.

translation: And indeed, among them is a group who twist their tongues while reciting the Scripture, so that you may think it is part of the Scripture, though it is not part of the Scripture. They say, “It is from God,” though it is not from God, and they knowingly attribute lies to God.
interpretation: The verse warns against deliberately distorting revelation through speech and presenting human fabrication as divine truth. Its condemnation is especially grave because those who do this know that their claims are false.

translation: It is not for any human being to whom God has given the Scripture, wisdom, and prophethood to say to people, “Be servants to me instead of God.” Rather, he would say, “Be devoted servants of the Lord, because you teach the Scripture and study it.”
interpretation: True prophethood directs people toward God, never toward the prophet’s own worship. A person entrusted with revelation is to cultivate people as learned, God-centered servants through teaching and studying Scripture.

translation: Nor would he command you to take the angels and the prophets as lords. Would he command you to disbelieve after you had submitted to God?
interpretation: A true prophet calls people to worship God alone, not to elevate prophets or angels into objects of worship. Such a command would contradict the very faith and submission he teaches.

translation: And [remember] when Allah took the covenant of the prophets: “Whatever I have given you of Scripture and wisdom, then when a messenger comes to you confirming what is with you, you must believe in him and support him.” He said, “Do you affirm this and accept My commitment on these terms?” They said, “We affirm.” He said, “Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses.”
interpretation: The verse presents divine revelation as one connected message: the prophets are bound to recognize and support a messenger who confirms the truth they received. Their covenant underscores that loyalty to God’s guidance requires accepting its confirmation, rather than treating earlier revelation as a reason to reject what comes afterward.

translation: Whoever turns away after that—those are the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: After the truth and its implications have been made clear, turning away is not a mere lapse; it is a deliberate departure from obedience to God.

translation: Do they seek a way of life other than Allah’s, when all who are in the heavens and the earth submit to Him, willingly or unwillingly, and to Him they will be returned?
interpretation: The verse challenges the idea that anyone can ultimately stand outside Allah’s authority. All creation is subject to His will; people may accept that truth willingly or resist it, but none can escape the reality of their dependence on Him or their return to Him. It calls people to embrace consciously the submission that already governs all existence.

translation: Say, “We believe in Allah, in what has been sent down to us, in what was sent down to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Tribes, and in what Moses, Jesus, and the prophets were given by their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and to Him we submit.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that genuine faith accepts the prophets and the revelations entrusted to them as one continuous guidance from Allah, rather than choosing among them according to preference. Submission to Allah therefore entails honoring every prophet while worshipping and obeying Allah alone.

translation: Whoever seeks a religion other than Islam, it will never be accepted from him, and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers.
interpretation: The verse teaches that true devotion is surrender to God and faithful acceptance of the guidance He has sent. A person’s chosen path cannot replace that submission; turning away from God’s guidance carries consequences beyond this life.

translation: How would Allah guide a people who disbelieved after having believed, testified that the Messenger is true, and received clear proofs? Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: The verse condemns a deliberate rejection of truth after it has been recognized and made clear. Their wrongdoing is the cause of their being deprived of Allah’s guidance; it does not imply that sincere repentance is impossible.

translation: Those—their recompense is that upon them is the curse of Allah, the angels, and all people.
interpretation: The verse portrays their consequence as being cast away from divine mercy, with the condemnation of the angels and all people affirming the gravity of their rejection of the truth.

translation: They will remain therein; the punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be given respite.
interpretation: The verse conveys the severity and enduring nature of the punishment: those addressed will find neither relief from its intensity nor a delay that offers them reprieve.

translation: Except those who repent thereafter and make amends—for indeed Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse teaches that sincere repentance is shown through reform, and that those who turn back to Allah in this way may hope in His forgiveness and mercy.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve after having believed, then increase in disbelief—their repentance will never be accepted, and it is they who are astray.
interpretation: The verse warns of people who persist in rejecting faith and deepen that rejection until repentance is no longer sincere or possible—when they face death. Their condition is not beyond forgiveness while they genuinely turn back in time; rather, it is their continued defiance that leaves them astray.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and die as disbelievers—none of them would be accepted even an earthful of gold, were he to offer it as ransom. They will have a painful punishment, and they will have no helpers.
interpretation: The verse teaches that wealth cannot buy deliverance from the consequences of dying in disbelief: no amount offered as ransom can replace faith or avert the punishment, and no one will be able to help.

translation: You will never attain true righteousness until you give from what you love. Whatever you give, Allah knows it fully.
interpretation: True devotion is shown by being willing to give what is genuinely precious to you, rather than only what is easy to part with. Allah knows the worth and sincerity of every act of giving.

translation: All food was lawful for the Children of Israel, except what Israel had forbidden himself before the Torah was revealed. Say, “Bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful.”
interpretation: The verse distinguishes Jacob’s personal abstention from a divine prohibition: it was not a rule imposed on all the Children of Israel. It challenges those attributing such a restriction to God to support their claim from the Torah itself.

translation: Whoever fabricates a lie against God after that—those are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: Knowingly attributing falsehood to God after the truth has been clarified is a grave injustice: it distorts divine guidance and wrongs both oneself and those who may be misled by it.

translation: Say, “Allah has spoken the truth. So follow the way of Abraham, who was devoted to pure monotheism; he was not among the polytheists.”
interpretation: The verse calls people to make Abraham’s sincere devotion to the one God their guide, turning away from every form of associating partners with Him.

translation: Indeed, the first House established for humanity was the one at Bakkah, blessed and a guidance for all people.
interpretation: The verse presents the Kaaba as a sacred center of worship whose blessing and guidance reach beyond any one community, calling people toward devotion to God.

translation: In it are clear signs, including the Station of Abraham. Whoever enters it is safe. Pilgrimage to the House is a duty owed to Allah by all people who are able to make their way there. And whoever rejects this duty—Allah is truly independent of all the worlds.
interpretation: The verse presents the Sacred House as a place marked by enduring signs of God, with the Station of Abraham recalling the faith and devotion associated with its foundations. Its sanctuary is a refuge, and the pilgrimage obligation applies according to a person’s ability; refusing it does not diminish God, who depends on no one.

translation: Say, “O People of the Scripture, why do you disbelieve in the signs of God, while God is witness to what you do?”
interpretation: The verse rebukes those who knowingly reject God’s signs, reminding them that their actions are fully known to Him and cannot be concealed.

translation: Say, “O People of the Book, why do you turn those who believe away from the path of Allah, seeking to make it seem crooked, while you yourselves bear witness? Allah is not unaware of what you do.”
interpretation: The verse condemns knowingly obstructing people from faith and distorting its truth, especially when one has clear knowledge of it. It warns that such conduct is fully known to Allah and will not escape His judgment.

translation: O you who believe, if you obey a group of those who were given the Scripture, they will turn you back, after your faith, into disbelievers.
interpretation: This is a warning to believers to remain firm in their faith and not let the influence or arguments of a hostile group undermine it. The verse speaks of a particular group, not a blanket judgment about everyone given Scripture.

translation: How can you disbelieve while God’s verses are recited to you and His Messenger is among you? Whoever holds fast to God has indeed been guided to a straight path.
interpretation: The verse presents disbelief as especially difficult to justify when divine guidance is being made clear through revelation and the Messenger’s presence. It urges the believers to remain firmly reliant on God, since steadfast attachment to Him is the way to sound guidance.

translation: O you who believe, be mindful of Allah as He truly deserves, and do not die except in a state of submission to Him.
interpretation: The verse calls believers to sincere, wholehearted devotion to Allah and to sustain that commitment throughout their lives, so that when death comes they are found steadfast in submission to Him.

translation: And hold fast, all together, to the rope of Allah, and do not divide. Remember Allah’s favor upon you: when you were enemies, He brought your hearts together, and by His favor you became brothers. You were on the brink of a pit of Fire, and He rescued you from it. Thus Allah makes His signs clear to you so that you may be guided.
interpretation: The verse teaches that unity grounded in devotion to Allah is itself a divine mercy: it can transform deep hostility into fellowship and rescue people from the ruin toward which their divisions lead. Remembering this gift should lead believers to preserve their bonds and seek guidance in Allah’s signs.

translation: Let there be among you a community that calls to what is good, enjoins what is right, and forbids what is wrong. Those are the ones who will succeed.
interpretation: The verse teaches that a community’s success depends not only on individual goodness, but also on taking shared responsibility for guiding society toward what is beneficial and resisting what harms it.

translation: And do not be like those who became divided and differed after clear proofs had come to them. Those will have a tremendous punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns believers that division over matters made clear by revelation is not a harmless disagreement: it can reflect a departure from guidance and bring grave accountability. It calls for holding fast to the truth with humility and resisting the impulses that turn differences into schism.

translation: On the Day when some faces will shine bright and others will grow dark, those whose faces have grown dark will be told: “Did you disbelieve after having believed? Then taste the punishment for your persistent disbelief.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the Day of Judgment as a moment when a person’s inward response to faith is made manifest. The rebuke to those whose faces are dark underscores the gravity of turning away from belief after accepting it, and the punishment is presented as the consequence of their chosen disbelief.

translation: As for those whose faces are radiant, they will be within Allah’s mercy, abiding there forever.
interpretation: The radiance of their faces signifies the joy and honor of those who are accepted by God. Their lasting place within His mercy points to a security and felicity that do not end.

translation: These are the signs of Allah that We recite to you in truth, and Allah does not intend injustice for any of the worlds.
interpretation: The verse affirms that Allah’s message and judgment are grounded in truth: He wrongs no one, and no person or community is treated unjustly in what they are given or held accountable for.

translation: To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and to Allah all affairs return.
interpretation: This verse teaches that no power or possession is ultimately independent of God. Human choices and worldly events may seem to unfold beyond our control, but their final outcome and judgment rest with Him, inviting trust in His authority and accountability for our actions.

translation: You are the best community brought forth for humankind: you enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and believe in Allah. If the People of the Book had believed, it would have been better for them. Among them are believers, but most of them are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: The honor given to this community is tied to its faith and its responsibility to uphold what is right and resist wrongdoing; it is not a license for pride or wrongdoing. The verse also distinguishes among the People of the Book, affirming that they are not all alike.

translation: They will never harm you except with hurtful annoyance; and if they fight you, they will turn their backs, then they will not be helped.
interpretation: The verse offers reassurance that hostile opposition may cause distress, but it will not ultimately prevail. Believers are encouraged to remain steadfast, trusting that aggression without lasting support will end in retreat.

translation: Humiliation was imposed upon them wherever they were encountered, except through a bond with God and a bond with people. They incurred God’s wrath, and misery was imposed upon them. That was because they rejected God’s signs and killed the prophets unjustly; that was because they disobeyed and transgressed.
interpretation: The verse presents humiliation and hardship as the consequence of persistent rejection of God’s signs, unjust violence against prophets, and habitual disobedience. The exception of a bond with God and a bond with people points to protection through divine terms and human agreements, rather than an unconditional security.

translation: They are not all alike. Among the People of the Scripture is an upright community who recite God’s revelations during the night and prostrate themselves.
interpretation: The verse cautions against judging the People of the Scripture as one group: some are sincere in faith, devoted to worship, and steadfast in their obedience to God.

translation: They believe in Allah and the Last Day, enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and hasten to do good. Those are among the righteous.
interpretation: The verse portrays righteousness as faith made active: belief in Allah and accountability in the Hereafter should shape how people guide one another and prompt them to pursue good without delay.

translation: Whatever good they do will never be denied them, and Allah knows those who are mindful of Him.
interpretation: No good deed done by the God-conscious is lost or overlooked; Allah knows their devotion and will fully recognize their deeds.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve will be of no avail against Allah at all, neither their wealth nor their children. They are the companions of the Fire, where they will remain forever.
interpretation: The verse teaches that worldly power and family ties cannot protect anyone from God’s judgment; lasting security comes not from possessions or status, but from turning to God in faith.

translation: The likeness of what they spend in this worldly life is that of a wind carrying bitter cold, which strikes the crops of people who have wronged themselves and destroys them. Allah has not wronged them; rather, they wrong themselves.
interpretation: The verse teaches that worldly spending cannot bring lasting benefit or salvation when it is cut off from faith and obedience to God. Like a crop ruined by a devastating wind, its expected reward is lost—not through injustice from Allah, but through the people’s own choices.

translation: O you who believe, do not take as intimate confidants those outside your own ranks. They spare no effort to harm you; they wish you hardship. Hatred has already shown in their words, and what their hearts conceal is even greater. We have made the signs clear to you, if you will reason.
interpretation: The verse warns believers against entrusting their most private affairs to people whose hostility and intent to harm them are evident. Its concern is betrayal and malicious counsel, not a license to mistreat others merely because they differ in faith or community.

translation: Here you are, loving them, while they do not love you. You believe in the whole Book. When they meet you, they say, “We believe,” but when they are alone, they bite their fingertips in rage against you. Say, “Die in your rage.” Surely God knows what is within the hearts.
interpretation: The verse exposes the contrast between the believers’ sincere regard and their opponents’ concealed hostility: outward professions of faith cannot hide inward resentment from God. “Die in your rage” is a forceful assurance that such malice will not overturn God’s truth or the believers’ faith; what is hidden in the heart is already known to Him.

translation: If good fortune touches you, it grieves them; but if hardship befalls you, they rejoice. Yet if you remain patient and mindful of God, their scheming will not harm you at all. God encompasses all that they do.
interpretation: The verse reassures believers that hostile people’s reactions and schemes do not determine their ultimate security. Patient steadfastness and mindfulness of God keep them from being overcome by that hostility, while God fully knows and oversees the schemes and actions of those who oppose them.

translation: And [remember] when you set out from your family early in the day, assigning the believers their positions for battle. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: The verse recalls the Prophet’s careful preparation of the believers for battle, showing that reliance on God goes hand in hand with disciplined planning. God hears what is said and knows the intentions and circumstances behind every action.

translation: When two groups among you were about to lose heart, though Allah was their Protector. So let the believers place their trust in Allah.
interpretation: The verse teaches that a moment of fear or wavering does not mean a believer has been abandoned: Allah was caring for those two groups even as they faltered. Trust in Him is therefore the believers’ steady reliance on His protection and guidance, especially when courage is tested.

translation: God certainly helped you at Badr when you were weak and outnumbered. So be mindful of God, that you may be grateful.
interpretation: The victory at Badr was a favor from God, not something the believers could attribute to their own strength. Remembering that support should lead them to obey God and respond with gratitude.

translation: When you said to the believers, “Is it not enough for you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?”
interpretation: The verse recalls reassurance given to the believers in a moment of danger: God’s promised aid was meant to strengthen their hearts and confidence. The angels are instruments of that aid, while victory and support ultimately come from God.

translation: Yes indeed. If you are patient and mindful of God, and they attack you at once, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels, distinguished by marks.
interpretation: God’s promised aid is tied to steadfastness and reverent obedience: believers are to remain firm and mindful of Him even when danger comes suddenly, trusting that He can grant them support beyond what they can see.

translation: Allah made it only as good tidings for you and so that your hearts might be reassured by it. Victory comes only from Allah, the Almighty, the Wise.
interpretation: The promised aid is a reassurance and a sign of hope, not the source of victory in itself. Believers are taught to place their trust in Allah, whose power and wisdom alone bring victory.

translation: So that He might cut off a part of those who disbelieve, or humble them, so that they return disappointed.
interpretation: The verse presents the setback of the disbelievers as serving God’s purpose: whether their strength is reduced or their pride broken, their hostility does not secure the outcome they seek. It also reminds believers that victory and defeat are ultimately subject to God’s wisdom.

translation: You have no say in the matter. He may turn to them in mercy or punish them, for they are indeed wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse teaches that ultimate judgment belongs to God alone: the Prophet cannot decide whether wrongdoers are forgiven or punished. Their fate rests with God, who may accept their repentance or hold them accountable.

translation: To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. And Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: All creation belongs to Allah, and ultimate judgment rests with Him alone. His forgiveness and punishment are exercised with perfect knowledge and wisdom, while His attributes of forgiveness and mercy invite people to seek His pardon and hope in His compassion.

translation: O you who believe, do not consume usury, multiplied many times over; and be mindful of Allah, so that you may prosper.
interpretation: The verse warns believers against exploiting people through usurious dealings and calls them to conduct their affairs with consciousness of God. The phrase “multiplied many times over” evokes the severe debt burdens such practices could create; it is not a permission for usury at lower rates. True prosperity is linked to obedience to God rather than unjust gain.

translation: And fear the Fire prepared for those who disbelieve.
interpretation: This is a warning to guard oneself from God’s punishment by turning away from disbelief and living in obedience to Him.

translation: And obey Allah and the Messenger so that you may receive mercy.
interpretation: The verse calls believers to follow God’s guidance and the Messenger’s teaching, seeking the mercy that comes through faithful obedience.

translation: And hasten toward forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden as vast as the heavens and the earth, prepared for the God-conscious.
interpretation: The command to hasten teaches that seeking God’s forgiveness and living in obedience should not be postponed; the Garden’s immense breadth emphasizes the generosity of the reward prepared for those who are mindful of God.

translation: Those who spend in times of ease and hardship, restrain their anger, and pardon people—Allah loves those who do good.
interpretation: The verse presents goodness as a discipline of the heart: a person remains generous when circumstances change, does not let anger govern their response, and chooses forgiveness over retaliation. Such conduct is not weakness; it is an expression of moral excellence that seeks Allah’s pleasure.

translation: And those who, when they commit an indecency or wrong themselves, remember God and seek forgiveness for their sins—and who can forgive sins except God?—and do not knowingly persist in what they have done.
interpretation: The verse presents repentance as a return to moral clarity: remembering God interrupts the pull of wrongdoing, while seeking forgiveness acknowledges that no one can erase sin apart from Him. Its emphasis is not on never having fallen, but on refusing to make wrongdoing a settled way of life once its truth is recognized.

translation: Those— their reward is forgiveness from their Lord and gardens beneath which rivers flow, where they will remain forever. How excellent is the reward of those who strive!
interpretation: The verse teaches that sincere obedience and striving for good are met not merely with pardon for past faults, but with lasting nearness to God; this enduring reward is presented as the finest outcome for those who work faithfully.

translation: Patterns of life have indeed passed before you, so travel through the land and see what was the end of those who denied the truth.
interpretation: The verse calls people to learn from the fate of earlier communities: rejecting truth and persisting in wrongdoing have consequences. Reflecting on their history should awaken humility and encourage people to heed guidance before the same outcome befalls them.

translation: This is a clear explanation for all people, and guidance and admonition for those mindful of God.
interpretation: The verse points to the Qur’an’s ability to make divine truths and the patterns of human life clear to everyone, while its guidance and admonition are especially received by those who are mindful of God and willing to learn from it.

translation: Do not lose heart or grieve, for you will have the upper hand if you are believers.
interpretation: The verse teaches that faith should keep believers steadfast through hardship: a setback need not define them, because their true strength and honor come from remaining faithful to God.

translation: If a wound has touched you, a similar wound has touched the other people. Such days We alternate among people, so that Allah may make evident those who believe and take martyrs from among you. Allah does not love the wrongdoers.
interpretation: Victory and setback are not permanent measures of who is right; their changing turns test faith and bring it into the open. Even amid loss, those who remain steadfast may be honored as martyrs, while wrongdoing remains hateful to God.

translation: And so that Allah may purify those who believe and utterly efface the disbelievers.
interpretation: Hardship distinguishes and refines the believers, while it causes the disbelievers’ strength and influence to be diminished.

translation: Or did you think you would enter Paradise before God had made evident those among you who strive and those who remain steadfast?
interpretation: The verse teaches that faith is tested through hardship: striving for God’s sake and remaining patient become manifest in a person’s actions. God’s knowing is not acquired through these trials; rather, they reveal what people choose and do.

translation: You used to long for death before you encountered it; now you have seen it before your eyes.
interpretation: The verse reminds the believers who had yearned for martyrdom that facing death in battle is a grave test: their longing was now being put to the test in the reality they witnessed.

translation: Muhammad is only a messenger; messengers have passed away before him. If he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels? Whoever turns back will not harm Allah in the least. And Allah will reward those who are grateful.
interpretation: The verse teaches that faith and commitment to Allah must not depend on the continued presence of the Prophet. His death would not undo the truth he conveyed; turning away would only harm those who abandon their faith, while Allah rewards those who remain steadfast and grateful.

translation: No soul can die except by Allah’s permission, at a term appointed. Whoever desires the reward of this world, We grant him some of it; and whoever desires the reward of the Hereafter, We grant him some of it. And We will reward the grateful.
interpretation: The verse reassures believers that neither fear nor human action can bring death before its divinely appointed time, so they should not abandon faith or duty out of fear. It also directs them to examine what they seek: worldly gains may be granted, but lasting reward belongs to those who turn toward the Hereafter and remain grateful to Allah.

translation: How many a prophet fought, accompanied by many devoted servants of God; yet they did not lose heart over what befell them in God’s cause, nor did they weaken or give in. God loves those who are steadfast.
interpretation: The verse teaches that hardship and loss do not make faithful people abandon what is right. Those devoted to God remain steadfast without losing courage or surrendering to their opponents, trusting that God loves and supports the patient.

translation: Their only words were: “Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our excesses in our affairs, make our feet firm, and grant us victory over the disbelieving people.”
interpretation: The verse portrays believers responding to hardship by turning humbly to God: they acknowledge both their sins and their excesses, ask for steadfastness, and seek His help in facing their opponents. It teaches that perseverance and victory are sought through repentance and reliance on God.

translation: So Allah gave them the reward of this world and the best reward of the Hereafter. And Allah loves those who do good.
interpretation: Those who remain sincere and steadfast in obedience may receive blessings in this life, but the greater reward is with Allah in the Hereafter. Their excellence in faith and conduct is beloved to Him.

translation: O you who believe, if you obey those who disbelieve, they will turn you back on your heels, and you will become losers.
interpretation: This warns believers not to follow those who reject faith when doing so would lead them away from God’s guidance. Such obedience can undo their spiritual progress and bring them loss in this life and the Hereafter.

translation: Rather, Allah is your Protector, and He is the best of helpers.
interpretation: True protection and help come from Allah; no ally can match His support, so believers should place their trust in Him.

translation: We will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve because they associate with Allah that for which He has sent down no authority. Their refuge will be the Fire—how wretched is the abode of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse presents the terror that overtakes the disbelievers as a consequence of their baseless association of partners with Allah: they have no divine warrant for it. It also warns that their ultimate abode is the Fire, a fittingly wretched end for those who persist in wrongdoing.

translation: God certainly fulfilled His promise to you when, by His permission, you were cutting them down—until you lost heart, disputed about the command, and disobeyed after He had shown you what you desired. Some of you wanted the present world, while others wanted the Hereafter. Then He turned you away from them to test you; yet He pardoned you. God is gracious to the believers.
interpretation: The verse teaches that victory is not a guarantee detached from faithfulness: at Uhud, the believers’ success was followed by a trial when some faltered and contested the command. Their mixed motives exposed the need for steadfast obedience, but the setback was not abandonment by God. His pardon and continuing grace show that believers may learn from failure and return to Him with renewed trust.

translation: When you were climbing away, turning to no one, while the Messenger was calling you from behind, He then afflicted you with distress upon distress, so that you would not grieve over what had passed you by or what had befallen you. And Allah is fully aware of what you do.
interpretation: In the aftermath of Uhud, the believers’ flight and their failure to answer the Messenger’s call brought one anguish after another. This hardship also redirected their attention from mourning what they had lost or suffered toward recognizing the consequences of their actions; nothing they did was hidden from Allah.

translation: Then, after distress, He sent down upon you reassurance—a drowsiness that came over a group of you. Another group was consumed by concern for themselves, thinking wrongly of Allah, as people of ignorance do. They said, “Do we have any say in the matter?” Say, “The whole matter belongs to Allah.” They conceal within themselves what they do not disclose to you, saying, “Had we had any say in the matter, we would not have been killed here.” Say, “Even if you had been in your homes, those decreed to be killed would have gone out to the places where they would fall.” This was so that Allah might test what is in your hearts and purify what is within them. Allah knows what lies within hearts.
interpretation: The verse teaches that hardship exposes the difference between trust grounded in faith and fear that assumes events are outside Allah’s wisdom. Its reassurance is not that believers will be spared every loss, but that neither human calculations nor attempts to escape can overturn what Allah has decreed; the trial can instead reveal and refine what is within a person.

translation: Those of you who turned back on the day the two armies met were only caused to stumble by Satan because of some of what they had done. Yet Allah has indeed pardoned them. Surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Forbearing.
interpretation: The verse teaches that a believer’s failure may be exploited by Satan through the consequences of earlier missteps, but it need not define them: Allah’s pardon remains open, and His forbearance gives people time to repent and return to obedience.

translation: O you who believe, do not be like those who disbelieved and said of their brothers, when they traveled through the land or went out on a campaign, “If they had stayed with us, they would not have died or been killed.” God made this a source of anguish in their hearts. God gives life and causes death, and God sees all that you do.
interpretation: The verse warns believers against blaming a person’s death on having traveled or gone to battle, as though staying home could have prevented what God had decreed. Such counterfactual blame only deepens grief; believers are instead to trust that life and death belong to God while remaining mindful that He sees their actions.

translation: And if you are killed in the way of Allah or die, forgiveness from Allah and mercy are surely better than all that they accumulate.
interpretation: The verse teaches that a believer’s ultimate hope is not worldly wealth or possessions, but Allah’s forgiveness and mercy. Whether death comes while striving in His cause or otherwise, His reward is worth more than anything people gather in this life.

translation: And if you die or are slain, it is surely to Allah that you will be gathered.
interpretation: Whether death comes naturally or through being killed, every person ultimately returns to Allah. The verse directs believers to look beyond the manner or timing of death to their final return to Him.

translation: It was by mercy from Allah that you were gentle with them. Had you been harsh and hard-hearted, they would have scattered from around you. So pardon them, ask forgiveness for them, and consult them in the matter. Then, when you have made your decision, put your trust in Allah. Indeed, Allah loves those who put their trust in Him.
interpretation: The verse presents gentleness as a mercy that sustains trust and unity, especially after hardship. A leader should respond to others’ failings with pardon, seek God’s forgiveness for them, and include them in consultation; after deliberating and deciding, he should entrust the outcome to Allah rather than be consumed by doubt or rely only on his own power.

translation: If Allah helps you, none can overcome you; but if He forsakes you, who is there that can help you after Him? So let the believers place their trust in Allah.
interpretation: The verse teaches that success does not ultimately depend on numbers or worldly strength: all aid and victory are in Allah’s hands. Believers should therefore rely on Him, while recognizing that no one can replace His help if He withholds it.

translation: It is not for a prophet to act dishonestly. Whoever acts dishonestly will come on the Day of Resurrection bearing what they misappropriated. Then every soul will be fully repaid for what it earned, and none will be wronged.
interpretation: The verse declares that betrayal and misappropriation are incompatible with prophetic trustworthiness, and warns that concealed wrongdoing will not remain hidden: each person will face full accountability for their deeds, with justice done to all.

translation: Is one who seeks the pleasure of Allah like one who incurs wrath from Allah, whose abode is Hell? What an evil destination!
interpretation: The verse teaches that seeking Allah’s approval and persisting in what brings His displeasure are not morally or ultimately equivalent. A person’s choices shape their end, so the believer should seek what pleases Allah rather than be deceived into treating the two paths as alike.

translation: They are of varying ranks before Allah, and Allah sees all that they do.
interpretation: People’s standing before Allah is not equal; it reflects the reality of their deeds, all of which are fully known to Him. His judgment of their ranks is therefore perfectly informed and just.

translation: God has indeed bestowed a favor upon the believers when He sent among them a messenger from their own people, reciting His revelations to them, purifying them, and teaching them the Book and wisdom—though before that they were clearly astray.
interpretation: The verse presents prophetic guidance as a profound act of divine mercy: the messenger’s mission is not only to convey revelation, but to help people become spiritually purified and live by its wisdom. Being sent from among them makes this guidance close and accessible, while their former state underscores how greatly it can transform a community.

translation: When a calamity struck you, though you had inflicted twice as much, you said, “How did this happen?” Say, “It came from yourselves.” Indeed, God has power over all things.
interpretation: The verse teaches the believers to reflect on their own choices when hardship comes: the setback at Uhud was connected to their failure to heed the Prophet’s command. Their responsibility does not place events beyond God’s power; rather, the verse holds human actions accountable while affirming that all things remain within God’s sovereignty.

translation: And what befell you on the day the two armies met was by Allah’s permission, and so that He might make the believers known.
interpretation: The setback at Uhud occurred within Allah’s decree, and it became a means of making clear who remained steadfast in faith and obedience.

translation: And so that He might make evident those who acted hypocritically. It was said to them, “Come, fight in the cause of God, or at least defend yourselves.” They replied, “If we knew there would be fighting, we would have followed you.” That day they were nearer to disbelief than to faith. They say with their mouths what is not in their hearts, and God knows best what they conceal.
interpretation: The verse shows how a moment of trial revealed the difference between sincere faith and hypocrisy. Those who refused to join the believers offered an excuse that disguised their unwillingness, while their words of support did not reflect what they held within. Their true intentions were known to God, even when they tried to conceal them.

translation: Those who, while staying behind, said of their brothers, “If they had obeyed us, they would not have been killed.” Say, “Then ward off death from yourselves, if you are truthful.”
interpretation: The verse exposes the emptiness of their claim that staying away from battle could have guaranteed their brothers’ survival: if they truly had power to keep death at bay, they should be able to ward it off from themselves. Life and death are not controlled by their speculation or caution.

translation: Do not think of those who have been killed in the way of Allah as dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision.
interpretation: The verse teaches that those who give their lives in God’s cause are not lost or forgotten: they possess a real, honored life with their Lord beyond ordinary human perception, and God sustains them there. Their death in this world is therefore not the end of their existence or the measure of their worth.

translation: Rejoicing in what Allah has bestowed upon them of His bounty, and glad for those who have not yet joined them after them: they will have no fear, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: Those granted this honor rejoice not only in Allah’s bounty to themselves, but also in the promise awaiting the faithful who come after them. Their joy reflects confidence in Allah’s reassurance: those who remain steadfast in faith need not fear what lies ahead or grieve over what they have left behind.

translation: They rejoice in a blessing and favor from God, and in the assurance that God does not let the reward of the believers go to waste.
interpretation: The verse portrays the believers’ joy as grounded in trust that God’s generosity and justice endure: no sincere faith or sacrifice is forgotten, even when its reward is not fully visible in this life.

translation: Those who responded to Allah and the Messenger after they had been wounded—for those among them who did good and were mindful of Allah is a great reward.
interpretation: The verse teaches that sincere faith is shown by continuing to obey Allah and His Messenger even after suffering. Those who meet hardship with excellence and mindfulness of Allah are promised a great reward.

translation: Those to whom people said, “The people have gathered against you, so fear them,” were only increased in faith, and they said, “Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best disposer of affairs.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that sincere faith turns threats into an occasion for deeper trust in God: rather than being overcome by fear, believers place their reliance on Him while facing danger.

translation: So they returned with favor from Allah and bounty; no harm touched them, and they followed Allah’s pleasure. And Allah is the possessor of great bounty.
interpretation: Their steadfast trust in Allah brought them back unharmed and enriched by His favor. More importantly, they sought what pleased Him, and the verse affirms that His generosity is immense.

translation: That is only Satan, who frightens you with his allies. So do not fear them; fear Me, if you are truly believers.
interpretation: Satan seeks to weaken believers by making hostile people seem more powerful and frightening than they are. Trust in God should outweigh that fear: remain steadfast rather than letting threats turn you from what is right, and hold God in reverent awe.

translation: Do not let those who hasten into disbelief grieve you. They will never harm Allah in the least. Allah wills that they have no share in the Hereafter, and theirs is a tremendous punishment.
interpretation: The verse consoles the Prophet ﷺ not to be overcome with sorrow over those who eagerly reject faith: their rejection cannot diminish Allah’s power or harm Him. Their choices instead bring consequences for themselves, leaving them without a share in the Hereafter and facing a grave punishment.

translation: Indeed, those who have exchanged disbelief for faith will never harm Allah in the least, and they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: Their rejection of faith does not diminish Allah’s power or sovereignty; its consequences fall upon them, not upon Him.

translation: Let not those who disbelieve think that Our granting them respite is good for them. We grant them respite only so that they may increase in sin, and they will have a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: The delay of punishment is not a sign of divine approval or lasting benefit. It gives those who persist in disbelief more time in which their own choices deepen their wrongdoing, before they face a humiliating reckoning.

translation: God would not leave the believers in the state you are in until He separates the corrupt from the good. Nor would God disclose the unseen to you; rather, God chooses from among His messengers whom He wills. So believe in God and His messengers. If you believe and remain mindful of God, you will have a great reward.
interpretation: God’s testing of the believers brings their true character to light, distinguishing sincere faith from hypocrisy; people are not given unrestricted access to the unseen, though God reveals what He wills to chosen messengers. The verse therefore calls believers to trust God’s guidance, believe in His messengers, and remain mindful of Him, knowing that this faithfulness will be greatly rewarded.

translation: Let not those who are miserly with what Allah has granted them from His bounty think that this is good for them. Rather, it is bad for them. What they withheld will be placed around their necks on the Day of Resurrection. To Allah belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is fully aware of what you do.
interpretation: The verse challenges the illusion that keeping blessings solely for oneself is a form of security or success. Wealth is a trust, not a lasting possession; when it is used to justify selfishness, it becomes a source of moral burden. The reminder that all things ultimately belong to Allah calls people to act responsibly with what they have, knowing their choices are neither hidden nor inconsequential.

translation: Allah has indeed heard those who said, “Allah is poor, while we are rich.” We will record what they said and their unjust killing of the prophets, and We will say, “Taste the punishment of the burning Fire.”
interpretation: The verse condemns those who mocked the call to give for God’s cause by portraying God as needy. God is utterly free of need; the call to give is a test of people’s faith and generosity. Their contemptuous words and grave wrongdoing are not forgotten, and the warning of punishment underscores their accountability before God.

translation: That is for what your hands have sent ahead, and Allah is never unjust to His servants.
interpretation: The consequences people face are not imposed arbitrarily; they accord with what they have done, for Allah wrongs no one.

translation: Those who said, “Allah has pledged to us that we should not believe any messenger until he brings us an offering that fire consumes.” Say, “Messengers before me came to you with clear signs and with the very thing you have mentioned. So why did you kill them, if you are truthful?”
interpretation: The verse exposes the claim as a pretext rather than a sincere test of prophethood: earlier messengers had brought clear evidence, including the sign they demanded, yet they were rejected and killed. Their actions therefore contradict their claim that they were simply waiting for proof.

translation: If they deny you, messengers before you were denied, though they came with clear proofs, scriptures, and an illuminating Book.
interpretation: The denial you face does not show that your message is false; it follows a pattern endured by earlier messengers. Their rejection did not undo the truth made clear through the signs and revelation they brought.

translation: Every soul will taste death, and you will be fully recompensed only on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever is kept far from the Fire and admitted into Paradise has truly succeeded. The life of this world is nothing but a deceptive enjoyment.
interpretation: The verse redirects our measure of success away from worldly possessions and status, which are temporary and can mislead, toward the lasting outcome in the Hereafter: being spared the Fire and admitted to Paradise.

translation: You will surely be tested in your wealth and yourselves, and you will surely hear much hurtful speech from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associate others with God. But if you are patient and mindful of God, that is among the matters requiring firm resolve.
interpretation: The verse teaches that hardship and hurtful opposition are not signs that faith has failed; they are trials in which believers are called to remain steadfast and guided by reverence for God. Such patience is not weakness, but a deliberate strength of character.

translation: And [remember] when God took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture: “You must make it clear to the people and not conceal it.” But they cast it behind their backs and traded it for a small price. How vile is what they trade for!
interpretation: The verse warns that knowledge of divine guidance is a trust, not something to conceal or manipulate for worldly advantage. Those who exchange that responsibility for a fleeting gain betray their covenant, and the verse condemns the bargain as profoundly worthless.

translation: Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have done and love to be praised for what they have not done are safe from punishment. They will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns against self-righteousness and the desire for undeserved praise: delight in one’s actions and public approval cannot shield a person from accountability before God.

translation: To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and Allah has power over all things.
interpretation: The verse teaches that all authority and ownership ultimately belong to God, so nothing in creation lies beyond His power.

translation: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of night and day are signs for people of understanding.
interpretation: The ordered vastness of the heavens and earth, and the recurring change between night and day, invite thoughtful people to recognize the wisdom and power of their Creator.

translation: Those who remember Allah while standing, sitting, and lying on their sides, and reflect on the creation of the heavens and the earth, saying, “Our Lord, You did not create this in vain. Glory be to You, so protect us from the punishment of the Fire.”
interpretation: True remembrance of Allah accompanies a person in every state and deepens through reflection on creation. Recognizing that the universe is not without purpose leads them to glorify their Lord, turn to Him humbly, and seek protection from the consequences of wrongdoing.

translation: Our Lord, indeed whoever You admit into the Fire, You have disgraced; and the wrongdoers will have no helpers.
interpretation: The verse expresses the gravity of being condemned to the Fire: it is a profound humiliation from which no worldly ally or advocate can rescue a person. It urges the believer to seek God’s protection from wrongdoing and its ultimate consequence.

translation: Our Lord, we heard a caller calling us to faith: “Believe in your Lord,” and we believed. Our Lord, forgive us our sins, erase our misdeeds, and cause us to die among the righteous.
interpretation: The supplication expresses a faith that answers revelation with belief and then turns to God in humble hope. The speakers seek not merely pardon for their sins, but cleansing from their harmful effects, and ask that their final state be joined with the righteous—recognizing that steadfast faith and a good end both depend on God’s mercy.

translation: Our Lord, grant us what You promised us through Your messengers, and do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection. Surely You never break Your promise.
interpretation: This supplication joins confident trust in God’s promise with humble dependence on His mercy. The believers ask not merely for the promised reward, but to be received with honor on the Day of Resurrection, recognizing that their hope rests on God’s faithfulness.

translation: Their Lord answered them: “I will never let the work of any worker among you go to waste, whether male or female—you are of one another. Those who emigrated, were driven from their homes, suffered harm in My cause, fought, and were killed—I will surely erase their misdeeds and admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, as a reward from God. God holds the finest reward.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that God values sincere deeds equally from women and men, and that no sacrifice made in faith is lost. Those who endure displacement, harm, and even death for God’s cause are promised forgiveness and lasting reward; their hope rests not on worldly recognition, but on God, whose reward is best.

translation: Do not let the movements of those who disbelieve through the lands deceive you.
interpretation: Their freedom to travel and apparent prosperity in worldly life should not be mistaken for lasting success or divine approval; worldly ease is temporary and does not determine their ultimate standing.

translation: A brief enjoyment; then Hell will be their abode—and what a wretched resting place.
interpretation: The verse warns that worldly pleasures are fleeting and cannot compensate for the final punishment awaiting those who reject God; Hell is a dreadful and lasting abode.

translation: But those who are mindful of their Lord will have gardens beneath which rivers flow, where they will abide forever—a welcome from Allah. And what is with Allah is better for the righteous.
interpretation: The verse contrasts fleeting worldly advantage with the lasting reward Allah has prepared for those who remain mindful of Him. Their welcome in the gardens is a gift from Allah, and the ultimate good is not merely the blessings themselves but what He has reserved for the righteous.

translation: And indeed, among the People of the Scripture are those who believe in Allah and in what was sent down to you and what was sent down to them, humbling themselves before Allah. They do not trade Allah’s signs for a paltry price. They will have their reward with their Lord. Indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning.
interpretation: The verse honors sincere believers among the People of the Scripture who accept the revelation given to the Prophet alongside the revelation given to them, approaching Allah with humility and refusing to compromise His signs for worldly gain. Their reward rests with Allah, whose reckoning is swift.

translation: O you who believe, be patient, outdo others in steadfastness, remain steadfast at your posts, and be mindful of Allah, so that you may succeed.
interpretation: The verse calls believers to sustain patience in hardship, strengthen one another in perseverance, and remain vigilant and committed in their responsibilities. This steadfastness must be joined with mindfulness of Allah, for true success comes through faithful endurance and obedience.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. O mankind, be mindful of your Lord, who created you from a single soul and created from it its mate, and spread from the two of them many men and women. Be mindful of Allah, in whose name you appeal to one another, and honor the ties of kinship. Indeed, Allah is ever watchful over you.
interpretation: The verse calls people to live with reverence for God and care for one another, recognizing that humanity shares a common origin. It grounds the obligations between people—especially within families and kinship—in God’s watchful presence, so that appeals made in His name and family bonds are treated with seriousness, justice, and compassion.

translation: Give the orphans their property. Do not exchange what is good for what is bad, and do not consume their property along with your own; surely that is a grave sin.
interpretation: The verse treats the care of an orphan’s wealth as a trust, not an opportunity for personal gain. Its warning reaches both obvious theft and deceptive dealings that leave the orphan with less, emphasizing the seriousness of exploiting someone who depends on others for protection.

translation: If you fear that you will not deal fairly with orphan girls, then marry women who are lawful and pleasing to you—two, three, or four. But if you fear that you will not be just, then marry only one, or those whom your right hands possess. That is more likely to keep you from injustice.
interpretation: The verse addresses the danger of exploiting vulnerable orphan girls under one’s guardianship, and directs guardians toward marriage arrangements that do not compromise their rights. It permits marriage to more than one woman, but sets justice as the decisive condition: when a person fears he cannot treat his wives fairly, he should marry only one. The permission is therefore bounded by responsibility, and the verse’s guiding aim is to prevent injustice.

translation: Give the women their bridal gifts graciously. But if they willingly give up any part of it to you, then enjoy it with ease and comfort.
interpretation: The verse safeguards a wife’s independent right to her bridal gift: it is hers, not something her husband may take or demand back. Any portion she relinquishes is lawful for him only when her choice is genuine and free of pressure.

translation: Do not entrust your wealth to those who lack sound judgment—the wealth Allah has made a means of support for you. Provide for them from it, clothe them, and speak to them kindly.
