interpretation: The verse teaches those responsible for managing the property of people unable to handle it wisely to protect it as a source of their security, while still providing for their needs and treating them with dignity and kindness.

translation: Test the orphans until they reach the age of marriage. Then, if you perceive sound judgment in them, hand over their property to them. Do not consume it extravagantly or hastily before they come of age. Let whoever is wealthy abstain, and whoever is poor take only what is reasonable. When you hand over their property to them, have witnesses present. God is sufficient as a Reckoner.
interpretation: The verse treats guardianship as a trust, not an entitlement: a guardian must protect an orphan’s property, assess their readiness to manage it responsibly, and return it once they are capable. Any use of the property by a needy guardian is limited by fairness and restraint, with witnesses helping safeguard the transfer and accountability before God.

translation: For men is a share of what parents and close relatives leave behind, and for women is a share of what parents and close relatives leave behind—whether it is little or much—a share ordained.
interpretation: This verse affirms that inheritance is a right for both men and women, not a privilege reserved for men. Their entitlement remains valid regardless of the size of the estate, because it is a prescribed right rather than a gift that others may withhold.

translation: When relatives, orphans, and the needy are present at the distribution, give them something from it and speak to them in a kind and gracious manner.
interpretation: This verse teaches that the division of wealth should be accompanied by compassion: those in need who are present should not be treated as invisible, and any generosity toward them should be offered with words that preserve their dignity.

translation: Let those who, were they to leave behind vulnerable offspring, would fear for them, be mindful of Allah and speak with fairness and care.
interpretation: The verse calls people to let the compassion they would want shown to their own vulnerable children guide how they treat those left in their care, especially orphans. Awareness of God should lead them to protect the vulnerable and speak justly, particularly when decisions about their rights are being made.

translation: Indeed, those who consume the property of orphans unjustly are only consuming fire into their bellies, and they will burn in a blazing fire.
interpretation: The verse presents the unjust taking of an orphan’s wealth as a grave betrayal for which worldly gain is ultimately ruinous: its true consequence is represented as fire, underscoring both the severity of the wrong and accountability before God.

translation: Allah instructs you concerning your children: the share of a male is equal to that of two females. If there are two or more daughters, they receive two-thirds of what he leaves; if there is only one, she receives half. Each of his parents receives one-sixth of what he leaves if he has a child. If he has no child and his parents inherit from him, his mother receives one-third; but if he has siblings, his mother receives one-sixth—all after any bequest he made or debt. You do not know which of your parents or children is of greater benefit to you. This is an obligation from Allah. Surely Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: The verse establishes inheritance shares as binding rights rather than matters to be decided by personal preference or guesses about which relatives will prove most useful. Its closing words direct believers to entrust these allocations to Allah’s knowledge and wisdom, while ensuring that debts and valid bequests are accounted for in settling an estate.

translation: You will have half of what your wives leave if they have no child. If they have a child, you will have a quarter of what they leave, after any bequest they make or debt. They will have a quarter of what you leave if you have no child; if you have a child, they will have an eighth of what you leave, after any bequest you make or debt. If a man or woman leaves an inheritance with neither parent nor child, but has a brother or sister, each of them will receive a sixth. If they are more than that, they will share one-third, after any bequest made or debt, without causing harm. This is a command from God; and God is All-Knowing, Forbearing.
interpretation: These shares establish a divinely prescribed order for distributing an estate: the surviving spouse and, in the specified case of an inheritance without parent or child, the siblings receive defined portions after debts and bequests are accounted for. The warning against causing harm makes clear that a bequest must not be used to undermine anyone’s rightful share; the ruling is to be carried out with fairness, mindful that God knows what is done and is Forbearing.

translation: These are the limits set by Allah. Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, He will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, where they will remain forever. That is the supreme triumph.
interpretation: The prescribed limits are not arbitrary rules but part of divine guidance. Faithful obedience to Allah and His Messenger—including honoring these limits—leads to lasting reward with Allah.

translation: Whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger and transgresses His limits, He will admit into a Fire, remaining there, and for him is a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns that knowingly rejecting divine guidance and crossing the bounds it sets carries grave consequences. Its mention of humiliation underscores that such defiance ultimately strips a person of the honor and security they may have sought apart from obedience to God.

translation: As for those of your women who commit sexual immorality, call four of your own people to testify against them. If they testify, confine the women to their homes until death takes them or God provides a way for them.
interpretation: The verse makes any response to this grave accusation depend on testimony from four witnesses, guarding against punishment based on suspicion or rumor. Its confinement instruction is expressly temporary—lasting only until death or until God provides a further ruling—so it is not presented as an unchanging final penalty.

translation: And the two among you who commit it, punish them. But if they repent and mend their ways, then leave them alone. Indeed, Allah is ever accepting of repentance and merciful.
interpretation: The verse teaches that wrongdoing should be confronted, but when those responsible sincerely repent and reform, they should no longer be pursued or reproached. It closes by emphasizing Allah’s readiness to accept repentance and show mercy.

translation: Allah’s acceptance of repentance is for those who do evil out of ignorance, then repent soon; Allah turns in mercy to them. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: “In ignorance” can describe wrongdoing committed in heedlessness or folly, not only wrongdoing done without knowing it is wrong. The verse holds open the way back for those who turn sincerely to God before death leaves them no chance to repent, while affirming that His acceptance is guided by perfect knowledge and wisdom.

translation: Repentance is not for those who persist in doing evil until, when death comes to one of them, he says, “I repent now”; nor is it for those who die as disbelievers. For them We have prepared a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse teaches that repentance must be sincere and made while a person still has the opportunity to turn back and change. A declaration made only when death is upon someone is not a genuine return, and those who die rejecting faith cannot seek repentance after death.

translation: O you who believe, it is not lawful for you to inherit women against their will, nor to pressure them in order to take back some of what you have given them—unless they commit a manifest indecency. Live with them honorably. If you dislike them, it may be that you dislike something in which God has placed abundant good.
interpretation: The verse rejects treating women as possessions or using power over them to seize their property. It makes honorable companionship a moral duty, including when affection is strained: dislike alone is not a license for injustice, and patience may reveal goodness that was not initially apparent.

translation: If you wish to replace one wife with another, and you have given one of them a great amount, do not take anything back from it. Would you take it through slander and manifest sin?
interpretation: The verse protects a wife’s right to the marriage gift: a husband may not reclaim it merely because he chooses to end the marriage, even if he had given her a very large amount. Taking it unjustly is condemned as both a grave wrong against her and an evident sin before God.

translation: How can you take it back, when you have been intimate with one another and they have taken from you a solemn covenant?
interpretation: The verse treats marriage as a bond of profound trust and obligation: intimacy and the solemn commitment between spouses make it unjust for a husband to reclaim what he gave his wife as a marital gift.

translation: Do not marry women whom your fathers married, except what has already occurred. Indeed, it is an indecency, hateful, and an evil way.
interpretation: The exception refers to marriages that took place before this prohibition was revealed; they are not treated as grounds for blame. The verse therefore establishes a firm boundary protecting family relationships and condemns violating it as morally shameful and deeply repugnant.

translation: Forbidden to you in marriage are your mothers, your daughters, your sisters, your paternal aunts, your maternal aunts, your brothers’ daughters, your sisters’ daughters, your mothers who nursed you, your sisters through nursing, your wives’ mothers, and your stepdaughters in your care, born of wives with whom you have consummated marriage. But if you have not consummated marriage with them, there is no blame upon you [for marrying their daughters]. Also forbidden are the wives of your biological sons, and marrying two sisters at the same time—except what has already occurred. Indeed, Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse establishes marriage boundaries rooted in close family ties and the protection of family relationships. It treats certain bonds formed through nursing as kinship, and distinguishes between a stepdaughter’s prohibition, which applies after consummation with her mother, and the other listed prohibitions. The allowance concerning past unions reflects Allah’s forgiveness and mercy toward those who acted before these limits were known or established.

translation: And [forbidden to you are] married women, except those whom your right hands possess. This is Allah’s decree for you. Lawful to you are all others, provided you seek them with your wealth in lawful marriage, desiring chastity, not illicit relations. So for whatever you enjoy of them, give them their due bridal gifts as an obligation. There is no blame upon you regarding what you mutually agree upon after the obligation. Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: The verse lays down the boundaries of lawful sexual relations and emphasizes that they belong within a legitimate, chaste marriage, with the woman’s bridal gift as a required right. Its closing words allow spouses to reach further mutual agreements about that obligation, while reminding them that such matters are known to God and should be handled with justice and care.

translation: Whoever among you lacks the means to marry free, believing women may marry believing women from among those under your authority. God knows best the reality of your faith; you are all of one another. So marry them with the permission of their people, and give them their bridal dues fairly, as women who are chaste—not sexually promiscuous nor taking secret lovers. Once they are married, if they commit a sexual offense, they are subject to half the penalty prescribed for free women. This permission is for those among you who fear falling into sin; yet patience is better for you. God is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse addresses a society in which slavery existed and regulates marriage involving enslaved women: it permits this marriage when a man cannot afford to marry a free believing woman, while requiring the woman’s community or guardians’ permission, a fair bridal payment, and a chaste marriage rather than exploitation or casual relations. By affirming that believers are “one of another,” it stresses their shared faith despite differences in social status. It also sets a lesser legal penalty for an enslaved wife who commits the specified offense after marriage, and counsels patience when one can avoid the hardship and moral risks involved.

translation: Allah wants to make things clear to you, guide you to the ways of those who came before you, and turn toward you in forgiveness. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: The verse presents divine guidance as both instruction and mercy: Allah clarifies what people need to know and directs them toward sound paths, while keeping the door of repentance open when they fall short. His knowledge and wisdom mean that these teachings and opportunities for forgiveness are perfectly suited to human needs.

translation: Allah wants to turn toward you in mercy, while those who follow their desires want you to stray far from the right path.
interpretation: The verse contrasts God’s merciful intention to guide people back to Him with the aim of those ruled by their desires: to draw others into serious deviation. It warns believers to recognize how seductive desires can pull them away from the path of repentance and obedience.

translation: God wants to lighten your burdens, for the human being was created weak.
interpretation: The verse portrays divine guidance as mercifully attuned to human frailty: our weakness is a reason to turn to God and receive the ease He provides, not to despair of living rightly.

translation: O you who believe, do not consume one another’s wealth wrongfully, but only through trade conducted by mutual consent. And do not kill yourselves [or one another]. Surely Allah is ever Merciful to you.
interpretation: The verse teaches that dealings among believers must rest on justice and genuine consent, not exploitation or wrongful appropriation. Its prohibition of killing protects human life within the community, while its closing reminder of God’s mercy grounds these limits in care for people’s well-being.

translation: Whoever does that in transgression and wrongdoing, We shall cast him into a Fire; and that is easy for Allah.
interpretation: The verse warns that deliberately committing such wrongdoing is a grave matter before God: no act of injustice escapes His judgment, and exacting its consequence is effortless for Him.

translation: If you avoid the major sins from which you are forbidden, We will erase your lesser misdeeds and admit you to an honorable place of entry.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God’s generous mercy: faithfully turning away from grave wrongdoing is met with forgiveness for lesser failings and the promise of an honored welcome in the Hereafter. This is encouragement to obey God, not permission to treat lesser sins casually.

translation: Do not covet what Allah has bestowed on some of you more than others. Men will have a share of what they earn, and women will have a share of what they earn. Ask Allah for His bounty. Allah has always been fully aware of all things.
interpretation: The verse teaches believers to resist envy over differences in provision or circumstance. Rather than longing for another person’s share, each should pursue what is rightfully theirs and seek increase through Allah’s generosity, trusting that His knowledge encompasses every person and situation.

translation: For everyone We have appointed heirs to what parents and close relatives leave behind. And those with whom you have made covenants—give them their due share. Surely Allah is witness over all things.
interpretation: The verse establishes that inheritance belongs to those entitled through family ties, while people bound by solemn agreements must also be given what is due to them under those agreements. Its reminder that Allah witnesses everything underscores that these rights are obligations to be upheld faithfully, not matters to be ignored or manipulated.

translation: Men are responsible for the care of women because God has given some of them advantages over others, and because they spend of their wealth. Righteous women are devoted and guard, in their husbands’ absence, what God has entrusted to them. As for those whose serious marital defiance you fear, admonish them, leave them in their beds, and strike them. Then if they comply with you, seek no means against them. Surely God is Most High, Great.
interpretation: The verse ties men’s authority within the household to obligations of care and financial provision, rather than declaring men inherently superior in worth. Its measures address serious marital conflict and are presented as steps toward resolving it, not as permission for domination or abuse. The instruction traditionally understood as striking was restricted by Muslim interpreters to an act that causes no injury or humiliation; the verse’s closing warning forbids using any measure as a pretext to mistreat a wife once the conflict has ended.

translation: And if you fear a breach between the two, appoint an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from hers. If they both desire reconciliation, God will bring about harmony between them. Surely God is All-Knowing, All-Aware.
interpretation: The verse calls for a serious marital rift to be addressed through trusted representatives from both families, who can seek a fair resolution rather than deepen the conflict. Their sincere commitment to reconciliation is met with God’s help, while the closing names remind us that He knows the intentions and circumstances behind their efforts.

translation: Worship Allah and associate nothing with Him. Show kindness to parents, relatives, orphans, the needy, the near neighbor and the distant neighbor, the companion at your side, the traveler, and those whom your right hands possess. Surely Allah does not love anyone who is arrogant and boastful.
interpretation: The verse presents devotion to Allah as inseparable from humility and care for others. Its broad range of relationships challenges people to let worship shape how they treat those around them, while warning that pride and self-importance undermine such kindness.

translation: Those who are miserly, urge others to be miserly, and conceal what Allah has bestowed upon them of His bounty—for the disbelievers We have prepared a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns that miserliness becomes especially blameworthy when people encourage it in others and hide God’s favors rather than acknowledge them or use them generously. This conduct reflects a rejection of gratitude and carries the warning of humiliation before God.

translation: And those who spend their wealth to be seen by people, and do not believe in God or the Last Day—whoever takes Satan as a companion has an evil companion.
interpretation: Spending for public admiration rather than sincere devotion is hollow, especially when it springs from rejection of God and accountability. The verse warns that choosing this path means accepting Satan’s influence, which leads a person away from what is good.

translation: And what harm would it do them if they believed in Allah and the Last Day and spent from what Allah had provided for them? Allah is fully aware of them.
interpretation: The verse gently rebukes those who withhold faith and generosity: they have nothing to lose by believing sincerely and giving from their provision. Their actions and the intentions behind them are known to Allah.

translation: Indeed, God does not wrong anyone by even the weight of an atom. And if there is a good deed, He multiplies it and grants from Himself a great reward.
interpretation: This verse assures that no one will be treated unjustly, even in the smallest matter. God’s justice preserves every good deed, while His generosity can multiply its reward far beyond what the deed alone would merit.

translation: So how will it be when We bring a witness from every community, and bring you, O Muhammad, as a witness over these people?
interpretation: The verse evokes the certainty and gravity of the Day of Judgment: every community will be confronted with testimony about how it responded to its messenger, and the Prophet will testify concerning his people. It is a warning to take divine guidance seriously while there is still time to respond to it.

translation: On that Day, those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth had been made level over them, and they will conceal nothing from Allah.
interpretation: Their wish to disappear reflects the depth of their regret when they face the consequences of rejecting the Messenger. Before Allah, denial offers no escape: every truth is exposed, and nothing can be hidden.

translation: O you who believe, do not approach prayer while intoxicated until you know what you are saying, nor while in a state of major impurity—except as passers-through—until you have washed. If you are ill or traveling, or one of you has relieved himself, or you have been intimate with women, and you find no water, then seek clean earth and wipe your faces and hands with it. Indeed, Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that prayer calls for both conscious awareness and ritual purity, while also making clear that the requirements are not meant to impose hardship: when water cannot be used or found, dry ablution provides a lawful alternative. Its closing names Allah’s pardon and forgiveness, underscoring the mercy behind these concessions.

translation: Have you not considered those who were given a portion of the Scripture, yet choose misguidance and want you to lose the way?
interpretation: The verse warns against those who, despite having received knowledge from scripture, turn away from guidance and seek error for themselves and others. Their rejection is especially harmful because they also wish to lead believers away from the right path.

translation: And Allah knows best who your enemies are. Allah is sufficient as a guardian, and Allah is sufficient as a helper.
interpretation: The verse calls believers to trust Allah’s complete knowledge of those who oppose them and to rely on His protection and help rather than fear their enemies.

translation: Among those who are Jews are some who distort words from their proper places, saying, “We hear and disobey,” and, “Hear—may you not be heard,” and “Raʿinā,” twisting their tongues and disparaging the religion. Had they instead said, “We hear and obey,” “Hear,” and “Look upon us,” it would have been better for them and more upright. But God has rejected them for their disbelief, so only a few of them believe.
interpretation: The verse condemns using speech to evade or mock religious truth: these people twist words and answer guidance with defiance, whereas sincere and respectful speech would reflect a more upright response. Their deliberate rejection of faith brings divine rejection and leaves only a few believing.

translation: O you who were given the Scripture, believe in what We have sent down, confirming what is with you, before We erase faces and turn them backward, or curse them as We cursed the Sabbath-breakers. And God’s command is always carried out.
interpretation: This is a grave warning to those who have received earlier revelation: they are called to accept the Qur’an because it confirms the truth they already possess. The threatened punishment underscores the seriousness of knowingly rejecting that call, recalling the fate of those who violated God’s command concerning the Sabbath.

translation: Indeed, Allah does not forgive associating anything with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whoever He wills. Whoever associates anything with Allah has committed a tremendous sin.
interpretation: The verse warns that dying while associating partners with Allah is uniquely grave and is not forgiven, whereas a person who dies with lesser sins remains subject to Allah’s will: He may forgive them or hold them accountable. It does not mean that sincere repentance from shirk is beyond Allah’s forgiveness.

translation: Have you not seen those who declare themselves pure? Rather, Allah purifies whom He wills, and they will not be wronged even by a thread’s breadth.
interpretation: The verse warns against self-righteousness: a person’s own claim to moral purity does not establish it. True purification belongs to Allah, who judges with perfect justice and wrongs no one in the slightest.

translation: See how they fabricate lies against God; that alone is enough as a clear sin.
interpretation: The verse exposes the grave wrongdoing of falsely attributing claims to God: the act itself is unmistakable evidence of serious sin and warrants condemnation.

translation: Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture, yet believe in false gods and false authorities, and say of those who disbelieve, “These are more rightly guided than those who believe”?
interpretation: The verse rebukes people entrusted with revealed knowledge who abandon its guidance through allegiance to falsehood and prejudice, going so far as to call the disbelievers’ way better guided than that of the believers. Their judgment shows how bias can distort the recognition of truth even among those who possess scripture.

translation: Those are the ones whom Allah has cursed; and whoever Allah curses, you will never find any helper for him.
interpretation: Allah’s judgment cannot be overturned by human support: one deprived of His mercy has no protector able to save them from the consequences of that deprivation.

translation: Or do they have a share in dominion? If so, they would not give people even the smallest speck.
interpretation: The verse rebukes those who begrudge others God’s favor: their own stinginess is such that, were they given authority, they would withhold even the tiniest share from people.

translation: Or do they envy people for what Allah has granted them of His bounty? We indeed gave the family of Abraham the Scripture and wisdom, and bestowed upon them a great kingdom.
interpretation: The verse rebukes resentment toward those whom God has favored: divine gifts are granted by His wisdom, not distributed according to people’s envy. The mention of Abraham’s family reminds the objectors that God had already bestowed revelation, wisdom, and authority upon others, so begrudging such blessings is inconsistent and unjust.

translation: Among them are those who believe in it, and among them are those who turn away from it. And Hell is sufficient as a blazing fire.
interpretation: People respond differently to divine guidance: some accept it, while others reject it or obstruct others from it. The verse warns that Hell is a sufficient consequence for such persistent opposition.

translation: Those who disbelieve in Our signs—we shall make them enter a Fire. Whenever their skins are consumed, We shall replace them with other skins so that they may taste the punishment. Indeed, God is Almighty, All-Wise.
interpretation: The verse portrays the punishment as continually renewed, emphasizing its severity and the persistence of its consequence. Its closing names God’s might and wisdom, presenting the judgment as an exercise of power governed by wisdom.

translation: As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, We shall admit them into gardens beneath which rivers flow, where they will remain forever. There they will have purified spouses, and We shall admit them into abundant, cooling shade.
interpretation: The verse presents lasting reward as a state of complete well-being and purity, granted by God to those whose faith is expressed through righteous action.

translation: Indeed, Allah commands you to return trusts to their rightful owners, and when you judge between people, to judge with justice. Excellent is what Allah admonishes you with. Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.
interpretation: The verse makes public authority and private responsibility forms of worship: a trust is not ours to use for personal advantage, and judgment must not be swayed by favoritism or self-interest. Allah’s knowledge of what is said and done means that fairness and fidelity remain obligations even when no one else can hold us to account.

translation: O you who believe, obey Allah, obey the Messenger, and those among you who hold authority. If you disagree about anything, refer it to Allah and the Messenger, if you truly believe in Allah and the Last Day. That is better and best in outcome.
interpretation: The verse establishes a hierarchy of guidance: obedience to those entrusted with authority is part of an ordered community, but disagreements are ultimately judged by Allah’s guidance and the Messenger’s teaching. Returning disputes to that shared standard protects believers from making personal preference or power the final measure of what is right.

translation: Have you not seen those who claim to believe in what was revealed to you and what was revealed before you, yet wish to seek judgment from false authorities, even though they were commanded to reject them? Satan wishes to lead them far astray.
interpretation: The verse exposes the contradiction between professing faith in revelation and turning for judgment to authorities that oppose its guidance. Such a choice undermines that professed faith, and the verse presents Satan’s aim as drawing people further from the truth.

translation: And when they are told, “Come to what Allah has revealed and to the Messenger,” you see the hypocrites turning away from you with utter aversion.
interpretation: Their refusal to turn to revelation and the Messenger for guidance exposes a hypocrisy rooted in resisting divine authority when it conflicts with their wishes.

translation: How will it be when a calamity befalls them because of what their own hands have done, and then they come to you swearing by Allah, “We intended nothing but good and reconciliation”?
interpretation: The verse exposes the contradiction of those who turn away from God’s guidance but, when the consequences of their actions catch up with them, claim that they meant well. Their oath cannot conceal their evasion: sincere good intentions would be shown by accepting God’s judgment and seeking reconciliation through it.

translation: Those are the ones whose hearts Allah knows; so turn away from them, admonish them, and speak to them words that reach them deeply.
interpretation: Their hidden intentions are fully known to God, even when they conceal them from others. The verse directs the Prophet to entrust their inner reality to God while still addressing them with sincere counsel—words clear and forceful enough to awaken their conscience.

translation: We did not send any messenger except to be obeyed by Allah’s permission. If, when they had wronged themselves, they had come to you and sought Allah’s forgiveness, and the Messenger had sought forgiveness for them, they would have found Allah Accepting of repentance, Merciful.
interpretation: Messengers are sent with Allah’s authority to be followed, and those who have disobeyed should not persist in their wrongdoing or despair of mercy. They should turn back to Allah sincerely, seeking His forgiveness, and seek the Messenger’s prayer for them; Allah welcomes repentance and shows mercy.

translation: But no, by your Lord, they will not truly believe until they make you judge between them in their disputes, then feel no inner resistance to your decision and submit to it completely.
interpretation: The verse teaches that sincere faith is not merely professed: it is shown by trusting the Prophet’s judgment in disputes, accepting its outcome inwardly without resentment, and acting upon it wholeheartedly.

translation: If We had prescribed for them, “Kill yourselves” or “Leave your homes,” they would not have done so, except for a few of them. But if they had done what they were admonished to do, it would have been better for them and would have made them more steadfast.
interpretation: The verse teaches that sincere obedience to God’s guidance—even when it demands great sacrifice—benefits the believers themselves, strengthening their resolve and helping them remain firm in faith.

translation: And then We would surely have granted them a tremendous reward from Us.
interpretation: This promises that sincere obedience to God and His Messenger would be met with an immense reward, granted through God’s own generosity.

translation: And We would surely have guided them to a straight path.
interpretation: Had they followed the guidance given to them, God would have led them toward the way of truth and obedience.

translation: Whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger will be among those whom Allah has favored: the prophets, the steadfastly truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous. What excellent companions they are!
interpretation: The verse teaches that the highest reward of obedience is not merely a particular blessing, but nearness to the finest people in the Hereafter. Their ranks may differ, yet the obedient are honored by sharing their company.

translation: That is a bounty from Allah, and Allah is sufficient as the All-Knowing.
interpretation: The honored rank and companionship mentioned here are gifts from Allah, who fully knows the sincerity and deeds of His servants.

translation: O you who believe, take your precautions, then advance in groups, or advance all together.
interpretation: The verse teaches believers to combine vigilance with readiness to act, organizing themselves in the way best suited to the circumstances—whether in smaller units or as a united whole.

translation: And indeed, among you is one who holds back. If a misfortune befalls you, he says, “God has favored me, since I was not there with them.”
interpretation: The verse exposes a self-serving attitude: this person treats faith and fellowship as a burden when they involve risk, yet regards another’s hardship only as an opportunity to congratulate himself on having escaped it.

translation: But if bounty from Allah reaches you, he will surely say—as though there had never been affection between you and him—“If only I had been with them, so that I might have achieved a great triumph.”
interpretation: The verse portrays someone whose loyalty is governed by personal gain: when believers prosper, he distances himself from them and speaks as though he had never shared a bond with them. His regret is not for failing to stand with them, but for missing the worldly advantage he imagines their success brought.

translation: So let those who trade the life of this world for the Hereafter fight in the way of God. Whoever fights in the way of God and is killed or prevails, We will grant him a great reward.
interpretation: The verse presents devotion to God’s cause as a commitment that places the Hereafter above worldly gain. Its promise applies whether a person is killed or achieves victory: the reward rests with God and is not measured solely by worldly outcomes.

translation: And what is the matter with you that you do not fight in the cause of Allah and for the oppressed among men, women, and children who say, “Our Lord, bring us out of this town whose people are oppressive, and appoint for us from Yourself a protector, and appoint for us from Yourself a helper”?
interpretation: The verse presents defending the vulnerable from oppression as a serious moral responsibility, not merely a matter of communal advantage. Their plea asks for both rescue and support, showing that seeking God’s help is joined here to action on behalf of those who cannot free themselves.

translation: Those who believe fight in God’s cause, while those who disbelieve fight in the cause of falsehood. So fight the allies of Satan; indeed, Satan’s scheme is weak.
interpretation: The verse contrasts the purposes behind the two sides’ fighting and urges believers not to be intimidated by those aligned against them. Its reassurance is that Satan’s plans, however threatening they may seem, are ultimately weak before God.

translation: Have you not considered those who were told, “Restrain your hands, establish prayer, and give zakah”? Then, when fighting was prescribed for them, a group of them feared people as they should fear God—or even more—and said, “Our Lord, why have You prescribed fighting for us? If only You had delayed it for us until a near term.” Say, “The enjoyment of this world is little, and the Hereafter is better for one who is mindful of God. You will not be wronged by even as much as a date-thread.”
interpretation: The verse exposes how fear of loss and attachment to worldly life can become stronger than trust in God when a difficult duty arrives. Its answer redirects the believers from the briefness of worldly security to the enduring good of the Hereafter, while assuring them that God’s judgment is perfectly just: no one will suffer even the smallest injustice.

translation: Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you are in fortified towers. If good fortune befalls them, they say, “This is from Allah”; but if hardship befalls them, they say, “This is from you.” Say, “All is from Allah.” What is the matter with these people, that they can hardly understand what is said to them?
interpretation: The verse teaches that no refuge or worldly strength can prevent the death God has decreed. It rebukes those who welcome blessings as gifts from God but blame the Messenger for hardship, reminding them that events unfold within God’s decree. Their failure is not merely to hear the words, but to understand their meaning and stop making the Messenger a scapegoat for what befalls them.

translation: Whatever good comes to you is from Allah, and whatever harm comes to you is from yourself. We have sent you to all people as a messenger, and Allah is sufficient as a witness.
interpretation: Every blessing ultimately comes through Allah’s grace, while the harm people experience may arise from their own choices and deeds. The verse also affirms that the Messenger has faithfully conveyed his mission, with Allah as witness to it.

translation: Whoever obeys the Messenger has indeed obeyed Allah; and whoever turns away, We have not sent you as a guardian over them.
interpretation: Obeying the Messenger is obedience to Allah because he conveys and teaches Allah’s guidance. Those who reject that guidance bear responsibility for their choice; the Messenger’s role is to convey it, not to compel them or answer for their refusal.

translation: They say, “We obey,” but when they leave you, a group of them secretly plans something contrary to what you say. Allah records what they scheme. So turn away from them and put your trust in Allah; Allah is sufficient as a guardian of affairs.
interpretation: The verse warns that outward professions of loyalty do not conceal inward opposition from Allah. The Prophet is urged not to be overcome by their hypocrisy or secret schemes, but to entrust the matter to Allah, whose knowledge and care are fully sufficient.

translation: Do they not reflect upon the Qur’an? Had it been from anyone other than Allah, they would surely have found many inconsistencies in it.
interpretation: The verse invites careful reflection rather than unexamined reading. It presents the Qur’an’s coherence across its varied passages as a sign of its divine origin, since a work produced by human beings would be liable to contain substantial contradictions.

translation: When news of security or fear comes to them, they spread it. But if they had referred it to the Messenger and to those in authority among them, those able to draw conclusions from it would have understood it. Were it not for Allah’s favor and mercy upon you, you would have followed Satan, except for a few.
interpretation: The verse teaches that reports with serious consequences should not be spread impulsively. They should be referred to the Messenger and to qualified people of authority, whose knowledge enables them to assess what the reports mean and how to respond. This sound judgment is also a mercy from Allah, protecting people from being misled into harmful actions.

translation: So fight in the way of God; you are responsible only for yourself, and encourage the believers. Perhaps God will restrain the force of those who disbelieve. God is stronger in might and more severe in punishment.
interpretation: The verse calls the Prophet to carry out his duty faithfully even if others hesitate, while urging him to strengthen the believers. Their effort is not the sole measure of the outcome: God can restrain their opponents, and His power and judgment surpass all human force.

translation: Whoever intercedes with a good intercession will have a share in its reward, and whoever intercedes with an evil intercession will bear a share of its burden. And Allah is ever Watchful over all things.
interpretation: A person is accountable not only for what they do directly, but also for the causes they support and the influence they lend to others. Helping bring about good carries its own reward, while helping wrongdoing brings a corresponding burden; nothing escapes Allah’s knowledge or judgment.

translation: When you are greeted with a greeting, respond with one better than it, or return it in kind. Surely God keeps account of all things.
interpretation: This verse teaches that ordinary exchanges should reflect generosity and respect: meet another person’s courtesy with greater kindness when you can, and never with less. God’s complete accounting reminds people that even small acts of consideration matter.

translation: Allah—there is no god but Him. He will surely gather you on the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt. And who is more truthful than Allah in speech?
interpretation: Because Allah alone is worthy of worship and His word is perfectly true, the gathering on the Day of Resurrection is certain, not merely a possibility. The verse calls people to place their trust in that promise above every doubt or competing claim.

translation: What is the matter with you that you have become two parties regarding the hypocrites, when God has turned them back because of what they earned? Do you wish to guide those whom God has led astray? Whoever God leads astray, you will never find a way for him.
interpretation: The verse rebukes the believers for dividing over people whose own choices and conduct have returned them to disbelief and hypocrisy. It cautions against assuming that human persuasion can guide those who persistently reject guidance: their straying is a consequence of what they have earned, and no one can direct them to the truth unless God grants them guidance.

translation: They wish that you would disbelieve as they disbelieved, so that you would be alike. So do not take any of them as allies until they migrate in the way of God. But if they turn away, then seize them and kill them wherever you find them; and take neither ally nor helper from among them.
interpretation: The verse addresses a particular group in a setting of armed conflict and political allegiance, not people simply because they hold a different faith. Its severe command concerns those who rejected the community’s protection and stood against it; it should be read within that wartime context, rather than as a general license for violence.

translation: Except for those who join a people with whom you have a treaty, or who come to you feeling constrained from fighting either you or their own people. Had God willed, He could have given them power over you, and they would have fought you. So if they withdraw from you, do not fight you, and offer you peace, God has given you no cause to act against them.
interpretation: The verse establishes that people who are bound by a treaty, or who refrain from taking part in hostilities and seek peace, are not to be treated as enemies. Their restraint and peaceful overture leave no grounds for fighting them.

translation: You will find others who wish to be safe from you and safe from their own people. Whenever they are drawn back into hostility, they plunge into it again. If they do not keep away from you, offer you peace, and restrain their hands, then seize them and kill them wherever you encounter them. Against these, We have given you clear authority.
interpretation: This addresses a specific group in the setting of armed conflict: people who repeatedly return to hostility while refusing to withdraw, make peace, or cease fighting. The permission to fight them is tied to those conditions and is not a general command to harm people who are peaceful.

translation: It is not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake. Whoever kills a believer by mistake must free a believing slave and pay blood money to the victim’s family, unless they remit it. If the victim was a believer from a people at war with you, then the killer must free a believing slave. If the victim was from a people with whom you have a treaty, then the killer must pay blood money to the victim’s family and free a believing slave. Whoever cannot find the means must fast for two consecutive months as repentance to God. God is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: The verse teaches that even an unintended killing carries serious responsibility: it calls for repair to the bereaved family and an act of expiation, while allowing the family to forgo compensation. Its distinctions also show that obligations are shaped by the victim’s circumstances and existing covenants. The provision for fasting when emancipation is not possible makes repentance a sustained act of accountability, and the closing names remind readers that these rulings rest on divine knowledge and wisdom.

translation: Whoever deliberately kills a believer, his recompense is Hell, where he will remain; Allah’s wrath and curse are upon him, and He has prepared for him a tremendous punishment.
interpretation: The verse gives a grave warning against the intentional killing of a believer, presenting it as a violation so severe that it brings divine wrath, exclusion from mercy, and immense punishment. It underscores the sanctity of human life and the profound accountability attached to taking it unjustly.

translation: O you who believe, when you travel in the cause of Allah, verify the facts, and do not say to anyone who offers you peace, “You are not a believer,” seeking the fleeting gains of worldly life. With Allah are abundant gains. You were once like that, then Allah bestowed His favor upon you, so verify the facts. Indeed, Allah is fully aware of what you do.
interpretation: The verse warns believers not to judge another person’s faith or reject their offer of peace hastily, especially for worldly advantage. It calls for careful discernment and humility: remember that guidance is a favor Allah granted you, and act knowing that He sees the motives behind your decisions.

translation: Those believers who stay behind—except those with a disabling excuse—are not equal to those who strive in the way of God with their wealth and their lives. God has granted those who strive with their wealth and their lives a degree above those who stay behind. To each, God has promised the best reward; yet God has given those who strive a tremendous reward above those who stay behind.
interpretation: The verse teaches that God recognizes the difference between those who make a genuine sacrifice in His cause and those who do not, while excluding people prevented by a valid disability or excuse from blame. Those who remain behind are still promised good, but the greater rank belongs to those who expend their wealth and lives in service of God.

translation: Degrees from Him, and forgiveness and mercy. And Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: The phrase points to the honor God grants: elevated ranks by His favor, together with forgiveness and mercy. His forgiveness and mercy are enduring, giving hope to those who turn to Him and seek His pleasure.

translation: Indeed, those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves—the angels will say, “What were you doing?” They will reply, “We were oppressed in the land.” The angels will say, “Was God’s earth not spacious enough for you to migrate elsewhere?” Their refuge will be Hell—what an evil destination.
interpretation: The verse warns that claiming helplessness does not excuse abandoning one’s religious obligations when a viable way to preserve them is available. Its rebuke is directed at those who had the means to leave an environment that prevented them from living faithfully, yet failed to do so.

translation: Except for the oppressed among men, women, and children who have no means to escape and can find no way.
interpretation: This exception shows that accountability is not applied blindly: those genuinely trapped, without the ability or means to seek a way out, are not blameworthy for what lies beyond their power.

translation: As for those, it may be that Allah will pardon them; and Allah is ever Pardoning, Forgiving.
interpretation: The verse offers hope of pardon for those whose circumstances left them unable to act, emphasizing that their weakness does not place them beyond Allah’s mercy and forgiveness.

translation: Whoever migrates for the sake of God will find in the land many places of refuge and abundant provision. And whoever leaves his home as a migrant to God and His Messenger, then death overtakes him, his reward is assured with God. God is ever Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: The verse reassures those who leave hardship or oppression for the sake of their faith: their circumstances need not define their future, for God can open ways to safety and provision. Their sincere intention is itself precious; even if death prevents them from reaching their destination, their reward rests with God, whose mercy and forgiveness encompass them.

translation: When you travel through the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer if you fear that those who disbelieve may harm you. Indeed, the disbelievers are an open enemy to you.
interpretation: The verse grants travelers a concession to shorten the prayer when they fear hostile people may endanger them. It recognizes the reality of that danger while affirming the clear hostility of those who oppose the believers.

translation: When you are among them and lead them in prayer, let a group of them stand with you, taking their weapons. When they have prostrated, let them move behind you, and let another group who have not yet prayed come and pray with you, taking their precautions and their weapons. Those who disbelieve wish that you would neglect your weapons and belongings so that they could attack you all at once. There is no blame on you if rain causes you hardship or you are ill and so lay down your weapons, but remain on your guard. Indeed, God has prepared a humiliating punishment for the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse teaches that worship is not abandoned even in danger, but its manner may be adapted to meet the circumstances: the community takes turns praying while remaining alert and prepared. The allowance to set weapons aside when hardship or illness makes carrying them difficult shows that vigilance is required alongside consideration for genuine need.

translation: When you have completed the prayer, remember God standing, sitting, and lying on your sides. Then, when you are secure, perform the prayer in full. Indeed, prayer is prescribed for the believers at appointed times.
interpretation: The verse teaches that remembrance of God is not confined to formal prayer but continues in every posture and circumstance. When danger or hardship has passed, believers should return to performing the prescribed prayers fully and at their appointed times.

translation: Do not lose heart in pursuing the enemy. If you suffer, they too suffer as you suffer; yet you hope from God for what they do not hope for. God is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: The verse urges believers not to let hardship make them falter: their opponents endure pain too, but faith gives believers a hope beyond the struggle. Their perseverance rests in trust that God knows their circumstances and governs matters with wisdom.

translation: Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, so that you may judge between people according to what Allah has shown you. Do not be an advocate for those who betray trust.
interpretation: The verse teaches that judgment must be guided by divine revelation and fairness, not by loyalty or persuasion. A person must not use their position to defend someone who has acted treacherously, even when that person seeks their support.

translation: And seek Allah’s forgiveness. Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: The verse urges sincere repentance and turning to Allah for forgiveness, trusting in His enduring mercy.

translation: And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves. Indeed, God does not love anyone who is habitually treacherous and sinful.
interpretation: The verse warns against using one’s words or influence to shield someone from accountability for wrongdoing. Such betrayal ultimately harms the wrongdoer as well, and persistent deception and sin place a person far from God’s love.

translation: They conceal themselves from people, but they cannot conceal themselves from Allah. He is with them when they secretly plan words that He does not approve of; and Allah encompasses all that they do.
interpretation: The verse exposes the contradiction of fearing people’s judgment while acting as though one can hide wrongdoing from God. His being “with them” means that their secret deliberations are fully known to Him, so concealment offers no escape from accountability.

translation: Here you are, arguing on their behalf in the life of this world—but who will argue with Allah on their behalf on the Day of Resurrection, or who will be their protector?
interpretation: The verse warns that human defense cannot make wrongdoing right or shield its perpetrators from God’s judgment. Those who plead for them now should recognize that no advocate can stand against God or protect them on the Day of Resurrection.

translation: Whoever does evil or wrongs himself, then seeks Allah’s forgiveness, will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: The verse offers hope to anyone who has sinned: they should turn to Allah for forgiveness rather than despair, trusting in His mercy and forgiveness.

translation: Whoever commits a sin brings its burden only upon himself. And God is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: A person is answerable for their own wrongdoing; its blame cannot be shifted onto someone else. God knows every deed and judges with wisdom.

translation: Whoever commits a sin or wrongdoing, then lays the blame for it on an innocent person, has burdened himself with slander and a manifest sin.
interpretation: The verse warns that trying to escape responsibility by accusing an innocent person does not erase one’s own wrongdoing; it adds the grave injustice of false accusation to the original sin.

translation: Had it not been for Allah’s favor and mercy upon you, a group of them would have tried to lead you astray. Yet they lead none astray but themselves, and they cannot harm you in any way. Allah has sent down to you the Book and wisdom, and taught you what you did not know. Allah’s favor upon you is truly immense.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the Prophet’s sound guidance and protection from those seeking to deceive him come through Allah’s mercy and the knowledge revealed to him. Their schemes ultimately damage only themselves, while Allah’s teaching and favor remain a profound gift to him.

translation: There is no good in much of their private conversation, except for one who urges charity, what is right, or reconciliation between people. Whoever does this seeking God’s pleasure—we shall grant them a tremendous reward.
interpretation: The verse shifts attention from how much people speak privately to what their words are meant to accomplish: counsel becomes virtuous when it serves others and repairs relationships, and its deepest worth lies in being offered sincerely for God’s pleasure.

translation: Whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him, and follows a way other than that of the believers, We will leave him to the course he has chosen and admit him to Hell—what an evil destination.
interpretation: The verse warns that knowingly rejecting the Messenger’s guidance and turning away from the believers’ way is a grave choice for which a person is held accountable: God lets that person pursue the path they have chosen, whose ultimate end is Hell.

translation: Indeed, Allah does not forgive associating partners with Him, but He forgives anything less than that for whom He wills. Whoever associates partners with Allah has certainly strayed far away.
interpretation: The verse warns that dying in the state of associating partners with God is uniquely grave, while the fate of those guilty of lesser sins remains subject to God’s will and mercy. It does not exclude sincere repentance, through which a person may turn back to God.

translation: They call upon, besides Him, none but female deities; they call upon none but a rebellious Satan.
interpretation: The verse exposes the spiritual reality behind worshipping idols: although people direct their prayers to figures they regard as divine, they are in effect following Satan’s rebellion against God. Calling the idols “female” also reflects the feminine names or forms associated with the deities worshipped by the verse’s audience.

translation: Allah cursed him, and he said, “I will surely take a prescribed share of Your servants.”
interpretation: Satan’s words express his defiant resolve to lead a portion of humanity astray, drawing them away from obedience to God. The verse warns that this temptation is deliberate, while also implying that people remain responsible for whether they follow it.

translation: “I will surely lead them astray, fill them with false hopes, and command them, so they will slit the ears of livestock; and I will command them, so they will alter Allah’s creation. Whoever takes Satan as a protector instead of Allah has certainly suffered a manifest loss.”
interpretation: Satan’s boast describes how he misguides people through deception, empty promises, and corrupt practices that they may treat as acceptable or sacred. “Altering Allah’s creation” includes distorting what God has made wholesome and the way He has guided people; the verse warns that surrendering one’s allegiance to Satan in place of Allah leads to unmistakable ruin.

translation: He makes them promises and fills them with hopes, but Satan promises them nothing except delusion.
interpretation: The verse warns that temptation can take the form of appealing assurances and hopes that seem comforting but have no trustworthy foundation. Such promises draw people away from God’s guidance by encouraging them to rely on wishful thinking rather than truth and accountability.

translation: Those are the ones whose abode is Hell, and they will find no escape from it.
interpretation: The verse warns that those who turn away from God and follow the path of falsehood will face an inescapable reckoning; no refuge can shield them from its consequence.

translation: As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, We will admit them into gardens beneath which rivers flow, where they will remain forever. This is God’s true promise—and who is more truthful in speech than God?
interpretation: The verse offers believers assurance that their faith and righteous actions lead, by God’s promise, to lasting reward. Its closing question emphasizes that this promise is wholly trustworthy because no one speaks more truthfully than God.

translation: It is not according to your wishes nor the wishes of the People of the Book. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, and will find for himself no protector or helper besides Allah.
interpretation: Neither group’s hopes or claims can replace moral accountability: a person’s standing before God is not secured by affiliation or wishful thinking, and no one can ultimately shield them from His judgment.

translation: Whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer—those will enter Paradise, and they will not be wronged even as much as the speck on a date seed.
interpretation: This verse teaches that God’s promise of Paradise is open equally to believing men and women who do good, and that divine judgment will not diminish anyone’s reward, however slightly.

translation: Who is better in religion than one who submits himself to Allah, does good, and follows the way of Abraham, inclining toward truth? Allah took Abraham as an intimate friend.
interpretation: True excellence in faith lies in wholehearted submission to Allah joined with righteous action and sincere devotion to the pure monotheism exemplified by Abraham. Abraham’s honored closeness to Allah affirms the dignity of this way.

translation: To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and Allah encompasses all things.
interpretation: Nothing lies beyond Allah’s ownership or knowledge: every part of creation is under His authority, and nothing is hidden from Him.

translation: They ask you for a ruling concerning women. Say, “Allah gives you a ruling concerning them, and so does what is recited to you in the Book concerning orphan girls to whom you do not give what is prescribed for them, though you desire to marry them; and concerning vulnerable children; and that you deal justly with orphans. Whatever good you do, Allah knows it.”
interpretation: The verse directs the Prophet to affirm that divine guidance governs the treatment of women and vulnerable children. In particular, guardians must not exploit orphan girls in their care by withholding their due rights while seeking to marry them, and they must uphold justice for all orphans. The closing assurance reminds them that no good deed or act of fairness is hidden from Allah.

translation: If a woman fears ill-treatment or abandonment from her husband, there is no blame on them if they reach a settlement between themselves; and settlement is better. Selfishness is ever present in human souls. If you act with kindness and remain mindful of God, surely God is fully aware of what you do.
interpretation: The verse permits spouses facing serious strain to seek a mutually acceptable reconciliation, while affirming that such a settlement should be grounded in fairness and goodwill rather than pressure. It recognizes how self-interest can make compromise difficult, and calls both parties to act generously and with awareness that God knows their conduct.

translation: You will never be able to be perfectly equal between wives, even if you strive; so do not incline entirely toward one, leaving another as though suspended. If you make amends and are mindful of God, then God is ever Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: The verse recognizes that complete equality in inward affection is beyond human control, but this does not excuse injustice in conduct. A person must not let a stronger attachment lead them to neglect another wife’s rights or leave her in an uncertain, unsupported position; sincere efforts to act justly and remain mindful of God are met with His forgiveness and mercy.

translation: If the two separate, God will provide each of them from His abundance. God is All-Encompassing, All-Wise.
interpretation: The verse reassures those facing marital separation that their well-being is not confined to the marriage: God’s provision and care extend beyond what they can presently see. It also teaches that such outcomes occur within His wisdom, even when their reasons are not fully apparent.

translation: To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. We have indeed instructed those who were given the Scripture before you, and you yourselves, to be mindful of Allah. If you disbelieve, then to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Allah is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy.
interpretation: The command to be mindful of Allah is for humanity’s own guidance, not because Allah needs anyone’s obedience. His sovereignty and worthiness of praise remain unchanged whether people believe or turn away.

translation: To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and Allah is sufficient as the One entrusted with all affairs.
interpretation: Because all creation belongs to Allah, people may entrust their affairs to Him with confidence: His care and authority are sufficient, and nothing lies beyond His power or knowledge.

translation: If He wills, He can remove you, O people, and bring others in your place. And Allah is fully capable of doing so.
interpretation: The verse reminds people that their existence and place in the world are not beyond God’s control. He is not dependent on any generation or community, and can replace them with others whenever He wills; this calls people to humility and obedience rather than presuming their position is secure.

translation: Whoever desires the reward of this world, then with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.
interpretation: The verse directs people not to restrict their hopes to worldly gain: every kind of reward lies with God, so one should seek His favor with sincerity, knowing that He hears what people ask for and sees what they do.

translation: O you who believe, stand firmly for justice as witnesses for Allah, even if it is against yourselves, your parents, or your close relatives. Whether someone is rich or poor, Allah has greater claim over both. So do not follow your desires and turn away from justice. If you distort your testimony or refuse to give it, Allah is fully aware of what you do.
interpretation: The verse calls believers to make justice a matter of loyalty to God, not personal advantage or family allegiance. A person’s wealth or poverty must not sway judgment, because God knows what is truly best for everyone. The warning against distorting testimony or withholding it makes clear that impartial justice requires both speaking truthfully and not evading the truth.

translation: O you who believe, believe in Allah and His Messenger, and in the Book He has sent down to His Messenger, and the Scriptures He sent down before. Whoever disbelieves in Allah, His angels, His Scriptures, His messengers, and the Last Day has indeed strayed far away.
interpretation: The address calls believers to make their faith whole and steadfast: faith in the Qur’an and the Prophet ﷺ belongs together with recognition of the earlier revelations and all the foundations of faith named here. Rejecting any of these is not a minor departure, but a turning away from the guidance that leads to Allah.

translation: Indeed, those who believe, then disbelieve, then believe, then disbelieve, and then increase in disbelief—Allah will not forgive them, nor guide them to a way.
interpretation: The verse warns of a settled pattern of rejecting faith: repeated reversals that culminate in deeper disbelief harden a person against guidance. Its warning concerns those who persist in that state, turning away from the path that leads to forgiveness.

translation: Give the hypocrites the news that they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: The wording is deliberately ironic: a message normally associated with good news is used to warn that hypocrisy and concealed disbelief lead to severe punishment.

translation: Those who take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers—do they seek honor from them? Surely all honor belongs to God.
interpretation: The verse warns against seeking dignity, security, or influence through allegiance that turns one away from the believing community and from God. Any lasting honor comes from God, not from those whose approval or power people hope to gain.

translation: He has already revealed to you in the Book that when you hear Allah’s verses being denied and mocked, you must not sit with those who do so until they turn to a different conversation. Otherwise, you would be like them. Surely Allah will gather the hypocrites and the disbelievers all together in Hell.
interpretation: The verse teaches that a believer must not remain in a gathering where Allah’s revelation is being mocked as though it were acceptable. Staying silent in that setting can make one complicit; one should leave until the conversation changes.

translation: Those who wait to see what happens to you: if you gain a victory from Allah, they say, “Were we not with you?” But if the disbelievers gain a share of success, they say, “Did we not gain influence over you and protect you from the believers?” Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection, and Allah will never grant the disbelievers a decisive way over the believers.
interpretation: The verse condemns those who shift their loyalties to suit whoever seems likely to prevail, claiming closeness to the believers when they succeed and using their dealings with them to curry favor with their opponents when they do not. Their claims cannot settle the truth: Allah will expose and judge their conduct, and the final outcome will not give the disbelievers ultimate authority over the believers.

translation: Indeed, the hypocrites seek to deceive Allah, but He turns their deception back upon them. When they rise for prayer, they rise lazily, showing off before people, and remember Allah only a little.
interpretation: Their outward worship is driven by appearances rather than sincere devotion. Allah’s “deception” means that their attempt to conceal their hypocrisy does not escape Him; instead, their own conduct leads them toward the consequence they sought to evade.

translation: Wavering between the two, belonging neither to these nor to those. And whoever Allah lets go astray—you will never find a way for him.
interpretation: This describes people who shift between opposing sides without sincere commitment or a settled faith. Their wavering leaves them without a true path, and no one can guide them when Allah has left them to their misguidance.

translation: O you who believe, do not take disbelievers as allies in place of the believers. Do you wish to give Allah clear grounds against yourselves?
interpretation: The verse warns believers against giving their loyalty and support to those who oppose the believing community in a way that betrays their faith. Such a choice makes them accountable before God, as though they had supplied clear grounds for judgment against themselves.

translation: Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire, and you will find no helper for them.
interpretation: The verse warns that knowingly presenting oneself as faithful while concealing rejection is a grave betrayal, not a harmless outward pretense. Its mention of the lowest depths underscores the severity of this wrongdoing, and the absence of a helper conveys that no one can shield them from its consequence.

translation: Except for those who repent, set things right, hold fast to Allah, and devote their religion sincerely to Him: they will be with the believers. And Allah will grant the believers a tremendous reward.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that a person’s past wrongdoing need not define their standing: sincere repentance must be joined with changed conduct, steadfast reliance on Allah, and worship free of hypocrisy. Through this sincere return, a person is restored to the company of the believers and may hope for Allah’s great reward.

translation: Why should Allah punish you if you are grateful and believe? Allah is ever appreciative, all-knowing.
interpretation: The verse affirms that Allah has no need to punish people who respond to His blessings with faith and gratitude. He knows their sincerity and appreciates their faith and thankfulness, rewarding them for it.

translation: Allah does not love the public utterance of evil, except by someone who has been wronged. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: The verse permits a person who has suffered injustice to speak openly about the wrong and seek redress, while discouraging harmful speech for its own sake. Allah hears what is said and knows both the circumstances and the intent behind it.

translation: Whether you make a good deed known or keep it hidden, or pardon a wrong, surely Allah is Ever-Pardoning, All-Powerful.
interpretation: The verse teaches that sincere goodness is valued whether seen by others or kept private, and that forgiving someone who has wronged you is especially noble. Allah’s power to punish does not prevent Him from choosing pardon, offering believers a model of mercy joined with strength.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers, and wish to make a distinction between Allah and His messengers, saying, “We believe in some and reject others,” and seeking to adopt a way in between—
interpretation: True faith cannot be divided into selective acceptance: to affirm Allah while rejecting messengers He sent is to reject the authority of the One who sent them. Claiming a middle course between belief and disbelief does not reconcile the two; it undermines faith by refusing to accept Allah’s guidance in its entirety.

translation: Those are truly the disbelievers, and We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: The verse emphatically identifies them as genuine disbelievers and warns that their rejection will lead to punishment marked by humiliation.

translation: As for those who believe in God and His messengers and make no distinction between any of them, He will grant them their rewards. God is ever Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: True faith receives God’s messengers as one connected chain of guidance, rather than accepting some while rejecting others. The promise of reward is paired with God’s forgiveness and mercy, reassuring believers that divine acceptance rests not on flawless people but on sincere faith and God’s grace.

translation: The People of the Book ask you to bring down to them a scripture from heaven. Yet they asked Moses for something even greater, saying, “Show us God openly,” and the thunderbolt seized them for their wrongdoing. Then, after clear proofs had come to them, they took the calf as a god; but We pardoned them for that. And We gave Moses clear authority.
interpretation: The verse presents these demands as part of a pattern of defiance rather than a sincere search for guidance: even after clear signs, they persisted in wrongdoing. At the same time, God’s pardon and the authority given to Moses show that divine guidance and mercy were made clear to them.

translation: And We raised the Mount above them in connection with their covenant, and We said to them, “Enter the gate bowing,” and We said to them, “Do not transgress concerning the Sabbath.” And We took from them a solemn covenant.
interpretation: The verse portrays the covenant as a binding charge to obey God’s commands with humility and faithfulness. The commands concerning entering the gate and observing the Sabbath were not mere formalities; violating them meant breaking a solemn commitment made before God.

translation: So, because of their breaking of their covenant, their rejection of God’s signs, their killing of the prophets unjustly, and their claim, “Our hearts are wrapped,” God sealed their hearts because of their disbelief; therefore, they believe only a little.
interpretation: Their claim that their hearts were closed to the message is rejected: the verse presents their spiritual unresponsiveness not as an excuse, but as the consequence of persistent disbelief and violation of their covenant.

translation: And for their disbelief and their uttering against Mary a tremendous slander.
interpretation: The verse condemns those who disbelieved and wronged Mary by making a grave false accusation against her, emphasizing the enormity of their injustice.

translation: And for their saying, “We killed the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, the Messenger of Allah”—though they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him; rather, it was made to appear so to them. Those who differed about him are surely in doubt concerning him. They have no knowledge of it, but only follow conjecture. They certainly did not kill him.
interpretation: The verse rejects the claim that Jesus was killed or crucified by his opponents and stresses that their certainty was unfounded. Their conflicting accounts arose from doubt and conjecture, not knowledge; the event was made to appear to them otherwise, while the truth of what happened remained beyond their grasp.

translation: Rather, Allah raised him to Himself. And Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.
interpretation: Allah’s raising of Jesus shows that his enemies could not overcome God’s decree: God protected and honored him by His power, and this occurred according to His wisdom.

translation: There is none among the People of the Book who will not believe in him before his death; and on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them.
interpretation: On this interpretation, “his death” refers to Jesus’s death: when Jesus returns before the end of time, the People of the Book then living will recognize the truth about him, and he will testify on the Day of Resurrection concerning their response to his message.

translation: So, because of wrongdoing by those who became Jews, We forbade them good things that had previously been lawful to them, and because they turned many away from the way of Allah.
interpretation: The verse presents the restriction of these lawful blessings as a consequence of persistent wrongdoing and obstructing others from faith—not as an arbitrary decree. It warns that rejecting moral responsibility can bring spiritual and communal consequences.

translation: And for their taking of usury, though they had been forbidden from it, and for their wrongful consumption of people’s wealth; and We have prepared a painful punishment for the disbelievers among them.
interpretation: The verse presents knowingly violating divine limits and exploiting others’ wealth as serious moral wrongdoing, while making clear that the threatened punishment applies to the disbelievers among those addressed.

translation: But those firmly grounded in knowledge among them, and the believers, believe in what has been sent down to you and what was sent down before you; and those who establish prayer, give zakah, and believe in Allah and the Last Day—those We will grant a great reward.
interpretation: In contrast to those who knowingly reject or distort revelation, sincere understanding leads to faith in God’s guidance across generations.
