That faith is made evident through worship, generosity, and accountability before God; the promise of great reward rests on this sincere commitment, not merely on affiliation or inherited status.

translation: Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him. And We revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob and the Tribes, Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron, and Solomon; and We gave David the Psalms.
interpretation: The verse affirms that revelation to Muhammad belongs to the same divine guidance given to earlier prophets. By naming prophets from different generations and communities, it presents their message as one continuous source of guidance, rather than something unprecedented.

translation: And messengers We have already told you about, and messengers We have not told you about. And Allah spoke to Moses directly.
interpretation: The verse teaches that God’s messengers were more numerous than those named in revelation, so people should not assume that only the known prophets were sent. It also highlights Moses’s distinct honor: God addressed him directly, affirming the reality and special nature of his communication with God.

translation: Messengers bringing good news and giving warning, so that people would have no argument against God after the messengers. And God is Almighty, All-Wise.
interpretation: God sent messengers to make His guidance clear, so people could not claim they were left without direction or warning. His power and wisdom are evident in both sending them and holding people accountable after the message has reached them.

translation: But Allah bears witness to what He has sent down to you: He sent it down with His knowledge, and the angels bear witness as well. And Allah is sufficient as a witness.
interpretation: The verse reassures the Prophet that the truth of the revelation does not depend on people’s acceptance of it: Allah Himself testifies to its origin and knows fully what He revealed, while the angels also bear witness. His testimony alone is sufficient to establish the revelation’s truth.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieved and turned others away from the path of Allah have strayed far astray.
interpretation: Rejecting the truth is itself a departure from guidance, and actively obstructing others from it deepens that departure, taking a person far from the way that leads to Allah.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and commit wrongdoing—Allah will not forgive them, nor guide them to any path.
interpretation: The verse warns that those who persist in rejecting the truth and doing wrong shut themselves off from forgiveness and divine guidance.

translation: Except to the path of Hell, where they will remain forever; and that is easy for Allah.
interpretation: Those who persist in disbelief and wrongdoing after rejecting guidance are being warned that their end is the path to Hell. Their everlasting punishment is no difficulty for Allah, whose judgment is carried out with complete power.

translation: O mankind, the Messenger has come to you with the truth from your Lord, so believe—it is better for you. But if you disbelieve, then to Allah belongs all that is in the heavens and the earth. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: Belief is urged as a good that benefits people themselves, not something God needs from them. Their disbelief cannot diminish His dominion over creation; His knowledge and wisdom encompass both His call to faith and the consequences of accepting or rejecting it.

translation: O People of the Book, do not go to excess in your religion, and say of God only what is true. The Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, was only a messenger of God, His word which He conveyed to Mary, and a spirit from Him. So believe in God and His messengers, and do not say, “Three.” Desist; that is better for you. God is only one God. Glory be to Him—far above having a child! To Him belongs all that is in the heavens and all that is on earth, and God is sufficient as Trustee.
interpretation: The verse calls for reverence for Jesus without exceeding what it presents as his proper status: he is God’s messenger, brought into being by God’s command and honored as a spirit from Him, but not divine or God’s son. Its central teaching is that God is utterly one, and that belief should affirm this oneness while avoiding claims that compromise it.

translation: The Messiah would never disdain to be a servant of Allah, nor would the angels brought near. Whoever disdains worshipping Him and acts arrogantly, He will gather them all to Himself.
interpretation: Even the Messiah and the angels nearest to Allah are honored as His servants; true honor does not lie in refusing worship. Those who reject devotion out of pride will ultimately stand together before Allah.

translation: As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, He will give them their rewards in full and increase them from His bounty. But those who disdain and act arrogantly, He will punish with a painful punishment, and they will find no guardian or helper for themselves besides God.
interpretation: The verse contrasts God’s justice with His generosity: He grants the faithful what they have earned and gives them even more by His grace. It also warns that prideful refusal to submit to God cannot shield anyone from accountability; no other power can replace His protection.

translation: O humanity, a clear proof has come to you from your Lord, and We have sent down to you a manifest light.
interpretation: The verse presents God’s revelation as both decisive evidence and illuminating guidance: it calls all people to recognize the truth through clear proof and to let that guidance dispel confusion and direct their lives.

translation: As for those who believe in Allah and hold fast to Him, He will admit them into mercy and grace from Himself, and guide them to Himself along a straight path.
interpretation: Holding fast to Allah means relying on Him and remaining steadfast in His guidance; the verse assures believers that this devotion leads, by His mercy and grace, to a life directed toward Him without deviation.

translation: They ask you for a ruling. Say, “Allah gives you a ruling concerning kalālah: If a man dies leaving no child but has a sister, she receives half of what he leaves; and he inherits from her if she leaves no child. If there are two sisters, they receive two-thirds of what he leaves. If there are brothers and sisters, the male receives the share of two females.” Allah makes things clear to you, lest you go astray; and Allah has knowledge of all things.
interpretation: The verse clarifies how inheritance is to be apportioned among siblings when the deceased leaves no child, setting out their shares so that family claims are governed by divine guidance rather than uncertainty or dispute. Its closing words emphasize that these rulings are part of Allah’s comprehensive knowledge and are intended to keep people from going astray.

translation: In the name of God, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. O you who believe, fulfill your commitments. Grazing livestock are lawful for you, except what is recited to you, and do not make hunting lawful while you are in a state of consecration. God decrees whatever He wills.
interpretation: The verse teaches that faith entails honoring one’s commitments while accepting that God alone determines what is lawful and forbidden. Its specific restriction on hunting during consecration shows that devotion requires obeying divine limits even when an otherwise permitted act is involved.

translation: O you who believe, do not violate the rites of God, nor the sacred month, nor the sacrificial offerings, nor the garlands, nor those traveling to the Sacred House seeking bounty from their Lord and His pleasure. When you have left the state of consecration, you may hunt. Do not let hatred of a people who barred you from the Sacred Mosque lead you to transgress. Cooperate in righteousness and mindfulness of God, and do not cooperate in sin and aggression. Be mindful of God; surely God is severe in punishment.
interpretation: The verse teaches that reverence for sacred worship must be joined with justice toward others: even when wronged, believers must not let resentment justify wrongdoing. Their dealings should instead be guided by cooperation in what is right and restraint from harm, knowing that they are accountable to God.

translation: Forbidden to you are carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, and that over which any name other than God’s has been invoked; animals strangled, beaten to death, killed by a fall, gored, or partly eaten by a predator—except what you are able to slaughter properly—and what is sacrificed on stone altars. Also forbidden is seeking decisions by divining arrows. That is sinful disobedience. Today those who disbelieve have despaired of overcoming your religion, so do not fear them; fear Me. Today I have perfected your religion for you, completed My favor upon you, and chosen Islam for you as a religion. But whoever is compelled by severe hunger, without inclining toward sin, will find God All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse presents religious obedience as both a clear moral boundary and a source of security: devotion is not to be mixed with idolatrous rites or claims to divine knowledge through omens. The declaration that the religion is perfected grounds believers’ confidence in God’s guidance rather than in their opponents’ approval or power. Yet the allowance in genuine necessity shows that this guidance is not heedless of human vulnerability: preserving life is not itself a sin, and God’s mercy accompanies sincere restraint.

translation: They ask you what has been made lawful for them. Say, “Lawful for you are all good things, and what your trained hunting animals catch for you, which you train in accordance with what Allah has taught you. So eat from what they catch for you, and mention Allah’s name over it. Be mindful of Allah; surely Allah is swift in reckoning.”
interpretation: The verse permits wholesome food and game caught by animals trained to hunt under human direction, provided the believer remembers Allah when taking the game. Its permission is joined to responsibility: people should follow the limits Allah has taught and remain mindful that they will answer to Him.

translation: Today, the good things have been made lawful for you. The food of those who were given the Book is lawful for you, and your food is lawful for them. Also lawful for you are chaste women from among the believers and chaste women from among those who were given the Book before you, provided you give them their bridal gifts, seeking marriage—not fornication or secret affairs. Whoever rejects faith, their deeds have come to nothing, and in the Hereafter they will be among the losers.
interpretation: The verse permits marriage to chaste women from the People of the Book, as well as the exchange of lawful food, while placing marriage within a committed bond marked by the bridal gift—not illicit relationships. It closes by warning that outwardly good deeds cannot benefit a person who rejects faith.

translation: O you who believe, when you rise to pray, wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows, wipe your heads, and wash your feet up to the ankles. If you are in a state of major ritual impurity, purify yourselves. If you are ill, travelling, have come from relieving yourselves, or have been intimate with women, and cannot find water, then seek clean earth and wipe your faces and hands with it. God does not intend to place you in difficulty; rather, He intends to purify you and complete His blessing upon you, so that you may be grateful.
interpretation: The prescribed washing and the allowance of dry purification together show that the purpose of these rites is not hardship, but to prepare believers for prayer in a state of purity. When water is unavailable or its use is not feasible, the concession preserves that purpose, reminding believers that God’s guidance joins reverence in worship with mercy toward human need.

translation: And remember Allah’s favor upon you and the covenant He made with you when you said, “We hear and obey.” Be mindful of Allah; surely Allah knows what is within hearts.
interpretation: The verse calls believers to keep their pledge of obedience to Allah with genuine sincerity, remembering His favors and knowing that He is fully aware of the intentions and feelings they conceal.

translation: O you who believe, stand steadfast for Allah, bearing witness with justice. Do not let hatred of a people lead you to act unjustly. Be just; that is nearer to God-consciousness. Be mindful of Allah; surely Allah is fully aware of what you do.
interpretation: Faithful devotion to God requires justice even toward those one dislikes or opposes. Personal hostility must never distort judgment, because fairness is a mark of God-consciousness, and nothing people do is hidden from Allah.

translation: Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds that they will have forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: The verse offers reassurance that sincere faith, expressed through righteous action, is met by God’s forgiveness and an immense reward.

translation: As for those who disbelieve and deny Our signs, they are the companions of the Fire.
interpretation: The verse warns that rejecting faith and refusing the signs God has made clear carries the grave consequence of belonging to the Fire.

translation: O you who believe, remember God’s favor upon you when a people intended to reach out against you, but He restrained their hands from you. Be mindful of God, and let the believers place their trust in God.
interpretation: The verse teaches believers to remember that their safety and deliverance ultimately come from God. Such remembrance should deepen gratitude and mindfulness of Him, while strengthening trust in His protection rather than in one’s own power.

translation: God took a covenant from the Children of Israel and raised among them twelve leaders. God said, “I am with you: if you establish prayer, give alms, believe in My messengers, support and honor them, and offer God a goodly loan, I will surely erase your misdeeds and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow. But whoever among you disbelieves after that has strayed from the right path.”
interpretation: The covenant makes clear that divine support is tied to lived faith: worship, generosity, and steadfast support for God’s messengers. The promise of forgiveness and Paradise shows God’s mercy toward those who honor that commitment, while the warning stresses that turning away after receiving such clear guidance is a serious departure from the path.

translation: So, because they broke their covenant, We condemned them and made their hearts hard. They distort words from their proper meanings and have forgotten a portion of what they were reminded of. You will continue to discover treachery among them, except for a few. Yet pardon them and overlook their wrongs; indeed, God loves those who do good.
interpretation: The verse portrays covenant-breaking as a cause of spiritual estrangement: hearts become hardened, revelation is distorted, and guidance is neglected. Yet the Prophet is instructed to respond to wrongdoing with pardon and graciousness, showing that steadfast justice can be joined with mercy and that God loves those who act with excellence.

translation: And from those who said, “We are Christians,” We took their covenant, but they forgot a portion of what they had been reminded of. So We stirred up among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection. And God will inform them of what they used to do.
interpretation: The verse teaches that neglecting the guidance and obligations people have been given can fracture their community and foster lasting hostility. Their actions are not forgotten: God will make their full consequences clear and hold them accountable.

translation: O People of the Scripture, Our Messenger has come to you, making clear much of what you used to conceal from the Scripture, and overlooking much. There has come to you from Allah a light and a clear Book.
interpretation: The verse portrays revelation as a restoration of moral and spiritual clarity: the Messenger exposes concealed teachings where doing so is needed, while not dwelling on every hidden matter. The light and clear Book offer guidance by which people can recognize truth and orient their lives toward God.

translation: Through it, Allah guides those who seek His pleasure to the ways of peace, brings them out of darkness into light by His permission, and guides them to a straight path.
interpretation: The verse teaches that sincere devotion to Allah’s approval opens a person to the guidance of revelation: it leads them away from confusion and wrongdoing toward clarity, peace, and upright living. This transformation ultimately depends on Allah’s permission and guidance.

translation: Those who say, “God is the Messiah, son of Mary,” have surely disbelieved. Say, “Who could have any power against God if He willed to destroy the Messiah, son of Mary, his mother, and everyone on earth?” To God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them. He creates whatever He wills, and God has power over all things.
interpretation: The verse rejects identifying Jesus with God by pointing to his dependence on God’s will: if Jesus and his mother are subject to God’s power over life and death, they are not themselves the ultimate sovereign. The closing affirmation grounds this distinction in God’s exclusive dominion and freedom to create as He wills.

translation: The Jews and the Christians say, “We are the children of Allah and His beloved.” Say, “Then why does He punish you for your sins? Rather, you are human beings among those He created. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and to Him is the return.”
interpretation: No community can claim immunity from accountability or a guaranteed place with God on the basis of its identity. People stand before Him as His created servants, and judgment belongs to Him alone; His sovereign authority and the return of all creation to Him make humility and repentance more fitting than presumption.

translation: O People of the Scripture, Our Messenger has come to you, making things clear to you after an interval in which no messengers came, lest you say, “No bringer of good news or warner came to us.” Indeed, a bringer of good news and a warner has now come to you. And Allah has power over all things.
interpretation: The verse presents the Prophet’s mission as a mercy and a clear proof for the People of the Scripture: after a long pause in revelation, God sent a messenger to clarify the truth and remove the excuse that no warning or good news had reached them. His sending testifies to God’s power and wisdom.

translation: And [remember] when Moses said to his people, “O my people, recall God’s favor upon you: He raised prophets among you, made you people of authority, and gave you what He had given no one else among the worlds.”
interpretation: Moses calls his people to recognize that their prophetic guidance, freedom, and distinctive blessings are gifts entrusted to them by God. Remembering these favors should lead to gratitude and faithful obedience, not pride or a sense of entitlement.

translation: O my people, enter the holy land that God has decreed for you, and do not turn back, or you will become losers.
interpretation: The verse presents obedience and courage as essential to fulfilling a divine command: turning away out of fear would mean forfeiting the opportunity God had given them.

translation: They said, “O Moses, there are people of great strength in it, and we will never enter it until they leave. If they leave it, then we will enter.”
interpretation: Their reply reveals that fear of the people inside had become a condition for obedience: they would act only once the danger was gone. The verse thus portrays a hesitation to trust God’s command when it required courage in the face of a formidable challenge.

translation: Two men among those who feared God, whom He had blessed, said, “Enter upon them through the gate. When you enter it, you will surely prevail. And place your trust in God, if you are believers.”
interpretation: The two men encourage their people to meet fear with both action and reliance on God: they must take the step before them, while placing their confidence in Him. Their words show that faith is not passive; it gives people courage to act despite danger.

translation: They said, “O Moses, we will never enter it while they remain there. So go—you and your Lord—and fight; we will stay right here.”
interpretation: Their reply reveals a fearful and defiant refusal to obey God’s command: instead of trusting Him and joining Moses, they leave the struggle to him and speak with contemptuous disregard for the duty placed upon them.

translation: He said, “My Lord, I have authority over none but myself and my brother, so judge between us and the defiantly disobedient people.”
interpretation: Moses acknowledges that he cannot compel the rebellious people to obey; his responsibility extends only to himself and his brother. He therefore entrusts the matter to God, asking Him to distinguish them from those who have persisted in disobedience.

translation: He said, “Then it is forbidden to them for forty years; they will wander through the land. So do not grieve over the defiantly disobedient people.”
interpretation: Their refusal to trust and obey God brings a consequence that delays their entry into the land. The command not to grieve reassures Moses that their fate is not his burden to carry.

translation: And recite to them in truth the account of the two sons of Adam: when they each offered a sacrifice, it was accepted from one of them but not accepted from the other. He said, “I will surely kill you.” The other said, “Allah accepts only from the mindful of Him.”
interpretation: Acceptance by Allah is not secured merely by performing an outward act; it depends on God-consciousness and sincere devotion. The verse also exposes how envy can turn disappointment into wrongful aggression, while the response points back to the true measure of a deed rather than retaliating in kind.

translation: If you reach out your hand to kill me, I will not reach out my hand to kill you. Indeed, I fear Allah, Lord of all worlds.
interpretation: The speaker’s refusal to retaliate reflects a commitment to obeying God even when threatened, recognizing that fear of divine judgment must restrain the urge to answer violence with violence.

translation: I would rather you incur the sin of killing me along with your own sin, and so become one of the people of the Fire. That is the recompense of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The speaker refuses to answer the threat of violence with violence. He warns that murdering an innocent person would add the grave sin of that killing to the aggressor’s own wrongdoing, bringing the consequence of the Fire.

translation: Then his soul made killing his brother seem easy to him, so he killed him and became one of the losers.
interpretation: The verse shows how a person’s unchecked inner desires can dull moral judgment until a grave wrong seems bearable. By yielding to that impulse, he brought upon himself a profound spiritual and moral loss.

translation: Then Allah sent a raven scratching at the earth to show him how to conceal his brother’s body. He said, “Woe to me! Could I not be like this raven and conceal my brother’s body?” And he became one of the remorseful.
interpretation: The verse portrays how the killer, confronted with the raven burying something in the earth, learned how to bury his brother. His words express belated remorse: he recognizes his helplessness and wrongdoing only after the deed is done.

translation: For that reason We decreed for the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul—unless in retribution for a life or for corruption in the land—it is as though he had killed all humanity; and whoever saves a life, it is as though he had saved all humanity. Our messengers came to them with clear proofs, yet many of them, even after that, continued to transgress in the land.
interpretation: The verse teaches the immense sanctity of human life: an unjust killing is not merely a private crime but an assault on the principle that protects all people, while preserving a life affirms that same principle for everyone. Its force is moral rather than a claim that one act literally equals countless deaths or rescues; it calls people to uphold life and warns that clear divine guidance does not prevent many from exceeding its bounds.

translation: The recompense of those who wage war against God and His Messenger and strive to spread corruption in the land is that they be killed, or crucified, or have their hands and feet cut off on opposite sides, or be banished from the land. That is their disgrace in this world, and in the Hereafter they will have a tremendous punishment.
interpretation: Classical Muslim interpretation understands this warning in the context of violent acts that terrorize people and destroy public safety, such as armed banditry—not mere disagreement or dissent. The prescribed penalties are matters for legitimate judicial authority, applied with due process and according to the circumstances; the verse does not authorize private individuals to punish others.

translation: Except for those who repent before you gain power over them; then know that Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse presents sincere repentance before capture as a meaningful return to God, whose mercy remains open even after grave wrongdoing. In the context of this passage, such repentance also affects the worldly punishment for the offense, while the rights of any people harmed are not thereby erased.

translation: O you who believe, be mindful of Allah, seek the means of drawing near to Him, and strive in His cause, so that you may prosper.
interpretation: True success comes through a life oriented toward God: guarding oneself against disobedience, seeking closeness to Him through what He approves, and exerting sincere effort in His cause. The verse joins inward devotion with purposeful action, making prosperity the fruit of both.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve—if they possessed everything on earth, and as much again, to offer as ransom from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, it would not be accepted from them; and they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the Hereafter is not governed by wealth or bargaining. No worldly possession, however vast, can undo a person’s rejection of faith or serve as a substitute for sincere belief and accountability before God.

translation: They will wish to leave the Fire, but they will not leave it; and theirs will be an abiding punishment.
interpretation: The verse portrays the hopelessness of those condemned to the Fire: their desire to escape will not be fulfilled, and their punishment will endure.

translation: As for the male thief and the female thief, cut off their hands as recompense for what they have earned, a deterrent from God. And God is Almighty, Wise.
interpretation: The verse presents theft’s prescribed penalty as a deterrent and a protection for people’s property, while attributing the law to God’s wisdom and authority. Its application belongs to lawful judgment under the relevant legal conditions, not to private individuals acting on their own.

translation: Whoever repents after committing wrongdoing and makes things right—Allah will accept his repentance. Indeed, Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse teaches that sincere repentance is more than regret: it involves turning away from the wrongdoing and repairing what one can. A person who does so should not despair of Allah’s forgiveness and mercy.

translation: Do you not know that to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth? He punishes whom He wills and forgives whom He wills. And Allah has power over all things.
interpretation: The verse calls people to recognize that judgment and forgiveness belong to God alone. His decisions are not constrained by anyone, so people should neither presume upon His mercy nor despair of it; they should turn to Him with humility and hope.

translation: O Messenger, do not let those who hasten toward disbelief grieve you—those who say, “We believe,” with their mouths while their hearts do not believe, and those among the Jews. They eagerly listen to falsehood and listen on behalf of other people who have not come to you. They distort words from their proper meanings, saying, “If you are given this, accept it; but if you are not given it, beware.” Whoever God wills to leave in trial, you can do nothing for him against God. Those are the ones whose hearts God has not willed to purify. They will have disgrace in this world, and a tremendous punishment in the Hereafter.
interpretation: The verse reassures the Messenger that the schemes of people who manipulate revelation for their own ends do not diminish the truth or place its outcome in his hands. Its warning is that knowingly twisting guidance and treating it as useful only when it serves one’s interests leaves the heart exposed to corruption; the resulting disgrace and punishment are consequences of that deliberate refusal of sincerity.

translation: They are avid listeners to falsehood and devourers of illicit gain. So if they come to you, judge between them or turn away from them. If you turn away from them, they can do you no harm at all. But if you judge, judge between them with justice. Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly.
interpretation: The verse condemns those who willingly heed falsehood and profit from what is forbidden, while affirming that any judgment must be impartial: the Prophet may decline to adjudicate their case, but if he does judge, he must uphold justice, which Allah loves.

translation: How is it that they ask you to judge when they have the Torah, which contains God’s judgment, and then turn away after that? Such people are not believers.
interpretation: The verse rebukes those who appeal to the Prophet for a ruling while possessing God’s revealed guidance, yet turn away when the judgment does not suit them. Their selective acceptance shows that they are not sincerely submitting to God’s authority.

translation: Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which there was guidance and light. By it the prophets who submitted to God judged for the Jews, as did the devoted scholars and religious authorities, according to what they had been entrusted to preserve of God’s Book, and to which they bore witness. So do not fear people; fear Me. And do not trade My revelations for a small price. Whoever does not judge by what God has revealed—those are the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse calls those entrusted with scripture to uphold God’s guidance faithfully and without letting fear, self-interest, or worldly gain distort their judgments. Its stern warning concerns turning away from God’s revealed authority; the surrounding context directs the charge particularly at those who knowingly conceal or alter the guidance they were responsible for preserving.

translation: And We prescribed for them in it: a life for a life, an eye for an eye, a nose for a nose, an ear for an ear, a tooth for a tooth, and for wounds, equal retaliation. But whoever waives it as charity, it will be an expiation for him. And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed—those are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse establishes that justice must be proportionate: an injury must not be answered with excess. Yet it also honors forgiveness, presenting the voluntary relinquishment of a rightful claim as an act of charity and a means of expiation. Its warning condemns those entrusted with judgment who knowingly abandon God’s guidance and thereby wrong others.

translation: And We sent, following in their footsteps, Jesus son of Mary, confirming what came before him of the Torah. And We gave him the Gospel, in which was guidance and light, confirming what came before it of the Torah, and as guidance and an admonition for the mindful.
interpretation: The verse presents Jesus’ mission and the Gospel as part of the continuing divine guidance revealed through earlier prophets. The Gospel’s confirmation of the Torah affirms that the revelations share a common source, while its guidance, light, and admonition benefit those who are mindful of God and receptive to His direction.

translation: Let the people of the Gospel judge by what Allah has revealed in it. Whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed—those are the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: The verse calls those entrusted with scripture to uphold and judge by the guidance God revealed, rather than setting it aside or following their own preferences; knowingly turning away from that guidance is an act of disobedience.

translation: We have sent down to you the Book in truth, confirming the Scripture that came before it and standing as a guardian over it. So judge between them by what Allah has sent down, and do not follow their desires, turning away from the truth that has come to you. For each of you We appointed a law and a way. Had Allah willed, He could have made you one community, but He tests you through what He has given you. So strive to excel in good deeds. To Allah you will all return, and He will then make clear to you the matters over which you differed.
interpretation: The different laws given to communities are presented as a test of how people respond to divine guidance, not as a reason to pursue personal preference or rivalry. The verse directs people instead to prove their faith through good deeds, trusting that ultimate judgment—and the resolution of disputes—belongs to Allah.

translation: And judge between them by what Allah has revealed, and do not follow their desires. Beware lest they turn you away from some of what Allah has revealed to you. If they turn away, then know that Allah intends to afflict them for some of their sins. Indeed, many people are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: The verse calls for integrity in judgment: a person entrusted with applying divine guidance must not bend it to satisfy others’ preferences or pressure. Their rejection does not justify abandoning that duty; it is instead a consequence for which they remain accountable, as wrongdoing and defiance have consequences.

translation: Is it the judgment of ignorance that they seek? And who is better than Allah in judgment for a people who are certain?
interpretation: The verse challenges those who turn away from God’s guidance in favor of human judgments shaped by ignorance or desire. It invites people of conviction to trust that Allah’s judgment is the most just and wise.

translation: O you who believe, do not take the Jews and Christians as allies; they are allies of one another. Whoever among you takes them as allies is one of them. Surely Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: The verse warns believers against giving their ultimate loyalty and protection to powers whose allegiance conflicts with the Muslim community’s faith and security. It is not a command to mistreat Jews or Christians as individuals: the Qur’an elsewhere calls for justice and kind conduct toward those who do not fight or persecute Muslims.

translation: You see those in whose hearts is sickness hastening toward them, saying, “We fear that a turn of fortune may befall us.” But perhaps God will bring victory or a command from Him, and then they will regret what they had concealed within themselves.
interpretation: The verse portrays people whose faith is compromised by fear: anticipating a change in power, they rush to secure the support of those they regard as likely victors. Their concealed loyalties may soon be exposed when God brings victory or otherwise decides the matter, leaving them regretful for having acted out of distrust and self-interest.

translation: Those who believe will say, “Are these the ones who swore their strongest oaths by Allah that they were surely with you?” Their deeds have come to nothing, and they have become losers.
interpretation: When the truth of people’s loyalties becomes clear, the believers will wonder at those who had solemnly promised to stand with them. Their betrayal exposes the emptiness of their claims, and their deeds bring them no lasting benefit.

translation: O you who believe, whoever among you turns away from his religion, God will bring forth a people whom He loves and who love Him: humble toward the believers, steadfast before the disbelievers, striving in God’s cause and fearing no blame from anyone who blames. That is God’s favor; He grants it to whomever He wills. God is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: The verse teaches that faithfulness is not sustained by any one group’s claim to it: if people abandon their trust, God can raise others to carry it forward. The qualities named describe a community shaped by devotion to God—tender and unassuming with fellow believers, resolute in defending what is right, and not governed by fear of criticism. These qualities are themselves a favor from God, not grounds for arrogance or self-congratulation.

translation: Your only allies are Allah, His Messenger, and the believers who establish prayer and give alms while bowing.
interpretation: The verse teaches that a believer’s deepest loyalty is to Allah and His Messenger, and to the community of believers whose faith is shown through worship and generosity. Their giving even while bowing portrays charity as a sincere, integral part of their devotion.

translation: Whoever takes Allah, His Messenger, and those who believe as allies—then indeed the party of Allah will be victorious.
interpretation: True allegiance to God, His Messenger, and the faithful means standing with their guidance and values. Those who do so belong to God’s party, whose ultimate success is assured through His support, even when victory is not immediate or apparent in worldly terms.

translation: O you who believe, do not take as allies those among the People of the Book who came before you, and the disbelievers, who have made your religion a mockery and amusement. Be mindful of Allah, if you are truly believers.
interpretation: The verse calls believers to be discerning about close loyalties: faith should not be placed in the hands of those who deliberately demean it or undermine the community’s religious commitments. Its warning concerns allegiance and trust, not a license to treat others unjustly; the closing appeal makes mindfulness of God the measure of faithful conduct.

translation: When you call to prayer, they take it as a matter of mockery and amusement. That is because they are people who do not understand.
interpretation: Their ridicule reflects a failure to recognize the seriousness and spiritual purpose of worship; it reveals their own heedlessness, not any deficiency in the prayer.

translation: Say, “O People of the Scripture, do you resent us for any reason other than that we believe in Allah, in what has been sent down to us, and in what was sent down before—and because most of you are defiantly disobedient?”
interpretation: The verse challenges the People of the Scripture to recognize that the believers’ faith in Allah and in His revelations, both earlier and later, is no legitimate cause for hostility. It points instead to the disobedience of many among them as the source of their opposition.

translation: Say, “Shall I tell you of something worse in its recompense from Allah? Those whom Allah has cursed and with whom He is displeased; some of whom He made apes and swine, and who worshipped false gods. They are in a worse position and farther astray from the straight path.”
interpretation: The verse turns the mockery back on its speakers: true disgrace is not the label people use against others, but a condition brought on by defying God and straying from His guidance. Its reference to past punishments warns against such rebellion; it should not be read as a license to condemn people today with those descriptions.

translation: When they come to you, they say, “We believe,” though they entered in disbelief and departed with it. And Allah knows best what they were concealing.
interpretation: The verse exposes the gap between these people’s outward profession of faith and their inward rejection: their words do not change what they hold in their hearts, which is fully known to Allah.

translation: You see many of them hastening toward sin, transgression, and consuming what is forbidden. How evil is what they have been doing.
interpretation: The verse condemns a pattern of deliberate wrongdoing: people not only commit sin and violate others’ rights, but also pursue unlawful gain. Their haste suggests that such conduct has become habitual, and the closing judgment warns that persistent corruption is gravely blameworthy.

translation: Why do the rabbis and religious scholars not forbid them from speaking sinfully and consuming what is unlawful? How evil is what they have been doing!
interpretation: The verse condemns religious leaders who neglect their duty to speak against wrongdoing. By failing to challenge sinful speech and the taking of unlawful wealth, they allow such conduct to continue and share responsibility for its persistence.

translation: The Jews said, “God’s hand is chained.” May their own hands be chained, and may they be condemned for what they said. Rather, His two hands are outstretched; He gives as He wills. What has been sent down to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in defiance and disbelief. We have cast enmity and hatred among them until the Day of Resurrection. Whenever they kindle a fire for war, God puts it out. They strive throughout the land to spread corruption, and God does not love those who spread corruption.
interpretation: Their claim that God’s hand is chained expresses the accusation that He withholds His favor. The verse rejects that claim, affirming God’s boundless generosity and freedom to give as He wills. It also portrays how some respond to revelation with greater defiance, fostering lasting hostility and conflict; their attempts to spread corruption are ultimately checked by God, who does not approve of such wrongdoing.

translation: If the People of the Book had believed and been mindful of God, We would have blotted out their misdeeds and admitted them to Gardens of Bliss.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that sincere faith and God-consciousness open the way to divine forgiveness and lasting reward; inherited religious identity alone is not what brings these gifts.

translation: If they had upheld the Torah and the Gospel and what was sent down to them from their Lord, they would have had abundant provision from above them and beneath their feet. Among them is a community of moderation, but many of them—how evil is what they do.
interpretation: Upholding God’s guidance would bring them both spiritual well-being and plentiful provision, pictured as blessings coming from every direction. The verse also distinguishes those among them who follow a balanced course from the many whose deeds are wrong.

translation: O Messenger, convey what has been sent down to you from your Lord. If you do not, you will not have conveyed His message. Allah will protect you from the people. Indeed, Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.
interpretation: The verse commands the Messenger to deliver God’s revelation faithfully and completely, without allowing fear of people’s opposition to make him withhold any part of it. God’s promise of protection reassures him as he carries out this duty; those who reject the truth remain beyond the guidance they refuse.

translation: Say, “O People of the Scripture, you are not grounded in anything until you uphold the Torah and the Gospel and what has been sent down to you from your Lord.” What has been sent down to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in defiance and disbelief. So do not grieve over the disbelieving people.
interpretation: The verse calls the People of the Scripture to make their faith genuine by living according to the guidance God revealed, rather than merely claiming religious identity. It also consoles the Prophet: some people’s rejection of further revelation will deepen their defiance, but their response is not his burden to carry.

translation: Indeed, those who believe, the Jews, the Sabians, and the Christians—whoever believes in God and the Last Day and does righteous deeds—will have no fear, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: The verse teaches that a person’s religious label alone is not the measure of their standing before God: what matters is sincere faith in God and the Last Day, joined with righteous action. Those who meet this condition are promised security from fear and grief.

translation: We took a covenant from the Children of Israel and sent messengers to them. Whenever a messenger brought them something their desires opposed, they denied some and killed others.
interpretation: The verse portrays a recurring failure to honor their covenant: instead of accepting revelation when it challenged their desires, some rejected the messengers and others resorted to killing them.

translation: They thought no trial would befall them, so they became blind and deaf. Then Allah accepted their repentance; yet many of them again became blind and deaf. And Allah sees all that they do.
interpretation: The verse warns that feeling secure from consequences can make people ignore truth and moral guidance. Even after being given the opportunity to repent, many returned to that heedlessness—yet none of their actions are hidden from Allah.

translation: Those who say, “Allah is the Messiah, son of Mary,” have certainly disbelieved. The Messiah said, “Children of Israel, worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord.” Whoever associates anything with Allah—Allah has forbidden Paradise to them, and their refuge is the Fire. The wrongdoers will have no helpers.
interpretation: The verse presents Jesus’ own call to worship Allah as evidence that he is a servant of God, not God Himself. It warns that assigning divinity to another alongside Allah is a grave injustice with ultimate consequences, and that no one can rescue those who persist in it.

translation: Those who say, “Allah is one of three,” have certainly disbelieved. There is no deity except the One God. If they do not desist from what they say, a painful punishment will surely befall those among them who disbelieve.
interpretation: The verse affirms God’s absolute oneness and rejects attributing divinity to more than one. Its warning is directed at those who persist in that belief rather than turning away from it.

translation: Will they not turn to Allah in repentance and ask His forgiveness? Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse calls those who have gone astray to return sincerely to Allah, holding out hope that repentance and seeking forgiveness are met with His abundant mercy.

translation: The Messiah, son of Mary, was only a messenger; messengers had passed away before him. His mother was a woman of truth. They both ate food. See how We make the signs clear to them, then see how they are turned away.
interpretation: The verse honors Jesus and Mary while rejecting the claim that either is divine: Jesus was a messenger like those before him, and both he and his mother shared the ordinary human need for food. These clear signs point to their humanity, yet people turn away from their meaning.

translation: Say, “Do you worship besides Allah that which has no power to harm or benefit you, while Allah is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing?”
interpretation: The verse challenges the worship of anything powerless to affect one’s welfare, and directs worship toward Allah alone, who hears every plea and knows all things.

translation: Say, “O People of the Book, do not go to excess in your religion beyond the truth, and do not follow the desires of a people who went astray before, led many others astray, and strayed from the right path.”
interpretation: The verse warns that sincere faith must remain within the bounds of truth: exaggeration in religion and uncritical pursuit of misguided desires can distort belief and lead both oneself and others away from the straight path.

translation: Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed through David and Jesus, son of Mary. That was because they disobeyed and persistently transgressed.
interpretation: The verse presents the condemnation voiced by David and Jesus as a consequence of persistent defiance: their rejection of God’s commands and repeated crossing of moral bounds brought them under divine rejection, rather than it being an arbitrary punishment.

translation: They would not forbid one another from the evil they committed. How vile was what they used to do!
interpretation: The verse condemns a community in which people tolerate one another’s wrongdoing instead of trying to restrain it. Their failure to speak against evil makes them collectively blameworthy.

translation: You see many of them taking those who disbelieve as allies. How evil is what they have sent ahead for themselves: that Allah’s wrath is upon them, and they will remain in the punishment forever.
interpretation: The verse warns that choosing allegiance in opposition to faith has grave spiritual consequences: such choices earn God’s displeasure and, if persisted in, lasting punishment.

translation: Had they believed in God, the Prophet, and what was revealed to him, they would not have taken them as allies; but many of them are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: The verse presents a contradiction between professed faith and allegiance: genuine belief should guide whom people trust and support. Their choice of allies is portrayed as evidence that many have departed from obedience to God.

translation: You will surely find the strongest in hostility toward the believers to be the Jews and those who associate others with God; and you will surely find the nearest of them in affection toward the believers to be those who say, “We are Christians.” That is because among them are priests and monks, and because they are not arrogant.
interpretation: The verse presents humility and sincere religious devotion as qualities that can bring people closer to recognizing and responding kindly to faith. Its explanation points to these qualities among the Christians it describes, rather than treating religious identity alone as the measure of a person’s character.

translation: When they hear what has been sent down to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because they recognize the truth. They say, “Our Lord, we believe, so record us among the witnesses.”
interpretation: Their tears express a heart moved by truth once it is recognized: sincere faith is not merely acknowledgment, but a humble response that turns recognition into belief and a willingness to stand witness to it.

translation: Why should we not believe in Allah and in the truth that has come to us, while hoping that our Lord will admit us among the righteous people?
interpretation: The words express a conscience awakened by the truth: once it is recognized, turning away from faith has no reasonable justification. The speaker joins belief with humble hope, trusting that Allah will gather those who sincerely seek Him among the righteous.

translation: So Allah rewarded them, for what they said, with gardens beneath which rivers flow, where they will remain forever. That is the reward of those who do good.
interpretation: Their sincere acknowledgment of the truth, joined with righteous conduct, is presented as deserving lasting reward from Allah; the verse assures that goodness is not lost, but is met with enduring blessing.

translation: And those who disbelieve and deny Our signs—they are the companions of the Fire.
interpretation: The verse warns that knowingly rejecting God’s guidance has lasting consequences: a person’s response to divine signs is not merely an intellectual position but a moral choice with spiritual accountability.

translation: O you who believe, do not forbid yourselves the good things Allah has made lawful for you, and do not transgress. Indeed, Allah does not love those who transgress.
interpretation: The verse teaches that devotion does not mean rejecting lawful blessings or inventing prohibitions for oneself. Believers should practice faith within the limits Allah has set, without excess or disregard for those limits.

translation: Eat from what Allah has provided for you, lawful and wholesome, and be mindful of Allah, in whom you believe.
interpretation: Faith calls for receiving God’s provision with gratitude and choosing what is lawful and wholesome; mindfulness of Allah should guide those choices in everyday life.

translation: God does not hold you accountable for thoughtless oaths, but He does hold you accountable for oaths you have deliberately bound yourselves by. Their expiation is to feed ten needy people with the average of what you feed your families, or to clothe them, or to free a slave. Whoever cannot afford this must fast for three days. That is the expiation for your oaths when you have sworn them. Guard your oaths. Thus God makes His signs clear to you, so that you may be grateful.
interpretation: The verse distinguishes careless words from a considered oath, making clear that deliberate commitments carry moral responsibility. When such an oath is breached, its expiation both makes amends and serves those in need; fasting is prescribed for someone unable to provide the other forms of expiation. The command to guard oaths calls for restraint in swearing and faithfulness to one’s commitments.

translation: O you who believe, intoxicants, gambling, idolatrous altars, and divining arrows are an abomination from Satan’s handiwork; so avoid them, that you may prosper.
interpretation: The verse calls believers to distance themselves completely from practices that corrupt sound judgment and devotion to God, presenting their avoidance as a path to well-being and success.

translation: Satan only seeks to sow enmity and hatred among you through intoxicants and gambling, and to turn you away from remembering God and from prayer. Will you then desist?
interpretation: The verse presents these practices as more than private indulgences: they can damage relationships and draw people away from spiritual awareness and worship. Its closing question is a forceful appeal to recognize that harm and give them up.

translation: Obey Allah and obey the Messenger, and beware. If you turn away, then know that Our Messenger’s only duty is clear conveyance.
interpretation: The verse makes clear that the Messenger has conveyed the guidance plainly; turning away does not diminish that duty, but leaves each person accountable for whether they obey.

translation: There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they consumed, so long as they are mindful of God, believe, and do righteous deeds; then remain mindful and believe; then remain mindful and excel in goodness. And God loves those who excel in goodness.
interpretation: The verse reassures believers that they are not held accountable for what they consumed before its prohibition, while making clear that this is no license to disregard God’s commands: their path is sustained mindfulness, faith, righteous action, and excellence in doing good.

translation: O you who believe, Allah will surely test you with some game within reach of your hands and spears, so that He may make evident who fears Him unseen. Whoever transgresses after that will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: In the context of the restrictions on hunting while in a state of consecration, the ease of catching nearby game makes obedience a real test: true reverence for God is shown by restraining oneself even when able to take what is forbidden and no one else may see.

translation: O you who believe, do not kill game while you are in a state of consecration. Whoever among you kills it deliberately must make amends with an equivalent from livestock, as judged by two just men among you, to be offered at the Kaaba; or expiate by feeding needy people; or by fasting an equivalent amount, so that he may taste the consequence of his deed. Allah has pardoned what happened in the past. But whoever does it again, Allah will take retribution from him; and Allah is Mighty, Lord of retribution.
interpretation: The verse teaches that entering the sacred state of consecration entails restraint even from harming game, and that deliberate violation carries a real moral cost. Its prescribed forms of amends connect accountability with restoring what was harmed and caring for those in need, while the warning about repetition underscores that forgiveness of past conduct is not permission to persist in wrongdoing.

translation: Lawful to you is the game of the sea and its food, as provision for you and for travelers. But the game of the land is forbidden to you while you are in a state of consecration. Be mindful of Allah, to whom you will be gathered.
interpretation: The verse reflects the balance of sacred discipline and divine ease: consecration calls for restraint within its appointed limits, not needless hardship. Remembering the final return to Allah gives that obedience its deeper seriousness.

translation: Allah has made the Ka‘bah, the Sacred House, a means of support for people, and likewise the sacred month, the sacrificial offerings, and the garlanded offerings. This is so that you may know that Allah knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and that Allah has knowledge of all things.
interpretation: By setting apart the Ka‘bah, sacred times, and offerings, Allah established signs and practices that uphold people’s religious and communal life. Their order and purpose point to His complete knowledge of creation and of what is best for it.

translation: Know that Allah is severe in punishment, and that Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: This teaches that a believer should neither feel secure enough to persist in wrongdoing nor despair of returning to God: awareness of His justice restrains, while trust in His forgiveness and mercy gives hope to those who repent.

translation: The Messenger is only responsible for conveying the message, and Allah knows what you make known and what you conceal.
interpretation: The verse clarifies that the Messenger’s duty is to deliver God’s message, not to compel people to accept it. Each person remains accountable for their response, since nothing they openly express or keep hidden is unknown to Allah.

translation: Say, “The impure and the pure are not equal, even if the abundance of the impure impresses you. So be mindful of God, O people of understanding, that you may succeed.”
interpretation: What is plentiful or impressive is not necessarily good; true worth lies in purity and righteousness. People of understanding should therefore judge by God’s guidance rather than by numbers or appearances, and choose what is right even when it is less common.

translation: O you who believe, do not ask about things which, if made clear to you, would distress you. But if you ask about them while the Qur’an is being revealed, they will be made clear to you. Allah has pardoned you; Allah is Forgiving, Forbearing.
interpretation: The verse teaches believers not to pursue needless questions that may bring hardship or expose matters best left unexamined. They should trust Allah’s guidance, accept what He has made clear, and remember His forgiveness and forbearance.

translation: A people before you asked about such things, then came to disbelieve on account of them.
interpretation: The verse warns against pursuing needless questions about matters whose answers may bring difficulty or expose one to a test of faith; earlier people let such questions lead them to reject what became clear to them.

translation: Allah has not ordained any bahīrah, sā’ibah, waṣīlah, or ḥām; rather, those who disbelieve invent lies about Allah, and most of them do not reason.
interpretation: The verse rejects the claim that inherited customs concerning these animals were divinely prescribed. It warns against turning human inventions into God’s law and blindly attributing them to Him.

translation: When it is said to them, “Come to what Allah has revealed and to the Messenger,” they say, “What we found our fathers following is enough for us.” Even if their fathers knew nothing and were not guided?
interpretation: The verse warns against treating inherited custom as proof of truth. Loyalty to one’s forebears cannot replace sound knowledge and guidance from Allah; a belief must be judged by its truth, not merely by how long it has been followed.

translation: O you who believe, take care of yourselves. Those who have gone astray will not harm you when you are rightly guided. To Allah is the return of you all, and He will inform you of what you used to do.
interpretation: The verse teaches that believers are accountable for their own faith and conduct, not for whether others accept guidance. Being rightly guided includes carrying out one’s duties toward others, such as advising them to do what is right when appropriate; after doing so, one should not let their refusal or wrongdoing undermine one’s own commitment. Ultimately, God alone will judge everyone’s deeds.

translation: O you who believe, when death approaches one of you at the time of making a bequest, let two just men from among you bear witness—or two others from outside your community, if you are traveling through the land and the calamity of death befalls you. Detain them after the prayer; then, if you have doubts, let them swear by Allah: ‘We will not exchange this testimony for any price, even for the sake of a close relative, nor conceal Allah’s testimony. Indeed, if we did so, we would be among the sinners.’
interpretation: The verse establishes safeguards for testimony concerning a person’s bequest when death may prevent them from confirming it later. In particular, it addresses the vulnerability of travelers by allowing witnesses from outside their community and requiring a solemn oath if their truthfulness is doubted. The oath rejects both personal gain and favoritism toward relatives, presenting honest testimony as a moral duty before God.

translation: Then, if it is discovered that the two have incurred sin, two others shall take their place from among those whose rights were wronged—the two most entitled. They shall swear by Allah: “Our testimony is truer than their testimony, and we have not transgressed; for then we would indeed be among the wrongdoers.”
interpretation: The verse provides a remedy when the original witnesses are found to have testified dishonestly: those with the strongest rightful claim may replace them and affirm their account under oath. Their oath also restrains them from exaggerating or taking more than is due, making accountability and fairness central to resolving the dispute.

translation: That is more likely to make them give testimony in its proper form, or fear that other oaths will be taken after their oaths. Be mindful of God and listen; God does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.
interpretation: The prescribed process is meant to protect the truth: witnesses should testify faithfully, knowing that their claims may be challenged by further oaths. The closing command calls people to heed God’s guidance, since deliberate disobedience turns them away from it.

translation: On the Day Allah gathers the messengers and asks, “What response were you given?” they will say, “We have no knowledge. You alone are the Knower of all unseen things.”
interpretation: The messengers’ answer expresses their utter humility before Allah and acknowledges that complete knowledge of how people responded belongs to Him alone. It does not mean they were unaware of their mission or its events, but that before Allah’s all-encompassing knowledge, they defer the final accounting of people’s responses to Him.

translation: When Allah said, “O Jesus, son of Mary, remember My favor upon you and upon your mother: how I strengthened you with the Holy Spirit, so that you spoke to people in the cradle and in maturity; how I taught you the Book, wisdom, the Torah, and the Gospel; how, by My permission, you fashioned from clay something in the form of a bird, then breathed into it and it became a bird, by My permission; how you healed the one blind from birth and the leper, by My permission; and how you brought the dead forth, by My permission; and how I restrained the Children of Israel from you when you came to them with clear proofs, and those among them who disbelieved said, ‘This is nothing but obvious magic.’”
interpretation: The verse presents Jesus’ extraordinary signs as favors granted by Allah and repeatedly stresses that they occurred by His permission. Its meaning is that Jesus’ miracles affirmed his prophetic mission, not independent power or divinity; and when clear signs did not persuade some of his people, Allah protected him from their hostility.

translation: And [remember] when I inspired the disciples: “Believe in Me and in My messenger.” They said, “We believe; bear witness that we are Muslims.”
interpretation: The verse presents the disciples’ faith as a response to God’s guidance: they affirm belief in God and in Jesus as His messenger, and declare their willing submission to God. Their request for God to bear witness emphasizes the sincerity and public commitment of that submission.

translation: When the disciples said, “Jesus, son of Mary, can your Lord send down to us a table spread with food from heaven?” He said, “Be mindful of Allah, if you are truly believers.”
interpretation: The disciples’ request tests the boundary between seeking reassurance and relying on faith. Jesus first calls them to reverence for God, reminding them that genuine belief should be accompanied by trust rather than making a sign the condition of their faith.

translation: They said, “We wish to eat from it, so that our hearts may be reassured, and that we may know you have spoken truthfully to us, and be among those who bear witness to it.”
interpretation: Their request expresses a desire for reassurance through direct experience: witnessing the sign would deepen their certainty and enable them to testify to what they had seen.

translation: Jesus, son of Mary, said, “O Allah, our Lord, send down to us a table spread from heaven, to be a festival for us, for the first and the last of us, and a sign from You. Provide for us; You are the best of providers.”
interpretation: Jesus asks God for a tangible blessing that would strengthen his people’s faith: a sign from heaven and a shared occasion of gratitude for generations to come. His prayer also expresses reliance on God as the ultimate source of provision.

translation: Allah said, “Indeed, I am sending it down to you. Then whoever among you disbelieves after that, I will punish him with a punishment with which I have punished no one among all peoples.”
interpretation: The promised table would be a manifest sign and a special favor; receiving such clear evidence would also bring a grave responsibility. The warning underscores that knowingly rejecting the truth after witnessing such a sign would merit an especially severe punishment.

translation: And [remember] when Allah will say, “O Jesus, son of Mary, did you tell the people, ‘Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah’?” He will say, “Glory be to You! It was not for me to say what I had no right to say. Had I said it, You would surely have known it. You know what is within me, while I do not know what is within You. Indeed, You alone are the Knower of all unseen things.”
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that worship belongs to Allah alone and that even Jesus, honored as a prophet, rejects any claim to divinity or authority to direct people to worship him or Mary. His reply also affirms the complete knowledge of Allah, in contrast with the limited knowledge of human beings.

translation: I said to them nothing except what You commanded me: “Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord.” I was a witness over them as long as I remained among them; but when You took me, You were the Watcher over them. And You are witness over all things.
interpretation: Jesus disavows having taught anything beyond worship of Allah, affirming that his knowledge of his people was limited to the time he was among them. After that, their actions were under Allah’s watch, whose knowledge and witness encompass everything.

translation: If You punish them, they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, You are indeed the Almighty, the Wise.
interpretation: The verse entrusts the matter entirely to God: His servants remain under His authority whether He punishes or forgives them. His forgiveness is no limitation on His power, and His judgment—whatever it is—proceeds from perfect wisdom.

translation: Allah will say, “This is the Day when the truthful will benefit from their truthfulness. They will have gardens beneath which rivers flow, remaining there forever. Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. That is the supreme triumph.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that sincerity and faithfulness have their fullest consequence in the Hereafter: those who were truthful in their belief and conduct receive everlasting joy, and their ultimate reward is the mutual pleasure of Allah and His servants.

translation: To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them, and He is capable of all things.
interpretation: Nothing exists beyond God’s authority or ability; this calls the believer to rely on Him and to recognize that every source of power is dependent upon Him.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Praise belongs to Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light; yet those who disbelieve set up equals to their Lord.
interpretation: The creation of the heavens and earth, and the bringing forth of darkness and light, point to Allah’s sole power and lordship. The verse therefore portrays associating partners with Him as a profound contradiction: those who witness His signs still treat others as equal to the One who created them.

translation: He is the One who created you from clay, then decreed a term; and a term fixed with Him. Yet you still doubt.
interpretation: Humanity’s creation from humble clay and its life governed by divinely appointed limits point to God’s power and authority. The term known and fixed with Him includes the final appointed time beyond this life, so doubting resurrection is unwarranted.

translation: And He is Allah in the heavens and on the earth. He knows what you conceal and what you reveal, and He knows what you earn.
interpretation: Allah alone is the true God of all creation, and nothing about human beings is hidden from Him—not their private thoughts, their public words, or the deeds they acquire. This knowledge calls people to sincerity and responsibility before Him.

translation: Whenever a sign from their Lord comes to them, they turn away from it.
interpretation: Their repeated turning away suggests that the obstacle is not a lack of signs, but a refusal to reflect on them and respond to their guidance.

translation: They denied the truth when it came to them, so soon the news of what they used to mock will come to them.
interpretation: Their mockery cannot make the truth or its warnings disappear; in time, they will face the reality and consequences of what they dismissed.

translation: Have they not seen how many generations before them We destroyed? We had established them in the land more firmly than We have established you, sent abundant rain upon them, and made rivers flow beneath them. Yet We destroyed them for their sins and brought forth other generations after them.
interpretation: The verse warns that material power, fertile land, and abundance are not guarantees of divine approval or lasting security. Earlier peoples possessed great advantages, but wrongdoing brought their downfall; those who hear this warning should therefore not be deceived by prosperity, but turn away from sin.

translation: Even if We had sent down to you a book written on parchment, and they touched it with their own hands, those who disbelieve would still say, “This is nothing but obvious magic.”
interpretation: The verse points to the way entrenched denial can resist even direct, tangible evidence: the obstacle is not a lack of signs, but a refusal to accept them, recasting revelation as magic instead.

translation: They say, “Why has an angel not been sent down to him?” Had We sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided, and they would not have been given any further respite.
interpretation: Their demand for an angel overlooks that such a decisive manifestation would end the period of testing and reprieve: once the truth was made unmistakable, judgment would follow without delay.

translation: Had We made him an angel, We would have made him appear as a man, and We would have made unclear to them what they themselves make unclear.
interpretation: The verse answers those who demanded an angel as a messenger: people could only receive an angel in a human appearance, which would leave them with the same doubts and objections. It points to the wisdom of sending a human messenger, whose nature and guidance people can directly understand.

translation: Messengers before you were mocked, but those who ridiculed them were overtaken by what they used to mock.
interpretation: The verse reassures the Prophet that ridicule does not discredit the truth of his message. It warns that those who mock God’s warnings may ultimately face the very consequence they dismiss.

translation: Say, “Travel through the land, then see what was the end of those who denied the truth.”
interpretation: The verse calls people to learn from the fate of earlier communities: reflecting on their remains should awaken humility and caution, and show that persistent denial carries consequences.

translation: Say, “To whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth?” Say, “To Allah.” He has prescribed mercy for Himself. He will surely gather you all on the Day of Resurrection—there is no doubt about it. Those who have lost their own souls do not believe.
interpretation: The verse presents Allah’s ownership of all creation as the basis for His authority to resurrect and judge it. His gathering of everyone is certain, and His mercy is assured; yet those who refuse to believe lose themselves by denying the reality for which they were created and toward which they will be brought.

translation: To Him belongs whatever dwells in the night and the day, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: Everything that exists, whether hidden in the night or apparent in the day, remains wholly under God’s ownership and care; nothing is beyond His hearing or knowledge.

translation: Say, “Shall I take as a protector anyone other than Allah, the Originator of the heavens and the earth, who provides food and is not provided for?” Say, “I have been commanded to be the first of those who submit to Allah, and not to be among the polytheists.”
interpretation: Because Allah alone brought all things into existence and is wholly self-sufficient, while every creature depends on Him, ultimate devotion and reliance belong to Him alone. The command to submit rejects giving any share of worship or divine authority to another.

translation: Say, “Indeed, I fear that if I disobey my Lord, I will face the punishment of a tremendous Day.”
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that no one is exempt from accountability before God: even the Messenger speaks with humility and fear of disobedience, urging people to take divine judgment seriously.

translation: Whoever is spared from it that Day has indeed been shown mercy by Him; that is the clear triumph.
interpretation: Being spared the punishment of that Day is not something a person can claim as a right; it is a manifestation of God’s mercy. The verse therefore presents true success as deliverance by that mercy.

translation: If Allah afflicts you with harm, none can remove it except Him; and if He grants you good, He has power over all things.
interpretation: The verse teaches that ultimate reliance belongs to Allah alone: no hardship or blessing lies beyond His authority, so a believer should turn to Him in distress and receive His gifts with trust and gratitude.

translation: And He is the Supreme Overpowering over His servants, and He is the All-Wise, the All-Aware.
interpretation: God’s authority over all creation is absolute, yet His power is exercised with perfect wisdom and complete knowledge of every matter.

translation: Say, “What is greatest in testimony?” Say, “Allah is witness between me and you. This Qur’an has been revealed to me so that I may warn you by it and all whom it reaches. Do you truly testify that there are other gods alongside Allah?” Say, “I do not testify.” Say, “He is only One God, and I am free of what you associate with Him.”
interpretation: The verse presents Allah’s testimony as decisive over every human claim and the Qur’an as a warning entrusted to the Prophet for all whom its message reaches. The Prophet is commanded to reject any testimony that grants divinity to others beside Allah, affirming that worship belongs to the One God alone and disavowing every form of association with Him.

translation: Those to whom We gave the Scripture recognize him as they recognize their own sons. Those who have brought loss upon themselves do not believe.
interpretation: The verse refers to people given earlier Scriptures who recognize the Prophet’s identity from what they have been taught, as plainly as they recognize their own children. Yet those who reject this recognition harm themselves by refusing to believe.

translation: Who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie about God or denies His signs? Surely, the wrongdoers will not prosper.
interpretation: The verse presents deliberate falsehood about God and rejection of His signs as the height of injustice: both distort the truth and turn people away from guidance. Such wrongdoing may seem to bring advantage for a time, but it cannot lead to true or lasting success.

translation: And [remember] the Day We will gather them all together, then say to those who associated others with God, “Where are your partners whom you used to claim?”
interpretation: The question is a rebuke, not a request for information: on the Day of Judgment, those who claimed that others shared in God’s divinity will be confronted with the failure of those supposed partners to help or answer for them.

translation: Then their only reply was to say, “By Allah, our Lord, we were not idolaters.”
