interpretation: When confronted with the truth, they will resort to denying their association of partners with God, even swearing by Him; their denial will not conceal what they had done.

translation: See how they have lied against themselves, and how what they used to fabricate has deserted them.
interpretation: Their denial cannot protect them: when the truth is exposed, the falsehoods they relied on offer no help, leaving them to face the consequences of their own self-deception.

translation: Among them are those who listen to you, but We have placed coverings over their hearts so that they do not understand it, and deafness in their ears. Even if they see every sign, they will not believe in it. When they come to you to argue, those who disbelieve say, “This is nothing but tales of the ancients.”
interpretation: The verse portrays people who hear the Prophet’s message yet refuse to receive it with open hearts. Their persistent rejection leaves them unable to recognize the truth even when signs are clear, so they dismiss the revelation as old tales and argue against it.

translation: They forbid others from it and keep away from it. They destroy none but themselves, though they do not realize it.
interpretation: The verse warns that those who try to prevent others from accepting the truth while turning away from it themselves ultimately harm only their own souls, even if they fail to recognize the consequence.

translation: If only you could see when they are made to stand before the Fire, they will say, “If only we could be sent back, we would not deny the signs of our Lord, and we would be among the believers.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the regret that comes when the truth can no longer be denied, warning that faith should be embraced sincerely before its consequences are witnessed firsthand.

translation: Rather, what they used to conceal before has become clear to them. And if they were returned, they would surely go back to what they had been forbidden; indeed, they are liars.
interpretation: Their plea to be sent back and live righteously is not sincere: even after the truth has been exposed to them, they would return to their former wrongdoing.

translation: And they say, “There is nothing but our life in this world, and we will not be raised again.”
interpretation: Their denial reflects a view that treats what can be seen and experienced in this life as the whole of reality, leaving no place for resurrection or accountability beyond it.

translation: If only you could see when they are made to stand before their Lord. He will say, “Is this not the truth?” They will say, “Yes indeed, by our Lord!” He will say, “Then taste the punishment for your disbelief.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the moment when denial can no longer conceal the truth: faced with their Lord, those who rejected it will acknowledge its certainty, but that acknowledgment will come too late to spare them the consequence of their disbelief.

translation: Those who deny the meeting with Allah have truly lost. When the Hour comes upon them suddenly, they will say, “Alas for us, for what we neglected concerning it!” They will carry their burdens on their backs. Surely, evil is the burden they carry.
interpretation: The verse warns that denying accountability can make a person treat life’s responsibilities as though they have no ultimate consequence. When the truth becomes undeniable, regret cannot undo what was neglected, and the “burdens” evoke the weight of one’s own deeds and choices.

translation: The life of this world is nothing but play and amusement, while the Home of the Hereafter is better for those who are mindful of God. Will you not then understand?
interpretation: The verse calls people to look beyond temporary pleasures and distractions, recognizing that lasting good belongs to the Hereafter. Those mindful of God live with this greater reality in view, and the closing question urges people to reflect and choose accordingly.

translation: We know that what they say grieves you. It is not you they call a liar; rather, the wrongdoers reject the signs of God.
interpretation: The verse consoles the Prophet by distinguishing rejection of his message from a judgment on his honesty: the deniers’ refusal stems from their injustice in rejecting God’s signs, not from any lack of truthfulness in the messenger.

translation: Messengers before you were indeed denied, but they patiently endured the denial and the harm they suffered until Our help came to them. No one can alter the words of God, and accounts of the messengers have surely come to you.
interpretation: The verse reassures the Prophet that rejection and persecution do not mean God has abandoned His messengers: they endure with patience until His promised support arrives. The unalterable words of God affirm the certainty of His promise, while the stories of earlier messengers offer strength to remain steadfast.

translation: If their turning away is hard for you to bear, then, if you can, seek a passage into the earth or a ladder into heaven and bring them a sign. Had God willed, He would have gathered them all upon guidance. So do not be among the ignorant.
interpretation: The verse consoles the Prophet ﷺ in the face of persistent rejection: no extraordinary sign can force faith upon those who turn away, for guidance is not produced by signs alone. He is urged not to let grief over their refusal obscure the wisdom of God’s will or lead him to despair.

translation: Only those who listen truly respond. As for the dead, Allah will raise them, and then to Him they will be returned.
interpretation: The verse distinguishes those whose hearts are receptive to the truth from those who remain spiritually unresponsive, while reminding that even the dead will be raised by Allah and brought back to Him for judgment.

translation: They say, “Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord?” Say, “Allah is surely able to send down a sign, but most of them do not know.”
interpretation: Their demand does not reflect any lack of power on God’s part; rather, they fail to understand that signs are sent according to His wisdom, not merely to satisfy demands.

translation: There is no creature on earth, nor any bird flying with its wings, except that they are communities like you. We have omitted nothing from the Book. Then they will be gathered to their Lord.
interpretation: The verse teaches that living creatures are not without order or purpose: they form communities within God’s encompassing knowledge and care. Their gathering to their Lord affirms that His reckoning extends beyond humanity, inviting people to humility and awareness of their responsibility before Him.

translation: Those who deny Our signs are deaf and mute, lost in darkness. Whomever Allah wills, He leaves to stray; and whomever He wills, He places on a straight path.
interpretation: The verse portrays denial as a condition that shuts a person off from recognizing and responding to truth: the darkness is spiritual confusion, and the imagery of deafness and muteness describes an inability or unwillingness to receive guidance. It also affirms that ultimate guidance belongs to Allah, who knows whom to guide onto the straight path.

translation: Say, “Have you considered: if Allah’s punishment were to come upon you, or the Hour were to come upon you, would you call upon anyone other than Allah, if you are truthful?”
interpretation: The verse challenges those who worship other deities to consider a moment of ultimate danger: when Allah’s punishment arrives or the Resurrection begins, they will turn to Allah alone, revealing that the beings they claim can help them have no power to save them.

translation: Rather, it is Him you call upon; He removes the affliction for which you call upon Him, if He wills, and you forget those you associate with Him.
interpretation: In moments of distress, people turn to God alone, recognizing that only He can remove their hardship. Their reliance on other objects of worship falls away, revealing that ultimate power and deliverance belong to Him.

translation: Indeed, We sent messengers to nations before you, then afflicted them with hardship and adversity, so that they might humble themselves.
interpretation: The trials were meant to awaken those communities from heedlessness and turn them toward God in humility and supplication; hardship can serve as a call to return to Him.

translation: Why, then, when Our punishment came upon them, did they not humble themselves? Instead, their hearts hardened, and Satan made pleasing to them what they used to do.
interpretation: The verse points to a spiritual danger: hardship does not necessarily lead people to repentance. When the heart becomes hardened, wrongdoing can seem acceptable, and a person may resist the very humility that could turn them back to God.

translation: When they forgot what they had been reminded of, We opened to them the gates of every good thing, until, as they rejoiced in what they had been given, We seized them suddenly; and then they were utterly despairing.
interpretation: The abundance they received was not proof of divine approval. It became a test that deepened their heedlessness, until punishment came without warning and left them without hope.

translation: So the last remnant of the people who did wrong was cut off. And praise belongs to Allah, Lord of all worlds.
interpretation: The verse presents the end of persistent wrongdoing as an act of divine justice, while directing praise to Allah, whose judgment is ultimately just and whose mercy brings relief to those who remain faithful.

translation: Say, “Have you considered: if Allah were to take away your hearing and your sight, and seal your hearts, what god besides Allah could restore them to you?” See how We present the signs in different ways, yet they turn away.
interpretation: The verse confronts people with their complete dependence on Allah: the faculties through which they perceive and understand are gifts no other power can take away or restore. The varied signs are meant to awaken reflection, but those who turn away choose to resist what should lead them to recognize their dependence on Him.

translation: Say, “Consider: if God’s punishment comes upon you suddenly or openly, will anyone be destroyed except the wrongdoing people?”
interpretation: The verse confronts those who dismiss the warning: however unexpectedly or plainly divine punishment arrives, its ultimate ruin falls upon those who persist in wrongdoing and reject the truth.

translation: We send the messengers only as bearers of good news and as warners. So whoever believes and sets things right will have no fear, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: The verse teaches that the messengers convey God’s guidance and its promise and warning; people are accountable for how they respond. Those who embrace faith and let it shape their conduct with righteousness may trust in God’s assurance of safety from fear and grief.

translation: As for those who deny Our signs, punishment will befall them because of their persistent defiance.
interpretation: The verse warns that rejecting God’s signs is not merely an intellectual disagreement: when it is joined with ongoing disobedience, it brings accountability and punishment.

translation: Say, “I do not claim to possess Allah’s treasures, nor do I know the unseen, nor do I claim to be an angel. I follow only what is revealed to me.” Say, “Are the blind and the seeing equal? Will you not reflect?”
interpretation: The verse teaches that a messenger’s authority comes from faithfully conveying revelation, not from possessing divine powers or independent knowledge of the unseen. It also calls people to recognize the difference between spiritual blindness and insight: those who reflect should not treat guidance and heedlessness as though they were the same.

translation: Warn by it those who fear that they will be gathered before their Lord: they will have no protector or intercessor besides Him, so that they may become mindful of God.
interpretation: The verse presents awareness of standing before God as a reason to heed revelation: no one can independently shield or intercede for a person apart from Him, and this awareness may lead them to live with greater reverence and care.

translation: Do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His pleasure. You are not accountable for them in any way, nor are they accountable for you in any way; if you drive them away, you will be among the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse teaches that a person’s worth before God is not determined by wealth or social standing. Those who sincerely worship Him must not be excluded to satisfy the preferences of the powerful; each person is answerable for their own deeds.

translation: Thus We tested some of them by means of others, so they would say, “Are these the ones Allah has favored among us?” Is Allah not best aware of those who are grateful?
interpretation: Differences in worldly status can test people: those who judge others as unworthy may reveal their own arrogance, while Allah alone knows who is truly grateful and deserving of His favor.

translation: When those who believe in Our signs come to you, say, “Peace be upon you. Your Lord has prescribed mercy for Himself: whoever among you does wrong in ignorance, then repents afterward and makes amends—indeed, He is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.”
interpretation: The verse teaches the Prophet to welcome believers with peace and reassurance, and to remind them that God’s mercy is open to those who turn back after wrongdoing. Repentance is shown through making amends, not merely expressing regret, and the closing names assure the repentant of God’s forgiveness and mercy.

translation: And thus We make the signs clear, so that the way of the evildoers may become evident.
interpretation: By clarifying His signs, God makes the path of those who reject or oppose the truth recognizable, enabling people to distinguish it from the path of guidance and avoid following it.

translation: Say, “I have been forbidden to worship those you call upon besides Allah.” Say, “I will not follow your desires; for then I would have gone astray and would not be among the guided.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that worship must be directed to Allah alone, not shaped by people’s wishes or inherited practices. The Prophet’s refusal shows that true guidance comes from obedience to Allah, while yielding to desires in matters of faith leads away from it.

translation: Say, “I am indeed upon clear proof from my Lord, though you have rejected it. What you are urging to come quickly is not in my power. Judgment belongs only to Allah. He sets forth the truth, and He is the best of judges.”
interpretation: The Prophet is commanded to affirm that his message rests on clear evidence from God, regardless of his opponents’ rejection. He cannot bring about the punishment they demand; its timing and all judgment belong to God, who makes the truth clear and judges with perfect authority.

translation: Say, “If I had what you are urging to come quickly, the matter between me and you would already have been settled. And Allah knows best who the wrongdoers are.”
interpretation: The Prophet is told to make clear that he does not control the punishment his opponents demand; its timing and judgment belong to Allah, whose perfect knowledge of the wrongdoers governs when and how they are held to account.

translation: With Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them except Him. He knows what is on land and in the sea. No leaf falls without His knowing it, nor is there a grain in the darknesses of the earth, nor anything fresh or dry, but it is recorded in a clear Book.
interpretation: The verse teaches that God’s knowledge is complete and independent: what is hidden from creation is never hidden from Him, and even the smallest, most obscure event lies within His awareness and decree. This invites trust that nothing in one’s life is overlooked, while also reminding people that their actions are known and answerable before Him.

translation: He is the One who takes you in sleep by night and knows what you do by day. Then He raises you during it, so that a decreed term may be completed. Then to Him is your return, and He will inform you of what you used to do.
interpretation: The verse presents sleep and waking as signs of God’s power: He holds people’s souls at night and restores them by day, while fully knowing their deeds. This daily renewal points to the final return to Him, when every person will be made aware of their actions.

translation: He is the One who holds absolute power over His servants, and He appoints guardians over you. Then, when death comes to one of you, Our messengers take his soul, and they do not fail in their duty.
interpretation: The verse teaches that no one lies beyond God’s authority: human life is watched over by His appointed angels, and its end is carried out precisely as He wills.

translation: Then they are returned to Allah, their true Master. Surely judgment belongs to Him alone, and He is the swiftest of reckoners.
interpretation: All authority and ultimate judgment belong to Allah, so no one can escape being answerable to Him; His reckoning is complete and requires no delay.

translation: Say, “Who rescues you from the darknesses of the land and the sea, when you call upon Him humbly and privately: ‘If He saves us from this, we will surely be among the grateful’?”
interpretation: The verse draws attention to how hardship strips away people’s false sense of self-sufficiency: when danger overwhelms them, they turn sincerely to God, recognizing that their security ultimately depends on Him. It also challenges them to let the gratitude they pledge in crisis shape their lives beyond it.

translation: Say, “Allah saves you from it and from every distress; yet afterward you associate others with Him.”
interpretation: The verse censures the contradiction of turning to Allah alone in moments of danger, then forgetting His favor and directing worship to others once relief comes. It calls for gratitude and steadfast devotion, not worship that depends on hardship.

translation: Say, “He is able to send upon you a punishment from above you or from beneath your feet, or to divide you into factions and make some of you taste the violence of others.” See how We explain the signs in different ways, so that they may understand.
interpretation: The verse presents both external calamity and conflict among people as possible forms of divine punishment, urging people to heed the signs and seek understanding before discord and harm take hold.

translation: Your people have denied it, though it is the truth. Say, “I am not your guardian over you.”
interpretation: Their rejection does not diminish the truth of the message. The Prophet is to convey it, not compel people to accept it or take responsibility for their choices.

translation: For every piece of news there is an appointed time, and you will come to know.
interpretation: Every promised event has a time set for it to become clear. Those who doubt or deny the warning will eventually see its truth when that time arrives.

translation: When you see those who engage in mockery or false argument about Our verses, turn away from them until they speak of something else. And if Satan should make you forget, then, once you remember, do not remain seated with the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: The verse teaches that faithfulness sometimes requires quietly withdrawing from a setting where God’s signs are being treated with contempt. Remaining there can suggest acceptance of that conduct; once the conversation changes, one may return, while remembering to leave if one had forgotten.

translation: Those who are mindful of God bear no responsibility for their account in the least; they are only to remind them, so that they may become mindful.
interpretation: Believers are not answerable for the wrongdoing of others, but they should offer sincere reminders that may lead them to become mindful of God.

translation: Leave those who have made their religion a plaything and amusement, and whom the life of this world has deluded. Remind them by it, lest a soul be given over to ruin for what it has earned. It will have no protector or intercessor besides Allah; and even if it offered every possible ransom, none would be accepted from it. Those are the ones given over to ruin for what they have earned. They will have a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment for their disbelief.
interpretation: The verse warns against treating faith as a source of mockery or passing amusement while being deceived by worldly life. The reminder is meant to awaken people before their choices leave them answerable for what they have done: on that Day, neither a protector nor an intercessor nor any ransom can avert the consequence of rejecting the truth.

translation: Say, “Shall we call upon, besides Allah, that which can neither benefit us nor harm us, and turn back on our heels after Allah has guided us—like someone whom the devils have lured away in the land, bewildered, while companions call him to guidance, ‘Come to us’?” Say, “Indeed, Allah’s guidance is the true guidance, and we have been commanded to submit to the Lord of all worlds.”
interpretation: The verse warns against abandoning the truth for powerless objects of worship. It portrays such a reversal as being lost and bewildered, despite having companions calling one back to the right path. Allah’s guidance alone is the way to follow, and the proper response is submission to Him, the Lord of all creation.

translation: And [we were commanded] to establish prayer and be mindful of Him; He is the One to whom you will be gathered.
interpretation: The command joins worship with reverence for God: prayer should shape a life lived with awareness of Him. The certainty of being gathered before Him gives this devotion lasting significance, since every person will ultimately answer to Him.

translation: He is the One who created the heavens and the earth in truth. On the Day He says, “Be,” and it is, His word is the truth. To Him belongs all dominion on the Day the Trumpet is blown. He knows the unseen and the witnessed; He is the All-Wise, the All-Aware.
interpretation: The verse presents creation and the Resurrection as expressions of God’s absolute authority: nothing exists or comes to pass except by His command, and His judgment is wholly true. The mention of His knowledge and wisdom assures that His reckoning encompasses what is hidden as well as what is evident, and is never arbitrary.

translation: And [remember] when Abraham said to his father, Azar: “Do you take idols as gods? I see that you and your people are clearly astray.”
interpretation: Abraham’s question challenges the idea that lifeless idols can rightly be worshipped as gods. His words express his clear recognition that his father and his people have turned away from the truth by directing worship to what cannot deserve it.

translation: Thus We showed Abraham the dominion of the heavens and the earth, so that he might be among those who are certain.
interpretation: God enabled Abraham to perceive the signs of divine sovereignty throughout creation, deepening his certainty in God’s oneness and power.

translation: When night covered him, he saw a star and said, “This is my Lord.” But when it set, he said, “I do not love those that set.”
interpretation: Abraham’s words present a reasoned challenge to the worship of celestial bodies: anything that appears and disappears, subject to change and setting, cannot be the everlasting Lord. His remark is part of an argument leading his people away from false worship, not a lasting confession of belief in the star.

translation: When he saw the moon rising, he said, “This is my Lord.” But when it set, he said, “If my Lord does not guide me, I will surely be among the people who have gone astray.”
interpretation: Abraham is reasoning against the worship of celestial bodies: the moon’s setting shows that it cannot be the eternal, sovereign Lord. His words also express his need for God’s guidance so that he will not follow those who are astray.

translation: When he saw the sun rising, he said, “This is my Lord; this is greater.” Then, when it set, he said, “My people, I am indeed free of what you associate with God.”
interpretation: Abraham points to the sun’s greater apparent power, then its setting shows that it too is subject to change and cannot be the Lord. By this reasoning, he rejects the worship of created things and disavows his people’s associations with God.

translation: Indeed, I have turned my face toward the One who created the heavens and the earth, inclining toward the truth, and I am not among those who associate others with God.
interpretation: This is a declaration of wholehearted devotion to the Creator alone: true faith turns away from every form of idolatry and directs worship and allegiance exclusively to God.

translation: His people argued with him. He said, “Do you dispute with me concerning Allah when He has guided me? I do not fear what you associate with Him, unless my Lord wills something. My Lord encompasses all things in knowledge. Will you not then take heed?”
interpretation: Abraham’s confidence rests on Allah’s guidance and absolute sovereignty: the things his people worship cannot harm him by their own power, and nothing occurs apart from Allah’s will. Since Allah’s knowledge encompasses everything, his people should reflect and abandon their baseless fear of false gods.

translation: “How should I fear what you associate with Allah, when you do not fear that you have associated with Him something for which He has sent down no authority? So which of the two groups is more deserving of security, if you know?”
interpretation: Abraham exposes the inconsistency of fearing powerless idols while feeling no fear about the far graver act of associating partners with God without any divine warrant. True security belongs to those who worship God alone, not to those who place their trust in what has no authority or power.

translation: Those who believe and do not mix their faith with wrongdoing—for them is security, and they are rightly guided.
interpretation: True security and guidance belong to those whose faith is not tainted by shirk, the gravest form of wrongdoing; their trust in God directs them to the right path.

translation: That was Our argument, which We gave Abraham against his people. We raise in rank whom We will. Indeed, your Lord is Wise, Knowing.
interpretation: The verse presents true insight and spiritual distinction as gifts from God, granted according to His wisdom and complete knowledge. Abraham’s reasoning shows how divine guidance can equip someone to challenge false beliefs with clarity.

translation: And We bestowed upon him Isaac and Jacob; each We guided. And Noah We had guided before. And among his descendants were David, Solomon, Job, Joseph, Moses, and Aaron. Thus do We reward those who excel in goodness.
interpretation: The verse portrays guidance as a divine favor bestowed across generations, while its closing phrase emphasizes that such favor is connected with excellence in faith and conduct—not simply with belonging to a distinguished family.

translation: And Zechariah, John, Jesus, and Elijah—each was among the righteous.
interpretation: Their shared description as righteous emphasizes that, despite their distinct lives and circumstances, each was devoted to God and steadfast in obedience to Him.

translation: And [We guided] Ishmael, Elisha, Jonah, and Lot; each We favored above all people.
interpretation: Their distinction lies in the guidance and prophetic honor God granted them; the verse presents this favor as a gift from God, not as a claim that they surpassed every person in every respect.

translation: And [We guided] some of their forefathers, descendants, and brothers; We chose them and guided them to a straight path.
interpretation: Their family ties alone did not confer righteousness: God chose and guided those among them whom He willed, showing that true distinction lies in following the straight path.

translation: That is Allah’s guidance, with which He guides whom He wills of His servants. Had they associated others with Allah, all they had done would have been rendered worthless.
interpretation: The verse teaches that guidance is a gift from Allah, and that sincere worship of Him is essential for deeds to be accepted. Even the righteous servants mentioned in the surrounding passage would have lost the reward of their deeds had they committed shirk.

translation: Those are the ones to whom We gave the Scripture, wisdom, and prophethood. If these people reject it, We have entrusted it to a people who will not reject it.
interpretation: The revelation and guidance entrusted to the prophets do not depend on the acceptance of those who deny them. If one people reject God’s message, He will entrust it to others who believe in it and uphold it faithfully.

translation: Those are the ones whom Allah guided, so follow their guidance. Say, “I ask you for no reward for it. It is only a reminder for all peoples.”
interpretation: The verse presents the guidance given to earlier prophets as a model for the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: he is to uphold their faithfulness to God and their commitment to truth. His message is not offered for personal gain, but as a reminder whose call is meant for all people.

translation: They did not rightly esteem Allah when they said, “Allah has sent down nothing to any human being.” Say, “Who sent down the Book that Moses brought—a light and guidance for people—which you make into separate sheets, displaying some of it and concealing much? And you were taught what neither you nor your forefathers knew.” Say, “Allah.” Then leave them to their vain discourse, amusing themselves.
interpretation: To deny that Allah has revealed anything is to fail to recognize His wisdom and authority. The revelation given to Moses stands as evidence against that denial, especially when people selectively display parts of it while concealing others. The Prophet is therefore told to affirm that Allah is the source of revelation and not to be drawn into their frivolous disputation.

translation: This is a blessed Book that We have sent down, confirming what came before it, so that you may warn the Mother of Cities and those around it. Those who believe in the Hereafter believe in it, and they are steadfast in guarding their prayers.
interpretation: The verse presents the Qur’an as a divinely blessed revelation in continuity with earlier scripture, entrusted to the Prophet to convey its warning beginning in Mecca and extending to those beyond it. It also links sincere belief in the Hereafter with accepting the revelation and faithfully maintaining prayer.

translation: Who is more unjust than one who invents a lie against Allah, or says, “It has been revealed to me,” when nothing has been revealed to him, or one who says, “I will bring down the like of what Allah has revealed”? If only you could see the wrongdoers in the agonies of death, while the angels stretch out their hands, saying, “Give up your souls! Today you will be repaid with humiliating punishment for what you used to say about Allah without truth, and for your arrogance toward His signs.”
interpretation: The verse warns that claiming divine authority falsely—or treating revelation as something one can rival—is an extreme form of injustice, rooted in arrogance toward God’s truth. At death, that arrogance can no longer shield a person from accountability: the angels’ command and the promised humiliation reveal the grave consequence of misrepresenting Allah and rejecting His signs.

translation: You have come to Us alone, just as We created you the first time, leaving behind what We granted you. We do not see with you the intercessors you claimed were partners in your affairs. The bonds between you have been severed, and what you used to claim has vanished from you.
interpretation: The verse portrays the final meeting with God as a stripping away of worldly supports: wealth and status remain behind, and those imagined to intercede or share in God’s power cannot help. Each person stands alone, confronted with the truth of their deeds and the emptiness of the claims they relied upon.

translation: Indeed, Allah is the One who splits the grain and the date-stone. He brings forth the living from the dead, and brings forth the dead from the living. That is Allah—so how are you turned away?
interpretation: The familiar transformation of seemingly lifeless seeds into living growth is a sign of Allah’s unmatched power: life and death are in His hands. The same power makes resurrection possible, so turning to other gods or doubting His ability to raise the dead has no sound basis.

translation: He brings forth the dawn, makes the night a time of rest, and has appointed the sun and moon for reckoning. That is the ordainment of the Almighty, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: The ordered rhythm of darkness, dawn, and the celestial cycles is presented as a sign of deliberate divine wisdom: the world is governed with precision, and its patterns make human life and the reckoning of time possible.

translation: He is the One who made the stars for you, so that you may find your way by them in the darknesses of land and sea. We have made the signs clear for people who know.
interpretation: The stars’ usefulness for navigation points to deliberate order and care in creation: what appears as distant lights also serves human life. Those who reflect on this purpose can recognize in it a sign of God’s wisdom and provision.

translation: He is the One who brought you into being from a single soul; then there is a place of settlement and a place of deposit. We have made the signs clear for people who understand.
interpretation: Humanity’s shared origin points to God’s power and knowledge: every person’s course through life—where they dwell and where they are entrusted along the way—is within His ordering. Reflecting on these signs should lead people to recognize His wisdom.

translation: He is the One who sent down water from the sky, and by it We brought forth the growth of every kind. Then We brought forth from it greenery, from which We bring forth grains arranged in clusters; and from the palm trees, from their spathes, hanging clusters; and gardens of grapes, and olives and pomegranates, alike yet different. Look at their fruit when they bear fruit and as it ripens. Surely in that are signs for people who believe.
interpretation: The verse invites reflection on how one life-giving source produces an astonishing variety of plants and fruits, each with its own form and course of ripening. This diversity and order point to God’s wisdom and power, and contemplating them can deepen the believer’s faith and gratitude.

translation: They have attributed partners to Allah from among the jinn, although He created them; and without knowledge they have fabricated sons and daughters for Him. Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they describe.
interpretation: The verse rejects treating any created being as a partner of the Creator and condemns inventing claims about God’s offspring without knowledge. Allah is utterly exalted above these descriptions, which wrongly liken Him to His creation.

translation: The Originator of the heavens and the earth. How could He have a child when He has no consort? He created all things, and He knows all things.
interpretation: The verse rejects the idea that God has offspring: having a child belongs to created beings and presupposes a consort, whereas God is the Originator of all creation and fully knows it. His relationship to creation is therefore not one of parentage, but of sovereign creation and knowledge.

translation: That is Allah, your Lord. There is no deity except Him, the Creator of all things; so worship Him. And He is the Guardian over all things.
interpretation: The verse grounds worship in Allah’s unique lordship: because all existence depends on Him and nothing shares in His creative power, worship belongs to Him alone. His guardianship also assures that every affair remains under His care and authority.

translation: Sight cannot encompass Him, while He encompasses all sight. He is the Most Subtle, the All-Aware.
interpretation: No created gaze can fully grasp or contain God, whereas nothing seen escapes His knowledge and awareness. His subtle reality is beyond perception, and His knowledge reaches even what is hidden.

translation: Clear insights have come to you from your Lord. Whoever sees clearly does so for his own benefit, and whoever is blind does so to his own detriment. I am not a guardian over you.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that divine guidance makes the truth available, but does not compel anyone to accept it. Each person bears the consequence of how they respond, while the messenger’s role is to convey the guidance, not to control people’s choices.

translation: Thus do We explain the signs in various ways, so that they may say, “You have studied,” and so that We may make them clear to people who know.
interpretation: The same varied signs that clarify the truth for sincere, discerning people may be twisted by those who reject it into an accusation that the Prophet learned his message from others. The verse points to the difference between a person’s willingness to recognize guidance and a person’s determination to dismiss it.

translation: Follow what has been revealed to you from your Lord. There is no deity except Him, and turn away from the polytheists.
interpretation: The verse calls the Prophet to remain faithful to God’s revelation and to affirm that worship belongs to God alone. He is not to be drawn away from this mission by the polytheists’ opposition, but to turn aside from their rejection.

translation: Had God willed, they would not have associated others with Him. We have not appointed you as a guardian over them, nor are you their keeper.
interpretation: Their choice to associate others with God occurs within what He permits, but this does not make it pleasing to Him or remove their responsibility. The Prophet’s role is to convey the message, not to compel people to believe or answer for their choices.

translation: Do not insult those they call upon besides Allah, lest they insult Allah out of hostility and without knowledge. Thus We have made the deeds of every community seem pleasing to them. Then to their Lord they will return, and He will inform them of what they used to do.
interpretation: The verse teaches that calling people to faith must not become an excuse for needless provocation: insulting what others revere may drive them to insult Allah in return. Believers should therefore speak with restraint, while recognizing that people can become attached to their own ways; ultimate judgment and the full disclosure of their deeds belong to Allah.

translation: They swore by Allah with their strongest oaths that if a sign came to them, they would surely believe in it. Say, “The signs are only with Allah.” And what will make you realize that, when it comes, they will not believe?
interpretation: Their emphatic promises do not mean that a sign would truly bring them to faith: signs come only by Allah’s will, and a heart set on rejection may refuse even when confronted with one.

translation: We will turn their hearts and their eyes away, just as they did not believe in it the first time, and We will leave them wandering blindly in their rebellion.
interpretation: This warns that persistently rejecting the truth can bring a person to a state in which their heart and perception turn further from guidance; left to their chosen rebellion, they become increasingly confused and unable to see the way.

translation: Even if We sent down the angels to them, and the dead spoke to them, and We gathered every thing before them face to face, they would still not believe unless Allah willed it. Yet most of them are ignorant.
interpretation: The verse teaches that overwhelming signs alone cannot bring faith to those determined to reject them; true belief depends on Allah’s will, while ignorance blinds many to the signs they demand.

translation: And so We made for every prophet enemies: devils from among humankind and jinn, who inspire one another with alluring words to deceive. Had your Lord willed, they would not have done so. So leave them to what they fabricate.
interpretation: The verse teaches that opposition to prophetic guidance can come from both human and unseen sources, working together through persuasive but deceptive speech. Their actions occur within what God permits, yet this does not make their deception true or excuse it. The Prophet is told not to be drawn into their fabrications, but to remain steadfast in conveying God’s guidance.

translation: So that the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter may incline toward it, be pleased with it, and commit what they are committing.
interpretation: Deceptive, embellished words can draw those who reject the Hereafter toward falsehood; when they become satisfied with it, they persist in the sinful deeds they have chosen.

translation: Shall I seek a judge other than Allah, when He is the One who has sent down to you the Book, clearly set out? Those to whom We gave Scripture know that it has been sent down from your Lord in truth. So do not be among those who doubt.
interpretation: The verse affirms that ultimate judgment belongs to Allah, whose revealed Book makes the truth clear. The recognition of its truth by people familiar with earlier Scripture reinforces that it is from the same divine source. The Prophet is therefore urged to remain steadfast and not let others’ rejection create doubt about the revelation.

translation: The word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice. None can alter His words, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: God’s revelation and judgment are complete, truthful, and just; no one can change or overturn them. His perfect knowledge and hearing affirm that His words and judgments are never based on ignorance or injustice.

translation: If you obey most of those on earth, they will lead you away from Allah’s path. They follow nothing but conjecture, and do nothing but guess.
interpretation: The verse cautions that truth is not established by majority opinion: people may be numerous yet rely on assumptions rather than sound knowledge. One should therefore remain guided by what Allah has revealed, rather than follow others merely because they are many.

translation: Indeed, your Lord knows best who strays from His path, and He knows best who is rightly guided.
interpretation: Guidance and misguidance are known fully to God, who sees people’s realities beyond outward appearances. This cautions against judging the truth by popular opinion and calls for trust in God’s complete knowledge.

translation: So eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, if you believe in His signs.
interpretation: The verse teaches that faith is expressed through obedience to God’s guidance, including observing His instruction when choosing what to eat.

translation: Why should you not eat of that over which Allah’s name has been mentioned, when He has already made clear to you what He has forbidden you—except what you are compelled to eat? Many people lead others astray through their own desires, without knowledge. Your Lord knows best those who transgress.
interpretation: The verse calls believers to follow the limits God has made clear rather than inventing prohibitions or permissions out of personal desire. Necessity is an acknowledged exception, while those who mislead others without knowledge remain accountable to God, who knows the true extent of their transgression.

translation: Abandon the outward and inward forms of sin. Indeed, those who commit sin will be recompensed for what they used to do.
interpretation: The command reaches beyond avoiding visible wrongdoing: it calls for integrity in private as well as in public, since hidden acts are no less known to God and carry their own accountability.

translation: Do not eat of that over which Allah’s name has not been mentioned, for that is indeed disobedience. The devils inspire their allies to argue with you; but if you obey them in this, you will indeed be associating partners with Allah.
interpretation: The verse warns against treating as lawful what Allah has forbidden, including meat slaughtered without invoking His name. Its warning of shirk concerns yielding to arguments that set aside Allah’s ruling and grant others authority to make the forbidden lawful.

translation: Is one who was dead, then We gave him life and provided him with a light by which he walks among people, like one who is in darknesses and cannot emerge from them? Thus the disbelievers’ deeds have been made appealing to them.
interpretation: The verse contrasts spiritual life through faith and divine guidance with a state of rejection that leaves a person trapped in confusion. The light enables the believer to discern and live by what is true, while the disbeliever’s distorted perception makes his own deeds seem attractive to him.

translation: Thus We placed in every town its leading criminals, so that they might scheme there. Yet they scheme only against themselves, though they do not realize it.
interpretation: The verse portrays the powerful wrongdoers who oppose the truth as a trial for their communities: their schemes may seem directed against others, but they ultimately bring harm upon themselves, even as they remain unaware of the consequences.

translation: When a sign comes to them, they say, “We will not believe unless we are given the like of what God’s messengers were given.” God knows best where to place His message. Those who commit wrongdoing will be struck by humiliation before God and a severe punishment for the schemes they used to devise.
interpretation: The verse rebukes those who make belief conditional on receiving prophetic status or extraordinary privilege themselves. Revelation is entrusted according to God’s wisdom, not human demands; those who scheme out of arrogance to resist it will face disgrace and punishment.

translation: Whoever Allah wills to guide, He opens his heart to Islam; and whoever He wills to leave astray, He makes his heart tight and constricted, as though he were climbing into the sky. Thus Allah places defilement upon those who do not believe.
interpretation: The verse portrays faith as a God-given openness that allows a person to receive and live by the truth, while persistent rejection leaves the heart increasingly constricted and burdened. The image of struggling to climb into the sky conveys how alien and difficult faith can feel to someone who turns away from it.

translation: And this is the straight path of your Lord. We have made the signs clear for people who take heed.
interpretation: God’s way is clear and leads rightly; its signs have been explained so that those who reflect may recognize that guidance and follow it.

translation: For them is the Abode of Peace with their Lord, and He is their protector because of what they used to do.
interpretation: The Abode of Peace signifies a lasting life free from fear and harm. God’s guardianship there is the ultimate fulfillment of the good they pursued: their deeds are met with security and closeness to their Lord.

translation: On the Day He gathers them all, He will say, “O company of jinn, you have drawn many people from among mankind to yourselves.” Their allies among mankind will say, “Our Lord, some of us benefited from others, and we have reached the term You appointed for us.” He will say, “The Fire is your home, to remain there, except as Allah wills. Your Lord is All-Wise, All-Knowing.”
interpretation: The verse depicts a mutual entanglement in wrongdoing: jinn mislead people, while people willingly follow them and seek what they offer, so each side gains some worldly gratification at the other’s expense. Their admission that they benefited from one another does not excuse them; it reveals their shared responsibility. Their final fate remains under Allah’s will, governed by His perfect wisdom and knowledge.

translation: Thus We cause some wrongdoers to become allies of others because of what they used to earn.
interpretation: The verse teaches that wrongdoing has consequences beyond the individual: people who persist in it may be drawn into mutual alliance and influence, as their own choices shape the company and power they find themselves among.

translation: “O company of jinn and mankind, did messengers from among yourselves not come to you, reciting My signs to you and warning you of the meeting of this Day of yours?” They will say, “We testify against ourselves.” The life of this world deluded them, and they will testify against themselves that they were disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse depicts the certainty of accountability: on the Day of Judgment, no one will be able to claim that they were left without warning or guidance. Those who let the attractions of worldly life turn them away from the truth will have to acknowledge their own rejection, and their testimony will stand against them.

translation: That is because your Lord would not destroy towns unjustly while their people were unaware.
interpretation: God’s justice means that people are not held to account for rejecting the truth before they have been made aware of it through clear guidance.

translation: And for all are درجات according to what they have done, and your Lord is not unaware of what they do.
interpretation: People’s standing in the Hereafter reflects their deeds, with no one’s actions overlooked; this assures that divine judgment is perfectly informed and just.

translation: And your Lord is the Self-Sufficient, the Possessor of mercy. If He wills, He can remove you and bring after you whomever He wills, just as He brought you forth from the descendants of another people.
interpretation: Humanity’s existence is not something God depends on: His power and dominion are complete, while His mercy is freely given. The rise of one people after another reminds us that no community is irreplaceable, and that those who receive God’s blessings should respond with humility rather than presume upon them.

translation: Indeed, what you are promised will surely come, and you cannot escape it.
interpretation: God’s promised reckoning is inevitable; no one can evade its arrival or escape accountability before Him.

translation: Say, “O my people, act according to your position; I too am acting. You will soon know who will have the final outcome of the abode. Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed.”
interpretation: The verse calls the people to choose their course while affirming the Prophet’s steadfastness in carrying out his mission. Its warning is that the ultimate judgment belongs to God: apparent strength or worldly advantage cannot secure a good end for those who persist in wrongdoing.

translation: They assign to Allah a share of what He has brought forth of crops and livestock, and say, “This is for Allah”—as they claim—“and this is for our partners.” Whatever is assigned to their partners does not reach Allah, while whatever is assigned to Allah reaches their partners. How evil is their judgment!
interpretation: Their practice reveals the injustice and inconsistency of associating partners with God: they treat what they claim is God’s share as expendable whenever it benefits their idols, while never allowing the idols’ share to be given to God. The verse condemns the arbitrary rules by which they elevate their false deities over the One who provided everything.

translation: Thus their supposed partners made the killing of their children seem fair to many of the polytheists, in order to ruin them and confuse them about their religion. Had Allah willed, they would not have done so. So leave them to what they fabricate.
interpretation: The verse portrays how false objects of devotion and the ideas associated with them can make grave wrongdoing appear religiously acceptable, leading people toward ruin and distorting their faith. Allah’s permitting them to act does not mean He approves of their actions; the Prophet is told to leave their fabrications to them while the truth is made clear.

translation: They say, “These livestock and crops are forbidden; none may eat them except those we permit,” according to their claim. They also declare certain livestock forbidden to ride, and other livestock over which they do not mention Allah’s name—fabricating lies against Him. He will repay them for what they used to invent.
interpretation: The verse condemns people who impose religious rules of their own making and falsely attribute them to God. By turning custom into divine command, they distort worship and wrongfully restrict what God has provided; they will be held accountable for these fabrications.

translation: They say, “What is in the wombs of these livestock is reserved for our men and forbidden to our wives. But if it is stillborn, then they all share in it.” He will repay them for what they have fabricated. Indeed, He is All-Wise, All-Knowing.
interpretation: The verse condemns the people’s invented rules about who could eat the livestock’s offspring: they reserved it for men when it was born alive but allowed women to share it if it was stillborn. By calling these customs their fabrication, the verse warns against attributing arbitrary religious rulings to God; He knows their deeds and will judge them justly.

translation: Those who killed their children foolishly and without knowledge, and declared forbidden what Allah had provided for them, inventing lies against Allah, have surely suffered loss. They have gone astray and were not rightly guided.
interpretation: The verse warns against allowing ignorance, superstition, or self-interest to override moral responsibility and then claiming divine authority for such choices. True guidance requires humility before God and care for the lives and blessings entrusted to people.

translation: He is the One who brought forth gardens, trellised and untrellised, date palms, crops of varied produce, and olives and pomegranates, alike and unlike. Eat of their fruit when they bear fruit, and give its due on the day of harvest. Do not be wasteful; surely He does not love those who are wasteful.
interpretation: The verse teaches that the abundance and variety of the earth are gifts to be enjoyed with gratitude, while also carrying a responsibility toward others. Giving what is due at harvest and avoiding excess make stewardship—not selfish consumption—the proper response to God’s provision.

translation: And among the livestock are some fit for carrying loads and some [too small for that]. Eat of what Allah has provided for you, and do not follow Satan’s footsteps; surely he is your manifest enemy.
interpretation: The verse teaches that people should receive God’s provision with gratitude and follow His guidance about what is lawful, rather than letting Satan lead them into baseless restrictions or disobedience.

translation: Eight pairs: two of sheep and two of goats. Say, “Has He forbidden the two males, or the two females, or what the wombs of the two females contain? Tell me on the basis of knowledge, if you are truthful.”
interpretation: The verse challenges those who claimed that certain livestock were forbidden by God: they must show clear knowledge for distinguishing what is prohibited, rather than assigning prohibitions without evidence.

translation: And of camels, two, and of cattle, two. Say, “Has He forbidden the two males, or the two females, or what the wombs of the two females contain? Or were you witnesses when Allah instructed you to do this?” Who, then, is more unjust than one who invents a lie about Allah in order to mislead people without knowledge? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: The verse challenges those who claimed that certain livestock were forbidden by God, asking them to produce genuine revelation or direct evidence for their claim. It warns that inventing religious rulings and attributing them to Allah in order to mislead others is a grave injustice, and that those who persist in such wrongdoing are not guided by Him.

translation: Say, “I find nothing in what has been revealed to me that is forbidden for anyone to eat, except carrion, flowing blood, the flesh of swine—for it is impure—or an animal slaughtered in disobedience, dedicated to other than God. But whoever is compelled by necessity, without seeking it or exceeding the limit, then surely your Lord is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.”
interpretation: The verse grounds dietary prohibitions in revelation rather than custom or invention, while showing that necessity is treated with mercy: a person forced to eat what is normally forbidden may do so only to the extent needed, without deliberate desire or excess.

translation: And to those who were Jews, We forbade every animal with an undivided hoof. Of cattle and sheep, We forbade them their fat, except what their backs carry, or what is on the entrails, or what is attached to a bone. Thus We recompensed them for their transgression; and surely We speak the truth.
interpretation: These dietary restrictions are presented as a consequence of the people’s transgression, not as an arbitrary ruling; the verse affirms that God’s account of this recompense is truthful.

translation: If they deny you, say, “Your Lord is vast in mercy, yet His punishment cannot be turned away from the people who persist in wrongdoing.”
interpretation: The verse instructs the Prophet to answer denial with both hope and warning: God’s mercy is immense, but it does not make persistent wrongdoing consequence-free. Those who reject the truth cannot assume they will escape His judgment.

translation: Those who associate others with Allah will say, “Had Allah willed, neither we nor our forefathers would have associated anything with Him, nor would we have forbidden anything.” In the same way, those before them denied the truth until they tasted Our punishment. Say, “Do you have any knowledge that you can present to us? You follow nothing but conjecture, and you do nothing but guess.”
interpretation: The verse rejects using Allah’s will as an excuse for shirk and invented prohibitions: knowing that something occurs by Allah’s will does not make it a command or remove human responsibility. The challenge to produce knowledge shows that such claims have no revealed proof and rest only on conjecture; earlier peoples made the same excuse, yet it did not shield them from accountability.

translation: Say, “Allah has the decisive proof. Had He willed, He would have guided you all.”
interpretation: Allah’s proof is complete and cannot be overturned; people cannot use divine decree as an excuse for rejecting guidance, since their choices remain accountable even though Allah could have guided everyone by His will.

translation: Say, “Bring your witnesses who testify that Allah has forbidden this.” If they testify, do not testify with them. Do not follow the desires of those who deny Our signs, those who do not believe in the Hereafter, and those who set equals to their Lord.
interpretation: The verse calls for religious claims to be tested rather than accepted merely because people assert them. Even if those making a false claim produce witnesses, believers must not endorse it; they must remain steadfast and not let the desires of those who reject revelation, deny the Hereafter, or associate partners with Allah shape their faith.

translation: Say, “Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you: do not associate anything with Him; show kindness to your parents; do not kill your children out of poverty—we provide for you and for them; do not approach indecencies, whether openly or secretly; and do not take a life that God has made sacred, except by right. This is what He has instructed you, so that you may understand.”
interpretation: These commands establish the foundations of a life lived in faith and justice: worship God alone, treat parents with kindness, protect children rather than letting poverty drive their destruction, avoid every form of indecency, and uphold the sanctity of human life. Their purpose is to guide people toward sound understanding and responsible conduct.

translation: Do not approach the property of the orphan except in the best manner, until he reaches maturity. Give full measure and weight with justice. We do not burden any soul beyond its capacity. When you speak, be just, even if it concerns a close relative, and fulfill God’s covenant. This is what He has enjoined upon you, so that you may take heed.
interpretation: This passage establishes integrity as a form of worship: power over another’s property must be exercised with care, fairness must not bend to personal ties, and promises to God must be honored. Its recognition of human capacity calls for conscientious effort without demanding what a person cannot reasonably bear.

translation: And [He has commanded:] “This is My straight path, so follow it, and do not follow other paths, lest they lead you away from His path. This is what He has enjoined upon you, so that you may be mindful of God.”
interpretation: The verse presents devotion to God’s guidance as a single, coherent way of life. Following competing paths can divide a person’s loyalties and draw them away from that guidance; mindfulness of God is cultivated by holding firmly to it.

translation: Then We gave Moses the Scripture, completing Our favor upon him who did good, and setting out all things, as guidance and mercy, so that they might believe in the meeting with their Lord.
interpretation: The verse presents the Scripture given to Moses as a complete blessing and a source of guidance and mercy. Its clarification of what people need for faith and righteous living was meant to lead them to believe that they would meet their Lord and be answerable to Him.

translation: And this is a blessed Book that We have sent down, so follow it and be mindful of Allah, so that you may be shown mercy.
interpretation: The verse presents the Qur’an as a source of enduring blessing and guidance, and calls people to let its teachings direct their lives. Following it with God-consciousness is the way toward His mercy.

translation: Lest you say, “The Scripture was sent down only to two communities before us, and we were unaware of their study.”
interpretation: The verse presents a possible excuse being removed: people should not claim that divine revelation was given only to earlier communities and that they had no access to its teachings.

translation: Or lest you say, “If the Scripture had been sent down to us, we would surely have been better guided than they.” Now a clear proof from your Lord has come to you, along with guidance and mercy. Who, then, is more unjust than one who denies Allah’s signs and turns away from them? We will repay those who turn away from Our signs with a dreadful punishment for their turning away.
interpretation: The verse closes off the excuse that people would have followed guidance if it had been given to them: the clear proof, guidance, and mercy have now come, so turning away from them is a deliberate rejection of what could lead a person to God. The warning emphasizes that such rejection is not merely a failure to know, but a culpable refusal to respond to the truth made available.

translation: Do they await anything but that the angels should come to them, or that your Lord should come, or that some of your Lord’s signs should come? On the day when some of your Lord’s signs come, no soul will benefit from its faith if it had not believed before, or had not earned good through its faith. Say, “Wait; we too are waiting.”
interpretation: The verse warns against delaying faith and righteous action until the truth becomes undeniable: when the decisive signs arrive, belief begun then will not benefit someone who had not believed before, and faith is not a substitute for having done good while there was still time.

translation: Indeed, those who divided their religion and became factions—you have nothing to do with them. Their affair rests with God; then He will inform them of what they used to do.
interpretation: The verse warns against fragmenting God’s guidance into rival factions and makes clear that the Prophet is not responsible for their divisions. Their final judgment belongs to God, who will hold them accountable for their deeds.

translation: Whoever comes with a good deed will receive ten times its like; and whoever comes with an evil deed will be recompensed only with its like, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: The verse shows that God’s judgment combines generosity with perfect justice: goodness is rewarded beyond its measure, while wrongdoing is never punished beyond what it deserves. No one’s deeds or rights are treated unfairly.

translation: Say, “Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path: an upright religion, the way of Abraham, inclining toward pure faith. He was not among those who associated others with God.”
interpretation: The verse presents Abraham’s sincere devotion to God alone as the model of the straight path, affirming that true guidance is an upright way of life free from associating partners with God.

translation: Say, “Indeed, my prayer, my sacrifice, my life and my death are for Allah, Lord of all worlds.”
interpretation: This is a declaration of complete devotion: worship and every part of one’s life are to be directed sincerely to Allah alone, acknowledging His sole lordship and setting aside all partners or rivals.

translation: He has no partner. This is what I have been commanded, and I am the first of those who submit.
interpretation: The speaker affirms that worship and devotion belong to God alone, and that wholehearted submission to Him is a divine command he is foremost in carrying out.

translation: Say, “Shall I seek a lord other than Allah, when He is Lord of all things?” Every soul earns only against itself, and no bearer of burdens bears the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you about that over which you used to differ.
interpretation: Worship and ultimate reliance belong to Allah alone. Each person is accountable for their own choices, not another’s, and all disputes about truth will ultimately be made clear by Allah when everyone returns to Him.

translation: And it is He who made you successors upon the earth and raised some of you above others in rank, so that He may test you through what He has given you. Indeed, your Lord is swift in punishment, and He is surely Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: The differences in people’s status and blessings are a trust and a test, not grounds for pride: each person is accountable for how they use what they have been given. The verse holds that accountability together with hope, warning of swift consequences while affirming that God’s forgiveness and mercy remain open to those who turn to Him.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Alif, Lam, Mim.
interpretation: The opening invokes Allah’s mercy and then presents the mysterious letters Alif, Lam, Mim, whose full meaning is known to Him; they remind the reader that the Qur’an’s revelation reaches beyond human knowledge.

translation: A Book revealed to you—so let there be no distress in your heart concerning it—so that you may warn by it and remind the believers.
interpretation: The verse reassures the Prophet ﷺ that resistance to the revelation should not make him hesitate or feel burdened in conveying it. Its authority comes from God, and his task is to deliver its warning faithfully and strengthen the believers through its guidance.

translation: Follow what has been sent down to you from your Lord, and do not follow protectors besides Him. How little you take heed.
interpretation: The verse calls believers to let God’s revelation be their guiding authority, rather than surrendering their judgment and loyalty to other powers or guides when they conflict with it. Its closing words warn that people often fail to reflect on the consequences of turning away from that guidance.

translation: How many a town We destroyed! Our punishment came upon it by night or while its people were resting at midday.
interpretation: The verse warns that no people should feel secure from the consequences of persistent wrongdoing: reckoning may come when they least expect it, even in moments of rest and apparent safety.

translation: Their only plea when Our punishment came upon them was to say, “Indeed, we were wrongdoers.”
interpretation: When God’s punishment overtook them, they had no defense or appeal; they could only admit their wrongdoing. Their confession came after the chance to repent had passed.

translation: We will surely question those to whom messengers were sent, and We will surely question the messengers.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, people will be held accountable for how they responded to God’s guidance, and the messengers will be asked whether they faithfully conveyed it.

translation: Then We will surely recount to them with full knowledge, for We were never absent.
interpretation: God’s account of people’s deeds is grounded in complete knowledge: nothing they did was hidden or beyond His awareness, so His judgment is perfectly informed and just.

translation: The weighing on that Day is true. So those whose scales are heavy—they are the successful ones.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, God’s accounting will be perfectly just, and a person’s true standing will be shown by the weight of their good deeds. True success is therefore not worldly gain, but being found worthy of God’s mercy and reward.

translation: As for those whose scales are light, they are the ones who have lost themselves because they used to wrong Our signs.
interpretation: The verse warns that a person’s ultimate loss comes from treating God’s signs unjustly—by denying or disregarding them—so that, on the Day of Judgment, their deeds carry no weight sufficient for salvation.

translation: We have established you upon the earth and provided for you there means of livelihood. Little are you grateful.
interpretation: The verse reminds people that their ability to live and flourish on earth, and the provisions that sustain them, are gifts from God. It gently rebukes the human tendency to take these blessings for granted and calls for sincere gratitude expressed in how one lives.

translation: And We certainly created you, then fashioned you, then said to the angels, “Prostrate before Adam.” So they prostrated, except Iblis; he was not among those who prostrated.
interpretation: The verse teaches that human dignity comes from God’s creative act and honor, not from any claim to superiority. Iblis’s refusal shows how pride can turn knowledge of God’s command into disobedience.

translation: He said, “What prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you?” He replied, “I am better than him: You created me from fire and created him from clay.”
interpretation: Iblis’s reply reveals how pride distorted his judgment: he treated the material of his creation as proof of superiority and used that claim to resist God’s command. The verse warns that self-admiration can turn perceived status into an excuse for disobedience.

translation: He said, “Then descend from it, for you have no right to be arrogant in it. So get out; indeed, you are among the humiliated.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that pride cannot claim a place of honor before God: Iblis’s arrogance and refusal to submit strip him of his standing and lead to humiliation.

translation: He said, “Grant me respite until the day they are resurrected.”
interpretation: His request reveals his determination to persist in rebellion: rather than repent, he seeks to remain until the Resurrection, intending to continue his defiance throughout his allotted time.

translation: He said, “You are indeed among those granted respite.”
interpretation: God grants Iblis a delay until the appointed time, not approval of his defiance; the respite allows the trial of human beings to unfold.

translation: He said, “Since You have caused me to stray, I will surely lie in wait for them on Your straight path.”
interpretation: Iblīs declares that he will try to turn people away from guidance, targeting them as they seek to follow God’s path.

translation: “Then I will surely come at them from before them and from behind them, from their right and from their left; and You will find most of them ungrateful.”
interpretation: This is Iblīs’s boast that he will use every avenue of temptation to turn people away from obedience to God. His aim is not merely to lead them into particular sins, but to weaken their gratitude and devotion, though his influence does not compel them and does not encompass every person.

translation: He said, “Get out of it, disgraced and banished. Whoever among them follows you—I will surely fill Hell with all of you.”
interpretation: The verse warns that defying God and following Satan leads to exclusion from divine favor and ultimate accountability; Satan’s influence does not remove the responsibility of those who choose to follow him.

translation: “And, O Adam, dwell—you and your wife—in the Garden, and eat from wherever you wish; but do not approach this tree, or you will be among the wrongdoers.”
interpretation: The verse presents human freedom alongside moral responsibility: Adam and his wife are granted abundant provision, while one clear limit marks the importance of obedience. To cross that limit would be to wrong themselves by violating the guidance given to them.

translation: Then Satan whispered to them, seeking to expose to them what had been concealed from them of their nakedness. He said, “Your Lord has forbidden you this tree only so that you might not become angels or become immortal.”
interpretation: The verse shows how Satan deceives by presenting disobedience as a path to greater status or everlasting life, while portraying God’s prohibition as an attempt to keep those benefits from them.

translation: And he swore to them, “Indeed, I am truly one of your sincere advisers.”
interpretation: The verse warns that deception can be made persuasive by appearing as sincere counsel; a solemn oath alone does not prove that someone’s intentions are trustworthy.

translation: So he brought them down through deception. When they tasted of the tree, their nakedness became apparent to them, and they began fastening together leaves from the Garden over themselves. Their Lord called to them: “Did I not forbid you from that tree and tell you that Satan is indeed a clear enemy to you?”
interpretation: Their haste to cover themselves reveals the shame and vulnerability that followed their disobedience, while God’s reminder makes clear that they had been warned: the harm came from trusting Satan’s deceptive promise over the guidance they had received.

translation: They said, “Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves. If You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers.”
interpretation: Their words express sincere repentance: they openly acknowledge their wrongdoing and turn to God, recognizing that only His forgiveness and mercy can rescue them from loss.

translation: He said, “Descend, some of you enemies to others. On earth you will have a dwelling place and provision for a time.”
interpretation: Earthly life is a temporary place of residence and enjoyment, marked by conflict among its inhabitants; its provisions last only until the time God has appointed.

translation: He said, “In it you will live, in it you will die, and from it you will be brought forth.”
interpretation: By connecting human life, death, and resurrection with the earth, the verse teaches that our earthly existence is temporary and that returning to life by God’s command is certain—so people should live humbly and remain mindful of their accountability to Him.

translation: O children of Adam, We have provided you with clothing to cover your nakedness and as adornment. But the clothing of God-consciousness is best. That is one of God’s signs, so that they may take heed.
interpretation: The verse teaches that outward clothing serves human dignity and adornment, while the deeper protection is God-consciousness: a life shaped by reverence for God and moral restraint. By calling this the better garment, it directs people not to let outward appearance eclipse the inner character that preserves them from wrongdoing.

translation: O children of Adam, do not let Satan tempt you as he caused your parents to leave the Garden, stripping them of their garments to expose their nakedness. He and his followers see you from where you cannot see them. We have made the devils allies of those who do not believe.
interpretation: The verse warns that Satan’s deception can work unseen, drawing people away from obedience by exploiting their weaknesses, just as he once deceived Adam and his wife. Believers should therefore remain alert and guard their faith and dignity, rather than trusting what appears harmless; persistent rejection of faith leaves a person increasingly open to Satan’s influence.

translation: When they commit an indecent act, they say, “We found our forefathers doing it, and Allah has commanded us to do it.” Say, “Allah does not command indecency. Do you attribute to Allah what you do not know?”
interpretation: Inherited custom cannot justify wrongdoing or be treated as divine command. The verse warns against falsely attributing beliefs or practices to Allah without knowledge.

translation: Say, “My Lord has commanded justice. Set your faces toward Him at every place of worship, and call upon Him, devoting your religion sincerely to Him. Just as He brought you into being, you will return to Him.”
interpretation: The verse calls people to make worship an expression of justice and wholehearted devotion, turning to God sincerely wherever they worship. Its closing reminder that they will return as He first brought them into being grounds this life of worship in accountability before God.

translation: He guided one group, while another group deserved misguidance. They took the devils as allies instead of Allah, yet they thought they were rightly guided.
interpretation: The verse teaches that people may mistake their path when they turn away from Allah and follow deceptive influences. Those who choose such allies can become convinced that they are guided, even as their choices lead them astray.

translation: O children of Adam, wear your adornment at every place of worship, and eat and drink, but do not be excessive. Surely, He does not love those who are excessive.
interpretation: The verse teaches that devotion does not require rejecting the good things God has permitted: one should approach worship with dignity and enjoy lawful food and drink, while keeping desire within balanced limits. Excess is discouraged because it turns blessings away from their proper use.
