translation: Say, “Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah that He has brought forth for His servants, and the wholesome provisions?” Say, “They are for those who believe during the life of this world, and exclusively theirs on the Day of Resurrection.” Thus We make the signs clear for people who know.”
interpretation: The verse rejects declaring Allah’s lawful adornments and wholesome provisions forbidden without His authority. Such blessings may be enjoyed in this worldly life, but in the Hereafter they will belong exclusively to the believers, perfected and free from hardship.

translation: Say, “My Lord has forbidden only indecencies, whether open or hidden, sin, wrongful aggression, associating with Allah what He has sent down no authority for, and saying about Allah what you do not know.”
interpretation: The verse warns against treating personal assumptions as divine truth. To attribute a command or belief to Allah without knowledge is a serious violation, because it misrepresents the source of religious guidance and can lead others astray.

translation: For every community there is an appointed term. When its term comes, they can neither delay it for a moment nor bring it forward.
interpretation: The verse teaches that the time appointed by God for every community is fixed: human beings cannot change it once it arrives. It calls people to heed divine guidance before that time is reached.

translation: O children of Adam, if messengers from among yourselves come to you, recounting My signs to you, then whoever is mindful of God and sets things right will have no fear, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: The verse presents God’s guidance as reaching people through messengers from their own kind, making its message accessible to them. Its promise is for those who respond with mindfulness of God and sincere reform: they need not fear what lies ahead or grieve over what has passed.

translation: As for those who deny Our signs and disdain them, they are the companions of the Fire; they will remain there forever.
interpretation: The verse warns that rejecting God’s signs out of arrogance is not mere disbelief but a deliberate refusal to heed the truth, with lasting consequences in the Hereafter.

translation: Who, then, is more unjust than one who invents lies about Allah or denies His signs? They will receive their allotted share from the decree. Then, when Our messengers come to take their souls, they will say, “Where are those you used to call upon besides Allah?” They will reply, “They have abandoned us,” and they will testify against themselves that they were disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse warns that fabricating claims about God and rejecting His signs are grave injustices whose consequences are already decreed. At death, those who relied on other objects of worship will find that they cannot help them, and their own admission will expose the truth they had denied.

translation: He will say, “Enter the Fire among nations of jinn and humans who passed away before you.” Whenever a nation enters, it curses its sister-nation. When they have all gathered there, the later ones will say of the earlier ones, “Our Lord, these led us astray, so give them twice the punishment of the Fire.” He will say, “Each will have twice the punishment, but you do not know.”
interpretation: The verse shows that those who mislead others bear a grave burden, but those who follow them are not absolved of responsibility. Each receives a doubled punishment: the harm of their own wrongdoing and the consequences of the wrongdoing they helped perpetuate. Blaming one another in the Hereafter cannot undo the choices they made.

translation: Their predecessors will say to their successors, “You had no advantage over us. So taste the punishment for what you used to earn.”
interpretation: Those who came earlier and those who followed them will each face the consequences of their own choices; following others does not excuse wrongdoing, nor does being first make anyone exempt from judgment.

translation: Indeed, those who deny Our signs and arrogantly turn away from them—the gates of heaven will not be opened for them, nor will they enter Paradise until a camel passes through the eye of a needle. Thus do We recompense the wicked.
interpretation: The comparison makes clear that entry into Paradise is utterly impossible for those who persist in rejecting God’s signs out of arrogance, unless the impossible were to occur. Their exclusion is a just consequence of their chosen defiance.

translation: For them there will be a bed from Hell, and above them coverings. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse portrays the wrongdoers as wholly surrounded by punishment: Hell beneath them as a resting place and coverings above them, leaving no refuge or escape. This is the just consequence of their wrongdoing.

translation: As for those who believe and do righteous deeds—we do not burden any soul beyond its capacity—they are the people of Paradise, where they will remain forever.
interpretation: The verse offers reassurance that God’s judgment takes a person’s real capacity into account: faith and righteous effort are not measured by what lies beyond one’s ability. Those who strive sincerely within that capacity are promised lasting life in Paradise.

translation: We will remove whatever rancor is in their hearts, and rivers will flow beneath them. They will say, “Praise belongs to God, who guided us to this. We would never have been guided had God not guided us. The messengers of our Lord truly came with the truth.” And they will be called, “This is the Garden you have been given to inherit for what you used to do.”
interpretation: The verse portrays Paradise as a gift whose joy is made complete by both inner peace and clear recognition of its source: its people are free of resentment, affirm that God’s guidance enabled them to reach it, and see their righteous deeds as the path by which they received the promised inheritance.

translation: The people of Paradise will call to the people of the Fire, “We have found what our Lord promised us to be true. Have you found what your Lord promised you to be true?” They will say, “Yes.” Then a caller among them will announce, “May Allah’s curse be upon the wrongdoers.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the final certainty of Allah’s promises: what people may have doubted in worldly life becomes undeniable, and the wrongdoers’ injustice is exposed as the cause of their being cut off from Allah’s mercy.

translation: Those who bar others from the way of God, seek to make it crooked, and disbelieve in the Hereafter.
interpretation: The verse portrays deliberate obstruction and distortion of God’s guidance, rooted in denying the ultimate accountability of the Hereafter.

translation: Between them is a barrier, and upon the heights are men who recognize each by their distinguishing marks. They call out to the people of Paradise, “Peace be upon you!” They have not yet entered it, though they hope to.
interpretation: The men upon the heights are understood as those whose good and bad deeds are equal: they can recognize the people of both destinations, and they remain hopeful of entering Paradise by God’s mercy.

translation: When their eyes are turned toward the people of the Fire, they say, “Our Lord, do not place us among the wrongdoing people.”
interpretation: Seeing the fate of those who rejected God’s guidance, they turn to Him in humble fear, asking not to share the wrongdoers’ end. The verse presents this plea as a reminder that witnessing another’s punishment should deepen one’s own reliance on God and resolve to avoid wrongdoing.

translation: The people of the Heights will call to men they recognize by their marks and say, “What benefit did your multitude bring you, and your arrogance?”
interpretation: The verse shows that worldly power, status, and pride cannot save a person from divine judgment. Those who once relied on their numbers and looked down on others are confronted with the failure of that confidence.

translation: “Are these the ones you swore Allah would never grant His mercy? Enter Paradise: you will have no fear, nor will you grieve.”
interpretation: The verse exposes the arrogance of those who presumed to judge who deserved God’s mercy. Their contemptuous certainty is overturned: the people they dismissed are welcomed into Paradise, while true honor and safety belong to God’s judgment, not human status or opinion.

translation: The people of the Fire will call to the people of Paradise, “Pour some water over us, or some of what Allah has provided for you.” They will reply, “Allah has forbidden both to the disbelievers.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the final consequence of rejecting faith: those who once had opportunities to turn toward Allah find themselves utterly dependent, yet the blessings they ask for are beyond their reach. It warns that worldly provision is not a guarantee of salvation; what matters is whether one responds faithfully to Allah’s guidance.

translation: Those who took their religion as amusement and play, and whom the life of this world deceived. So today We will leave them to their fate, just as they forgot the meeting of this Day of theirs and used to deny Our signs.
interpretation: The verse warns that treating faith as something to mock or play with, while being absorbed by worldly life, leads to a grave reckoning. God’s “forgetting” them means withholding His mercy and leaving them to their consequence—not that He literally forgets them—as they had disregarded their meeting with Him and rejected His signs.

translation: We have certainly brought them a Book that We have set out in detail with knowledge, as guidance and mercy for people who believe.
interpretation: The Qur’an’s teachings are laid out with perfect knowledge, not conjecture, so that those who believe may find in it a clear guide and a source of mercy.

translation: Do they await anything but its fulfillment? On the Day its fulfillment comes, those who had forgotten it before will say, “Our Lord’s messengers truly came with the truth. Are there any intercessors to intercede for us, or could we be sent back so that we might do other than what we used to do?” They will have lost their own souls, and what they used to fabricate will have abandoned them.
interpretation: The verse portrays the moment when the realities promised by God become undeniable. Those who had neglected the messengers’ warnings will then recognize the truth, but their pleas for intercession or another chance will come too late; their former reliance on false claims will avail them nothing.

translation: Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then established Himself over the Throne. He makes the night cover the day, pursuing it swiftly; and the sun, the moon, and the stars are subjected to His command. Surely, to Him belong creation and command. Blessed is Allah, Lord of all worlds.
interpretation: The verse presents the ordered workings of the universe as signs of Allah’s complete sovereignty: the One who brings creation into being also governs it. This calls people to recognize that ultimate authority belongs to Him alone and to turn to Him with reverence.

translation: Call upon your Lord humbly and privately. Indeed, He does not love those who transgress.
interpretation: The verse teaches that supplication should be offered with humility and sincerity, without arrogance or crossing proper bounds in what one asks of God.

translation: Do not spread corruption on the earth after it has been set right, and call upon Him in fear and hope. Surely Allah’s mercy is near to those who do good.
interpretation: The verse teaches that devotion to God must shape how people treat the world and one another: worship is inconsistent with causing harm or undoing what is beneficial. Calling upon God with both fear and hope keeps the heart humble without despair, while excellence in conduct is the way of those who draw near to His mercy.

translation: He is the One who sends the winds as heralds of His mercy. Then, when they carry heavy clouds, We drive them to a lifeless land, send down water there, and bring forth every kind of fruit by it. In this way We bring the dead to life, so that you may take heed.
interpretation: The renewal of barren land through rain is a sign of God’s power to restore life after death. The verse invites people to recognize that resurrection is no less within His power than the earth’s transformation from lifelessness to abundance.

translation: As for the good land, its vegetation grows by the permission of its Lord; but what is bad yields only scantily. Thus We explain the signs in varied ways for people who are grateful.
interpretation: The verse invites reflection on how the same divine guidance meets different dispositions: a receptive heart flourishes through it, while a hardened one gains little. Gratitude is presented as the quality that helps people recognize and benefit from the signs.

translation: We sent Noah to his people, and he said, “My people, worship Allah; you have no god but Him. I fear for you the punishment of a tremendous day.”
interpretation: Noah’s warning calls his people to recognize Allah alone as worthy of worship and to take the consequences of rejecting that truth seriously; his fear expresses sincere concern for their ultimate fate.

translation: The leaders of his people said, “We surely see you in clear error.”
interpretation: Their words show how those invested in their status can mistake sincere guidance for error, dismissing a warning without honestly considering its message.

translation: He said, “My people, there is no misguidance in me; rather, I am a messenger from the Lord of all worlds.”
interpretation: His reply presents the truth of his message as grounded in his commission from God, not in the judgments or suspicions of his people. It also answers their accusation without hostility, reaffirming his role as a messenger sent to guide them.

translation: I convey to you the messages of my Lord, offer you sincere counsel, and know from Allah what you do not know.
interpretation: Noah explains that his warning comes from his duty as a messenger and from sincere concern for his people. What he knows beyond their awareness is knowledge given by Allah, guiding him to warn them of truths and consequences they cannot perceive on their own.

translation: Do you wonder that a reminder from your Lord has come to you through a man from among you, to warn you, so that you may be mindful and perhaps receive mercy?
interpretation: The verse challenges the people’s surprise at receiving God’s message through a human being from their own community. His familiarity and humanity are not reasons to reject him; rather, the warning is an opportunity to become mindful of God and thereby be shown mercy.

translation: But they denied him, so We saved him and those with him aboard the Ark, and We drowned those who denied Our signs. They were indeed a people blind to the truth.
interpretation: Their rejection of the truth left them unable to recognize the signs before them; deliverance came to Noah and his companions, while the deniers faced the consequence of their blindness.

translation: And to ʿĀd [We sent] their brother Hūd. He said, “My people, worship Allah; you have no god other than Him. Will you not then be mindful of Him?”
interpretation: Hūd’s appeal joins the trust of kinship with the central call of faith: sincere worship belongs to Allah alone. His closing question urges his people to let awareness of Allah guide their choices and turn them from wrongdoing.

translation: The chiefs of his people who disbelieved said, “We surely see you as foolish, and we certainly think you are one of the liars.”
interpretation: Their response shows how pride can lead people to reject a messenger by insulting his character and calling him a liar, rather than considering the truth of his message.

translation: He said, “My people, there is no foolishness in me; rather, I am a messenger from the Lord of all worlds.”
interpretation: He answers the charge of irrationality with calm clarity, affirming that his message is not the product of delusion or personal whim, but a trust conveyed from God, the Lord of all creation.

translation: I convey to you the messages of my Lord, and I am a sincere and trustworthy adviser to you.
interpretation: The speaker affirms that his guidance is a faithful delivery of his Lord’s message, offered with genuine concern for his people and without deceit or personal interest.

translation: “Do you find it strange that a reminder from your Lord has come to you through a man from among you, so that he may warn you? Remember when He made you successors after the people of Noah and increased you in stature. So remember God’s blessings, that you may prosper.”
interpretation: The people of ʿĀd are being called to see that a messenger’s being one of their own is no reason to reject him: God has sent him to warn them for their good. Their place after Noah’s people and their exceptional strength are gifts entrusted to them, not grounds for pride. Remembering those blessings should lead them to gratitude and heedfulness—the path to true prosperity.

translation: They said, “Have you come to us so that we may worship Allah alone and abandon what our forefathers used to worship? Then bring upon us what you threaten us with, if you are truthful.”
interpretation: Their response reveals that they reject the call to worship Allah alone because it requires them to leave the inherited practices of their forefathers. Rather than consider the truth of the message, they challenge the messenger to bring the punishment he has warned them about.

translation: He said, “Punishment and wrath from your Lord have already fallen upon you. Do you dispute with me about names you and your forefathers have invented, for which God has sent down no authority? Then wait; I too am among those waiting.”
interpretation: The prophet rejects the idols as human inventions rather than divinely authorized objects of worship, and answers his people’s argument with a warning: they should await the consequence of their defiance, just as he awaits God’s judgment.

translation: So We saved him and those with him through mercy from Us, and We wiped out the last remnant of those who denied Our signs; they were not believers.
interpretation: The verse teaches that deliverance comes through God’s mercy, while persistent denial of His signs ultimately leaves no trace of those who reject them.

translation: And to Thamud We sent their brother Salih. He said, “My people, worship Allah; you have no god other than Him. A clear proof has come to you from your Lord. This she-camel of Allah is a sign for you, so let her graze on Allah’s land, and do not harm her, lest a painful punishment seize you.”
interpretation: The she-camel is presented as a clear sign that calls for trust and obedience, not as something to be controlled or mistreated. The warning makes clear that rejecting God’s guidance can be expressed through defying even a specific, unmistakable command—and that such defiance carries consequences.

translation: And remember when He made you successors after ʿĀd and settled you in the land, where you built palaces on its plains and carved homes into the mountains. So remember Allah’s blessings, and do not go about the earth spreading corruption.
interpretation: The people are being reminded that their security, skill, and prosperity are gifts from Allah, not grounds for pride or wrongdoing. True gratitude means using those gifts responsibly and refusing to corrupt the land.

translation: The leaders who were arrogant among his people said to those they had regarded as weak—those among them who believed, “Do you know that Ṣāliḥ has been sent by his Lord?” They replied, “Indeed, we believe in the message with which he was sent.”
interpretation: The believers’ answer shows that their faith rested on the truth of Ṣāliḥ’s message, not on their social standing or the approval of the arrogant leaders. Their confidence contrasts with the leaders’ attempt to make belief seem like a question of status or authority.

translation: Those who were arrogant said, “We indeed reject what you have believed in.”
interpretation: Their pride led them to reject the faith embraced by others, showing how arrogance can keep a person from accepting the truth.

translation: So they hamstrung the she-camel, defiantly disobeyed their Lord’s command, and said, “O Ṣāliḥ, bring us what you threaten us with, if you are truly one of the messengers.”
interpretation: Their challenge reveals that their rejection was not due to lack of evidence: they had witnessed a clear sign, yet arrogance led them to violate God’s command and demand punishment as though it could not reach them.

translation: Then the earthquake seized them, and they lay lifeless in their homes.
interpretation: The verse portrays how swiftly a people’s worldly strength and security can vanish when they persistently reject God’s warning; their homes could not shield them from the consequence of their defiance.

translation: So he turned away from them and said, “My people, I have delivered to you the message of my Lord and sincerely advised you, but you do not love those who give sincere advice.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the painful consequence of rejecting sincere guidance: a messenger has fulfilled his duty, while those who refuse honest counsel bear responsibility for their own choice.

translation: And Lot, when he said to his people, “Do you commit this shameful deed, which no one in all the worlds has ever committed before you?”
interpretation: Lot’s rebuke portrays his people’s conduct as a grave violation of moral bounds, and stresses its unprecedented character as a warning against treating wrongdoing as acceptable merely because a community practices it.

translation: Indeed, you approach men with desire instead of women. Rather, you are a people who exceed all bounds.
interpretation: The verse presents their conduct as a willful crossing of divinely set limits, driven by desire and described as excess rather than as an innocent or accidental act.

translation: And the only reply of his people was to say, “Drive them out of your town; they are people who keep themselves pure.”
interpretation: Their demand to expel Lot and those with him reveals how completely they had rejected his moral counsel: they treated the very people seeking purity as the ones who did not belong among them.

translation: So We saved him and his family, except his wife; she was among those left behind.
interpretation: God rescued Lot and his household, while his wife was excluded because she remained with the people destined for punishment; “those left behind” refers to those who did not escape the destruction.

translation: And We rained down upon them a rain. So look at how the end of the criminals was.
interpretation: The verse calls the listener to reflect on the fate of those who persisted in wrongdoing: divine punishment overtook them, making their outcome a warning against defying God.

translation: And to Midian We sent their brother Shuʿayb. He said, “My people, worship God; you have no god besides Him. Clear proof has come to you from your Lord. So give full measure and weight, do not deprive people of what is rightfully theirs, and do not spread corruption in the land after it has been set right. That is better for you, if you are believers.”
interpretation: Shuʿayb’s call joins worship of God alone with honesty and justice in people’s dealings: faith must be evident in giving others their full due and protecting the good order of society. Corrupt trade and wrongdoing undo what has been set right, so the verse presents ethical conduct not as separate from belief, but as one of its necessary expressions.

translation: Do not lie in wait on every path, threatening people and turning those who believe in Him away from Allah’s way, while seeking to make it crooked. And remember when you were few and He made you many. And see what was the end of the corrupters.
interpretation: Shuʿayb warns his people not to intimidate travelers or obstruct those who follow Allah, nor to distort His way for their own ends. Their growth from a small community to a larger one is a blessing to remember with gratitude, while the fate of earlier corrupters is a warning against persisting in wrongdoing.

translation: If a group among you has believed in what I was sent with, while another group has not believed, then be patient until Allah judges between us; He is the best of judges.
interpretation: When a community is divided over a prophet’s message, the faithful are called to remain steadfast rather than force an immediate outcome, entrusting the final and perfectly just judgment to Allah.

translation: The leaders who were arrogant among his people said, “We will surely drive you, O Shuʿayb, and those who believe with you out of our town, unless you return to our faith.” He said, “Even if we are unwilling?”
interpretation: Shuʿayb’s question exposes the coercion in their demand: they treat belief as something to be imposed by force, while his reply makes clear that returning to their faith is not an option merely because they threaten him and his followers.

translation: We would have surely invented a lie against Allah if we returned to your religion after Allah had rescued us from it. It is not for us to return to it unless Allah, our Lord, wills. Our Lord encompasses all things in knowledge. In Allah we place our trust. Our Lord, judge between us and our people in truth, for You are the best of judges.
interpretation: The speakers’ refusal is grounded not in confidence in their own strength, but in recognizing that faith and steadfastness are gifts from Allah. By acknowledging His will and perfect knowledge, they entrust the outcome of their conflict to His just judgment rather than surrendering to pressure.

translation: The chiefs who disbelieved among his people said, “If you follow Shuʿayb, you will surely be losers.”
interpretation: The disbelieving leaders try to deter their people from accepting Shuʿayb’s message by portraying obedience to him as a path to ruin. Their warning reveals how those invested in the existing order can label moral and spiritual change a loss in order to preserve their influence.

translation: Then the earthquake seized them, and they lay lifeless in their homes.
interpretation: The verse conveys how suddenly and completely divine judgment overtook them: their homes offered no refuge from the consequences of rejecting their messenger.

translation: Those who denied Shuʿayb were as though they had never lived there. Those who denied Shuʿayb were the true losers.
interpretation: Their sudden ruin made it seem as if they had never flourished in their homeland. The verse underscores that their rejection brought them utter loss, while Shuʿayb and the truth he conveyed were vindicated.

translation: So he turned away from them and said, “My people, I have indeed delivered to you the messages of my Lord and sincerely advised you. How, then, could I grieve for a people who reject the truth?”
interpretation: Having faithfully conveyed God’s guidance and counsel, he could only lament that his people had chosen disbelief and brought its consequences upon themselves; their rejection was no failure of his duty.

translation: Whenever We sent a prophet to a town, We afflicted its people with hardship and suffering so that they might humble themselves.
interpretation: The verse portrays hardship as a divine wake-up call: it can unsettle people’s self-reliance and invite them to turn sincerely to God before they become heedless of the prophet’s warning.

translation: Then We replaced hardship with ease until they prospered and said, “Adversity and prosperity also befell our forefathers.” So We seized them suddenly, while they were unaware.
interpretation: The alternation of hardship and ease was a test, but they dismissed it as nothing more than the ordinary turns of fortune. Their complacency left them unprepared for God’s sudden judgment.

translation: If the people of the towns had believed and been mindful of God, We would have opened for them blessings from heaven and earth. But they denied, so We seized them for what they used to earn.
interpretation: The verse presents faith and mindfulness of God as the foundation for a community’s well-being, with blessings that may reach both its spiritual and worldly life. It also warns that persistent denial and wrongdoing carry consequences: a society cannot presume upon prosperity while turning away from the moral responsibility that sustains it.

translation: Do the people of the towns feel secure that Our punishment will come upon them by night while they are asleep?
interpretation: The verse warns against mistaking a period of safety for a guarantee of protection. People should not grow heedless or presume they are beyond accountability; instead, they should turn to God with humility and remain mindful of their conduct.

translation: Or do the people of the towns feel secure that Our punishment will come upon them in the morning while they are occupied in play?
interpretation: This rhetorical question warns against complacency: people cannot assume they are safe from God’s judgment simply because life seems ordinary and they are absorbed in their pursuits.

translation: Did they feel secure from Allah’s plan? None feels secure from Allah’s plan except the people who are lost.
interpretation: The verse warns against complacency in wrongdoing: a person should not assume that past blessings or apparent security mean they are beyond accountability. It calls for humility and vigilance, while trusting in God’s mercy rather than presuming upon it.

translation: Has it not become clear to those who inherit the land after its former people that, if We willed, We could strike them for their sins and seal their hearts, so that they would not hear?
interpretation: Those who follow earlier peoples should take heed from their fate: inheriting their land does not make them safe from divine judgment. If they persist in wrongdoing, they may be punished, and their hearts may become so hardened that they no longer heed the truth.

translation: Those are the towns whose accounts We recount to you. Their messengers had indeed come to them with clear proofs, but they were not going to believe in what they had already denied before. Thus Allah seals the hearts of the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse teaches that persistent rejection of clear guidance can harden a person’s heart: when someone repeatedly turns away from truth, the very capacity to receive it may grow increasingly closed. This sealing is presented as the consequence of their chosen disbelief, not as an excuse for it.

translation: And We found no faithfulness to a covenant in most of them; indeed, We found most of them defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: The verse portrays persistent unfaithfulness: most of those addressed did not honor their commitments to God, and their disregard for those obligations reflected a broader pattern of rebellion against His guidance.

translation: Then, after them, We sent Moses with Our signs to Pharaoh and his chiefs, but they wronged themselves by rejecting them. So see what the end of the corrupters was.
interpretation: The verse presents the rejection of clear divine signs as an act of injustice and corruption, and invites reflection on the fate of those who persist in it: worldly power cannot shield people from the consequences of their wrongdoing.

translation: And Moses said, “O Pharaoh, indeed I am a messenger from the Lord of all worlds.”
interpretation: Moses grounds his mission in God’s authority, not his own, calling Pharaoh to recognize that the message comes from the Lord who rules over all creation.

translation: “It is incumbent upon me to say nothing about Allah except the truth. I have come to you with clear proof from your Lord, so send the Children of Israel with me.”
interpretation: Moses declares that his message is not his own invention but a truth he is bound to convey from Allah, supported by clear evidence. On that authority, he calls on Pharaoh to let the Children of Israel go free.

translation: He said, “If you have brought a sign, then produce it, if you are truthful.”
interpretation: The speaker challenges the claimant to substantiate his message with evidence. The verse presents the demand for a sign as the point at which the claim will be tested.

translation: So he cast down his staff, and behold, it was a clear, unmistakable serpent.
interpretation: The staff’s transformation was a sign of God’s power and a clear proof supporting Moses’ mission, beyond what ordinary human skill could produce.

translation: And he drew out his hand, and behold, it was white to the onlookers.
interpretation: The hand’s striking whiteness was a clear, visible sign of God’s power, confirming Moses’ message to those who witnessed it.

translation: The chiefs among Pharaoh’s people said, “This is indeed a learned magician.”
interpretation: By labeling Moses a magician, Pharaoh’s chiefs sought to discredit the signs he brought and turn people away from recognizing them as evidence of God’s message.

translation: He intends to drive you out of your land, so what do you advise?
interpretation: The speaker portrays the message as a threat to the people’s hold on their homeland and calls the leaders to advise him, framing their response as a matter of political security and power.

translation: They said, “Give him and his brother some time, and send gatherers throughout the cities.”
interpretation: The chiefs urged Pharaoh not to confront Moses and Aaron immediately, but to delay them while agents were sent across the land to assemble those who could challenge Moses’ signs.

translation: They will bring you every skilled magician.
interpretation: The phrase conveys a deliberate effort to gather the most accomplished magicians, setting their human skill against the sign given to Moses.

translation: And the magicians came to Pharaoh, saying, “Will we surely have a reward if we are the victors?”
interpretation: The magicians sought assurance of payment before taking part, showing that their challenge was motivated by worldly reward and Pharaoh’s favor.

translation: He said, “Yes, and you will surely be among those brought near.”
interpretation: Pharaoh promises them special favor and closeness to his court as an inducement to secure their loyalty.

translation: They said, “O Moses, either you cast first, or we will be the ones to cast.”
interpretation: Their words frame the encounter as a contest and give Moses the choice of who acts first, conveying the magicians’ confidence in their own skill.

translation: He said, “Throw!” When they threw, they bewitched the people’s eyes, terrified them, and produced a great magic.
interpretation: The verse portrays the magicians’ power as an impressive deception: they made their display seem real and used fear to sway the crowd. Its force lay in manipulating perception, not in possessing the truth or genuine divine power.

translation: And We revealed to Moses, “Throw down your staff.” Then it devoured what they had fabricated.
interpretation: The staff’s transformation showed that God’s truth overcomes the falsehood people devise, however convincing it may appear.

translation: Thus the truth prevailed, and what they had been doing came to nothing.
interpretation: The verse portrays the decisive defeat of the sorcerers’ deception: when God’s truth became clear, their tricks were exposed as powerless.

translation: So they were defeated there and returned humbled.
interpretation: Their defeat shows that spectacle and arrogance cannot prevail when truth is made clear; those who sought to dominate were instead brought low.

translation: And the magicians fell down in prostration.
interpretation: Their prostration expresses their immediate recognition that Moses’ sign was from God, and their wholehearted submission to Him.

translation: They said, “We believe in the Lord of all worlds.”
interpretation: Their declaration is a public commitment to God alone, acknowledging His sovereignty over all creation rather than submitting to Pharaoh’s claims of power.

translation: The Lord of Moses and Aaron.
interpretation: This phrase affirms that Moses and Aaron are servants of the one Lord who created, sustains, and guides them.

translation: He said, “Have you believed in him before I gave you permission? This is surely a plot you devised in the city to drive its people out of it. You will soon know.”
interpretation: Pharaoh treats faith as something subject to his permission and recasts the magicians’ conviction as a conspiracy. His accusation and threat expose a ruler trying to preserve power by intimidating people whose consciences he cannot control.

translation: I will surely cut off your hands and feet on opposite sides, then I will surely crucify you all.
interpretation: This is a forceful threat of severe punishment, intended to terrorize and break the resolve of those being addressed.

translation: They said, “Indeed, we are returning to our Lord.”
interpretation: Their certainty that they would return to God gave them courage to remain faithful, undeterred by Pharaoh’s threats, because they recognized that his power was temporary and God’s judgment ultimate.

translation: “You resent us only because we believed in the signs of our Lord when they came to us. Our Lord, pour patience upon us and let us die in submission to You.”
interpretation: They answer Pharaoh’s threat by declaring that their faith is the only ground for his hostility. Their prayer asks God to grant them steadfastness under persecution and to preserve them in faithful submission until death.

translation: The chiefs among Pharaoh’s people said, “Will you leave Moses and his people to spread corruption in the land and abandon you and your gods?” He said, “We will kill their sons and spare their women, and we have absolute power over them.”
interpretation: The chiefs frame Moses’ call for faith and freedom as a threat to public order, urging Pharaoh to defend his rule. Pharaoh’s answer exposes the coercion beneath that claim: rather than address the people’s grievances, he threatens their families to preserve his domination.

translation: Moses said to his people, “Seek help from Allah and be patient. Indeed, the earth belongs to Allah; He grants it as inheritance to whomever He wills among His servants. And the ultimate outcome is for the God-conscious.”
interpretation: Moses teaches his people that oppression and hardship do not determine their final fate: they should turn to Allah and remain steadfast, trusting that authority is His to grant and that lasting success belongs to those who are mindful of Him.

translation: They said, “We were oppressed before you came to us and after you came to us.” He said, “Perhaps your Lord will destroy your enemy, make you successors in the land, and then see how you act.”
interpretation: Moses responds to his people’s despair by pointing them toward hope in God’s deliverance, while reminding them that freedom and power bring responsibility: their conduct after being rescued will itself be a test.

translation: We certainly afflicted Pharaoh’s people with years of drought and a scarcity of crops, so that they might take heed.
interpretation: The affliction was a warning meant to turn them from heedlessness toward reflection and recognition of their dependence on God.

translation: When good fortune came to them, they said, “This is ours”; but when hardship struck them, they blamed Moses and those with him. Surely, their ill omen is with Allah, but most of them do not know.
interpretation: The verse exposes the injustice of crediting oneself for blessings while blaming a messenger for hardship. Their misfortune is not caused by Moses; its true measure and consequence lie with Allah, though they fail to recognize this.

translation: They said, “Whatever sign you bring us to bewitch us with, we will never believe you.”
interpretation: Their response reveals a rejection fixed in advance: they dismiss every sign as sorcery so they can avoid accepting the truth, whatever evidence is presented.

translation: So We sent upon them the flood, locusts, lice, frogs, and blood as distinct signs; yet they grew arrogant, for they were a people given to wrongdoing.
interpretation: These unmistakable signs were warnings and evidence of the truth brought by Moses, but the people’s pride and persistent wrongdoing kept them from responding with humility.

translation: When the affliction struck them, they said, “Moses, call upon your Lord for us, by the covenant He has made with you. If you remove this affliction from us, we will surely believe in you and let the Children of Israel go with you.”
interpretation: Their plea shows that, when hardship overwhelmed them, they recognized Moses’ standing with God and promised faith and obedience in return for relief. The verse exposes the weakness of a commitment made under pressure: a promise is not the same as sincere, lasting faith.

translation: When We lifted the affliction from them until a term they were destined to reach, they immediately broke their promise.
interpretation: The verse shows that Pharaoh’s people treated relief as a chance to return to their old ways: once the affliction was lifted, they abandoned the pledge they had made, revealing that their apparent commitment had not been sincere.

translation: So We took retribution on them and drowned them in the sea because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them.
interpretation: The verse presents their destruction as the consequence of persistent rejection: they not only denied the signs that called them to recognize the truth, but also remained heedless of their warning. Their fate thus reflects divine justice toward those who knowingly turn away from guidance.

translation: And We made the people who had been oppressed inherit the eastern and western regions of the land We had blessed. Your Lord’s gracious promise to the Children of Israel was fulfilled because of their patience. And We destroyed what Pharaoh and his people had made and what they had built.
interpretation: The verse presents the reversal of oppression as the fulfillment of God’s promise: the Israelites’ patient endurance was met with deliverance and inheritance, while Pharaoh’s power and the works that sustained it were brought to ruin. Their patience is shown not as passive acceptance of injustice, but as steadfastness through hardship until God’s promised relief came.

translation: We brought the Children of Israel across the sea, and then they came upon a people devoted to their idols. They said, “Moses, make for us a god like the gods they have.” He replied, “You are indeed an ignorant people.”
interpretation: The request reveals how quickly the Israelites’ understanding of God could be obscured by what they saw around them, even after they had witnessed a great deliverance. Moses calls them ignorant because they fail to recognize that worship belongs to God alone and cannot be shaped by imitation of other peoples’ practices.

translation: Indeed, these people’s way is doomed to perish, and all they have been doing is in vain.
interpretation: The verse warns that practices founded on falsehood cannot bring lasting benefit; when they turn people away from God’s guidance, their apparent value ultimately comes to nothing.

translation: He said, “Shall I seek for you a god other than Allah, when He has favored you above all peoples?”
interpretation: Moses reminds his people that the blessings Allah has bestowed on them should deepen their devotion to Him, not lead them to seek another deity.

translation: And [remember] when We rescued you from Pharaoh’s people, who inflicted the worst torment upon you, killing your sons and sparing your women. In that was a tremendous trial from your Lord.
interpretation: The trial lay both in enduring oppression and in being delivered from it: hardship called for patience and steadfastness, while rescue called for gratitude and faithfulness to God.

translation: We appointed for Moses thirty nights, then completed them with ten, so the appointed time with his Lord was forty nights. Moses said to his brother Aaron, “Take my place among my people, set things right, and do not follow the way of those who spread corruption.”
interpretation: The passage presents Moses’ absence as a test of faithful leadership: responsibility for the community continues even when its leader is away. His instructions to Aaron join two duties—actively promoting what is right and refusing to imitate those who cause corruption—showing that stewardship requires both constructive reform and moral resolve.

translation: When Moses came to Our appointed meeting and his Lord spoke to him, he said, “My Lord, show Yourself to me, that I may look upon You.” He said, “You will not see Me, but look at the mountain: if it remains firm in its place, then you will see Me.” When his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble, and Moses fell unconscious. When he recovered, he said, “Glory be to You! I turn to You in repentance, and I am the first of the believers.”
interpretation: The encounter teaches that God’s majesty exceeds the capacity of creation to bear direct vision in this worldly life: even the mountain is shattered by the manifestation, and Moses faints. His response is one of reverence and renewed submission, affirming God’s transcendence and the limits of human perception.

translation: He said, “O Moses, I have chosen you above the people through My messages and through My speaking to you. So hold firmly to what I have given you, and be among the grateful.”
interpretation: Moses’ distinction is presented as a gift from God, not a ground for pride: the proper response to such favor is to hold faithfully to what God has entrusted to him and to show gratitude through obedience.

translation: And We wrote for him on the Tablets an admonition and an explanation of all things: “So take them firmly, and command your people to hold fast to the best of them. I will show you the abode of the defiantly disobedient.”
interpretation: God gave Moses guidance on the Tablets and commanded him to uphold it with resolve and teach his people to follow its finest teachings. The warning that follows makes clear that rejecting this guidance leads to the fate of those who defy God.

translation: I will turn away from My signs those who act arrogantly on earth without right. Even if they see every sign, they will not believe in it; if they see the path of guidance, they will not take it as their way, but if they see the path of error, they will take it as their way. That is because they rejected Our signs and were heedless of them.
interpretation: The verse teaches that persistent arrogance and disregard for divine guidance can harden a person’s heart until even clear signs fail to move them. Their rejection is presented as the cause of their being turned away from the signs: they have become disposed to avoid what is right and follow what leads them astray.

translation: Those who denied Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter—their deeds have come to nothing. Are they repaid for anything other than what they used to do?
interpretation: The verse teaches that denying God’s signs and accountability in the Hereafter undermines the lasting spiritual worth of one’s deeds. The judgment they face is not arbitrary; it corresponds to what they themselves chose and did.

translation: After Moses had gone, his people fashioned from their ornaments a calf—a body that made a lowing sound. Did they not see that it could neither speak to them nor guide them to a way? They took it as an object of worship, and they were wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse exposes the folly of treating something powerless as divine: a sound or impressive appearance cannot make an object worthy of worship. By turning away from God’s guidance toward an idol that could neither communicate nor guide them, the people wronged themselves.

translation: When they were filled with remorse and realized that they had gone astray, they said, “If our Lord does not show us mercy and forgive us, we will surely be among the losers.”
interpretation: Their regret over worshipping the calf led them to recognize that they had strayed and to seek God’s mercy and forgiveness, acknowledging that without them they would be lost.

translation: When Moses returned to his people, angry and grieved, he said, “How badly you have acted in my place after I left! Were you impatient for your Lord’s command?” He cast down the tablets and seized his brother by the head, pulling him toward himself. Aaron said, “Son of my mother, the people overpowered me and nearly killed me. So do not let the enemies gloat over me, and do not count me among the wrongdoing people.”
interpretation: Moses’ anger reflects the gravity of his people’s betrayal of the covenant while he was away. Aaron’s plea makes clear that he had not approved their wrongdoing: he had been overpowered and feared that confronting them further would lead to his death. He asks Moses to distinguish his constrained position from the people’s rebellion and not give their enemies cause to rejoice.

translation: He said, “My Lord, forgive me and my brother, and admit us into Your mercy; You are the Most Merciful of those who show mercy.”
interpretation: This is a humble appeal for Allah’s forgiveness and protection through His mercy, extending the supplication to one’s brother as well. By affirming that Allah is the most merciful, the speaker places his hope in divine compassion above all else.

translation: Indeed, those who took the calf as an object of worship will be overtaken by wrath from their Lord and humiliation in the life of this world. Thus do We recompense those who invent falsehoods.
interpretation: The verse warns that making falsehood about God—whether by worshipping what He has not authorized or attributing to Him what He has not said—brings spiritual and worldly consequences. Its mention of the calf worshippers also makes their fate a warning to anyone who persists in such fabrication.

translation: As for those who did evil deeds, then repented afterward and believed, your Lord, after that, is indeed All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse offers hope to those who have sinned: sincere repentance and faith open the way to God’s forgiveness and mercy, no matter what they did before.

translation: When Moses’ anger had subsided, he took up the tablets. Their inscription contained guidance and mercy for those who stand in awe of their Lord.
interpretation: The verse shows that divine guidance is a mercy received with humility and reverence: those who are mindful of their Lord are most ready to be guided by what He has revealed.

translation: Moses chose seventy men from his people for Our appointed meeting. When the trembling seized them, he said, “My Lord, had You willed, You could have destroyed them before this, and me too. Will You destroy us for what the foolish among us have done? This is only a trial from You: through it You let whom You will go astray and guide whom You will. You are our Protector, so forgive us and have mercy on us; You are the best of those who forgive.”
interpretation: Moses’ plea recognizes that a divine trial can reveal people’s choices and lead some away from guidance while strengthening others in it. He asks God, their true Protector, not to let the wrongdoing of the foolish determine the fate of the whole community, but to answer them with forgiveness and mercy.

translation: And ordain for us good in this world and in the Hereafter; indeed, we have turned to You. He said, “My punishment—I afflict with it whom I will, but My mercy encompasses all things. So I shall decree it for those who are mindful of God, give the prescribed alms, and believe in Our signs.”
interpretation: The verse joins a plea for God’s favor with the assurance that His mercy is vast, while emphasizing the qualities through which people seek its promised share: mindfulness of God, giving zakah, and faith in His signs.

translation: Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, whom they find described in the Torah and the Gospel: he enjoins upon them what is right, forbids them what is wrong, makes wholesome things lawful for them, forbids them what is vile, and relieves them of their burdens and the restraints that were upon them. So those who believe in him, honor and support him, and follow the light sent down with him—they are the ones who will prosper.
interpretation: The verse presents the Prophet’s mission as a restoration of sound moral life: revelation guides people toward what is good while freeing them from burdensome restrictions. Its promise of success is tied not merely to recognizing the message, but to trusting it and standing by its bearer.

translation: Say, “O people, I am the Messenger of Allah to you all—the One to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. There is no god but Him. He gives life and causes death. So believe in Allah and His Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, who believes in Allah and His words, and follow him so that you may be guided.”
interpretation: The Prophet’s message is for all people, and its authority rests on God alone, the sovereign who gives life and death. The verse calls people to recognize that truth, trust the Messenger who faithfully believes in God’s revelation, and follow his guidance as the path toward right direction.

translation: And among the people of Moses is a community that guides by the truth and, by it, acts justly.
interpretation: The verse affirms that Moses’ people were not all alike: among them was a group faithful to God’s guidance, who upheld the truth and judged fairly according to it.

translation: We divided them into twelve tribes, as communities. And We revealed to Moses, when his people asked him for water, “Strike the rock with your staff.” Then twelve springs gushed forth from it; each people knew its drinking place. We shaded them with clouds and sent down for them manna and quails: “Eat of the good things We have provided for you.” They did not wrong Us; rather, they wronged themselves.
interpretation: The verse portrays divine care as both abundant and thoughtfully apportioned: each community is given a known share of water and wholesome provision. Its closing words stress that when people fail to respond rightly to such care, the resulting harm is not injustice from God but a consequence of their own choices.

translation: And when it was said to them, “Dwell in this town and eat from it wherever you wish. Say, ‘Relieve us of our burdens,’ and enter the gate bowing down; We will forgive your sins. We will grant even more to those who do good.”
interpretation: The command joins gratitude for provision with humble repentance: they were to enter without pride and sincerely ask God to remove their sins. God promises forgiveness for obedience and further favor for those who go beyond it in doing good.

translation: But those who did wrong among them changed the words they had been told, so We sent down upon them a punishment from heaven because of their wrongdoing.
interpretation: The verse warns against deliberately distorting a divine command: changing its wording does not evade its meaning or responsibility. It presents punishment as a just consequence of persistent wrongdoing and a warning against treating sacred guidance with contempt.

translation: Ask them about the town by the sea, when they transgressed the Sabbath: their fish came to them visibly on the day of their Sabbath, but on days when they did not observe the Sabbath, they did not come. In this way We tested them because of their disobedience.
interpretation: The people’s test made their disobedience unmistakable: what they desired was brought before them precisely when taking it would violate God’s command. The verse warns that temptation can reveal whether faithfulness is sincere or merely observed when obedience is easy.

translation: And when a group among them said, “Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy or punish with a severe punishment?” They replied, “As an excuse before your Lord, and perhaps they will become mindful.”
interpretation: The admonishers continued not because they expected a certain outcome, but to fulfill their duty before Allah and in hope that the people might still turn away from wrongdoing. The verse thus presents sincere counsel as worthwhile even when its success seems unlikely.

translation: When they disregarded what they had been reminded of, We saved those who forbade evil and seized those who did wrong with a severe punishment because they persisted in disobedience.
interpretation: Their deliberate disregard of the warning exposed the difference between those who actively opposed wrongdoing and those who persisted in it: God rescued the former, while the latter faced punishment for their defiance.

translation: When they arrogantly persisted in what they had been forbidden, We said to them, “Be apes, humiliated.”
interpretation: Their defiant persistence after being warned brought them a humiliating divine punishment, showing the consequence of knowingly rejecting God’s command.

translation: And when your Lord declared that He would surely send against them, until the Day of Resurrection, those who would subject them to grievous torment. Indeed, your Lord is swift in punishment, and He is surely Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: The verse presents the hardships that would befall them through those who dominate and oppress them as a consequence of their persistent wrongdoing, while affirming that God’s swift justice does not close the door to forgiveness and mercy for those who turn back to Him.

translation: We scattered them throughout the land as communities. Among them were the righteous, and among them were those otherwise; and We tested them with blessings and hardships so that they might return.
interpretation: The verse presents both prosperity and adversity as tests that can turn people back toward God. Neither ease nor hardship alone proves a person’s standing; what matters is whether they respond by returning to what is right.

translation: Then successors came after them, inheriting the Scripture. They grasped at the fleeting gains of this world and said, “We will be forgiven.” Yet whenever a similar gain came their way, they took it again. Had they not pledged, through the Scripture, to say nothing about God except the truth—and had they not studied what it contained? The home of the Hereafter is better for those mindful of God. Will you not understand?
interpretation: The verse warns that religious learning does not protect a person who treats forgiveness as a guarantee while knowingly repeating wrongdoing. To know the Scripture is to be accountable to its truth; hope in God’s mercy cannot be used to excuse deliberate self-interest. True understanding is shown by choosing lasting reward over immediate gain.

translation: As for those who hold fast to the Book and establish prayer, indeed, We do not let the reward of those who work for good go to waste.
interpretation: True devotion to revelation is shown not merely by knowing it, but by living by its guidance and sustaining worship. God assures those who do so that their efforts to set things right will be rewarded and never lost.

translation: And [remember] when We raised the mountain above them as though it were a canopy, and they thought it would fall upon them: “Hold firmly to what We have given you, and remember what it contains, so that you may become mindful of God.”
interpretation: The mountain’s looming presence impressed upon the people the gravity of their covenant with God. They were commanded not merely to possess the revelation, but to uphold it earnestly and keep its teachings in mind, so that it might guide them toward reverence and obedience.

translation: And [remember] when your Lord brought forth from the children of Adam, from their descendants, and made them testify about themselves: “Am I not your Lord?” They said, “Yes indeed; we testify”—so that on the Day of Resurrection you would not say, “We were unaware of this.”
interpretation: This verse portrays humanity as having been bound to acknowledge God’s lordship before Him. That testimony grounds human responsibility: people cannot claim that God’s claim over them was wholly unknown, since recognition of the Creator is rooted in the human condition and is reinforced by His signs and messengers.

translation: Or lest you say, “Our forefathers associated others with God before us, and we were descendants after them. Will You then destroy us for what those who followed falsehood did?”
interpretation: The verse rejects the idea that people can excuse their rejection of God by blaming the beliefs of their ancestors. A person’s inherited circumstances do not make falsehood true or remove personal responsibility; God’s establishing of the covenant leaves no one able to claim that ancestral wrongdoing alone determined their fate.

translation: Thus We make the signs clear, so that perhaps they may return.
interpretation: The clarification of God’s signs is an invitation for people to reconsider their course and turn back from error toward faith and obedience.

translation: And relate to them the account of one to whom We gave Our signs, but he cast them off; then Satan pursued him, and he became one of those who went astray.
interpretation: The verse warns that being given knowledge of God’s guidance does not by itself protect a person: if they turn away from it, they become vulnerable to Satan’s influence and may lose their way. True benefit comes from holding fast to the guidance one has been given.

translation: Had We willed, We could have raised him through them, but he clung to the earth and followed his own desire. So his likeness is that of a dog: if you drive it away, it pants; and if you leave it alone, it pants. Such is the likeness of people who deny Our signs. So relate the stories, that they may reflect.
interpretation: The verse warns that knowledge of divine signs does not by itself ennoble a person: when someone gives themselves over to worldly attachment and desire, they forfeit the guidance they were given. The dog’s panting portrays a persistent, unremitting state, suggesting that this person’s craving is not corrected either by warning or by being left alone. The story is recounted so that people may reflect and avoid the same choice.

translation: How evil is the example of the people who denied Our signs and wronged themselves.
interpretation: Those who reject God’s signs bring disgrace and harm upon themselves; their wrongdoing does not diminish the truth of the signs, but reveals the injustice they inflict on their own souls.

translation: Whoever Allah guides is truly guided; and whoever He leaves to stray—those are the losers.
interpretation: True guidance comes from Allah, and those who turn away from it and are left to their misguidance ultimately lose what matters most.

translation: Indeed, We have created for Hell many of the jinn and humankind. They have hearts with which they do not understand, eyes with which they do not see, and ears with which they do not hear. They are like cattle—rather, even more astray. They are the heedless.
interpretation: The verse warns of people who fail to use their capacity for understanding and perception to recognize and follow guidance. Their heedlessness leaves them more astray than animals, which simply follow their nature, while people neglect the truth despite having the faculties to discern it.

translation: To Allah belong the most beautiful names, so call upon Him by them, and leave those who deviate concerning His names. They will be repaid for what they used to do.
interpretation: The verse teaches that God’s names express His perfection and are a proper way to call upon Him. It warns against distorting or misusing those names, while affirming that those who do so will be held accountable for their actions.

translation: And among those We have created is a community that guides by the truth and acts justly by it.
interpretation: The verse teaches that God has placed among people those who uphold truth and let it—not personal desire—guide their judgments and conduct.

translation: As for those who deny Our signs, We will gradually lead them on from where they do not know.
interpretation: This warns that continued denial may be met not with immediate punishment but with a gradual unfolding of consequences. A person may mistake continued ease for approval, while it instead allows their heedlessness and wrongdoing to deepen.

translation: And I will give them respite; indeed, My plan is firm.
interpretation: Their reprieve is not a sign that they have escaped accountability; God’s purpose remains certain, and the time they are given unfolds within His just and unerring plan.

translation: Have they not reflected? Their companion is not afflicted with madness; he is only a clear warner.
interpretation: The verse calls people to think carefully rather than dismiss the Prophet’s message with accusations of madness. His clarity and the seriousness of his warning invite them to consider what he says with reason and fairness.

translation: Have they not reflected on the dominion of the heavens and the earth and all that Allah has created, and on the possibility that their appointed time may have drawn near? In what message, then, after this will they believe?
interpretation: The verse calls people to recognize God’s signs in creation while they still have time to reflect and turn back. Since life is uncertain and its end may be near, rejecting this clear reminder leaves no later message to seek as a substitute.

translation: Whoever Allah leaves to stray has no guide, and He leaves them wandering blindly in their transgression.
interpretation: The verse teaches that when people persist in defiance, no created guide can bring them to faith against Allah’s judgment; they are left confused in the very excess they have chosen.

translation: They ask you about the Hour: “When will it come?” Say, “Its knowledge is only with my Lord. None but He will disclose it at its appointed time. It weighs heavily upon the heavens and the earth; it will not come upon you except suddenly.” They ask you as though you were fully informed about it. Say, “Its knowledge is only with Allah, but most people do not know.”
interpretation: The Hour’s timing belongs to the unseen, a matter God has kept beyond even the Prophet’s knowledge. Its concealment warns against treating ultimate realities as things people can master through speculation; instead, it calls for humility before God and readiness for what may arrive without warning.

translation: Say, “I have no power to bring benefit or harm to myself except as Allah wills. If I knew the unseen, I would have secured much good, and no harm would have touched me. I am only a warner and a bearer of good news to people who believe.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that the Prophet’s authority and knowledge are not independent of Allah: he knows of the unseen only what Allah chooses to reveal. His role is to warn people of the consequences of rejecting guidance and to give glad tidings to those who believe.

translation: He is the One who created you from a single soul and made from it its mate, so that he might find comfort in her. When he was intimate with her, she conceived a light burden and carried it about. Then, when it grew heavy, they both prayed to God, their Lord: “If You grant us a righteous child, we will surely be among the grateful.”
interpretation: The verse points to the shared human origin of spouses and the comfort and closeness intended between them. It also portrays how, as the burden of pregnancy grows, people turn to God in hope and promise gratitude, recognizing that the gift of a righteous child is ultimately in His hands.

translation: When He granted them a righteous child, they ascribed partners to Him in what He had given them. Exalted is Allah above all that they associate with Him.
interpretation: The verse warns against crediting anyone besides Allah with a share in His gifts or in the worship owed to Him. Every blessing comes from Allah alone, so gratitude for a child—or any other gift—must not become devotion to another.

translation: Do they associate with Allah those who create nothing, while they themselves are created?
interpretation: The verse challenges the worship of beings that have no power to create and are themselves dependent on a Creator. It points to Allah alone as worthy of worship.

translation: They cannot help them, nor can they help themselves.
interpretation: The verse exposes the impotence of anything treated as divine when it cannot protect even itself; true divinity belongs only to the One with real power to aid and protect.

translation: If you call them to guidance, they will not follow you. It is all the same to you whether you call them or remain silent.
interpretation: Those invoked besides God are powerless to respond or guide; calling upon them cannot change their incapacity, so placing hope in them is futile.

translation: Indeed, those you call upon besides Allah are servants like you. So call upon them and let them answer you, if you are truthful.
interpretation: Those invoked besides Allah are themselves created and subject to Him; they cannot answer or help those who call upon them. The verse challenges their worshippers to test their claims and recognize that such beings are not divine.

translation: Do they have feet with which to walk, hands with which to grasp, eyes with which to see, or ears with which to hear? Say, “Call upon your partners, then plot against me and give me no respite.”
interpretation: The verse challenges those who worship other than God to recognize that their supposed partners lack even the faculties of living creatures, let alone the power to help or harm. The command to summon them and plot against the Prophet exposes their helplessness and underscores that only God possesses true power.

translation: Indeed, my protector is Allah, who sent down the Book, and He takes care of the righteous.
interpretation: The verse expresses complete reliance on Allah: the One who revealed guidance is also the true guardian of those who follow what is right, so their security and support rest with Him rather than with powerless idols.

translation: Those whom you call upon besides Him cannot help you, nor can they help themselves.
interpretation: The verse exposes the helplessness of anything worshipped besides God: it has no power to protect its devotees and no power to protect itself. It therefore warns against placing trust or worship in what cannot truly provide aid.

translation: If you call them to guidance, they do not hear you; and you see them looking toward you, yet they do not see.
interpretation: The verse exposes the helplessness of the idols invoked besides God: though they appear to face those who call upon them, they cannot hear, understand, or respond. Their appearance of awareness is no substitute for the power to guide or help.

translation: Accept what is readily given, enjoin what is right, and turn away from the ignorant.
interpretation: This verse teaches a measured and gracious way of dealing with others: be accommodating and forgiving, encourage what people recognize as good, and do not let the foolish draw you into needless conflict.

translation: And if a prompting from Satan stirs you, seek refuge in Allah. Surely He is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: When a satanic impulse unsettles you or draws you toward wrongdoing, turn to Allah for protection rather than letting the impulse govern your response. His hearing and knowledge assure you that He hears your plea and knows the struggle within you.

translation: Indeed, those who are mindful of God, when a whisper from Satan touches them, remember, and then they see clearly.
interpretation: The verse teaches that God-consciousness does not mean a person is never troubled by temptation; rather, when temptation clouds judgment, remembering God restores clarity and helps them recognize it for what it is.

translation: And their brothers [the devils] draw them further into error, and they do not desist.
interpretation: Those who persist in wrongdoing are aided by their satanic companions in going deeper into misguidance; the companions keep at it without relenting.

translation: When you do not bring them a sign, they say, “Why have you not devised one?” Say, “I follow only what is revealed to me from my Lord.” This is clear insight from your Lord, and guidance and mercy for people who believe.
interpretation: The Prophet is to convey revelation, not invent signs to satisfy demands. The verse directs attention to the Qur’an itself as the God-given source of insight: for those who believe, it makes the way clear and offers guidance and mercy.

translation: When the Qur’an is recited, listen to it attentively and be silent, so that you may receive mercy.
interpretation: The verse teaches that receiving guidance from the Qur’an calls for attentive, respectful listening rather than distraction; this openness to its message is a means of attaining God’s mercy.

translation: And remember your Lord within yourself, humbly and with awe, without raising your voice, in the mornings and evenings, and do not be among the heedless.
interpretation: The verse teaches that remembrance of God is most fitting when it comes from a humble, attentive heart, expressed quietly rather than ostentatiously. Making this remembrance part of the day’s regular rhythm helps keep the heart awake to God and guards it from heedlessness.

translation: Indeed, those who are with your Lord are not too proud to worship Him. They glorify Him, and to Him they prostrate.
interpretation: Those nearest to God exemplify that true honor does not breed arrogance: nearness to Him is expressed through humble worship, remembrance, and submission.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. They ask you about the spoils. Say, “The spoils belong to Allah and the Messenger. So be mindful of Allah, make peace among yourselves, and obey Allah and His Messenger, if you are believers.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that disputes over spoils should not be settled by personal claims or rivalry: their disposition is governed by Allah’s command and the Messenger’s authority. True faith therefore calls people to fear Allah, repair divisions, and obey divine guidance rather than let worldly gain break their unity.

translation: The believers are only those whose hearts tremble when God is mentioned, whose faith increases when His verses are recited to them, and who place their trust in their Lord.
interpretation: The verse portrays faith as a living inward response rather than a mere claim: awareness of God awakens reverence, engagement with revelation deepens conviction, and reliance on God shapes how a believer faces uncertainty.

translation: Those who establish prayer and spend from what We have provided them.
interpretation: True faith is shown through both devotion to God and generosity toward others, using the blessings one has received responsibly.

translation: Those are the true believers. They will have ranks with their Lord, forgiveness, and a generous provision.
interpretation: True faith is more than a claim: it is reflected in a person’s inward conviction and conduct. God honors such believers with nearness and elevated ranks, forgives their shortcomings, and grants them abundant, gracious provision.

translation: Just as your Lord brought you out of your home for a just purpose, though a group of the believers were reluctant.
interpretation: The verse recalls that the Prophet’s departure from home toward Badr was guided by God’s purpose, even though some believers disliked the prospect. Their reluctance did not mean the course was wrong; it reminds them to trust God’s wisdom when His command leads them into what they find difficult.

translation: They argue with you about the truth after it has become clear, as though they were being driven toward death while watching it approach.
interpretation: The verse portrays the believers’ intense fear and reluctance when faced with the course God had made clear to them: their dread was so great that obeying seemed to them like being led toward death in full view.

translation: And [remember] when Allah promised you that one of the two groups would be yours, and you wished that the group without weapons would be yours. But Allah willed to establish the truth by His words and to cut off the roots of the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse contrasts the believers’ understandable wish for an easier victory with God’s greater purpose: through the encounter with the armed Quraysh, He would make the truth manifest and bring the power arrayed against it to an end. It teaches that divine wisdom may lead believers beyond the outcome they would naturally choose.

translation: So that He may establish the truth and nullify falsehood, even though the guilty detest it.
interpretation: God brings about events to make the truth prevail and falsehood collapse; the opposition of those who persist in wrongdoing cannot overturn that purpose.

translation: When you called upon your Lord for help, He answered you: “I will reinforce you with a thousand angels, following one another.”
interpretation: The verse portrays divine aid as an answer to sincere dependence on God. The promised angels reassured the believers that victory was not theirs to secure by their own strength alone, but came through God’s support.

translation: Allah made it only as good news, and so that your hearts might be reassured by it. Victory comes only from Allah. Surely Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.
interpretation: The glad tidings and signs of support are meant to strengthen believers’ hearts, not to make them believe that victory is guaranteed by any particular means. Its true source is Allah, whose power is absolute and whose decisions accord with wisdom.

translation: When He caused drowsiness to overcome you as reassurance from Him, and sent down water from the sky to purify you with it, remove Satan’s defilement from you, strengthen your hearts, and make your feet firm.
interpretation: The verse portrays God’s care for the believers at a moment of fear: He granted them calm and practical relief, dispelling Satan’s influence and reinforcing their resolve. Their steadiness in the face of danger came not from their own strength alone, but from divine support.

translation: When your Lord revealed to the angels, “I am with you, so strengthen those who believe. I will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve; so strike above the necks and strike every fingertip of them.”
interpretation: In the context of the battle being described, the verse portrays God strengthening the believers through the angels and unsettling their opponents. The command to strike belongs to that specific battle setting; it is not a general instruction for violence.
