translation: That is because they opposed Allah and His Messenger. Whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger—indeed, Allah is severe in punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns that knowingly setting oneself against God’s guidance and the Messenger’s authority is a grave matter, with consequences that should make a person reconsider such defiance.

translation: That is for you, so taste it; and know that the disbelievers will have the punishment of the Fire.
interpretation: The defeat and suffering they face are a foretaste of the greater consequence awaiting those who persist in disbelief: the punishment of the Fire.

translation: O you who believe, when you meet those who disbelieve advancing in battle, do not turn your backs to them.
interpretation: The verse calls believers to remain steadfast and disciplined when facing an advancing enemy in battle, rather than abandoning their position out of fear.

translation: Whoever turns his back to them that day—except as a maneuver for battle or to join another group—has incurred wrath from Allah, and his refuge is Hell. What an evil destination.
interpretation: The verse condemns abandoning the fighting in a way that breaks the ranks and leaves others exposed, while distinguishing it from a purposeful tactical maneuver or regrouping with another force. Its warning is about faithless flight, not every movement away from the enemy.

translation: So it was not you who killed them, but Allah who killed them; and when you threw, it was not you who threw, but Allah who threw—so that He might graciously test the believers. Surely Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: The verse teaches that the believers’ actions were real, yet the decisive force behind their victory came from Allah. Their success was a gracious trial: a sign of divine support that called them to recognize His aid and remain faithful, rather than attribute the outcome to themselves alone.

translation: That is so; and Allah will weaken the schemes of the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse reassures the believers that their opponents’ plans cannot prevail when Allah wills to thwart them; their apparent strength does not place them beyond His power.

translation: If you sought a decisive judgment, the judgment has now come to you. If you desist, that is better for you; but if you return, We will return. Your faction will not benefit you at all, even if it is numerous, for Allah is with the believers.
interpretation: The verse warns those opposing the believers that the outcome they called for has been decided by Allah. They are urged to abandon hostility: strength in numbers cannot shield them if they persist, while Allah’s support is with the believers.

translation: O you who believe, obey Allah and His Messenger, and do not turn away from him while you hear.
interpretation: The verse calls believers to make their hearing of divine guidance an occasion for willing obedience. To turn away while hearing is to reject in practice what one has understood; faith therefore calls for responding to Allah and His Messenger, not merely listening to their commands.

translation: And do not be like those who say, “We hear,” while they do not truly hear.
interpretation: The verse warns against claiming to heed divine guidance while refusing to take it to heart or act upon it. Genuine hearing entails openness and obedience, not merely hearing the words.

translation: Indeed, the worst of creatures in the sight of God are those who are deaf and dumb, who do not use reason.
interpretation: The verse condemns those who turn away from truth: they are “deaf” to guidance and “mute” in acknowledging it, though they have the capacity to understand. Its censure concerns this deliberate refusal to use reason, not physical deafness or inability to speak.

translation: Had Allah known any good in them, He would have made them hear; but even if He had made them hear, they would have turned away, rejecting it.
interpretation: The verse describes people whose unwillingness to accept guidance runs deeper than simply not hearing it: they lack the sincere openness that would let it benefit them, and even if they were made to hear and understand, they would still turn away.

translation: O you who believe, respond to Allah and the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life. And know that Allah comes between a person and their heart, and that to Him you will be gathered.
interpretation: The verse urges believers not to treat divine guidance as something to postpone: its call brings the heart to true life and well-being. The reminder that Allah comes between a person and their heart underscores that human intentions and opportunities are not entirely in our control; hearts can change, and the chance to respond may not remain. Believers should therefore answer sincerely while they are able, mindful that they will ultimately return to Allah.

translation: Beware of a trial that will not afflict only those among you who do wrong; and know that Allah is severe in punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns that when wrongdoing is allowed to spread unchecked, its turmoil can reach the wider community, not only those who caused it. It therefore calls people to resist injustice and remember the seriousness of Allah’s judgment.

translation: And remember when you were few and regarded as weak in the land, fearing that people would seize you; then He gave you refuge, strengthened you with His support, and provided you with good things, so that you might be grateful.
interpretation: The verse teaches believers to remember their former vulnerability not to dwell on hardship, but to recognize that safety, strength, and provision are gifts from God. Such remembrance should deepen their gratitude and keep them from treating their security and blessings as something they achieved alone.

translation: O you who believe, do not betray Allah and the Messenger, nor betray the trusts entrusted to you while you know.
interpretation: The verse warns believers that faith requires integrity: they must honor their obligations to God and His Messenger and safeguard what others entrust to them, rather than knowingly violate those responsibilities.

translation: Know that your wealth and your children are only a trial, and that with Allah is a great reward.
interpretation: Wealth and children can draw a person toward distraction or wrongdoing, so they are a test of whether one remains faithful and acts rightly; the lasting reward with Allah is greater than anything they offer.

translation: O you who believe, if you are mindful of God, He will grant you a criterion, erase your misdeeds, and forgive you. God is the possessor of immense grace.
interpretation: Mindfulness of God gives believers clarity to distinguish truth from falsehood and to choose rightly. This guidance is itself a gift of divine grace, accompanied by forgiveness and the removal of sins.

translation: And [remember] when those who disbelieved plotted against you, to imprison you, kill you, or drive you out. They plotted, and God devised a plan; and God is the best of those who devise plans.
interpretation: The verse teaches that hostile schemes cannot overcome God’s purpose: He protects His messenger and brings the plotters’ plans to nothing. God’s “devising” here means His wise and just counter-plan, not blameworthy deception.

translation: When Our revelations are recited to them, they say, “We have heard. If we wished, we could say something like this. This is nothing but tales of the ancients.”
interpretation: Their words portray a defiant dismissal: rather than engage with the revelation, they boast that they could imitate it and reduce it to old stories, turning their hearing into a way to reject its authority.

translation: And when they said, “O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down stones upon us from the sky, or bring us a painful punishment,”
interpretation: Their words reveal defiant disbelief: instead of sincerely seeking guidance, they treated the truth as a challenge and demanded punishment as proof. The verse exposes the arrogance of preferring destruction over accepting what God had made clear.

translation: But Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness.
interpretation: The verse points to Allah’s mercy in withholding collective punishment when a community has means of protection and return: the Prophet’s presence among them, and their seeking forgiveness. It also holds out repentance as a continuing refuge from punishment.

translation: What reason do they have for Allah not to punish them, when they bar people from the Sacred Mosque and are not its rightful guardians? Its rightful guardians are only the God-conscious, but most of them do not know.
interpretation: Their claim to authority over the Sacred Mosque is hollow: by obstructing worshippers, they act against its sanctity rather than protect it. True guardianship belongs to those mindful of God, not merely to those who control the sanctuary; their ignorance keeps them from recognizing this, and their conduct leaves them with no grounds to presume they are beyond God’s judgment.

translation: Their prayer at the House was nothing but whistling and clapping. So taste the punishment for your disbelief.
interpretation: The verse condemns those who treated worship at the Kaʿbah as a hollow display, replacing reverence and devotion with whistling and clapping. It warns that such mockery and rejection of faith have consequences.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth to turn people away from the way of Allah. They will spend it, then it will become a source of regret for them, and then they will be defeated. And those who disbelieve will be gathered to Hell.
interpretation: The verse teaches that wealth and influence cannot ultimately overcome divine guidance. When they are used to oppose it, they become instruments of loss: apparent power proves temporary, while the moral and spiritual consequences endure.

translation: So that Allah may distinguish the wicked from the good, place the wicked one upon another, heap them all together, and put them in Hell. Those are the losers.
interpretation: The verse portrays divine judgment as a complete separation of moral character: wrongdoing is gathered with its like and brought to its fitting end, while the good are not confused with it. The true loss lies in choosing evil and facing its ultimate consequence.

translation: Say to those who disbelieve: “If they desist, they will be forgiven for what has already passed; but if they return, then the precedent of those who came before has already been set.”
interpretation: The verse offers those who oppose the truth a genuine opportunity to turn back: their past wrongdoing can be forgiven if they desist. But persisting in opposition brings the warning that they will face the same divine judgment that befell earlier peoples who continued in wrongdoing.

translation: Fight them until persecution is ended and devotion is wholly to Allah. But if they desist, then surely Allah sees what they do.
interpretation: The verse presents the fighting as directed toward ending persecution that obstructs people’s faith and worship, not as compulsion in religion. If the opponents desist, the fighting is to cease; Allah knows and sees their actions.

translation: And if they turn away, then know that Allah is your Protector. What an excellent Protector and what an excellent Helper.
interpretation: The verse reassures believers that others’ rejection or withdrawal cannot deprive them of support: they can remain steadfast, entrusting their affairs to Allah, whose protection and help are perfect.

translation: Know that whatever spoils you acquire, one fifth belongs to Allah and the Messenger, and to close relatives, orphans, the needy, and the stranded traveler—if you believe in Allah and in what We sent down to Our servant on the Day of Distinction, the day the two forces met. And Allah has power over all things.
interpretation: The verse establishes that the distribution of war spoils is governed by divine command rather than private claim: a fifth is set aside for the named recipients, including those in need. By connecting this duty to belief in Allah and the revelation given on the Day of Distinction, it presents fair distribution as an expression of faith and obedience.

translation: When you were on the nearer side of the valley, they were on the farther side, and the caravan was below you. Had you agreed to meet, you would have disagreed over the appointed time. But it was so that God might bring about a matter already decreed: that whoever was to perish would perish upon clear evidence, and whoever was to live would live upon clear evidence. Surely God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: The encounter was brought about without either side arranging it, so that the decisive outcome would make the truth unmistakable and leave no room for doubt or excuse. God’s hearing and knowledge encompass both the people’s intentions and what unfolded.

translation: When Allah showed them to you in your dream as few, had He shown them to you as many, you would have lost heart and disputed over the matter. But Allah spared you; surely He knows what is within the hearts.
interpretation: The verse teaches that Allah, in His wisdom, prepared the believers for the encounter by showing the Prophet the opposing force as small, so fear and disagreement would not undermine their resolve. His protection was not merely from outward harm: He knew the doubts and anxieties in their hearts and guided events in a way that sustained their unity.

translation: And when you met, He made them appear few in your eyes and made you appear few in theirs, so that Allah might bring about a matter that was already decreed. And to Allah all affairs return.
interpretation: The contrasting impressions of each side’s strength served Allah’s purpose: they helped bring the encounter about and allowed His decree to unfold, reminding us that events ultimately remain under His control.

translation: O you who believe, when you encounter a force, stand firm and remember God often, so that you may succeed.
interpretation: The verse teaches that steadfastness in moments of trial is strengthened by frequent remembrance of God. Faithful resolve and reliance on Him help believers remain composed and persevere toward success.

translation: Obey Allah and His Messenger, and do not dispute with one another, lest you lose heart and your strength depart. Be patient; indeed, Allah is with the patient.
interpretation: The verse teaches that steadfast obedience and mutual unity preserve a community’s resolve, while internal conflict can weaken its ability to stand firm. Patience in difficulty is sustained by trust in Allah, who supports those who remain steadfast.

translation: And do not be like those who left their homes in arrogance and to show off before people, turning others away from the path of God. God encompasses all that they do.
interpretation: The verse warns that outwardly impressive action is corrupted when driven by pride and the desire for public admiration, especially when it is used to hinder others from following God’s way. Such motives and deeds are never hidden from God, who fully knows and will judge them.

translation: And [remember] when Satan made their deeds seem pleasing to them and said, “No one among the people can overcome you today, and I am your protector.” But when the two armies came into sight of one another, he turned back on his heels and said, “Indeed, I am free of you. I see what you do not see; indeed, I fear Allah. And Allah is severe in punishment.”
interpretation: The verse warns that Satan’s encouragement is deceptive: he fuels pride and false confidence, then abandons those he has misled when they face the consequences. His claim to fear Allah exposes the weakness of his supposed protection; real security lies not in Satan’s promises but in obedience to Allah.

translation: When the hypocrites and those in whose hearts was disease said, “These people have been deluded by their religion.” But whoever places their trust in Allah—indeed, Allah is Mighty, Wise.
interpretation: The verse contrasts the cynicism of those who mistook the believers’ faith and trust in God for delusion with the reality that reliance on Allah is not weakness or folly. Allah’s might and wisdom mean that those who trust Him are not abandoned, even when others misjudge their faith.

translation: If only you could see when the angels take the souls of those who disbelieved, striking their faces and their backs, and saying, “Taste the punishment of the blazing Fire!”
interpretation: The verse depicts the terror and humiliation awaiting those who reject the truth at the moment of death, warning that their denial has grave consequences beyond this life.

translation: That is because of what your own hands have sent ahead, and because Allah is never unjust to His servants.
interpretation: The verse teaches that people are accountable for the consequences of their choices, while God’s judgment is perfectly just: no one is wronged or punished without cause.

translation: Like the people of Pharaoh and those before them, they rejected Allah’s signs, so Allah seized them for their sins. Surely Allah is mighty and severe in punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns that rejecting divine guidance is not without consequence: the fate of earlier peoples shows that no power can shield a community from accountability when it persists in wrongdoing.

translation: That is because God would never change a blessing He had bestowed upon a people until they changed what was within themselves. And God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: God’s favor is not withdrawn arbitrarily: when a people turn away from the qualities and conduct that sustain it, their changed inner state becomes the cause of its loss. God hears what they say and knows what lies within them.

translation: Like the way of Pharaoh’s people and those before them: they denied the signs of their Lord, so We destroyed them for their sins, and We drowned Pharaoh’s people. All of them were wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse presents the fate of earlier peoples as a warning: when people persistently reject clear guidance and act unjustly, their power cannot shield them from the consequences of their choices.

translation: Indeed, the worst of all creatures in the sight of Allah are those who disbelieve, for they will not believe.
interpretation: The verse describes those who persist in rejecting faith as the worst in Allah’s sight because they refuse to accept the truth and remain closed to belief.

translation: Those with whom you made a covenant, then they break their covenant every time, and they do not fear God.
interpretation: The verse condemns persistent betrayal as a sign of moral heedlessness: a covenant is not merely an agreement between people, but a trust for which one is accountable before God.

translation: So, if you encounter them in battle, make their fate a deterrent to those behind them, so that they may take heed.
interpretation: In its context, this addresses hostile groups who repeatedly broke their agreements: confronting them decisively in battle is meant to deter others from renewed aggression and encourage them to reconsider, rather than to authorize violence against people generally.

translation: If you fear betrayal from a people, then openly terminate your treaty with them, so that you stand on equal terms. Surely Allah does not love those who betray.
interpretation: The verse teaches that even when betrayal is feared, one must not answer it with secret treachery. Any pact should be ended openly, giving both sides clear notice and preserving fairness.

translation: Do not let those who disbelieve think that they have escaped; they cannot thwart God.
interpretation: Those who oppose God may appear to evade consequences for a time, but they cannot escape His power or prevent His judgment from reaching them.

translation: Prepare against them whatever strength you can, including warhorses, so that by it you may deter the enemy of God and your enemy, and others besides them whom you do not know; God knows them. Whatever you spend in God’s cause will be repaid to you in full, and you will not be wronged.
interpretation: The verse calls for readiness and strength sufficient to deter aggression, while entrusting to God knowledge of threats beyond human awareness. It also assures believers that resources devoted sincerely to God’s cause are not lost or diminished in their ultimate reward.

translation: If they incline toward peace, then incline toward it, and put your trust in Allah. Surely He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: The verse teaches that when the opposing side shows a willingness to make peace, Muslims should respond to that opening rather than let fear or suspicion prevent reconciliation. Their confidence should rest in Allah, who hears what is said and knows the intentions behind it.

translation: If they intend to deceive you, then Allah is sufficient for you. He is the One who strengthened you with His help and through the believers.
interpretation: The verse reassures the Prophet that no scheme of deception can prevail against him when Allah supports him, as He has already done through divine help and the faithful community.

translation: And He brought their hearts together. If you had spent all that is on earth, you could not have brought their hearts together; but God brought them together. Indeed, He is Almighty, Wise.
interpretation: The unity between believers was not something wealth or human effort alone could secure; it was a gift God placed in their hearts. His power brings about what people cannot achieve, and His wisdom gives that unity its purpose.

translation: O Prophet, Allah is sufficient for you and for the believers who follow you.
interpretation: The verse reassures the Prophet and the believers who stand with him that their strength and security rest in Allah’s support, so they should remain steadfast and trust in Him.

translation: O Prophet, urge the believers to fight. If there are twenty steadfast among you, they will overcome two hundred; and if there are one hundred among you, they will overcome a thousand of those who disbelieve, because they are a people who do not understand.
interpretation: The verse calls the believers to meet the enemy with steadfastness and trust in God, teaching that disciplined resolve can outweigh a much larger force when that force lacks understanding of the truth and the purpose for which the believers stand.

translation: Now Allah has lightened your burden, knowing that there is weakness among you. So if there are among you a hundred who persevere, they will overcome two hundred; and if there are among you a thousand, they will overcome two thousand, by Allah’s permission. And Allah is with those who persevere.
interpretation: The verse acknowledges the believers’ human limits and sets a more attainable measure of steadfastness: their strength lies not in numbers alone, but in perseverance and reliance on Allah. His support accompanies those who remain steadfast.

translation: It is not fitting for a prophet to take captives until he has decisively subdued the enemy in the land. You seek the gains of this world, while Allah wills the Hereafter. Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.
interpretation: The verse corrects the believers for prioritizing ransom and worldly gain before the opposing force had been decisively overcome. It teaches that decisions in conflict must serve the higher purpose of establishing justice and protecting the community, rather than being driven by immediate material benefit; Allah’s wisdom and authority guide what leads ultimately to the Hereafter.

translation: Had it not been for a decree from Allah that had already come to pass, a tremendous punishment would have touched you for what you took.
interpretation: The verse warns that taking ransom from the captives before receiving divine guidance about it was a grave matter; Allah’s prior decree of pardon spared the believers from the punishment they otherwise would have faced.

translation: So eat from what you have taken as spoils, lawful and good, and be mindful of Allah. Surely Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: The verse permits believers to benefit from their lawful share of the spoils, while reminding them that such permission must be exercised with mindfulness of Allah. His forgiveness and mercy offer reassurance that those who turn back to Him are not shut out by past mistakes.

translation: O Prophet, say to those captives in your hands: “If Allah knows goodness in your hearts, He will give you something better than what was taken from you and forgive you.” Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse offers the captives hope: if they are sincere in their hearts and turn toward what is good, Allah can replace their loss with something better and forgive them. Their past does not close the door to divine mercy.

translation: And if they intend to betray you, they have already betrayed Allah before, so He gave you power over them. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: The verse reassures the Prophet that any treachery by the captives cannot escape Allah’s knowledge or overturn His decree. Their earlier rejection and betrayal had already led to their defeat, and Allah’s response is governed by perfect knowledge and wisdom.

translation: Indeed, those who believed, emigrated, and strove with their wealth and their lives in the way of God, and those who gave them shelter and support—these are allies of one another. As for those who believed but did not emigrate, you have no share in their alliance until they emigrate. Yet if they seek your help in matters of religion, you must help them, except against a people with whom you have a treaty. And God sees all that you do.
interpretation: The verse presents the early Muslim community as bound by practical solidarity: those who made the costly move and those who sheltered them shared a responsibility to protect and support one another. It distinguishes that communal bond from the faith of believers who had not emigrated, while still requiring help for them when their religion was under threat. That duty is not permission to violate agreements with other peoples; loyalty and aid remain constrained by justice and treaties, and all such actions are under God’s scrutiny.

translation: Those who disbelieve are allies of one another. If you do not act accordingly, there will be turmoil in the land and great corruption.
interpretation: The verse warns that when believers fail to uphold their mutual bonds of loyalty and support, they leave their community vulnerable to division and oppression, allowing widespread disorder and harm to take hold.

translation: Those who believe, migrate, and strive in the way of God, and those who give them refuge and support—they are the true believers. They will have forgiveness and a noble provision.
interpretation: The verse presents faith as a commitment expressed through sacrifice and solidarity: some believers leave what is familiar and strive for God’s cause, while others make room for them and stand by them. Their different forms of service share the same sincerity, and God’s forgiveness and generous reward are promised to them.

translation: Those who believed afterward, migrated, and struggled alongside you—they are of you. And those related by blood are closer to one another, according to God’s decree. Surely God knows all things.
interpretation: Believers who later joined the community through faith and shared struggle belong fully to it; yet when rights such as inheritance are determined, kinship takes precedence as God has ordained. The verse thus affirms communal solidarity while directing people to observe the divinely established claims of family ties.

translation: A declaration of disavowal from Allah and His Messenger to those among the polytheists with whom you made a treaty.
interpretation: This opens a formal announcement that the existing covenant with the named polytheist groups is being brought to an end; it does not, by itself, refer to every polytheist or erase the obligations of treaties still in force.

translation: So travel freely through the land for four months, but know that you cannot escape Allah, and that Allah will disgrace the disbelievers.
interpretation: The four-month period is a declared reprieve, not a sign that accountability has been waived. Those addressed may move about during it, but they cannot evade God’s judgment, and the verse warns that disbelief will ultimately bring humiliation.

translation: A proclamation from Allah and His Messenger to the people on the day of the Greater Pilgrimage: Allah is free of obligation to the polytheists, and so is His Messenger. If you repent, that is better for you; but if you turn away, then know that you cannot thwart Allah. And give those who disbelieve tidings of a painful punishment.
interpretation: The public declaration makes clear that no pact with the polytheists can shield them from the consequences of rejecting the truth. Yet the door to repentance remains open; turning away does not weaken Allah’s power, but leaves those who persist answerable to Him.

translation: Except for those among the polytheists with whom you made a treaty, who have not failed you in anything or supported anyone against you: fulfill your treaty with them until its term. Indeed, Allah loves those who are mindful of Him.
interpretation: The verse teaches that a treaty must be honored when the other party has kept its commitments and has not joined in hostility. Their religious identity alone does not justify breaking the agreement; keeping it faithfully until its appointed end is an act of God-consciousness.

translation: When the sacred months have passed, then fight the polytheists wherever you encounter them; capture them, besiege them, and lie in wait for them at every place of ambush. But if they repent, establish the prayer, and give the alms, then let them go their way. Surely God is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: This command addresses the hostile polytheist groups in the passage’s setting, after the announcement that certain treaties would end—not polytheists indiscriminately. It authorizes action against those groups in that conflict while making their renunciation of hostility and return to the Muslim community a reason to release them. The surrounding passage also instructs Muslims to grant protection to a polytheist who seeks refuge and escort that person to safety (9:6), underscoring that the command is bounded by its particular circumstances and does not license aggression against everyone who holds another faith.

translation: And if any of the polytheists seeks your protection, grant him protection so that he may hear the words of God; then escort him to a place where he is safe. That is because they are a people who do not know.
interpretation: The verse establishes a duty to protect even a polytheist who asks for refuge: he is to be given a safe opportunity to hear the message and then escorted to safety. His lack of knowledge calls for patient, secure treatment, not harm.

translation: How can the polytheists have a covenant with Allah and His Messenger—except those with whom you made a covenant at the Sacred Mosque? So, as long as they remain faithful to you, remain faithful to them. Indeed, Allah loves those who are mindful of Him.
interpretation: The verse teaches that a covenant is not dismissed merely because it was made with people who differ in faith. Those who honor their agreement are to be treated with fidelity in return; keeping one’s word, rather than acting from hostility or suspicion, is part of God-consciousness.

translation: How can they be trusted? If they gain the upper hand over you, they will honor neither kinship nor covenant. They please you with their words, but their hearts refuse, and most of them are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: The verse warns that pleasing words alone cannot establish trust when a people’s conduct shows they would disregard bonds and agreements if they had the power to do so. True loyalty is shown by honoring commitments, not merely by what is said.

translation: They have sold Allah’s signs for a small price and turned people away from His way. How evil is what they have been doing.
interpretation: The verse condemns those who trade the truth for fleeting worldly gain and then actively hinder others from following it. Their wrongdoing lies not only in rejecting divine guidance for personal benefit, but also in obstructing others from reaching it.

translation: They honor no bond of kinship or covenant with a believer. Those are the transgressors.
interpretation: The verse describes people who disregard both family ties and agreements when dealing with believers, and identifies this betrayal of obligations as transgression.

translation: But if they repent, establish prayer, and give the prescribed charity, then they are your brothers in faith. We make the signs clear for people who know.
interpretation: The verse presents repentance and commitment to worship and charitable obligation as signs of entering the Muslim community, whose members are bound by religious kinship. Its concluding phrase invites people of understanding to recognize the distinction these signs make.

translation: If they break their oaths after making a treaty and attack your religion, then fight the leaders of disbelief. They have no trustworthy oaths, so that they may desist.
interpretation: The verse addresses those who violate a treaty and wage hostility against the Muslim community, directing resistance toward the leaders responsible for that aggression. It is not a general command against people merely for holding a different faith; its stated setting is broken pledges and active attack, with the aim of ending that hostility.

translation: Will you not fight a people who broke their oaths, resolved to expel the Messenger, and were the first to begin hostilities against you? Do you fear them? Allah is more deserving that you fear Him, if you are believers.
interpretation: The verse calls believers not to let fear of those who have violated their pledges and initiated aggression keep them from standing against injustice. Their conduct should be guided by reverence for God rather than fear of their opponents.

translation: Fight them; Allah will punish them by your hands, disgrace them, grant you victory over them, and bring comfort to the hearts of a believing people.
interpretation: Addressed in its context to believers confronting opponents who had broken their covenants and initiated hostility, the verse presents their struggle as a means by which Allah brings justice and relieves the believers’ distress. It is not a command to attack people indiscriminately.

translation: And He will remove the anger from their hearts. Allah accepts the repentance of whomever He wills, and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: Allah can heal the hurt and anger in people’s hearts, while opening the way to repentance according to His knowledge and wisdom. His judgment takes account of what is hidden within people and is never without purpose.

translation: Or did you think you would be left alone before God made evident which of you strive and take none besides God, His Messenger, and the believers as intimate allies? God is fully aware of what you do.
interpretation: The verse teaches that sincere faith is shown through steadfast action and loyalty, especially when believers are tested. God’s knowledge is complete; the trials make clear in people’s lives who truly strives and where their deepest allegiance lies.

translation: It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of God while bearing witness against themselves to disbelief. Their deeds have come to nothing, and they will remain in the Fire.
interpretation: The verse teaches that the outward upkeep of sacred places cannot make up for a rejection of faith: worship and service are meaningful when grounded in sincere belief, not when they coexist with knowingly affirming disbelief.

translation: Only those who believe in Allah and the Last Day, establish prayer, give zakah, and fear none but Allah maintain the mosques of Allah. It is hoped that they will be among the rightly guided.
interpretation: The verse presents care for Allah’s mosques as an expression of sincere faith and obedience, not merely the upkeep of buildings. Such care is rooted in worship and devotion to Allah alone, and those who embody it are promised hope of guidance.

translation: Do you consider providing water to the pilgrims and maintaining the Sacred Mosque equal to believing in Allah and the Last Day and striving in the way of Allah? They are not equal in the sight of Allah. And Allah does not guide wrongdoing people.
interpretation: The verse teaches that honored acts of service, such as caring for pilgrims and the Sacred Mosque, cannot be treated as equivalent to faith in Allah and the Last Day joined with striving sincerely in His cause. It is not a belittling of those acts, but a reminder that their worth is not a substitute for faith and devotion, and that injustice lies in assigning them equal standing before Allah.

translation: Those who believe, emigrate, and strive in the way of Allah with their wealth and their lives are greater in rank in the sight of Allah; they are the ones who truly succeed.
interpretation: The verse teaches that faith is proven through costly, sincere commitment. A person’s standing with Allah is not established by claims alone, but by devotion expressed through sacrifice and action; true success is His approval and the rank He grants.

translation: Their Lord gives them good news of mercy from Him, His approval, and gardens where they will have lasting bliss.
interpretation: The verse portrays salvation as more than reward: it is God’s gracious welcome and approval, with a lasting joy grounded in closeness to Him.

translation: Abiding therein forever; indeed, Allah has with Him a great reward.
interpretation: The verse conveys that Allah’s promised reward is lasting and beyond worldly measure, offering believers a firm hope in what He has prepared.

translation: O you who believe, do not take your fathers and brothers as allies if they prefer disbelief to faith. Whoever among you takes them as allies—those are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse teaches that loyalty to faith must take precedence when close family members oppose it; family ties do not justify siding with them against one’s religious commitment. It warns against misplaced allegiance, rather than forbidding kindness or good treatment toward relatives.

translation: Say, “If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your spouses, your clan, the wealth you have acquired, the trade whose decline you fear, and the homes you cherish are dearer to you than Allah, His Messenger, and striving in His cause, then wait until Allah brings about His command.” And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.
interpretation: The verse calls believers to examine what ultimately governs their loyalties. Family, livelihood, and security are not condemned; the warning is against allowing attachment to them to outweigh devotion to God and commitment to what He requires. Its closing admonition stresses that knowingly choosing disobedience over that commitment places a person beyond divine guidance.

translation: God has already aided you on many occasions, and on the day of Hunayn, when your large numbers impressed you but benefited you nothing, and the earth, vast as it is, seemed constricted around you, then you turned and fled.
interpretation: The verse teaches that victory does not come from numbers or worldly strength alone: when people become self-assured because of their own resources, those resources may fail them, while success ultimately depends on God’s aid.

translation: Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and the believers, and sent down forces that you did not see, and punished those who disbelieved. That is the recompense of the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse teaches that when the believers faced severe trial, their steadiness and eventual support came from Allah: He granted them reassurance and aided them through forces beyond their sight. Those who rejected the truth and persisted in opposition faced the consequence of their actions.

translation: Then, after that, Allah turns in mercy to whoever He wills. And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: Even after grave wrongdoing, the door to repentance remains open: Allah may accept the return of whoever He wills, for His forgiveness and mercy are vast.

translation: O you who believe, the polytheists are indeed impure, so let them not approach the Sacred Mosque after this year. If you fear poverty, Allah will enrich you from His bounty, if He wills. Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: The verse teaches that worship of God must be protected from shirk: here, the polytheists’ impurity is understood as the spiritual impurity of associating partners with God. The restriction concerning the Sacred Mosque may bring concern about lost income, but believers are urged to trust that their provision rests with God, whose knowledge and wisdom govern what He gives and commands.

translation: Fight those among the People of the Book who do not believe in God and the Last Day, who do not forbid what God and His Messenger have forbidden, and who do not follow the religion of truth, until they pay the jizya by hand, while submitting to the authority of the Muslim polity.
interpretation: The verse is traditionally understood as addressing the Muslim community’s political and military dealings with opposing groups in its historical setting, and establishing jizya as a levy paid by non-Muslim People of the Book under Muslim rule. It is not a warrant for individuals to attack people because of their religion; its application concerns public authority and the rules governing conflict and political allegiance.

translation: The Jews say, “Ezra is the son of God,” and the Christians say, “The Messiah is the son of God.” These are merely words they utter; they echo the claims of those who disbelieved before them. May God condemn them—how far they have been turned from the truth!
interpretation: The verse rejects attributing divine sonship to any human being, presenting such claims as human assertions that resemble earlier deviations from belief in God’s oneness. Its closing words express condemnation and wonder at how people can be led away from that truth.

translation: They have taken their scholars and monks as lords besides Allah, and the Messiah, son of Mary, though they were commanded only to worship one God. There is no deity except Him. Glory be to Him, far above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: The verse warns against granting religious authorities or any created being the devotion and ultimate obedience due to God alone. It condemns following people when they presume to alter God’s commands, and it rejects associating the Messiah with God, affirming that worship belongs to the one God alone.

translation: They seek to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah wills only to bring His light to completion, even though the disbelievers detest it.
interpretation: The verse portrays attempts to undermine God’s guidance through denial and hostile words as futile: its truth and completion do not depend on people’s approval, and opposition cannot overturn God’s will.

translation: He is the One who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, so that He may make it prevail over all religion, even though the polytheists dislike it.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the Messenger’s mission is grounded in divine guidance and truth, and that opposition cannot ultimately prevent this message from being made manifest and prevailing over competing ways of worship and belief.

translation: O you who believe, indeed many of the rabbis and monks consume people’s wealth unjustly and turn them away from the way of God. And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of God—give them news of a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns that religious standing does not excuse exploitation: those entrusted with guiding others are especially culpable when they use that trust for wrongful gain or obstruct people from faith. It also challenges the idea that wealth is an end in itself, teaching that possessions carry moral responsibility and must not be withheld from God’s cause and the good of others.

translation: On the Day it is heated in the Fire of Hell and their foreheads, sides, and backs are branded with it, they will be told: “This is what you hoarded for yourselves, so taste what you used to hoard.”
interpretation: The verse warns that wealth hoarded and withheld from its rightful obligations becomes a source of punishment rather than security. The branding dramatizes the painful consequence of treating possessions as an end in themselves instead of using them in obedience to God.

translation: Indeed, the number of months with Allah is twelve months, in Allah’s decree, from the day He created the heavens and the earth. Four of them are sacred. That is the upright way, so do not wrong yourselves during them. And fight the polytheists together as they fight you together; and know that Allah is with those who are mindful of Him.
interpretation: The verse presents the sacred months as part of the order God established, calling people to honor their sanctity and avoid wrongdoing. Its call to fight is framed in terms of a collective response to those who fight collectively, not as permission for unrestrained aggression; the closing reminder places such conduct under the discipline of mindfulness of God.

translation: The postponement [of a sacred month] is only an increase in disbelief. By it, those who disbelieve are led astray: they declare it lawful one year and sacred another year, so as to match the number of months God has made sacred, thereby making lawful what God has forbidden. Their evil deeds have been made alluring to them, and God does not guide the disbelieving people.
interpretation: The verse condemns manipulating religious rules to serve one’s own desires while maintaining the appearance of obedience. Shifting the sanctity of a month did not honor God’s command; it distorted it, showing how self-deception can make wrongdoing seem acceptable and lead people further from guidance.

translation: O you who believe, what is the matter with you that, when you are told, “Go forth in the cause of God,” you cling heavily to the earth? Are you content with the life of this world instead of the Hereafter? The enjoyment of worldly life, compared with the Hereafter, is but little.
interpretation: The verse rebukes believers for letting attachment to comfort and worldly security hold them back when they are called to fulfill a duty in God’s cause. It urges them to weigh temporary worldly enjoyment against the lasting reward of the Hereafter, and not let the lesser outweigh the greater.

translation: If you do not go forth, He will punish you with a painful punishment and replace you with another people; you will not harm Him in the least. And Allah has power over all things.
interpretation: The verse warns that refusing to fulfill a duty in God’s cause brings consequences, yet does not diminish God in any way. God can bring forth others to carry out what is required, for His power is complete and independent of people’s support.

translation: If you do not help him, Allah has already helped him when those who disbelieved drove him out as one of two, when they were in the cave and he said to his companion, “Do not grieve; surely Allah is with us.” Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon him, strengthened him with forces you did not see, and made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest, while the word of Allah is supreme. Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.
interpretation: The verse teaches that the Prophet’s mission did not depend on people’s support: when he appeared most vulnerable, Allah protected and reassured him, and ultimately overturned the strength of his opponents. His companion’s fear is met with the assurance that Allah’s presence and aid are greater than any danger.

translation: Go forth, whether lightly equipped or heavily burdened, and strive in the way of God with your wealth and your lives. That is better for you, if you only knew.
interpretation: The verse urges believers not to let comfort, hardship, or personal circumstance keep them from fulfilling their duty in God’s cause, and to contribute whatever resources and effort they can. Its assurance of what is better rests on the understanding that sincere obedience serves a lasting good beyond immediate ease.

translation: Had there been some immediate gain and an easy journey, they would have followed you. But the distance seemed too great to them. They will swear by God, “Had we been able, we would have gone out with you.” They bring ruin upon themselves, and God knows that they are surely lying.
interpretation: The verse exposes how people may disguise unwillingness with claims of inability: their oath cannot conceal their true motives from God. By choosing deception over sincere commitment, they ultimately harm themselves.

translation: May Allah pardon you! Why did you give them permission before it became clear to you who were truthful and you knew who were lying?
interpretation: The verse gently reproaches the Prophet for granting people permission to stay behind before their sincerity had been made clear. It teaches that claims and excuses should be examined carefully when the welfare of the community is at stake.

translation: Those who believe in Allah and the Last Day do not ask you to excuse them from striving with their wealth and their lives. And Allah knows those who are mindful of Him.
interpretation: True faith and mindfulness of Allah move a person to accept the call to sacrifice rather than seek an excuse to hold back; Allah knows the sincerity behind people’s choices.

translation: It is only those who do not believe in God and the Last Day, whose hearts are filled with doubt, who ask you for permission; they waver in their doubt.
interpretation: The verse portrays their request for permission as an outward sign of inward uncertainty: because faith has not settled firmly in their hearts, they remain hesitant and unable to act with conviction.

translation: Had they intended to set out, they would have made preparations for it. But Allah disliked their setting out, so He held them back, and it was said, “Remain with those who stay behind.”
interpretation: Their failure to prepare revealed that their claim to be willing to join the expedition was not sincere. Their being held back is presented as a consequence of that insincerity: they were left among those who remained behind rather than going forth with the believers.

translation: Had they gone out with you, they would have added nothing to you but disorder, and would have hurried among your ranks, seeking to sow discord among you. And among you are those who would listen to them. Allah knows the wrongdoers.
interpretation: Their absence was a protection for the believers: harmful influence can spread not only through open opposition but also through sowing suspicion and drawing receptive people into it. The closing reminder affirms that Allah knows the true motives behind such conduct, even when they are concealed.

translation: They had already sought to stir up discord before and had turned matters against you, until the truth came and Allah’s command became clear, though they were averse to it.
interpretation: The verse describes those who had previously tried to undermine the Prophet’s mission through discord and schemes. Their efforts could not prevent the truth from becoming evident and Allah’s command from prevailing, even though they disliked its outcome.

translation: Among them is one who says, “Grant me leave, and do not put me to trial.” Surely, they have already fallen into trial; and indeed Hell encompasses the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse exposes the excuse of those who claim that staying behind will protect them from temptation: their refusal itself reveals that they have succumbed to the trial of faith and obedience. Their outward excuse cannot shield them from the consequence of their disbelief.

translation: If good fortune comes to you, it grieves them; but if hardship befalls you, they say, “We took precautions beforehand,” and turn away rejoicing.
interpretation: The verse exposes the hostility and self-interest of those who resent the believers’ success and treat their own escape from hardship as a triumph. Their reactions reveal their true loyalties; the believers should not let such people’s delight or displeasure define the worth of their cause.

translation: Say, “Nothing will befall us except what Allah has decreed for us. He is our Protector, and upon Allah let the believers rely.”
interpretation: The verse teaches believers to face whatever comes with confidence in Allah’s wisdom and care. Their reliance is on Him, not on the expectation that events will always unfold as they wish.

translation: Say, “Do you await for us anything but one of the two good outcomes? We await for you that God afflict you with a punishment from Him or at our hands. So wait; indeed, we too are waiting with you.”
interpretation: The verse expresses the believers’ confidence: whether they prevail or suffer martyrdom, they regard either outcome as good. By contrast, those opposing them have reason to fear punishment from God or defeat at the believers’ hands. The closing words turn their waiting into a challenge, affirming that the believers remain steadfast as events unfold.

translation: Say, “Spend willingly or unwillingly; it will never be accepted from you. Indeed, you have been a defiantly disobedient people.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that an outward act of generosity cannot earn God’s acceptance when it arises from a life of persistent disobedience rather than sincere faith and devotion.

translation: Nothing prevented their contributions from being accepted except that they disbelieved in God and His Messenger; they come to prayer only sluggishly, and they give only unwillingly.
interpretation: The verse teaches that outward religious acts do not, by themselves, make a person’s giving acceptable to God: their worth depends on genuine faith and willing devotion, not on performing them reluctantly or merely as an outward display.

translation: So do not let their wealth or their children impress you. God only intends to punish them through these in the life of this world, and that their souls depart while they are disbelievers.
interpretation: Material prosperity is not necessarily a sign of divine favor. For those who persist in disbelief, wealth and family can become sources of anxiety, attachment, and accountability rather than lasting good; their worldly abundance does not spare them from facing death in that state.

translation: They swear by Allah that they are indeed with you, but they are not of you; rather, they are a people who are afraid.
interpretation: Their oath disguises fear as loyalty: they claim to belong to the believers, yet their allegiance is not sincere, and fear is what drives them to make the claim.

translation: If they could find a refuge, or caves, or somewhere to enter, they would rush toward it headlong.
interpretation: The verse portrays the depth of their reluctance: they would flee from the believers at any opportunity, seeking even the narrowest hiding place rather than remain with them.

translation: Among them are those who criticize you regarding the distribution of alms: if they are given a share, they are pleased; but if they are not given a share, they become resentful.
interpretation: The verse exposes a self-serving attitude: these people measure the Prophet’s fairness by whether they personally benefit, rather than trusting his judgment or seeking what is right. Their approval depends on receiving a share, revealing that their criticism springs from resentment and attachment to worldly gain.

translation: If only they had been content with what Allah and His Messenger had given them, and had said, “Allah is sufficient for us. Allah will grant us from His bounty, and so will His Messenger. Indeed, we turn to Allah with longing.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that believers should meet what Allah provides through His Messenger with contentment and trust, rather than resentment or greed. Their hope rests ultimately in Allah, whose bounty is the source of every provision.

translation: The obligatory alms are only for the poor, the needy, those appointed to administer them, those whose hearts are to be reconciled, the freeing of those in bondage, those burdened by debt, in the cause of God, and the stranded traveler—a duty ordained by God. God is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: The verse makes almsgiving a principled trust rather than an unrestricted act of generosity: its resources are to reach people facing hardship and serve defined communal needs. By assigning this duty to God’s wisdom and knowledge, it calls for distribution that is deliberate, fair, and responsive to people’s circumstances.

translation: Among them are those who hurt the Prophet and say, “He is all ears.” Say, “He listens for your good: he believes in God and trusts the believers, and he is a mercy to those among you who believe.” Those who hurt the Messenger of God will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: The hypocrites use the Prophet’s willingness to listen as a way to mock and discredit him. The reply reframes that quality as a virtue: he listens to what is good, trusts the believers, and is a source of mercy to them. The verse warns that harming God’s Messenger is not a harmless insult but a grave offense with painful consequences.

translation: They swear by Allah to you in order to please you, but Allah and His Messenger are more deserving that they should seek to please Him, if they are believers.
interpretation: The verse exposes the emptiness of seeking people’s approval through oaths while neglecting what truly matters: sincere obedience to Allah and His Messenger. Genuine faith is shown by making Allah’s pleasure the highest priority.

translation: Do they not know that whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger will have the Fire of Hell, abiding therein forever? That is the tremendous disgrace.
interpretation: The verse warns that deliberately defying Allah and His Messenger is a grave act whose consequence is enduring punishment; the ultimate disgrace is being exposed as one who rejected divine guidance.

translation: The hypocrites fear that a sūrah will be sent down revealing what is in their hearts. Say, “Go on mocking; Allah will bring to light what you fear.”
interpretation: Their mockery cannot conceal their inward disbelief or protect them from its exposure: revelation makes clear that Allah knows what they hide, and their fear itself reflects their awareness that their secrets may be revealed.

translation: If you ask them, they will surely say, “We were only engaged in idle talk and joking.” Say, “Was it Allah, His signs, and His Messenger that you were mocking?”
interpretation: The verse makes clear that calling such mockery a joke does not excuse it: ridiculing Allah, His revelations, or His Messenger is a grave matter, not harmless amusement.

translation: Do not make excuses; you have disbelieved after having believed. If We pardon some of you, We will punish others, because they persisted in wrongdoing.
interpretation: The verse warns that mocking or belittling faith is a grave offense that excuses cannot erase. Its mention of pardon and punishment shows that people are judged according to their response: those who truly repent may be forgiven, while those who persist in wrongdoing face punishment.

translation: The hypocrite men and hypocrite women are allies of one another: they urge what is wrong, forbid what is right, and hold back their hands. They have forgotten Allah, so He has left them to be forgotten. Indeed, the hypocrites are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: Their shared hypocrisy binds them together in a way of life that opposes goodness and resists giving. Allah’s “forgetting” them does not mean that He literally forgets; it means He withdraws His care and leaves them to the consequences of the path they chose.

translation: Allah has promised the hypocrite men and women and the disbelievers the Fire of Hell, where they will abide forever. It is sufficient for them; Allah has cursed them, and they will have an enduring punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns that persistent hypocrisy and disbelief are not merely hidden attitudes without consequence: they place a person in opposition to God and lead to lasting punishment. The Fire is described as “sufficient for them” to convey the severity of that recompense, while the curse signifies their exclusion from divine mercy.

translation: Like those before you, they were stronger than you in power and greater in wealth and children. They enjoyed their allotted share, and you have enjoyed your allotted share, just as those before you enjoyed theirs; and you have indulged in falsehood as they indulged. Their deeds have come to nothing in this world and the Hereafter, and they are the losers.
interpretation: The verse warns that worldly strength, wealth, and family are no proof of God’s favor. When people use their worldly share to indulge in heedlessness and follow the same corrupt course as those before them, their deeds lose their worth before God, leaving them with real loss in both this life and the next.

translation: Has the account of those who came before them not reached them—the people of Noah, ʿĀd and Thamūd, the people of Abraham, the people of Midian, and the overturned cities? Their messengers came to them with clear proofs. Allah would never wrong them; rather, they wronged themselves.
interpretation: The verse teaches that divine judgment is never arbitrary: when people persistently reject clear guidance, the harm that follows comes from their own choices, not from injustice on God’s part. The histories of earlier peoples are therefore a warning to heed guidance before wrongdoing brings its consequences.

translation: The believing men and believing women are allies of one another: they enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, establish prayer, give zakat, and obey Allah and His Messenger. Those—Allah will have mercy upon them. Indeed, Allah is Mighty and Wise.
interpretation: Faith creates a bond of mutual care and responsibility: believers support one another in upholding what is right and resisting wrongdoing, while grounding their lives in worship and obedience. The promised mercy is assured by Allah’s power and granted with His wisdom.

translation: Allah has promised the believing men and believing women gardens beneath which rivers flow, where they will abide, and pleasant dwellings in the Gardens of Eternity. But Allah’s pleasure is greater still. That is the supreme triumph.
interpretation: The verse teaches that the highest reward is not merely lasting comfort, but being accepted and beloved by God. The gardens and their blessings are immense, yet Allah’s pleasure surpasses them, making true success a relationship with Him that endures.

translation: O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be firm with them. Their refuge is Hell—what a wretched destination.
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet, calling him to oppose rejection and hypocrisy with firmness. “Strive” is understood in light of the different ways each group was confronted, including armed struggle against hostile disbelievers and admonition and steadfastness in dealing with hypocrites; it is not a general authorization for individuals to use violence.

translation: They swear by Allah that they said nothing, yet they certainly uttered words of disbelief and rejected faith after professing Islam. They also plotted to do what they did not manage to carry out. They resented nothing except that Allah and His Messenger had enriched them from His bounty. So if they repent, that will be better for them; but if they turn away, Allah will punish them with a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter, and they will have no protector or helper on earth.
interpretation: The verse exposes the hypocrisy of denying words and intentions that reveal rejection of faith, despite the blessings they had received. Their grievance against the Messenger is shown to be ingratitude, not a just complaint. Yet the door to repentance remains open; those who persist in turning away will face the consequences without any earthly protector able to save them.

translation: And among them are those who pledged to Allah, “If He grants us from His bounty, we will surely give in charity and be among the righteous.”
interpretation: The verse warns against making devotion conditional on receiving worldly blessings: a promise to do good is a trust before God, not merely words spoken in hope of gain.

translation: But when He gave them of His bounty, they became stingy with it and turned away, refusing.
interpretation: The verse portrays a failure of gratitude and sincerity: once they received the blessing they had hoped for, they withheld what they had pledged and turned away from their commitment.

translation: So He caused hypocrisy to take root in their hearts until the day they meet Him, because they broke their promise to Allah and because they used to lie.
interpretation: The verse warns that repeatedly breaking one’s commitments to Allah and persisting in falsehood can harden the heart into hypocrisy, a condition that remains until one meets Him.

translation: Do they not know that Allah knows their secrets and their private conversations, and that Allah is the Knower of all unseen things?
interpretation: The verse warns that no concealed intention or private counsel is hidden from Allah. People should not imagine that secrecy can shield their words or motives from His knowledge, and should be mindful of Him in both what they reveal and what they conceal.

translation: Those who criticize the believers who give willingly in charity, and those who can offer nothing but their utmost effort, and ridicule them—Allah will requite them for their mockery, and they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns against belittling people for the amount they give: a sincere offering, however small, is not a cause for ridicule. Such contempt reveals the critic’s own moral failure, for God will judge the mockers and hold them accountable.

translation: Ask forgiveness for them, or do not ask forgiveness for them; even if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will never forgive them. That is because they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger, and Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.
interpretation: The verse makes clear that no amount of intercession can overcome the persistent, deliberate rejection of Allah and His Messenger described here. “Seventy times” emphasizes that repeated appeals will not change the outcome while they remain in that state; it is not a limit on seeking forgiveness for others generally.

translation: Those who stayed behind rejoiced at remaining behind the Messenger of Allah. They disliked striving with their wealth and their lives in the way of Allah, and they said, “Do not go forth in the heat.” Say, “The Fire of Hell is far hotter,” if only they understood.
interpretation: Their delight in avoiding hardship reveals how they mistook temporary comfort for true safety. The reply turns their excuse on its head: a believer who understands the lasting consequences of their choices would not let the heat of this world outweigh the far greater heat of Hell.

translation: So let them laugh a little and weep much, as recompense for what they used to earn.
interpretation: This is a stern warning that those who persisted in wrongdoing and turned away from their duty may enjoy only fleeting amusement; their deeds will bring lasting regret and sorrow.

translation: If Allah brings you back to a group of them and they ask your permission to go out, say, “You will never go out with me, nor will you ever fight an enemy alongside me. You were content to stay behind the first time, so remain with those who stay behind.”
interpretation: The verse makes clear that those who deliberately chose to shirk their duty could not simply return when it suited them. Their earlier choice had revealed their lack of commitment, so they were told to remain with those who stayed behind.

translation: And never pray over any of them who dies, nor stand at his grave. They disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger, and died while defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: The verse forbids the Prophet from performing the funeral prayer for, or seeking forgiveness at the grave of, those who persisted in hypocrisy and disbelief until death. It marks a clear distinction between them and believers, and warns against treating outward affiliation as faith when a person dies rejecting Allah and His Messenger.

translation: And do not let their wealth and children impress you. Allah only intends to punish them through them in this worldly life, and that their souls depart while they are disbelievers.
interpretation: Their outward prosperity is not proof of divine favor or a reason for envy; it may instead deepen their worldly burdens and attachment. The verse warns that such possessions offer no lasting benefit if a person dies rejecting faith.

translation: When a surah is revealed commanding, “Believe in Allah and strive alongside His Messenger,” those among them who have means ask you for permission to stay behind, saying, “Leave us to remain with those who stay behind.”
interpretation: Their request exposes a gap between the command of faith and their willingness to act on it: despite having the means to join the Messenger, they choose comfort and avoidance, placing themselves among those who remain behind.

translation: They were content to remain with those who stayed behind, and their hearts were sealed, so they do not understand.
interpretation: Their willingness to stay behind rather than answer the call to duty reflects a settled preference for comfort over responsibility; as a result, they are unable to grasp the truth and seriousness of their choice.

translation: But the Messenger and those who believed with him strove with their wealth and their lives. Those are the ones for whom are the good things, and those are the successful.
interpretation: True success belongs to those whose faith is sincere enough to move them to sacrifice for what is right; their reward and ultimate good come from God, not from worldly comfort or recognition.

translation: Allah has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, where they will abide forever. That is the supreme triumph.
interpretation: The verse teaches that lasting success lies not in temporary worldly gains, but in the enduring reward and favor of God.

translation: Those among the Bedouins who offered excuses came seeking permission, while those who had lied about Allah and His Messenger stayed behind. A painful punishment will befall those among them who disbelieved.
interpretation: The verse distinguishes between those who sought leave with genuine excuses and those whose falsehood kept them from responding faithfully. Their outward explanations do not conceal their true stance from Allah, and those who persisted in disbelief will face a painful punishment.

translation: There is no blame upon the weak, the sick, or those who have nothing to spend, so long as they are sincere toward God and His Messenger. There is no cause for reproach against those who do good; and God is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse teaches that responsibility is measured by a person’s ability: those unable to take part or provide the means are not blameworthy when their loyalty and intentions remain sincere. God does not censure those who do what they can with excellence, and His forgiveness and mercy encompass them.

translation: Nor is there blame upon those who came to you for mounts, and when you said, “I can find nothing on which to carry you,” they turned away, their eyes overflowing with tears out of sorrow that they had nothing to spend.
interpretation: This verse shows that God distinguishes sincere inability from unwillingness: those who longed to join the effort but lacked even the means to travel are not blameworthy. Their grief itself bears witness to the sincerity of their commitment.

translation: The grounds for blame are only against those who ask your permission to stay behind despite being well-off. They were content to remain with those who stayed behind, and God has sealed their hearts, so they do not know.
interpretation: The verse reproaches those who had the means to take part but chose comfort and sought permission to withdraw, willingly placing themselves among those who remained behind. Their settled refusal to act in faith leaves them unable to recognize the seriousness of their choice; the reproach is directed at this deliberate avoidance, not at people with a genuine excuse.

translation: They will make excuses to you when you return to them. Say, “Do not make excuses; we will not believe you. God has already informed us about you. God and His Messenger will see your deeds; then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the seen, and He will tell you what you used to do.”
interpretation: The verse warns that fabricated excuses cannot hide the truth from God or restore trust. What matters is the reality shown by one’s deeds, for those deeds will be fully exposed and judged by God, who knows both what is hidden and what is apparent.

translation: They will swear by Allah to you when you return to them, so that you will turn away from them. So turn away from them; indeed, they are impure, and their refuge is Hell—a recompense for what they used to do.
interpretation: Their oaths are meant to secure your indulgence, but the command to turn away is not an endorsement of their excuses: it marks their moral corruption and leaves them to the consequence they have earned.

translation: They swear to you so that you may be pleased with them. But even if you are pleased with them, Allah is not pleased with a rebellious people.
interpretation: Their oaths may win human approval, but they cannot change the reality of persistent disobedience or secure Allah’s approval. The verse cautions against letting persuasive words outweigh a person’s actions and standing before God.

translation: The Bedouin Arabs are more severe in disbelief and hypocrisy, and more likely not to know the limits of what Allah has sent down to His Messenger. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: The verse speaks of Bedouin communities whose distance from the Prophet and the learning of revelation made disbelief, hypocrisy, and ignorance of religious guidance more likely among them. It is a warning about those circumstances, not a judgment that every Bedouin is alike; Allah knows each person fully and judges with wisdom.

translation: Among the Bedouins are those who regard what they spend as a burden and await misfortune to befall you. May the evil turn of fortune befall them! God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: This describes people who give reluctantly, treating their contributions as a loss, while hoping that hardship will undo the believers. Their hostile wish does not escape God’s knowledge, and the harm they expect for others is instead invoked against them.

translation: Among the Bedouins are those who believe in God and the Last Day, and regard what they spend as a means of nearness to God and of receiving the Messenger’s prayers. Indeed, it is a means of nearness for them. God will admit them into His mercy. Truly, God is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: True faith is shown not merely in belief but in sincere giving for God’s sake and in seeking the Messenger’s prayers. Such deeds draw a person nearer to God, whose mercy and forgiveness are promised to those who turn to Him sincerely.

translation: As for the foremost and first of the Emigrants and the Helpers, and those who followed them in excellence, Allah is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him. He has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, where they will remain forever. That is the supreme triumph.
interpretation: The verse presents the early believers’ sincere faith and the excellence of those who follow their example as a path to God’s pleasure. Their ultimate success lies not merely in receiving Paradise, but in the mutual contentment between them and their Lord.

translation: Among the Bedouins around you are hypocrites, and among the people of Medina are some who have become deeply rooted in hypocrisy. You do not know them, but We know them. We will punish them twice, then they will be returned to a tremendous punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns that hypocrisy can be deeply concealed, even within a community whose members appear familiar and trustworthy. Human beings cannot reliably judge what is hidden in people’s hearts, but God knows their true state and will hold them accountable; the mention of repeated punishment underscores the gravity of knowingly persisting in hypocrisy.

translation: And others have acknowledged their sins: they mingled a good deed with another that was bad. It may be that God will accept their repentance; surely God is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse offers hope to those who honestly face their wrongdoing: a person’s failure does not close the way back to God. By acknowledging their sins and turning toward Him, they may receive His forgiveness and mercy.

translation: Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and help them grow, and pray for them. Indeed, your prayer is a reassurance for them. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: Giving from one’s wealth cleanses the giver of the stain of wrongdoing and nurtures goodness within them. The Prophet’s prayer for them offers comfort and reassurance, while Allah knows the sincerity behind both their repentance and their giving.

translation: Do they not know that Allah is the One who accepts repentance from His servants and receives their charity, and that Allah is the Ever-Accepting of repentance, the Most Merciful?
interpretation: The verse reassures those who turn back to God that sincere repentance is welcomed, and that charity is received by Him—not because He needs it, but as an act of mercy that honors the giver. His acceptance and mercy leave the door open for people to reform and draw near to Him.
