translation: And say, “Act, for Allah will see your deeds, and so will His Messenger and the believers. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the seen, and He will inform you of what you used to do.”
interpretation: The verse calls people to let their faith be reflected in their actions, knowing that their deeds are not without consequence. Whatever others may or may not recognize, every action is ultimately known to Allah, and each person will be held accountable before Him.

translation: And others are deferred until Allah’s command—whether He will punish them or accept their repentance. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: Their fate is left open to Allah’s judgment: they may face punishment or be granted acceptance of their repentance. This teaches that neither outcome should be presumed, for Allah knows their true state and judges with perfect wisdom.

translation: And there are those who established a mosque to cause harm, promote disbelief, divide the believers, and provide a base for one who had previously waged war against Allah and His Messenger. They will surely swear, “We intended nothing but good,” but Allah bears witness that they are indeed liars.
interpretation: The verse warns that a religious institution or claim of good intentions does not make an act righteous when it is used to undermine faith and fracture the community. Its true purpose is known to Allah, regardless of the excuses offered by those behind it.

translation: Never stand in it. A mosque founded upon piety from the very first day is more worthy of your standing in it. There are men in it who love to purify themselves, and Allah loves those who purify themselves.
interpretation: The verse teaches that a place of worship is worthy of devotion when it is grounded in sincere faith and righteousness; outward religious appearance cannot make up for corrupt intentions, while purity of heart and conduct is beloved to Allah.

translation: Is one who founded his building upon mindfulness of God and seeking His pleasure better, or one who founded it on the edge of a crumbling bank, so that it collapsed with him into the Fire of Hell? God does not guide wrongdoing people.
interpretation: The verse teaches that the worth and lasting strength of a person’s religious work depend on its foundation: sincere reverence for God and seeking His approval make it sound, while deception and wrongdoing leave it unstable and ultimately ruinous.

translation: The building they built will continue to be a source of doubt in their hearts unless their hearts are torn apart. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: The mosque they built as a means of deception would keep the hypocrites troubled by doubt and guilt until death; Allah knows their true intentions and judges with wisdom.

translation: Indeed, God has purchased from the believers their lives and their wealth in exchange for Paradise. They fight in God’s cause, and they kill and are killed. This is a true promise binding upon Him in the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur’an. And who is more faithful to His covenant than God? So rejoice in the bargain you have made with Him; that is the supreme triumph.
interpretation: The verse presents wholehearted devotion to God as a covenant: believers entrust their lives and possessions to His cause, and God promises them Paradise in return. Its language of a “purchase” conveys the certainty and honor of that promise, not a license for violence apart from the verse’s stated cause. The reference to earlier scriptures emphasizes that this pledge is part of a consistent divine promise, so the believer’s ultimate success lies in faithfulness to God, confident that He will fulfill His word.

translation: The repentant, the worshippers, the praisers, those who fast, those who bow and prostrate, those who enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and those who observe the limits set by God—give good news to the believers.
interpretation: The verse presents sincere faith as a way of life joining repentance and worship with humility, moral responsibility, and obedience to God; these qualities are the grounds for the promised glad tidings.

translation: It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they are close relatives, after it has become clear to them that they are companions of the Fire.
interpretation: The verse teaches that kinship and affection cannot override what God has made clear: one must not ask forgiveness for those known to have died in rejection of faith. It addresses that specific matter, not the duty to treat relatives with kindness in this life.

translation: Abraham’s asking forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise he had made him. Then, when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God, he disavowed him. Abraham was indeed deeply compassionate and forbearing.
interpretation: Abraham’s earlier prayer arose from compassion and a promise, not from approval of his father’s opposition to God. Once that opposition was clear, he no longer sought forgiveness for him. His gentleness and patience did not mean compromising his devotion to God.

translation: Allah would not lead a people astray after guiding them until He has made clear to them what they should avoid. Indeed, Allah knows all things.
interpretation: God’s guidance is not withdrawn arbitrarily: people are not held to account for failing to avoid something until it has been made clear to them. His complete knowledge ensures that His judgment is just.

translation: Indeed, Allah possesses the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He gives life and causes death, and you have no protector or helper besides Allah.
interpretation: Because all dominion and power belong to Allah, people should place their ultimate trust in Him: no one else can provide the protection or help that only He can grant.

translation: Allah has indeed turned in mercy to the Prophet, the Emigrants, and the Helpers who followed him in the hour of hardship, after the hearts of a group among them had almost wavered. Then He turned to them in mercy. Surely He is Most Kind and Most Merciful to them.
interpretation: The verse teaches that God’s mercy encompassed the Prophet and his companions as they endured severe hardship, including those among them whose resolve nearly faltered. Their wavering did not place them beyond mercy: God renewed His favor toward them, showing His tenderness and compassion toward those who followed him.

translation: And [He also turned in mercy] to the three whose case had been deferred, until the earth, vast as it is, felt constricted to them, and their own souls felt constricted, and they realized that there is no refuge from God except in Him. Then He turned to them so that they might repent. Surely God is the Accepter of repentance, the Merciful.
interpretation: The verse portrays the three who had stayed behind as facing the full weight of their failure and finding no comfort in worldly escape. Their distress brought them to recognize that only God could receive them and restore them. His acceptance of them shows that sincere repentance is met with mercy, even after grave remorse and estrangement.

translation: O you who believe, be mindful of God and be with the truthful.
interpretation: The verse calls believers to let reverence for God shape their choices and to keep company with people whose words and actions are sincere and faithful. Truthfulness is not merely speaking honestly; it is living consistently with one’s commitments to God.

translation: It was not fitting for the people of Medina and the Bedouins around them to remain behind the Messenger of God, or to prefer their own lives to his. That is because no thirst, fatigue, or hunger afflicts them in God’s cause, nor do they take any step that angers the disbelievers, nor do they gain anything from an enemy, but a righteous deed is recorded for them because of it. Surely God does not let the reward of those who do good go to waste.
interpretation: The verse teaches that sincere commitment to a just cause is shown by sharing its burdens rather than choosing personal comfort over collective duty. Even hardships and efforts that may seem small are known to God and counted as good when endured in His cause.

translation: Nor do they spend anything, small or great, nor cross any valley, but it is recorded for them, so that Allah may reward them according to the best of what they used to do.
interpretation: The verse teaches that no sincere effort in Allah’s cause is overlooked: even modest giving and difficult journeys are preserved in the divine record. Allah rewards these deeds with generosity, judging them by their finest qualities rather than letting any act of devotion go to waste.

translation: The believers should not all go forth together. Why should not a group from each community go forth to gain deep understanding of the religion and, when they return to their people, warn them, so that they may be cautious?
interpretation: The verse teaches that a community’s responsibilities must be shared: while some undertake outward duties, others should devote themselves to learning the religion deeply, then return to guide and warn their people. Such knowledge is meant to shape people’s conduct and help them remain mindful of God.

translation: O you who believe, fight those of the disbelievers who are nearest to you, and let them find firmness in you. And know that Allah is with the God-conscious.
interpretation: The verse addresses believers in the setting of armed conflict, directing them to confront the hostile forces posing the most immediate threat and to stand firm rather than falter. Its closing reminder makes clear that such resolve must remain governed by mindfulness of God; divine support is associated with the God-conscious, not with aggression without restraint.

translation: Whenever a surah is revealed, some of them say, “Which of you has this increased in faith?” But as for those who believe, it increases them in faith, and they rejoice.
interpretation: The verse shows that revelation affects people according to the state of their hearts: those who approach it with sincere faith find their conviction strengthened and welcome its guidance, while those who question it dismissively reveal their resistance to it.

translation: But as for those in whose hearts is a disease, it increased them in impurity upon their impurity, and they died as disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse portrays how people inwardly resistant to faith can become further entrenched in corruption when confronted with revelation: rather than responding with humility, they deepen their rejection until they die in disbelief.

translation: Do they not see that they are tested once or twice every year, yet they do not repent, nor do they take heed?
interpretation: The recurring trials are opportunities to recognize their heedlessness, return to God, and learn from what happens; their failure to repent or reflect shows how persistently they ignore those warnings.

translation: Whenever a surah is revealed, some of them look at one another, [as if to ask], “Does anyone see you?” Then they slip away. Allah has turned their hearts away because they are a people who do not understand.
interpretation: The verse portrays people who, rather than attend to revelation, signal to one another and leave in secret. Their turning away expresses a deeper refusal to understand; their hearts are left turned from guidance as a consequence of that persistent evasion.

translation: There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves; your hardship weighs heavily upon him, he is deeply concerned for you, and toward the believers he is compassionate and merciful.
interpretation: The verse presents the Prophet’s authority as inseparable from sincere care: his closeness to the people means he understands their struggles, and his concern is directed toward their well-being rather than his own status. His tenderness toward believers shows that guidance is offered with mercy, not indifference or harshness.

translation: But if they turn away, say, “Allah is sufficient for me. There is no god but Him. In Him I place my trust, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that rejection by others does not diminish the believer’s reliance on Allah: true security rests in His sufficiency and sovereign care, not in people’s acceptance.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the Wise Book.
interpretation: The opening letters remind the reader that the Qur’an’s full reality is known to Allah, while the verses that follow are clear signs of a Book whose wisdom guides people toward truth.

translation: Is it astonishing to people that We have revealed to a man from among them: “Warn mankind, and give glad tidings to those who believe that they have an honored standing with their Lord”? The disbelievers said, “This is indeed an obvious sorcerer.”
interpretation: The verse challenges the assumption that divine guidance could not come through an ordinary human being. God’s message calls people to heed warning and offers believers the promise of an honored reward with Him; the disbelievers’ charge of sorcery reflects their rejection of that message, not a flaw in its source.

translation: Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then established Himself over the Throne. He governs all affairs. No intercessor can intercede except after His permission. That is Allah, your Lord, so worship Him. Will you not then take heed?
interpretation: The verse calls people to worship Allah alone because all creation and governance belong to Him, and even intercession is possible only by His permission. His rule is not shared or independent of anyone else; remembering this should lead people to rely on Him and obey Him.

translation: To Him is the return of you all. Allah’s promise is true: He originates creation and then brings it back, so that He may justly reward those who believe and do righteous deeds. As for those who disbelieve, they will have a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment for their persistent disbelief.
interpretation: The verse presents resurrection as a sure part of divine justice: life is not an end in itself, and people will return to God to be judged. Belief joined with good deeds will be met with a just reward, while rejecting the truth carries consequences.

translation: He is the One who made the sun a radiant light and the moon a light, and appointed for it phases, so that you may know the number of years and how to reckon time. Allah created all this only in truth. He makes the signs clear for people who know.
interpretation: The sun and moon follow an ordered course that serves human life and timekeeping; their precision is also a sign of divine wisdom. Those who reflect on this order can recognize that creation is purposeful, not without meaning.

translation: Indeed, in the alternation of night and day, and in all that Allah has created in the heavens and the earth, are signs for people who are mindful of Him.
interpretation: The changing cycles of night and day and the vast diversity of creation point to Allah’s wisdom and power. Those who are mindful of Him reflect on these signs and let them deepen their awareness of their Creator.

translation: Indeed, those who do not expect to meet Us, are content with the life of this world and find reassurance in it, and are heedless of Our signs—
interpretation: The verse warns that when people live as though they will never answer to God, worldly life can become their ultimate source of satisfaction and security, leaving them inattentive to the signs that call them back to Him.

translation: Those— their abode is the Fire, because of what they used to earn.
interpretation: Their deeds have brought them to this end: the Fire is the consequence of the wrongdoing they persisted in.

translation: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds—their Lord will guide them through their faith. Rivers will flow beneath them in Gardens of Bliss.
interpretation: Their faith is not merely a claim; it becomes a means by which God guides them toward what is right and grants them steadfastness. Their righteous deeds reflect that guidance, and their reward is lasting bliss in the Hereafter.

translation: Their prayer there will be, “Glory be to You, O Allah”; their greeting there will be, “Peace”; and the close of their prayer will be, “Praise be to Allah, Lord of all worlds.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the people of Paradise as living in a state of perfect peace and gratitude: their words naturally glorify Allah, their greetings express security and goodwill, and their praise reflects their recognition of Him as the source and Lord of every blessing.

translation: If Allah were to hasten evil for people as they hasten good, their term would already have been ended. But We leave those who do not expect to meet Us wandering blindly in their defiance.
interpretation: The verse shows that Allah’s restraint is a mercy: He does not immediately bring about the harm people may impulsively call for, since that would bring their lives to an end. Those who deny that they will meet Him are instead given time, yet persist in their rebellion and confusion.

translation: When hardship touches a person, they call upon Us while lying on their side, sitting, or standing. But when We remove their hardship, they carry on as though they had never called upon Us to relieve the hardship that touched them. Thus the deeds of those who exceed all bounds are made appealing to them.
interpretation: The verse warns against turning to God only in moments of need and then forgetting Him once relief comes. Persisting in excess can make such heedlessness seem acceptable, so a person should remember God and remain grateful in ease as well as in hardship.

translation: We destroyed generations before you when they did wrong. Their messengers came to them with clear proofs, yet they would not believe. Thus do We requite the people who persist in wrongdoing.
interpretation: The verse presents the fate of earlier peoples as a warning: divine judgment follows persistent wrongdoing and a deliberate refusal to respond to clear guidance. It calls people to take warning before their choices lead them to the same end.

translation: Then We made you successors on the earth after them, so that We might see how you act.
interpretation: Being entrusted with life on earth after earlier peoples is a test: people’s choices and deeds are made manifest, and they are accountable for how they use that trust. The wording does not imply that God lacks knowledge; rather, it points to deeds being brought into action and judged.

translation: When Our clear verses are recited to them, those who do not expect to meet Us say, “Bring a Qur’an other than this, or change it.” Say, “It is not for me to change it on my own. I follow only what is revealed to me. I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day.”
interpretation: The Prophet’s response makes clear that revelation is not subject to human preference: he is its faithful messenger, not its author, and cannot reshape God’s words to satisfy those who reject them. His fear of disobedience underscores the seriousness of that trust and the accountability owed to God.

translation: Say, “Had Allah willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made it known to you. I had lived among you for a lifetime before this. Will you not then reason?”
interpretation: The Prophet is told to point to his long, familiar life among his people: they had never known him to compose such a message or claim revelation before. They should therefore recognize that the Qur’an came by Allah’s will, not as something he invented.

translation: Who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about Allah or denies His signs? Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed.
interpretation: The verse presents knowingly misrepresenting God or rejecting His signs as grave wrongdoing, and warns that such conduct cannot lead to true or lasting success.

translation: They worship, besides God, what can neither harm nor benefit them, and they say, “These are our intercessors with God.” Say, “Do you inform God of something He does not know in the heavens or on earth?” Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: The verse challenges the claim that idols or other beings have a role as intercessors with God: such a role cannot be asserted without His authority. The rhetorical question underscores that nothing is hidden from God, and that what they claim as partners or intercessors has no basis in divine knowledge or permission.

translation: Mankind was but one community, then they differed. Had it not been for a decree already ordained by your Lord, judgment would have been made between them concerning that over which they differ.
interpretation: Human disagreement does not escape God’s knowledge or authority. By His prior decree, people are given respite in this life; the ultimate judgment over their differences is left to the time and wisdom He has appointed.

translation: They say, “Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord?” Say, “The unseen belongs only to God, so wait; indeed, I am with you among those who wait.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that revelation and its signs are subject to God’s wisdom, not human demands. The Prophet is to entrust what lies beyond human knowledge to God and remain steadfast, while those who reject the message must await God’s decision.

translation: When We let people taste mercy after hardship has touched them, they at once devise plots against Our signs. Say, “Allah is swifter in countering their schemes.” Indeed, Our messengers record what you plot.
interpretation: The verse warns against responding to relief from hardship with defiance and attempts to discredit God’s signs. Human schemes cannot escape God’s judgment, and their deeds are being recorded.

translation: He is the One who enables you to travel on land and at sea. Then, when you are aboard ships and they sail with them in a favorable wind, and they rejoice in it, a violent wind strikes them and waves come upon them from every side, and they realize they are surrounded. They call upon God, sincerely devoting their faith to Him: “If You deliver us from this, we will surely be among the grateful.”
interpretation: The verse portrays how danger can strip away the illusion of self-sufficiency: when every worldly means seems unable to save them, people turn with sincere devotion to God. Their vow also points to a spiritual test—whether the gratitude promised in distress will remain when safety returns.

translation: But when He saves them, they at once transgress in the land without right. O people, your transgression harms only yourselves; it is merely a passing enjoyment of worldly life. Then to Us is your return, and We will inform you of what you used to do.
interpretation: The verse warns that wrongdoing may seem to bring short-term advantage, but its consequences fall back upon those who commit it. Worldly gain is temporary, while every deed will ultimately be brought to account before God.

translation: The life of this world is like water We send down from the sky, with which the plants of the earth mingle, providing food for people and livestock. Then, when the earth has taken on its adornment and is made beautiful, and its people think they have power over it, Our command comes upon it by night or by day, and We make it as if it had been harvested, as though it had not flourished the day before. In this way We make the signs clear for people who reflect.
interpretation: The verse warns against mistaking prosperity and apparent control for permanence. Its sudden reversal calls people to reflect on how fragile worldly security is and to place their trust not in what can vanish, but in God and in what endures beyond this life.

translation: And Allah invites to the Home of Peace and guides whom He wills to a straight path.
interpretation: The verse presents God’s call as an invitation to lasting peace and salvation, while guidance to the straight path comes through His will and wisdom.

translation: For those who do good is the finest reward, and more besides. No dust or humiliation will cover their faces. They are the people of Paradise, where they will remain forever.
interpretation: The verse teaches that God’s generous reward exceeds even the highest hopes of those who do good: they are granted Paradise and an added blessing beyond it. Their faces are spared every trace of shame or distress, and their joy is lasting, not temporary.

translation: As for those who have earned evil deeds, the recompense for an evil deed is its like; humiliation will overwhelm them. They will have no protector against God. It will be as though their faces were covered with layers of pitch-dark night. They are the people of the Fire, where they will remain forever.
interpretation: The verse portrays the fitting consequence of persistent wrongdoing: neither injustice in punishment nor any refuge from God, while the image of faces swallowed by darkness conveys the complete disgrace and despair of those who face that final judgment.

translation: On the Day We gather them all, We will say to those who associated others with God, “Stay where you are—you and your partners.” Then We will separate them, and their partners will say, “You were not worshipping us.”
interpretation: When all are gathered for judgment, those who claimed partners alongside God will be separated from the beings they invoked. The partners will disavow them, exposing that the worshippers’ claims and hopes of intercession had no truth in them.

translation: Allah is sufficient as a witness between us and you; indeed, we were unaware of your worship.
interpretation: Those who were worshiped apart from Allah disavow their worshipers, affirming that they neither knew of nor consented to being worshiped. Allah alone bears witness to the truth between them.

translation: There, every soul will come to know what it sent ahead. They will be returned to Allah, their true Master, and all that they used to fabricate will vanish from them.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, no imagined power or false claim can shield anyone from the reality of their deeds. Only Allah’s rightful authority remains, and each person must face what they themselves have done.

translation: Say, “Who provides for you from the heaven and the earth? Who has control over hearing and sight? Who brings the living out of the dead and the dead out of the living? And who governs all affairs?” They will say, “Allah.” Say, “Will you not then be mindful of Him?”
interpretation: These questions lead people to acknowledge that Allah alone provides, gives life, and governs creation. The verse then calls them to let that recognition shape their worship and conduct, and to be mindful of Him rather than associating others with Him.

translation: That, then, is Allah, your true Lord. What is there beyond the truth except error? How, then, are you turned away?
interpretation: Once Allah is recognized as the ultimate truth and Lord, turning away from Him means abandoning guidance for misguidance. The closing question challenges those who reject this truth to consider what could possibly lead them away from it.

translation: Thus the word of your Lord has come true against those who rebelled: they will not believe.
interpretation: The verse indicates that those who persist in defying God become so entrenched in rejection that they do not accept the truth; their unbelief is the consequence of their sustained rebellion, not a passing failure to understand.

translation: Say, “Is there any of your partners who originates creation and then brings it back?” Say, “Allah originates creation and then brings it back.” How, then, are you turned away?
interpretation: The verse challenges those who worship other than Allah to identify any supposed partner capable of creating life and restoring it after death. Since only Allah has this power, turning to others in worship is a departure from the truth.

translation: Say, “Is there among your partners anyone who guides to the truth?” Say, “Allah guides to the truth. Is one who guides to the truth more worthy of being followed, or one who cannot find the way unless guided? What is the matter with you? How do you judge?”
interpretation: The verse challenges the logic of worshipping beings that have no independent power to guide, while affirming that true guidance comes from Allah. Sound judgment therefore calls for following the One who guides by His own knowledge and authority, not those who themselves depend on guidance.

translation: Most of them follow nothing but conjecture. Surely, conjecture cannot avail against the truth at all. Allah knows what they do.
interpretation: The verse warns that beliefs and judgments grounded only in guesswork cannot stand in place of truth. People may act on such assumptions, but nothing is hidden from Allah, who knows their deeds.

translation: It is not possible for this Qur’an to have been invented apart from Allah. Rather, it confirms what came before it and explains the Scripture; there is no doubt that it is from the Lord of all worlds.
interpretation: The verse presents the Qur’an as neither a human fabrication nor a break from earlier revelation: its confirmation of what came before and its clarification of divine guidance point to its source in the Lord of all worlds.

translation: Or do they say, “He has fabricated it”? Say, “Then bring a surah like it, and call upon whomever you can besides Allah, if you are truthful.”
interpretation: The verse challenges those who accuse the Prophet of inventing the Qur’an to produce even one comparable chapter, seeking whatever help they can. The challenge exposes the weakness of their accusation and points to the Qur’an’s divine origin.

translation: Rather, they have denied what they could not encompass in knowledge, and whose full explanation has not yet come to them. In the same way, those before them denied. So observe what was the end of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse points to the injustice of rejecting revelation before understanding it or seeing its realities unfold. Their lack of knowledge is no sound basis for denial; the fate of earlier rejecters stands as a warning.

translation: Among them are those who believe in it, and among them are those who do not believe in it. Your Lord knows best who the corrupters are.
interpretation: People respond differently to the truth: some accept it, while others reject it. The verse leaves their inner motives and ultimate standing to God, who knows fully who persists in wrongdoing and spreads corruption.

translation: If they reject you, say, “My deeds are mine, and your deeds are yours. You are not accountable for what I do, nor am I accountable for what you do.”
interpretation: The verse teaches a measured response to rejection: disagreement does not justify hostility or coercion, and each person remains responsible for their own choices before God.

translation: Among them are those who listen to you. But can you make the deaf hear, even when they do not understand?
interpretation: The verse teaches that hearing words is not the same as being receptive to their meaning. Those who have closed themselves to understanding cannot be made to accept guidance by the Prophet’s words alone.

translation: And among them are those who look at you. Can you guide the blind, even though they cannot see?
interpretation: Merely seeing the Prophet does not ensure that a person recognizes or accepts the truth. The verse points to a blindness of the heart: when someone is unwilling or unable to perceive guidance, the Prophet cannot compel insight in them.

translation: Indeed, Allah does not wrong people in the least; rather, people wrong themselves.
interpretation: The verse affirms God’s perfect justice: any loss or harm people bring upon themselves is not an injustice from God, but the consequence of their own choices and actions.

translation: And on the Day He gathers them, it will seem as though they had stayed only for an hour of the day, recognizing one another. Those who denied the meeting with God have truly lost, and they were not guided.
interpretation: The verse portrays how brief worldly life will seem when people are gathered for judgment: even their mutual recognition will not lessen the shock of that moment. It warns that denying accountability before God leads to the deepest loss, because such denial leaves a person without true guidance.

translation: Whether We show you some of what We have promised them, or cause you to die, to Us they will return; then Allah is witness to all that they do.
interpretation: The verse reassures the Prophet that the outcome of those who oppose the truth does not depend on his witnessing it in this life: they will return to God, whose complete knowledge and testimony ensure that no deed escapes account.

translation: Every community has a messenger. When their messenger comes, judgment is made between them with justice, and they are not wronged.
interpretation: God’s judgment of every community is based on justice: its people are not held accountable without a messenger having conveyed the message, nor is anyone deprived of what they deserve.

translation: And they say, “When will this promise come to pass, if you are truthful?”
interpretation: Their question is a taunt, not a sincere request for a date: they challenge the messenger to prove the promised outcome, treating its delay as evidence against its truth.

translation: Say, “I have no power to bring myself harm or benefit except as God wills. Every community has an appointed term; when its term arrives, they can neither delay it for an hour nor bring it forward.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that even the Prophet acts only within what God permits and cannot control events independently. The fate and appointed term of every community belong to God, so neither fear nor demands can hasten or postpone what He has decreed.

translation: Say, “Have you considered: if His punishment were to come upon you by night or by day, what part of it would the guilty be eager to hasten?”
interpretation: This is a rebuke to those who mockingly demand that punishment come sooner: when it actually arrives, at any time, they will not wish for even a moment of it to be hastened.

translation: Will you believe in it only when it has come to pass? Now? Yet you used to demand that it be hastened.
interpretation: The verse rebukes those who scoffed at the promised punishment and challenged its arrival: believing only once it has begun would be too late to count as sincere repentance. Their earlier demands that it come sooner are now turned back on them as a final reproach.

translation: Then it will be said to those who did wrong, “Taste the punishment of eternity. Are you being repaid for anything other than what you used to earn?”
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the wrongdoers’ punishment is not arbitrary: it is the just consequence of the deeds they themselves chose and persisted in doing.

translation: They ask you, “Is it true?” Say, “Yes, by my Lord, it is indeed true, and you cannot escape it.”
interpretation: The verse affirms with a solemn oath that what God has promised is certain; no one can evade His judgment or render His decree powerless.

translation: If every soul that had done wrong possessed all that is on earth, it would offer it as ransom. They will conceal their regret when they see the punishment; judgment will be passed between them with justice, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: The verse portrays the utter helplessness of wrongdoing before divine judgment: even everything one might offer cannot undo the consequences of one’s deeds. Their hidden regret reflects remorse that comes too late, while the final judgment remains perfectly just.

translation: Indeed, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. Indeed, Allah’s promise is true, but most of them do not know.
interpretation: Because all creation belongs to Allah, His promise—including the return to Him and the reckoning—is certain. The verse warns that many fail to recognize this truth, not that it is uncertain.

translation: He gives life and causes death, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: All life and death are under God’s authority, and every person will ultimately return to Him to be judged for their deeds.

translation: O mankind, there has come to you an admonition from your Lord, a healing for what is in the hearts, and guidance and mercy for the believers.
interpretation: The verse presents divine revelation as a remedy for inward troubles: it corrects false beliefs, unsettles harmful impulses, and directs people toward what is right. Its guidance and mercy are received by those who believe and respond to it.

translation: Say, “In Allah’s grace and mercy—in that let them rejoice. It is better than all they accumulate.”
interpretation: True joy is found in God’s grace and mercy, especially in the guidance and faith they bring, rather than in possessions or worldly gains, which are lesser and fleeting by comparison.

translation: Say, “Have you considered the provision Allah has sent down for you, then made some of it forbidden and some lawful?” Say, “Has Allah given you permission, or are you inventing lies about Allah?”
interpretation: The verse warns against claiming divine authority for rules Allah has not revealed. People must not arbitrarily declare Allah’s provision forbidden or permissible and then attribute those judgments to Him; doing so is a serious falsehood against God.

translation: What do those who invent lies about Allah think will happen to them on the Day of Resurrection? Allah is indeed full of favor toward people, but most of them are not grateful.
interpretation: The verse warns those who falsely attribute things to Allah that they will face accountability, not escape it. Their deception is especially blameworthy because Allah’s abundant favor gives people reason to recognize the truth and be grateful.

translation: You are not engaged in any matter, nor do you recite any portion of the Qur’an, nor do you perform any deed, but We are witnesses over you as you engage in it. Nothing escapes your Lord—not even the weight of an atom on earth or in heaven, nor anything smaller or greater—except that it is recorded in a clear Book.
interpretation: The verse teaches that God’s knowledge and witnessing encompass every moment and action, including what people may consider insignificant or hidden. This is both a reassurance that no deed is overlooked and a reminder that people are accountable for how they act.

translation: Indeed, the friends of God will have no fear, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This is a promise of spiritual reassurance: those who remain devoted to God need not be overwhelmed by fear of what lies ahead or sorrow over what has passed, because their trust rests in His care and their hope in His lasting reward.

translation: Those who believed and were mindful of God.
interpretation: True faith is reflected in a life shaped by awareness of God—seeking what pleases Him and guarding against what displeases Him.

translation: For them is good news in the life of this world and in the Hereafter. There is no change in the words of Allah. That is the great triumph.
interpretation: The glad tidings promised to those who are faithful and mindful of God are secure: circumstances may change, but Allah’s promise does not. Their true success lies in the lasting good He has promised in this life and the next.

translation: And let not their words grieve you. Indeed, all might and honor belong to Allah. He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: The verse reassures the Prophet that the opposition’s words cannot undermine the truth or diminish Allah’s authority. Allah hears what they say and knows what lies behind it, so their judgment is not the measure of his standing.

translation: Indeed, to Allah belongs everyone in the heavens and everyone on the earth. Those who call upon others besides Allah follow no true partners; they follow only conjecture, and they do nothing but guess.
interpretation: Since all that exists belongs to Allah, attributing divine partners to Him has no sound basis. Such claims arise from conjecture rather than knowledge or proof.

translation: He is the One who made the night for you to rest in and the day bright. Surely in that are signs for people who listen.
interpretation: The ordered alternation of night and day points to God’s wisdom and care: each is made to serve a purpose in human life. These signs become guidance for those who listen attentively and reflect on what they reveal about their Creator.

translation: They say, “Allah has taken a son.” Glory be to Him! He is the Self-Sufficient; to Him belongs all that is in the heavens and the earth. You have no authority for this claim. Do you say about Allah what you do not know?
interpretation: The claim that Allah has a son is incompatible with His complete independence: everything belongs to Him and depends on Him, while He depends on nothing. The verse also warns that speaking about Allah without knowledge or proof is a serious presumption.

translation: Say, “Indeed, those who invent lies about Allah will not succeed.”
interpretation: Those who falsely attribute words or teachings to God may gain temporary advantage, but their deception cannot lead to true or lasting success.

translation: A brief enjoyment in this world; then to Us is their return, and We will make them taste severe punishment for their disbelief.
interpretation: Worldly enjoyment is temporary and cannot shield anyone from the final return to God, where persistent disbelief is met with its just consequence.

translation: And recite to them the account of Noah, when he said to his people, “O my people, if my staying among you and my reminding you of God’s signs has become burdensome to you, then I put my trust in God. So agree upon your course of action, together with your partners; let your plan be clear to you, then carry it out against me without delay.”
interpretation: Noah’s words express unwavering trust in God despite his people’s hostility. By inviting them to unite and act without hesitation, he shows that he does not fear their opposition: his certainty rests not on his own strength, but on God’s protection and the truth of his message.

translation: If you turn away, I have asked you for no reward; my reward is only with Allah, and I have been commanded to be among those who submit to Him.
interpretation: The speaker makes clear that his call is not driven by personal gain: he seeks his reward from Allah alone and is himself bound to submit to Him. This underscores the sincerity of his message and leaves his people responsible for their own response.

translation: But they denied him, so We saved him and those with him in the Ark, made them successors, and drowned those who denied Our signs. So consider what was the end of those who had been warned.
interpretation: The verse presents Noah’s deliverance and his people’s destruction as a warning: rejecting God’s signs does not defeat the truth, and those who disregard clear warnings ultimately face the consequences of their denial.

translation: Then, after him, We sent messengers to their peoples, and they came to them with clear proofs. Yet they would not believe what they had already rejected before. Thus We seal the hearts of those who transgress.
interpretation: The verse portrays how persistent rejection can harden people against later evidence: when they repeatedly turn away from clear signs, their hearts become sealed against faith.

translation: Then, after them, We sent Moses and Aaron to Pharaoh and his chiefs with Our signs, but they acted arrogantly; they were a people given to wrongdoing.
interpretation: Their rejection of Moses and Aaron’s signs is portrayed as a consequence of pride and entrenched wrongdoing: the evidence was presented, but arrogance kept them from accepting it.

translation: When the truth came to them from Us, they said, “This is clearly magic.”
interpretation: Their response shows how people can reject a truth that challenges them by dismissing it as deception, rather than considering its message sincerely.

translation: Moses said, “Do you call the truth, when it has come to you, magic? Yet magicians do not prosper.”
interpretation: Moses rebukes those who dismiss clear divine truth as sorcery: their accusation does not change its reality, and the falsehood they attribute to it cannot ultimately succeed.

translation: They said, “Have you come to us to turn us away from what we found our forefathers following, and to make yourselves the masters in the land? We will not believe you.”
interpretation: They rejected the messengers by attributing their call to a desire for power, treating it as a threat to their inherited ways rather than considering its truth.

translation: And Pharaoh said, “Bring me every skilled magician.”
interpretation: Pharaoh’s command shows him trying to meet Moses’ challenge through the strongest practitioners he could gather, confident that their skill would protect his authority.

translation: When the magicians came, Moses said to them, “Cast whatever you are going to cast.”
interpretation: Moses’ words express confidence in the truth: he does not fear the magicians’ display, but allows it to be brought forth so that its falsehood can be exposed.

translation: When they had thrown, Moses said, “What you have brought is sorcery. God will surely render it null. God does not bring the work of those who spread corruption to completion.”
interpretation: Moses identifies their display as deceptive sorcery and answers it with confidence in God’s power: falsehood may appear impressive for a time, but it cannot ultimately prevail, because God does not grant lasting success to corrupt purposes.

translation: Allah establishes the truth through His words, even if the guilty hate it.
interpretation: God’s truth is not weakened by opposition: He brings it to prevail by His decree and revelation, despite the resistance of those who reject it.

translation: But none believed Moses except a few young people from his people, for fear of Pharaoh and their leaders, lest they persecute them. Pharaoh was indeed arrogant in the land, and he was among those who exceeded all bounds.
interpretation: The verse portrays faith taking root under oppression: only a small group dared believe, because Pharaoh’s power and his officials’ influence made persecution a real danger. Their fear did not mean their belief was insincere; it shows how tyranny can pressure people to conceal or abandon their convictions. Pharaoh’s arrogance and excess explain the atmosphere of intimidation surrounding them.

translation: Moses said, “O my people, if you have believed in Allah, then place your trust in Him, if you are Muslims.”
interpretation: Moses calls his people to make their faith evident through reliance on Allah: surrendering to Him means entrusting their fears and affairs to Him, especially when facing hardship.

translation: So they said, “In Allah we place our trust. Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people.”
interpretation: They entrust themselves to Allah and ask Him not to let the oppressors’ power over them become a cause of further wrongdoing or a test that turns people away from faith.

translation: And save us, by Your mercy, from the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This is a plea for God’s merciful protection, acknowledging that escape from the disbelievers’ harm ultimately depends on His grace.

translation: And We revealed to Moses and his brother: “Prepare houses for your people in Egypt, make your houses places of prayer, establish the prayer, and give the believers good tidings.”
interpretation: In the face of Pharaoh’s oppression, the believers were to make their homes centers of worship and spiritual solidarity, sustaining their trust in God through prayer. The promise of good tidings reassures them that their hardship would not last forever.

translation: Moses said, “Our Lord, You have bestowed on Pharaoh and his chiefs adornment and wealth in the life of this world, our Lord, so that they lead people away from Your path. Our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts, so that they will not believe until they see the painful punishment.”
interpretation: Moses’ prayer shows that worldly power and riches can become instruments of defiance when their owners use them to turn people from God’s way. In asking that Pharaoh and his chiefs be deprived of these means and remain steadfast in their refusal until punishment came, Moses invokes a just consequence for their persistent opposition—not a denial that they had been given the opportunity to believe.

translation: He said, “Your supplication has been answered. So remain steadfast, and do not follow the way of those who do not know.”
interpretation: God’s assurance calls Moses and Aaron to keep faith and act with steadfastness while awaiting the answer to their prayer, rather than letting impatience or ignorance turn them from the right course.

translation: We brought the Children of Israel across the sea, and Pharaoh and his soldiers pursued them in transgression and hostility. Then, when drowning overtook him, he said, “I believe that there is no god except the One in whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am among those who submit.”
interpretation: Pharaoh’s declaration came only when he was confronted with certain death, not through sincere faith freely embraced. The verse thus shows that a confession made under the undeniable force of punishment, when the opportunity for genuine repentance has passed, does not amount to the saving submission he claims.

translation: “Now? Yet you had disobeyed before and been among the corrupters.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that a last-minute profession of faith, made only when punishment has become undeniable, does not erase a life of deliberate defiance; sincere turning to God must come before one is overtaken by death or judgment.

translation: So today We will preserve your body, so that you may be a sign for those who come after you. Yet many people are heedless of Our signs.
interpretation: The verse presents the ruler’s bodily preservation as a warning to later generations: worldly power cannot save someone who persists in defying God, and the signs that should prompt reflection are often ignored.

translation: We settled the Children of Israel in a goodly place and provided them with wholesome things. They did not differ until knowledge came to them. Your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ.
interpretation: The verse teaches that disagreement can persist even after guidance has become clear: knowledge alone does not ensure people will follow the truth. Their disputes and the motives behind them are ultimately known to God, whose judgment on the Day of Resurrection will distinguish truth from falsehood with perfect justice.

translation: If you are in doubt about what We have sent down to you, then ask those who have been reading the Scripture before you. The truth has indeed come to you from your Lord, so do not be among those who doubt.
interpretation: The conditional address serves to affirm the certainty of the revelation, not to imply that the Prophet actually doubted. The earlier Scriptures bear witness to the same divine truth, while the verse calls for steadfastness in what has been revealed.

translation: And never be among those who deny Allah’s signs, lest you be among the losers.
interpretation: The verse stresses the seriousness of rejecting divine guidance: a person’s success depends on remaining steadfast in faith and not joining those who turn away from Allah’s signs.

translation: Indeed, those against whom your Lord’s decree has come to pass will not believe.
interpretation: The verse describes people whose persistent rejection has brought them under God’s settled decree: they remain closed to faith. It presents their disbelief as the consequence of that rejection, not as a license to dismiss others as beyond guidance.

translation: Even if every sign were to come to them, they would not believe until they saw the painful punishment.
interpretation: This describes the resolve of those who persist in rejecting the truth: no sign will persuade them while they remain obstinate, and they will only acknowledge it when the punishment becomes undeniable.

translation: Why was there no town that believed and benefited from its belief, except the people of Jonah? When they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world and let them enjoy life for a time.
interpretation: The people of Jonah are presented as an exception: they turned to faith in time, and God accepted their repentance and lifted the threatened punishment. Their story shows that sincere belief and return to God can bring mercy before judgment overtakes a people.

translation: Had your Lord willed, everyone on earth would have believed—all of them together. Will you then compel people to become believers?
interpretation: The verse teaches that faith cannot be imposed: God could have made everyone believe, but has allowed people to choose. The Prophet’s role is to convey the message, not to force belief upon anyone.

translation: No soul can believe except by Allah’s permission; and He places defilement upon those who do not use reason.
interpretation: True faith comes about only through Allah’s enabling, while those who refuse to use their reason become burdened with spiritual defilement and are deprived of guidance.

translation: Say, “Look at what is in the heavens and the earth.” Yet signs and warnings do not benefit people who do not believe.
interpretation: The verse calls people to reflect on the signs of God throughout creation. Such signs can guide a receptive heart, but they cannot benefit someone who refuses to believe and heed the warning.

translation: Are they waiting for anything but the like of the days that befell those who passed away before them? Say, “Then wait; I too am waiting with you.”
interpretation: Those who reject the truth should not imagine that they will escape the consequences faced by earlier rejecters. The Prophet is told to meet their defiance with patience and certainty, leaving the outcome to God’s judgment.

translation: Then We save Our messengers and those who believe. Thus it is Our binding promise to save the believers.
interpretation: God affirms that He delivers His messengers and the believers who stand with them from the punishment that overtakes those who persist in wrongdoing. Their rescue rests on God’s faithful promise, even when its timing and form are determined by His wisdom.

translation: Say, “O people, if you are in doubt about my religion, then I do not worship those you worship besides Allah. Rather, I worship Allah, who takes your souls, and I have been commanded to be among the believers.”
interpretation: The verse calls for unwavering devotion to Allah alone: the Prophet rejects every object of worship besides Him and directs worship to the One who holds people’s lives in His power. His command to be among the believers shows that this devotion is grounded in faithful obedience, not uncertainty or compromise.

translation: And [I was commanded], “Set your face steadfastly toward the religion, inclining to the truth, and do not be among those who associate others with God.”
interpretation: The verse calls for wholehearted devotion to the true religion, turning sincerely toward God alone and away from every form of associating partners with Him.

translation: And do not call upon anything besides Allah that can neither benefit you nor harm you. If you do, then you will be among the wrongdoers.
interpretation: Worship and supplication belong to Allah alone: turning to anything powerless to bring benefit or avert harm misplaces devotion and wrongs one’s own soul.

translation: If Allah touches you with harm, none can remove it except Him; and if He wills good for you, none can turn back His favor. He grants it to whomever He wills among His servants, and He is the All-Forgiving, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse teaches that a believer’s deepest reliance should be on Allah, since no created power can finally undo what He decrees or prevent the good He bestows. This calls for patience in hardship and gratitude and humility in times of ease, while Allah’s forgiveness and mercy remain a source of hope.

translation: Say, “O mankind, the truth has come to you from your Lord. Whoever is guided is guided only for their own benefit, and whoever goes astray does so only to their own detriment. I am not a guardian over you.”
interpretation: The verse affirms that divine guidance has been made clear, while each person bears the consequences of accepting or rejecting it. The Messenger’s role is to convey the truth, not to compel people to follow it.

translation: Follow what is revealed to you, and be patient until Allah gives judgment; He is the best of judges.
interpretation: The verse calls the Prophet to remain faithful to divine guidance and steadfast through hardship, leaving the timing and outcome to Allah, whose judgment is perfectly just and wise.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Alif Lām Rā. A Book whose verses have been made firm and then explained in detail, from One who is All-Wise, All-Aware.
interpretation: The verse presents the Qur’an as revelation whose teachings are sound and complete, and whose guidance is made clear by the One whose wisdom and knowledge encompass all things. The opening letters, Alif Lām Rā, are among the Qur’anic initials whose ultimate meaning is known to Allah.

translation: Worship none but Allah. Indeed, I am to you, from Him, a warner and a bearer of good tidings.
interpretation: The message calls people to devote their worship solely to Allah. The messenger conveys this call with both warning of the consequences of rejecting it and glad tidings for those who respond faithfully.

translation: Seek your Lord’s forgiveness, then turn back to Him in repentance. He will grant you a good life until an appointed time and give each person of merit their due reward. But if you turn away, I fear for you the punishment of a tremendous Day.
interpretation: The verse presents repentance as more than regret: it is a return to God that brings well-being in this life and reward fitting each person’s deeds. Turning away from that return leaves a person exposed to the reckoning of the Day of Judgment.

translation: To Allah is your return, and He has power over all things.
interpretation: Every person will ultimately return to Allah, whose complete power means that nothing can escape His authority or the judgment that follows.

translation: Indeed, they fold up their breasts, seeking to conceal themselves from Him. Indeed, when they cover themselves with their garments, He knows what they conceal and what they disclose. Surely He knows what lies within the breasts.
interpretation: The verse exposes the futility of imagining that inward thoughts can be hidden from God: no outward concealment can place a person beyond His knowledge, which encompasses both what is shown and the intentions held deep within.

translation: There is no creature on earth whose provision is not upon Allah. He knows where it lives and where it is entrusted, and all is recorded in a clear Book.
interpretation: The verse teaches that no creature lies beyond Allah’s care or knowledge: even what is hidden about its provision and its places of dwelling is known to Him and recorded. This invites trust in Allah without implying that one should abandon the means through which provision is sought.

translation: He is the One who created the heavens and the earth in six days, and His Throne was upon the water, in order to test you as to which of you is best in deeds. And if you say, “You will indeed be raised after death,” those who disbelieve will surely say, “This is nothing but manifest magic.”
interpretation: The verse presents creation as purposeful rather than aimless: human life is a moral trial in which the quality of one’s deeds matters. It also exposes how disbelief can resist the prospect of accountability by dismissing the promise of resurrection as deception.

translation: And if We delay the punishment from them until an appointed time, they will surely say, “What is holding it back?” Indeed, when it comes upon them, it will not be turned away from them, and what they used to mock will encompass them.
interpretation: The delay of punishment is not evidence that it will never come. Rather, those who mock the warning mistake postponement for safety; when the appointed time arrives, they will find that the punishment cannot be averted.

translation: If We let a person taste mercy from Us and then take it away from him, he is indeed despairing and ungrateful.
interpretation: The verse warns against letting hardship erase one’s awareness of mercy already received. It portrays despair and ingratitude as responses that arise when a person judges life only by what is present now, rather than trusting God through changing circumstances.

translation: And if We let him taste favor after hardship has touched him, he will surely say, “The misfortunes have gone from me.” Indeed, he is exultant and boastful.
interpretation: The verse warns that a person may mistake relief from hardship for lasting security, then become self-satisfied and boastful instead of remaining humble and grateful.

translation: Except those who are patient and do righteous deeds—those will have forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: True faith is shown by steadfastness when tested and by continuing to do what is right; such patience and good deeds are met with God’s forgiveness and generous reward.

translation: Perhaps you would leave aside some of what is revealed to you, and your heart feels constricted because they say, “Why has a treasure not been sent down to him, or an angel come with him?” You are only a warner, and Allah is Guardian over all things.
interpretation: The verse reassures the Prophet ﷺ amid the pressure of those who reject his message and demand extraordinary proof. Their objections may weigh heavily on him, but he is not charged with meeting their demands or controlling their response; his task is to warn, while Allah oversees all affairs.

translation: Or do they say, “He has fabricated it”? Say, “Then bring ten surahs like it that you have fabricated, and call upon anyone you can besides Allah, if you are truthful.”
interpretation: The verse challenges those who claim the Qur’an was invented to produce even ten comparable chapters and enlist whatever support they can. Its point is that their accusation is not proof: they are called to demonstrate it, and their inability to meet the challenge exposes the emptiness of their claim.

translation: Then, if they do not respond to you, know that it has been sent down with God’s knowledge, and that there is no god but Him. Will you, then, submit?
interpretation: If those you call upon cannot meet the challenge, recognize that the Qur’an comes with God’s knowledge and authority, and that its truth points to His oneness. The verse therefore calls its hearers to surrender themselves to Him.

translation: Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornment, We will repay them in full for their deeds in it, and they will not be deprived therein.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who make worldly life and its pleasures their sole aim may receive the full return for their efforts in this world, but that worldly recompense is not the same as reward in the Hereafter.

translation: Those are the ones who will have nothing in the Hereafter but the Fire. What they did in this life will come to nothing, and all that they used to do will be in vain.
interpretation: The verse warns that deeds pursued solely for worldly gain, without faith or concern for the Hereafter, cannot bring lasting benefit: their reward ends with this life, and they will find no good from them in the next.

translation: Is one who stands upon clear proof from his Lord, followed by a witness from Him, and preceded by the Book of Moses as a guide and mercy, [like one who does not]? Those believe in it. But whoever among the factions rejects it—the Fire is his appointed destination. So do not be in doubt about it: it is the truth from your Lord, though most people do not believe.
interpretation: The verse presents faith in the Qur’an as grounded in clear evidence from God and supported by confirming testimony, with the earlier revelation of Moses serving as a precedent and guide. It reassures the Prophet that the message is truly from his Lord, while warning that rejection carries consequences even though many people will not believe.

translation: Who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about God? Such people will be brought before their Lord, and the witnesses will say, “These are the ones who lied about their Lord.” Indeed, God’s curse is upon the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse warns that falsely speaking in God’s name is not merely a private error: on the Day of Judgment, the lie will be exposed before God and its witnesses, revealing the injustice of claiming divine authority for what God did not say.

translation: Those who turn others away from the path of Allah and seek to make it crooked, while they disbelieve in the Hereafter.
interpretation: The verse portrays people who do more than reject divine guidance themselves: they obstruct others from following it and distort its straight course to suit their aims. Their denial of the Hereafter reflects a rejection of the accountability that would expose and judge such conduct.

translation: Those were not beyond [God’s power] on earth, and they had no protectors besides God. The punishment will be multiplied for them. They were unable to hear, nor could they see.
interpretation: Their worldly position could not shield them from God, and no one could protect them from His judgment. Their punishment is multiplied because they persistently turned away from the truth: they would not listen to guidance or perceive it clearly.

translation: Those are the ones who have lost themselves, and what they used to invent has vanished from them.
interpretation: Their deepest loss is that they deceived themselves by relying on false claims and imagined partners; when the truth is revealed, those inventions offer them no help, leaving them to face the consequences of their own choices.

translation: Without a doubt, they will be the greatest losers in the Hereafter.
interpretation: Their rejection leads to the ultimate loss: in the Hereafter, they will find that they have forfeited lasting reward and salvation, with no worldly gain able to make up for it.

translation: Indeed, those who believe, do righteous deeds, and humble themselves before their Lord—those are the people of Paradise; they will remain there forever.
interpretation: True faith is not merely an inward claim: it takes shape in good conduct and a heart humbly turned toward God. The verse connects that sincere devotion with the enduring hope of Paradise.

translation: The likeness of the two groups is that of the blind and deaf, and the seeing and hearing. Are they alike in comparison? Will you not take heed?
interpretation: Those who reject guidance are like people unable to see or hear: the signs may be before them, but they do not receive or respond to them. Those who believe are like people who can see and hear, recognizing the truth and taking it in. The two groups are therefore not equal; the verse calls its listeners to reflect on the difference.

translation: We sent Noah to his people: “I am indeed a clear warner to you.”
interpretation: Noah’s message is presented as a direct, unmistakable warning: he makes clear both his role as a messenger and his people’s need to heed the truth before facing its consequences.

translation: Worship none but Allah. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a painful day.
interpretation: The warning calls people to sincere devotion to Allah alone and urges them to turn from disbelief before facing the severe consequences of rejecting His guidance.

translation: The chiefs among his people who disbelieved said, “We see you as nothing but a human being like ourselves, and we see that only the lowliest among us have followed you, at first glance. We see no superiority in you over us; rather, we think you are liars.”
interpretation: Their rejection stems from pride and social prejudice: they judge the truth by the status of those who accept it and expect a messenger to be distinguished by worldly rank. By dismissing Noah as an ordinary human and his followers as inferior, they avoid considering the substance of his message and accuse him of lying without proof.

translation: He said, “O my people, consider: if I have clear proof from my Lord and He has granted me mercy from Himself, but it has been hidden from you, should we force you to accept it when you are averse to it?”
interpretation: Noah explains that divine guidance is a gift from God, not something a messenger can impose by force. He can present the truth clearly, but he cannot make people recognize or welcome it when they turn away from it.

translation: “O my people, I ask you for no wealth in return for this. My reward is only with God. I will not drive away those who have believed; they are surely going to meet their Lord. But I see that you are a people who act ignorantly.”
interpretation: The speaker makes clear that his call is not for worldly gain and that he will not reject sincere believers to satisfy those who look down on them. Since all will meet God and answer for themselves, judging people by status and demanding that the believers be cast out reflects ignorance.

translation: And, O my people, who would protect me from Allah if I were to drive them away? Will you not then take heed?
interpretation: A person must not reject or mistreat sincere believers to please others; no one can shield them from God’s judgment for doing so.

translation: I do not say to you, ‘I possess God’s treasures,’ nor do I know the unseen, nor do I say, ‘I am an angel.’ And I do not say of those whom you look down upon that God will never grant them any good. God knows best what is within them; otherwise, I would surely be among the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse rejects judging people’s worth by their status or appearance. Their faith and inner state are known fully only to God, so dismissing them as undeserving of good would be an unjust claim beyond the speaker’s knowledge.

translation: They said, “O Noah, you have argued with us and argued at length. So bring upon us what you threaten us with, if you are truthful.”
interpretation: Their words express defiant impatience: rather than consider Noah’s warning, they challenge him to make the promised punishment happen, treating his message as something they can dismiss unless they see its consequences at once.

translation: He said, “Allah alone will bring it upon you, if He wills, and you cannot thwart Him.”
interpretation: Noah makes clear that the promised consequence is entirely in Allah’s power: it will come only by His will, and no one can evade or prevent it once He decrees it.

translation: My counsel will not benefit you, even if I sincerely wish to advise you, if Allah wills to let you go astray. He is your Lord, and to Him you will return.
interpretation: No messenger’s sincere advice can overcome a people’s rejection if Allah wills to leave them to the misguidance they have chosen. Their Lord alone has ultimate authority, and they will return to Him to be judged.

translation: Or do they say, “He has fabricated it”? Say, “If I have fabricated it, then my crime is upon me, and I am innocent of what you commit.”
interpretation: The verse answers the accusation of fabrication by placing responsibility where it belongs: if the Prophet had invented the message, he would bear the consequences, but he is not accountable for the rejection and wrongdoing of his accusers.

translation: And it was revealed to Noah: “None of your people will believe except those who have already believed, so do not grieve over what they have been doing.”
interpretation: God reassures Noah that his people’s continued rejection is not a failure of his mission: no one else among them will believe. He is therefore not to let their persistent wrongdoing consume him with sorrow, but to trust God’s judgment and continue as commanded.

translation: “Build the Ark under Our watchful care and by Our revelation, and do not plead with Me on behalf of those who have done wrong; they are surely to be drowned.”
interpretation: The verse portrays Noah’s work as guided and protected by God, while showing that compassion cannot avert a judgment already decreed against persistent wrongdoing.

translation: He was building the Ark, and whenever a group of his people passed by him, they mocked him. He said, “If you mock us, then we will mock you just as you mock us.”
interpretation: Noah’s calm reply shows his confidence in God’s command: his people’s mockery would not undo the truth of his mission, and in time they would face the consequences of their scorn.

translation: Then you will know who will be overtaken by a punishment that humiliates him, and upon whom an enduring punishment will descend.
interpretation: The warning conveys that the truth of the matter will soon become unmistakable: those who persist in rejecting God’s messenger will face a punishment that exposes and disgraces them, followed by lasting punishment.

translation: When Our command came and the oven overflowed, We said, “Bring aboard it two of every kind, and your family—except those against whom the decree has already gone forth—and those who believe.” Yet none believed with him except a few.
interpretation: The verse teaches that deliverance comes through obedience to God and faith, not merely through family ties. Even Noah’s household was not saved by kinship alone, and the small number of believers did not make their faith any less true.

translation: And he said, “Board it. In the name of Allah be its course and its anchorage. Indeed, my Lord is Ever-Forgiving, Most Merciful.”
interpretation: Noah calls those with him to enter the Ark, entrusting its journey and safe resting to Allah. His words express reliance on God’s power and hope in His forgiveness and mercy amid the flood.

translation: And it sailed with them amid waves like mountains. Noah called to his son, who was apart from them: “My son, come aboard with us, and do not be among the disbelievers.”
interpretation: Noah’s appeal shows that even in the face of overwhelming danger, he reaches out to his son with tenderness and urgency. The son’s separation from the believers cannot protect him; the passage points to faith and belonging with them, rather than family ties or physical distance, as the path to safety.

translation: He said, “I will seek refuge on a mountain that will protect me from the water.” He said, “Today there is no protector from Allah’s decree except for one whom He has mercy upon.” Then the waves came between them, and he was among those who drowned.
interpretation: The verse teaches that worldly safeguards cannot avail against Allah’s judgment; true deliverance rests not in human calculations or refuge, but in Allah’s mercy.

translation: And it was said, “O earth, swallow your water, and O sky, withhold your rain.” The water subsided, the decree was fulfilled, and the Ark came to rest upon al-Jūdī. And it was said, “Away with the wrongdoing people.”
interpretation: The flood ends at God’s command just as it began by His decree: the earth and sky obey, and the Ark is brought to safety. The closing words mark the judgment of those who persisted in wrongdoing, showing that divine power brings both deliverance and accountability.

translation: Noah called upon his Lord and said, “My Lord, my son is indeed of my family. Surely Your promise is true, and You are the wisest of judges.”
interpretation: Noah appeals to God on behalf of his son, believing that his family would be included in the promise of deliverance. His words also entrust the matter to God’s perfect wisdom and judgment.

translation: He said, “O Noah, he is not of your family; his conduct is unrighteous. So do not ask Me about that of which you have no knowledge. I admonish you, lest you be among the ignorant.”
interpretation: Noah’s son was his son by lineage, but not among the family promised deliverance because he rejected faith. The verse teaches that closeness to the righteous is not secured by kinship alone, and that even a prophet must entrust to God matters whose full wisdom he does not know.

translation: He said, “My Lord, I seek refuge in You from asking You for what I have no knowledge of. If You do not forgive me and have mercy on me, I will be among the losers.”
interpretation: Noah acknowledges that even a sincere plea must remain within the limits of what God has made known. His words express humility before divine wisdom and reliance on God’s forgiveness and mercy, without which no one can attain true success.

translation: It was said, “O Noah, disembark in peace from Us, with blessings upon you and upon communities among those with you. And there will be other communities whom We will allow to enjoy life for a time; then a painful punishment from Us will befall them.”
interpretation: Noah’s deliverance is presented as a divine gift of peace and blessing, extending to believing communities that would arise from those with him. Yet worldly comfort is not itself a sign of lasting favor: other communities will be given enjoyment for a time, but their rejection of God will ultimately bring painful judgment.

translation: That is among the reports of the unseen which We reveal to you. Neither you nor your people knew it before this. So be patient; indeed, the ultimate outcome belongs to the God-conscious.
interpretation: The account is presented as revealed knowledge, affirming that the Prophet’s message comes from God rather than prior learning. Its closing counsel teaches him to remain steadfast amid rejection: truth may face hardship for a time, but lasting success belongs to those who remain mindful of God.

translation: And to ʿĀd [We sent] their brother Hūd. He said, “My people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. You are only inventing falsehood.”
interpretation: Hūd calls his people back to sincere worship of Allah alone, pointing out that their claims about other gods have no truth behind them and are inventions of their own.

translation: O my people, I ask no reward from you for this. My reward is only from the One who created me. Will you not then use reason?
