interpretation: The speaker makes clear that his call is not driven by personal gain: he seeks his reward from his Creator alone. This sincerity should lead his people to consider his message fairly rather than dismiss it as self-interest.

translation: “My people, seek your Lord’s forgiveness, then turn back to Him in repentance. He will send abundant rain upon you and increase your strength; so do not turn away as wrongdoers.”
interpretation: The verse presents sincere repentance as a return to God that opens the way to His mercy and blessing. Its promise of rain and increased strength points to flourishing by God’s favor, while the warning cautions against rejecting that return and persisting in wrongdoing.

translation: They said, “O Hūd, you have brought us no clear proof, and we will not abandon our gods at your word, nor will we believe in you.”
interpretation: Their response shows a refusal to be guided: they demand proof from Hūd while remaining attached to their idols and rejecting him outright, rather than considering his message with openness.

translation: They said, “We can only say that some of our gods have afflicted you with harm.” He said, “I call Allah to witness, and you too bear witness, that I am free of what you associate with Him.”
interpretation: Hud rejects the claim that their idols have harmed him and openly disavows their worship. By calling Allah and the people to witness, he shows his firm trust in the truth of his message and his complete separation from idolatry.

translation: Besides Him. So scheme against me, all of you, and give me no respite.
interpretation: The speaker expresses complete confidence in God: even if his opponents unite and act without delay, their schemes cannot prevail unless God permits them.

translation: Indeed, I have placed my trust in Allah, my Lord and your Lord. There is no creature except that He holds it by its forelock. Surely my Lord is on a straight path.
interpretation: The verse grounds the speaker’s complete trust in God’s sovereignty over every living creature. God’s holding each creature by its forelock signifies that none can escape His power, while His being “on a straight path” means that His governance is always just and true.

translation: But if you turn away, I have delivered to you the message with which I was sent to you. My Lord will bring another people in your place, and you will not harm Him in the least. Indeed, my Lord is Guardian over all things.
interpretation: The warning makes clear that rejecting a messenger cannot defeat God’s purpose or diminish His power. The messenger’s duty is to convey the truth; those who refuse it bear the consequences, while God can replace them and remains fully in control of all things.

translation: And when Our command came, We saved Hūd and those who believed with him through mercy from Us, and We saved them from a severe punishment.
interpretation: The verse shows that deliverance is ultimately a gift of God’s mercy: faith is the path by which Hūd’s followers were distinguished from those facing punishment, but their safety came from God’s gracious protection.

translation: And those were ʿĀd: they rejected the signs of their Lord, disobeyed His messengers, and followed the command of every arrogant, defiant tyrant.
interpretation: The verse portrays ʿĀd’s wrongdoing as more than denial: they chose to heed tyrannical leaders who resisted the truth rather than submit to God’s guidance, which had been conveyed by His messengers.

translation: And they were pursued by a curse in this world and on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, ʿĀd disbelieved in their Lord. So away with ʿĀd, the people of Hūd!
interpretation: Their rejection of their Lord brought them lasting disgrace in this life and the Hereafter; the verse declares their ruin and distance from divine mercy as a warning against defiance.

translation: And to Thamud We sent their brother Salih. He said, “My people, worship Allah; you have no god besides Him. He brought you forth from the earth and settled you upon it, so seek His forgiveness and turn back to Him. Surely my Lord is near and responsive.”
interpretation: Salih reminds his people that their life and their ability to build and flourish on the earth are gifts from Allah, so they should direct their worship to Him alone and return to Him in repentance. Allah’s nearness and responsiveness assure them that sincere repentance is met with an answer.

translation: They said, “O Ṣāliḥ, we had placed our hopes in you before this. Do you forbid us to worship what our forefathers worshipped? We are truly in troubling doubt about what you call us to.”
interpretation: They reproach Ṣāliḥ for abandoning the role they had expected him to play and treat his call to worship God alone as a rejection of their inherited ways. Their appeal to ancestral practice and their professed doubt reveal how attachment to tradition has made them suspicious of his message.

translation: He said, “My people, consider: if I have clear proof from my Lord and He has granted me mercy from Himself, who could protect me from Allah if I disobey Him? You would only increase me in loss.”
interpretation: He makes clear that neither his people’s pressure nor their approval could justify disobeying God: having received guidance and mercy, he is accountable to God alone, and urging him away from the truth could only deepen his loss.

translation: And, O my people, this is Allah’s she-camel, a sign for you. So let her graze in Allah’s land, and do not harm her, lest a punishment soon overtake you.
interpretation: The she-camel is presented as a clear sign from God and as a trust whose freedom the people must respect. The warning makes their treatment of her a test of whether they will heed God’s command; harming her would bring swift consequences.

translation: So they hamstrung her, and he said, “Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days. That is a promise that will not be proved false.”
interpretation: The three-day respite marks the final, limited reprieve after they defied the sign; the words “a promise that will not be proved false” affirm that the punishment foretold would certainly come.

translation: When Our command came, We saved Ṣāliḥ and those who believed with him, by a mercy from Us, and from the disgrace of that day. Indeed, your Lord is the Strong, the Almighty.
interpretation: Their deliverance was an act of God’s mercy, while their people’s destruction brought humiliation. The verse affirms that God’s irresistible power and might protect those He wills and bring His judgment to pass.

translation: The wrongdoers were seized by the blast, and by morning they lay lifeless in their homes.
interpretation: The verse portrays the suddenness and finality of divine judgment: those who persisted in wrongdoing were overcome by a single blast, left powerless where they lived.

translation: As though they had never prospered there. Indeed, Thamūd rejected their Lord; so away with Thamūd.
interpretation: The verse presents Thamūd’s destruction as so complete that their former strength and settled life seemed erased, underscoring the grave consequence of rejecting God.

translation: Our messengers came to Abraham with good news. They said, “Peace.” He said, “Peace,” and soon brought them a roasted calf.
interpretation: Abraham’s immediate preparation of a meal shows the generosity and readiness to honor guests that marked his character; his peaceful welcome sets a tone of trust before the visitors disclose the purpose of their mission.

translation: When he saw that their hands did not reach for it, he found them strange and felt fear of them. They said, “Do not be afraid; we have been sent to the people of Lot.”
interpretation: Their refusal to eat made Abraham suspect that his visitors posed a threat, since refusing a host’s food was an alarming sign. They reassured him by revealing their mission: they were angels sent to the people of Lot.

translation: His wife was standing, and she laughed; then We gave her the good news of Isaac, and after Isaac, Jacob.
interpretation: The glad tidings reveal that God’s power and generosity extend beyond what people consider possible: not only would she have a son in old age, but the promise would continue through a grandson after him.

translation: She said, “Alas for me! Shall I bear a child when I am an old woman and my husband here is an old man? This is truly astonishing!”
interpretation: Sarah expresses amazement at the glad tidings of a child, since both she and her husband are advanced in age. Her reaction reflects how extraordinary the news seemed by ordinary human expectations, while the event points to God’s power to bring about what people might consider impossible.

translation: They said, “Do you marvel at God’s decree? May God’s mercy and blessings be upon you, people of the household. Surely He is Praiseworthy, Glorious.”
interpretation: The response gently corrects Sarah’s astonishment: what seems beyond ordinary expectation is not beyond God’s power or wisdom. The greeting of mercy and blessing affirms the special favor bestowed upon Abraham’s household, while God’s praise and glory ground their hope in His perfect attributes.

translation: When the fear had left Abraham and the good news had come to him, he pleaded with Us concerning the people of Lot.
interpretation: Abraham’s plea reflects his deep compassion and concern for others: even after receiving glad tidings himself, he turned his attention to the fate of Lot’s people, seeking mercy for them.

translation: Indeed, Abraham was forbearing, tenderhearted, and ever turning back to God.
interpretation: Abraham’s patience and deep compassion were joined with a heart that continually returned to God in humble devotion.

translation: “O Abraham, turn away from this. The command of your Lord has indeed come, and a punishment that cannot be averted is coming upon them.”
interpretation: Abraham is being told that the matter has passed beyond intercession: God’s judgment has been decreed, and no plea can avert the punishment appointed for them.

translation: When Our messengers came to Lot, he was distressed on their account and felt constrained for them, and said, “This is a terrible day.”
interpretation: Lot’s distress reflects his fear that he could not protect his guests from the wrongdoing of his people. The verse conveys the weight of a prophet’s concern when he sees danger approaching those under his care.

translation: His people came rushing toward him, though they had long been committing evil deeds. He said, “My people, here are my daughters; they are purer for you. So be mindful of Allah, and do not disgrace me concerning my guests. Is there not among you a man of sound judgment?”
interpretation: Lot appeals to his people to turn from their shameful pursuit of his guests toward what is lawful and pure, and calls on them to fear God and heed their better judgment. His offer of “my daughters” is understood as an appeal to lawful marriage—often explained as the women of his community, for whom he was a spiritual father. Their response would expose how far they had abandoned moral restraint.

translation: They said, “You know well that we have no interest in your daughters, and you certainly know what we want.”
interpretation: Their words reveal that their aim was not marriage or any lawful relationship: they rejected Lot’s offer and openly pursued what was forbidden. The verse thus exposes the depth of their moral corruption and the futility of Lot’s appeal to them.

translation: He said, “If only I had the strength to stand against you, or could take refuge in a mighty support!”
interpretation: Lot’s words express his anguish at being unable to protect his guests from his people. He longs for strength or a powerful ally, revealing the limits of his human means as he confronts their aggression.

translation: They said, “O Lot, we are messengers from your Lord. They will never reach you. So set out with your family during part of the night, and let none of you look back—except your wife; what befalls them will befall her. Their appointed time is the morning. Is the morning not near?”
interpretation: The messengers reassure Lot that his people cannot harm him, then instruct him to leave by night with those who are faithful. His wife is excluded from their rescue: she remains aligned with the people and will share their fate. The mention that morning is near underscores that the promised punishment is imminent.

translation: When Our command came, We turned its highest part upside down and rained upon it stones of baked clay, one after another.
interpretation: The verse portrays the decisive punishment that befell Lot’s people: their town was overturned and struck by a successive shower of stones, showing that when God’s judgment comes, no power can avert it.

translation: Marked by your Lord; and it is not far from the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The punishment was appointed by God, and its mention warns wrongdoers not to assume that divine justice is remote from them.

translation: And to Midian We sent their brother Shuʿayb. He said, “My people, worship Allah; you have no god but Him. Do not give short measure or weight. I see you in prosperity, and I fear for you the punishment of an all-encompassing Day.”
interpretation: Shuʿayb calls his people to understand that devotion to Allah must shape how they treat others: cheating in trade is not a merely private fault but a betrayal of justice and gratitude. Their prosperity should make them more mindful, not complacent, because wrongdoing can bring consequences that no one can escape.

translation: And, O my people, give full measure and weight with justice. Do not deprive people of what is rightfully theirs, and do not spread corruption throughout the land.
interpretation: The verse calls for honesty in every dealing: people must receive their full due, and no one should use power or opportunity to exploit others or damage the wider community.

translation: What Allah leaves for you [of lawful gain] is better for you, if you are believers; and I am not a guardian over you.
interpretation: The verse teaches that honest, lawful profit is better and more blessed than wealth gained through fraud. Faith should lead people to choose what is right willingly; the messenger’s role is to convey the warning, not to compel or police them.

translation: They said, “O Shuʿayb, does your prayer command you that we abandon what our forefathers worship, or that we stop doing with our wealth whatever we wish? Surely you are the forbearing, right-minded one.”
interpretation: Their words deride Shuʿayb’s moral authority: they treat inherited religious custom and unrestricted control of wealth as beyond challenge, while their “forbearing, right-minded” praise is likely sarcastic. The verse highlights how appeals to tradition and personal freedom can be used to resist ethical accountability.

translation: He said, “My people, consider: if I have clear evidence from my Lord and He has granted me good provision from Himself, would I then oppose you by doing what I forbid you? I seek only to bring about reform as far as I am able. My success comes only through Allah. In Him I place my trust, and to Him I turn.”
interpretation: True reform requires sincerity and consistency: one must not demand from others what one refuses to practice oneself. Yet a person’s efforts and success remain limited, so the reformer relies on Allah for help and continually turns back to Him.

translation: “My people, do not let your opposition to me bring upon you a fate like that which befell the people of Noah, Hūd, or Ṣāliḥ; and the people of Lot are not far from you.”
interpretation: Shuʿayb warns his people not to let their hostility toward him blind them to the consequences of rejecting a prophet: earlier communities were punished for doing so, and the people of Lot offer a nearby example they should take seriously.

translation: Seek your Lord’s forgiveness, then turn back to Him in repentance. Indeed, my Lord is Merciful and Loving.
interpretation: The call to repent is an invitation to return without despair: God’s mercy welcomes those who turn to Him, and His love makes that return more than the mere removal of guilt—it is a renewal of closeness to Him.

translation: They said, “O Shuʿayb, we do not understand much of what you say, and we see you as weak among us. Were it not for your clan, we would have stoned you; you hold no honor with us.”
interpretation: Their words reveal contempt for Shuʿayb’s call and a threat of violence: they regard his safety as dependent on his clan’s protection, not on any respect for him or his message.

translation: He said, “My people, are my family more honored by you than Allah, that you have cast Him behind your backs? My Lord surely encompasses all that you do.”
interpretation: Shuʿayb rebukes his people for relying on the protection and status of his family while disregarding Allah’s authority. Their disregard cannot conceal their actions from God, who fully knows and encompasses them.

translation: “And, O my people, act according to your position; I too am acting. You will soon know upon whom a punishment that disgraces him will come, and who is the liar. So wait; I am waiting with you.”
interpretation: The words express a firm challenge in the face of rejection: each side may persist in its course, but the outcome will reveal the truth. The speaker entrusts the judgment to what is to come, warning that no claim or defiance can shield anyone from God’s reckoning.

translation: When Our command came, We saved Shuʿayb and those who believed with him through mercy from Us; and the blast struck those who had done wrong, so that by morning they lay fallen in their homes.
interpretation: The verse presents deliverance and punishment as expressions of God’s justice: the believers’ rescue was not merely escape from danger, but a mercy granted by God, while the sudden destruction of the wrongdoers shows that persistent rejection of a messenger carries grave consequences.

translation: As though they had never prospered there. Away with Midian, just as Thamud were swept away.
interpretation: Their destruction left no trace of the life they had once enjoyed, showing how swiftly prosperity can vanish when a people persist in wrongdoing and reject God’s warning.

translation: And We certainly sent Moses with Our signs and clear authority.
interpretation: Moses was sent with divine signs and compelling proof, establishing that his message came from God and giving his people clear grounds to recognize and follow the truth.

translation: To Pharaoh and his chiefs. But they followed Pharaoh’s command, and Pharaoh’s command was not rightly guided.
interpretation: The verse portrays Pharaoh’s people as accepting his authority and following his direction, even though it led them away from what was right. It warns that obedience to a powerful leader does not make his guidance sound.

translation: He will lead his people on the Day of Resurrection and bring them to the Fire. What a wretched place to be brought to!
interpretation: The verse warns that a leader who guides people toward wrongdoing ultimately leads them to ruin; those who follow such a leader share in the consequence. Calling the Fire a place to be brought to sharply contrasts the relief of a watering place with the dreadful end awaiting them.

translation: They were followed by a curse in this world and on the Day of Resurrection. Wretched is the gift bestowed upon them.
interpretation: The people of Pharaoh were made to face condemnation both in worldly life and in the Hereafter. Calling this curse a “gift” is bitter irony: what they receive is no favor or support, but a grievous recompense.

translation: That is some of the news of the towns We recount to you: some of them still stand, while others have been cut down.
interpretation: The contrast between towns whose traces remain and those utterly laid low invites reflection on how worldly strength does not last; the remains of past peoples stand as a warning to those who ignore the consequences of wrongdoing.

translation: We did not wrong them; rather, they wronged themselves. Their gods, whom they called upon besides Allah, were of no benefit to them when your Lord’s decree came, and they brought them nothing but ruin.
interpretation: The verse teaches that people cannot blame God for the consequences of their rejection: their own choices led them astray. When divine judgment arrives, whatever they relied on besides God proves powerless, and that misplaced reliance only deepens their loss.

translation: Such is the seizure of your Lord when He seizes towns while they are wrongdoing. Indeed, His seizure is painful and severe.
interpretation: The warning is that continued wrongdoing should never be mistaken for immunity: a period of apparent respite does not mean that accountability has been waived.

translation: Surely in that is a sign for whoever fears the punishment of the Hereafter: that is a Day on which all people will be gathered, a Day witnessed by all.
interpretation: The account is a warning that worldly events point toward ultimate accountability: those mindful of the Hereafter should recognize that every person will stand together before God on a day whose reality none can evade.

translation: And We do not delay it except until a fixed, counted term.
interpretation: The delay is not neglect or uncertainty: the appointed time is precisely determined, and it will arrive when its term is complete.

translation: On the Day it comes, no soul will speak except by His permission. Among them will be some wretched and some blessed.
interpretation: The verse portrays the Day of Judgment as wholly under God’s authority: even speech depends on His permission, and people will face distinct final outcomes of misery or felicity.

translation: As for those who are wretched, they will be in the Fire, where they will groan and gasp.
interpretation: Their groaning and gasping portray the intense, unrelenting anguish of their punishment.

translation: They will abide therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills. Indeed, your Lord does whatever He wills.
interpretation: The statement affirms the vast duration of their abiding while making clear that its continuance is entirely subject to God’s will; no duration or outcome limits His authority.

translation: As for those who are blessed, they will be in Paradise, abiding there for as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills—a gift that will never be cut off.
interpretation: The verse promises the people of felicity lasting joy in Paradise, while the exception affirms that their destiny remains entirely under God’s will. Their reward is described as an unending gift, not one that will be withdrawn.

translation: So do not be in doubt about what these people worship. They worship only as their forefathers worshipped before them, and We will surely give them their full share, undiminished.
interpretation: The verse reassures the Prophet that the people’s worship is a continuation of inherited practices, not a reason for uncertainty about the truth. They will receive in full the recompense allotted to them for what they do.

translation: We certainly gave Moses the Scripture, but disagreement arose over it. Had not a decree already preceded from your Lord, judgment would have been made between them. They are indeed in deeply unsettling doubt about it.
interpretation: Disagreement over revealed guidance is not new and does not, by itself, undermine its truth. God’s judgment is deferred according to His prior decree, while those who dispute the revelation remain troubled by doubt.

translation: And indeed, your Lord will surely repay each of them in full for their deeds. He is fully aware of what they do.
interpretation: No one’s deeds are overlooked: God knows them completely and will give each person their just recompense.

translation: So remain steadfast as you have been commanded, along with those who have turned to God with you, and do not transgress. Surely He sees all that you do.
interpretation: Steadfastness means faithfully following God’s command without wavering or exceeding its limits. The verse also makes clear that this responsibility is shared by those who follow the Prophet, and that God sees their conduct, not merely their intentions.

translation: And do not incline toward those who do wrong, lest the Fire touch you; you have no protectors besides Allah, and then you will not be helped.
interpretation: The verse warns believers not to give even tacit approval or support to wrongdoing. Such an alliance can draw a person toward the oppressors’ injustice and expose them to punishment; no protector can save them if they turn away from Allah.

translation: Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and during the early parts of the night. Indeed, good deeds remove bad deeds. This is a reminder for those who take heed.
interpretation: The verse teaches that regular prayer and other righteous acts help cleanse a person of wrongdoing and turn them back toward God. Its reminder encourages believers to respond to mistakes with sincere repentance and renewed devotion.

translation: And be patient, for Allah does not let the reward of those who do good go to waste.
interpretation: This is a reassurance to remain steadfast in doing what is right, even when its reward is not immediately visible: sincere goodness is never overlooked by God.

translation: Why, then, were there not among the generations before you people of sound judgment who forbade corruption on earth—except for a few of those We saved from among them? Those who did wrong pursued the ease and luxury they had been given, and they were guilty of wrongdoing.
interpretation: The verse warns that communities become vulnerable to ruin when people of sound judgment fail to resist corruption. The few who speak against it may be saved, while those who wrong others become absorbed in their comforts and persist in wrongdoing.

translation: Your Lord would never destroy towns unjustly while their people were reforming.
interpretation: The verse teaches that God’s judgment is never arbitrary: a community that sincerely works to set things right is not treated as though it were wholly corrupt. Its emphasis is on reform and right conduct, not merely on professing belief.

translation: Had your Lord willed, He could have made all people one community; yet they continue to differ.
interpretation: Human diversity and disagreement exist within God’s will: He did not make people uniform by compulsion, so their differences reflect the freedom and responsibility with which they are tested.

translation: Except those upon whom your Lord has mercy. And for that He created them. And the decree of your Lord was fulfilled: “I will surely fill Hell with jinn and humankind, all together.”
interpretation: The verse points to divine mercy as the purpose for which God created people: those who receive His mercy are guided out of division and error. The final decree affirms that rejection has real consequences, while making clear that God’s mercy remains open to those He guides.

translation: And all that We recount to you of the stories of the messengers is what We strengthen your heart with. And in this has come to you the truth, an admonition, and a reminder for the believers.
interpretation: The accounts of earlier messengers are revealed to steady the Prophet in the face of hardship: they show that the trials he meets are part of the way of prophethood, and that God’s support and final judgment are sure. For believers, these accounts also call them to heed the truth and remain steadfast.

translation: And say to those who do not believe, “Act according to your way; we too are acting.”
interpretation: This is a warning, not an endorsement of disbelief: each side is told to persist in its chosen course, while the consequences of their deeds will ultimately become clear.

translation: And wait; indeed, we too are waiting.
interpretation: This is a warning to those who reject the message: they may persist in their course, but the Prophet and the believers await God’s judgment, certain that the promised outcome will come.

translation: To Allah belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and to Him all affairs will return. So worship Him and put your trust in Him; your Lord is never unaware of what you do.
interpretation: Because all hidden realities and the ultimate outcome of every affair are in Allah’s hands, worship and rely on Him alone, knowing that every deed remains within His knowledge.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Alif Lam Ra. These are the verses of the clear Book.
interpretation: The opening letters are among the signs whose full meaning is known to Allah; they invite attention to the revelation that follows. The Qur’an is described as clear because it makes the truth and divine guidance plain to those who reflect on it.

translation: Indeed, We sent it down as an Arabic Qur’an so that you may understand.
interpretation: The verse points to the Qur’an’s language as a means of making its message clear and graspable to its first hearers, inviting them to reflect on its guidance rather than merely recite its words.

translation: We relate to you the finest account through what We have revealed to you of this Qur’an, though before it you were surely among those unaware.
interpretation: The verse presents the Qur’an’s account as knowledge granted by revelation, not something the Prophet had previously learned for himself. Its excellence lies in the guidance and truth it conveys.

translation: When Joseph said to his father, “My father, I saw eleven stars, and the sun and the moon—I saw them bowing down to me.”
interpretation: The dream points to the honor and elevated standing God would grant Joseph, and to his family’s eventual recognition of that favor. Their bowing signifies a gesture of respect and submission in the dream, not worship.

translation: He said, “My son, do not tell your brothers about your dream, lest they scheme against you. Surely Satan is a clear enemy to humankind.”
interpretation: The verse teaches prudent discretion: a cherished blessing or hope need not be shared with people who may respond with envy. It also points to Satan as the force that can inflame such feelings into harmful action.

translation: “And thus your Lord will choose you, teach you the interpretation of dreams, and complete His favor upon you and upon the family of Jacob, as He completed it before upon your forefathers Abraham and Isaac. Indeed, your Lord is All-Knowing, All-Wise.”
interpretation: Jacob reassures Joseph that the dream points to a divine calling: Joseph will be given insight to understand what is hidden and will carry forward the blessing granted to Abraham and Isaac. The closing names God’s knowledge and wisdom as the basis for this promise, even though its fulfillment and timing are not yet apparent.

translation: Indeed, in Joseph and his brothers are signs for those who ask.
interpretation: The story invites thoughtful inquiry: beneath painful and confusing events, God’s wisdom may be unfolding in ways that become clear only with time.

translation: When they said, “Joseph and his brother are dearer to our father than we are, though we are a strong group. Surely our father is clearly mistaken.”
interpretation: The verse reveals how envy can make people interpret another’s affection as injustice and speak with certainty about a judgment they do not fully understand.

translation: “Kill Joseph or cast him away to some land, and your father’s favor will be exclusively yours; then, afterward, you can become righteous people.”
interpretation: The verse exposes how jealousy can distort moral judgment: Joseph’s brothers imagine that they can commit a grave wrong to secure their father’s affection, then simply become righteous afterward. Their words reveal the self-deception of treating repentance as something that can be postponed until after wrongdoing.

translation: One of them said, “Do not kill Joseph. Instead, throw him into the depths of the well; some travelers may pick him up, if you are determined to act.”
interpretation: The proposal restrains the brothers from murder, but it does not make their intention just: Joseph is still treated as someone to be removed. The verse shows how a lesser harm can be offered as a compromise while the underlying wrongdoing remains.

translation: They said, “Our father, why do you not trust us with Joseph, when we are truly sincere in our concern for him?”
interpretation: The brothers appeal to their father’s confidence by presenting themselves as sincere guardians of Joseph. Their words reveal how trust can be invoked to persuade someone, even when the speaker’s intentions are not as caring as claimed.

translation: Send him with us tomorrow so that he may enjoy himself and play; we will surely take good care of him.
interpretation: The brothers reassure their father that Joseph will be safe in their company, presenting the outing as a chance for him to enjoy himself while promising to protect him.

translation: He said, “It grieves me that you should take him away, and I fear that a wolf may devour him while you are unaware of him.”
interpretation: Jacob’s words express a father’s deep anxiety at being separated from Joseph. His specific fear reflects how vulnerable Joseph would be if left unprotected, while the brothers’ distraction made that danger seem all the more troubling to him.

translation: They said, “If a wolf were to eat him while we are a strong group, then we would surely be losers.”
interpretation: The brothers appeal to their strength as a group to reassure their father that Yusuf will be safe in their care, treating any failure to protect him as an unmistakable disgrace.

translation: When they had taken him away and agreed to cast him into the depths of the well, We revealed to him: “You will surely remind them of this deed of theirs while they are unaware.”
interpretation: Even as Joseph faced betrayal and danger, God reassured him that this moment would not define his future: he would one day confront his brothers with what they had done, while they did not recognize who he was.

translation: And they came to their father at night, weeping.
interpretation: Their tears and the timing of their arrival suggest a carefully staged display of grief, showing how outward emotion can be used to conceal the truth.

translation: They said, “Our father, we went racing one another and left Joseph with our belongings, and the wolf devoured him. You would not believe us, even if we were telling the truth.”
interpretation: Their words anticipate their father’s distrust: they present an excuse while admitting that their claim alone would not persuade him. This reveals the strain between them and their father, and the weakness of their attempt to make their story credible.

translation: They brought his shirt with false blood upon it. He said, “Rather, your own selves have made something seem acceptable to you. So, [my response is] beautiful patience; and Allah is the One whose help is sought against what you describe.”
interpretation: Jacob recognizes that the evidence has been contrived, yet does not let grief drive him to despair or rash action. His “beautiful patience” is steadfast trust in Allah, while his appeal for help places the burden of the falsehood before God.

translation: And a caravan came, and they sent their water-drawer, who lowered his bucket. He said, “Good news! Here is a boy!” They concealed him as merchandise, but Allah knew well what they were doing.
interpretation: The travelers treated Yusuf as property to be traded, yet their attempt to conceal and exploit him was never hidden from Allah. The verse thus contrasts human schemes with Allah’s complete knowledge of what people do.

translation: They sold him for a paltry price—just a few dirhams—and had little regard for him.
interpretation: Those who sold Joseph were so indifferent to him that they accepted a meager price, unaware of his true worth.

translation: The man from Egypt who bought him said to his wife, “Treat him generously; perhaps he will benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son.” Thus We established Joseph in the land, so that We might teach him the interpretation of events. God prevails in carrying out His purpose, though most people do not know.
interpretation: Joseph’s arrival in Egypt appeared to be the result of human decisions, yet it became part of God’s wise plan: the very household that received him would help prepare him for the role he was destined to fulfil. The verse teaches that God’s purpose can unfold through ordinary circumstances, even when people cannot see where those circumstances are leading.

translation: When he reached maturity, We granted him sound judgment and knowledge. Thus do We reward those who excel in goodness.
interpretation: God’s gifts of wisdom and knowledge are presented as grace bestowed upon one who lives with excellence; the verse affirms that sincere goodness is met with divine favor.

translation: The woman in whose house he lived tried to seduce him. She shut the doors and said, “Come to me.” He said, “I seek refuge in God! My master has treated me well. Indeed, the wrongdoers will never prosper.”
interpretation: Joseph refuses to betray the trust placed in him, recognizing that yielding would be an act of wrongdoing; his appeal to God expresses the moral strength that keeps him faithful despite temptation.

translation: She certainly desired him, and he would have desired her had he not seen the proof of his Lord. Thus We turned evil and indecency away from him; indeed, he was one of Our chosen servants.
interpretation: The verse portrays Joseph as facing a powerful temptation, while making clear that he did not act upon it: seeing his Lord’s proof restrained him. God’s protection preserved him from wrongdoing, in keeping with his sincerity and devotion.

translation: They both raced to the door, and she tore his shirt from behind. They found her husband at the door. She said, “What should be the punishment of someone who intended harm against your wife, other than imprisonment or a painful punishment?”
interpretation: Her words reveal an attempt to turn the accusation against Joseph and secure his punishment before the facts are examined. The torn shirt, however, would become a piece of evidence by which the truth could be judged.

translation: He said, “She was the one who tried to seduce me.” And a witness from her household testified, “If his shirt is torn from the front, then she has spoken the truth, and he is among the liars.”
interpretation: Yusuf denies the accusation and states that she pursued him. The witness proposes examining the shirt as evidence: a tear at the front would support her claim that he approached her and she resisted him, thereby identifying Yusuf as the liar.

translation: And if his shirt is torn from the back, then she has lied, and he is truthful.
interpretation: The verse shows that claims should be judged by clear evidence: the direction of the tear reveals who was pursuing whom, distinguishing truth from falsehood.

translation: When he saw that his shirt had been torn from the back, he said, “This is indeed part of your scheming; your scheming is truly great.”
interpretation: The torn shirt provides clear evidence that Joseph was fleeing rather than pursuing her. The speaker recognizes that she had tried to deceive him by accusing him, and his words condemn the calculated attempt to turn the truth against him.

translation: Joseph, turn away from this. And you, [my wife], seek forgiveness for your sin; indeed, you were among those who did wrong.
interpretation: The speaker recognizes Joseph’s innocence and tells him not to pursue the matter further, while calling his wife to acknowledge her wrongdoing and seek God’s forgiveness.

translation: And some women in the city said, “The wife of al-ʿAzīz is trying to seduce her young servant. Love for him has pierced her heart; we clearly see her in error.”
interpretation: Their words reveal the scandal and gossip surrounding her desire: they portray it as having overwhelmed her judgment and condemn her conduct from the standpoint of their own social and moral expectations.

translation: When she heard of their scheming, she sent for them, prepared a gathering for them, and gave each of them a knife. Then she said, “Come out before them.” When they saw him, they were so struck by him that they cut their hands and exclaimed, “Glory be to God! This is no human being; he is nothing but a noble angel.”
interpretation: Their astonishment at Joseph’s beauty was so overwhelming that they momentarily lost awareness of what they were doing. The scene shows how powerful attraction can be, while reminding us that being overcome by it does not itself make a person’s choices morally right.

translation: She said, “This is the one about whom you blamed me. I did try to seduce him, but he firmly resisted. If he does not do what I command him, he will surely be imprisoned and become one of the humiliated.”
interpretation: Her admission confirms that Joseph’s innocence was not merely a claim: he had resisted her advances despite the power she could wield against him. Her threat also reveals how she sought to turn that power into coercion when he would not yield.

translation: He said, “My Lord, prison is dearer to me than what they invite me to. If You do not turn their scheme away from me, I may incline toward them and become one of the ignorant.”
interpretation: Joseph’s prayer shows that resisting temptation is not merely a matter of personal resolve: he seeks God’s protection, humbly acknowledging his own vulnerability. He would rather endure hardship than compromise his faith and integrity.

translation: So his Lord answered him and turned their schemes away from him. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: Allah protected Joseph from the women’s enticement in response to his sincere prayer. The verse reassures that God hears those who call upon Him and knows their circumstances and intentions.

translation: Then, after they had seen the signs, it seemed best to them to imprison him for a time.
interpretation: Though the evidence pointed to Joseph’s innocence, those in authority chose imprisonment to contain the scandal and protect their standing.

translation: Two young men entered the prison with him. One of them said, “I see myself pressing wine.” The other said, “I see myself carrying bread on my head, with birds eating from it. Tell us its interpretation; we see that you are one of those who do good.”
interpretation: The two prisoners turn to Joseph for the meaning of their dreams because they recognize his goodness and trustworthiness. Their request also sets the stage for Joseph to show the wisdom God has granted him.

translation: He said, “No food will come to you as provision but that I will tell you its interpretation before it comes to you. This is among what my Lord has taught me. Indeed, I have left the way of a people who do not believe in Allah and who are deniers of the Hereafter.”
interpretation: Joseph presents his insight not as a power of his own, but as knowledge granted by God. He also makes clear that his faith and integrity are inseparable from rejecting the beliefs of those who deny God and the Hereafter.

translation: “I have followed the way of my forefathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. It was not for us to associate anything with Allah. This is a favor from Allah upon us and upon all people, but most people are not grateful.”
interpretation: Joseph presents pure worship of Allah as the shared teaching of the prophets, not a distinction belonging to one family or community. By calling this guidance a favor upon both himself and humanity, he points to divine guidance as a gift offered for people’s benefit; failing to recognize and respond to that gift is a form of ingratitude.

translation: O my two companions in prison, are many separate lords better, or Allah, the One, the Overwhelming?
interpretation: Joseph invites his fellow prisoners to reflect that worship belongs not to powerless, competing deities, but to Allah alone: the One whose sovereignty is absolute and whose power prevails over all.

translation: Those whom you worship besides Him are only names that you and your fathers have given them; Allah has sent down no authority for them. Judgment belongs to Allah alone. He has commanded that you worship none but Him. That is the upright religion, but most people do not know.
interpretation: The verse teaches that objects of worship have no divine authority merely because people have named or revered them. True worship belongs exclusively to Allah, whose command is the basis of the upright religion; people’s failure to recognize this stems from their ignorance.

translation: O my two companions in prison, one of you will serve wine to his master; as for the other, he will be crucified, and birds will eat from his head. The matter about which you both asked has been decided.
interpretation: Joseph delivers the two dream interpretations plainly and without evasion: one man will be restored to serving the king, while the other will face execution. His words present the outcome as settled, underscoring that he speaks with confidence about what God has made known to him.

translation: He said to the one of the two whom he thought would be saved, “Mention me to your master.” But Satan caused him to forget to mention him to his master, so Joseph remained in prison for several years.
interpretation: Joseph sought the cupbearer’s help in bringing his case before the king, but the request was forgotten and his release was delayed. The verse portrays this delay as part of his trial, while showing how events beyond a person’s control can prolong hardship.

translation: The king said, “I see seven fat cows being eaten by seven lean ones, and seven green ears of grain and others dry. O assembly, explain my dream to me, if you can interpret dreams.”
interpretation: The dream points to seven years of abundance followed by seven years of hardship, and serves as a warning that prosperity should be used wisely to prepare for scarcity.

translation: They said, “A jumble of dreams—and we have no knowledge of how to interpret dreams.”
interpretation: Their response reflects the limits of their understanding: they dismiss the king’s vision as confused rather than claiming certainty about its meaning.

translation: And the one of the two who had been released remembered after a time and said, “I will tell you its interpretation, so send me forth.”
interpretation: The verse shows how God may bring relief through a seemingly forgotten connection: the cupbearer’s memory returns at the moment the king needs an answer, opening the way for Joseph’s knowledge to be recognized.

translation: “Joseph, O man of truth, explain to us the meaning of seven fat cows devoured by seven lean ones, and seven green ears of grain and others dry, so that I may return to the people and perhaps they may understand.”
interpretation: The speaker’s address reflects his confidence in Joseph’s truthfulness and wisdom: he seeks an interpretation that will bring understanding to the people and help them know how to respond to what the dream signifies.

translation: He said, “You will sow for seven consecutive years. Whatever you harvest, leave it in its ear, except for a little that you eat.”
interpretation: The verse teaches the wisdom of preparing for hardship during times of plenty: preserve resources carefully and consume only what is needed, so that present abundance can sustain people through future scarcity.

translation: Then after that will come seven years of hardship, which will consume what you stored for them, except a little that you preserve.
interpretation: The seven years of hardship will use up the harvest saved during the years of plenty, so people should conserve a small portion carefully for what they will need afterward.

translation: Then, after that, a year will come in which people will be given relief and in which they will press [their produce].
interpretation: The verse points to God’s mercy in bringing relief after hardship: abundance will return, allowing people to benefit from the fruits of their crops and labor.

translation: The king said, “Bring him to me.” When the messenger came to him, Joseph said, “Return to your master and ask him about the women who cut their hands. Indeed, my Lord knows their scheming.”
interpretation: Joseph did not leave prison immediately; he sought to have the accusation against him clarified first, so that his innocence would be established openly. His words show confidence that God knows the women’s intentions and that the truth will come to light.

translation: He said, “What was your affair when you tried to entice Joseph?” They said, “God forbid! We know no evil of him.” The wife of the noble official said, “Now the truth has become clear: I tried to entice him, and he is surely among the truthful.”
interpretation: The confession reveals that Joseph’s innocence is established not by his own claim alone but by the admission of the one who accused him. The wife’s acknowledgment that he spoke truthfully marks the moment when deception gives way to clear truth.

translation: “That is so he may know that I did not betray him in his absence, and that Allah does not guide the schemes of those who betray.”
interpretation: The speaker seeks to make clear that her confession is meant to establish her innocence toward the man who was absent, while affirming that treachery cannot ultimately prosper against Allah’s guidance and justice.

translation: “I do not claim my self to be free of fault. The soul is indeed prone to evil, except when my Lord shows mercy. Surely my Lord is Forgiving, Merciful.”
interpretation: The verse teaches humility about one’s own moral weakness: a person should not trust their soul as though it were beyond wrongdoing, but seek God’s mercy, forgiveness, and help to resist evil.

translation: The king said, “Bring him to me; I will make him one of my trusted advisers.” When he spoke with him, he said, “Today you hold a position of authority and trust with us.”
interpretation: The king’s words show that Yusuf’s integrity and wisdom were recognized through direct conversation, earning him both authority and confidence. The verse highlights how trustworthiness can lead to responsibility and standing.

translation: He said, “Appoint me over the storehouses of the land. Indeed, I am a trustworthy guardian and knowledgeable.”
interpretation: Joseph asks to oversee the land’s provisions because he knows he can safeguard them and manage them wisely. His request presents responsible service—grounded in both integrity and competence—as a means of protecting people’s resources.

translation: And thus We established Joseph in the land, where he could settle wherever he wished. We bestow Our mercy upon whom We will, and We do not let the reward of those who do good go to waste.
interpretation: Joseph’s rise to security and authority shows that God’s mercy can bring relief and a place of honor after hardship. His story also affirms that sincere goodness is never lost, even when its reward is delayed.

translation: And the reward of the Hereafter is better for those who believe and are mindful of God.
interpretation: The verse directs attention beyond the immediate gains of worldly life: lasting reward belongs to those whose faith shapes their choices and whose awareness of God leads them to avoid wrongdoing. Their patience in doing what is right is ultimately rewarded in a way greater and more enduring than anything this world can offer.

translation: And Joseph’s brothers came and entered his presence. He recognized them, but they did not recognize him.
interpretation: The contrast in recognition underscores how circumstances had transformed Joseph’s position: he could see who stood before him, while his brothers could not yet perceive the identity and authority of the man whose fate they had once shaped.

translation: When he had supplied them with their provisions, he said, “Bring me a brother of yours from your father. Do you not see that I give full measure and am the best of hosts?”
interpretation: Joseph reassures his brothers that they will be treated generously and hospitably, while asking them to bring their brother Benjamin on their next visit. His words offer them a reason to trust his invitation and return.

translation: “If you do not bring him to me, then you will receive no measure from me, and you must not come near me.”
interpretation: The speaker makes any further provision contingent on their bringing the person requested, and the forceful warning underscores that this condition is not open to negotiation.

translation: They said, “We will try to persuade his father to let him come with us, and we will surely do so.”
interpretation: Their emphatic promise expresses confidence that they can win their father’s consent, though the wording suggests persuasion rather than certainty that he will agree.

translation: And he said to his attendants, “Put their goods back into their saddle-bags, so that they may recognize them when they return to their family; perhaps they will come back.”
interpretation: Joseph had their payment secretly returned as an act of generosity and as a means of encouraging them to come back, while allowing them to discover his kindness on their own.

translation: When they returned to their father, they said, “Our father, the measure of grain has been withheld from us, so send our brother with us that we may obtain our measure. We will surely guard him.”
interpretation: The brothers appeal to their father’s concern for the family’s provisions, while promising to protect their brother in order to gain his consent to the journey.

translation: He said, “Should I entrust him to you as I entrusted his brother to you before? Allah is the best guardian, and He is the most merciful of those who show mercy.”
interpretation: Jacob’s words reflect the pain of his earlier loss and his understandable caution, yet his ultimate trust rests with Allah. He recognizes that human protection has limits, while Allah’s guardianship and mercy are perfect.

translation: When they opened their baggage, they found that their goods had been returned to them. They said, “Father, what more could we ask for? Here are our goods, returned to us. We can provision our family, protect our brother, and obtain an additional camel-load. That is an easy measure.”
interpretation: The brothers present the returned goods as reassurance to their father: they can use them to secure provisions for the family, while bringing Benjamin would allow them to receive an extra measure. Their words are meant to persuade him that entrusting Benjamin to them would benefit the whole family.

translation: He said, “I will not send him with you until you give me a solemn pledge before God that you will surely bring him back to me, unless you are overwhelmed by circumstances.” When they gave him their pledge, he said, “God is the Guardian over what we say.”
interpretation: Jacob’s pledge reflects a father’s caution after the loss of Joseph: he asks his sons to take serious responsibility for Benjamin, while recognizing that events beyond their control may make their promise impossible to fulfill. By invoking God as Guardian, he places their words and intentions under divine witness and accountability.

translation: He said, “My sons, do not enter by one gate; enter by separate gates. Yet I cannot protect you from Allah in any way. Judgment belongs to Allah alone. In Him I place my trust, and in Him let all who trust place their trust.”
interpretation: Jacob’s advice shows that reliance on God does not mean neglecting sensible precautions. He takes steps to guard his sons, while recognizing that no precaution can override God’s judgment; therefore, the outcome is entrusted to Him alone.

translation: When they entered by the way their father had instructed them, it could not protect them from anything decreed by God; it only fulfilled a concern in Jacob’s heart. He was indeed possessed of knowledge because We had taught him, though most people do not know.
interpretation: Jacob’s advice was a sensible precaution and a way to ease his concern for his sons, not a means of escaping God’s decree. His knowledge lay in understanding that precautions do not control outcomes: all unfolds under God’s will, a truth many people fail to recognize.

translation: When they entered upon Joseph, he drew his brother close to him and said, “I am indeed your brother, so do not grieve over what they used to do.”
interpretation: Joseph privately reassures his brother that their bond remains, comforting him over the harm caused by their other brothers and giving him hope amid the trial.

translation: When he had furnished them with their provisions, he placed the drinking cup in his brother’s saddlebag. Then a caller called out, “O caravan, you are surely thieves!”
interpretation: The placement of the cup sets in motion a plan by which Joseph can keep his brother with him. The accusation is part of that unfolding plan; it does not mean the brothers had actually stolen anything.

translation: They said, turning toward them, “What is it that you are missing?”
interpretation: Their question invites the others to identify the loss, opening the way for the matter to be clarified rather than answered with assumption.

translation: They said, “We are missing the king’s measuring cup. Whoever brings it shall receive a camel-load, and I guarantee it.”
interpretation: The public promise of a substantial reward, backed by a personal guarantee, underscores the speaker’s confidence and responsibility in ensuring that the pledge will be fulfilled.

translation: They said, “By God, you know that we did not come to spread corruption in the land, and we are not thieves.”
interpretation: The brothers appeal to what the people already know of them as evidence that they did not come intending wrongdoing and did not steal the missing cup. Their words express confidence in their innocence of the specific accusation before them.

translation: They said, “Then what is its punishment, if you are lying?”
interpretation: They ask what consequence should follow if the accusation is false, inviting the accusers to state the rule by which the matter should be judged.

translation: They said, “Its recompense is that the one in whose baggage it is found shall himself be its recompense. Thus do we requite the wrongdoers.”
interpretation: They declared the penalty according to their own law: whoever was found with the stolen object would be held in return for it. Their judgment would later allow Joseph to retain Benjamin, while they themselves acknowledged that such a penalty was just for wrongdoing.

translation: So he began with their bags before his brother’s bag, then he brought it out from his brother’s bag. Thus did We devise a plan for Joseph. He could not have taken his brother under the king’s law unless Allah willed. We raise in rank whom We will, and above every possessor of knowledge is one more knowing.
interpretation: Joseph’s plan unfolded through means that appeared to follow the king’s law, while ultimately serving Allah’s will: it allowed Joseph to keep his brother when the law otherwise gave him no right to do so. The verse also reminds us that human knowledge and wisdom are limited; however elevated someone may be, there is always knowledge beyond theirs, and all ranks of understanding are granted by Allah.

translation: They said, “If he has stolen, then a brother of his stole before him.” But Joseph kept it within himself and did not reveal it to them. He said, “You are worse in standing, and Allah knows best what you allege.”
interpretation: Joseph’s silence shows his restraint: he did not answer their hurtful accusation with an angry outburst. Inwardly, he recognized that their conduct was worse, while entrusting the truth of their claims to Allah, who knows what is concealed and what is spoken.

translation: They said, “O exalted one, he has a father who is very old, so take one of us in his place. We truly see you as one of those who do good.”
interpretation: Their appeal draws on the ruler’s compassion: they ask him to spare Benjamin out of consideration for their elderly father, offering themselves instead and trusting in the kindness they have seen from him.

translation: He said, “God forbid that we should take anyone except the one with whom we found our property. Indeed, then we would be wrongdoers.”
interpretation: He refuses to punish someone who was not found with the missing property, affirming that justice forbids taking an innocent person in another’s place.

translation: When they had despaired of him, they withdrew to confer privately. Their eldest said, “Do you not know that your father took from you a solemn pledge by Allah, and that before this you failed in your duty concerning Joseph? I will not leave this land until my father permits me or Allah decides for me; and He is the best of judges.”
interpretation: The eldest brother recognizes that their present predicament is bound up with the trust they had already betrayed over Joseph. He therefore refuses to return without Benjamin, treating his father’s pledge as a serious responsibility and leaving the outcome to his father’s decision or Allah’s judgment.

translation: Return to your father and say, ‘Our father, your son has stolen. We testified only to what we knew, and we could not have known what was hidden.’
interpretation: The brothers acknowledge the limits of their testimony: they can report only what they witnessed and understood, not claim knowledge of hidden circumstances or events beyond their awareness.

translation: Ask the town where we were and the caravan with which we came; indeed, we are telling the truth.
interpretation: The speakers appeal to witnesses in the town and among the caravan to affirm that their account is truthful.

translation: He said, “Rather, your own selves have made something seem right to you. So beautiful patience is fitting. Perhaps Allah will bring them all back to me. Surely He is the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.”
interpretation: Jacob responds to his sons’ account without surrendering to despair. His “beautiful patience” means bearing grief with dignity and turning his hope to Allah, trusting that Allah knows the full reality of his hardship and, in His wisdom, can reunite him with those he has lost.

translation: He turned away from them and said, “Oh, my sorrow for Joseph!” His eyes became white from grief, while he held his anguish within.
interpretation: The verse shows that profound sorrow is not incompatible with faith or patience: Jacob feels and contains his grief without letting it become despair or resentment toward God.

translation: They said, “By Allah, you will not cease remembering Joseph until you waste away or become one of those who perish.”
interpretation: They rebuke Jacob for allowing grief over Joseph to consume him, fearing that his continual longing will leave him utterly debilitated or bring him near death.

translation: He said, “I complain of my anguish and sorrow only to Allah, and I know from Allah what you do not know.”
interpretation: Jacob directs his deepest grief to God alone, finding in Him the refuge and hope that others cannot see. His sorrow does not extinguish his trust: he remains certain that God’s mercy and promise hold a reality beyond what his family knows.

translation: “O my sons, go and seek news of Joseph and his brother, and do not despair of God’s relief. Indeed, none despairs of God’s relief except the disbelieving people.”
interpretation: Jacob teaches that trust in God should sustain hope even when circumstances seem bleak. A believer continues to seek what is right while remaining confident that God can bring relief in ways one cannot foresee.

translation: When they entered upon him, they said, “O eminent one, hardship has afflicted us and our family, and we have brought goods of little value. So give us our full measure and be charitable to us. Indeed, Allah rewards those who give charity.”
interpretation: Their plea reveals how hardship has humbled them and places Joseph in a position to answer their vulnerability with mercy rather than vengeance. The verse thus points to the moral worth of generosity toward those in need, and assures that such kindness is never lost with Allah.

translation: He said, “Do you know what you did to Joseph and his brother when you were ignorant?”
interpretation: Joseph gently confronts his brothers with the harm they caused, inviting them to recognize their past wrongdoing. By describing them as ignorant, he acknowledges their moral blindness at the time and leaves room for remorse and reconciliation.

translation: They said, “Are you truly Joseph?” He said, “I am Joseph, and this is my brother. God has indeed favored us. Surely whoever is mindful of God and patient—God never lets the reward of those who do good go to waste.”
interpretation: Joseph recognizes that his eventual reunion and vindication are blessings from God, and he points to the enduring worth of righteousness: reverence for God and patience through hardship are never wasted, even when their reward is long delayed.

translation: They said, “By Allah, God has truly favored you over us, and we were indeed in the wrong.”
interpretation: Their words express a sincere admission that their envy and mistreatment of Joseph were wrong, while recognizing that God had raised him to a position of honor. The verse highlights the humility required to acknowledge wrongdoing when the truth becomes clear.

translation: He said, “There is no blame upon you today. May Allah forgive you; He is the Most Merciful of those who show mercy.”
interpretation: Joseph responds to his brothers’ wrongdoing with forgiveness rather than reproach, entrusting their forgiveness to Allah and showing that mercy can open the way to reconciliation.

translation: Take this shirt of mine and cast it over my father’s face; he will regain his sight. Then bring me all your family.
interpretation: The shirt is a means through which God brings relief and restores Jacob’s sight, showing that hope can remain alive even through long hardship. Joseph’s invitation to bring the whole family also points toward reconciliation and the healing of a family fractured by betrayal.

translation: And when the caravan had departed, their father said, “Indeed, I sense the scent of Joseph—if only you would not think me mistaken.”
interpretation: Jacob’s words express the depth of his enduring hope and attachment to Joseph: even after years of separation, he remains receptive to signs that his son may be near, though he knows his family may dismiss his conviction.

translation: They said, “By Allah, you are still in your old delusion.”
interpretation: They mistook Jacob’s enduring hope and grief for Joseph for a delusion rooted in the past; their words reveal how little they understood the truth behind his steadfast faith.

translation: Then, when the bearer of good news arrived, he placed it over his face, and he regained his sight. He said, “Did I not tell you that I know from Allah what you do not know?”
interpretation: Jacob’s words express his trust in Allah’s mercy and knowledge, even when others could not see a way forward. The reunion and restoration of his sight vindicate that trust: what seemed impossible to those around him remained within Allah’s power and wisdom.

translation: They said, “Our father, ask forgiveness for our sins; indeed, we were at fault.”
interpretation: Their words express remorse and an admission of guilt: they recognize that they have wronged Joseph and seek their father’s help in asking God for forgiveness.

translation: He said, “I will ask my Lord to forgive you. Indeed, He is the All-Forgiving, the Most Merciful.”
interpretation: The verse reflects the Prophet Ya‘qub’s hope in Allah’s mercy and his willingness to intercede for his sons, showing that sincere repentance is met with the possibility of forgiveness.

translation: When they came before Joseph, he drew his parents close to him and said, “Enter Egypt, God willing, in safety.”
interpretation: The long-awaited reunion marks the fulfillment of God’s promise to Joseph: after years of hardship and separation, his family is brought together in security. Joseph’s words also show that safety and blessing are ultimately by God’s will.

translation: He raised his parents onto the throne, and they bowed down before him. He said, “Father, this is the fulfillment of my earlier dream. My Lord has made it come true. He was gracious to me when He brought me out of prison and brought you from the desert, after Satan had stirred discord between me and my brothers. My Lord is subtle in accomplishing what He wills. He is truly All-Knowing, All-Wise.”
interpretation: Joseph recognizes that his long-awaited reunion and rise to honor are the fulfillment of his dream, while attributing the good in his life to God’s gracious care. He speaks of his brothers’ wrongdoing gently, without reopening old wounds, and sees even the painful events that separated his family as part of God’s wise and subtle plan. The bowing is an act of honor in the custom of that time, not worship.

translation: My Lord, You have granted me some authority and taught me the interpretation of events. Creator of the heavens and the earth, You are my protector in this world and the Hereafter. Let me die in submission to You, and join me with the righteous.
interpretation: The prayer teaches that worldly authority and knowledge are gifts from God, while true security rests in His care. Even after receiving great blessings, a believer asks above all to remain faithful until death and to be joined with the righteous.

translation: That is among the reports of the unseen that We reveal to you. You were not with them when they agreed upon their plan while they were plotting.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the account comes to the Prophet through divine revelation: he was not present to witness the events or their secret plotting. It therefore presents the Qur’anic account as knowledge granted by God, not knowledge acquired from those involved.

translation: And most people, however earnestly you may desire it, will not be believers.
interpretation: Even the Prophet’s sincere longing for people to believe cannot make faith universal; guidance is not achieved by human effort alone, and his responsibility is to convey the truth faithfully.

translation: And you ask them for no payment for it; it is only a reminder to all peoples.
interpretation: The message is not offered for worldly gain: its truth and guidance are meant freely for all people, calling them to remember God and live by His guidance.

translation: How many signs there are in the heavens and the earth that they pass by, turning away from them.
interpretation: The verse points to a deep heedlessness: signs of God are not distant or hidden, but people can encounter them continually and still refuse to reflect on what they reveal.

translation: Most of them believe in Allah only while associating others with Him.
interpretation: The verse warns that acknowledging Allah is not sufficient if a person also assigns to others a share in what belongs to Him alone, such as worship or ultimate devotion.

translation: Do they feel secure that an overwhelming punishment from God will not come upon them, or that the Hour will not arrive suddenly while they are unaware?
interpretation: The verse warns against complacency: no one should assume that worldly security will last or postpone turning to God, since accountability may arrive without warning.

translation: Say, “This is my way: I call to Allah with clear insight—I and those who follow me. Glory be to Allah, and I am not among those who associate others with Him.”
interpretation: The verse presents calling people to Allah as a path grounded in clear knowledge and conviction, shared by the Prophet and his followers. It affirms that this call is devoted to Allah alone, free of associating partners with Him.

translation: We sent before you only men to whom We revealed, from among the people of the towns. Have they not traveled through the land and seen what was the end of those who came before them? The home of the Hereafter is better for those who are mindful of God. Will you not reason?
interpretation: The passage reassures the Prophet that God’s messengers before him were human beings, not angels, and calls people to learn from the fate of earlier communities. Its warning is also a call to look beyond immediate worldly outcomes: for those who remain mindful of God, the lasting reward of the Hereafter is better.

translation: Until, when the messengers had despaired and thought they had been denied, Our help came to them. Then We saved whom We willed, and Our punishment cannot be averted from the guilty people.
interpretation: The verse depicts the moment when rejection and hardship had reached their utmost, yet the messengers’ trials ended with God’s decisive help. Their deliverance—and the punishment of those who persisted in wrongdoing—rests entirely with God.

translation: Indeed, in their stories is a lesson for people of understanding. This is not a tale invented, but a confirmation of what came before it, an explanation of all things, and guidance and mercy for people who believe.
interpretation: The accounts of earlier people are meant to teach those who reflect: they show how faith, patience, and trust in God matter through hardship and its outcome. The Qur’an presents these accounts not as fiction, but as part of its confirmation of earlier revelation and as guidance that brings mercy to those who believe.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Alif Lam Mim Ra. These are the verses of the Book. What has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth, but most people do not believe.
interpretation: The opening letters belong to the mysterious, disjointed letters whose full meaning is known to Allah. The verse affirms that the revelation given to the Prophet is truly from his Lord, even when many people reject it; their disbelief does not diminish its truth.

translation: Allah is the One who raised the heavens without pillars that you can see. Then He established Himself over the Throne, and subjected the sun and the moon; each runs its course for an appointed term. He directs every affair and makes the signs clear, so that you may be certain of the meeting with your Lord.
interpretation: The ordered heavens and the sun and moon’s appointed courses are signs of Allah’s power and governance. By reflecting on these signs and on how He makes His guidance clear, people are called to trust that their meeting with their Lord is certain.

translation: He is the One who spread out the earth and placed firm mountains and rivers in it. And of every kind of fruit He made two kinds. He makes the night cover the day. Surely in that are signs for people who reflect.
interpretation: The verse invites reflection on how the world’s variety and rhythms are ordered to sustain life. Its changing forms and paired kinds point beyond themselves to the wisdom and power of the One who brings them into being, encouraging people to recognize purpose in creation rather than regard it as happenstance.

translation: And on the earth are neighboring plots, gardens of grapevines, crops, and date palms—some growing in clusters from a shared root and others separately. They are watered with the same water, yet We make some of them better than others in their produce. Surely in this are signs for people who reason.
interpretation: The verse invites reflection on how diversity and distinction emerge even where the conditions are shared. This points to a Creator whose power and wisdom are not limited by apparent sameness, and whose signs can be recognized through thoughtful observation.

translation: If you are astonished, then astonishing indeed is their saying: “When we have become dust, shall we really be created anew?” Those are the ones who disbelieve in their Lord; shackles will be around their necks, and they are the companions of the Fire, where they will remain forever.
interpretation: The verse presents denial of resurrection as the real cause for wonder: they regard being raised from dust as impossible despite their Lord’s power. Their rejection is portrayed as a bondage that leads to the lasting consequences of the Fire.

translation: They ask you to hasten the punishment before the good, though exemplary punishments have already befallen those before them. Surely your Lord is full of forgiveness for people despite their wrongdoing, and surely your Lord is severe in punishment.
interpretation: The delay of punishment is an expression of God’s forbearance, giving wrongdoers room to repent; it is not a sign that wrongdoing goes unanswered. The fate of earlier peoples stands as a warning that forgiveness and accountability are both real.

translation: Those who disbelieve say, “Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord?” You are only a warner, and every people has a guide.
interpretation: The verse redirects attention from demands for a sign to the Prophet’s mission: he is charged with warning, while guidance for every people is ultimately provided by God through those who lead them toward the truth.

translation: Allah knows what every female carries, what the wombs diminish and what they increase; and everything with Him is by a precise measure.
interpretation: Nothing about creation is hidden from Allah—not even the changes within the wombs—and every matter unfolds according to His exact knowledge and decree.

translation: Knower of the unseen and the seen, the Most Great, the Most Exalted.
interpretation: God’s knowledge encompasses all that is hidden and all that is manifest, while His greatness and exaltedness place Him above every limitation and beyond comparison with creation.

translation: It is the same whether any of you conceals his speech or declares it, and whether he is hidden by night or moves about openly by day.
interpretation: The verse teaches that nothing about a person is beyond God’s knowledge: neither private words nor concealed movements escape His awareness.

translation: He has angels who follow one another, before him and behind him, guarding him by Allah’s command. Indeed, Allah does not change a people’s condition until they change what is within themselves. And when Allah wills harm for a people, none can turn it back, and they have no protector apart from Him.
interpretation: The verse teaches that a people’s lasting change begins with what they cultivate within themselves— their beliefs, intentions, and conduct—while all protection and outcomes remain subject to Allah’s will. When His decree comes, no one can override it or provide protection in His place.

translation: He is the One who shows you lightning, inspiring fear and hope, and brings forth heavy clouds.
