interpretation: The lightning’s danger and the promise of rain awaken both awe and hope, directing people to recognize God’s power and care in the forces of nature.

translation: The thunder glorifies Him with praise, as do the angels in awe of Him. He sends thunderbolts, striking with them whom He wills, while they dispute about God; and He is mighty in power.
interpretation: The verse presents the thunder and the angels as signs of God’s majesty, contrasting their glorification and awe with people’s dispute about Him. Such dispute cannot diminish God’s power, which is beyond human resistance.

translation: To Him alone belongs the true invocation. Those whom they call upon besides Him answer them nothing—like someone stretching out his hands toward water, hoping it will reach his mouth, though it never reaches it. The invocation of the disbelievers is only in vain.
interpretation: The verse portrays calling upon anything besides God as futile: such objects cannot hear or fulfill the caller’s need, just as water does not reach someone merely because they stretch their hands toward it. True help and response belong to God alone.

translation: To Allah prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly, as do their shadows in the mornings and the evenings.
interpretation: All creation is subject to Allah’s authority: some submit to Him knowingly and willingly, while all beings are bound by the order He has set for them. The shadows’ changing forms likewise point to the dependence of creation on Him, even when that submission is not a conscious act.

translation: Say, “Who is the Lord of the heavens and the earth?” Say, “Allah.” Say, “Have you then taken protectors besides Him, who possess no power to bring benefit or harm even to themselves?” Say, “Are the blind and the seeing equal, or are darknesses and light equal? Or have they assigned partners to Allah who created as He creates, so that creation has become indistinguishable to them?” Say, “Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is the One, the All-Subduing.”
interpretation: The verse calls people to recognize that the power to create and govern belongs uniquely to Allah. Anything worshipped besides Him is unable even to secure its own benefit or ward off harm, and therefore cannot be His equal. Just as sight is not like blindness and light is not like darkness, recognizing Allah’s oneness is not equivalent to confusing Him with powerless beings. Allah alone is the Creator and sovereign over all.

translation: He sends down water from the sky, and valleys flow according to their measure; then the torrent carries swelling foam. And from what they heat in the fire to make ornaments or other goods comes foam like it. Thus God sets forth the comparison of truth and falsehood: the foam vanishes as refuse, while what benefits people remains on the earth. Thus God sets forth parables.
interpretation: The image teaches that falsehood may rise conspicuously and seem powerful, like foam on a flood or molten metal, but it has no lasting substance. Truth may be less showy, yet it endures and brings benefit; its lasting worth is not measured by how much noise or display surrounds it.

translation: For those who respond to their Lord is the finest reward. But those who do not respond to Him—even if they possessed everything on earth, and as much again, they would offer it all as ransom. They will face an evil reckoning, and their home will be Hell. What a wretched resting place!
interpretation: The verse teaches that no worldly wealth can substitute for responding faithfully to God or undo the consequences of rejecting Him. True security lies in turning to God, not in possessions that cannot avert accountability.

translation: Can one who knows that what has been sent down to you from your Lord is the truth be like one who is blind? Only people of understanding take heed.
interpretation: The verse distinguishes clear-sighted faith from a heart closed to truth: recognizing revelation as true should shape how one sees and lives, while sound understanding moves a person to reflect and heed its guidance.

translation: Those who fulfill Allah’s covenant and do not break the pact.
interpretation: This describes people whose faith is shown through integrity: they honor the obligations they have undertaken before Allah and remain trustworthy in their commitments, even when keeping them is difficult.

translation: And those who maintain what Allah has commanded to be maintained, fear their Lord, and dread the evil reckoning.
interpretation: Their devotion is shown by preserving the bonds and responsibilities Allah has enjoined—especially ties of kinship and faith—while living with reverence for Him and awareness that they will be held accountable.

translation: And those who are patient, seeking the pleasure of their Lord, establish prayer, give in charity from what We have provided for them, privately and publicly, and repel evil with good—for them is the ultimate home.
interpretation: True steadfastness is not mere endurance: it is patience directed toward God’s approval and expressed through worship, generosity, and responding to harm with what is better. The verse teaches that these qualities shape a person toward the lasting reward of the Hereafter.

translation: Gardens of everlasting residence, which they will enter along with the righteous among their parents, spouses, and descendants; and the angels will enter upon them through every gate.
interpretation: The verse portrays the reward of faith as both lasting security and joyful fellowship: the righteous are reunited with loved ones who shared their goodness, and the angels’ welcome from every gate conveys their honored and peaceful arrival.

translation: “Peace be upon you for your patience. How excellent is the final home!”
interpretation: The greeting honors the believers’ steadfastness through hardship and obedience: their patience was not in vain, but brought them to the lasting security and joy of Paradise.

translation: As for those who break God’s covenant after affirming it, sever what God has commanded to be joined, and spread corruption in the land—for them is the curse, and theirs is the evil abode.
interpretation: The verse presents fidelity to God as inseparable from honoring the bonds and responsibilities He has established among people. Deliberately tearing those bonds apart is not merely a private failing: it damages the moral order of life, and its lasting consequence is estrangement from God’s mercy.

translation: Allah enlarges provision for whomever He wills and restricts it. They rejoice in the life of this world, but the life of this world, compared with the Hereafter, is only a brief enjoyment.
interpretation: Material abundance is not a measure of ultimate worth or lasting success. The verse calls people not to let temporary worldly pleasures distract them from the enduring life of the Hereafter.

translation: Those who disbelieve say, “Why has no sign been sent down to him from his Lord?” Say, “Indeed, Allah leaves astray whom He wills, and guides to Himself whoever turns back to Him.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that demanding a further sign does not by itself open a person to faith. Guidance is found by turning sincerely to God; those who persist in turning away are left to the path they have chosen, while God guides those who seek Him.

translation: Those who believe and whose hearts find peace in the remembrance of Allah—surely, in the remembrance of Allah hearts find peace.
interpretation: The verse teaches that lasting inner peace is rooted in remembering Allah: turning the heart toward Him brings reassurance and steadiness amid life’s uncertainty.

translation: Those who believe and do righteous deeds—blessedness is theirs, and a beautiful return.
interpretation: True prosperity belongs to those whose faith is expressed through righteous action: God grants them a blessed life and, in the end, a gracious homecoming to Him.

translation: Thus We sent you to a community before whom other communities had passed away, so that you might recite to them what We have revealed to you, while they deny the Most Merciful. Say, “He is my Lord; there is no god but Him. In Him I place my trust, and to Him I turn back.”
interpretation: The verse presents the Prophet’s mission as part of a continuing divine guidance: rejection by his people does not diminish the truth of the revelation. By commanding him to affirm his trust and return to God alone, it teaches that steadfastness amid denial rests on recognizing God as the sole Lord and turning back to Him.

translation: Had there been a Qur’an by which mountains were set in motion, the earth split apart, or the dead were made to speak, it would still be so that all affairs belong to Allah. Have the believers not understood that, had Allah willed, He would have guided all people? Those who disbelieve will continue to be struck by calamity for what they have done, or calamity will fall close to their homes, until Allah’s promise comes. Surely Allah does not fail in His promise.
interpretation: The verse answers those who demand extraordinary signs: even the greatest miracle would not compel faith, for authority over all things—and over guidance—belongs to Allah. Believers are reminded that Allah could guide everyone if He willed, while those who reject the truth remain answerable for their deeds and face the consequences until His promised judgment comes.

translation: Messengers before you were surely mocked, but I gave the disbelievers respite; then I seized them. So how terrible was My punishment!
interpretation: The mockery faced by earlier messengers did not mean that God had abandoned them or approved of their deniers. The delay in punishment was a respite, not safety: in time, those who persisted in disbelief faced the consequence of their rejection. The verse therefore reassures the Prophet and warns those who mock the message not to mistake patience for impunity.

translation: Is He who watches over every soul and what it has earned [like their supposed partners]? Yet they have set up partners for Allah. Say, “Name them!” Or are you informing Him of something He does not know on earth, or is it merely a claim made in words? Rather, the schemes of those who disbelieve have been made alluring to them, and they have been turned away from the path. Whoever Allah allows to stray has no guide.
interpretation: The verse challenges the claim that anything shares in God’s authority: if these alleged partners were real, they could be identified and supported by knowledge, not merely asserted. Their supposed power is instead an illusion sustained by their own schemes, which turns them from the truth; without God’s guidance, no one can lead them back.

translation: For them is punishment in the life of this world, and the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe; and they will have no protector against God.
interpretation: The verse warns that worldly consequences are not the limit of accountability: the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe, and no one can shield those who face it from God’s judgment.

translation: The description of the Garden promised to the God-conscious is this: rivers flow beneath it; its food is everlasting, as is its shade. That is the final abode of those who are mindful of God, while the final abode of the disbelievers is the Fire.
interpretation: The verse presents lasting fulfillment as the fruit of God-consciousness: unlike worldly pleasures that fade, Paradise’s provision and shade endure. Its closing contrast makes clear that a person’s ultimate destination is shaped by whether they respond to God with faith and obedience.

translation: Those to whom We gave the Scripture rejoice in what has been sent down to you, while among the factions are those who reject part of it. Say, “I have only been commanded to worship Allah and associate none with Him. To Him I call, and to Him is my return.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the Qur’an as continuing the guidance known through earlier revelation: those who recognize that continuity welcome it, while selective rejection by others does not alter the Prophet’s charge. His call rests on undivided devotion to Allah, and his return to Him underscores that this mission is ultimately answerable to God.

translation: Thus We have sent it down as an Arabic judgment. If you were to follow their desires after the knowledge that has come to you, you would have no protector or defender against God.
interpretation: The verse presents the Qur’an as divine guidance expressed in Arabic and warns that no one—even the Prophet—could set aside God’s revealed knowledge to satisfy others’ desires and still expect protection from Him. The conditional warning underscores the absolute authority of revelation.

translation: We certainly sent messengers before you and gave them spouses and offspring. No messenger could bring a sign except by God’s permission. For every appointed time there is a decree.
interpretation: The verse presents messengers as human beings with family lives, while affirming that their mission and any signs they bring remain wholly under God’s authority. Revelation and its events unfold according to the time and decree God has appointed, not by a messenger’s independent power.

translation: Allah erases whatever He wills and confirms whatever He wills, and with Him is the Mother of the Book.
interpretation: The verse teaches that God, in His wisdom, may alter or affirm what is decreed, while the ultimate source and knowledge of all decrees remain with Him.

translation: Whether We show you some of what We have warned them of, or take you in death, your duty is only to deliver the message; the reckoning is Ours.
interpretation: The verse reassures the Prophet that the outcome of his people’s rejection does not depend on his witnessing it in this life. His responsibility is to convey the message faithfully; ultimate judgment belongs to God.

translation: Have they not seen that We come to the land, diminishing it at its edges? Allah decrees, and none can overturn His decree; and He is swift in reckoning.
interpretation: The verse points to the gradual contraction of the deniers’ lands and power as a sign that their resistance cannot escape God’s decree. Their decline is a warning that His judgment will come, and no one can hold it back.

translation: Those before them also plotted, but all counter-scheming belongs to Allah. He knows what every soul earns, and the disbelievers will come to know for whom the final home is.
interpretation: Human schemes cannot escape Allah’s knowledge or overcome His power. Every person’s deeds are known to Him, and the true outcome will become clear: the lasting good end belongs to those whom Allah favors, not to those who rely on plotting against the truth.

translation: Those who disbelieve say, “You are not a messenger.” Say, “Allah is sufficient as a witness between me and you, as is whoever possesses knowledge of the Book.”
interpretation: The denial of the disbelievers does not diminish the truth of the Messenger’s mission. Allah’s testimony is decisive, and those who truly know the revealed scriptures can recognize the signs that confirm it.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Alif Lām Rā. A Book We have sent down to you so that, by their Lord’s permission, you may bring people out of darkness into light—to the path of the Almighty, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: The Qur’an is presented as divine guidance that leads people from the darkness of error and heedlessness into the light of faith and right conduct. The Prophet conveys this guidance by Allah’s permission, calling people to the way of the One who is mighty in authority and worthy of all praise.

translation: Allah is the One to whom belongs all that is in the heavens and all that is on the earth. Woe to the disbelievers because of a severe punishment.
interpretation: Since all creation belongs to Allah, rejecting Him is a grave defiance of the One with ultimate authority, and it brings a dire consequence.

translation: Those who prefer the life of this world to the Hereafter, turn people away from the path of God, and seek to make it crooked—they are far astray.
interpretation: The verse describes a deep misguidance rooted in putting worldly gain above the lasting life to come. It is compounded when people not only turn away from God’s guidance themselves, but also obstruct others and try to distort the path so that it no longer leads clearly to the truth.

translation: We did not send any messenger except in the language of his people, so that he might make the message clear to them. Then Allah allows whom He wills to stray and guides whom He wills. He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: The message is conveyed in a language its first hearers can understand, removing the barrier of obscurity; but clarity alone does not compel belief. The outcome of guidance belongs to Allah, whose authority is absolute and whose decisions are governed by wisdom.

translation: Indeed, We sent Moses with Our signs, saying, “Bring your people out of darkness into light, and remind them of the Days of Allah.” Surely in that are signs for everyone who is patient and grateful.
interpretation: Moses was commanded to lead his people from disbelief and oppression into faith and guidance, and to remind them of God’s decisive events—His blessings and deliverance, as well as His punishment of those who rejected Him. These events are lessons especially clear to those who endure hardship with patience and recognize God’s favors with gratitude.

translation: And when Moses said to his people, “Remember God’s favor upon you when He saved you from Pharaoh’s people, who inflicted terrible suffering upon you, slaughtered your sons, and spared your women. In that was a tremendous trial from your Lord.”
interpretation: Moses calls his people to see their deliverance not as mere escape from oppression, but as a profound test: their memory of God’s favor should lead them to gratitude and faithful obedience.

translation: And when your Lord proclaimed: “If you are grateful, I will surely increase you; but if you are ungrateful, surely My punishment is severe.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that gratitude is more than acknowledging blessings: it means recognizing their source in God and responding to them faithfully. Such gratitude becomes a cause of increase by God, while rejecting or misusing His blessings exposes a person to the consequences of ingratitude.

translation: Moses said, “If you and everyone on earth were to disbelieve, Allah is surely Self-Sufficient and Praiseworthy.”
interpretation: God’s worth and perfection do not depend on anyone’s faith or gratitude. Belief benefits those who believe; even universal disbelief could neither diminish God nor lessen His deserved praise.

translation: Has the account of those before you not reached you—the people of Noah, ʿĀd and Thamūd, and those who came after them, whom none knows but God? Their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they put their hands to their mouths and said, “We disbelieve in what you have been sent with, and we are in grave doubt about that to which you call us.”
interpretation: The verse recalls earlier nations who were given clear evidence through their messengers yet stubbornly rejected it. Their defiant gesture and words show a deliberate refusal to believe, rooted in deep doubt about the message; the full account of some later peoples is known only to God.

translation: Their messengers said, “Can there be any doubt about God, the Originator of the heavens and the earth? He calls you so that He may forgive you some of your sins and grant you respite until an appointed time.” They replied, “You are only human beings like us. You want to turn us away from what our forefathers worshipped, so bring us clear proof.”
interpretation: The messengers point to the created heavens and earth as signs that make belief in their Creator reasonable, and describe the call to faith as an invitation to forgiveness and a chance to live until one’s appointed term. Their opponents, instead of engaging with that evidence, reject the messengers on the grounds that they are human and demand a manifest proof—revealing how inherited custom and suspicion can obstruct a sincere response to truth.

translation: Their messengers said to them, “We are only human beings like you, but Allah grants His favor to whichever of His servants He wills. It is not for us to bring you any sign of authority except by Allah’s permission. So let the believers place their trust in Allah.”
interpretation: The messengers affirm that being human does not prevent them from carrying a divinely granted message: their selection is Allah’s favor, and any sign they bring is by His permission, not their own power. This calls believers to trust Allah as the source of guidance and authority.

translation: And why should we not rely upon Allah, when He has guided us to our ways? We will surely be patient with the harm you have inflicted upon us. And upon Allah let those who trust place their trust.
interpretation: Having been guided by God, the believers see no reason to abandon their reliance on Him, even when others harm them. Their trust is expressed through steadfast patience, and the verse calls all who place their trust in God to make Him their ultimate support.

translation: Those who disbelieved said to their messengers, “We will surely drive you out of our land, or you must return to our faith.” Then their Lord revealed to them, “We will surely destroy the wrongdoers.”
interpretation: The messengers were threatened with expulsion unless they abandoned their faith and adopted the disbelievers’ way. God’s revelation assured them that such oppression would not prevail: the wrongdoers would be brought to ruin.

translation: And We will surely settle you in the land after them. That is for whoever fears standing before Me and fears My warning.
interpretation: The promise of lasting security and settlement is linked to reverence for God: those who remain mindful that they will answer to Him and take His warning seriously are called to steadfast faith and obedience.

translation: They sought a decisive judgment, and every stubborn tyrant was brought to ruin.
interpretation: The verse portrays the outcome of the conflict between truth and oppression: those who sought God’s judgment were answered, while the arrogant tyrants who stubbornly resisted the truth were left defeated and without hope.

translation: Ahead of him lies Hell, and he will be made to drink a foul, festering fluid.
interpretation: The verse portrays the punishment awaiting the one who persists in wrongdoing: even what he is given to drink is itself a source of torment.

translation: He will gulp it down, though he can hardly swallow it. Death will come to him from every side, yet he will not die; and beyond him lies a severe punishment.
interpretation: The verse portrays punishment so agonizing that death seems to press in from every direction, yet offers no escape. Its force is to warn that this suffering is not a release from accountability, but part of a graver punishment still to come.

translation: The deeds of those who disbelieve in their Lord are like ashes swept away by a fierce wind on a stormy day. They will have no power over anything they have earned. That is the far-reaching loss.
interpretation: The verse teaches that deeds cannot secure lasting benefit if they are severed from faith in God: like ashes scattered by a storm, they leave their authors unable to recover or rely on what they once did.

translation: Have you not seen that Allah created the heavens and the earth in truth? If He wills, He can remove you and bring forth a new creation.
interpretation: The verse calls people to recognize that creation is neither purposeless nor beyond its Creator’s control. Human beings should therefore not mistake their present existence for something independent or permanent: Allah can replace them with another creation, and this awareness should lead them to humility and attentiveness to His guidance.

translation: And that is not difficult for Allah.
interpretation: The phrase affirms that nothing is beyond Allah’s power; restoring people to life is no difficulty for Him.

translation: They will all appear before Allah, and the weak will say to those who were arrogant, “We followed you, so can you relieve us of any part of Allah’s punishment?” They will reply, “If Allah had guided us, we would have guided you. It makes no difference to us whether we panic or endure patiently; there is no escape for us.”
interpretation: The exchange reveals that following powerful or influential people does not excuse anyone before Allah: each person remains answerable for their own choices. When the consequences arrive, neither blaming one’s leaders nor their inability to help can avert the punishment, and regret offers no escape.

translation: And Satan will say, when the matter has been decided, “Indeed, God promised you a true promise, and I promised you, but I failed you. I had no authority over you except that I called you, and you answered me. So do not blame me; blame yourselves. I cannot come to your aid, nor can you come to mine. Indeed, I reject your having associated me with God before.” Surely the wrongdoers will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: Satan’s words expose the limits of his influence: he could entice, but he could not compel anyone to follow him. The verse places responsibility on those who chose to answer his call, warning that blaming a tempter cannot undo one’s own choices. His final disavowal underscores the futility of treating Satan as a partner or ally against God: at judgment, neither side can rescue the other.

translation: And He will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding there by their Lord’s permission. Their greeting therein will be, “Peace.”
interpretation: The verse presents lasting felicity as a gift from God to those whose faith is expressed through righteous action. Their welcome of peace points to a life free from fear and distress, granted and sustained by their Lord.

translation: Have you not considered how Allah sets forth a parable: a good word is like a good tree, firmly rooted, with branches reaching into the sky?
interpretation: A sincere word of faith is not merely spoken; when rooted in conviction, it sustains a person’s life and continually gives rise to goodness, whose effects endure and are elevated in worth.

translation: It yields its fruit at every season by permission of its Lord. And Allah sets forth examples for people so that they may remember.
interpretation: Like a sound tree that continually bears good fruit, sincere faith produces enduring words and deeds of benefit—not by one’s own power alone, but through God’s permission. The parable invites people to reflect on the lasting goodness that faith can bring.

translation: And the likeness of a foul word is that of a foul tree, uprooted from the surface of the earth, with no firm footing.
interpretation: Falsehood has no sound foundation to sustain it; however forceful it may seem, it cannot endure or yield lasting good.

translation: Allah makes those who believe steadfast through the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter. And Allah allows the wrongdoers to stray; Allah does whatever He wills.
interpretation: The “firm word” is faith grounded in truth: Allah grants believers the steadiness to remain faithful amid the trials of this life and, in the Hereafter, to stand firm when they are questioned. Those who persist in wrongdoing are left to the misguidance they have chosen, while all outcomes remain subject to Allah’s will and wisdom.

translation: Have you not considered those who exchanged Allah’s blessing for disbelief and brought their people to the abode of ruin?
interpretation: The verse warns that rejecting God’s blessings is not merely a private failure: those who turn from gratitude and faith can lead others toward destruction, with consequences that extend beyond this life.

translation: Hell—they will burn in it, and wretched is the abode.
interpretation: The verse presents Hell as a grim and lasting destination, warning that those who arrive there will find no comfort or refuge in it.

translation: They have set up rivals to Allah in order to lead people away from His way. Say, “Enjoy yourselves for now; your destination is the Fire.”
interpretation: The warning exposes the false confidence of those who oppose God’s guidance: any worldly pleasure they gain is brief and cannot shield them from the consequence of turning others away from the truth.

translation: Tell My servants who believe to establish prayer and spend from what We have provided for them, privately and publicly, before a Day comes when there will be no commerce and no friendship.
interpretation: Believers are urged to make devotion and generosity a steady part of life, giving whether openly or discreetly. They should act while they can, for on the Day of Judgment neither wealth nor worldly bonds can secure what righteous deeds could have earned.

translation: Allah is the One who created the heavens and the earth and sent down water from the sky, bringing forth by it fruits as provision for you. He subjected ships to you, so they sail upon the sea by His command, and He subjected rivers to you.
interpretation: The verse directs people to recognize that the provisions and means of life they rely on are gifts made possible by Allah’s creation and sustaining command; human benefit from them should therefore lead to gratitude and humility, not a sense of independence.

translation: He has subjected the sun and the moon to you, continually pursuing their courses, and He has subjected the night and the day to you.
interpretation: The ordered, ceaseless rhythms of the heavens are signs of God’s care and wisdom, inviting people to recognize their dependence on Him and respond with gratitude.

translation: And He has given you of all that you have asked of Him. If you tried to count Allah’s blessings, you could never enumerate them. Indeed, the human being is truly unjust and ungrateful.
interpretation: The verse draws attention to how deeply human life depends on blessings that cannot be fully counted or repaid. Its warning is that people may wrong themselves by overlooking these gifts and responding to them with ingratitude rather than gratitude to Allah.

translation: And [remember] when Abraham said, “My Lord, make this city secure, and keep me and my sons from worshipping idols.”
interpretation: Abraham’s prayer shows that faithfulness is not something one takes for granted: even a prophet asks God to protect him and his descendants from idolatry. His plea joins concern for the city’s safety with a deeper concern for its people’s devotion to God alone.

translation: My Lord, they have led many people astray. Whoever follows me is truly of me, and whoever disobeys me—You are indeed Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: Abraham disavows the idols that mislead people, while leaving those who turn away from his guidance to God’s mercy. His words express both firm commitment to faith and hope that God may forgive those who have gone astray.

translation: Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants in a valley without vegetation, near Your Sacred House, our Lord, so that they may establish prayer. So make the hearts of some people yearn toward them, and provide them with fruits, that they may be grateful.
interpretation: Abraham’s prayer joins worship with the means that sustain a community: he asks God to help his descendants remain devoted in a barren place, to draw caring people toward them, and to provide what they need. Their provision is sought not merely for comfort, but so that they may recognize God’s favor and respond with gratitude.

translation: Our Lord, You know what we conceal and what we make known; nothing in the earth or the heavens is hidden from Allah.
interpretation: This prayer expresses complete trust in Allah’s knowledge: outward words and hidden intentions are equally known to Him. It teaches that sincerity does not depend on what others can see, and that nothing needs to be concealed from Allah.

translation: Praise be to God, who granted me Ishmael and Isaac despite my old age. Indeed, my Lord hears supplication.
interpretation: Abraham’s words express gratitude for a gift that seemed unlikely in old age and trust that God hears prayers, even when their answer comes after a long wait.

translation: My Lord, make me steadfast in prayer, and [make] some of my descendants so as well. Our Lord, accept my supplication.
interpretation: This prayer asks not merely for the ability to pray, but for lasting devotion to prayer as a foundation of faith and life. By including his descendants, the supplicant seeks that devotion to continue through his family, while asking God to accept the plea with humility and trust.

translation: Our Lord, forgive me, my parents, and the believers on the Day when the reckoning is established.
interpretation: This supplication expresses a hope for God’s mercy at the final reckoning, extending beyond oneself to one’s parents and all believers. It teaches that a person should remember others in prayer and recognize that everyone depends on God’s forgiveness.

translation: Do not think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do. He only gives them respite until a Day when eyes will stare in terror.
interpretation: The wrongdoers’ apparent freedom from immediate punishment is not a sign that their deeds escape Allah’s knowledge or judgment. Their respite serves a wisdom and ends at the appointed Day of reckoning, when the reality of their fate will leave them utterly overwhelmed.

translation: Hastening forward, with their heads raised, their gaze fixed and unable to return to them, and their hearts hollow.
interpretation: The verse portrays people overwhelmed by terror on the Day of Judgment: their raised heads and fixed eyes express their helpless shock, while their hollow hearts suggest that fear has emptied them of composure and resolve.

translation: Warn the people of the Day when the punishment comes upon them, and the wrongdoers will say, “Our Lord, give us respite for a little while; we will answer Your call and follow the messengers.” But will they not be told, “Did you not previously swear that you would never pass away?”
interpretation: When the truth of the Hereafter becomes undeniable, those who rejected guidance will beg for another chance and promise obedience. Their plea comes too late: their former certainty that their worldly life would never end is exposed as false, and they must face the consequences of having ignored the messengers when they had the opportunity.

translation: And you lived in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves, and it had become clear to you how We dealt with them; and We set forth examples for you.
interpretation: The verse warns that knowing the fate of earlier wrongdoers carries a responsibility: their history is meant to teach later people to turn away from injustice and heed the lessons before they face a similar end.

translation: They devised their schemes, but their schemes are known to God—even if they were powerful enough to make mountains vanish.
interpretation: However formidable their plots may seem, they remain within God’s knowledge and power; no scheme can escape His judgment or defeat His purpose.

translation: So never think that Allah will fail His messengers in His promise. Indeed, Allah is Almighty, the Lord of retribution.
interpretation: The verse reassures that no delay in the fulfillment of God’s promise means it will be abandoned: His power is irresistible, and those who persist in opposing His messengers will ultimately face His justice.

translation: On the Day the earth will be changed into another earth, and the heavens as well, and all will appear before Allah, the One, the Overpowering.
interpretation: The verse portrays the final upheaval of the familiar world and humanity’s complete exposure before the sole, irresistible Sovereign. Every worldly refuge and source of power will fall away, leaving all creation subject to His judgment.

translation: And you will see the guilty that Day bound together in chains.
interpretation: The verse portrays the utter helplessness of those who persisted in wrongdoing when divine judgment arrives: they can no longer evade accountability or act freely, and their bondage makes their disgrace and the consequence of their deeds manifest.

translation: Their garments will be of tar, and the Fire will cover their faces.
interpretation: The image portrays punishment that strips away every comfort and dignity: even what should cover and protect them becomes part of their torment, while the Fire leaves them exposed to its full force.

translation: So that Allah may recompense every soul for what it has earned. Indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that every person will be judged with perfect justice according to their deeds, and that no one’s reckoning is difficult or delayed for Allah.

translation: This is a message for all people, so that they may be warned by it, know that He is only One God, and be mindful—those who possess sound understanding.
interpretation: The verse presents the Qur’an as a universal call whose warning is meant to awaken people to the oneness of God; those who reflect deeply let that truth shape their awareness and response.

translation: In the name of God, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the Book and a clear Qur’an.
interpretation: The opening letters point to the Qur’an’s divine mystery, while the verse affirms that its revelations are clear signs from God, recited plainly to guide people toward the truth.

translation: Perhaps those who disbelieve will wish they had been Muslims.
interpretation: The verse evokes the regret that will arise when the truth and its consequences become unmistakable: those who rejected faith will long to have submitted to God, though that realization will come too late to change their choice.

translation: Leave them to eat and enjoy themselves, and let hope distract them; soon they will know.
interpretation: The verse warns against treating worldly pleasures and distant hopes as protection from accountability. Its final words emphasize that the truth people defer reckoning about will become unmistakable in time.

translation: We did not destroy any town except that it had a decree set down and known.
interpretation: The verse teaches that the fate of every community unfolds according to God’s established knowledge and decree; its destruction is neither arbitrary nor before its appointed time.

translation: No community can outstrip its appointed term, nor can they delay it.
interpretation: The verse teaches that the time decreed for a community’s end is fixed by God: neither its coming nor its passing can be brought forward or postponed.

translation: And they said, “O you to whom the Reminder has been sent down, you are surely mad.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the opponents’ derision of the Prophet ﷺ: rather than consider the revelation he conveyed, they tried to discredit him by calling him mad.

translation: “Why do you not bring us the angels, if you are truthful?”
interpretation: The speakers challenge the messenger to produce angels as proof, treating a demand for a spectacular sign as a condition for belief. The verse conveys their defiance rather than a sincere search for guidance.

translation: We do not send down the angels except with the truth; and then they would not be granted any respite.
interpretation: The angels are not sent down merely to satisfy demands for a sign. When they come with a decisive judgment from God, the people facing it are not given time to reconsider or escape its consequences.

translation: Indeed, We have sent down the Reminder, and indeed We will preserve it.
interpretation: This verse presents the Qur’an’s preservation as a divine promise: its revealed message will remain protected from loss and corruption, so that it continues to be available as guidance for people.

translation: And indeed, We sent messengers before you among the communities of earlier peoples.
interpretation: The verse reassures the Prophet that his mission is part of a long history of divine guidance: earlier peoples, too, were sent messengers from among themselves.

translation: No messenger came to them except that they mocked him.
interpretation: The verse points to a recurring human response to divine guidance: those unwilling to face its challenge may ridicule its bearer rather than consider the truth being conveyed.

translation: Thus We cause it to enter the hearts of the guilty.
interpretation: Their persistent wrongdoing and rejection become so deeply rooted that they meet God’s message with the same resistance and mockery as those before them.

translation: They do not believe in it, though the way of those who came before has already been established.
interpretation: Their rejection follows the same pattern as that of earlier peoples who denied the truth: their persistent disbelief did not change the consequences that befell those who came before them.

translation: And even if We were to open for them a gate in heaven, and they were to keep ascending through it…
interpretation: The verse presents an extraordinary sign as a test of the deniers’ attitude: people fixed in rejection may resist even what they see with their own eyes, so the obstacle is not a lack of evidence but an unwillingness to accept it.

translation: They would surely say, “Our eyes have been dazzled; rather, we are a bewitched people.”
interpretation: The verse portrays people so committed to denial that even a clear, extraordinary sign would be dismissed as distorted perception or magic. Their response reveals not a lack of evidence, but an unwillingness to accept what it shows.

translation: And We have placed in the heaven constellations and adorned it for those who look.
interpretation: The ordered constellations and beauty of the heavens invite attentive observers to recognize the wisdom and artistry of their Creator.

translation: And We protected it from every accursed devil.
interpretation: The verse presents the heavens as guarded by God against rebellious devils, affirming that they cannot trespass upon the divine order as they wish.

translation: Except one who stealthily snatches a hearing, then a clear, blazing flame pursues him.
interpretation: The verse describes the heavens as guarded against devils seeking to overhear heavenly matters: any who try to listen in are pursued by a conspicuous, piercing flame, showing that access to such knowledge is not theirs to take freely.

translation: And the earth We spread out, and set upon it firm mountains, and caused to grow in it every thing in due measure.
interpretation: The verse points to a world shaped with purpose and proportion: its features and living growth are not random, but established according to a wise measure that sustains life.

translation: And We have provided for you therein the means of livelihood, and for those whom you do not provide for.
interpretation: The provision found on earth is not limited to what people earn or supply themselves; God also sustains living beings whose needs lie beyond human care or control.

translation: There is nothing whose treasuries are not with Us, and We send it down only in a known measure.
interpretation: All provision and resources ultimately belong to God, and He apportions what reaches creation with precise wisdom and measure; nothing is beyond His knowledge or control.

translation: And We send the winds to fertilize; then We send down water from the sky and give it to you to drink, though you are not its keepers.
interpretation: The verse points to the dependence of life on processes and provision beyond human control. People may benefit from water and store some of it, but they do not command its source or guarantee its continued supply; it is a gift entrusted to them.

translation: And indeed, it is We who give life and cause death, and We are the inheritors.
interpretation: Life and death are wholly under God’s authority, and all things ultimately return to Him; when every creature and possession passes away, God alone remains.

translation: And indeed, We have known those of you who have gone ahead and those who have held back.
interpretation: Nothing about people is hidden from God: He knows both those who precede others and those who come after them, and will judge each with complete knowledge.

translation: And indeed, your Lord will gather them all. He is truly All-Wise, All-Knowing.
interpretation: Their gathering for judgment is certain: Allah’s perfect knowledge encompasses them all, and His wisdom ensures that each is judged with complete justice.

translation: Indeed, We created man from sounding clay, from molded black mud.
interpretation: The verse points to humanity’s humble earthly origin and to God’s power to bring life into being from lifeless material.

translation: And the jinn We created earlier from the fire of scorching heat.
interpretation: The verse points to the jinn as a distinct creation that preceded humankind and has an origin different from humanity’s. Its description as arising from scorching fire conveys an unseen, subtle nature, rather than implying that jinn are simply ordinary flames.

translation: And when your Lord said to the angels, “Indeed, I am creating a human being from sounding clay, formed from dark, altered mud.”
interpretation: The verse draws attention to the humble earthly material from which humanity was created, while emphasizing that human existence begins by God’s deliberate act and command.

translation: When I have fashioned him and breathed into him of My Spirit, then fall down before him in prostration.
interpretation: The “Spirit” is a created spirit honored by its attribution to God, not a part of God. The command to prostrate before Adam is an act of reverence and obedience to God, not worship of Adam.

translation: So the angels prostrated, all of them together.
interpretation: Their unanimous prostration shows their complete obedience to God’s command and the honor He bestowed upon Adam; the prostration was worship of God, not of Adam.

translation: Except Iblis; he refused to be among those who prostrated.
interpretation: Iblis’s refusal set him apart from those who obeyed God’s command. His rejection was an act of disobedience, rooted in pride, and marked the beginning of his estrangement from divine favor.

translation: He said, “O Iblis, what kept you from being among those who prostrated?”
interpretation: The question is a rebuke that confronts Iblis with his deliberate refusal, making clear that his disobedience arose from his own arrogance rather than ignorance of the command.

translation: He said, “I would never prostrate to a human being whom You created from clay, from molded dark mud.”
interpretation: Satan’s refusal reveals the arrogance of judging another by the material of their creation and placing his own supposed superiority above God’s command. The verse warns that pride can turn a person’s reasoning into a defense of disobedience.

translation: He said, “Then leave it, for you are truly cast out.”
interpretation: The command marks Iblīs’s definitive rejection from the honored presence he had defied; his pride has made him an outcast, cut off from divine favor.

translation: And indeed, upon you is the curse until the Day of Judgment.
interpretation: This is God’s declaration to Iblis that his defiance has brought lasting exclusion from divine mercy, a sentence that remains upon him until the Day of Judgment.

translation: He said, “My Lord, grant me respite until the day they are resurrected.”
interpretation: Rather than turn back from his rebellion, Iblīs asks for time, revealing his resolve to persist in defiance until the final resurrection.

translation: He said, “You are indeed among those granted respite.”
interpretation: The reprieve is granted by God’s decree; it is a postponement, not freedom from eventual accountability.

translation: Until the day of the appointed time.
interpretation: The respite granted to Iblis is limited by a time fixed by God; it is not an escape from His decree.

translation: He said, “My Lord, because You have let me go astray, I will surely make [evil] seem attractive to them on earth, and I will surely lead them all astray.”
interpretation: Iblis responds to his own rebellion by blaming God and vowing to draw people away through worldly attractions. The verse portrays temptation as something that often works by making wrongdoing appear appealing, while also exposing the arrogance of refusing responsibility for one’s choices.

translation: Except Your servants among them who are sincere.
interpretation: Satan acknowledges that he cannot lead astray those servants whom God has chosen and whose devotion to Him is sincere.

translation: He said, “This is a straight path leading to Me.”
interpretation: God’s declaration affirms that the path of sincere devotion leads directly to Him. Satan may tempt people, but he cannot turn those who truly seek God away from that path.

translation: Indeed, you have no authority over My servants, except over those among the misguided who follow you.
interpretation: God reassures that Satan cannot compel His servants to disobey; his influence reaches those who choose to follow him and turn away from guidance.

translation: And indeed, Hell is the appointed destination for them all.
interpretation: The verse stresses the certainty of divine judgment: those referred to in the preceding passage cannot escape the consequence appointed for them.

translation: It has seven gates, and for each gate is an allotted share of them.
interpretation: The gates signify that those destined for Hell are assigned their place according to their deeds; its divisions are deliberate, not arbitrary.

translation: Indeed, the God-conscious will be in gardens and beside flowing springs.
interpretation: The verse presents God-consciousness as leading to lasting nearness to divine favor: the gardens and springs signify a life of enduring comfort and abundance granted by God.

translation: Enter it in peace and security.
interpretation: The welcome into Paradise conveys that its people will be free from fear and harm, received into lasting peace and safety.

translation: And We will remove whatever resentment is in their hearts; they will be brothers, seated on couches facing one another.
interpretation: The verse portrays the people of Paradise as made wholly free of the grudges and rivalries that trouble earthly relationships. Their brotherhood is sincere and peaceful, and their facing one another suggests open, joyful companionship without estrangement.

translation: No fatigue will touch them there, nor will they ever be brought out of it.
interpretation: The verse presents the bliss of Paradise as a gift made secure by God: unlike worldly comfort, it is free from exhaustion and from the fear of loss.

translation: Tell My servants that I am indeed the All-Forgiving, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: This is an invitation to hope in God’s mercy: no one should despair of forgiveness, but turn back to Him with trust and sincere repentance.

translation: And that My punishment is the painful punishment.
interpretation: This warns that God’s punishment is truly severe, urging people not to take wrongdoing lightly.

translation: And tell them about the guests of Abraham.
interpretation: The command directs attention to Abraham’s encounter with his visitors as a lesson in how God’s decree unfolds, even when its purpose is not yet clear to those involved.

translation: When they entered upon him and said, “Peace,” he said, “We are indeed apprehensive of you.”
interpretation: Abraham’s words convey his unease at the visitors’ unfamiliar presence: their greeting had not yet revealed who they were or why they had come.

translation: They said, “Do not be afraid. We bring you glad tidings of a knowledgeable son.”
interpretation: The angels reassure him that their visit is not a cause for fear, and announce that the son he will have will be distinguished by knowledge.

translation: He said, “Do you give me this good news even though old age has overtaken me? What, then, are you giving me good news of?”
interpretation: Ibrāhīm (Abraham) expresses astonishment at the promise of a child despite his advanced age. His question reflects how extraordinary the news seemed by ordinary human expectations, not a denial that God could fulfill it.

translation: They said, “We have given you good news in truth, so do not be among those who despair.”
interpretation: The messengers reassure Abraham that God’s promise is certain, even when its fulfillment seems unlikely; a believer should not despair of God’s mercy or power.

translation: He said, “And who despairs of the mercy of his Lord except those who are astray?”
interpretation: The verse teaches that no hardship or apparent impossibility should lead a person to believe that God’s mercy is beyond reach; despair arises when one loses sight of His boundless power and guidance.

translation: He said, “What, then, is your mission, O messengers?”
interpretation: Abraham’s question seeks the purpose behind the messengers’ visit, suggesting that he understood they had come not only with the glad tidings but also with a further task.

translation: They said, “Indeed, we have been sent to a people who are criminals.”
interpretation: Their words convey that the mission is a response to the people’s grave wrongdoing, and that the punishment to come is a matter of divine justice rather than arbitrary harm.

translation: Except the family of Lot; indeed, We will surely save them all.
interpretation: God declares that Lot and his household will be rescued from the punishment destined for their people, affirming His protection of them.

translation: Except for his wife; We had decreed that she would be among those left behind.
interpretation: Her fate was already decreed: she would remain with those who faced the punishment, rather than leave with Lot and the believers.

translation: Then, when the messengers came to Lot’s household,
interpretation: The arrival of the messengers marks the moment when God’s decree begins to unfold: Lot’s household is about to be distinguished from the people facing judgment.

translation: He said, “You are indeed an unfamiliar people.”
interpretation: Lot recognized that his visitors were strangers to him and did not know who they were or why they had come, so their presence made him uneasy.

translation: They said, “No; rather, we have come to you with that about which they used to doubt.”
interpretation: The messengers reassure Lot that they have not come as strangers with ill intent; they have come to carry out the decisive matter his people had doubted would come to pass.

translation: We have come to you with the truth, and indeed we are truthful.
interpretation: The speakers assure their listener that their message and what they have brought are true, leaving no doubt about their sincerity.

translation: So set out with your family during part of the night, follow behind them, let none of you look back, and go on to where you are commanded.
interpretation: The command calls for Lot and his family to leave promptly and obey the direction given to them without turning back toward the place they are leaving. Their safety depends on trusting that guidance and continuing onward as instructed.

translation: And We made known to him this decree: the last remnant of these people would be cut off by morning.
interpretation: The decree was already settled: at daybreak, the people’s destruction would leave none of them behind.

translation: And the people of the city came, rejoicing.
interpretation: Their rejoicing exposes the corruption of their intentions: they were eager to pursue the visitors for a shameful purpose, mistaking wrongdoing for pleasure.

translation: He said, “These are my guests, so do not disgrace me.”
interpretation: Lot appeals to the duty of hospitality and the dignity owed to those under his protection, urging his people not to violate that responsibility.

translation: And be mindful of Allah, and do not disgrace me.
interpretation: Lūṭ urges his people to fear God and not bring shame upon him by mistreating his guests.

translation: They said, “Did we not forbid you from offering hospitality to anyone?”
interpretation: Their words reveal their attempt to control Lot’s conduct through intimidation: they opposed his welcoming and protecting visitors, treating hospitality as something they had the power to prohibit.

translation: He said, “These are my daughters, if you are going to act.”
interpretation: Lot directs his people toward lawful marriage with women rather than their intended sinful conduct. “My daughters” may refer to the women of his community, whom a prophet may describe as his daughters, or to his own daughters offered in marriage; in either reading, he is urging them toward what is lawful.

translation: By your life, they were indeed wandering blindly in their intoxication.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the depth of the people’s heedlessness: overwhelmed by their corrupt desires, they had lost sound judgment and could not see the truth or the consequences of their actions.

translation: So the blast seized them at sunrise.
interpretation: The sudden blast at daybreak shows that when God’s judgment came, they could neither escape it nor prepare themselves against it.

translation: So We turned its uppermost part upside down and rained upon them stones of baked clay.
interpretation: The verse portrays a decisive divine punishment: the people’s settled world was overturned, and the rain of baked-clay stones made clear that their destruction was not an accident but a judgment from God.

translation: Indeed, in that are signs for those who discern.
interpretation: The verse points to signs that become clear to those who look thoughtfully and perceive what lies beneath the surface. It invites attentive reflection, through which people recognize the lessons and warnings in what they witness.

translation: And indeed, it is on a well-established road.
interpretation: The destroyed town lies along a lasting, familiar route, so its traces remain a visible warning to those who pass by.

translation: Indeed, in that is a sign for the believers.
interpretation: What has been mentioned points beyond itself to God’s wisdom and power. Believers recognize its significance through reflection and take it as a reason to deepen their faith.

translation: And indeed, the people of the thicket were surely wrongdoers.
interpretation: Their wrongdoing lay in rejecting God’s guidance and persisting in injustice; their fate was therefore not arbitrary, but a consequence of their own actions.

translation: So We punished them; and both [of their settlements] lie along a clear, well-known road.
interpretation: Their locations were visible beside a familiar route, so travelers could see them as a lasting sign of what befell those who rejected God’s messengers.

translation: And indeed, the people of al-Ḥijr denied the messengers.
interpretation: The people of al-Ḥijr—understood to be the people of Thamūd—rejected the messenger sent to them. Since the messengers called to the same truth, denying one of them was a denial of the messengers as a whole.

translation: We gave them Our signs, but they turned away from them.
interpretation: Their rejection was not due to a lack of guidance; they deliberately ignored the signs placed before them, showing how pride and stubbornness can prevent people from recognizing the truth.

translation: And they would carve homes into the mountains, feeling secure.
interpretation: Their sturdy mountain homes gave them a sense of safety, but no earthly shelter could protect them from God’s decree.

translation: So the cry seized them in the morning.
interpretation: The sudden cry overtook them at daybreak, showing that when God’s judgment arrives, no sense of security can avert it.

translation: But what they used to earn did not benefit them at all.
interpretation: The verse points to the helplessness of worldly gains when divine judgment arrives: what people rely on or accumulate cannot shield them from the consequences of turning away from God.

translation: We did not create the heavens and the earth and all that is between them except in truth. Surely the Hour is coming, so pardon with gracious forgiveness.
interpretation: Because creation is founded on truth and the final judgment is certain, the Prophet is called to meet the wrongdoing of his opponents with dignified patience and forgiveness, trusting that justice ultimately belongs to God.

translation: Indeed, your Lord is the Supreme Creator, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: The verse affirms that God creates with complete power and knows fully every detail of what He creates; nothing in creation is beyond His knowledge or control.

translation: And We have certainly given you the seven oft-repeated verses and the Magnificent Qur’an.
interpretation: The seven oft-repeated verses are understood as Sūrat al-Fātiḥah, recited again and again in prayer. Its place beside the Qur’an as a whole highlights the honor of this concise prayer, through which believers praise God and seek His guidance.

translation: Do not let your eyes linger longingly on what We have granted some of them, and do not grieve over them; rather, be humble and gentle toward the believers.
interpretation: The verse teaches that a believer should not measure worth by the worldly comforts others possess or let their choices become a cause for despair. Instead, the Prophet is directed to meet the believers with humility and compassion.

translation: And say, “Indeed, I am the clear warner.”
interpretation: The warning is meant to be delivered plainly and unmistakably, so people cannot claim they were unaware of the consequences of turning away from God.

translation: Just as We sent down upon those who divided [themselves].
interpretation: This warns those who fragmented the revealed message—disparaging it, distorting it, or accepting some parts while rejecting others—that such opposition to God’s revelation brings consequence.

translation: Those who have divided the Qur’an into parts.
interpretation: The verse rebukes those who treated God’s revelation selectively, accepting what suited them and rejecting or distorting the rest, rather than receiving its guidance as a unified whole.

translation: So, by your Lord, We will surely question them all.
interpretation: The emphatic oath underscores that no one will escape divine accountability: every person will be questioned by God.

translation: About what they used to do.
interpretation: The phrase emphasizes that people are accountable for their deeds, which are fully known to God.

translation: So proclaim openly what you are commanded, and turn away from the polytheists.
interpretation: The command calls the Prophet to make the revealed message clear and public without fear, while refusing to let the polytheists’ opposition distract or deter him from his mission.

translation: Indeed, We are sufficient for you against those who mock.
interpretation: God reassures the Prophet that He will protect him from the harm of those who ridicule him and his message; their mockery cannot thwart the mission entrusted to him.

translation: Those who set up another god alongside God will soon know.
interpretation: The verse warns that those who associate partners with God will ultimately face the truth and consequences of their choice; their present denial cannot avert that reckoning.

translation: And We certainly know that your heart is distressed by what they say.
interpretation: The verse reassures the Prophet that God is fully aware of the hurt caused by his opponents’ words; his distress is seen and understood, not overlooked.

translation: So glorify your Lord with praise, and be among those who prostrate.
interpretation: The verse calls the believer to worship God with both gratitude and humility: praise Him in remembrance, and express devotion through prostration.

translation: And worship your Lord until certainty comes to you.
interpretation: Worship your Lord faithfully throughout your life, until death comes; devotion is not limited to a particular stage or moment.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Allah’s command has come, so do not seek to hasten it. Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: The verse affirms that Allah’s decree is certain, even if its fulfillment has not yet appeared to people; they should not demand that it be brought sooner. Allah is utterly exalted above the partners attributed to Him.

translation: He sends down the angels with the Spirit, by His command, to whomever He wills of His servants, [saying], “Warn [people] that there is no god but Me, so be mindful of Me.”
interpretation: The verse presents revelation as a message entrusted by God to the angels and delivered to chosen servants: its central call is to recognize God’s oneness and let awareness of Him shape one’s conduct.

translation: He created the heavens and the earth in truth. Exalted is He above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: The world’s purposeful creation points to the wisdom and sovereignty of its Creator, who is far above having any partner or rival.

translation: He created the human being from a drop of fluid, and then he becomes a clear-cut disputant.
interpretation: The verse draws attention to the striking contrast between humanity’s humble, fragile beginning and its later confidence in argument. It invites people to recognize their dependence on God rather than let their ability to dispute become a source of arrogance.

translation: And He created livestock for you: from them you obtain warmth and other benefits, and from them you eat.
interpretation: The verse presents livestock as a provision made accessible for human well-being, inviting people to recognize the care and generosity of God in the warmth, practical uses, and nourishment they receive from them.

translation: And in them you have beauty when you bring them home in the evening and when you send them out to pasture in the morning.
interpretation: The verse draws attention to the quiet dignity and pleasure people find in caring for their livestock, inviting reflection on how ordinary blessings can be signs of God’s generosity.

translation: They carry your burdens to a land you could not reach except with great hardship. Surely your Lord is Most Kind, Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse draws attention to the ease God provides through the animals placed at people’s service: they make difficult journeys and transport possible. This provision reflects God’s kindness and mercy toward human beings.

translation: And [He created] horses, mules, and donkeys for you to ride and as adornment; and He creates what you do not know.
interpretation: The verse invites reflection on the breadth of God’s provision: these animals serve people not only through their usefulness but also through their beauty, while the closing words remind us that creation extends beyond what people know or can yet perceive.

translation: And it is for Allah to make the straight path clear, though some paths turn aside from it. Had He willed, He would have guided you all.
interpretation: Allah has made the way of truth clear, while people may turn away from it. His power to guide everyone shows that their differing choices occur by His will, yet they remain responsible for the path they follow.

translation: He is the One who sends down water from the sky. From it you have drink, and from it grows vegetation among which you pasture your animals.
interpretation: The verse invites reflection on how a single gift—rain—sustains both human and animal life, revealing our dependence on God’s provision and calling us to gratitude.

translation: He causes crops, olives, date palms, grapevines, and every kind of fruit to grow for you by it. Surely in that is a sign for people who reflect.
interpretation: The variety and abundance of what grows from the earth invite people to look beyond the produce itself and recognize the wisdom and power of the One who provides it.

translation: He has subjected for you the night and the day, the sun and the moon, and the stars are subject to His command. Surely in that are signs for people who reason.
interpretation: The regular order of these celestial bodies points to a single sustaining authority; their benefits are not independent powers, but signs inviting thoughtful recognition of the One who governs them.

translation: And whatever He has brought forth for you on earth, varying in its colors—surely in that is a sign for people who take heed.
interpretation: The diversity found in earthly creation invites reflection on the Creator’s wisdom: its many forms and colors are not random, but signs of purposeful design for those willing to look beyond the familiar.

translation: And He is the One who has subjected the sea for you, so that you may eat fresh meat from it, bring forth from it ornaments that you wear, and see ships plowing through it; and so that you may seek of His bounty and be grateful.
interpretation: The verse invites people to recognize that the sea’s resources and its usefulness for travel and livelihood are gifts made available by God, not merely ordinary features of nature. Their proper response is gratitude to the One who enables these benefits and sustains their means of life.

translation: And He placed firm mountains in the earth lest it sway with you, and rivers and paths, so that you may find your way.
interpretation: The verse presents the earth’s stability and its pathways as signs of deliberate care: the same order that makes life possible also gives people means to find their way, inviting them to recognize the wisdom and guidance of their Creator.

translation: And [He made] landmarks; and by the stars they find their way.
interpretation: God has placed recognizable signs in the world, and made the stars a means by which people can navigate. Their ability to find direction through these signs reflects the order and provision God has placed in creation.

translation: Is the One who creates like one who does not create? Will you not then reflect?
interpretation: The verse invites people to use their reason to recognize that only the Creator possesses true divinity and deserves worship; created beings and powerless idols cannot be His equals or partners.

translation: If you were to count the blessings of God, you could never number them. Indeed, God is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse invites a person to recognize how deeply dependent they are on God: His gifts exceed human ability to account for them, and even imperfect gratitude does not place a person beyond His forgiveness and mercy.

translation: And Allah knows what you conceal and what you make known.
interpretation: Nothing is hidden from Allah—not inner thoughts and intentions nor outward words and actions—so a person should be sincere and mindful of Him in both private and public.

translation: Those whom they call upon besides Allah create nothing; they themselves are created.
interpretation: The verse teaches that anything worshipped besides Allah is dependent and created, and therefore cannot share in the divine power of the Creator.

translation: They are dead, not living, and they do not perceive when they will be resurrected.
interpretation: The verse describes the beings invoked besides God as utterly powerless: they have no life or awareness, not even knowledge of their own resurrection. They therefore cannot hear or answer those who call upon them, and are unworthy of worship.

translation: Your God is one God. Those who do not believe in the Hereafter have hearts that reject the truth, and they are arrogant.
interpretation: The verse links rejection of the Hereafter with a heart closed to divine truth and a proud refusal to submit. Belief in one God calls a person to humility and accountability, while arrogance resists both.

translation: Without a doubt, Allah knows what they conceal and what they make known. Indeed, He does not love the arrogant.
interpretation: The verse warns that no attempt to hide arrogance can escape Allah’s knowledge. It also makes clear that prideful self-importance is not merely a flaw in conduct; it places a person at odds with what Allah loves.

translation: When they are asked, “What has your Lord sent down?” they say, “Tales of the ancients.”
interpretation: Their answer reflects a dismissive rejection of revelation: rather than consider its message, they portray it as merely inherited stories from the past.

translation: So that they may bear their burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection, and also some of the burdens of those whom they lead astray without knowledge. How evil is what they bear!
interpretation: Those who mislead others are accountable not only for their own wrongdoing but also for the harm their influence causes. This does not erase the responsibility of those who follow them; rather, it adds the burden of having led others astray.

translation: Those before them plotted, but Allah struck their structure at its foundations, so the roof fell upon them from above, and the punishment came upon them from where they did not perceive.
interpretation: The verse teaches that schemes devised against the truth can be undone at their very foundations by Allah, bringing consequences upon their plotters from an unexpected direction.

translation: Then, on the Day of Resurrection, He will disgrace them and say, “Where are My partners for whose sake you used to contend?” Those who were given knowledge will say, “Today, disgrace and evil are indeed upon the disbelievers.”
interpretation: The question exposes the partners the disbelievers had falsely attributed to God: when faced with judgment, those supposed allies cannot answer or help them. The testimony of those granted knowledge confirms that disgrace and punishment rightly fall upon those who rejected the truth.

translation: Those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves then offer submission, saying, “We were not doing any evil.” Indeed, Allah knows well what you used to do.
interpretation: The verse warns that a last-minute surrender or denial cannot conceal a life of wrongdoing: when death strips away excuses, a person’s deeds remain fully known to Allah.

translation: So enter the gates of Hell, abiding therein. How wretched is the abode of the arrogant!
interpretation: The verse warns that arrogant defiance of God leads to lasting punishment, portraying Hell as a dreadful and fitting dwelling for those who exalt themselves and reject the truth.

translation: And it will be said to those who are mindful of God, “What has your Lord sent down?” They will say, “Good.” For those who do good in this world is goodness, and the home of the Hereafter is better. How excellent is the home of the God-conscious!
interpretation: Those who are mindful of God recognize His revelation as a good that guides and nurtures them. The verse teaches that goodness in this life is real, but the lasting reward of the Hereafter is greater; the finest home belongs to those whose piety is shown through doing good.

translation: Gardens of everlasting residence, which they will enter, with rivers flowing beneath them. They will have there whatever they desire. Thus Allah rewards the mindful of Him.
interpretation: The verse presents lasting nearness to God as the culmination of a life shaped by reverence and obedience: the reward is not only secure and enduring, but generous enough to fulfill the desires of those who are mindful of Him.

translation: Those whom the angels take in death while they are pure and righteous, saying, “Peace be upon you. Enter Paradise for what you used to do.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the believers’ death as a moment of reassurance: because they remained devoted to God, the angels greet them with peace and welcome them into Paradise. Their deeds are the path by which they have earned this welcome, through God’s mercy.

translation: Do they await anything but that the angels should come to them, or that your Lord’s command should come? Thus did those before them. Allah did not wrong them, but they used to wrong themselves.
interpretation: في الآية إنذارٌ لمن يصرّ على التكذيب حتى لا يبقى أمامه إلا نزول الملائكة لقبض الأرواح أو حلول أمر الله بالعقوبة. وما جرى للأمم السابقة لم يكن ظلمًا من الله؛ بل كان جزاءً لما اختاروه من كفرٍ ومعصية، فكانت عاقبة ظلمهم لأنفسهم.

translation: So the evil consequences of what they had done befell them, and what they used to ridicule surrounded them.
interpretation: Those who persist in wrongdoing and mock the warnings they receive ultimately face the consequences they dismissed; the very punishment they treated as impossible overtakes them.

translation: Those who associate others with Allah say, “If Allah had willed, neither we nor our forefathers would have worshipped anything besides Him, nor would we have forbidden anything apart from Him.” In the same way acted those who came before them. So are the messengers responsible for anything other than clear conveyance?
interpretation: They invoke Allah’s will to justify their worship and prohibitions, but the verse rejects this as an excuse: divine permission for human choice does not make people’s choices right or remove their responsibility. The messengers’ duty is to convey the truth clearly; each person remains accountable for how they respond.

translation: We certainly sent to every community a messenger, [saying], “Worship Allah and shun false gods.” Among them were those whom Allah guided, and among them were those upon whom misguidance became due. So travel through the land and see what was the end of those who denied the truth.
interpretation: The verse presents the call to worship Allah alone and reject every rival authority as the shared message of the messengers. It also warns that people are accountable for how they respond to that call: the fate of earlier deniers, visible in the history of nations, stands as a lesson to those who follow.

translation: If you are deeply concerned for their guidance, then Allah does not guide those whom He leaves to stray, and they will have no helpers.
interpretation: The verse reassures the Prophet that his sincere concern cannot compel guidance for those who persistently reject it; their turning away leaves them without anyone able to rescue them from its consequences.

translation: They swear by Allah with their strongest oaths that Allah will not resurrect those who die. Indeed, He will—this is a promise binding upon Him, though most people do not know.
interpretation: The certainty of resurrection rests on Allah’s promise, not on what people can presently perceive; widespread denial cannot make that promise less true.
