translation: So that He may make clear to them that about which they differed, and so that those who disbelieved may know that they were liars.
interpretation: The verse points to the final judgment as the moment when disputed truths will be made unmistakable and those who denied them will see that their denial was false.

translation: When We will something to be, Our only word to it is, “Be,” and it is.
interpretation: The verse teaches that nothing can thwart God’s will: bringing creation into existence—and restoring it after death—requires no effort or delay from Him.

translation: And those who emigrated for God’s sake after being wronged—we will surely grant them a good home in this world. Yet the reward of the Hereafter is greater, if only they knew.
interpretation: The verse assures those driven from their homes by injustice that their sacrifice for God will not go unrewarded: they will find goodness and a place of security in this life, while the lasting reward of the Hereafter is far greater. It invites believers to see worldly relief as a mercy, but not as the measure of their ultimate reward.

translation: Those who are patient and place their trust in their Lord.
interpretation: Their patience reflects steadfastness through hardship, while their trust in God means they rely on Him for support and entrust the outcome to His wisdom.

translation: We sent before you only men to whom We revealed. So ask the people of knowledge if you do not know.
interpretation: The verse answers the objection that a messenger could not be human: God’s messengers before Muhammad were human beings who received revelation. It directs those uncertain about this to consult people knowledgeable about earlier scriptures, making informed inquiry—not assumption—the way to resolve the question.

translation: “With clear proofs and scriptures. And We sent down to you the Reminder so that you may make clear to people what was sent down to them, and so that they may reflect.”
interpretation: The verse indicates that the Prophet’s role includes clarifying the revelation for people, helping them understand its guidance, while inviting them to reflect thoughtfully upon it.

translation: Do those who devise evil feel secure that Allah will not cause the earth to swallow them, or that punishment will not come upon them from where they do not perceive?
interpretation: The verse warns that those who scheme wrongdoing should not mistake a delay in punishment for safety: Allah’s judgment can overtake them suddenly, beyond their awareness or control.

translation: Or that He seize them as they go about, while they cannot escape Him.
interpretation: The verse warns that no one is beyond God’s power: even amid ordinary activity, people cannot thwart His will or evade His reckoning.

translation: Or that He seize them while they are apprehensive? Indeed, your Lord is Most Kind, Most Merciful.
interpretation: The warning is that divine punishment may come even while people live in fear of its approach; any delay is not proof of safety, but an expression of God’s gentleness, leaving room for people to turn back.

translation: Have they not observed what Allah has created, whose shadows shift to the right and to the left, prostrating to Allah in humility?
interpretation: The changing shadows of created things reveal their complete submission to Allah’s order. The verse calls people to recognize this sign of divine sovereignty and to humble themselves before their Creator.

translation: To Allah prostrates whatever is in the heavens and whatever creatures are on the earth, as do the angels; they are not arrogant.
interpretation: All creation is subject to Allah’s authority, whether its submission is expressed through its natural obedience to the order He has set or through deliberate worship. The angels exemplify conscious, willing humility: they never resist or consider themselves above obedience to their Lord.

translation: They fear their Lord above them, and they do what they are commanded.
interpretation: Their fear reflects reverent awareness of their Lord’s supreme authority, shown through complete obedience to His commands.

translation: And Allah said, “Do not take two gods; He is only one God. So fear Me alone.”
interpretation: God’s oneness means that ultimate reverence and accountability belong to Him alone; no rival should share the place of God in a person’s worship or devotion.

translation: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, and to Him belongs obedience forever. Will you then fear anyone other than Allah?
interpretation: Since all creation belongs to Allah and obedience to Him is enduring, reverence and fear that shape one’s worship should be directed to Him alone, not to anything else.

translation: Whatever blessing you have is from Allah. Then, when hardship touches you, to Him you cry out for help.
interpretation: The verse directs people to recognize that every blessing ultimately comes from God, and that in moments of distress they instinctively turn to Him. It calls for this awareness to endure in prosperity as well as hardship, rather than acknowledging God only when help is needed.

translation: Then, when He removes the hardship from you, a group of you immediately associate others with their Lord.
interpretation: The verse warns against turning to God only in distress, then forgetting His favor and giving others a share in the devotion due to Him once relief comes.

translation: So they may be ungrateful for what We have given them. So enjoy yourselves; soon you will know.
interpretation: The words warn those who respond to God’s blessings with denial and ingratitude that their worldly enjoyment is temporary, and that they will soon face the consequences of their choices.

translation: They assign a share of what We have provided them to things they know nothing about. By God, you will surely be questioned about what you used to invent.
interpretation: The verse condemns the baseless practice of dedicating part of God’s provision to supposed partners or idols, which have no power or rightful claim. Such fabricated beliefs and acts of devotion are not beyond accountability before God.

translation: They attribute daughters to Allah—glory be to Him!—while for themselves they claim what they desire.
interpretation: The verse rebukes those who falsely ascribe daughters to God while reserving what they prefer for themselves. This exposes the inconsistency and arrogance of their claim, for God is exalted above having offspring or being described by their inventions.

translation: When one of them is told the news of a daughter, his face darkens, and he is filled with suppressed anguish.
interpretation: The verse condemns the shame and resentment some people felt at the birth of a daughter, exposing this reaction as an unjust prejudice rather than any failing in the child.

translation: He hides himself from the people because of the bad news he has been given. Should he keep the child in humiliation, or bury her in the ground? How evil is their judgment!
interpretation: The verse condemns the belief that a daughter’s birth is a disgrace: by exposing the father’s shame and the horrific choices he considers, it shows how prejudice can corrupt moral judgment and lead to grave injustice.

translation: Those who do not believe in the Hereafter have the worst description, while Allah possesses the highest attributes. He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: The verse rejects the flawed and degrading notions about God held by those who deny the Hereafter, affirming that every perfection belongs to Allah and that His power and wisdom are beyond any imperfection.

translation: If Allah were to take people to task for their wrongdoing, He would not leave any creature upon the earth. But He gives them respite until an appointed term; when that term arrives, they can neither delay it by a moment nor bring it forward.
interpretation: The verse highlights Allah’s forbearance: wrongdoing does not bring immediate destruction, because He grants people time before the fixed moment of accountability. That respite is not escape from consequence, since the appointed term cannot be altered.

translation: They assign to Allah what they themselves dislike, while their tongues falsely claim that they will have the best outcome. Without doubt, the Fire is theirs, and they will be hastened into it.
interpretation: The verse condemns the hypocrisy of attributing to God what people reject for themselves, then inventing assurances of their own privileged fate. Their self-serving claims cannot alter the judgment that awaits them.

translation: By Allah, We certainly sent messengers to nations before you, but Satan made their deeds seem fair to them. So he is their ally today, and they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse explains that earlier peoples were led to reject guidance when Satan made their wrongdoing attractive to them. His influence may seem like support, but it only leads them toward painful punishment.

translation: We sent down the Book to you only so that you may clarify for them what they differ about, and as guidance and mercy for people who believe.
interpretation: The verse presents the Qur’an as a criterion that clarifies disputed matters and guides believers toward truth; its guidance becomes a mercy for those who receive it with faith.

translation: Allah has sent down water from the sky and, through it, brought the earth to life after its death. Surely in this is a sign for people who listen.
interpretation: The revival of barren land through rain points to God’s power to bring life after death. Those who listen attentively can recognize this sign and take it to heart.

translation: And indeed, in livestock there is a lesson for you: We give you drink from what is within their bellies—between digested matter and blood—pure milk, pleasant for those who drink it.
interpretation: The verse invites reflection on God’s provision: from within the animal, milk emerges pure and nourishing, despite its proximity to what is impure. This transformation is presented as a sign of divine wisdom and care, calling people to recognize the Creator in the ordinary blessings that sustain them.

translation: And from the fruits of date palms and grapevines you make an intoxicant and wholesome provision. Surely in that is a sign for people who reason.
interpretation: The verse points to God’s provision in these fruits and invites thoughtful reflection on how people use them. By distinguishing intoxicants from wholesome provision, it directs people of reason to recognize that not every use of a blessing is good.

translation: And your Lord inspired the bee: “Make homes in the mountains, in the trees, and in the structures people raise.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the bee’s instinctive way of life as a form of divine guidance, inviting reflection on the wisdom and care woven into creation.

translation: Then eat from every kind of fruit and follow the ways of your Lord, made easy for you. From their bellies comes a drink of varying colors, in which there is healing for people. Surely in this is a sign for people who reflect.
interpretation: The verse invites reflection on how the bee is guided to gather nourishment and produce honey, whose varied qualities can bring healing. This intricate provision points to God’s wisdom and care, and to signs of divine power in the natural world.

translation: Allah created you, then He causes you to die. And among you are those who are returned to the most feeble age, so that after having knowledge they know nothing. Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing, All-Powerful.
interpretation: Human knowledge and strength are gifts that can fade with age, reminding people not to take their abilities for granted and to recognize that Allah’s knowledge and power remain complete and encompass every stage of life.

translation: Allah has favored some of you over others in provision. Yet those who have been favored do not give their provision to those whom their right hands possess so that they become equal partners in it. Will they then deny Allah’s favor?
interpretation: The verse points to an inconsistency: people recognize differences in provision and do not make those under their authority equal partners in their wealth, yet they attribute partners to Allah from among His creation. It calls them to acknowledge that all provision is Allah’s favor and to worship Him alone.

translation: Allah has made for you spouses from among yourselves, and from your spouses He has granted you children and descendants, and He has provided you with wholesome things. Will they then believe in falsehood and deny Allah’s favor?
interpretation: The verse calls people to recognize that the blessings of family and good provision come from Allah, and to respond with gratitude and worship of Him rather than turning to false beliefs or denying His gifts.

translation: They worship, besides Allah, that which has no power to provide them with anything from the heavens or the earth, nor can it do so.
interpretation: Worship belongs to Allah alone, for only He has the power to provide; turning to powerless beings for provision places devotion where it cannot be answered.

translation: So do not make comparisons for Allah. Indeed, Allah knows, while you do not know.
interpretation: Do not define Allah by analogies drawn from creation or claim to know what exceeds your understanding; trust His knowledge and avoid speaking about Him without knowledge.

translation: Allah presents the example of an enslaved person who has no power over anything, and someone whom We have provided with good provision from Us, so that he spends from it privately and openly. Are they equal? Praise belongs to Allah, but most of them do not know.
interpretation: The parable challenges the idea that powerless idols can be equated with God, the true giver of provision and all power. Recognizing this difference should lead people to worship God alone, though many fail to understand it.

translation: Allah presents the example of two men: one of them is mute, unable to do anything, and is a burden to his guardian. Wherever he sends him, he brings no good. Is he equal to one who enjoins justice and is upon a straight path?
interpretation: The verse exposes the folly of worshipping powerless idols: they can neither speak nor benefit those who turn to them. They are nothing like the Lord who commands justice and guides upon the straight path.

translation: To Allah belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth. The coming of the Hour is no more than the blink of an eye—or even nearer. Surely Allah has power over all things.
interpretation: The Hour may seem distant to people, but its arrival is entirely within Allah’s knowledge and will; bringing it about requires no time or effort beyond His command.

translation: And Allah brought you forth from your mothers’ wombs knowing nothing, and gave you hearing, sight, and hearts, so that you might be grateful.
interpretation: The verse directs people to see their ability to learn and understand as gifts from God: since knowledge was not theirs from birth, they should use their senses and minds to recognize His blessings and respond with gratitude.

translation: Do they not see the birds, held aloft in the sky? None holds them up except Allah. Surely in that are signs for people who believe.
interpretation: The birds’ ability to remain aloft and move through the sky points to the wisdom and sustaining power of Allah. Those who believe recognize in this a sign that creation is not independent, but upheld by its Creator.

translation: And Allah has made your homes a place of rest for you, and from the hides of livestock He has made for you shelters that are easy for you to carry on your travels and when you settle. And from their wool, hair, and fur He has provided furnishings and goods for you to use for a time.
interpretation: The verse draws attention to the care and wisdom in how God has provided for human life: people have both a settled refuge and lightweight shelter for travel, while the animals around them supply useful materials. These everyday comforts are signs of divine generosity, yet their usefulness is limited to the span of worldly life.

translation: God has made for you shade from what He has created, and shelters in the mountains. He has made garments for you to protect you from the heat, and garments to protect you from your own violence. Thus He completes His favor upon you, so that you may submit to Him.
interpretation: The verse points to God’s care expressed through both the natural world and the means people make for their protection. Recognizing these provisions should lead people to gratitude and willing submission to Him.

translation: So if they turn away, your duty is only to convey the message clearly.
interpretation: If people reject the message, the messenger’s responsibility is to communicate it plainly and faithfully; he is not responsible for compelling them to accept it.

translation: They recognize Allah’s blessings, then deny them; and most of them are ungrateful.
interpretation: The verse describes people who know that their blessings come from Allah yet refuse to acknowledge Him with gratitude and obedience, turning recognition into denial through their actions.

translation: And on the Day We raise up a witness from every community, those who disbelieved will not be granted permission, nor will they be allowed to make amends.
interpretation: The verse portrays judgment as a moment when each community’s witness establishes the truth, leaving those who rejected it without an opportunity to plead their case or repair their deeds.

translation: When those who did wrong see the punishment, it will not be eased for them, nor will they be given respite.
interpretation: The verse warns that once the punishment has arrived, those who persisted in wrongdoing will find no relief or delay; it therefore calls people to turn away from injustice before that moment comes.

translation: When those who associated others with God see their partners, they will say, “Our Lord, these are our partners whom we used to invoke besides You.” But they will throw their words back at them: “You are indeed liars.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the worshippers’ final attempt to shift responsibility, only for the beings they relied on to disown them. Their reply exposes the falsehood of claiming that these partners had any divine authority or could serve as intermediaries with God.

translation: On that Day they will surrender themselves to Allah, and what they used to fabricate will vanish from them.
interpretation: When judgment comes, the excuses and falsehoods they relied on will offer no protection. They will submit to Allah’s authority, while their fabricated beliefs prove powerless and disappear.

translation: Those who disbelieved and turned others away from the path of Allah—we will increase their punishment upon punishment because of the corruption they used to spread.
interpretation: The verse teaches that deliberately obstructing others from guidance adds a further burden to disbelief: those who misuse their influence to spread corruption face punishment corresponding to the harm they cause.

translation: And [mention] the Day We will raise up in every community a witness from among themselves, and bring you as a witness over these. We have sent down to you the Book as a clarification of all things, and as guidance, mercy, and glad tidings for those who submit to God.
interpretation: The verse presents revelation as both a source of guidance in this life and a basis for accountability in the next: each community will be judged with testimony arising from its own experience, while the Prophet bears witness over those addressed by his message. The Qur’an’s clarification of “all things” means that it provides what people need for guidance—through its teachings and principles—not that it catalogs every fact or detail. Its guidance becomes mercy and good news for those who respond with submission to God.

translation: Indeed, God commands justice, excellence, and giving to relatives, and forbids indecency, wrongdoing, and aggression. He admonishes you so that you may take heed.
interpretation: The verse presents a moral framework that joins fairness with generous goodness: people are to uphold others’ rights, go beyond mere obligation in kindness, and honor family ties. Its prohibitions guard personal and communal life from shameful conduct, injustice, and the abuse of power. The closing admonition calls people to keep these principles in mind and let them shape their choices.

translation: Fulfill the covenant of Allah when you make it, and do not break your oaths after confirming them, when you have made Allah your guarantor. Surely Allah knows what you do.
interpretation: This verse teaches that a commitment made in Allah’s name is a serious moral trust, not a formality. A believer must honor it sincerely and consistently, remembering that Allah knows whether the promise is kept or betrayed.

translation: Do not be like the woman who unraveled her yarn after making it strong, turning it into loose strands. Do not use your oaths as a means of deceit between you because one community is more numerous than another. Allah is testing you by this, and on the Day of Resurrection He will surely make clear to you what you used to differ about.
interpretation: The verse warns against abandoning a firm covenant for advantage, like undoing carefully spun yarn. A believer must not treat oaths as tools of deception or shift allegiance to a stronger group for worldly gain; such conduct is a test of faithfulness, and God will ultimately expose the truth in disputes over these commitments.

translation: Had God willed, He could have made you one community. But He lets whom He wills go astray and guides whom He wills, and you will surely be questioned about what you used to do.
interpretation: The verse teaches that human beings’ differing paths exist within God’s will, yet this does not remove their responsibility: each person will answer for their own deeds.

translation: Do not use your oaths as a means of deception among yourselves, lest a foot slip after it has been firmly planted, and lest you suffer evil for turning others away from the path of Allah; and you face a tremendous punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns against invoking solemn promises while intending to betray them. Such deceit can undermine trust and lead people away from faith and what is right; those who cause this harm are accountable before Allah.

translation: And do not trade Allah’s covenant for a small price. What is with Allah is better for you, if only you knew.
interpretation: The verse warns against abandoning or violating one’s commitments to Allah for temporary worldly gain. Its meaning is that faithfulness to the covenant is worth more than any immediate benefit, because what Allah gives is better and lasting.

translation: Whatever you have will come to an end, but what is with God endures. And We will surely reward those who are patient according to the best of what they used to do.
interpretation: The verse teaches that lasting worth lies not in possessions that pass away, but in what God preserves. It therefore encourages steadfastness through hardship, with trust that God’s enduring reward will exceed the measure of one’s deeds.

translation: Whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer—We will surely grant them a good life, and We will surely reward them according to the best of what they used to do.
interpretation: The verse teaches that faith joined with righteous action is the foundation of a truly good life. This goodness is not limited to worldly comfort; it includes the steadiness, purpose, and contentment that come from living in trust and obedience to God. God also promises a generous reward in the Hereafter, judging people by the best of their deeds.

translation: So when you recite the Qur’an, seek refuge in Allah from Satan, the accursed.
interpretation: The verse teaches that approaching the Qur’an calls for humility and reliance on Allah: the reciter seeks His protection from Satan’s influence so that distractions and temptations do not hinder attentive, sincere engagement with the revelation.

translation: Indeed, he has no authority over those who believe and place their trust in their Lord.
interpretation: Satan cannot compel or dominate those whose faith and reliance on God protect them from his influence; his power is limited to tempting, not controlling, them.

translation: His authority is only over those who take him as an ally, and those who associate partners with God.
interpretation: Satan does not have power to compel people against their will; his influence takes hold of those who choose to follow him and turn from devotion to God alone.

translation: When We replace one verse with another—and Allah knows best what He sends down—they say, “You are only making it up.” Rather, most of them do not know.
interpretation: The verse answers those who accused the Prophet of inventing revelation when a divine ruling or passage was replaced: such changes occur by Allah’s knowledge and wisdom, not by fabrication. Their accusation reflects ignorance of how revelation unfolds and of Allah’s authority over what He sends down.

translation: Say, “The Holy Spirit has brought it down from your Lord in truth, to strengthen those who believe, and as guidance and glad tidings for those who submit to God.”
interpretation: The verse affirms that the Qur’an is a true revelation from God, conveyed by the angel Gabriel, and that its divine origin is what gives believers firmness in faith. Its guidance and glad tidings are for those who turn to God in submission.

translation: And We certainly know that they say, “It is only a human being who teaches him.” The language of the one to whom they attribute this is foreign, while this is a clear Arabic language.
interpretation: The verse rejects the claim that the Qur’an was taught to the Prophet by a person: the person they named spoke a foreign language, whereas the Qur’an was delivered in clear Arabic. The contrast exposes the weakness of their accusation and affirms the Qur’an’s divine origin.

translation: Indeed, those who do not believe in Allah’s signs—Allah does not guide them, and they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns that those who reject God’s signs turn away from the guidance that could lead them to faith, and remain answerable for that rejection.

translation: Only those who do not believe in Allah’s signs invent falsehood; they are the liars.
interpretation: The verse answers the charge that the Prophet fabricated revelation: such deliberate falsehood comes from rejecting Allah’s signs, not from the one conveying them. It identifies the accusers’ denial and fabrication as the source of the lie.

translation: Whoever disbelieves in Allah after having believed—except one who is compelled while his heart remains firm in faith—but whoever willingly opens their heart to disbelief, upon them is wrath from Allah, and theirs is a tremendous punishment.
interpretation: The verse distinguishes between words of disbelief uttered under compulsion by someone whose faith remains intact, and a willing inward acceptance of disbelief. It teaches that coercion does not make a believer’s heart faithless, while freely embracing disbelief brings divine accountability.

translation: That is because they preferred the life of this world over the Hereafter, and Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.
interpretation: The verse explains that turning away from faith stems from giving worldly gains greater worth than the lasting reward of the Hereafter. By choosing and persisting in disbelief, people turn from the guidance Allah offers.

translation: Those are the ones whose hearts, hearing, and sight Allah has sealed; those are the heedless.
interpretation: The sealing describes the consequence of persistent rejection: their inner understanding and their ability to hear and see the signs of guidance have become unresponsive. Their heedlessness is therefore a settled turning away, not simply a momentary failure to notice.

translation: Without a doubt, they are the losers in the Hereafter.
interpretation: Their rejection carries its true and lasting cost beyond this life: worldly gains cannot compensate for forfeiting God’s mercy and the reward of the Hereafter.

translation: Then, indeed, your Lord is—for those who emigrated after they had been persecuted, then strove and remained patient—indeed, your Lord thereafter is Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: The verse offers reassurance that persecution and past trials do not place a person beyond God’s mercy: steadfastness and sincere effort are met with His forgiveness and compassion.

translation: On the Day when every soul will plead for itself, each soul will be repaid in full for what it has done, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: The verse portrays the Day of Judgment as a moment of complete personal accountability: each person will be occupied with their own case, and God’s judgment will give everyone exactly what their deeds merit, without injustice or loss.

translation: God sets forth the example of a town that was secure and at ease, with its provision coming to it abundantly from every place. Yet it was ungrateful for God’s blessings, so God made it taste the garment of hunger and fear because of what its people used to do.
interpretation: The verse teaches that a community’s security and well-being are blessings entrusted to it, not guarantees independent of how it lives. When people respond to those blessings with ingratitude and wrongdoing, the very stability they took for granted can be replaced by hardship and fear.

translation: A messenger from among them had indeed come to them, but they rejected him, so punishment overtook them while they were doing wrong.
interpretation: The verse shows that their punishment came after clear guidance had reached them through one of their own, and that their rejection was a culpable act of wrongdoing.

translation: So eat from what Allah has provided for you—lawful and wholesome—and be grateful for Allah’s blessing, if it is Him you worship.
interpretation: True worship is reflected in how one receives Allah’s provision: seeking what is lawful and wholesome, recognizing the blessing as coming from Him, and responding with gratitude and obedience.

translation: He has forbidden you only carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, and that over which a name other than God’s has been invoked. But whoever is compelled, neither seeking it nor exceeding the limit, incurs no sin. Surely God is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse sets out dietary prohibitions while making clear that they do not require a person to endanger their life: in genuine necessity, a person may take only what is needed to survive, without seeking excess or transgression, and is not blameworthy. This exception reflects God’s mercy and the principle that religious obligations do not demand the impossible.

translation: Do not say, about what your tongues falsely describe, “This is lawful and this is forbidden,” thereby fabricating lies against God. Those who fabricate lies against God will not succeed.
interpretation: The verse warns against presenting personal opinions or inventions as God’s commands. Declaring something lawful or forbidden in God’s name requires truthfulness and sound grounds; otherwise, religious authority is being misused, with spiritual consequences.

translation: A brief enjoyment, and for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: Whatever worldly pleasure they receive is temporary and cannot shield them from the painful punishment awaiting them; fleeting prosperity should not be mistaken for lasting success.

translation: And to those who were Jews, We forbade what We related to you before. We did not wrong them; rather, they were wronging themselves.
interpretation: The verse presents these prohibitions as just, not arbitrary: they were connected to the people’s own wrongdoing, so the blame for their consequences rests with them, not with God.

translation: Then indeed your Lord, for those who do evil in ignorance, then repent thereafter and make amends—indeed your Lord, after that, is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: “In ignorance” can describe wrongdoing done in heedlessness or under the sway of impulse, even when a person knows it is wrong. The verse holds out hope to such a person: sincere repentance followed by changed conduct and making things right is met by God’s forgiveness and mercy.

translation: Indeed, Abraham was a model of devotion, obedient to Allah and upright in faith; he was not among those who associated others with Him.
interpretation: Abraham is presented as an exemplary guide whose steadfast obedience and wholehearted devotion to Allah made him a model of pure monotheism, even while rejecting the beliefs of those around him.

translation: He was grateful for His blessings; He chose him and guided him to a straight path.
interpretation: Abraham’s gratitude was a sincere acknowledgment of God’s favors, reflected in how he lived. His being chosen and guided shows that steadfastness upon the truth is a gift from God as well as a response to His blessings.

translation: And We granted him goodness in this world, and in the Hereafter he will surely be among the righteous.
interpretation: God honored Abraham with goodness in worldly life and affirmed that his lasting station in the Hereafter would be among those of righteousness.

translation: Then We revealed to you: “Follow the way of Abraham, inclining toward pure faith; he was not one of the polytheists.”
interpretation: Abraham’s way is presented as wholehearted devotion to God alone, turning away from every form of associating partners with Him. The verse affirms that this pure faith is the enduring path the Prophet is to uphold.

translation: The Sabbath was prescribed only for those who differed concerning it. And your Lord will surely judge between them on the Day of Resurrection regarding that over which they used to differ.
interpretation: The verse presents the Sabbath as a specific obligation connected to the dispute of those addressed by it, rather than a rule imposed on everyone in the same way. Their disagreement and conduct are ultimately for God to judge, and His judgment will settle what they contested.

translation: Call to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good counsel, and reason with them in the best manner. Surely your Lord knows best who has strayed from His way, and He knows best those who are rightly guided.
interpretation: The verse teaches that inviting others to faith should be guided by wisdom, compassionate counsel, and respectful discussion—not harshness or humiliation. The caller’s role is to communicate with care; ultimate knowledge of who is truly misguided or rightly guided belongs to God alone.

translation: If you retaliate, then retaliate only with the like of what you have suffered; but if you are patient, that is surely better for those who are patient.
interpretation: The verse permits justice in response to wrongdoing, but sets a firm limit: retaliation must not exceed the harm suffered. It also teaches that patience and restraint are better than taking retribution.

translation: Be patient, and your patience is only through Allah. Do not grieve over them, and do not be distressed by what they plot.
interpretation: The verse teaches that steadfastness is sustained by reliance on Allah, not by one’s own strength alone. When others reject the truth or scheme against it, the believer is urged to seek that support and not let grief or anxiety weaken their resolve.

translation: Indeed, Allah is with those who are mindful of Him and those who do good.
interpretation: Allah grants His support, guidance, and care to those who avoid disobedience out of reverence for Him and strive to act with excellence. This assurance encourages steadfastness in doing what is right, even in hardship.

translation: Glory be to Him who took His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque, whose surroundings We have blessed, so that We might show him some of Our signs. Surely He alone is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.
interpretation: The verse presents the Night Journey as a sign of God’s limitless power and a special honor bestowed upon His servant. Its closing words affirm that God fully hears and sees, underscoring His complete knowledge of the journey and all that it signifies.

translation: We gave Moses the Scripture and made it guidance for the Children of Israel: “Do not take any protector besides Me.”
interpretation: The verse presents revelation as guidance that leads people to rely on God alone as their ultimate protector and guardian, rather than placing that trust in anyone besides Him.

translation: O descendants of those We carried with Noah, he was indeed a grateful servant.
interpretation: The descendants of those saved with Noah are reminded of their inherited blessing and urged to follow Noah’s example of devoted gratitude to God.

translation: And We declared to the Children of Israel in the Scripture: “You will surely spread corruption in the land twice, and you will surely rise to great arrogance.”
interpretation: This is a divine warning that the Israelites’ wrongdoing and arrogance would recur, urging them to heed the guidance given to them and turn back from corruption.

translation: When the promise concerning the first of the two occasions came to pass, We sent against you servants of Ours, mighty in war, and they searched through the homes; and it was a promise fulfilled.
interpretation: This refers to the first of the two punishments foretold for the Children of Israel after they had spread corruption. Their defeat and the invaders’ advance through their dwellings are presented as the fulfillment of God’s warning, showing that a people’s power cannot shield them from the consequences of persistent wrongdoing.

translation: Then We restored the upper hand to you over them, supported you with wealth and children, and made you greater in number.
interpretation: The reversal of fortune shows that power and prosperity are ultimately in God’s hands. Their renewed strength was also an opportunity to respond with gratitude and faithfulness, not a guarantee of lasting favor.

translation: If you do good, you do good for yourselves; and if you do evil, it is against yourselves. Then, when the promise of the latter occasion comes, [We send them] to bring humiliation to your faces, to enter the mosque as they entered it the first time, and to utterly destroy whatever they gain dominion over.
interpretation: The verse teaches that the consequences of a people’s choices ultimately return to them: righteousness benefits those who practice it, while wrongdoing brings harm upon its own perpetrators. Its warning is that persistent corruption can lead to profound humiliation and loss, reminding people that divine justice is not arbitrary but answers to their deeds.

translation: It may be that your Lord will have mercy on you. But if you return [to wrongdoing], We will return [to punishment]. And We have made Hell a confinement for the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse leaves the door open to divine mercy while warning that returning to corruption brings renewed consequences. Its final clause stresses that persistent disbelief ends in an inescapable confinement in Hell.

translation: Indeed, this Qur’an guides to what is most upright and gives good news to the believers who do righteous deeds: they will have a great reward.
interpretation: The verse presents the Qur’an as a guide toward the soundest way of life—one that leads people toward truth and right conduct. Its promise of reward is connected to faith expressed through righteous action, offering believers both direction for their lives and hope in God’s generosity.

translation: And indeed, for those who do not believe in the Hereafter, We have prepared a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns that denying the Hereafter is not merely a mistaken belief: it rejects the reality of accountability before God, and those who persist in that denial face a punishment already prepared for them.

translation: And man calls for evil as he calls for good; indeed, man is ever hasty.
interpretation: In his haste, a person may ask for something harmful with the same urgency as something beneficial, without weighing its consequences. The verse cautions against impulsive words and prayers, especially in moments of anger or distress.

translation: We made the night and the day two signs. Then We blotted out the sign of the night and made the sign of the day illuminating, so that you may seek bounty from your Lord and know the number of years and the reckoning. And We have explained everything in detail.
interpretation: The alternating darkness and light are presented as signs of purposeful order: night offers rest, while daylight makes activity and earning possible. Their dependable cycle also lets people measure time and keep count. In this way, ordinary patterns of life point to divine wisdom, and the verse closes by affirming that God has made His guidance and signs clear in detail.

translation: Every person’s deeds We have fastened around their neck, and on the Day of Resurrection We will bring forth for them a record that they will find laid open.
interpretation: A person’s own choices and actions remain inseparably their responsibility; on the Day of Resurrection, their complete record will be openly presented, leaving no room to deny what they did.

translation: “Read your record. Today, you are sufficient as your own reckoner.”
interpretation: You will be shown the record of your deeds and recognize their truth for yourself; no outside testimony is needed to make you account for them.

translation: Whoever is guided is guided only for their own benefit, and whoever goes astray goes astray only to their own detriment. No bearer of burdens bears the burden of another. And We would never punish until We had sent a messenger.
interpretation: The verse establishes that moral and spiritual accountability is personal: one cannot transfer one’s choices or their consequences to someone else. It also affirms God’s justice, that punishment does not come before a clear message has been conveyed through a messenger.

translation: When We will to destroy a town, We command its people of privilege to obey Us, but they defiantly disobey there; then the decree becomes due against it, and We destroy it utterly.
interpretation: The verse describes destruction as the consequence of persistent rebellion after divine command and warning. It particularly highlights the privileged, whose influence makes their corruption especially consequential; the punishment is not arbitrary, but follows when defiance becomes entrenched.

translation: How many generations We destroyed after Noah! And your Lord is sufficient as One fully aware of His servants’ sins, ever seeing them.
interpretation: The destruction of earlier peoples is a warning that no community escapes accountability: God knows every wrongdoing and sees every deed, so His judgment is never based on ignorance or injustice.

translation: Whoever desires the immediate life, We hasten for him in it whatever We will, for whomever We will. Then We assign him Hell, where he will burn, condemned and cast away.
interpretation: The verse warns that making worldly life one’s ultimate aim does not guarantee that every desire will be fulfilled: worldly gains remain subject to God’s will. Those who pursue them while turning away from the Hereafter face a final loss and rejection.

translation: Whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it as it should be striven for, while being a believer—those are the ones whose striving is appreciated.
interpretation: The verse teaches that seeking lasting reward requires more than wishing for it: one must make a sincere, fitting effort guided by faith. Such effort is not lost; God accepts and rewards it.

translation: We provide for both these and those from the bounty of your Lord, and the bounty of your Lord is never withheld.
interpretation: God grants worldly provision to people of every kind, so receiving abundance is not by itself proof of divine approval; His generosity reaches all, while ultimate judgment belongs to Him.

translation: Look at how We have favored some of them over others; yet the Hereafter is greater in degrees and greater in favor.
interpretation: Worldly differences in provision, status, and circumstance are only a limited measure of distinction. The lasting and greater distinction is in the Hereafter, where people’s degrees and reward reflect their faith and deeds.

translation: Do not set up another god alongside Allah, lest you sit disgraced and forsaken.
interpretation: The verse warns against associating anything with Allah in worship, affirming that worship belongs to Him alone. Turning away from this truth leads to disgrace and abandonment, while devotion to Allah is the foundation of a person’s dignity and guidance.

translation: Your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and that you treat your parents with kindness. If one or both of them reach old age in your care, do not even say “uff” to them or scold them; speak to them with gracious words.
interpretation: The verse presents care for parents as a devotion inseparable from worshipping God. Its prohibition of even the smallest expression of irritation teaches that kindness is measured not only by what one does for parents, but also by the respect and tenderness with which one speaks to them—especially when age makes them more dependent and vulnerable.

translation: And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy, and say, “My Lord, have mercy upon them as they raised me when I was small.”
interpretation: The verse calls for treating one’s parents with gentle humility, moved by compassion rather than mere duty, and for asking God to show them mercy in return for the care they gave during childhood.

translation: Your Lord knows best what is within yourselves. If you are righteous, then He is indeed ever forgiving to those who continually turn back to Him.
interpretation: God knows the sincerity behind a person’s actions. This gives hope to those who strive to do what is right: when they falter, they should return to Him in repentance, for He forgives those who repeatedly turn back to Him.

translation: Give the relative his due, and the needy person and the wayfarer; and do not squander wastefully.
interpretation: The verse frames wealth as a trust, not merely a personal possession: caring for those with a legitimate claim on one’s resources is part of justice, while wasteful spending violates responsible stewardship.

translation: Indeed, the wasteful are brothers of the devils, and Satan has always been ungrateful to his Lord.
interpretation: Calling the wasteful “brothers of the devils” describes their resemblance to satanic conduct: they squander blessings instead of using them responsibly and gratefully. It is a warning that extravagance is not merely careless spending, but a misuse of what God has entrusted to people.

translation: And if you turn away from them, seeking mercy from your Lord that you hope for, then speak to them a gentle word.
interpretation: When you cannot provide what others ask of you, turn them away with kindness rather than harshness, while hoping for God’s provision and mercy.

translation: Do not keep your hand chained to your neck, nor extend it completely, lest you sit blameworthy and exhausted.
interpretation: The verse teaches moderation in giving and spending: neither stinginess nor reckless generosity is sustainable, and both can leave a person regretting their choices and unable to meet their responsibilities.

translation: Indeed, your Lord grants abundant provision to whom He wills and restricts it. He is ever fully aware of His servants, seeing all that concerns them.
interpretation: Differences in people’s provision are governed by God’s complete knowledge of their circumstances, not by a measure of their worth. The verse invites trust in His wisdom rather than envy or despair.

translation: Do not kill your children for fear of poverty. We provide for them and for you. Indeed, killing them is a grave sin.
interpretation: The verse rejects fear of material hardship as a justification for taking a child’s life, grounding its prohibition in trust that provision is ultimately from God and affirming the sacredness of life.

translation: And do not approach unlawful sexual intercourse. Indeed, it is an abomination and an evil way.
interpretation: The command not to approach it extends beyond the act itself to the choices and circumstances that lead toward it, emphasizing the protection of chastity and the harm such conduct can bring to individuals and society.

translation: Do not take a life that God has made sacred, except by right. If anyone is killed unjustly, We have granted their heir authority; but let them not exceed the limits in seeking justice. Indeed, they have been supported.
interpretation: The verse affirms the sanctity of human life while allowing a victim’s heir to seek lawful justice for an unjust killing. That authority is not permission for revenge without restraint: justice must remain proportionate and within its proper bounds.

translation: Do not go near the property of the orphan except in the best manner, until they reach maturity. And fulfill your covenant; surely the covenant will be called to account.
interpretation: The verse treats both an orphan’s property and a person’s commitments as trusts for which one is answerable before God. Managing an orphan’s wealth is permitted only for their genuine benefit, and it must be safeguarded until they are mature enough to take responsibility for it.

translation: Give full measure when you measure, and weigh with a just balance. That is better and fairest in outcome.
interpretation: The verse teaches that honesty in trade is a matter of justice, not merely good business practice. By refusing to shortchange others and using fair measures, people uphold trust and choose what is better in its lasting consequences.

translation: Do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge. Indeed, hearing, sight, and the heart—each of these will be questioned.
interpretation: The verse calls for intellectual and moral restraint: a person should not accept, repeat, or act on claims without sound grounds, because the faculties through which they receive and judge information carry responsibility before God.

translation: Do not walk upon the earth arrogantly. You will never split the earth open, nor reach the mountains in height.
interpretation: The verse teaches that human power and stature are limited, so pride has no basis. A person should move through life with humility, remembering that no display of superiority can make them greater than they are.

translation: All of that—the evil in it—is detestable in the sight of your Lord.
interpretation: The deeds and conduct just mentioned are morally harmful and displeasing to God, so a believer should avoid them in seeking His approval.

translation: That is among the wisdom your Lord has revealed to you. Do not set up another deity alongside God, lest you be cast into Hell, blameworthy and rejected.
interpretation: The verse presents devotion to God alone as the foundation of the revealed wisdom: treating anything else as divine leads not merely to punishment, but to arriving there with no rightful defense and cut off from God’s mercy.

translation: Has your Lord then favored you with sons and taken daughters for Himself from among the angels? You are indeed saying something monstrous.
interpretation: The verse condemns the claim that angels are God’s daughters, exposing its contradiction: people preferred sons for themselves yet attributed daughters to God. It rejects both assigning offspring to God and making such claims without knowledge.

translation: We have certainly presented in this Qur’an in many ways so that they may take heed, but it only increases them in aversion.
interpretation: The Qur’an offers its reminders in varied forms to invite reflection, yet those who persist in turning away respond by becoming even more resistant to its guidance.

translation: Say, “If there were other gods alongside Him, as they claim, they would surely have sought a way to the Lord of the Throne.”
interpretation: The verse challenges the claim that God has partners: if those supposed gods truly existed, they would seek access to or authority over the Lord of the Throne. Their inability to do so points to God’s absolute sovereignty and the falsehood of associating others with Him.

translation: Glorified and exalted is He, far above what they say.
interpretation: This declares that God is utterly beyond every false or unworthy description people attribute to Him; His majesty and perfection surpass all such claims.

translation: The seven heavens, the earth, and all who are in them glorify Him. There is nothing that does not glorify Him with praise, but you do not understand their glorification. Indeed, He is ever Forbearing, Forgiving.
interpretation: The verse teaches that all creation is engaged in praise of God in ways beyond human perception. Our inability to comprehend this worship should inspire humility, while God’s forbearance and forgiveness offer hope to those who fall short in recognizing and honoring Him.

translation: When you recite the Qur’an, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter a hidden barrier.
interpretation: The barrier signifies that those who reject the Hereafter are prevented from truly receiving the Qur’an’s guidance: though they may hear its words, their refusal keeps them from understanding and responding to its message.

translation: And We have placed coverings over their hearts, so they do not understand it, and deafness in their ears. When you mention your Lord alone in the Qur’an, they turn away in aversion.
interpretation: The verse portrays a deepening refusal to accept the Qur’an: their hostility has become like a barrier to understanding, and their aversion is especially clear when God alone is invoked, without the partners they associate with Him.

translation: We know best what they listen for when they listen to you, and what they whisper among themselves, when the wrongdoers say, “You follow only a man who is bewitched.”
interpretation: God knows that their listening is not sincere: they seek grounds to reject the Prophet, and in private they dismiss his message by accusing him of being bewitched.

translation: Look how they make comparisons about you; they have gone astray and can find no way.
interpretation: The verse points to the opponents’ conflicting descriptions of the Prophet as a sign of their confusion: instead of approaching the truth sincerely, they distort his message and so lose their way to it.

translation: And they say, “When we have become bones and dust, will we really be raised as a new creation?”
interpretation: Their question expresses disbelief in resurrection: they regard the body’s decay as making a new creation impossible, overlooking that the One who created them in the first place is able to bring them back.

translation: Say, “Become stones or iron.”
interpretation: This is a rhetorical challenge to those who doubt resurrection: even if they became something as hard or lifeless as stone or iron, that would not place them beyond God’s power to bring them back to life.

translation: “Or [be] some other creation that seems immense to you.” They will then ask, “Who will bring us back?” Say, “The One who brought you into being the first time.” They will shake their heads at you and ask, “When will that be?” Say, “Perhaps it is near.”
interpretation: The verse challenges the assumption that resurrection is impossible: the One who originated human beings can restore them, whatever form they imagine themselves taking. Their dismissive gestures do not change the reality that the promised return may be close.

translation: On the Day He calls you, you will respond with praise of Him, and you will think that you remained only a little while.
interpretation: The verse portrays the resurrection as a moment when God’s call makes the truth unmistakable: people answer Him, and the vastness of the Hereafter makes their earthly life seem brief. Their response with praise reflects God’s overwhelming majesty and power.

translation: And tell My servants to speak in the best manner. Indeed, Satan sows discord among them; surely Satan is a manifest enemy to humankind.
interpretation: The verse teaches that gracious, measured speech is not merely good manners: it helps prevent Satan from turning words into resentment and division. Believers should therefore choose what is most respectful and constructive, especially when disagreement might provoke conflict.

translation: Your Lord knows you best. If He wills, He will show you mercy, and if He wills, He will punish you. We have not sent you as a guardian over them.
interpretation: The verse reminds the Prophet that he is not responsible for controlling people’s choices or determining their ultimate fate. His role is to convey the message; judgment and mercy belong to God, whose knowledge of every person is complete.

translation: And your Lord knows best who is in the heavens and the earth. We have indeed favored some of the prophets over others, and We gave David the Psalms.
interpretation: The verse teaches that God alone fully knows the worth and circumstances of all creation, so the differing ranks and gifts He grants His prophets rest on wisdom beyond human judgment. David’s receiving of the Psalms is one example of that divinely appointed distinction.

translation: Say, “Call upon those you claim besides Him; they have no power to remove hardship from you or to shift it elsewhere.”
interpretation: The verse challenges people to test the power they attribute to other beings: true authority over hardship and its removal belongs to God alone, so none of those beings can be relied upon as independent protectors or deliverers.

translation: Those whom they call upon themselves seek a way of nearness to their Lord, striving to see which of them is nearest. They hope for His mercy and fear His punishment. Indeed, your Lord’s punishment is ever to be feared.
interpretation: Those invoked besides God are themselves His servants, seeking closeness to Him through obedience and relying on His mercy while fearing His punishment. The verse therefore directs worship and ultimate reliance to God alone.

translation: There is no town but that We will destroy it before the Day of Resurrection or punish it with a severe punishment. That is inscribed in the Book.
interpretation: The verse teaches that every community’s fate lies within God’s prior decree: before the Resurrection, it will either be brought to an end or face severe punishment. No worldly power or apparent security can place a community beyond His judgment.

translation: Nothing prevents Us from sending signs except that the earlier peoples denied them. We gave Thamud the she-camel as a clear sign, but they wronged her. We send signs only as a warning.
interpretation: The verse explains that miraculous signs are not sent merely to satisfy demands: earlier nations received them yet rejected them, as Thamud did when they mistreated the she-camel, and brought judgment upon themselves. Such signs are meant to warn people and call them to heed God before it is too late.

translation: And [remember] when We said to you, “Your Lord encompasses the people.” We made the vision We showed you only a trial for the people, as was the accursed tree mentioned in the Qur’an. We warn them, but it only increases them in great transgression.
interpretation: God’s encompassing knowledge and power assure the Prophet that his opponents remain within divine control. The vision shown to him and the accursed tree—understood as the tree of Zaqqum—serve as tests: they expose whether people will respond to revelation with faith or rejection. For those who persist in defiance, even a warning becomes an occasion for deeper rebellion.

translation: And when We said to the angels, “Prostrate to Adam,” they prostrated, except Iblis. He said, “Should I prostrate to one You created from clay?”
interpretation: Iblis’s question reveals pride: he judged Adam by the material he was made from and treated that as a reason to reject God’s command. The verse warns against letting arrogance and self-assessment override obedience to God; the commanded prostration was an act of honoring Adam, not worshipping him.

translation: He said, “Tell me: this one whom You have honored above me—if You grant me respite until the Day of Resurrection, I will surely bring his descendants under my sway, except for a few.”
interpretation: Iblis’s boast reveals his determination to turn resentment into a campaign of temptation against humanity. Yet his own words acknowledge that his influence will not prevail over everyone: some will remain beyond his reach through steadfastness and devotion to God.

translation: He said, “Go! Whoever among them follows you—Hell will be your recompense, a full recompense.”
interpretation: God allows Satan to pursue his temptation, but those who choose to follow him will face the complete consequence of that choice: Hell. The verse warns that Satan’s influence does not remove people’s responsibility for following him.

translation: “And incite whoever you can among them with your voice; muster against them your cavalry and infantry; share with them in wealth and children, and make them promises.” Satan promises them nothing but delusion.
interpretation: This is a warning that Satan seeks to mislead people through every available means: enticing words, human allies who advance wrongdoing, corruption in how wealth is gained or spent, and the distortion of family life. His promises may make disobedience seem rewarding or secure, but they ultimately deceive; the verse therefore calls people to recognize such enticements and not be taken in by them.

translation: Indeed, over My servants you have no authority; and your Lord is sufficient as a guardian.
interpretation: The verse reassures that Satan cannot compel God’s servants or control their choices; his influence is limited to temptation. God is enough to protect and guide those who turn to Him.

translation: Your Lord is the One who sends ships sailing for you across the sea, so that you may seek of His bounty. Surely He is ever Merciful to you.
interpretation: The passage invites people to recognize that the means by which they travel and earn a living are gifts of God’s mercy, and to respond with gratitude and trust in Him.

translation: When adversity touches you at sea, those you call upon besides Him vanish from your thoughts; but when He brings you safely to land, you turn away. The human being is ever ungrateful.
interpretation: The verse points to how danger can strip away a person’s illusions of control and reveal their dependence on God alone. Yet once safety returns, people may forget the One they called upon and return to heedlessness—an example of human ingratitude.

translation: Do you then feel secure that He will not cause a part of the land to swallow you, or send a storm of stones upon you, leaving you with no protector?
interpretation: The verse warns against assuming that safety is guaranteed: just as God can deliver people from danger, He can bring punishment upon them on land, where no one can shield them from His decree.

translation: Or do you feel secure that He will return you to the sea another time, then send against you a violent gale and drown you for your disbelief? Then you would find no one to plead your cause against Us.
interpretation: The verse warns against mistaking rescue for lasting immunity: people remain dependent on God’s mercy, and no power can guarantee their safety or compel Him to answer for what He decrees.

translation: We have indeed honored the children of Adam, carried them on land and sea, provided them with good things, and greatly favored them over many of those We created.
interpretation: Human dignity is a gift from God, shared by the children of Adam. The verse invites people to recognize that honor in themselves and others, and to respond with gratitude and responsible care for the abilities and provisions entrusted to them.

translation: The Day We call every people with their leader, whoever is given their record in their right hand will read their record, and they will not be wronged in the least.
interpretation: This verse portrays the Day of Judgment as one of personal accountability: people will be summoned in connection with the guide they followed, and each will face the truth of their own record. Those who receive it in their right hand will find that even the smallest measure of injustice has not been done to them.

translation: Whoever is blind in this world will be blind in the Hereafter, and even farther astray from the way.
interpretation: The verse warns that whoever turns away from recognizing God’s signs and guidance in this life will face the consequences in the Hereafter, where they will be more lost still. The blindness meant here is spiritual, not physical.

translation: They nearly tempted you away from what We revealed to you, so that you might invent something else and attribute it to Us; then they would surely have taken you as a close friend.
interpretation: The verse underscores the pressure placed on the Prophet to compromise the revelation for the sake of acceptance. Its warning is that seeking approval by altering what God has revealed would trade fidelity to divine guidance for human favor.

translation: And had We not made you firm, you would almost have inclined to them a little.
interpretation: The verse shows that the Prophet’s steadfastness was upheld by God amid pressure to compromise the revelation. His near inclination was a possibility warded off by divine support, not an actual departure from his duty.

translation: Then We would surely have made you taste a double punishment in this life and a double punishment at death; then you would have found no one to help you against Us.
interpretation: The verse expresses the gravity of the Prophet’s responsibility: had he yielded to pressure to compromise the revelation, his punishment would have been doubled, and no one could have shielded him from God’s judgment.

translation: They nearly provoked you into driving you from the land; but had you left, they would have remained there only a little while after you.
interpretation: The verse warns that the opponents’ efforts to force the Prophet from his homeland would not secure their own future: their power there would soon come to an end. It also reassures him that their hostility cannot overturn God’s purpose.

translation: This was the way We followed with the messengers We sent before you, and you will find no change in Our way.
interpretation: God’s established way with those who try to drive His messengers out will not be altered: their schemes cannot undo His decree, and their power will not endure.

translation: Establish prayer from the sun’s decline until the darkness of night, and [also] the recitation at dawn. Indeed, the recitation at dawn is witnessed.
interpretation: The verse marks the appointed prayers across the day and night and gives special emphasis to dawn prayer: its recitation is witnessed by the angels, underscoring the spiritual distinction of this quiet, devoted hour.

translation: And during part of the night, keep vigil in prayer with it as an additional devotion for you; perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station.
interpretation: The verse gives night prayer a special place in the Prophet’s devotion, linking this extra worship with the honored station Allah will grant him—a station traditionally understood to include his great intercession on the Day of Judgment.

translation: And say, “My Lord, bring me in with a truthful entrance and bring me out with a truthful departure, and grant me from Yourself a supporting authority.”
interpretation: This is a prayer for God to guide every beginning and ending toward what is right and sincere, and to provide decisive help and strength from Him in carrying out His mission.

translation: And say, “The truth has come, and falsehood has vanished. Indeed, falsehood is bound to vanish.”
interpretation: The verse affirms that falsehood has no lasting foundation: when God’s truth is made clear, it exposes falsehood’s weakness and its hold is destined to end.

translation: And We send down of the Qur’an that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers, but it increases the wrongdoers in nothing but loss.
interpretation: The Qur’an heals the believers by guiding and strengthening their hearts, and its guidance is a mercy to them. Those who persist in wrongdoing and reject it instead grow further from guidance, so their response to it deepens their loss.

translation: When We bestow favor upon a person, he turns away and withdraws; but when adversity touches him, he becomes despairing.
interpretation: The verse warns against a heart that lets comfort breed heedlessness and lets hardship extinguish hope. Its deeper lesson is to remain humble and mindful of God in times of ease, and to hold fast to hope and trust in Him in times of difficulty.

translation: Say, “Everyone acts according to their own disposition, and your Lord knows best who is most rightly guided.”
interpretation: People’s actions reflect their inner disposition and way of life, but their true standing is known fully to God. The verse therefore cautions against claiming certainty about who is rightly guided and calls each person to examine the way they follow.

translation: They ask you about the Spirit. Say, “The Spirit is of the command of my Lord, and you have been given only a little knowledge.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that the Spirit’s deepest reality lies beyond human knowledge and belongs to God’s domain. It calls people to humility about what they cannot fully know, rather than claiming certainty where revelation has left the matter undisclosed.

translation: If We willed, We could surely take away what We have revealed to you; then you would find no one to plead for you against Us concerning it.
interpretation: The verse teaches that revelation is bestowed by God’s will, not something anyone can claim independently. Its continued presence is therefore a divine favor, calling the recipient to humility and gratitude.

translation: Except through a mercy from your Lord. Indeed, His favor upon you has been great.
interpretation: God’s mercy is what preserves the revelation for the Prophet; its continued guidance is a great favor from Him, not something the Prophet can secure by his own power.

translation: Say, “If humankind and jinn were to gather to produce the like of this Qur’an, they could not produce its like, even if they supported one another.”
interpretation: The verse presents the Qur’an as beyond the reach of human and jinn ability: even their combined knowledge and cooperation could not reproduce it. Its challenge points to its divine origin and calls its hearers to consider its message seriously.

translation: We have certainly presented people in this Qur’an with every kind of example, yet most people insist on nothing but disbelief.
interpretation: The verse suggests that rejection is not always caused by a lack of clear guidance: even when truth is explained in varied ways, many may refuse it because they are unwilling to turn toward it.

translation: And they said, “We will never believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth.”
interpretation: Their demand made belief conditional on a particular miracle of their choosing, revealing that they were challenging the Prophet rather than approaching his message with openness.

translation: Or [until] you have a garden of date palms and grapes, and make rivers gush forth abundantly through it.
interpretation: The speakers demand a lush, miraculous sign as a condition for belief, revealing that their resistance is not simply a lack of evidence but an insistence on proof of their own choosing.

translation: “Or cause the sky to fall upon us in pieces, as you have claimed, or bring Allah and the angels before us.”
interpretation: These demands express the opponents’ defiance, not a sincere search for guidance: they insist on spectacular proof on their own terms, even demanding to see Allah and the angels, rather than responding to the message already presented to them.

translation: “Or you have a house adorned with gold, or ascend into heaven—and we will not believe in your ascent until you bring down to us a book that we can read.” Say, “Glory be to my Lord! Am I anything but a human messenger?”
interpretation: The verse portrays demands for ever more extraordinary signs as a condition of belief, while affirming that a messenger does not command revelation or miracles at will; his task is to convey what God entrusts to him.

translation: Nothing prevented people from believing when guidance came to them except that they said, “Has Allah sent a human being as a messenger?”
interpretation: The verse identifies a mistaken objection that can obstruct faith: people reject the guidance not because it is unclear, but because its messenger is human. Yet a human messenger can speak to people in a way they understand and embody the guidance in a life they can follow.

translation: Say, “If there were angels walking securely on earth, We would have sent down to them from heaven an angel as a messenger.”
interpretation: God’s messengers are suited to those they are sent to: because people live human lives on earth, their messenger is human, so they can understand and follow his example.

translation: Say, “Allah is sufficient as a witness between me and you. Surely He is ever fully aware of His servants and all-seeing.”
interpretation: The Prophet is told to entrust the truth of his message to Allah’s testimony: Allah knows the sincerity of His servants and sees their actions, so no denial or accusation can escape His judgment.

translation: Whoever Allah guides is truly guided; but whoever He leaves astray, you will find no protectors for them besides Him. On the Day of Resurrection, We will gather them on their faces, blind, dumb, and deaf. Their abode will be Hell; whenever its flames subside, We will increase them in blazing fire.
interpretation: The verse teaches that true guidance and ultimate misguidance lie in Allah’s hands, and that those who turn away from His guidance will have no protector able to save them from His judgment. Their gathering in a state of blindness, silence, and deafness portrays their utter humiliation and loss of ability, while the fire’s renewed blaze expresses the unrelenting consequence of their rejection.

translation: That is their recompense because they disbelieved in Our signs and said, “When we have become bones and dust, will we really be raised as a new creation?”
interpretation: Their denial of resurrection rests on treating bodily decay as a limit on God’s power. The verse presents their punishment as the consequence of rejecting God’s signs and dismissing the possibility that He can bring creation back into being.

translation: Have they not seen that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth, is able to create the like of them? He has appointed for them a term about which there is no doubt, yet the wrongdoers insist on nothing but disbelief.
interpretation: The One who brought the heavens, the earth, and humanity into existence has the power to bring people back to life. Their appointed term—and the reckoning that follows—is certain, but those who do wrong persist in rejecting it.

translation: Say, “If you possessed the treasuries of my Lord’s mercy, you would surely withhold them for fear of spending; for man is ever miserly.”
interpretation: The verse exposes how fear of scarcity can make people cling to what they have: even if they held the treasures of God’s mercy, they would hesitate to give lest it run out. It contrasts this human stinginess with the boundless generosity of God.

translation: We certainly gave Moses nine clear signs. So ask the Children of Israel about when he came to them; Pharaoh said to him, “Moses, I truly think you are bewitched.”
interpretation: The verse highlights how clear signs do not compel someone who is determined to reject them: Pharaoh answered Moses’ evidence with an accusation against him rather than engaging with its meaning.

translation: He said, “You know that none has sent these [signs] down except the Lord of the heavens and the earth, as clear proofs. And I truly think, O Pharaoh, that you are doomed.”
interpretation: Moses confronts Pharaoh with the truth he already recognizes: the signs are unmistakable evidence from God, and Pharaoh’s stubborn rejection will lead to his ruin.

translation: So he intended to drive them from the land, but We drowned him and all who were with him.
interpretation: The verse shows that Pharaoh’s power could not make his oppression succeed: his attempt to expel Moses and his people ended in his own destruction, illustrating that worldly authority cannot withstand God’s judgment.

translation: And We said after him to the Children of Israel, “Dwell in the land; then, when the promise of the Hereafter comes, We will bring you all together.”
interpretation: The verse points to God’s final gathering of the Children of Israel after their time of earthly settlement: however dispersed they may be, they will all be brought together at the appointed time, ultimately for the reckoning.

translation: We sent it down with the truth, and it descended with the truth. We sent you only as a bearer of good news and a warner.
interpretation: The Qur’an’s origin and revelation are rooted in truth, and the Prophet’s mission is to convey it faithfully—offering hope to those who respond to God and warning those who turn away.

translation: And We have sent down the Qur’an in portions, so that you may recite it to the people deliberately and gradually; and We have sent it down in stages.
interpretation: Its gradual revelation made room for people to hear, reflect on, and absorb the guidance over time. The Prophet’s measured recitation likewise invites careful attention rather than hurried reading.

translation: Say, “Believe in it or do not believe.” Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it, when it is recited to them, fall down in prostration, face down.
interpretation: The verse teaches that the truth of revelation does not depend on whether people accept it. Those sincerely grounded in knowledge recognize its divine message and respond with humility and submission.

translation: And they say, “Glory be to our Lord! Surely our Lord’s promise has been fulfilled.”
interpretation: Their words express humble awe and recognition that God’s promise is true and certain to come to pass.

translation: And they fall upon their faces, weeping, and it increases them in humility.
