interpretation: The verse portrays hearts so receptive to divine truth that it deepens their reverence and softens them into sincere humility.

translation: Say, “Call upon Allah, or call upon the Most Merciful; whichever name you call upon, to Him belong the Most Beautiful Names.” And do not recite your prayer too loudly, nor too quietly, but seek a way between the two.
interpretation: Allah and the Most Merciful are names of the one God, and whichever of His beautiful names a person invokes, the supplication is directed to Him. The instruction about recitation calls for a balanced voice—neither so loud that it causes disturbance nor so quiet that the worshipper can scarcely hear it.

translation: And say, “Praise belongs to Allah, who has taken no son, has no partner in sovereignty, and needs no protector to shield Him from weakness. And proclaim His greatness with all due magnificence.”
interpretation: The verse grounds Allah’s greatness in His absolute independence: He neither derives power from family or partnership nor relies on anyone for protection. Praise and glorification therefore belong to Him alone, without qualification or limit.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Praise belongs to Allah, who sent down the Book upon His servant and made no crookedness in it.
interpretation: The verse praises Allah for revealing the Qur’an to His servant as a sound and straight guidance, free from deviation or defect.

translation: An upright [Book], to warn of severe punishment from Him and to give good news to the believers who do righteous deeds that they will have a good reward.
interpretation: The Qur’an is described as sound and free from deviation: its warning and promise guide people toward accountability before God, while assuring those who believe and act righteously of a gracious reward.

translation: Abiding therein forever.
interpretation: The phrase emphasizes that their stay there is permanent, with no end or return.

translation: And to warn those who say, “Allah has taken a son.”
interpretation: This warning rejects attributing offspring to Allah: it conflicts with His absolute oneness and perfection, and is a grave claim made without sound knowledge.

translation: They have no knowledge of it, nor did their forefathers. Terrible is the word that comes from their mouths; they speak nothing but lies.
interpretation: The verse condemns asserting that God has a son without any knowledge or evidence. The gravity of such a claim is heightened by its being repeated as inherited belief, when it is in fact a falsehood about God.

translation: Perhaps you would nearly destroy yourself with grief, following after them, if they do not believe in this message.
interpretation: The verse gently consoles the Prophet ﷺ: his deep concern for those who reject the revelation is understandable, but he must not let their refusal consume him. He is responsible for conveying the guidance, not for compelling people to accept it.

translation: Indeed, We have made whatever is on the earth an adornment for it, so that We may test which of them is best in deeds.
interpretation: The beauty and attractions of earthly life are a test, not a measure of a person’s worth. What matters is how one responds to them—with sincere and upright deeds—rather than how much of them one possesses.

translation: And indeed, We will make all that is upon it barren ground.
interpretation: The verse reminds us that the earth’s beauty and abundance are temporary, and that worldly life should not be mistaken for something lasting or ultimate.

translation: Or did you think that the companions of the cave and the inscription were among Our most wondrous signs?
interpretation: The verse places their remarkable story in perspective: it is a sign of God’s power, but not beyond the wonder of His other signs or the act of bringing the dead back to life.

translation: When the young men took refuge in the cave, they said, “Our Lord, grant us mercy from Yourself and guide us to what is right in our situation.”
interpretation: Their prayer expresses trust in God when they faced danger and uncertainty: they sought not merely safety, but God’s mercy and the wisdom to choose the right course.

translation: So We sealed their hearing in the cave for a number of years.
interpretation: The expression means that God caused them to sleep so deeply that they could not hear or be awakened, preserving them in the cave for the appointed years.

translation: Then We awakened them so that We might make clear which of the two groups had more accurately calculated how long they had remained.
interpretation: Their awakening brought the question of their time in the cave into the open, revealing the limits of human estimates and making clear that the full knowledge of their stay belongs to God.

translation: We relate to you their story in truth: they were young men who believed in their Lord, and We increased them in guidance.
interpretation: Their steadfast faith was met with further guidance from God: as they sincerely turned to their Lord, He strengthened them in the right path.

translation: We strengthened their hearts when they stood and said, “Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth. We will never call upon any god besides Him; if we did, we would indeed have spoken an outrageous falsehood.”
interpretation: God granted them steadfastness to proclaim His oneness openly despite the pressure they faced. Their words show that worship belongs to the Creator alone, and that assigning divinity to anything else is a grave departure from the truth.

translation: These are our people, who have taken gods besides Him. Why do they not bring clear proof for them? And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about Allah?
interpretation: The speakers reject their people’s worship of other gods because it has no clear evidence from God. They regard attributing partners to Him as a grave falsehood, since no one is more unjust than a person who knowingly invents a lie about Allah.

translation: “Since you have withdrawn from them and from what they worship besides Allah, take refuge in the cave. Your Lord will spread His mercy over you and make your situation easy for you.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that when believers leave a setting that threatens their faith, seeking refuge in Allah, He can turn their hardship into a means of mercy and provide a way forward they could not secure for themselves.

translation: You would have seen the sun, as it rose, inclining away from their cave to the right, and as it set, passing away from them to the left, while they lay in an open space within it. That is among the signs of Allah. Whoever Allah guides is truly guided, and whoever He lets go astray—you will never find for him a protector to guide him.
interpretation: The careful position of the cave protected its sleepers from the sun while leaving them in an open space, revealing Allah’s care over them. The verse also points beyond this remarkable protection to the deeper truth that lasting guidance comes from Allah; no protector can guide someone whom He leaves astray.

translation: You would have thought them awake, though they were asleep. We turned them over to the right and to the left, while their dog stretched its forelegs across the entrance. Had you come upon them, you would have turned away in flight and been filled with terror.
interpretation: Their sleep and fearsome appearance served as a means of divine protection, keeping others from disturbing them while they remained in the cave.

translation: And thus We awakened them so that they might question one another. One of them said, “How long have you been here?” They said, “We have been here a day, or part of a day.” They said, “Your Lord knows best how long you have been here. So send one of you with these silver coins of yours to the town; let him find which food is purest, and bring you provision from it. Let him be discreet, and do not let anyone become aware of you.”
interpretation: Their uncertainty about the passage of time shows how completely God had preserved them through an extraordinary span. Their careful plan to obtain food and avoid notice reflects prudent action amid danger, while their words acknowledge that the true measure of their ordeal is known to God alone.

translation: Indeed, if they discover you, they will stone you or force you back into their religion, and then you will never prosper.
interpretation: The warning reflects the young believers’ fear that their persecutors would use violence or coercion to make them abandon their faith. Their concern is not merely for their safety: being forced away from sincere belief would mean losing the ultimate success they sought.

translation: Thus We caused them to be discovered, so that people might know that God’s promise is true and that the Hour is beyond doubt. As they disputed among themselves about what to do with them, some said, “Build a structure over them.” Their Lord knows them best. Those whose authority prevailed said, “We will surely establish a place of worship over them.”
interpretation: The discovery of the sleepers became a sign that God can raise the dead, confirming the truth of His promise and the certainty of the Hour. The verse also recounts how people disagreed about what to do with them, while affirming that their true state is known best to God.

translation: They will say, “They were three, and their dog was the fourth”; and they will say, “They were five, and their dog was the sixth,” guessing at the unseen. And they will say, “They were seven, and their dog was the eighth.” Say, “My Lord knows best their number; none knows them except a few.” So do not argue about them except with a clear argument, and do not ask any of them about them.
interpretation: The verse teaches restraint when knowledge is uncertain: speculation should not be treated as fact, and arguments should not go beyond what can be established. It directs attention away from details God has not made clear and toward humility before His knowledge.

translation: And never say of anything, “I will surely do that tomorrow,”
interpretation: This teaches that people should not speak with certainty about what they will do in the future, since their plans depend on what Allah wills.

translation: Unless Allah wills. Remember your Lord when you forget, and say, “Perhaps my Lord will guide me to what is nearer than this to right guidance.”
interpretation: The verse teaches humility about the future: human intentions and plans remain subject to Allah’s will. If one forgets to acknowledge this, one should remember Allah when it comes to mind, and seek His guidance with hope that He will lead to what is more rightly guided.

translation: And they remained in their cave for three hundred years, and added nine.
interpretation: The verse gives the length of their stay as three hundred years, with nine more counted according to a different calendar reckoning—commonly understood as the difference between three hundred solar years and three hundred and nine lunar years. Their long stay unfolded by God’s will.

translation: Say, “Allah knows best how long they remained. To Him belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth. How perfectly He sees and hears! They have no protector besides Him, and He shares His judgment with no one.”
interpretation: The true measure of their stay is known to Allah alone, whose knowledge and perception encompass all that is hidden and apparent. Since all authority belongs to Him, no one can protect or share in His judgment; people should therefore entrust such unseen matters to Him rather than claim certainty without knowledge.

translation: Recite what has been revealed to you from the Book of your Lord. No one can alter His words, and you will find no refuge apart from Him.
interpretation: The verse calls the Prophet to remain faithful to the revelation, whose truth and decree no one can change. It also teaches that no one can provide ultimate shelter or protection apart from God.

translation: And keep yourself patiently with those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His pleasure. Do not let your eyes turn away from them, desiring the adornment of worldly life, and do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance, who follows his desires, and whose conduct is excessive.
interpretation: The verse teaches that closeness to God is not measured by worldly status. A believer should value the company of sincere worshippers, remain devoted to them even when they seem unimpressive by worldly standards, and resist the influence of those who neglect remembrance of God and let their desires govern their lives.

translation: And say, “The truth is from your Lord. So whoever wills, let him believe; and whoever wills, let him disbelieve.” Indeed, We have prepared for the wrongdoers a Fire whose walls will encompass them. If they plead for relief, they will be given water like molten metal that scalds their faces. What a wretched drink, and what an evil resting place!
interpretation: The choice to accept or reject faith is presented as a real human responsibility, not as permission to treat both choices as equally sound or without consequence. The truth does not depend on people’s acceptance of it; each person must choose, and answer for that choice before God.

translation: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds—We never let the reward of anyone who does good deeds go to waste.
interpretation: The verse assures that God’s justice and generosity preserve the value of sincere goodness: no one who strives to do what is right is overlooked or deprived of its reward.

translation: Those are the ones who will have the Gardens of Eden, beneath which rivers flow. There they will be adorned with bracelets of gold and wear green garments of fine silk and brocade, reclining upon couches. What an excellent reward and what a beautiful resting place.
interpretation: The verse presents Paradise as a lasting fulfillment of dignity, beauty, and repose: the signs of honor and comfort familiar in this life are perfected there, while the inhabitants enjoy security and nearness to God’s reward.

translation: And set forth for them the example of two men: We gave one of them two gardens of grapevines, surrounded them with palm trees, and placed crops between them.
interpretation: The carefully cultivated abundance in this example points to worldly prosperity as a gift entrusted by God, not something a person should mistake for proof of their own independence or lasting security.

translation: Both gardens yielded their produce and withheld nothing of it, and We caused a river to flow between them.
interpretation: The gardens’ complete yield and flowing water show that their prosperity was a gift from God, not something their owner could claim as proof of his own power or security.

translation: He had abundant produce, and he said to his companion as he conversed with him, “I have more wealth than you and greater support in men.”
interpretation: His words reveal the arrogance of measuring worth by worldly riches and social standing. He treats his prosperity and followers as proof of superiority, overlooking that such blessings are temporary and do not make him inherently better than his companion.

translation: And he entered his garden, wronging himself, and said, “I do not think this will ever perish.”
interpretation: His words reveal how attachment to worldly prosperity can distort judgment: he mistakes a temporary blessing for something permanent and, in doing so, becomes heedless of his dependence on God.

translation: “I do not think the Hour will ever come. And if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely find something better than this as my destination.”
interpretation: The speaker’s confidence in his worldly prosperity has become arrogance: he doubts the Resurrection, yet presumes that even then he will be rewarded with something better. The verse exposes the false assumption that wealth in this life guarantees favor with God in the next.

translation: His companion said to him, as he was speaking with him, “Do you disbelieve in the One who created you from dust, then from a drop, and then fashioned you into a man?”
interpretation: The question confronts him with the contradiction between denying God and the very existence God brought about. Remembering his humble beginnings and gradual creation calls him to humility and recognition that his life and form are gifts, not grounds for arrogance.

translation: But as for me, He is Allah, my Lord, and I associate no one with my Lord.
interpretation: The speaker declares that his security and worth rest in recognizing Allah as his sole Lord, rejecting the pride and false confidence that come from treating anything or anyone as a partner with Him.

translation: Why, when you entered your garden, did you not say, “What Allah has willed; there is no power except through Allah”? Though you see me as having less than you in wealth and children…
interpretation: The verse teaches that a person should meet worldly blessings with humility, recognizing that they come by Allah’s will and are not secured by one’s own power. Such recognition guards against pride and the illusion that prosperity is entirely one’s own achievement.

translation: Perhaps my Lord will give me something better than your garden, and send upon it a calamity from the sky, leaving it barren, slippery ground.
interpretation: The speaker recognizes that worldly wealth is neither secure nor proof of divine favor: God may replace it with something better or remove it entirely. The verse therefore cautions against pride in possessions and affirms that ultimate power and provision belong to God.

translation: Or its water may sink deep into the earth, and you will never be able to recover it.
interpretation: The verse warns that blessings people take for granted can be withdrawn beyond their power to restore, so prosperity should inspire humility and reliance on God rather than arrogance.

translation: And his fruits were utterly destroyed. So he began wringing his hands over what he had spent on it, while it lay fallen upon its trellises, and he said, “If only I had not associated anyone with my Lord!”
interpretation: The ruin of his garden exposes how fragile worldly wealth is and how misplaced his confidence had been. Faced with the loss, he recognizes that associating partners with God was a grave error—but only after the consequences have come upon him.

translation: He had no group to help him against Allah, nor could he defend himself.
interpretation: The verse teaches that worldly power and supporters cannot shield anyone from Allah’s judgment; when His decree comes, a person’s own strength is of no avail.

translation: There, all authority belongs to Allah, the True. He is best in reward and best in outcome.
interpretation: When worldly power and possessions prove unable to protect anyone, it becomes clear that ultimate authority belongs to Allah alone. His judgment is true, and the lasting reward and final outcome He grants are better than anything the world can offer.

translation: Set forth for them the example of the life of this world: it is like water We send down from the sky, with which the plants of the earth flourish; then they become dry fragments scattered by the winds. And Allah has power over all things.
interpretation: The verse teaches that worldly life, however flourishing and beautiful it may seem, is temporary and can swiftly fade away. Its attractions should not be mistaken for lasting security, for all things remain subject to Allah’s power.

translation: Wealth and children are the adornment of worldly life, but lasting righteous deeds are better with your Lord in reward and better as a source of hope.
interpretation: Worldly possessions and family may bring beauty and comfort, but their value is temporary. What endures is a person’s righteous deeds, whose reward with God is greater and whose promise offers more reliable hope than anything the world can provide.

translation: And [remember] the Day We set the mountains in motion, and you see the earth laid bare; We gather them all, leaving none of them behind.
interpretation: The verse portrays the complete exposure of reality on the Day of Resurrection: worldly landmarks and concealments are removed, and no person can escape being brought before God for judgment.

translation: They will be presented before your Lord in ranks: “You have come to Us just as We created you the first time. Yet you claimed that We would never appoint a meeting for you.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the Day of Judgment, when all people stand before God without the worldly distinctions or power they once possessed, as helpless as they were at their first creation. Their denial that they would be raised and brought to account is then confronted by the reality before them.

translation: The record will be placed, and you will see the guilty fearful of what it contains. They will say, “Woe to us! What kind of record is this? It leaves out nothing, small or great, without recording it!” They will find all they did present before them, and your Lord wrongs no one.
interpretation: The verse portrays the Day of Judgment as a moment when every person’s actions are fully brought to light. The guilty are terrified not merely by the record itself, but by the certainty that nothing has been omitted; yet this complete accounting also affirms God’s perfect justice: each person encounters the truth of their deeds, and no one is treated unfairly.

translation: And [remember] when We said to the angels, “Prostrate to Adam,” and they prostrated, except Iblis. He was one of the jinn, and he defied the command of his Lord. Will you then take him and his offspring as allies instead of Me, even though they are your enemies? What a wretched exchange for the wrongdoers!
interpretation: The verse warns that Iblis’s refusal was a deliberate rebellion against God, and that making him and his descendants guides or allies means turning away from the One who deserves obedience toward those who seek human harm. Such allegiance is a grievous loss for those who wrong themselves.

translation: I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor their own creation; nor would I take those who lead others astray as helpers.
interpretation: The verse rejects any claim that the rebellious beings have special knowledge or authority over creation: they neither witnessed its making nor have a role in sustaining it. God’s guidance and governance do not depend on those who mislead, so they cannot rightly be treated as divine partners or trusted sources of authority.

translation: And on the Day He will say, “Call upon My partners whom you claimed.” They will call upon them, but they will not answer them, and We will place between them a gulf of destruction.
interpretation: Those who relied on false gods will discover that their supposed partners have no power to help them. Their bond will end in ruin, leaving them separated and abandoned when they most need aid.

translation: The guilty will see the Fire and realize that they are about to fall into it, and they will find no way to turn away from it.
interpretation: The verse portrays the moment when denial gives way to certainty: those who have turned from truth recognize the consequence before them, with no escape or refuge left. That inevitability warns that worldly heedlessness cannot undo what a person has chosen.

translation: We have certainly presented for people in this Qur’an every kind of example, yet the human being is, of all things, the most argumentative.
interpretation: The verse points to how guidance is made clear through many different examples, while people may still resist it through argument. It cautions against using one’s ability to debate as a way to evade truth rather than recognize and follow it.

translation: Nothing prevented people from believing when guidance came to them and seeking forgiveness from their Lord except that the fate of earlier peoples should befall them, or that punishment should come upon them face to face.
interpretation: The verse warns against postponing faith and repentance until punishment becomes undeniable. Guidance and the chance to seek forgiveness have already been given; refusing them leaves a person to confront the consequences that befell earlier peoples or to witness punishment directly.

translation: We send the messengers only as bearers of good news and warners. Yet those who disbelieve argue with falsehood to try to defeat the truth by it, and they take My signs and the warnings given to them as a joke.
interpretation: The verse distinguishes the messengers’ sincere purpose—to offer hope and caution people against wrongdoing—from the conduct of those who reject their message. Their disputes are not a genuine search for truth: they use falsehood to obscure what is true and treat revelation and its warnings with contempt.

translation: Who is more unjust than one who is reminded of the signs of their Lord, yet turns away from them and forgets what their own hands have sent ahead? We have placed coverings over their hearts, lest they understand it, and heaviness in their ears. Even if you call them to guidance, they will never be guided, then, ever.
interpretation: The verse warns that persistent rejection of divine reminders can leave a person increasingly unable to recognize or respond to the truth: turning away and disregarding one’s own deeds becomes a barrier to guidance.

translation: And your Lord is the All-Forgiving, the Possessor of Mercy. If He were to take them to task for what they have earned, He would hasten the punishment for them. Rather, they have an appointed time, from which they will find no refuge.
interpretation: God’s delay in punishing wrongdoing is an expression of His mercy and forbearance, not a sign that people are beyond accountability. Their reckoning has been set for its appointed time, and when it comes, no refuge can avert it.

translation: Those towns—we destroyed them when their people did wrong, and We set an appointed time for their destruction.
interpretation: Their destruction was not arbitrary or without warning: wrongdoing brought its consequence, but it came only at the appointed time set by God.

translation: And when Moses said to his young companion, “I will not stop until I reach the meeting place of the two seas, even if I travel for a long time.”
interpretation: Moses’ words show his firm resolve to pursue what he sought: he was willing to endure a long journey rather than abandon his goal. The verse thus highlights the perseverance required in seeking knowledge.

translation: When they reached the place where the two seas met, they forgot their fish, and it made its way into the sea, slipping away.
interpretation: The fish’s unusual escape was a sign marking the place they had been seeking, though its significance was not noticed at the time.

translation: When they had gone farther, he said to his attendant, “Bring us our meal; we have indeed suffered weariness on this journey of ours.”
interpretation: The verse shows that even a journey undertaken for knowledge is marked by ordinary human needs and limits. Their weariness also signals that the journey is approaching a moment when an overlooked detail will become important.

translation: He said, “Do you remember when we took shelter by the rock? I forgot the fish, and none made me forget to mention it except Satan. It took its way into the sea in a wondrous manner.”
interpretation: The young man’s admission shows that even an extraordinary sign may go unnoticed when attention is diverted; the verse also acknowledges forgetfulness without excusing it, by urging awareness of how Satan can distract a person from remembering what matters.

translation: He said, “That is what we were seeking!” So they returned, retracing their footsteps.
interpretation: The event they had initially overlooked became the sign that guided them to their destination. Their return shows the importance of recognizing meaningful signs and responding to them with persistence.

translation: Then they found one of Our servants, to whom We had granted mercy from Us and taught knowledge from Our own presence.
interpretation: The verse shows that God may grant a servant both special mercy and knowledge beyond ordinary human understanding, reminding us that human knowledge is limited and that divine wisdom may not be immediately apparent.

translation: Moses said to him, “May I follow you so that you may teach me some of the right guidance you have been taught?”
interpretation: Moses’ request reflects humility in seeking knowledge: even with his own prophetic wisdom, he approaches someone granted knowledge by God as a learner, asking respectfully to accompany him and benefit from what he has been taught.

translation: He said, “You will not be able to be patient with me.”
interpretation: The words warn that patience is difficult when events seem confusing or troubling; understanding may require waiting until their wisdom becomes clear.

translation: “And how can you be patient with what you have not fully understood?”
interpretation: The verse points to the difficulty of remaining patient when events seem troubling or inexplicable: a person’s understanding is limited, and the wisdom behind what they witness may not yet be clear.

translation: He said, “If Allah wills, you will find me patient, and I will not disobey any instruction of yours.”
interpretation: His promise reflects both earnestness and humility: he intends to remain patient and follow his teacher’s instructions, while acknowledging that his resolve ultimately depends on Allah’s will.

translation: He said, “If you follow me, do not ask me about anything until I explain it to you.”
interpretation: Moses is asked to be patient and refrain from questioning what he witnesses until his companion has explained it; the condition makes room for understanding that may not be apparent at first.

translation: So they went on until, when they boarded a ship, he made a hole in it. He said, “Did you make a hole in it to drown its people? You have certainly done a dreadful thing.”
interpretation: The verse shows Moses reacting to an act that appears to put innocent people in grave danger. His protest reflects the natural judgment that damaging the ship could bring harm to its passengers, while the scene also sets up the contrast between what appears wrong and what may have a wisdom not yet known to him.

translation: He said, “Did I not tell you that you would never be able to remain patient with me?”
interpretation: The reminder underscores that patience is difficult when the wisdom behind what one witnesses is still hidden; Moses is being asked to wait for the explanation before judging what has happened.

translation: He said, “Do not take me to task for what I forgot, and do not make my affair difficult for me.”
interpretation: Moses asks for patience and leniency after breaking the agreement through forgetfulness, acknowledging his mistake while pleading not to be burdened beyond what he can bear.

translation: So the two went on until they met a boy, and he killed him. Moses said, “Have you killed an innocent soul, though he had killed no one? You have certainly done a terrible thing.”
interpretation: Moses’s protest reflects the moral judgment warranted by what was visible to him: taking an apparently innocent life without just cause is an enormity. The verse highlights the seriousness of that act and the limits of judging an unseen matter before its full grounds are known.

translation: He said, “Did I not tell you that you would never be able to bear patiently with me?”
interpretation: The words point to the limits of judging events by what is immediately visible: patience may require trust when the wisdom behind another’s actions has not yet been disclosed.

translation: He said, “If I ask you about anything after this, then do not keep me as your companion. You have received from me a sufficient excuse.”
interpretation: Moses acknowledges that he has broken his promise again and gives his companion the right to part ways if it happens once more, accepting that he will then have no grounds to object.

translation: So the two set out, until, when they came to the people of a town, they asked its people for food, but they refused to host them. Then they found a wall there that was about to collapse, and he set it upright. Moses said, “If you had wished, you could have taken payment for it.”
interpretation: Moses’s remark reflects the immediate hardship of being refused hospitality: taking payment for repairing the wall could have provided them with food. Yet the act was done without reward, hinting that its purpose lay beyond what Moses could see. The verse therefore underscores the limits of judging an action before its hidden wisdom is made known.

translation: He said, “This is the parting between me and you. I will explain to you the meaning of what you could not bear patiently.”
interpretation: The verse points to the limits of what one can learn when patience and trust are required: events may appear troubling or inexplicable, while their deeper wisdom is not yet known. The promised explanation shows that judgment based only on what is immediately visible can be incomplete.

translation: As for the ship, it belonged to poor people who worked at sea. I intended to damage it because there was a king ahead of them who seized every ship by force.
interpretation: The ship’s flaw was a temporary protection: by making it seem unworthy of seizure, the damage spared its owners from losing their livelihood to the king.

translation: As for the boy, his parents were believers, and we feared that he would overwhelm them with rebellion and disbelief.
interpretation: The boy’s death was a hidden act of mercy for his believing parents: had he lived, his rebelliousness and disbelief might have deeply afflicted them and drawn them away from their faith.

translation: So we desired that their Lord replace him for them with one better in purity and closer in affection.
interpretation: The replacement was meant to be a mercy for the parents: a child of greater purity and a more loving bond with them.

translation: “As for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city, and beneath it was a treasure belonging to them. Their father had been righteous, so your Lord willed that they should reach maturity and retrieve their treasure, as a mercy from your Lord. I did not do it on my own accord. This is the explanation of what you could not bear patiently.”
interpretation: The wall’s preservation shows that God may protect the interests of the vulnerable through wisdom hidden from human sight; the father’s righteousness is linked to this care for his children. The speaker makes clear that the act was carried out by God’s command, not personal judgment, and that its purpose could only be understood once its concealed wisdom was revealed.

translation: They ask you about Dhul-Qarnayn. Say, “I will recite to you an account of him.”
interpretation: The verse presents the account as a purposeful reminder: what follows is not an exhaustive biography, but a revelation-guided telling from which people may draw understanding.

translation: Indeed, We established him in the land and granted him the means to accomplish all things.
interpretation: His authority and resources were divinely granted, enabling him to pursue his aims through the means God placed at his disposal.

translation: So he followed a course.
interpretation: It conveys purposeful action: he took the means available to him and proceeded toward his goal.

translation: Until, when he reached the place where the sun sets, he found it setting in a muddy spring, and he found a people there. We said, “O Dhul-Qarnayn, either punish them or treat them kindly.”
interpretation: The verse describes what appeared to Dhul-Qarnayn from his vantage point as he reached the far west. He was then given authority to punish wrongdoing or deal kindly with the people, implying that his rule was to be exercised with justice and discernment.

translation: He said, “As for whoever does wrong, we shall punish him; then he will be returned to his Lord, and He will punish him with a dreadful punishment.”
interpretation: Dhul-Qarnayn recognizes both the limits and responsibilities of his earthly authority: wrongdoing may be punished in this life, but every person ultimately answers to God, whose judgment is final.

translation: As for whoever believes and does righteous deeds, he will have the finest reward, and we will give him easy instructions from our command.
interpretation: The verse presents just authority as both rewarding what is good and dealing with people gently: faith and righteous action are met with a good reward, while guidance is given without needless hardship.

translation: Then he followed a course.
interpretation: The phrase emphasizes that purposeful resolve is accompanied by taking practical means and continuing toward one’s goal.

translation: Until, when he reached the place where the sun rises, he found it rising upon a people for whom We had provided no shelter from it.
interpretation: The verse portrays a people living with no protection from the sun, highlighting the striking diversity of human circumstances encountered in Dhul-Qarnayn’s journey.

translation: Thus it was, and We had full knowledge of all that was with him.
interpretation: The verse affirms that nothing about his affairs was hidden from God: his actions, circumstances, and the power entrusted to him were all known to Him.

translation: Then he followed a way.
interpretation: The phrase conveys that Dhul-Qarnayn pursued the means and course of action available to him, taking practical steps toward his purpose.

translation: When he reached the space between the two barriers, he found nearby a people who could scarcely understand speech.
interpretation: The verse portrays a people separated by a serious barrier of communication, reminding us that understanding others may require patience and effort, not merely power or authority.

translation: They said, “O Dhul-Qarnayn, Gog and Magog are causing corruption in the land. Shall we pay you a tribute on the condition that you build a barrier between us and them?”
interpretation: The people appeal to Dhul-Qarnayn for protection from a destructive threat and offer payment for his help. Their request presents leadership as a trust: power and resources can be used to safeguard a vulnerable community and restrain harm.

translation: He said, “What my Lord has granted me is better. So help me with your strength, and I will build a barrier between you and them.”
interpretation: He refuses their offer of payment, relying instead on what God has given him, and asks them to contribute their labor and strength to build a barrier against the threat.

translation: “Bring me blocks of iron.” Then, when he had filled the space between the two mountain sides, he said, “Blow!” When he had made it glow like fire, he said, “Bring me molten copper to pour over it.”
interpretation: The passage portrays Dhul-Qarnayn using practical skill and coordinated effort to build a strong barrier: he has iron fitted into the gap, heated by blowing, and sealed with molten copper. His command of resources serves the protection of the people, while the work itself is carried out through their participation.

translation: So they could neither climb over it nor make a breach in it.
interpretation: The barrier was made so formidable that the people it was meant to restrain could not overcome it by either climbing over or breaking through it.

translation: He said, “This is a mercy from my Lord. But when my Lord’s promise comes, He will level it to the ground; and my Lord’s promise is true.”
interpretation: The barrier’s strength is not independent of God: it stands by His mercy and will be brought down when His appointed promise arrives. The verse thus presents even the greatest human work as temporary before God’s certain decree.

translation: And We will leave them that Day surging over one another; then the Trumpet will be blown, and We will gather them all together.
interpretation: The verse depicts the overwhelming disorder of that Day: people will surge together in immense numbers, with no refuge from the upheaval. The blowing of the Trumpet then marks their gathering before God for judgment, where all will be brought together without exception.

translation: And We will present Hell on that Day before the disbelievers, fully exposed.
interpretation: The verse portrays the disbelievers facing the reality of their fate with no veil or denial left to shield them; what they rejected will be made unmistakably present before them.

translation: Those whose eyes were veiled from My remembrance, and who were unable to hear.
interpretation: This describes a profound spiritual heedlessness: they had turned away from God’s reminders so completely that they could neither recognize the truth before them nor respond to it.

translation: Do those who disbelieve suppose that they can take My servants as protectors besides Me? Indeed, We have prepared Hell as a lodging for the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse challenges the false security of relying on created beings in place of God: no chosen protector can shield someone from accountability or make disobedience safe. Its warning calls people to place their ultimate trust and devotion in God alone.

translation: Say, “Shall We inform you of those who are greatest losers in their deeds?”
interpretation: The verse warns that sincere effort alone does not guarantee success: deeds can be rendered fruitless when they are built on misguidance, even if their doers believe they are doing good.

translation: Those whose efforts are misguided in the life of this world, while they think they are doing good.
interpretation: The verse warns that confidence in one’s own goodness is not proof that one’s actions are truly right; deeds must be judged by God’s guidance, not merely by the doer’s intentions or self-assessment.

translation: Those are the ones who disbelieved in the signs of their Lord and in meeting Him, so their deeds came to nothing; and on the Day of Resurrection We will assign them no weight.
interpretation: The verse presents faith in God and accountability before Him as the foundation that gives deeds their lasting worth: outwardly impressive actions cannot secure standing with God when that foundation is rejected.

translation: That is their recompense: Hell, because they disbelieved and made a mockery of My signs and My messengers.
interpretation: The verse warns that persistently rejecting divine truth and treating its guidance and messengers with contempt is a grave moral choice for which people are held accountable.

translation: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds will have the Gardens of Paradise as their welcome.
interpretation: Calling Paradise their “welcome” portrays it as an honored reception prepared for them: their faith, expressed through good deeds, is met with lasting and generous hospitality from God.

translation: They will abide therein, never wishing to leave it for any other place.
interpretation: The verse portrays Paradise as a lasting, wholly satisfying home, so its inhabitants have no desire to depart or exchange it for anything else.

translation: Say, “If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would surely run dry before the words of my Lord ran out—even if We brought another sea like it to replenish it.”
interpretation: The image teaches that God’s knowledge, wisdom, and decrees are beyond all measure: even the vastest created resources could not encompass them. It invites humility before the limits of human understanding and recognition of the boundlessness of God’s words.

translation: Say, “I am only a human being like you. It is revealed to me that your God is one God. So whoever hopes to meet his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and associate no one in the worship of his Lord.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that sincere hope of meeting God must shape both what a person does and whom they worship: righteous deeds are to be done for God alone, without giving any partner a share in worship.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Kaf, Ha, Ya, ‘Ayn, Sad.
interpretation: These are among the disconnected letters that open certain surahs. Their precise meaning is not known with certainty; they invite humility before the depth of divine revelation.

translation: A mention of your Lord’s mercy toward His servant Zechariah.
interpretation: The account that follows is presented as a sign of God’s compassionate care for Zechariah, showing that divine mercy reaches His devoted servants.

translation: When he called upon his Lord in a quiet prayer,
interpretation: The quietness of Zakariya’s prayer conveys humble intimacy with God: his plea was sincere and personal, offered with reverence rather than display.

translation: He said, “My Lord, my bones have grown frail, and my head has blazed with gray hair. Yet never, my Lord, have I been disappointed in calling upon You.”
interpretation: Zakariyya speaks with humility, acknowledging the weakness of old age while holding fast to his trust in God. His words express a hope grounded in a lifetime of turning to God and never finding that trust in vain.

translation: Indeed, I fear my relatives after me, and my wife has been barren, so grant me, from Yourself, an heir.
interpretation: Zakariya’s plea reflects his concern that, after his death, those who would inherit his responsibility might not preserve his religious mission. Though the circumstances seemed to make an heir unlikely, he turns to God, asking for a successor as a gift from Him.

translation: Who will inherit from me and inherit from the family of Jacob; and make him, my Lord, pleasing to You.
interpretation: Zakariya asks God for a successor who will carry on the faithful legacy of his family and be devoted to what pleases God.

translation: “O Zechariah, We give you good news of a boy whose name will be John. We have not given this name to anyone before him.”
interpretation: The announcement emphasizes the child’s singular distinction: God Himself names him, marking his birth and life as a special sign of divine favor.

translation: He said, “My Lord, how can I have a son when my wife is barren and I have reached extreme old age?”
interpretation: Zechariah expresses wonder at the extraordinary promise, since both his wife’s barrenness and his advanced age made having a child seem impossible by ordinary means.

translation: He said, “So it will be. Your Lord says, ‘That is easy for Me, for I created you before, when you were nothing.’”
interpretation: Zakariya’s extraordinary circumstances do not limit what can happen: the One who brought him into existence from nothing can grant him a child with ease. The verse reassures that divine power is not constrained by the causes people ordinarily regard as necessary.

translation: He said, “My Lord, appoint for me a sign.” He said, “Your sign is that you will not speak to people for three nights, while being sound and well.”
interpretation: Zakariya asks for a sign confirming the glad tidings he has received. His inability to speak for three nights—despite being otherwise well—is appointed as that sign, and a reminder that what God promises comes to pass by His command.

translation: Then he came out to his people from the prayer chamber and signaled to them, “Glorify God morning and evening.”
interpretation: Though unable to address them in words, he guided his people to keep God’s remembrance at the beginning and end of each day.

translation: “O John, hold firmly to the Scripture.” And We granted him wisdom while he was still a boy.
interpretation: The command calls Yahya to embrace and uphold divine guidance with resolve and devotion. His being granted wisdom in childhood shows that sound judgment and spiritual maturity are gifts from God, not qualities limited by age.

translation: And [We gave him] tenderness from Us and purity, and he was God-conscious.
interpretation: His tenderness and purity are portrayed as gifts granted by God, showing that spiritual virtue is not merely innate disposition but a grace that shapes a person into devoted obedience.

translation: He was devoted to his parents, and was neither arrogant nor disobedient.
interpretation: The verse portrays a character marked by humility and faithful care: he treated his parents with kindness and did not let authority or strength become prideful defiance.

translation: And peace be upon him on the day he was born, the day he dies, and the day he is raised to life.
interpretation: The verse presents God’s peace as encompassing the most vulnerable thresholds of Yahya’s existence—his entrance into life, his death, and his resurrection—affirming his honored place and divine care in this world and the Hereafter.

translation: And mention in the Book Mary, when she withdrew from her family to a place toward the east.
interpretation: Mary’s withdrawal suggests a deliberate search for solitude and devotion, setting the scene for a profound encounter in which her faith would be tested.

translation: So she secluded herself from them behind a screen, and We sent to her Our Spirit, who appeared to her as a well-formed human being.
interpretation: Maryam withdrew into privacy, and God sent Gabriel to her in human form so that he could deliver the message entrusted to him.

translation: She said, “I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you are God-fearing.”
interpretation: Her appeal invokes God’s protection and confronts the stranger with his moral responsibility: true reverence for God should keep him from harming her.

translation: He said, “I am only a messenger of your Lord, [sent] to grant you a pure son.”
interpretation: The messenger explains that this extraordinary announcement comes by God’s command: Maryam is to be given a son distinguished by purity, while the messenger is only the bearer of that divine gift.

translation: She said, “How can I have a boy when no man has touched me, and I have not been unchaste?”
interpretation: Her words express astonishment at a birth that seems impossible by ordinary means, while affirming her chastity; the verse points to God’s power to bring about what lies beyond human expectations.

translation: He said, “So it will be. Your Lord says: ‘That is easy for Me. We will make him a sign for people and a mercy from Us. It is a matter already decreed.’”
interpretation: The miraculous birth is presented as a sign of God’s power: what lies beyond ordinary human means is effortless for Him. It also carries mercy and purpose, unfolding according to a decree already established by God.

translation: So she conceived him and withdrew with him to a distant place.
interpretation: Maryam’s withdrawal conveys her separation from the people around her as she faced the burden of her extraordinary situation in solitude.

translation: Then the pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a palm tree. She said, “If only I had died before this and become something forgotten, utterly forgotten.”
interpretation: Mary’s words express the depth of her anguish and fear in a moment of overwhelming physical and emotional suffering, revealing her human vulnerability as she faces an ordeal she feels unable to bear.

translation: Then he called to her from beneath her: “Do not grieve; your Lord has placed a stream beneath you.”
interpretation: The words reassure Mary in her distress: God has not abandoned her, but has provided immediate comfort and sustenance for her. The stream is a sign of His care at a moment when she feels alone and overwhelmed.

translation: And shake toward yourself the trunk of the palm tree; it will drop fresh, ripe dates upon you.
interpretation: The verse teaches that trusting in God does not mean remaining passive: Mary is told to make an effort, while the provision that follows is ultimately granted by God.

translation: So eat, drink, and be comforted. If you see anyone, say, ‘I have vowed a fast to the Most Merciful, so today I will speak to no one.’
interpretation: Mary is reassured and directed to take comfort in the provision God has given her. Her vow of silence is a sign that she is to leave the coming explanation of her situation to God, rather than defend herself to others.

translation: Then she brought him to her people, carrying him. They said, “Mary, you have done something truly astonishing.”
interpretation: Their words express shock and condemnation: seeing Mary return with a child, they assume the worst rather than knowing the truth, and confront her with a grave accusation.

translation: “O sister of Aaron, your father was not an evil man, nor was your mother unchaste.”
interpretation: They invoke Mary’s family as a rebuke, suggesting that her conduct seems at odds with the good character of her parents. “Sister of Aaron” is understood as an expression linking her to a righteous family or community, rather than necessarily identifying Aaron as her literal brother.

translation: So she pointed to him. They said, “How can we speak to one who is a child in the cradle?”
interpretation: Their question expresses astonishment: they assume an infant cannot speak, while Mary’s gesture directs them to the child as the answer to their accusation and the means by which God’s sign will become clear.

translation: He said, “Indeed, I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet.”
interpretation: By identifying himself first as Allah’s servant, Jesus affirms that his honored status and mission come from Allah; they do not make him divine. His prophethood and Scripture are gifts entrusted to him by Allah.

translation: And He has made me a blessing wherever I may be, and He has enjoined upon me prayer and almsgiving for as long as I live.
interpretation: True blessing is not confined to a place or circumstance: it is a life through which goodness reaches others. Prayer and almsgiving give that goodness its direction—devotion to God and care for people—and remain commitments throughout life.

translation: And [He made me] dutiful to my mother, and He did not make me arrogant or wretched.
interpretation: Jesus describes a life shaped by God’s grace: honoring his mother and remaining free of the pride and rebelliousness that bring misery.

translation: And peace is upon me the day I was born, the day I die, and the day I am raised alive.
interpretation: Jesus declares that God’s peace and protection accompany him through the three great transitions of human life—birth, death, and resurrection—affirming both his human mortality and his being raised to life by God.

translation: That is Jesus, son of Mary—the true account about whom they dispute.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the account given of Jesus is the truth, correcting the conflicting claims people make about him.

translation: It is not for Allah to take a son. Glory be to Him! When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, “Be,” and it is.
interpretation: The verse affirms that Allah is utterly beyond having offspring or needing a successor. His will alone brings anything into existence, without effort, delay, or dependence on another.

translation: Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path.
interpretation: True devotion is directed to Allah alone, who is Lord of all; worshipping Him is the clear and upright way to follow.

translation: The factions differed among themselves; so woe to those who disbelieve when they witness a tremendous Day.
interpretation: The verse warns that disputes over the truth do not make people answerable any less: on the Day of Judgment, the reality they rejected will be unmistakable, and those who persisted in disbelief will face its consequence.

translation: How well they will hear and see on the Day they come to Us! But today the wrongdoers are in clear error.
interpretation: The verse contrasts the clarity people will have when they stand before God with their heedlessness in this life: then the truth will be impossible to miss, but recognizing it only after the time for choosing has passed will not undo their present rejection.

translation: And warn them of the Day of Regret, when the matter will have been decided, while they remain heedless and do not believe.
interpretation: The verse warns that those who turn away from faith will face a moment when judgment is settled and the chance to respond has passed; their present heedlessness will then give way to regret.

translation: Indeed, We will inherit the earth and all who are upon it, and to Us they will be returned.
interpretation: “Inherit” signifies that all worldly possession and authority are temporary: when creation passes away, God alone remains as its ultimate owner, and every person returns to Him for judgment.

translation: And mention in the Book Abraham. Indeed, he was a man of great truthfulness, a prophet.
interpretation: Abraham’s enduring example rests on the unity of sincere truthfulness and divine guidance: his unwavering honesty made him worthy of trust, while his prophethood entrusted him with conveying God’s message.

translation: When he said to his father, “O my father, why do you worship what neither hears nor sees, and cannot help you in any way?”
interpretation: Abraham appeals to his father with tenderness and reason: worship is due to the One who truly hears, sees, and can benefit or protect, not to something powerless to respond or help.

translation: My father, knowledge has come to me that has not come to you, so follow me; I will guide you to a straight path.
interpretation: Abraham speaks to his father with tenderness while making clear that the guidance he has received is a gift from God. His invitation is not a claim of personal superiority, but a plea to follow the truth that leads to a sound and upright way of life.

translation: “O my father, do not worship Satan. Indeed, Satan has always been disobedient to the Most Merciful.”
interpretation: Worshipping Satan includes following his promptings into idolatry and disobedience. The verse presents a gentle warning: turning away from God’s guidance is alignment with one who rebels against the Most Merciful.

translation: O my father, I fear that a punishment from the Most Merciful may touch you, and that you may become an ally of Satan.
interpretation: Abraham speaks to his father with tenderness and concern, warning that rejecting God may lead him into punishment and allegiance to Satan. By calling God “the Most Merciful,” he emphasizes that this warning comes from care and hope for his father’s guidance, not hostility.

translation: He said, “Do you turn away from my gods, O Abraham? If you do not stop, I will surely stone you. So leave me alone for a long while.”
interpretation: The response shows how deeply attachment to inherited worship can harden into hostility toward sincere counsel: instead of answering Abraham’s reasoning, the speaker resorts to a threat and demands separation. The verse thus marks the painful cost of remaining faithful while facing rejection from someone close.

translation: He said, “Peace be upon you. I will ask my Lord to forgive you; indeed, He has always been gracious to me.”
interpretation: Ibrahim responds to his father’s rejection with gentleness rather than hostility, while entrusting the matter of forgiveness to God. His confidence rests on God’s kindness and care toward him.

translation: “I will withdraw from you and from what you invoke besides Allah, and I will call upon my Lord. I hope that, in calling upon my Lord, I will not be disappointed.”
interpretation: The verse joins firm commitment to worshipping Allah alone with humility: separation from false worship is accompanied not by self-reliance, but by hopeful dependence on one’s Lord.

translation: When he had withdrawn from them and from what they worshipped besides Allah, We bestowed upon him Isaac and Jacob, and We made each of them a prophet.
interpretation: The verse shows that sincere devotion to Allah may require separation from false worship, and that Allah can reward such steadfastness with blessings that carry forward faith and guidance through generations.

translation: And We bestowed upon them of Our mercy and granted them an exalted reputation for truth.
interpretation: God’s mercy includes not only guidance and blessing in their lives but also an enduring, honorable legacy: people remember them with truthful praise and regard their example with esteem.

translation: And mention Moses in the Book. Indeed, he was devoted to God, and he was a messenger and a prophet.
interpretation: Moses is presented as a model of wholehearted devotion to God, whose prophetic mission was entrusted to him by divine choice.

translation: And We called to him from the right side of the Mount and drew him near for a private conversation.
interpretation: This describes God honoring Moses with direct, intimate communication, granting him a closeness of address and revelation rather than implying physical nearness.

translation: And We bestowed upon him, out of Our mercy, his brother Aaron as a prophet.
interpretation: Aaron’s prophethood was a gift of divine mercy to Moses, granting him a trusted brother and fellow messenger in his mission.

translation: And mention Ishmael in the Book. He was indeed true to his promise, and he was a messenger and a prophet.
interpretation: Ishmael’s honored mention shows that steadfast honesty is a mark of prophetic character: his faithfulness in keeping promises reflected the trustworthiness of his calling.

translation: He would instruct his family to pray and give alms, and he was pleasing to his Lord.
interpretation: The verse shows that devotion to God extends beyond one’s own worship: a person should also lovingly guide their family toward prayer and generosity. Such steady obedience is a source of God’s approval.

translation: And mention Idris in the Book. Indeed, he was a man of truth and a prophet.
interpretation: Idris is presented as an example of how steadfast truthfulness marks a person worthy of divine honor; his prophetic rank is a gift from God, not merely a worldly distinction.

translation: And We raised him to a high station.
interpretation: This expresses the honor God bestowed upon Idrīs, elevating him to a distinguished rank through his faithfulness and obedience.

translation: Those are the ones whom Allah blessed among the prophets: from the descendants of Adam, from those We carried with Noah, from the descendants of Abraham and Israel, and from among those We guided and chose. When the verses of the Most Merciful were recited to them, they fell down in prostration, weeping.
interpretation: Their honored status is shown not merely by their lineage, but by hearts transformed through divine guidance: when they heard their Lord’s words, they responded with humble surrender and sincere awe.

translation: Then successors came after them who neglected the prayer and pursued their desires, so they will encounter ruin.
interpretation: The verse warns that when a community lets devotion to God fall away and makes its desires the measure of its choices, it abandons the guidance that safeguards it and moves toward a grievous end. The warning calls people back to prayer and to governing their desires rather than being governed by them.

translation: Except those who repent, believe, and do righteous deeds—those will enter Paradise, and they will not be wronged in the least.
interpretation: The verse holds open the way back to God: sincere repentance, faith, and righteous action can transform a person’s course. God’s judgment is perfectly just, so those who return to Him will receive their due without any loss or unfairness.

translation: Gardens of everlasting abode, which the Most Merciful has promised His servants though they have not seen them. Surely, His promise is destined to be fulfilled.
interpretation: The verse presents faith in Paradise as trust in a promise whose reality is not yet visible: its certainty rests not on human sight, but on the faithfulness of the Most Merciful, whose promise will indeed come to pass.

translation: They will hear no idle talk there, but only words of peace; and they will have their provision there morning and evening.
interpretation: The verse presents Paradise as a place of complete serenity: speech is free of anything harmful or pointless, and its inhabitants enjoy provision continually, expressed in the familiar rhythm of morning and evening.

translation: That is the Garden which We shall give as an inheritance to whoever among Our servants is mindful of God.
interpretation: Describing the Garden as an inheritance emphasizes that its enduring possession is a gift from God, granted to those whose reverence for Him shapes how they live.

translation: We do not descend except by the command of your Lord. To Him belongs all that is before us, all that is behind us, and all that is between; and your Lord is never forgetful.
interpretation: The delay in revelation is not a sign of neglect or abandonment: the angels act only by God’s command, and all times and circumstances are under His authority. His timing reflects His wisdom, and He does not forget what His servants need.

translation: The Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them—so worship Him and persevere in His worship. Do you know of anyone comparable to Him?
interpretation: Because God alone sustains all creation and has no equal, worship belongs to Him alone; the command to persevere calls for steadfast devotion even when it is difficult.

translation: And man says, “When I have died, will I really be brought forth alive?”
interpretation: The verse portrays a person questioning the reality of resurrection after death, treating it as implausible despite the power of God to bring life into being.

translation: Does the human being not remember that We created him before, when he was nothing?
interpretation: The verse calls attention to the first creation as evidence that resurrection is possible: the One who brought a person into existence when they were nothing can surely restore them after death.

translation: By your Lord, We will surely gather them and the devils, then We will bring them around Hell, kneeling.
interpretation: The emphatic oath underscores the certainty of resurrection and judgment: those who rejected the truth will be brought with the devils before Hell, humbled and unable to escape accountability.

translation: Then We will surely single out from every faction whichever of them was most insolent toward the Most Compassionate.
interpretation: The verse portrays the judgment of the Hereafter: among those who followed each faction, God will bring forward those most stubbornly defiant toward Him, exposing the extremity of their rebellion for judgment.

translation: Then We surely know best who is most deserving of burning in it.
interpretation: God’s judgment is based on perfect knowledge: He knows who is truly most deserving of the Fire, so no one is condemned unjustly.

translation: There is none among you who will not come to it; this is a decree your Lord has made inevitable.
interpretation: All people will be brought to the Fire’s approach as part of the final judgment. The following verse clarifies that God will rescue those who were mindful of Him, while the wrongdoers will be left there—making this an encounter that reveals the outcome of each person’s life and God’s justice.

translation: Then We will save those who were mindful of God, and leave the wrongdoers there, kneeling.
interpretation: The verse contrasts the fate of the God-conscious with that of those who persisted in wrongdoing: God will deliver the former, while the latter remain in the Fire, humbled and unable to escape.

translation: When Our clear verses are recited to them, those who disbelieve say to those who believe, “Which of the two groups is better in standing and more impressive in gathering?”
interpretation: The disbelievers use their worldly status and prominent gatherings to claim that they are superior to the believers. The verse exposes the flaw in measuring truth by wealth, influence, or social standing: such appearances do not establish whose path is right or whose ultimate outcome is better.

translation: How many generations We destroyed before them, who were finer in furnishings and more impressive in appearance!
interpretation: Material comfort and outward splendor are no proof of true worth or divine favor; they cannot protect a people from the consequences of rejecting God.

translation: Say, “Whoever is in error, let the Most Merciful grant him respite—until, when they see what they were promised, whether punishment or the Hour, they will know who is worse in standing and weaker in forces.”
interpretation: The delay granted to those who persist in error is not a sign of divine approval or lasting success. When the promised judgment arrives, their apparent advantage will give way to the truth of their standing and their powerlessness.

translation: And Allah increases those who are guided in guidance. The enduring good deeds are better with your Lord in reward and better in their final outcome.
interpretation: Those who respond sincerely to guidance are granted greater clarity and steadfastness, while lasting acts of righteousness have a worth that worldly gains cannot match, bringing a better reward and ultimate end with God.

translation: Have you seen the one who disbelieved in Our signs and said, “I will surely be given wealth and children”?
interpretation: The verse exposes the arrogance of someone who rejects God’s signs yet confidently assumes he will be favored with worldly abundance— even in the Hereafter—without faith or grounds for such certainty.

translation: Has he looked into the Unseen, or taken a covenant with the Most Merciful?
interpretation: The question challenges the person’s unwarranted certainty: he has no knowledge of what lies beyond human sight and no divine promise guaranteeing what he claims.

translation: No indeed! We shall record what he says and extend the punishment for him at length.
interpretation: The verse rejects his presumptuous words and warns that they are not forgotten: he will be held accountable for them, and his punishment will be prolonged.

translation: And We will inherit from him what he speaks of, and he will come to Us alone.
interpretation: Whatever wealth or status he boasts of will pass away, while he will stand before God alone, without the possessions or support he claimed as his own.

translation: They have taken gods besides Allah, hoping they would be a source of honor and strength for them.
interpretation: The verse exposes the futility of seeking security or status through worship of anything besides God: what people imagine will protect and exalt them has no power to do so. True honor and refuge belong to God alone.

translation: No! They will reject their worship of them and will become their adversaries.
interpretation: Those whom people worship besides God will not come to their aid on the Day of Judgment. Instead, they will disown that worship and stand against their worshippers.

translation: Do you not see that We have set the devils upon the disbelievers, goading them on relentlessly?
interpretation: The verse portrays persistent wrongdoing as being fueled by satanic prompting: the devils intensify the disbelievers’ impulses and draw them further into defiance. This incitement does not remove their responsibility; it exposes the path they have chosen and the forces they have allowed to influence them.

translation: So do not hasten against them; We are only counting out their days for them.
interpretation: God reassures the Prophet not to seek the hastening of the disbelievers’ reckoning: their respite is limited, and every moment brings them closer to the appointed judgment.

translation: The day We gather the God-conscious to the Most Merciful as an honored delegation.
interpretation: The image of a delegation suggests welcome and honor: those who lived with reverence for God are brought near to Him as cherished guests, not merely assembled for judgment.

translation: And We will drive the guilty to Hell, thirsty.
interpretation: Their being driven there thirsty conveys their utter humiliation and distress: they arrive in desperate need, with no relief from the punishment awaiting them.

translation: They will have no power to intercede, except those who have made a covenant with the Most Merciful.
interpretation: Intercession is not something anyone can claim or exercise independently; it belongs only within the covenant God grants. The verse therefore directs hope toward faithfulness to God, rather than reliance on an intercessor apart from Him.

translation: And they say, “The Most Compassionate has taken a son.”
interpretation: The verse condemns attributing offspring to God: He is wholly independent and unlike His creation, so having a son is incompatible with His divine nature.

translation: You have indeed uttered something monstrous.
interpretation: This is a grave rebuke of attributing a child to God: such a claim is profoundly incompatible with His absolute oneness and transcendence.

translation: The heavens nearly split apart because of it, the earth cleaves open, and the mountains collapse in ruin.
interpretation: The verse portrays, in striking cosmic imagery, the enormity of claiming that God has a child: such a claim is utterly incompatible with His oneness and majesty.

translation: Because they ascribed a son to the Most Merciful.
interpretation: The phrase conveys the gravity of claiming that God has offspring: such a claim is utterly incompatible with His absolute oneness and majesty.

translation: It is not befitting the Most Merciful to take a son.
interpretation: The verse affirms that God is exalted above human relationships and needs; divine sonship does not apply to Him.

translation: There is none in the heavens and the earth who will not come to the Most Compassionate as a servant.
interpretation: Every created being belongs to God and is subject to Him; no one can claim independence from Him, and all will ultimately stand before Him in the reality of their servitude.

translation: He has encompassed them and counted them precisely.
interpretation: Nothing about them is hidden from God: He knows every one of them completely and has counted them without omission.

translation: And each of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone.
interpretation: Every person will stand before God individually, without relying on wealth, family, or allies; each will answer for their own deeds.

translation: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds—the Most Merciful will grant them affection.
interpretation: God promises that sincere faith and good deeds will be met with His favor, and that He will place love and acceptance for such people in the hearts of others.

translation: So We have made it easy in your tongue, so that you may bring good news through it to the God-conscious and warn through it a fiercely disputatious people.
interpretation: The Qur’an’s clarity in the Prophet’s own language makes its guidance accessible: it offers hope to those mindful of God, while confronting those whose stubborn disputes keep them from accepting the truth.

translation: And how many generations before them We have destroyed! Can you perceive even one of them, or hear from them the faintest sound?
interpretation: The verse turns the silence left by vanished peoples into a warning: worldly strength and denial cannot shield a people from God’s judgment, and those who disregard the warning should not mistake their present power for lasting security.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Ta-Ha.
interpretation: “Ta-Ha” is one of the Qur’an’s disjointed-letter openings. Its precise intended meaning is known to Allah; its placement invites the listener to attend to the revelation that follows.

translation: We have not sent down the Qur’an to you to cause you distress.
interpretation: The verse reassures the Prophet that the Qur’an is not meant to burden him with hardship; its guidance is a mercy, not a source of misery.

translation: But only as a reminder for those who are mindful of God.
interpretation: The reminder reaches its purpose in a heart willing to take God’s guidance seriously; reverent awareness makes a person receptive to its counsel.

translation: A revelation from Him who created the earth and the lofty heavens.
interpretation: The Qur’an is presented as a message from the Creator of all things, affirming that its source is divine rather than human.

translation: The Most Merciful rose over the Throne.
interpretation: The verse affirms God’s supreme sovereignty over all creation, in a manner befitting Him and unlike anything in creation; its precise nature is beyond human knowledge.

translation: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens, whatever is on the earth, whatever is between them, and whatever lies beneath the soil.
interpretation: God’s sovereignty extends over all existence, including what is hidden beyond human sight; nothing lies outside His ownership or authority.

translation: Whether you speak aloud, He knows what is secret and what is even more hidden.
interpretation: Nothing is concealed from God—not only what a person keeps secret, but even the unspoken thoughts and intentions hidden within the heart. His knowledge is complete whether or not anything is voiced.

translation: Allah—there is no god but Him. To Him belong the Most Beautiful Names.
interpretation: The verse directs worship and supplication exclusively to Allah, whose names express the perfection of His attributes. Knowing these names deepens recognition of His greatness and shapes how believers call upon and trust Him.

translation: Has the story of Moses come to you?
interpretation: This rhetorical question invites the listener to attend closely to Moses’ story, preparing them to reflect on how God guides and supports His messengers through hardship.

translation: When he saw a fire, he said to his family, “Stay here. I have caught sight of a fire; perhaps I can bring you a burning brand from it, or find someone at the fire to guide us.”
interpretation: The verse presents Moses responding to uncertainty with practical hope: he seeks both light to meet an immediate need and guidance for the way ahead. It also shows how an ordinary search for help becomes the setting for a profound divine encounter.

translation: When he came to it, he was called: “O Moses!”
interpretation: The verse marks the moment Moses is summoned into a direct encounter with God: his journey to the fire becomes the beginning of his prophetic mission.

translation: Indeed, I am your Lord, so remove your sandals. You are in the sacred valley of Ṭuwā.
interpretation: God’s command to Moses to remove his sandals marks the holiness of the place and calls him to approach this divine encounter with reverence.

translation: And I have chosen you, so listen to what is being revealed.
