interpretation: God is addressing Moses, affirming that his calling is by divine choice and urging him to receive the revelation with full attention and readiness to carry out what it requires.

translation: Indeed, I am Allah; there is no deity except Me. So worship Me and establish prayer to remember Me.
interpretation: Because God alone is worthy of worship, devotion belongs to Him alone. Prayer is established as a means of keeping His remembrance present in one’s life and turning the heart back toward Him.

translation: Indeed, the Hour is coming. I have kept its time nearly hidden, so that every soul may be recompensed for what it strives for.
interpretation: The Hour’s arrival is certain, but its timing is concealed from people. That concealment directs them to live responsibly at all times, knowing that each person will be judged for their deeds and efforts.

translation: So do not let anyone who does not believe in it and follows his own desires turn you away from it, lest you perish.
interpretation: Remain steadfast in belief in the Hour and in preparing for it; do not let the disbelief or desires of others divert you from the truth, for that diversion leads to ruin.

translation: “And what is that in your right hand, O Moses?”
interpretation: God’s question draws Moses’ attention to the staff he carries, preparing him for the sign that will reveal its miraculous transformation.

translation: He said, “It is my staff. I lean on it, use it to shake leaves down for my sheep, and have other uses for it.”
interpretation: Moses answers with the familiar, practical uses of his staff, reflecting the ordinary details of his life as a shepherd. The exchange gives the moment a personal, conversational quality before the staff is shown to have a miraculous role.

translation: He said, “Throw it down, Moses.”
interpretation: The command begins the demonstration of the staff’s miraculous transformation, preparing Moses to witness a sign of God’s power.

translation: So he cast it down, and behold, it was a serpent moving swiftly.
interpretation: The staff’s sudden transformation is a manifest sign of God’s power, strengthening Moses for the mission entrusted to him.

translation: He said, “Take it, and do not fear. We will restore it to its former state.”
interpretation: God reassures Moses that what appeared frightening is fully under His control: he can take hold of it without fear, trusting that God will return it to the familiar form he knows.

translation: And draw your hand close to your side; it will come out white, without harm—another sign.
interpretation: The hand’s uninjured whiteness is a miraculous sign granted to Moses, confirming that his mission is supported by God.

translation: So that We may show you some of Our greatest signs.
interpretation: God is telling Moses that the signs he will witness are meant to reveal the truth of his mission and the power behind it; they are among God’s greatest signs, though not the limit of His signs.

translation: Go to Pharaoh; indeed, he has transgressed.
interpretation: Moses is being sent to confront Pharaoh because he has exceeded all bounds in arrogance and oppression; the command underscores the duty to call even a powerful tyrant back to what is right.

translation: He said, “My Lord, open my heart for me.”
interpretation: This is a prayer for inner spaciousness: relief from anxiety and the strength, clarity, and steadiness needed to fulfill a difficult responsibility.

translation: And make my task easy for me.
interpretation: Moses asks God to ease the burdens and obstacles of his mission, showing that success depends on seeking God’s help.

translation: And loosen the knot from my tongue,
interpretation: Moses asks God to remove the difficulty in his speech so that he can express himself clearly and be understood.

translation: That they may understand my speech.
interpretation: This expresses a wish for clear communication: that the speaker’s words be understood as intended, without confusion or impediment.

translation: And appoint for me a minister from my family,
interpretation: Moses is asking for a trusted relative to share the burden of his mission and strengthen him in carrying it out.

translation: Aaron, my brother.
interpretation: Moses names Aaron as the close and trusted brother he seeks as a companion in carrying out his mission.

translation: Strengthen me through him.
interpretation: Moses asks that Aaron’s support reinforce his ability to bear the responsibility of his mission.

translation: And make him share in my task.
interpretation: Moses is asking God to appoint Aaron as a partner in his mission, so they can bear its responsibilities and carry it out together.

translation: So that we may glorify You abundantly.
interpretation: The phrase expresses the desire to devote oneself more fully to declaring God’s perfection and engaging in His remembrance.

translation: And remember You often.
interpretation: Moses and Aaron ask for help in keeping Allah constantly in mind, showing that remembrance of Him is a source of strength and steadiness in carrying out their mission.

translation: Indeed, You have always been fully aware of us.
interpretation: The words express trust in God’s complete knowledge of their circumstances and needs: nothing about them is hidden from Him.

translation: He said, “Your request has been granted, Moses.”
interpretation: This assurance shows that God had heard Moses’ plea and would support him in the mission ahead, granting what he had asked for.

translation: And indeed, We had already shown you favor another time.
interpretation: Allah reminds Moses that divine care had been with him before, inviting him to trust that the protection and guidance he needed would continue.

translation: When We inspired your mother with what was to be inspired,
interpretation: This recalls God’s special care for Moses from the beginning: He guided his mother to protect him, showing that his preservation and mission were under divine providence.

translation: “Place him in the chest, then cast it into the river; let the river carry it to the shore, where an enemy of Mine and an enemy of his will take him. I bestowed upon you love from Me, so that you would be raised under My watchful care.”
interpretation: The verse portrays divine care working through events that seem perilous: Moses is carried toward danger, yet God’s protection and favor guide his upbringing. The love bestowed upon him marks him as beloved and watched over by God.

translation: When your sister went and said, “Shall I direct you to someone who will care for him?” We returned you to your mother so that she might be comforted and not grieve. You killed a person, and We saved you from distress; We tested you through many trials. Then you stayed for years among the people of Midian. Then you came at the appointed time, O Moses.
interpretation: The verse presents Moses’ life as guided preparation: even frightening events, separation, and years away were not signs of abandonment, but stages through which God protected and shaped him for the mission that awaited him.

translation: And I have chosen you for Myself.
interpretation: God is telling Moses that He specially selected and prepared him for His mission, granting him His care and support; the phrase expresses divine favor, not physical possession.

translation: Go, you and your brother with My signs, and do not grow weary of remembering Me.
interpretation: God instructs Moses and Aaron to carry out their mission with His signs while remaining steadfast in remembrance of Him. Their closeness to God is to sustain their courage and resolve in the face of the task ahead.

translation: Go, both of you, to Pharaoh; indeed, he has transgressed.
interpretation: The verse shows that when power exceeds its bounds, it must be confronted with the truth and a call back to what is right.

translation: Speak to him gently, so that perhaps he may take heed or become mindful of God.
interpretation: Even when addressing someone deeply resistant to the truth, begin with gentleness: the aim is to open a way to reflection and reverence, not to provoke or humiliate.

translation: They said, “Our Lord, we fear that he may act hastily against us or transgress.”
interpretation: Moses and Aaron express their fear that Pharaoh will react to their message with immediate violence or oppressive arrogance. Their words acknowledge the danger of confronting him and imply their need for God’s protection and support.

translation: He said, “Do not fear. I am with you both, hearing and seeing.”
interpretation: God’s reassurance means that Moses and Aaron were not alone before Pharaoh: God was fully aware of what they faced and would guide and support them. Their courage could rest on His presence, not on their own power.

translation: So go to him and say, ‘We are messengers from your Lord. Send the Children of Israel with us, and do not torment them. We have come to you with a sign from your Lord. Peace be upon whoever follows the guidance.’”
interpretation: The command presents the messengers’ appeal as both a demand for justice and an invitation to heed God’s guidance: Pharaoh is to stop oppressing the Children of Israel, while the sign makes clear that their mission is from God. The promise of peace is tied to following that guidance.

translation: Indeed, it has been revealed to us that punishment will be upon whoever denies the truth and turns away.
interpretation: The verse conveys that rejecting God’s message and deliberately turning away from it bring a grave consequence; it is a warning urging its hearers to accept the truth rather than persist in defiance.

translation: He said, “Who is your Lord, O Moses?”
interpretation: Pharaoh’s question challenges Moses to define the authority behind his message, reflecting Pharaoh’s refusal to acknowledge a Lord above himself.

translation: He said, “Our Lord is the One who gave each thing its form, then guided it.”
interpretation: The verse points to God’s wisdom and care: every creature is made with a nature suited to it and is guided toward the way of life intended for it.

translation: He said, “Then what became of the former generations?”
interpretation: Pharaoh invokes the fate of those who came before as a challenge to Moses’ message, implying that their ultimate destiny must be accounted for. The question shifts attention from the truth of Moses’ call to what lies beyond human knowledge—a matter Moses places in God’s keeping.

translation: He said, “Knowledge of them is with my Lord in a Record. My Lord neither errs nor forgets.”
interpretation: Moses directs the question about earlier generations to God, whose complete knowledge is preserved and never subject to error or omission.

translation: He is the One who made the earth a cradle for you, and laid out pathways for you upon it; and He sent down water from the sky, then by it We brought forth diverse kinds of plants.
interpretation: The verse draws attention to God’s care in making the earth a place where people can live and travel, and in bringing forth varied vegetation through rain. These provisions point to His power and mercy, and invite people to recognize the One who sustains them.

translation: Eat and pasture your livestock. Surely in that are signs for those endowed with reason.
interpretation: The provision of food for people and grazing for their livestock points to God’s wisdom and care. Those who reflect on these blessings can recognize the order and generosity behind them.

translation: From it We created you, into it We shall return you, and from it We shall bring you forth once again.
interpretation: The verse reminds people that their earthly origin and return to the earth do not mark the end of their existence. The One who first brought them into being has the power to raise them again, so human life is bound to accountability beyond death.

translation: And We certainly showed him all Our signs, but he denied them and refused.
interpretation: The verse portrays Pharaoh’s rejection as deliberate: despite being shown clear signs, he persisted in denial and refused to submit to the truth.

translation: He said, “Have you come to drive us out of our land by your magic, O Moses?”
interpretation: Pharaoh dismisses Moses’s message as sorcery and portrays it as a threat to their hold on the land, turning attention from its truth to fear of losing power.

translation: “Then we will surely bring you magic like it. So set a meeting between us and you that neither we nor you will fail to keep, at a place convenient to both.”
interpretation: The speaker challenges Moses to a public contest, proposing a time and place that both sides can readily attend, and expresses confidence that they can match what he has shown.

translation: He said, “Your appointed time is the day of the festival, and let the people be gathered in the forenoon.”
interpretation: Moses chose a public festival day and a time when people would be present, so the contest would be witnessed openly and the truth could be made clear to all.

translation: Then Pharaoh turned away, gathered his scheme, and came.
interpretation: The verse portrays Pharaoh’s response as calculated: he withdrew to organize a deliberate stratagem, showing that he treated the encounter with Moses as a contest of power and deception rather than seeking the truth.

translation: Moses said to them, “Woe to you! Do not fabricate lies about Allah, or He will utterly destroy you with punishment. Whoever invents lies has surely failed.”
interpretation: Moses warns that falsely attributing claims to Allah is not a harmless deception: it invites divine punishment and leads its perpetrator to ruin. His words urge them to abandon falsehood before its consequences overtake them.

translation: So they disputed among themselves about their affair and kept their private counsel secret.
interpretation: Their secret deliberation reflects their uncertainty and concern: rather than face Moses openly, they sought a strategy to preserve their position and influence.

translation: They said, “These two are indeed magicians who intend to drive you from your land by their magic and to put an end to your exemplary way.”
interpretation: The speakers portray Moses and Aaron as a threat to the people’s homeland and cherished way of life, using fear to turn the public against them and protect their own authority.

translation: So gather your stratagem, then come forward in formation; whoever gains the upper hand today will surely succeed.
interpretation: The call urges them to coordinate their efforts and face the contest together, expressing their confidence that victory will belong to whoever proves dominant.

translation: They said, “O Moses, either you cast, or we shall be the first to cast.”
interpretation: Their words frame the encounter as a contest and give Moses the choice of who will begin, reflecting their confidence that they are ready to proceed either way.

translation: He said, “No—you throw.” Then, by their magic, their ropes and staffs appeared to him as though they were moving swiftly.
interpretation: The verse depicts how their magic created a convincing illusion of movement, making the ropes and staffs seem alive to Moses without actually changing what they were.

translation: So Moses felt a fear within himself.
interpretation: Moses experienced a moment of human apprehension at the sight of the sorcerers’ display; this was not a loss of faith, but a natural fear of what might happen.

translation: We said, “Do not fear. Indeed, you will prevail.”
interpretation: God reassures Moses that he need not be intimidated by the magicians’ display: with God’s support, the truth he brings will overcome their deception.

translation: And throw what is in your right hand; it will swallow what they have made. What they have made is only a magician’s trick, and a magician does not succeed wherever he goes.
interpretation: The verse teaches that deception may appear powerful, but it cannot prevail against the truth God brings. Falsehood has no enduring success, however skillfully it is presented.

translation: Then the magicians fell down prostrate, saying, “We believe in the Lord of Aaron and Moses.”
interpretation: The magicians’ sudden prostration shows that, once the truth became clear to them, they surrendered sincerely to God without letting fear of Pharaoh’s power override their conviction.

translation: He said, “Have you believed him before I gave you permission? He must be your leader who taught you magic. I will surely cut off your hands and feet on opposite sides, then crucify you on the trunks of palm trees, and you will surely know which of us is more severe and enduring in punishment.”
interpretation: The ruler treats faith as an act requiring his approval and dismisses the believers’ conviction as a conspiracy, revealing how tyranny tries to protect its power by discrediting truth and threatening those who accept it.

translation: They said, “We will never choose you over the clear proofs that have come to us, nor over the One who created us. So decree whatever you will; you can decree only in this worldly life.”
interpretation: Their response expresses steadfast faith in the face of worldly threats: Pharaoh may wield power over their lives in this world, but that power cannot outweigh the truth they have recognized or reach beyond the limits God has set for him.

translation: Indeed, we have believed in our Lord, so that He may forgive us our sins and the magic you compelled us to perform. And Allah is better and more enduring.
interpretation: They affirm that faith in their Lord is their refuge from the ruler’s coercion and threats. They hope for forgiveness for both their sins and the magic they were forced to practice, declaring that Allah’s reward and lasting favor are better than any worldly power or punishment.

translation: Indeed, whoever comes to his Lord as a criminal will have Hell, where he neither dies nor lives.
interpretation: The verse portrays the criminal’s punishment as an unending state of misery: death does not bring release, and life there offers no true comfort or relief.

translation: Whoever comes to Him as a believer, having done righteous deeds—such people will have the highest ranks.
interpretation: The verse teaches that true honor with God is attained through faith expressed in righteous action; the highest standing in the Hereafter is a divine reward, not something secured by status in this world.

translation: Gardens of everlasting residence, beneath which rivers flow, where they will abide forever. That is the reward of whoever purifies himself.
interpretation: True purification is not merely outward cleanliness; it is the inward turning of the heart toward God, expressed through faith and righteous conduct. The verse presents lasting nearness and peace as the reward for such a life.

translation: And We revealed to Moses: “Set out by night with My servants, and make for them a dry path through the sea. You will not fear being overtaken, nor will you fear harm.”
interpretation: The command pairs a seemingly impossible escape with a promise of protection: Moses is to act on God’s direction without being paralyzed by the pursuing enemy or by the danger of the sea. The dry passage signifies deliverance made possible by God, not by human strength alone.

translation: Then Pharaoh pursued them with his armies, and the sea engulfed them in a way beyond description.
interpretation: The verse’s repeated, indefinite phrasing underscores the overwhelming scale of Pharaoh’s downfall: worldly power cannot protect those who defy God’s justice.

translation: And Pharaoh led his people astray and did not guide them.
interpretation: Pharaoh’s power did not make him a true guide: he used his influence to turn his people away from the truth, leading them toward ruin instead of guidance.

translation: O Children of Israel, We delivered you from your enemy, appointed for you a meeting on the right side of the Mount, and sent down to you manna and quails.
interpretation: The verse portrays God’s care for the Israelites as extending beyond their rescue: He also guided them toward revelation and provided for their needs, showing that deliverance carries both spiritual responsibility and divine sustenance.

translation: Eat of the good things We have provided for you, and do not transgress in them, lest My anger befall you. Whoever incurs My anger has surely fallen into ruin.
interpretation: God’s blessings are to be enjoyed with gratitude and restraint, not turned into means of disobedience or excess. The warning makes clear that rejecting these limits leads to spiritual ruin.

translation: And indeed, I am surely Most Forgiving to whoever repents, believes, does righteous deeds, and then remains guided.
interpretation: God’s forgiveness is open to those who turn back from wrongdoing with sincerity, affirm faith, and let that faith shape their actions. The closing phrase points to continuing on the path of guidance after repentance, rather than treating it as a momentary change.

translation: “And what has made you hurry ahead of your people, O Moses?”
interpretation: The question draws Moses’ attention to his haste and prepares him to explain why he came before his people, opening the way for what follows.

translation: He said, “They are close behind me, and I hastened to You, my Lord, so that You would be pleased.”
interpretation: Moses explains that his people are following him, while he hurried ahead in eagerness to answer God’s summons and seek His pleasure.

translation: He said, “We have indeed tested your people after you departed, and the Samiri has led them astray.”
interpretation: The verse shows that Moses’ absence became a test of his people’s faith: they were vulnerable to the Samiri’s misleading influence, revealing the need to remain steadfast in worship of God even when their prophet was not among them.

translation: So Moses returned to his people, angry and grieved. He said, “My people, did your Lord not make you a gracious promise? Has the time seemed too long to you, or did you wish for your Lord’s wrath to befall you, that you broke your promise to me?”
interpretation: Moses’ rebuke conveys both sorrow and urgency: his people had been given hope in God’s promise, yet during his absence they failed to keep their commitment to him. He challenges them to consider whether impatience or disregard for God’s warning led them to this breach.

translation: They said, “We did not break our appointment with you of our own accord; rather, we were burdened with ornaments from the people, so we threw them [into the fire]—and likewise did the Samiri.”
interpretation: They claimed that they had not deliberately disobeyed Moses: they had cast the ornaments into the fire, they said, and the Samiri had done the same. Their words offer an excuse for what happened, while pointing to the Samiri as the one who led the affair.

translation: Then he brought out for them a calf—a mere body that made a lowing sound. They said, “This is your god and the god of Moses, but he has forgotten.”
interpretation: The verse exposes the emptiness of the idol: although it had a visible form and made a sound, it was only an inanimate body, incapable of being divine. The people’s claim that Moses had “forgotten” was a false excuse for turning away from God.

translation: Do they not see that it cannot answer them, nor has power to harm or benefit them?
interpretation: The verse exposes the futility of worshipping an object that cannot even respond to its worshippers, let alone control what benefits or harms them. True divinity belongs to God alone, who hears, answers, and has power over all things.

translation: And Aaron had already said to them before, “My people, you have been tested by it. Indeed, your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me and obey my command.”
interpretation: Aaron warned his people that the calf was a trial that could lead them astray, and called them to return to God’s guidance, trusting in His mercy and following the counsel of a faithful messenger.

translation: They said, “We will remain devoted to it until Moses returns to us.”
interpretation: Their words reveal that they chose to persist in worshipping the calf despite Aaron’s warning, postponing any change until Moses returned rather than responding to the truth before them.

translation: He said, “O Aaron, what prevented you, when you saw them going astray?”
interpretation: Moses questions Aaron about what kept him from responding when he witnessed his people turning away from the right path.

translation: “Why did you not follow me? Have you then disobeyed my command?”
interpretation: Moses’ words express a sharp demand for an explanation: he holds Aaron accountable for not acting as instructed, while the question leaves room for Aaron to explain what happened.

translation: He said, “O son of my mother, do not seize me by my beard or by my head. I feared you would say, ‘You have divided the Children of Israel,’ and that you would accuse me of not heeding your instruction.”
interpretation: Aaron explains that he refrained from forcefully confronting the people because he feared that doing so would deepen divisions among the Children of Israel. He appeals to Moses as his brother and asks him to understand that his choice was meant to preserve unity, not to disregard his command.

translation: He said, “Then what was your purpose, O Samiri?”
interpretation: Moses confronts the Samiri and demands an explanation for his role in leading the people astray, signaling that his actions will be held to account.

translation: He said, “I saw what they did not see, so I took a handful from the Messenger’s trace and cast it away. This is how my soul made it seem fair to me.”
interpretation: The speaker admits that he used what he had witnessed to mislead his people, while blaming his own desires for making the act seem right. The verse exposes how inner temptation can dress wrongdoing as something justified.

translation: He said, “Then go. In this life, your lot is to say, ‘Do not touch me’; and you have an appointed time that you will not fail to meet. Look at your god to which you remained devoted: we will burn it, then scatter it completely into the sea.”
interpretation: Samiri’s punishment combines alienation in this life with an unavoidable reckoning before God. Destroying and scattering the calf also makes clear that an object people fashion and worship has no divine power and cannot be a true god.

translation: Your God is only Allah; there is no deity except Him. His knowledge encompasses all things.
interpretation: The verse affirms that worship belongs to Allah alone and that nothing is beyond His knowledge. This calls a person to rely on Him, while remembering that every intention and deed is known to Him.

translation: Thus We recount to you some of the accounts of what came before, and We have indeed given you a Reminder from Us.
interpretation: The stories of earlier peoples are related as a lesson, while the Reminder—understood as the Qur’an—is a divine gift that guides the Prophet and his community.

translation: Whoever turns away from it will indeed bear a burden on the Day of Resurrection.
interpretation: Turning away from God’s revelation carries real accountability: its consequences may be ignored in this life, but they will be made manifest before God on the Day of Resurrection.

translation: They will remain in it forever, and what an evil burden it will be for them on the Day of Resurrection.
interpretation: Their persistent turning away from God’s guidance leaves them bearing the consequences of their wrongdoing without escape; on the Day of Resurrection, that burden will be a source of terrible loss and punishment.

translation: On the Day the Trumpet is blown, We will gather the criminals that Day with their eyes turned blue.
interpretation: Their eyes turning blue conveys the fearsome, distressed state in which the criminals will be raised and gathered for judgment.

translation: They will whisper to one another, “You remained for no more than ten [days].”
interpretation: Overwhelmed by the Resurrection, they will speak in hushed voices and perceive their time in the world as fleeting, as though it had lasted only a few days.

translation: We know best what they say, when the most discerning of them will say, “You remained only a day.”
interpretation: When faced with the Resurrection, the life they once thought long will seem so brief that even their most judicious will describe it as only a day. Their differing estimates cannot obscure the truth from God, who knows exactly what they say.

translation: They ask you about the mountains. Say, “My Lord will grind them to dust, completely.”
interpretation: The verse points to the mountains’ complete destruction by God at the appointed end, reminding us that even what seems most solid and enduring is wholly subject to His power.

translation: Then He will leave it as a level, bare plain.
interpretation: The image conveys the complete leveling of the earth: its familiar rises and unevenness will be gone, revealing the all-encompassing power of God.

translation: You will see in it neither crookedness nor unevenness.
interpretation: This describes the earth on the Day of Resurrection as completely level, with no hollows, bends, or raised places to disrupt its even surface.

translation: On that Day, they will follow the caller, with no deviation from him, and voices will be humbled before the Most Merciful; you will hear only a faint whisper.
interpretation: The verse portrays the certainty and overwhelming awe of the Resurrection: no one can evade the summons, and human voices fall quiet before God, leaving only the slightest sound.

translation: On that Day, intercession will be of no benefit except from one whom the Most Merciful has permitted and whose words He approves.
interpretation: Intercession on the Day of Judgment is not an independent power: it can avail only by God’s permission, and only when He approves of what is said.

translation: He knows what is before them and what is behind them, but they cannot encompass Him in knowledge.
interpretation: God’s knowledge encompasses all things, while human beings cannot fully comprehend Him or the extent of His knowledge.

translation: All faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all; and whoever bears wrongdoing has indeed failed.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, every created being will stand in humble submission before God, whose life and sustaining power are absolute. Those who come burdened with wrongdoing will have lost, for no one can evade His judgment or escape the consequences of injustice.

translation: Whoever does righteous deeds while believing will fear neither injustice nor any diminishment of their reward.
interpretation: True faith joined with righteous action brings assurance before God: no one will be treated unfairly, and none of the good they have done will be reduced or withheld.

translation: Thus We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur’an, and We have varied within it the warnings, so that they may become mindful of God or that it may awaken remembrance in them.
interpretation: Its Arabic form makes the revelation accessible to its first hearers, while its varied warnings address people in different ways. The aim is not merely to inform them of consequences, but to move them toward reverent awareness of God or, at the least, to stir their hearts to remember and reflect.

translation: Exalted is Allah, the True King. Do not hasten to recite the Qur’an before its revelation to you is complete, and say, “My Lord, increase me in knowledge.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that divine revelation is to be received with patience rather than hurried ahead of its completion, while knowledge is sought humbly from Allah. Even the Prophet is instructed to ask for more knowledge, showing that learning is a continual need and a gift from the One whose authority and truth are absolute.

translation: And We had already made a covenant with Adam before, but he forgot, and We found in him no firm resolve.
interpretation: Adam’s lapse is presented as forgetfulness and a failure to remain steadfast in God’s instruction, not as calculated defiance. The verse points to the human need for vigilance in keeping a commitment once made.

translation: And when We said to the angels, “Prostrate before Adam,” they prostrated, except Iblis; he refused.
interpretation: The command honored Adam and tested obedience. The angels submitted, while Iblis’s refusal revealed his pride and disobedience.

translation: So We said, “O Adam, this is indeed an enemy to you and your wife. So do not let him drive you both out of the Garden, lest you suffer.”
interpretation: The warning points to the hardship that would follow separation from God’s provision: Satan’s deception threatens not only Adam and his wife’s dwelling in the Garden, but also the ease and security they enjoy there.

translation: Indeed, you will not go hungry there, nor be unclothed.
interpretation: The verse portrays the security and ease of life in the Garden: its inhabitants are free from the hardship of lacking food or clothing.

translation: And you will not thirst therein, nor be exposed to the sun’s heat.
interpretation: The verse portrays the Garden as a place of complete comfort and protection, where Adam would be spared both the need that causes thirst and the hardship of exposure to the sun.

translation: Then Satan whispered to him, saying, “O Adam, shall I guide you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that will never fade?”
interpretation: Satan tempted Adam by making disobedience appear to promise lasting life and enduring power, appealing to the human longing for permanence.

translation: Then the two of them ate from it, and their nakedness became apparent to them, so they began fastening leaves from the Garden over themselves. And Adam disobeyed his Lord and went astray.
interpretation: Adam’s lapse was a failure to remain within the limit his Lord had set: its immediate consequence was that what had been concealed became exposed, and he sought to cover himself. “Went astray” points to his having missed the right course in that moment, not to a rejection of God.

translation: Then his Lord chose him, accepted his repentance, and guided him.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that Adam’s lapse did not sever his relationship with God: divine mercy restored him, and God’s guidance enabled him to continue on the right path.

translation: He said, “Descend from it, all of you, as enemies to one another. Then, when guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor suffer.”
interpretation: Human life is marked by conflict and the risk of losing one’s way, but God’s revealed guidance is a dependable path: those who follow it are spared the deeper loss of straying from the truth and the misery that follows.

translation: But whoever turns away from My remembrance will have a constricted life, and We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind.
interpretation: Turning away from God’s guidance leaves a person without the peace and direction that give life its meaning, even if outward circumstances seem comfortable. The blindness on the Day of Resurrection expresses the consequence of having ignored the truth in life: the person is brought forth unable to see a way to salvation.

translation: He will say, “My Lord, why have You raised me blind, when I once could see?”
interpretation: The speaker laments being deprived of sight on the Day of Resurrection despite having been able to see in worldly life. The verse points to this blindness as a consequence of having turned away from God’s signs: one who disregarded guidance in life is left without the sight that could have helped him recognize the truth in the Hereafter.

translation: He will say, “Thus Our signs came to you, but you forgot them; and so today you will be forgotten.”
interpretation: The verse portrays a person being confronted with the consequence of having disregarded God’s guidance in worldly life. Being “forgotten” today means being left to face the punishment without the honor or mercy he had neglected to seek—not that God has literally forgotten him.

translation: Thus do We recompense whoever transgresses and does not believe in the signs of his Lord; and the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe and more lasting.
interpretation: The verse warns that worldly consequences are not the full measure of divine judgment: even if punishment is delayed or seems limited in this life, the reckoning of the Hereafter is far more severe and enduring. It connects such judgment to both exceeding the bounds and rejecting God’s signs.

translation: Has it not become clear to them how many generations We destroyed before them, whose dwellings they now walk among? Surely in that are signs for people of sound understanding.
interpretation: The ruins of past peoples are a warning that worldly power cannot protect those who persist in wrongdoing. People of sound judgment recognize in them a call to heed the truth before they meet the same fate.

translation: Had it not been for a decree already issued by your Lord, [the punishment] would have become inevitable; but it has an appointed time.
interpretation: God has decreed that punishment be deferred until its appointed time. The delay is therefore not a sign that wrongdoing goes unanswered, but part of the measure and timing set by the Lord.

translation: So be patient with what they say, and glorify your Lord with praise before sunrise and before sunset. Glorify Him during parts of the night and at the ends of the day, so that you may be content.
interpretation: The verse teaches that patience amid hurtful words is sustained through continual remembrance of God. By turning to Him in praise and worship throughout the day and night, the believer finds reassurance and contentment despite opposition.

translation: Do not fix your eyes on the worldly splendor We have granted to some groups among them, by which We test them. The provision of your Lord is better and more lasting.
interpretation: The verse teaches that another person’s worldly abundance is not evidence of divine favor; it may be a test. Believers should resist envy and comparison, and seek contentment in what God provides, keeping their hope oriented toward what endures.

translation: And enjoin prayer upon your family, and persevere in it. We ask no provision of you; We provide for you. And the good end belongs to those mindful of God.
interpretation: The verse teaches that devotion should be nurtured patiently within one’s household, without letting anxiety about livelihood displace worship: provision rests with God, while lasting success is tied to God-consciousness.

translation: They say, “Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?” Has there not come to them clear evidence of what was in the earlier scriptures?
interpretation: Their demand for another sign overlooks the evidence already given: the revelation affirms the truths conveyed in earlier scriptures and bears witness to the messenger’s message.

translation: Had We destroyed them with a punishment before it, they would surely have said, “Our Lord, why did You not send us a messenger so that we might follow Your signs before we were humiliated and disgraced?”
interpretation: The verse shows that God establishes clear guidance through messengers before bringing punishment, so people cannot claim they were denied the chance to recognize and follow His signs.

translation: Say, “Everyone is waiting, so wait. You will soon know who follows the even path and who is rightly guided.”
interpretation: The verse calls the disputing sides to leave the outcome to time and God’s judgment: claims alone do not establish who is right; the truth will become clear through the path each follows and where it leads.

translation: In the name of God, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. The reckoning of the people has drawn near, while they remain heedless and turn away.
interpretation: The verse warns that accountability before God is not remote, even when people live as though it were. Their heedlessness is not merely a lack of awareness; it is a turning away from the reminders that could awaken them to prepare for that meeting.

translation: No new reminder comes to them from their Lord but they listen to it while they are playing.
interpretation: The verse censures receiving divine guidance with heedlessness: they hear the reminder, yet treat it as something to pass time with rather than a message calling for reflection and response.

translation: Their hearts are distracted. Those who do wrong whisper among themselves: “Is this anything but a human being like you? Will you follow magic when you can see?”
interpretation: Their private whispering reveals a refusal to take the Prophet’s message seriously: they dismiss him as merely human and label the revelation magic, rather than considering its truth with open minds.

translation: He said, “My Lord knows every word spoken in the heavens and the earth; He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.”
interpretation: No speech is hidden from God, whether whispered or spoken openly. This assures the faithful that God is fully aware of what people say and intend, and that no accusation or scheme escapes His knowledge.

translation: Rather, they say, “A jumble of dreams!” Rather, “He has invented it!” Rather, “He is a poet!” So let him bring us a sign, just as the earlier messengers were sent with signs.
interpretation: Their accusations shift from one claim to another, revealing not a sincere search for understanding but a refusal to accept the message. They demand a sign on their own terms, even though earlier peoples who received signs were still not necessarily moved to believe.

translation: No town that We destroyed before them ever believed; will they, then, believe?
interpretation: The verse warns that people who persistently reject God’s message are not necessarily persuaded even by extraordinary signs. The fate of earlier communities is a warning to the listeners: they should not assume that witnessing a sign will make them believe if they remain committed to denial.

translation: We sent before you only men to whom We revealed. So ask the people of knowledge if you do not know.
interpretation: The verse reassures the Prophet’s opponents that human messengers are consistent with God’s way of sending revelation, and directs those who doubt this to consult people knowledgeable about earlier revelation.

translation: We did not make them bodies that did not eat food, nor were they immortal.
interpretation: God’s messengers were human beings, subject to ordinary needs and death; their divine mission did not make them exempt from the conditions of human life.

translation: Then We fulfilled Our promise to them, saving them and whoever We willed, and We destroyed those who exceeded all bounds.
interpretation: The verse teaches that God’s promise to His messengers is dependable: deliverance comes by His will, while those who persist in defying the limits He has set ultimately face the consequences of their excess.

translation: We have surely sent down to you a Book in which is your reminder. Will you not then understand?
interpretation: The Qur’an calls people to reflect on the guidance sent to them: their true honor and well-being lie in taking its teachings to heart and living by them.

translation: How many a town that was unjust We have shattered, and after it brought forth another people!
interpretation: The verse warns that power and permanence do not belong to societies that persist in injustice: their apparent strength cannot shield them from divine judgment, and their place may be taken by others.

translation: When they sensed Our punishment, they began fleeing from it.
interpretation: The verse portrays people recognizing the reality of divine judgment only when it reaches them; their frantic attempt to escape shows that worldly flight cannot avert the consequences of rejecting the truth.

translation: “Do not flee; return to the comforts you once enjoyed and to your homes, so that you may be questioned.”
interpretation: This is a reproachful, ironic command to people fleeing divine punishment: they are told to return to the luxuries and homes they trusted, as though they could still carry on as before. The words expose their helplessness and suggest that they will be held to account for their conduct.

translation: They said, “Woe to us! We have indeed been wrongdoers.”
interpretation: Their cry reveals the remorse of people who recognize their wrongdoing only when its consequences confront them. The verse warns that such recognition, when it comes too late, cannot undo the harm or avert accountability.

translation: So that remained their cry until We made them like a harvested field, utterly still.
interpretation: Their cries of regret continued until divine judgment brought their power and life to a complete end.

translation: We did not create the heaven and the earth and all that is between them in play.
interpretation: Creation is not without purpose or wisdom; its order points to a deliberate design and a meaningful end.

translation: Had We wished to take amusement, We would have taken it from Our own presence, if We were to do so.
interpretation: The verse rejects the notion that God has taken a child or companion for amusement. It states a hypothetical to affirm that creation is not play or a source of need for God; were He to take amusement, it would be by His own will and in a manner befitting Him—not through anything He created.

translation: Rather, We hurl the truth against falsehood, and it crushes it; then falsehood vanishes. Woe to you for what you attribute.
interpretation: The verse portrays truth as a force that decisively exposes and overcomes falsehood, however entrenched it may seem. Its warning is directed at those who make false claims about God: such claims cannot endure against the truth, and their authors face accountability for them.

translation: To Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth. Those who are with Him are not too proud to worship Him, nor do they grow weary.
interpretation: The verse presents worship as the fitting response to God’s complete sovereignty: even the angels nearest to Him serve without pride or fatigue, showing that devotion to God is neither beneath the honored nor a burden to those devoted to Him.

translation: They glorify Him night and day, never tiring.
interpretation: This portrays the angels’ worship as constant and wholehearted: unlike creatures who grow weary, they remain wholly devoted to God, affirming His transcendence and their complete obedience to Him.

translation: Or have they taken gods from the earth who can bring the dead to life?
interpretation: The verse challenges the claim that anything besides God deserves worship: if these supposed gods cannot restore the dead to life, they possess no power that could justify treating them as divine.

translation: Had there been gods in the heavens and the earth besides Allah, both would have fallen into ruin. So glory be to Allah, Lord of the Throne, far above what they ascribe to Him.
interpretation: The verse points to the ordered coherence of creation as a sign that its ultimate governance belongs to one God. Allah is exalted above any partners or limitations people attribute to Him.

translation: He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned.
interpretation: God’s authority and wisdom are absolute; no one has the standing to call Him to account. Human beings, by contrast, are accountable for their choices and will answer for them.

translation: Or have they taken gods besides Him? Say, “Bring your proof. This is the Reminder for those with me and the Reminder of those before me.” Rather, most of them do not know the truth, so they turn away.
interpretation: The verse challenges those who worship other gods to provide evidence for doing so. The revealed message given to the Prophet and the messages given to earlier peoples affirm the truth of worshipping God alone; their rejection stems not from a sound proof, but from failing to recognize the truth and turning away from it.

translation: We sent no messenger before you without revealing to him: “There is no god but Me, so worship Me.”
interpretation: The verse presents the worship of God alone as the unifying foundation of every prophetic message: religious guidance begins by directing devotion and obedience exclusively to Him.

translation: And they say, “The Most Merciful has taken a son.” Glory be to Him! Rather, they are honored servants.
interpretation: The verse rejects any notion that God has offspring or shares His divinity with another. The beings described as His “children” are honored through their devotion to Him; their honor does not make them divine or related to Him.

translation: They do not speak before He does, and they act by His command.
interpretation: The angels neither speak nor act on their own authority; their words and deeds are wholly governed by God’s command.

translation: He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they intercede only for those whom He approves; and they are in awe of Him.
interpretation: The verse presents even the most honored servants as wholly dependent on God: their intercession is not an independent power but occurs only within His approval. Their awe of Him reflects their complete humility before His authority.

translation: And whoever of them should say, “I am a deity besides Him,” We would recompense him with Hell. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse affirms that no being, not even one of the honored angels, has any share in divinity with God. To claim otherwise would be a grave injustice, and Hell is the fitting recompense for such rebellion.

translation: Have those who disbelieve not seen that the heavens and the earth were joined together, then We separated them, and made every living thing from water? Will they not then believe?
interpretation: The verse calls people to recognize in the ordering of the heavens and earth and in life’s dependence on water signs of God’s creative power. Such reflection should lead to faith in the One who brought creation into being and sustains it.

translation: We placed firm mountains in the earth lest it sway with them, and made broad passages through it as routes, so that they might find their way.
interpretation: The verse presents the earth’s stability and accessible routes as signs of deliberate provision: the world is ordered not only to sustain human life, but also to make people reflect on its Creator and find their way toward Him.

translation: And We made the sky a well-guarded ceiling, yet they turn away from its signs.
interpretation: The sky’s ordered and protective nature is a sign of God’s power, but people who refuse to reflect remain heedless of what it reveals.

translation: And it is He who created the night and the day, and the sun and the moon; each moves along in an orbit.
interpretation: The regular movement of the sun and moon, and the ordered succession of night and day, point to the wisdom and power of God, who created and governs the heavens. Each follows its appointed course by His design.

translation: We did not grant everlasting life to any human before you. So, if you die, will they live forever?
interpretation: The verse reminds the Prophet’s opponents that human life is mortal: his death would not make them immortal or exempt them from their own appointed end.

translation: Every soul will taste death. We test you with hardship and ease as a trial, and to Us you will return.
interpretation: Life’s hardships and blessings are both tests of how people respond; neither lasts forever, and the return to God gives every choice its ultimate significance.

translation: When those who disbelieve see you, they take you only in mockery, saying, “Is this the one who speaks against your gods?” Yet they themselves reject the remembrance of the Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse exposes the contradiction in their mockery: they take offense when the Prophet challenges their idols, while they themselves reject the remembrance of God, the Most Merciful. Their scorn does not refute his message; it reveals their own unwillingness to accept it.

translation: Humankind was created hasty. I will show you My signs, so do not urge Me to hasten them.
interpretation: The verse cautions against human impatience, especially demanding that God’s promised signs or judgment arrive immediately. What God has promised will come at its appointed time, so people should respond with patience rather than challenge its timing.

translation: And they say, “When will this promise come to pass, if you are truthful?”
interpretation: They challenge the messengers mockingly to name the time of the promised resurrection and judgment, treating its delay as a reason to doubt it.

translation: If only those who disbelieve knew the time when they will be unable to ward off the Fire from their faces or their backs, and will receive no help.
interpretation: The verse warns that denial cannot protect anyone from the consequences of rejecting the truth: when divine judgment comes, neither personal effort nor outside aid will offer escape.

translation: Rather, it will come upon them suddenly and leave them stunned. They will be unable to repel it, nor will they be granted respite.
interpretation: The warning is that what they dismiss will arrive without notice, leaving no time to prepare or escape. Their denial will not give them power to turn it away or delay its consequences.

translation: Messengers before you were certainly mocked, but those who ridiculed them were encompassed by what they used to mock.
interpretation: Mockery cannot diminish the truth of a messenger’s warning. Those who scorned it ultimately faced the very punishment they had treated as impossible.

translation: Say, “Who will protect you, night and day, from the Most Merciful?” Yet they turn away from the remembrance of their Lord.
interpretation: The verse confronts those who ignore God: they have no protection from harm except by His mercy, yet they turn away from remembering and acknowledging Him.

translation: Or do they have gods who can protect them from Us? They cannot even help themselves, nor can they be shielded from Us.
interpretation: Those they worship have no power to ward off God’s judgment: they cannot defend themselves, much less protect their worshippers, and no one can grant them refuge from Him.

translation: Rather, We have allowed these people and their forefathers to enjoy life until their years grew long. Do they not see that We come upon the land, diminishing it at its edges? Are they, then, the victors?
interpretation: Their long enjoyment is not proof that they are safe from God’s judgment. The gradual loss of their lands and power is a warning that their dominance is already being eroded; they should not imagine themselves victorious or beyond accountability.

translation: Say, “I only warn you through revelation.” But the deaf do not hear the call when they are warned.
interpretation: The warning reaches people through God’s revelation, but those who have closed themselves off from guidance are like the deaf: they cannot benefit from it even when it is plainly delivered.

translation: If even a waft of your Lord’s punishment were to touch them, they would surely cry, “Woe to us! We have indeed been wrongdoers.”
interpretation: The verse warns against mistaking the respite before judgment for safety: even the slightest encounter with divine punishment would shatter denial and expose the truth people had refused to acknowledge.

translation: We shall set up the just scales for the Day of Resurrection, and no soul will be wronged in the least. Even if a deed weighs no more than a mustard seed, We shall bring it forth. We are sufficient as reckoners.
interpretation: The verse teaches that God’s judgment is perfectly just and exact: no one’s deeds, however seemingly insignificant, will be overlooked or their due withheld.

translation: And We certainly gave Moses and Aaron the Criterion, a light, and a reminder for the mindful of God.
interpretation: The verse presents the revelation given to Moses and Aaron as guidance that distinguishes truth from falsehood, illuminates the way to God, and keeps those mindful of Him steadfast in their devotion.

translation: Those who stand in awe of their Lord though He is unseen, and who are apprehensive of the Hour.
interpretation: Their devotion is rooted in sincere awareness of God, not in what others can see; their concern for the coming judgment keeps them mindful of accountability and shapes how they live.

translation: And this is a blessed Reminder that We have sent down. Will you then deny it?
interpretation: The verse presents the Qur’an as a divinely revealed source of enduring guidance and blessing, and challenges its hearers to reflect on why they would reject it.

translation: And We had certainly granted Abraham sound judgment before, and We knew him well.
interpretation: Abraham’s discernment and readiness for guidance were gifts from God, who knew his character and worthiness completely.

translation: When he said to his father and his people, “What are these statues to which you are devoted?”
interpretation: Ibrahim’s question challenges his people to examine an unquestioned practice: their intense devotion to statues that cannot answer or help them. It invites them to recognize the gap between the reverence they give these objects and what the objects are actually capable of.

translation: They said, “We found our forefathers worshipping them.”
interpretation: They defend their worship by appealing to ancestral custom, but inherited practice alone does not establish that a belief is true.

translation: He said, “Indeed, you and your forefathers have been in manifest error.”
interpretation: Abraham challenges his people’s unexamined reliance on inherited beliefs, declaring that their worship of idols is not made right by its age or by their ancestors’ practice; it is plainly misguided.

translation: They said, “Have you come to us with the truth, or are you one of those who jest?”
interpretation: Their question reveals how far they were from taking the challenge to their worship seriously: rather than reflect on the truth, they treated Ibrahim’s words as so implausible that they wondered whether he was joking.

translation: He said, “Rather, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, who brought them into being, and I am among those who bear witness to that.”
interpretation: Abraham turns the people’s attention from their powerless idols to the One who truly deserves worship: the Creator of the heavens and the earth. His words express firm conviction and make clear that his rejection of their gods rests on his testimony to God’s creative power.

translation: By God, I will surely devise a plan against your idols after you have turned away and gone.
interpretation: Abraham swears that once the people have left, he will act against their idols to expose their inability to protect themselves or help their worshippers.

translation: So he smashed them to pieces, except for the largest of them, so that they might turn to it.
interpretation: Abraham left the largest idol intact as a deliberate challenge: when his people returned, they would be confronted with the idols’ inability to act or explain what had happened, prompting them to recognize that these objects were powerless.

translation: They said, “Who has done this to our gods? Surely, he is one of the wrongdoers.”
interpretation: Their outrage reflects how fiercely they defended their idols, even though those idols could neither protect themselves nor deserve worship. They judged the act by their attachment to the idols rather than considering whether their worship was right.

translation: They said, “We heard a young man speaking about them; he is called Abraham.”
interpretation: Their words identify Abraham as the one who challenged the idols, revealing how his bold opposition to their worship had become known among the people.

translation: They said, “Bring him before the people’s eyes, so that they may witness.”
interpretation: Their insistence on bringing him into public view suggests they wanted the matter witnessed by the community, making the confrontation—and the evidence surrounding it—public rather than private.

translation: They said, “Was it you who did this to our gods, O Abraham?”
interpretation: Their question reveals their outrage at the destruction of the idols, while the scene challenges them to recognize the contradiction of worshipping objects unable to protect themselves.

translation: He said, “Rather, this largest of them did it. So ask them, if they can speak.”
interpretation: Ibrahim spoke ironically to expose the weakness of his people’s belief: if these idols were truly worthy of worship, they should be able to speak and explain what happened. Their inability to answer revealed that they could neither act nor help anyone.

translation: So they turned to one another and said, “Indeed, you are the wrongdoers.”
interpretation: Confronted with the truth of Abraham’s challenge, they briefly recognized that their own worship of powerless idols—not Abraham’s words—was the wrongdoing.

translation: Then they were turned back to their own reasoning and said, “You know that these do not speak.”
interpretation: Their admission that the idols could not speak exposed the contradiction in their worship: they recognized the idols’ helplessness, yet still resisted the truth out of stubbornness.

translation: He said, “Do you worship, besides Allah, that which can neither benefit you in any way nor harm you?”
interpretation: The question challenges the worshippers to recognize that anything powerless to bring benefit or avert harm cannot rightfully be worshipped; worship belongs to Allah alone.

translation: Fie upon you and what you worship besides Allah! Will you not then use reason?
interpretation: Abraham condemns the worship of powerless idols as a profound failure of judgment, urging his people to recognize that worship belongs to Allah alone.

translation: They said, “Burn him, and defend your gods, if you are going to do anything.”
interpretation: Unable to answer Abraham’s challenge, his people turned to violence in an attempt to protect their idols—revealing that their devotion rested on stubborn zeal rather than truth.

translation: We said, “O fire, be coolness and peace for Abraham.”
interpretation: The verse shows that creation’s forces remain subject to God’s command: what would ordinarily destroy Abraham became harmless, demonstrating God’s power to protect him.

translation: They plotted against him, but We made them the greatest losers.
interpretation: Their scheme could not overcome God’s protection; instead, their hostility brought about their own defeat and loss.

translation: And We delivered Abraham and Lot to the land that We had blessed for all peoples.
interpretation: The verse shows that divine protection may take the form of guiding believers away from danger to a place where faith and goodness can flourish, with blessings meant to benefit humanity broadly.

translation: And We bestowed upon him Isaac and Jacob as an additional gift, and We made each of them righteous.
interpretation: The verse presents Isaac and Jacob as a further blessing granted by God, and emphasizes that their true distinction lay in the righteousness with which God endowed them.

translation: And We made them leaders, guiding by Our command. We inspired them to do good deeds, to establish prayer, and to give zakah; and they were devoted worshippers of Us.
interpretation: True spiritual leadership is shown through faithful obedience to God: those who guide others do so by His direction, embodying goodness and worship in both their devotion and their care for others.

translation: And to Lot We gave wisdom and knowledge, and We rescued him from the town whose people practiced vile deeds. They were an evil, rebellious people.
interpretation: Lot’s wisdom and knowledge were gifts that enabled him to recognize and uphold what is right amid widespread corruption. His rescue shows that God protects His faithful servants from the consequences of a society persistently given over to wrongdoing.

translation: And We admitted him into Our mercy; indeed, he was among the righteous.
interpretation: God’s mercy is both protection and honor, bestowed upon those whose righteousness is reflected in their faithful obedience.

translation: And Noah, when he called out before, We answered him and saved him and his family from the great distress.
interpretation: Noah’s deliverance shows that hardship does not place a person beyond God’s care: sincere appeal to Him can open a way out of even overwhelming distress.

translation: And We supported him against the people who denied Our signs. They were indeed an evil people, so We drowned them all.
interpretation: The verse teaches that God’s support ultimately prevailed for His messenger over those who persisted in rejecting His signs, and that their wrongdoing brought the consequence of their destruction.

translation: And [remember] David and Solomon, when they judged concerning the field, after the people’s sheep had grazed in it by night; and We were witnesses to their judgment.
interpretation: The verse presents David and Solomon’s judgment as a matter of accountable discernment: even in a practical dispute, their decisions took place under God’s knowledge and witness. Their example points to the need to judge carefully and fairly, recognizing that human judgments are never hidden from God.

translation: So We gave Solomon understanding of the case, and to each of them We granted judgment and knowledge. We subjected the mountains and the birds to join David in glorifying Us; We are indeed able to do all things.
interpretation: Solomon was granted particular insight into the matter, while David too was honored with divine wisdom and knowledge. The mountains and birds joining David in glorification show that all creation is subject to God’s power and can be made to praise Him in ways beyond ordinary human understanding.

translation: And We taught him the craft of making armor for you, to protect you from your own violence. Will you then be grateful?
interpretation: The verse presents practical knowledge and the means of protection as blessings from God. Its closing question calls people to respond with gratitude—not merely in words, but by recognizing these gifts and using them responsibly.

translation: And [We subjected] the raging wind to Solomon, running at his command toward the land We had blessed. And We know all things.
interpretation: Solomon’s command over the wind was a gift from God, who directs creation as He wills; the verse closes by affirming that nothing lies beyond God’s knowledge.

translation: And among the devils were those who dived for him and performed other work besides that; and We kept them under Our watch.
interpretation: The verse shows that their service to Solomon was granted and governed by God: even beings of great strength remained under divine control and could not act beyond the bounds He set.

translation: And [remember] Job, when he called to his Lord: “Affliction has touched me, and You are the most merciful of those who show mercy.”
interpretation: Job’s words express a humble plea grounded in trust: he lays his suffering before God without presuming to dictate the answer, confident that God’s mercy exceeds every hardship.

translation: So We answered him, removed the affliction he suffered, and restored his family to him, along with as many more, as a mercy from Us and a reminder for those devoted in worship.
interpretation: The verse teaches that sincere devotion and patient turning to God remain meaningful even in severe hardship: relief comes by His mercy, and the account encourages worshippers to trust in His compassion and power to restore what has been lost.

translation: And Ishmael, Idris, and Dhul-Kifl—each was among the patient.
interpretation: Their shared praise for patience shows that steadfastness in obeying God and bearing hardship is a central mark of those whom He honors and remembers.

translation: And We admitted them into Our mercy; indeed, they were among the righteous.
interpretation: God’s mercy encompasses the righteous, granting them His favor and care because of their faithfulness and good deeds.

translation: And [remember] the man of the fish, when he went away in anger, thinking that We would not constrain him. Then, in the depths of darkness, he called out: “There is no god but You. Glory be to You! I have indeed been among the wrongdoers.”
interpretation: Jonah’s words express a turning back to God with complete humility: he affirms God’s oneness, declares Him far above any imperfection, and admits his own fault. His prayer teaches that even in profound distress, a person can seek God through sincere repentance and trust in His mercy.

translation: So We answered him and rescued him from distress; and in this way We save the believers.
interpretation: The verse teaches that sincere faith and turning to God in hardship are met with His mercy, and that the deliverance granted to Jonah is an example of His care for believers.

translation: And Zechariah, when he called upon his Lord: “My Lord, do not leave me without an heir, though You are the best of inheritors.”
interpretation: Zechariah’s prayer expresses both his longing for a righteous successor and his trust that, even if he remains without one, God alone is the enduring guardian of all that is left behind.

translation: So We answered him, granted him John, and made his wife fit for him. They were indeed quick to do good, and called upon Us with hope and fear; and they were humbly devoted to Us.
interpretation: Their prayer was answered within a life already shaped by devotion: they eagerly pursued goodness and turned to God with both hopeful longing for His mercy and reverent fear of displeasing Him. Their humility before Him was the foundation of their supplication.

translation: And she who guarded her chastity—We breathed into her of Our spirit, and made her and her son a sign for all peoples.
interpretation: The verse presents Mary and Jesus as a sign of God’s power to bring about creation beyond ordinary causes. The expression “of Our spirit” honors the life God created in her; it does not imply that God’s spirit became part of her. Their story points to God’s command as the source of life and creation.

translation: Indeed, this community of yours is one community, and I am your Lord, so worship Me.
interpretation: The verse calls believers to recognize that the divine message is one across the prophets, and that their unity rests on worshipping God alone.

translation: But they divided their affair among themselves; all of them will return to Us.
interpretation: The verse warns that people’s divisions do not escape God’s knowledge or judgment: despite their disagreements, all will ultimately return to Him and answer for their choices.

translation: Whoever does righteous deeds while believing—his effort will not be rejected, and We are recording it for him.
interpretation: God assures the believer that no sincere effort in doing good is lost: it is recognized and preserved, even if its reward is not immediately apparent.

translation: It is forbidden for a town We have destroyed that its people should return.
interpretation: A community destroyed by God cannot return to its former worldly life; its people remain beyond return until the resurrection and judgment.

translation: Until, when Gog and Magog are released, they will surge down from every elevation.
interpretation: The verse depicts the release of Gog and Magog as a momentous sign of the approaching end, with their rapid descent from every height conveying the vastness and unstoppable force of the upheaval to come.

translation: The true promise draws near, and then the eyes of those who disbelieved will stare in terror. They will say, “Woe to us! We were indeed heedless of this; rather, we were wrongdoers.”
interpretation: When the promised Judgment becomes unmistakable, the disbelievers will be struck with terror and recognize that their failure was not merely heedlessness: they had also wronged themselves by turning away from the truth. Their recognition comes only when there is no longer time to change course.

translation: Indeed, you and whatever you worship besides Allah are fuel for Hell; you will all come to it.
interpretation: The verse warns those who worship others besides Allah that their idols cannot save them: they will be cast into Hell, and their worshippers will face it too.

translation: If these had been gods, they would not have entered it; yet all who are in it will remain there forever.
interpretation: The verse exposes the helplessness of the objects worshipped besides God: their being in Hell shows that they possess no divine power or protection.

translation: They will have groaning there, and they will hear nothing there.
interpretation: The verse portrays the people of Hell as overwhelmed by anguish: their groans fill their state, and they are deprived of hearing what might bring comfort or relief.

translation: Indeed, those for whom the best reward has already been promised by Us will be kept far away from it.
interpretation: The verse offers reassurance that God’s promise of ultimate good to the faithful is certain: they will be protected from the punishment and terror of Hell by His mercy.

translation: They will not hear even its faintest sound, and they will remain forever in what their souls desire.
interpretation: This expresses the complete security and lasting fulfillment granted to the righteous: they are spared even the slightest trace of Hell’s terror and enjoy enduring peace and joy.

translation: The Greatest Terror will not grieve them, and the angels will welcome them, saying, “This is the day you were promised.”
interpretation: The verse conveys God’s assurance that those He has favored will be protected from the overwhelming distress of the Resurrection. The angels’ welcome marks the fulfillment of His promise and confirms that their trust in Him was not in vain.

translation: On the Day We fold the heaven as a scroll is folded for writings, We will restore creation just as We began it the first time—a promise We have undertaken. Surely We will do it.
interpretation: The verse presents the ending of the present cosmos and the return of creation as equally within God’s power: the One who brought life into being initially can restore it after it has ended. Its certainty rests not on human expectation but on God’s own promise, which He will fulfill.

translation: Indeed, We have written in the Psalms, after the Reminder, that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants.
interpretation: This is a divine promise that lasting stewardship of the earth belongs to those who are faithful and upright. Their inheritance is not merely possession, but the responsibility to live by justice and obedience to God.

translation: Indeed, in this is a message for a people who worship.
interpretation: This points to the Qur’an’s guidance as a lasting source of direction for those devoted to worship: their reverence makes them receptive to its counsel and ready to live by it.

translation: We have not sent you except as a mercy to all worlds.
interpretation: The Prophet’s mission is a mercy whose reach is not confined to one people or place: through him, God offers guidance, compassion, and a path toward well-being to all creation.

translation: Say, “It has been revealed to me that your God is only One God. So will you submit?”
interpretation: The verse presents worship and obedience as the fitting response to recognizing God’s oneness: true faith calls for wholehearted submission to Him.

translation: If they turn away, say, “I have warned you all alike, and I do not know whether what you are promised is near or far.”
interpretation: The warning is delivered plainly and without distinction, while the timing of what God has promised remains unknown to the messenger. Those who turn away are therefore not left without clear notice, even though its fulfillment may be near or distant.

translation: Indeed, He knows what is spoken openly and knows what you conceal.
interpretation: Nothing is hidden from God: He knows both the words people voice and what they keep concealed, so a person’s private intentions are as fully known to Him as their public speech.

translation: And I do not know; perhaps it is a trial for you and enjoyment for a time.
interpretation: The delay of what has been promised may itself test whether people turn back to God or grow heedless during their temporary worldly ease.

translation: He said, “My Lord, judge with truth. Our Lord is the Most Merciful; it is He whose help is sought against what you claim.”
interpretation: The Prophet entrusts the dispute to God’s just judgment and seeks His help against the false claims made by his opponents, confident in God’s mercy.

translation: In the name of God, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. O humanity, be mindful of your Lord. The upheaval of the Hour is indeed tremendous.
interpretation: The universal address calls every person to live with reverent awareness of God. The enormity of the final Hour gives that mindfulness urgency: worldly life is not the ultimate measure, and people should prepare to answer for how they have lived.

translation: On the Day you see it, every nursing mother will be distracted from the child she is nursing, and every pregnant woman will deliver her burden. You will see people as though drunk, though they are not drunk; rather, Allah’s punishment is severe.
interpretation: The verse portrays the overwhelming terror of the Hour: its shock is so immense that even the strongest instinctive bonds are momentarily eclipsed, and people appear disoriented like the intoxicated. Their condition is caused not by drink, but by the severity of Allah’s punishment.

translation: Among people are those who dispute about Allah without knowledge and follow every rebellious devil.
interpretation: The verse warns that arguing about Allah without sound knowledge can lead a person away from truth and into the influence of defiant tempters.

translation: It has been decreed concerning him that whoever takes him as an ally, he will lead astray and guide to the punishment of the Blaze.
interpretation: The verse warns that accepting Satan as a guide means yielding to a path that steadily misleads a person and ends in punishment; it underscores the danger of choosing his influence over divine guidance.

translation: O people, if you are in doubt about the Resurrection, then indeed We created you from dust, then from a drop of fluid, then from a clinging substance, then from a lump of flesh, formed and unformed, so that We may make things clear to you. We settle in the wombs whatever We will for a specified term, then bring you forth as infants; then you reach your maturity.
