Some of you are taken in death, and some are returned to the weakest stage of life, so that after having knowledge they know nothing. And you see the earth lifeless; then when We send down water upon it, it stirs and swells and brings forth every delightful kind of plant.
interpretation: The passage answers doubt about resurrection by directing people to signs of renewal already within their experience. Human life unfolds through stages beyond human control, and the earth’s apparent lifelessness gives way to growth when rain comes. These transformations show that bringing life back after death is within God’s power, while the diversity and order of creation invite reflection on His wisdom.

translation: That is because Allah is the Truth, and He gives life to the dead, and He has power over all things.
interpretation: The verse grounds belief in resurrection in Allah’s absolute reality and unrestricted power: the One who brings life into being is fully able to restore it after death.

translation: And the Hour is surely coming—there is no doubt about it—and Allah will raise those who are in the graves.
interpretation: The certainty of the Resurrection means that death is not the end: every person will be brought back to life and stand before God for judgment. This assurance calls people to live with accountability and trust in God’s promise.

translation: And among the people is one who argues about God without knowledge, guidance, or an illuminating Book.
interpretation: The verse warns against making claims about God on the basis of conjecture or arrogance, rather than sound knowledge and guidance from revelation.

translation: Turning his neck aside in arrogance to lead others away from the path of Allah. For him there is disgrace in this world, and on the Day of Resurrection We will make him taste the punishment of the burning Fire.
interpretation: The verse portrays someone who, out of arrogance, turns away from guidance and seeks to draw others away from it. Such defiance brings humiliation in this life and severe punishment in the Hereafter.

translation: That is for what your own hands have sent ahead, and Allah is never unjust to His servants.
interpretation: The consequences a person faces are tied to what they have done; God does not wrong anyone, but judges with perfect justice.

translation: Among the people is one who worships Allah on the edge: if good comes to him, he is reassured by it; but if a trial comes upon him, he turns back. He loses this world and the Hereafter. That is the manifest loss.
interpretation: This describes faith made conditional on comfort and benefit: such a person remains devoted only while life goes well, but abandons worship when tested. The verse warns that this fragile commitment brings loss in both worldly life and the Hereafter.

translation: He calls upon, besides Allah, that which can neither harm him nor benefit him. That is the farthest misguidance.
interpretation: The verse warns against turning to anything other than Allah as a source of ultimate help or protection when it has no power to benefit or harm; doing so leads a person far from the truth.

translation: He calls upon one whose harm is closer than his benefit. What an evil protector, and what an evil companion!
interpretation: The verse warns that turning to anything besides God for ultimate help is a misplaced trust: what is invoked cannot truly protect its worshipper and may instead lead them further from guidance and well-being.

translation: Indeed, Allah admits those who believe and do righteous deeds into gardens beneath which rivers flow. Indeed, Allah does whatever He wills.
interpretation: The verse affirms that God’s reward is granted by His sovereign will, while showing that faith joined with righteous action is the path He has promised to honor with lasting blessing.

translation: Whoever thinks that God will not support him in this world and the Hereafter, let him stretch a rope up to the sky and then cut it; then let him see whether his scheme can remove what enrages him.
interpretation: The verse confronts anyone whose anger or despair comes from believing that God will withhold His support from the Prophet. It uses a stark image to show that even a desperate, self-destructive act cannot change God’s decree or prevent the support that He has promised.

translation: And thus We have sent it down as clear signs, and Allah guides whom He wills.
interpretation: The Qur’an’s signs are clear, yet recognizing their truth and being guided by them ultimately depends on Allah’s will and guidance.

translation: Indeed, those who believe, the Jews, the Sabians, the Christians, the Magians, and those who associate others with God—God will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection. Surely God is witness over all things.
interpretation: The verse entrusts the final judgment of people across different religious communities to God alone. No human can claim complete knowledge of their inner faith or deeds; God’s all-encompassing witness ensures that His judgment will be perfectly informed and just.

translation: Have you not seen that to Allah prostrates whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, and the sun, the moon, the stars, the mountains, the trees, and the moving creatures—and many among mankind? Yet for many, punishment has become due. Whoever Allah humiliates has no one to honor him. Allah does whatever He wills.
interpretation: The verse presents all creation as subject to God, each in the manner He has ordained. Human beings, unlike the rest of creation, may choose whether to worship Him; those who turn away cannot secure true honor or dignity apart from Him. Their standing, like all things, remains under His authority and will.

translation: These are two parties who have disputed concerning their Lord. As for those who disbelieve, garments of fire will be cut out for them, and boiling water will be poured over their heads.
interpretation: The verse portrays the grave consequence of rejecting God through vivid images of punishment. Its imagery makes clear that the dispute over faith is not merely an abstract argument: a person’s response to their Lord carries ultimate moral and spiritual consequences.

translation: By it, what is within their bellies and their skins will be melted.
interpretation: The verse portrays the torment as penetrating both inward and outward, emphasizing its terrible severity.

translation: And for them are iron clubs.
interpretation: The verse depicts the punishment awaiting them as severe and forceful, with iron clubs used to strike them.

translation: Whenever, in anguish, they try to get out of it, they are returned to it, and [it is said], “Taste the punishment of the Blaze.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the punishment as inescapable: every desperate attempt to flee the torment is thwarted, leaving its inhabitants to face the burning punishment again.

translation: Indeed, Allah admits those who believe and do righteous deeds into gardens beneath which rivers flow. There they will be adorned with bracelets of gold and pearls, and their garments will be silk.
interpretation: The verse presents faith joined with righteous action as the path to lasting divine reward, depicting Paradise through signs of honor, beauty, and comfort beyond the hardships of worldly life.

translation: And they were guided to the good word, and guided to the path of the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: The verse portrays guidance as shaping both belief and conduct: believers are led to speak the truth and to follow a way directed toward Allah, the One worthy of all praise.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and hinder others from the way of God and from the Sacred Mosque—which We have made for all people, alike for those who dwell there and those who come from afar—and whoever intends therein to commit deviation or wrongdoing, We will make him taste a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse stresses the inviolability of the Sacred Mosque: it is not to be claimed as the privilege of those who live nearby, but is open to all people. Its sanctity also makes obstructing worshippers or intending wrongdoing there especially grave; the warning calls for reverence and protection of the sanctuary.

translation: And [remember] when We established for Abraham the site of the House, [saying], “Do not associate anything with Me, and purify My House for those who circle it, those who stand in prayer, and those who bow and prostrate.”
interpretation: The sanctuary’s holiness rests on exclusive devotion to God. Its purification is both a physical act of reverence and a calling to keep worship there free from anything that compromises that devotion.

translation: “And proclaim the pilgrimage to the people: they will come to you on foot and on every lean camel, coming from every distant pass.”
interpretation: The verse presents pilgrimage as a response to a divine invitation that reaches beyond distance and circumstance: people make the journey through hardship because devotion draws them toward God.

translation: That they may witness benefits for themselves and mention the name of Allah on appointed days over the livestock He has provided for them. So eat from them and feed the distressed poor.
interpretation: The pilgrimage joins remembrance of God with gratitude for His provision: the sacrifice is not merely a ritual, but a way to honor Him and ensure that its blessings reach those in need.

translation: Then let them remove their untidiness, fulfill their vows, and circumambulate the Ancient House.
interpretation: This verse teaches that pilgrimage is completed through both outward and inward devotion: pilgrims conclude the rites associated with ihram, honor their commitments to God, and approach the Kaaba in worship. Its commands express the care, reverence, and obedience that should mark the completion of the pilgrimage.

translation: That is so. Whoever honors the sacred ordinances of Allah, it is better for him with his Lord. Livestock have been made lawful for you, except what is recited to you. So shun the impurity of idols and shun false speech.
interpretation: The verse teaches that honoring what God has made sacred is an expression of reverence that benefits a person before their Lord. It also places lawful permissions within the bounds of revelation, and pairs idolatry with false speech to show that devotion to God requires both sound worship and truthfulness.

translation: Devoted solely to Allah, not associating anything with Him. Whoever associates anything with Allah is like one who falls from the sky, then birds snatch him away or the wind carries him to a distant place.
interpretation: The verse portrays associating partners with Allah as a plunge into spiritual ruin: the person is torn from the grounding of faith and left exposed to forces that carry them further from safety and guidance.

translation: That is so. Whoever honors the symbols of Allah, that is indeed from the piety of hearts.
interpretation: Reverence for what Allah has made sacred reflects a heart mindful of Him; sincere devotion appears not only inwardly but also in how one treats His rites and signs.

translation: You may derive benefits from them until an appointed time; then their place of sacrifice is at the Ancient House.
interpretation: The verse refers to the sacrificial animals: people may benefit from them for a set period, but when they are offered, their appointed place is at the Sacred House—the Kaaba and its sanctuary.

translation: For every community We appointed a rite, so that they may mention the name of God over the livestock He has provided them. Your God is one God, so submit yourselves to Him; and give glad tidings to the humble.
interpretation: The rites of sacrifice are meant to direct people’s gratitude toward God, the giver of their provision. Though communities may have different rites, their devotion is to the one God, and the glad tidings are for those who submit to Him with humility.

translation: Those whose hearts tremble when Allah is mentioned, who patiently endure whatever befalls them, who establish prayer, and who spend from what We have provided for them.
interpretation: True devotion to Allah is not merely an inward feeling: reverence shapes a person’s response to hardship, commitment to worship, and willingness to share their blessings with others.

translation: And the sacrificial camels We have made among the sacred symbols of Allah for you; in them is good for you. So pronounce Allah’s name over them as they stand in rows. Then, when their sides have fallen, eat from them and feed both the needy who does not ask and the one who does. Thus We have subjected them to you, so that you may be grateful.
interpretation: The sacrifice is an act of worship whose purpose is to turn people toward Allah and cultivate gratitude, not merely to perform a ritual. The command to share its meat extends that gratitude into care for others, including both those who conceal their need and those who ask openly.

translation: Neither their flesh nor their blood reaches Allah; rather, what reaches Him is your God-consciousness. Thus He has subjected them to you so that you may glorify Allah for having guided you. And give glad tidings to those who do good.
interpretation: The verse teaches that worship is not measured by the material offering itself, but by the sincere reverence, obedience, and gratitude it expresses. The sacrifice is a means of honoring Allah’s guidance, and its spiritual value lies in the worshipper’s God-consciousness and doing what is good.

translation: Indeed, Allah defends those who believe. Indeed, Allah does not love anyone who is treacherous and ungrateful.
interpretation: The verse reassures believers that Allah is their defender, while warning that betrayal and persistent ingratitude are qualities that place a person far from His love.

translation: Permission is granted to those who are being fought, because they have been wronged. Surely Allah is fully able to grant them victory.
interpretation: The verse recognizes the right of people who have suffered injustice and aggression to defend themselves, while grounding their hope in Allah’s power to support them. It presents fighting here as a response to being wronged, not as permission for unrestrained aggression.

translation: Those who were driven from their homes without right, for no reason other than saying, “Our Lord is Allah.” Were it not that Allah repels some people by means of others, monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques—where Allah’s name is often mentioned—would have been demolished. Allah will surely help those who help Him. Allah is indeed Strong, Almighty.
interpretation: The verse presents resistance to oppression as a means by which Allah preserves the ability of people to worship and remember Him. Its mention of different houses of worship shows that defending the oppressed is not limited to protecting one community: those who stand for justice and uphold Allah’s cause may rely on His strength and support.

translation: Those who, if We establish them in the land, establish prayer, give zakah, enjoin what is right, and forbid what is wrong. And to Allah belongs the outcome of all affairs.
interpretation: True authority is a trust: when granted power, believers use it to uphold worship, fulfill their obligations toward others, and promote what is right while resisting wrongdoing. The ultimate outcome remains in God’s hands.

translation: If they deny you, then before them the people of Noah, ʿĀd, and Thamūd also denied [their messengers].
interpretation: Their denial does not diminish the truth of your message: earlier messengers faced the same rejection, and the fate of those communities warns that persistent denial has consequences.

translation: And the people of Abraham and the people of Lot.
interpretation: Their mention points to earlier communities that rejected God’s messengers, reminding the listener that such rejection has occurred before.

translation: And the people of Midian [were also destroyed], and Moses was denied. I granted the disbelievers respite, then seized them. So how terrible was My rejection of them!
interpretation: The verse teaches that being granted time is not a sign of divine approval: God may allow those who reject His messengers a period of respite, but when their appointed reckoning comes, they cannot escape it.

translation: How many a town We destroyed while it was committing wrongdoing, so that it lies collapsed upon its roofs—and how many an abandoned well and a lofty palace remain.
interpretation: The verse warns that prosperity and impressive buildings cannot shield a people from the consequences of injustice; their abandoned wells and ruined palaces stand as signs of how completely worldly flourishing can pass away.

translation: Have they not traveled through the land, so that they might have hearts with which to understand or ears with which to hear? Indeed, it is not the eyes that are blind, but the hearts within the chests that are blind.
interpretation: The verse teaches that witnessing the world’s signs is not enough on its own: true insight depends on a heart willing to recognize and reflect on what it sees and hears. Spiritual blindness is therefore a failure of understanding within, not a defect of physical sight.

translation: They urge you to hasten the punishment, but Allah will never fail His promise. Indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count.
interpretation: The delay of divine judgment is not a failure to keep the promise; it reflects that time and patience are measured differently by Allah than by human beings. Those demanding punishment should not mistake its postponement for its absence.

translation: How many a town I granted respite while it was committing wrongdoing; then I seized it, and to Me is the return.
interpretation: A delay in punishment should not be mistaken for approval or safety: wrongdoing may be allowed to continue for a time, but every community ultimately returns to God and faces His judgment.

translation: Say, “O people, I am only a clear warner to you.”
interpretation: The Prophet’s role is to convey God’s warning plainly, calling people to recognize the consequences of their choices; guidance and judgment belong to God.

translation: As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, they will have forgiveness and a generous provision.
interpretation: The verse assures believers who live out their faith through good deeds that God will pardon them and grant them an abundant, honorable reward.

translation: And those who strive against Our signs, seeking to thwart them—those are the companions of the Fire.
interpretation: They actively oppose God’s revelations and try to defeat their truth, but their efforts cannot escape God’s judgment; their opposition leads them to the Fire.

translation: We did not send before you any messenger or prophet without Satan casting something into his recitation; then Allah removes what Satan casts, and Allah makes His revelations firm. Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: Satan may try to confuse or distort the message conveyed by a prophet, but Allah removes that interference and firmly establishes His revelations. The verse assures that divine guidance ultimately remains clear and protected by Allah’s wisdom.

translation: So that He may make what Satan casts a trial for those whose hearts are diseased and whose hearts are hardened. Surely the wrongdoers are in deep opposition.
interpretation: Satanic insinuations serve as a test that exposes what people are inwardly inclined toward: spiritual weakness and hardened hearts make them vulnerable to error, while wrongdoing carries them farther from the truth.

translation: And so that those who have been given knowledge may know that it is the truth from your Lord, believe in it, and have their hearts humbled before it. Indeed, Allah guides those who believe to a straight path.
interpretation: True knowledge leads a person to recognize divine revelation as coming from their Lord, respond to it with faith, and become inwardly humble before it. Allah then guides believers onward along the straight path.

translation: Those who disbelieve will continue to doubt it until the Hour comes upon them suddenly, or the punishment of a barren day comes to them.
interpretation: Their persistent doubt will not last forever: the sudden arrival of the Last Hour or a decisive punishment will bring their denial to an end. “A barren day” suggests a day from which no relief or good can come.

translation: The dominion on that Day belongs to Allah; He will judge between them. Those who believe and do righteous deeds will be in Gardens of Bliss.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, ultimate authority and judgment belong to Allah, who will decide between people with perfect justice. The verse assures those who unite faith with righteous action that their end will be lasting bliss.

translation: As for those who disbelieve and deny Our signs, they will have a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns that knowingly rejecting God’s signs has a grave consequence: a punishment that brings abasement, in contrast to the honor and guidance found in faith.

translation: Those who emigrated in the cause of Allah and were then killed or died—Allah will surely provide them with a good provision. Indeed, Allah is the best of providers.
interpretation: The verse reassures those who leave their homes for God’s sake that neither death nor martyrdom can cause their sacrifice to be lost: Allah will honor them with enduring provision and reward, beyond what any worldly provider can give.

translation: He will surely admit them to a place they will be pleased with. Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing, Most Forbearing.
interpretation: Allah knows the sincerity and sacrifices of those who strive for His cause, and in His forbearance He grants them a gracious reward and a destination that brings them contentment.

translation: That is so. Whoever responds in kind to the harm inflicted upon them, and is then wronged again, Allah will surely aid them. Indeed, Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving.
interpretation: The verse affirms that a person may seek justice without exceeding the harm they suffered, and promises divine support when an aggressor wrongs them again. Its closing names Allah’s pardon and forgiveness, pointing to mercy as a virtue even while justice remains a right.

translation: That is because Allah causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night, and because Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.
interpretation: The changing balance of night and day points to Allah’s complete power over creation and its affairs. His hearing and sight are perfect, so no injustice or plea is hidden from Him; this assures the wronged that His judgment and support are never beyond reach.

translation: That is because Allah is the Truth, and whatever they call upon besides Him is falsehood, and Allah is the Most High, the Most Great.
interpretation: The verse grounds the distinction between truth and falsehood in God’s unique reality and sovereignty: no being invoked apart from Him possesses independent divinity, while His exalted greatness surpasses all creation.

translation: Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky, and then the earth becomes green? Indeed, Allah is Most Subtle, All-Aware.
interpretation: The gentle transformation of dry land into thriving greenery reveals Allah’s subtle care and knowledge: life unfolds through means that may seem ordinary, yet every detail is within His wisdom.

translation: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Indeed, Allah alone is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: Everything depends on God, while He depends on nothing; His worthiness of praise is inherent and does not rely on anyone’s recognition or gratitude.

translation: Have you not seen that Allah has made whatever is on the earth serve you, and that ships sail through the sea by His command? He holds the sky from falling upon the earth except by His permission. Indeed, Allah is Most Kind and Most Merciful to people.
interpretation: The verse draws attention to the care and power of Allah: people benefit from the world and travel across the seas, yet these blessings and the order that sustains life remain under His command. Recognizing this dependence should lead people to gratitude and humility.

translation: He is the One who gave you life, then causes you to die, then brings you to life again. Indeed, the human being is truly ungrateful.
interpretation: The succession of life, death, and resurrection points to God’s complete power and authority. Yet people often respond to these signs with ingratitude, overlooking the One who sustains them and denying the return to Him.

translation: For every community We appointed a rite which they observe. So let them not contend with you concerning the matter; call people to your Lord. Surely you are upon straight guidance.
interpretation: The verse teaches that communities have been given forms of worship to follow, so disagreement over ritual should not distract the Prophet from his mission. He is to continue calling people to God with confidence, grounded in the guidance that leads straight.

translation: And if they argue with you, say, “Allah knows best what you do.”
interpretation: When argument reaches an impasse, respond with calm certainty: people’s claims do not hide their actions or intentions from Allah, whose knowledge and judgment are complete.

translation: Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which you used to differ.
interpretation: The verse directs people to leave the final resolution of their disputes to God, whose judgment is perfectly just and whose knowledge reaches the truth behind every disagreement.

translation: Do you not know that Allah knows whatever is in the heavens and the earth? Surely that is recorded in a Book; surely that is easy for Allah.
interpretation: The verse affirms that nothing in creation is hidden from Allah: His knowledge encompasses all things, and all is recorded in the Preserved Record. Nothing about this knowledge or record is difficult for Him.

translation: They worship besides Allah that for which He has sent down no authority and of which they have no knowledge. The wrongdoers will have no helper.
interpretation: The verse condemns worship founded neither on divine revelation nor sound knowledge, and warns that those who persist in such wrongdoing will find no one able to rescue or support them before Allah.

translation: When Our clear revelations are recited to them, you can see disapproval on the faces of those who disbelieve. They nearly attack those who recite Our revelations to them. Say, “Shall I tell you of something worse than that? The Fire, which Allah has promised those who disbelieve—and what a miserable destination!”
interpretation: The verse warns that hostility toward the truth does not weaken its message; rather, it exposes the rejecters’ response and points to the far graver consequence awaiting them in the Hereafter.

translation: O people, an example is set forth, so listen to it: those you call upon besides Allah will never create a fly, even if they all joined together to do so. And if a fly were to take something from them, they could not retrieve it from the fly. Weak indeed are the seeker and the sought.
interpretation: The verse exposes the helplessness of anything worshipped besides Allah: those beings cannot create even the smallest creature, nor reclaim what it takes. Their weakness—and the weakness of those who rely on them—shows that worship and ultimate reliance belong to Allah alone.

translation: They have not esteemed Allah as He deserves to be esteemed. Indeed, Allah is All-Strong, Almighty.
interpretation: The verse warns against measuring Allah by human limitations or associating anything with Him: no created being can rival His power or diminish His sovereignty.

translation: Allah chooses messengers from among the angels and from among the people. Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.
interpretation: The choice of messengers belongs to Allah alone: He selects whom He wills, fully aware of their words and their inner and outward qualities.

translation: He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and to Allah all matters return.
interpretation: Nothing in their past, present, or future is hidden from God, and every affair ultimately comes back to Him for its final judgment and resolution.

translation: O you who believe, bow and prostrate, worship your Lord, and do good, so that you may succeed.
interpretation: The verse teaches that true success is pursued through wholehearted devotion to God, expressed both in humble worship and in goodness toward others; faith should shape a person’s conduct in every part of life.

translation: Strive for Allah with the striving due to Him. He has chosen you and placed no hardship upon you in religion—the way of your forefather Abraham. He named you Muslims before and in this [revelation], so that the Messenger may be a witness over you and you may be witnesses over humanity. So establish prayer, give the prescribed alms, and hold fast to Allah. He is your Protector—how excellent a Protector and how excellent a Helper.
interpretation: The verse calls believers to wholehearted devotion: to strive in obedience to God while remembering that faith is not meant to impose needless hardship. Their religious inheritance is the pure worship of Abraham, and their honored role as witnesses to humanity carries responsibility before God. Prayer, almsgiving, and holding fast to Him give that responsibility its practical form, while the closing promise grounds their effort in trust in God’s protection and help.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Indeed, the believers have succeeded.
interpretation: This verse declares that lasting success is found in faith and in the life shaped by devotion to God—not merely in worldly achievement.

translation: Those who are humble and reverent in their prayer,
interpretation: True prayer is marked by a heart attentive to God, inward humility, and reverence that shapes the worshipper’s conduct—not merely by outward movements.

translation: And those who turn away from idle talk,
interpretation: This describes people who avoid speech and pursuits that are futile or harmful, choosing instead what is truthful, beneficial, and pleasing to God.

translation: And those who are active in giving zakah, the prescribed alms.
interpretation: Their faith is expressed through caring for the purification and well-being of others: they willingly fulfill zakah and recognize that wealth carries responsibilities toward those in need.

translation: And those who guard their private parts,
interpretation: This praises believers who practice sexual modesty, restraining themselves from what God has forbidden.

translation: Except with their spouses or those whom their right hands possess, for then they are not blameworthy.
interpretation: The verse defines the limits of sexual conduct in its historical Qur’anic legal framework: relations within the categories it names are treated as permissible, while conduct beyond them falls outside that allowance.

translation: So whoever seeks beyond that—those are the transgressors.
interpretation: The verse describes seeking sexual relations beyond the lawful bounds just mentioned as crossing the limits set by God.

translation: And those who faithfully observe their trusts and their covenants.
interpretation: Faith is shown through integrity: a believer safeguards what is entrusted to them and honors commitments, whether in their relationship with God or with other people.

translation: And those who carefully maintain their prayers.
interpretation: They remain steadfast in prayer, giving it the care and consistency it deserves.

translation: Those are the inheritors.
interpretation: It refers to those described before, who will inherit Paradise as their lasting home through God’s grace.

translation: Those who inherit Paradise will abide therein forever.
interpretation: Their inheritance of Paradise signifies a lasting, secure reward: they will never be removed from it or lose its blessings.

translation: And We certainly created the human being from an extract of clay.
interpretation: The verse directs reflection to the human being’s humble earthly origin, affirming that life and human existence come into being through God’s creative power.

translation: Then We placed him as a drop of fluid in a secure resting place.
interpretation: The verse draws attention to the protected place in which human life begins, inviting reflection on how a vulnerable beginning is held within a setting suited to its development—an expression of God’s care and creative power.

translation: Then We fashioned the drop into a clinging substance, then fashioned the clinging substance into a lump, then fashioned the lump into bones, and clothed the bones with flesh; then We brought him forth as a new creation. So blessed is Allah, the Best of creators.
interpretation: The verse invites reflection on the human being’s passage through successive, unseen stages, each dependent on God’s sustaining power. The emergence of a complete, living person from such beginnings is presented as a sign of divine wisdom and a reason to glorify the Creator.

translation: Then, after all that, you will surely die.
interpretation: The verse confronts human beings with the certainty of death: no matter how life begins or unfolds, worldly existence is temporary, and this reality should shape how one understands and lives one’s life.

translation: Then, indeed, on the Day of Resurrection, you will be raised.
interpretation: The verse affirms that death is not the end: people will be brought back to life for the final reckoning.

translation: And We have certainly created above you seven ways, and We have never been unaware of creation.
interpretation: The “seven ways” refers to the seven heavens, fashioned above humanity in an ordered creation. Their existence points to God’s power and wisdom, while the closing phrase affirms that nothing in creation escapes His knowledge or care.

translation: And We sent down water from the sky in a measured amount, then settled it in the earth; and surely We are able to take it away.
interpretation: The verse presents water as a provision sustained by deliberate divine measure: it is sent down and made available within the earth, yet its continued presence is not guaranteed by human control. This invites gratitude and humility, recognizing that the life water supports depends on God’s continuing power and mercy.

translation: Then by means of it We brought forth for you gardens of date palms and grapevines. You have many fruits therein, and from them you eat.
interpretation: The verse directs attention to how God brings abundant nourishment from water, inviting people to recognize the care and generosity behind the provision they enjoy.

translation: And a tree that grows at Mount Sinai, producing oil and a seasoning for those who eat.
interpretation: This refers to the olive tree, whose oil and fruit are presented as a provision and benefit for people—a sign of God’s care in making nourishing and useful things grow from the earth.

translation: And surely, in livestock there is a lesson for you: We give you drink from what is within them, and you have many benefits from them, and from them you eat.
interpretation: The verse invites reflection on God’s care and power: from livestock, people receive nourishment and many other benefits. Recognizing these gifts should lead to gratitude and humility before the One who provides them.

translation: And upon them and upon ships you are carried.
interpretation: The verse draws attention to the means of travel Allah has made available, inviting people to recognize His provision and power in enabling them to journey across land and sea.

translation: Indeed, We sent Noah to his people, and he said, “My people, worship Allah. You have no god other than Him. Will you not then be mindful?”
interpretation: Noah’s call makes clear that true devotion and ultimate reliance belong to Allah alone. His question urges his people to recognize that abandoning false gods is not merely an act of belief, but a response to their responsibility before their Creator.

translation: The leaders who disbelieved among his people said, “This is only a human being like you, who wants to gain superiority over you. Had God willed, He would have sent down angels. We have never heard of this among our forefathers.”
interpretation: Their objection reflects how fear of losing status can turn into religious denial: they dismiss the messenger as an ordinary human, presume selfish motives, and treat inherited custom as proof against a new call from God.

translation: He is nothing but a man afflicted with madness, so wait awhile concerning him.
interpretation: The speakers dismiss the prophet by calling him mad and urge one another to wait, using insult and delay to evade the warning rather than answer it.

translation: He said, “My Lord, help me, for they have denied me.”
interpretation: After his people rejected his message, he turned to God for support, showing that when human efforts meet persistent denial, reliance and appeal belong to God.

translation: So We revealed to him: “Build the Ark under Our watchful care and by Our revelation. Then, when Our command comes and the oven overflows, take aboard a pair of every kind, and your household—except those against whom the decree has already been made. And do not plead with Me concerning those who have done wrong; they will surely be drowned.”
interpretation: The verse presents Noah’s ark as an act carried out through divine guidance and protection, while the coming flood makes clear that wrongdoing has consequences. It also marks the limit of even a prophet’s plea: compassion cannot undo a judgment already decreed by God.

translation: When you and those with you are settled aboard the Ark, say: “Praise be to Allah, who saved us from the wrongdoing people.”
interpretation: The command teaches Noah and his companions to meet deliverance with gratitude to God, recognizing that their safety came through His mercy rather than their own power, and that they were rescued from a people who persisted in wrongdoing.

translation: And say, “My Lord, bring me to a blessed place of landing, for You are the best of those who bring us to land.”
interpretation: This is a prayer for God to grant a safe and blessed place of arrival, acknowledging that lasting safety and blessing come from Him alone.

translation: Surely in that are signs, and surely We are testing.
interpretation: The events described are signs of God’s power and a test of how people respond to His guidance.

translation: Then We brought forth another generation after them.
interpretation: The verse points to God’s power to bring new peoples into existence after earlier ones have passed away, reminding us that no community is permanent and that human history unfolds under His will.

translation: So We sent among them a messenger from their own people, saying, “Worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. Will you not then be mindful of Him?”
interpretation: The messenger’s familiar origins make the call especially clear and accessible: devotion belongs to Allah alone, and recognizing this should awaken people to their responsibility before Him.

translation: The leading men of his people who disbelieved, denied the meeting of the Hereafter, and whom We had made prosperous in worldly life said, “This is only a human being like you: he eats what you eat and drinks what you drink.”
interpretation: Their denial was shaped by arrogance and attachment to worldly privilege: they treated the messenger’s ordinary human needs as proof that he could not be divinely sent. The verse exposes how people may use a messenger’s humanity to dismiss his call rather than consider its truth.

translation: “If you obey a human being like yourselves, you will surely be losers.”
interpretation: The words express the opponents’ attempt to discredit a messenger because he is human like them. They portray following him as a loss, using that fear to keep people from accepting his message.

translation: Does he promise you that when you have died and become dust and bones, you will be brought forth?
interpretation: The question is voiced as mockery: the speakers treat resurrection as absurd because they judge it by what seems possible to human experience, overlooking the power of the One who first created them.

translation: Far, far-fetched is what you are promised!
interpretation: The repetition intensifies the speakers’ dismissive denial: they regard the promised event as impossibly remote.

translation: “There is nothing but our worldly life: we die and live, and we will not be resurrected.”
interpretation: The verse presents the claim of those who deny the afterlife: they regard earthly existence as the whole of life and reject resurrection. It portrays a worldview in which human accountability beyond death is dismissed.

translation: He is only a man who has fabricated a lie against Allah, and we will not believe him.
interpretation: The speakers dismiss his message by accusing him of inventing a claim about God, revealing a settled refusal to accept him rather than a willingness to consider the truth of what he says.

translation: He said, “My Lord, help me, for they have denied me.”
interpretation: This is a plea for God’s support when people reject the truth: the believer turns to God for strength and vindication rather than relying on personal power.

translation: He said, “Before long, they will surely become regretful.”
interpretation: The warning foretells that those who reject the truth will soon recognize the consequences of their defiance, but their regret will come when it can no longer undo what they have done.

translation: So the blast seized them justly, and We made them like floating debris. So away with the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: The verse portrays the decisive end of a people who persisted in wrongdoing: they were struck by a punishment that was deserved, reduced to something as discarded and powerless as debris, and left far from God’s mercy.

translation: Then We brought forth, after them, other generations.
interpretation: The verse points to God’s power to replace one people with another: no generation or civilization endures forever, and those who come later inherit the consequences of those who came before.

translation: No community can bring forward its appointed term, nor can they delay it.
interpretation: The verse teaches that the time decreed for a community is fixed by God; human beings cannot make it arrive sooner or hold it back.

translation: Then We sent Our messengers one after another. Whenever a messenger came to a community, they denied him. So We caused them to follow one another into ruin and made them stories of the past. So away with a people who do not believe.
interpretation: The verse portrays the rejection of guidance as a recurring pattern whose consequence is not merely the end of each community, but its becoming a warning remembered by later generations. The closing expression conveys their estrangement from God’s mercy because they persistently refuse to believe.

translation: Then We sent Moses and his brother Aaron with Our signs and clear authority.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that Moses’ mission was grounded in divine authorization and unmistakable proof, and that he was supported in carrying it out through his brother Aaron.

translation: To Pharaoh and his chiefs; but they behaved arrogantly, for they were a people given to pride.
interpretation: Their power and high status made them regard themselves as above the truth and its demands, so they rejected the messengers out of arrogance rather than humility before God.

translation: So they said, “Are we to believe two human beings like ourselves, while their people are our servants?”
interpretation: Their refusal was driven by arrogance: they treated the two messengers’ humanity as a reason to reject them and saw the people under their power as proof of their own superiority. They let status and domination outweigh the truth of the message.

translation: But they rejected the two of them, and so they were among those destroyed.
interpretation: Their rejection of Moses and Aaron’s call brought about their ruin, showing that refusing the truth has grave consequences.

translation: And We certainly gave Moses the Scripture so that they might be guided.
interpretation: The Scripture given to Moses was a divine guide, calling his people to recognize the truth and live by God’s direction.

translation: And We made the son of Mary and his mother a sign, and gave them refuge on elevated ground, a place of settled security and flowing water.
interpretation: The miraculous story of Mary and Jesus is a sign of God’s power and care: He both brought about their extraordinary circumstances and provided them with a secure refuge and sustenance.

translation: O messengers, eat of the wholesome things and do righteous deeds. Indeed, I know all that you do.
interpretation: The verse teaches that devotion to God encompasses both what a person takes in and how they act: wholesome provision should be joined with righteous conduct. The reminder that God knows every deed calls people to sincerity and accountability, with the messengers addressed as an example for all who follow them.

translation: Indeed, this community of yours is one community, and I am your Lord, so be mindful of Me.
interpretation: The messengers share one essential way of faith: worshipping God alone. Since He is the Lord of all, people should remain mindful of Him and live in obedience rather than allowing divisions to draw them away from that common devotion.

translation: But they divided their affair among themselves into factions, each party rejoicing in what it has.
interpretation: The verse warns that people can take a shared divine guidance and fragment it through partisanship, until each group becomes pleased with its own position. Such satisfaction is no proof of truth; it can instead prevent people from humbly seeking and holding fast to what God has revealed.

translation: So leave them in their heedlessness for a time.
interpretation: The verse instructs the Prophet to refrain from trying to force acceptance upon those immersed in error: their respite is temporary, not a sign that their way is approved.

translation: Do they think that what We provide them with of wealth and children…
interpretation: The verse challenges the assumption that abundance in wealth and children proves God’s approval or guarantees success in the Hereafter. Such blessings are not, by themselves, a measure of a person’s standing with God.

translation: Do they think We are hastening good things for them? Rather, they do not realize.
interpretation: They mistake worldly blessings for a sign of God’s favor and success, failing to recognize that such gifts may be a test and do not guarantee salvation.

translation: Indeed, those who are in awe of their Lord are deeply apprehensive.
interpretation: Their fear is a reverent awareness of their Lord that makes them humble and watchful, careful not to fall short in their devotion.

translation: And those who believe in the signs of their Lord,
interpretation: Their faith is grounded in recognizing God’s signs as true, and in allowing His guidance to shape their lives.

translation: And those who associate no partners with their Lord,
interpretation: They worship God alone, directing their devotion and reliance to Him without attributing divinity or worship to anyone else.

translation: And those who give what they give while their hearts are apprehensive, knowing that they will return to their Lord.
interpretation: They do good deeds sincerely, yet remain humble and concerned that their deeds may not be accepted, mindful that they will stand before their Lord and answer for them.

translation: Those are hastening to do good deeds, and they are foremost in them.
interpretation: The verse portrays sincere believers as eager to obey God: they do not delay in doing good, but strive with commitment and are distinguished by their readiness to act.

translation: We do not burden any soul beyond its capacity. With Us is a record that speaks the truth, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: God’s commands and accountability are measured with perfect justice: no one is held to what they cannot bear, and the truthful record of each person’s deeds ensures that no one is treated unjustly.

translation: Rather, their hearts are heedless of this, and they have other deeds besides it that they continue to do.
interpretation: Their hearts are so immersed in heedlessness that they fail to grasp the truth being presented to them, while they remain occupied with other actions and pursuits, persisting in them.

translation: Until, when We seize their affluent ones with punishment, they suddenly cry out.
interpretation: The verse highlights the helplessness of those who ignore warnings while living in comfort: when punishment finally reaches them, their cries come too late to undo their rejection.

translation: Do not cry out today; surely you will not be helped by Us.
interpretation: The verse warns that appeals for rescue at the moment of judgment cannot undo a life spent turning away from guidance when there was still time to respond.

translation: My verses were recited to you, but you used to turn back on your heels.
interpretation: The verse rebukes those who deliberately recoil from divine guidance: when confronted with the truth, they retreat from it rather than receive it with humility.

translation: Arrogantly dismissing it, gathering by night and speaking foolishly.
interpretation: They responded to God’s revealed signs with pride, meeting at night to mock them and speak contemptuously instead of taking heed.

translation: Have they not reflected on the Word, or has something come to them that did not come to their forefathers?
interpretation: The verse challenges those who reject the Qur’an to consider its message carefully. Its being new to them is no sound reason for rejection, since revelation and divine guidance were not foreign to earlier generations.

translation: Or have they not recognized their Messenger, so that they reject him?
interpretation: Their rejection is not due to ignorance of the Messenger’s identity or character; they know him, yet still refuse to accept the truth he brings.

translation: Or do they say, “There is madness in him”? Rather, he has brought them the truth, but most of them are averse to the truth.
interpretation: Their accusation of madness is a way of dismissing the Messenger rather than engaging with his message. The real obstacle is that the truth he brought challenges what they prefer, so most of them turn away from it.

translation: If the Truth had followed their desires, the heavens and the earth and all who are in them would have been ruined. Rather, We have brought them their reminder, yet they turn away from their reminder.
interpretation: Truth is not reshaped to satisfy people’s conflicting desires; it is the measure by which life and creation remain rightly ordered. The reminder brought to them calls them back to that truth, but they turn away from it.

translation: Or do you ask them for payment? The provision of your Lord is better, and He is the best of providers.
interpretation: The verse reassures the Messenger that he seeks no worldly payment from those he calls to faith; his reward and sustenance come from God, whose provision is better and more lasting than anything people could offer.

translation: And indeed, you are calling them to a straight path.
interpretation: The Prophet’s call leads to the clear way of truth and obedience to God, free from deviation.

translation: Indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter are turning away from the path.
interpretation: Denial of accountability beyond this life leads people to veer from the right course, because they no longer orient their choices toward ultimate judgment and consequence.

translation: If We were to show them mercy and remove the distress afflicting them, they would surely persist, blindly wandering in their transgression.
interpretation: The verse shows that when people are deeply entrenched in rebellion, relief from hardship alone may not lead them to gratitude or reform; they can remain heedless even after their distress is lifted.

translation: And We have already afflicted them with punishment, yet they did not humble themselves before their Lord, nor did they supplicate.
interpretation: The verse points to hearts so hardened that even suffering did not lead them to humility or repentance. Its warning is that hardship should awaken a person to turn sincerely to God, rather than deepen their heedlessness.

translation: Until, when We open for them a gate of severe punishment, they will suddenly be utterly despairing within it.
interpretation: The verse warns that continued rejection may end in a punishment so overwhelming that those afflicted lose all hope and are left helpless, with no way to escape it.

translation: It is He who brought forth for you hearing, sight, and hearts—yet little are you grateful.
interpretation: These faculties are gifts from God that enable people to perceive, reflect, and recognize truth. The verse calls people to gratitude by using them responsibly, rather than taking them for granted or turning away from what they reveal.

translation: And He is the One who brought you forth and spread you across the earth, and to Him you will be gathered.
interpretation: Though people are scattered across the earth and live distinct lives, their ultimate return is to God, where earthly separation gives way to a shared reckoning before Him.

translation: And He is the One who gives life and causes death, and to Him belongs the alternation of night and day. Will you not reason?
interpretation: The power to grant life and bring death, together with the regular alternation of night and day, points to God’s complete authority over existence. The verse calls people to reflect on these signs and recognize that their lives and the world around them depend on Him.

translation: Rather, they say what the people of old said.
interpretation: Their denial repeats the stance of earlier peoples: instead of considering the truth, they cling to the same rejection passed down before them.

translation: They said, “When we have died and become dust and bones, will we really be raised again?”
interpretation: Their question expresses skeptical disbelief: they assume that bodily decay makes resurrection impossible, overlooking God’s power to restore life after death.

translation: We and our forefathers were promised this before. This is nothing but tales of the ancients.
interpretation: The speakers reject the promised resurrection and judgment, treating them as an old story repeated from one generation to the next rather than a truth for which they must prepare.

translation: Say, “To whom belong the earth and all who are in it, if you know?”
interpretation: The question calls people to acknowledge that the earth and everyone upon it have an ultimate Owner and sovereign, preparing them to recognize that only God holds rightful authority over all creation.

translation: They will say, “It belongs to Allah.” Say, “Will you not then take heed?”
interpretation: Their acknowledgment that all belongs to Allah should lead them to reflect on His authority and worship Him alone.

translation: Say, “Who is the Lord of the seven heavens and the Lord of the Mighty Throne?”
interpretation: The question calls its hearers to acknowledge a sovereignty beyond all creation: even the highest heavens and the greatest symbol of majesty are under God’s authority.

translation: They will say, “It belongs to Allah.” Say, “Will you not then be mindful?”
interpretation: Their acknowledgment that all belongs to Allah should lead them to revere Him and turn away from denying His authority.

translation: Say, “In whose hand is the dominion of all things, who grants protection, while none can be protected against Him, if you know?”
interpretation: The verse directs people to recognize that ultimate authority and security belong to God alone: every refuge depends on His power, and no one can overrule or shield anyone from His judgment.

translation: They will say, “To Allah.” Say, “Then how are you being deluded?”
interpretation: When people acknowledge that ultimate authority belongs to Allah, their worship of others alongside Him contradicts what they themselves recognize. The verse challenges them to consider how they can be turned away from that truth.

translation: Rather, We have brought them the truth, and they are indeed liars.
interpretation: God has made the truth clear to them; their denial and false claims do not alter it.

translation: Allah has not taken a son, nor has there ever been any god alongside Him. Otherwise, each god would have taken away what it created, and some would have sought to dominate others. Glory be to Allah, far above what they attribute to Him.
interpretation: The verse affirms that God’s absolute unity is evident in the ordered creation: if there were independent gods, each would rule over its own creation and contend for supremacy, disrupting that order. Allah is therefore exalted above the claims of partners or offspring.

translation: He is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed; exalted is He above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: Allah’s knowledge encompasses all that is hidden and all that is apparent. His greatness is far above every partner or attribute of divinity people assign to Him.

translation: Say, “My Lord, if You show me what they are promised…”
interpretation: This begins a supplication in which the Prophet turns to God concerning the threatened punishment, entrusting the matter to Him.

translation: My Lord, do not place me among the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: The speaker seeks God’s protection from being counted among those who commit injustice, affirming a desire to remain apart from their wrongdoing.

translation: And indeed, We are fully able to show you what We have promised them.
interpretation: God reassures the Prophet that the promised consequences for those who reject the truth are entirely within His power; their delay comes by His wisdom, not from any inability to bring them about.

translation: Repel evil with what is best. We know best what they attribute to Us.
interpretation: The verse calls for meeting hostility with the finest response—patience, restraint, and gracious conduct—rather than letting others’ wrongdoing dictate one’s own behavior. Their false claims are not hidden from God, so the believer can leave judgment to Him.

translation: And say, “My Lord, I seek refuge in You from the incitements of the devils.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that when faced with satanic whispers and impulses toward wrongdoing, one should turn to God for protection, trusting in His help to resist them.

translation: And I seek refuge in You, my Lord, lest they come near me.
interpretation: This is a prayer for God’s protection from the devils’ presence and influence, acknowledging that true refuge is found in Him alone.

translation: Until, when death comes to one of them, he says, “My Lord, send me back,”
interpretation: At the approach of death, a person may awaken to the consequences of their choices and desperately wish for another chance to live rightly. The plea expresses regret over an opportunity that can no longer be reclaimed.

translation: “So that I may do righteous deeds in what I have left behind.” No indeed! It is only a word he is saying, and behind them is a barrier until the Day they are resurrected.
interpretation: The verse teaches that death closes the opportunity to return and amend one’s deeds: regret may give rise to a plea, but it cannot undo what has passed. The barzakh is the boundary separating the dead from worldly life until resurrection.

translation: When the Trumpet is blown, there will be no ties of kinship among them that day, nor will they ask one another.
interpretation: The verse conveys that, when resurrection begins, worldly bonds and family relationships will offer no protection or advantage; each person will be wholly occupied with the gravity of that moment.

translation: So those whose scales are heavy—they are the successful.
interpretation: True success is determined by what a person brings before God: a life of faith and good deeds that outweighs wrongdoing and earns His favor.

translation: And those whose scales are light—it is they who have lost themselves, abiding in Hell.
interpretation: The verse warns that a life whose deeds do not weigh in the balance of accountability ends in profound loss: the person forfeits their own salvation and remains in Hell.

translation: The Fire will scorch their faces, and they will grimace within it.
interpretation: The verse portrays the humiliation and anguish of the people of Hell: the Fire’s torment leaves them visibly stricken, their faces twisted in suffering.

translation: Were My verses not recited to you, while you continued to deny them?
interpretation: This is a rebuke of those who rejected God’s revelations after they had been clearly conveyed to them, reminding them that their denial was a choice for which they would be held accountable.

translation: They will say, “Our Lord, our wretchedness overcame us, and we were a people astray.”
interpretation: They acknowledge that their ruinous inclinations prevailed over them and led them away from the truth. Their words are a confession of having gone astray, not a denial of responsibility for their choices.

translation: Our Lord, bring us out of it. If we return, then surely we will be wrongdoers.
interpretation: This is a plea of desperate remorse: those speaking acknowledge that their past choices brought them to punishment and promise not to repeat them.

translation: He will say, “Remain disgraced therein, and do not speak to Me.”
interpretation: This is a final rejection of those who persist in denial: they are left in humiliation, with no further opportunity to plead or address God.

translation: Indeed, a group of My servants used to say, “Our Lord, we believe, so forgive us and have mercy on us; You are the best of those who show mercy.”
interpretation: The verse presents sincere believers turning to God with both trust and humility: faith does not make them presume they are free of fault, but leads them to seek forgiveness and mercy from the One whose compassion surpasses all others.

translation: But you took them as objects of ridicule, until [your mockery of] them made you forget My remembrance, and you used to laugh at them.
interpretation: The verse rebukes those who mocked the faithful: their contempt became such a preoccupation that they neglected remembrance of God, while treating the believers’ hardship as something to laugh at.

translation: Indeed, today I have rewarded them for their patience; they are truly the successful ones.
interpretation: Their steadfastness through hardship and in remaining faithful is met with God’s recompense, showing that lasting success lies in the reward of the Hereafter.

translation: He will say, “How many years did you remain on earth?”
interpretation: The question draws attention to how brief earthly life was compared with the lasting reality of the Hereafter, prompting people to recognize that their time in the world was too short to justify neglecting what comes after it.

translation: They will say, “We stayed for a day, or part of a day. Ask those who keep count.”
interpretation: After resurrection, the long span of worldly life will seem so brief that they can scarcely estimate it. Their answer conveys how little that life amounts to when measured against the Hereafter, and they defer to those who kept count because their own sense of time has failed them.

translation: He will say, “You remained only a little—if only you had known.”
interpretation: Compared with the eternity that lies ahead, worldly life is fleeting. The words expose the regret of those who failed to recognize its shortness and use it to prepare for the Hereafter.

translation: Did you think that We created you without purpose, and that you would not be returned to Us?
interpretation: The verse calls people to recognize that their lives are not aimless: they were created with purpose and will return to God, where their choices and deeds will be brought to account.

translation: So exalted is Allah, the True Sovereign. There is no deity but Him, Lord of the Noble Throne.
interpretation: The verse directs the heart to recognize that Allah is far above every imperfection and alone possesses ultimate authority. Since all dominion belongs to Him, worship and reliance belong to Him alone; the Noble Throne points to the grandeur of His sovereignty.

translation: Whoever calls upon another god alongside Allah—though he has no proof of it—his reckoning is with his Lord alone. Indeed, the disbelievers will not prosper.
interpretation: The verse warns that worship directed to any being besides Allah has no legitimate basis, and that each person who does so will answer to Allah. True success cannot come through denying His oneness.

translation: And say, “My Lord, forgive and have mercy; You are the best of those who show mercy.”
interpretation: This prayer teaches the believer to seek both pardon for past shortcomings and mercy for what lies ahead, trusting that God’s compassion surpasses all others’.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. A surah We have sent down and made binding, and in it We have sent down clear signs, so that you may take heed.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that this surah is not merely guidance to consider but divine instruction to be followed. Its clear signs are meant to awaken people to their responsibility before Allah and move them to heed His commands.

translation: As for the woman who commits fornication and the man who commits fornication, flog each of them one hundred lashes. Let no compassion for them hold you back from upholding God’s law, if you believe in God and the Last Day; and let a group of believers witness their punishment.
interpretation: The verse presents the prescribed penalty as a matter of public justice rather than private vengeance: believers are warned not to let personal sympathy or favoritism override the law, and the presence of witnesses underscores that its enforcement is a communal, accountable act.

translation: The adulterer does not marry except an adulteress or a polytheist, and the adulteress is not married except by an adulterer or a polytheist. That has been forbidden to the believers.
interpretation: The verse warns believers against choosing a spouse who is persistently engaged in sexual immorality, affirming that marriage should be grounded in moral integrity. It addresses such conduct, not someone who has sincerely repented and turned away from it.

translation: As for those who accuse chaste women and then fail to produce four witnesses, flog them with eighty lashes, and never accept their testimony; they are the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: The verse establishes a stringent standard of proof for accusations of sexual misconduct, protecting people’s honor from reckless or malicious slander. Its prescribed consequences underscore that such accusations are not merely private insults but grave violations with legal and moral weight.

translation: Except those who repent afterward and set things right—indeed, Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: This offers a way back after wrongdoing: repentance must be joined with genuine reform, and Allah’s forgiveness and mercy remain open to those who turn back sincerely.

translation: As for those who accuse their wives and have no witnesses except themselves, the testimony of one of them is four oaths by Allah that he is indeed truthful.
interpretation: This verse establishes a solemn procedure for a husband who accuses his wife but lacks other witnesses: his claim must be affirmed through repeated oaths before Allah, rather than treated as an ordinary, unsupported accusation.

translation: And the fifth (oath is) that Allah’s curse be upon him if he is among the liars.
interpretation: This is the husband’s final oath in the procedure of mutual imprecation: he calls for Allah’s curse upon himself if his accusation is false, underscoring the grave responsibility of making such a charge.

translation: The punishment will be averted from her if she bears witness four times by Allah that he is indeed among the liars.
interpretation: In the procedure of mutual oaths described here, a wife accused by her husband may avert the prescribed punishment by swearing four times by Allah that her husband is lying in his accusation.

translation: And the fifth [oath is] that Allah’s wrath be upon her if he is among the truthful.
interpretation: This is the wife’s final oath in the prescribed procedure for a husband’s accusation: she invokes Allah’s wrath upon herself if her husband is truthful, affirming that she is willing to answer before God for denying the accusation.

translation: And were it not for Allah’s favor upon you and His mercy—and that Allah is Accepting of repentance, All-Wise…
interpretation: This closing reminder places the preceding rulings within God’s mercy: He provides a path back from wrongdoing through repentance, while His commands reflect perfect wisdom.

translation: Indeed, those who brought the slander are a group from among you. Do not think it bad for you; rather, it is good for you. Each of them will bear the share of sin they earned, and the one who took the greatest part in it will have a tremendous punishment.
interpretation: The verse teaches that even a grave false accusation can, through God’s wisdom, bring good to those harmed by it: the truth is made clear, the innocent are vindicated, and the community is taught to guard its speech and judge fairly. Yet this eventual good does not excuse the slanderers; each is accountable for their part, and the one who led or most actively drove the accusation faces especially severe punishment.

translation: Why, when you heard it, did believing men and women not think well of one another and say, “This is manifest slander”?
interpretation: The verse teaches believers to resist suspicion when faced with unverified accusations, especially against others in their community. A sound faith calls for charitable judgment and for rejecting claims that lack clear proof, rather than allowing rumor to damage someone’s honor.

translation: Why did they not produce four witnesses to support it? Since they did not produce the witnesses, they are the liars in the sight of God.
interpretation: An accusation of this grave kind must be supported by four witnesses. Without that proof, the accusers are judged liars before God.

translation: Had it not been for Allah’s favor upon you and His mercy in this world and the Hereafter, a tremendous punishment would have struck you for what you plunged into.
interpretation: In the context of the false accusation, the verse warns that treating unverified slander as something to repeat is a grave moral offense. Allah’s mercy gives people the chance to turn back, but it should not make them dismiss the harm of their words; believers must verify what they hear and guard one another’s honor.

translation: When you were passing it from tongue to tongue and saying with your mouths what you had no knowledge of, thinking it trivial, while in the sight of God it was grave.
interpretation: The verse warns that repeating an unverified accusation is not harmless gossip: treating it lightly does not lessen its seriousness before God, who holds people accountable for careless words that can wrong others.

translation: Why, when you heard it, did you not say, “It is not for us to speak of this. Glory be to You! This is a monstrous slander”?
interpretation: The verse teaches believers not to treat damaging allegations as casual talk: when a claim is unsupported, they should refuse to repeat it and recognize the grave injustice of harming someone’s honor.

translation: Allah admonishes you never to do anything like it again, if you are believers.
interpretation: True faith calls for taking this warning to heart: believers should guard their speech and never repeat grave accusations without truth or proof.

translation: And Allah makes the signs clear to you; and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: Allah’s guidance is made clear with perfect knowledge of what people need and wisdom in how they are guided; its teachings are therefore grounded in complete understanding and purposeful judgment.

translation: Indeed, those who love for indecency to spread among those who believe will have a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter. And Allah knows, while you do not know.
interpretation: The verse warns that delighting in the spread of indecency—including helping rumors or scandal reach others—is itself morally grave. It calls believers to protect people’s dignity and refrain from amplifying harm, trusting that God knows the motives and consequences that people may not see.

translation: Were it not for Allah’s favor and mercy upon you, and for the fact that Allah is Most Compassionate, Most Merciful…
interpretation: This phrase reminds the listener that Allah’s compassion and mercy are what protect people from the full consequences of their failings, and that they should not despair of His forgiveness.

translation: O you who believe, do not follow the footsteps of Satan. Whoever follows the footsteps of Satan—he urges indecency and wrongdoing. Were it not for Allah’s favor and mercy upon you, none of you would ever have been purified; but Allah purifies whom He wills. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: The verse warns believers that wrongdoing can begin with small steps that gradually lead toward grave sin, so they should resist its path from the outset. Their moral purification is not achieved by their own effort alone: it depends on Allah’s favor and mercy, while Allah knows and hears all that people do and purifies whom He wills.

translation: Let not those among you who have virtue and abundance swear that they will give nothing to relatives, the needy, and those who emigrated in the cause of Allah. Let them pardon and overlook. Do you not love that Allah should forgive you? Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse teaches that a person’s generosity and devotion should not be withdrawn in anger, even when someone has wronged them. By choosing to pardon and continue helping those in need, believers seek the forgiveness of Allah, who is Himself All-Forgiving and Merciful.

translation: Indeed, those who accuse chaste, unsuspecting, believing women have been cursed in this world and the Hereafter, and they will have a tremendous punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns that falsely accusing innocent, faithful women of sexual misconduct is a grave injustice: it violates their dignity and carries severe consequences both in this life and in the Hereafter.

translation: On the Day when their tongues, hands, and feet will testify against them concerning what they used to do.
interpretation: The verse conveys that no wrongdoing can be concealed from God: even the limbs people used in their deeds will bear witness, making the truth of their actions undeniable.

translation: On that Day, Allah will give them their full and just recompense, and they will know that Allah is the Manifest Truth.
interpretation: The reality of Allah’s judgment will become undeniable: every person will see that His decision is perfectly true and just, even if they had rejected it in this life.

translation: Impure women are for impure men, and impure men are for impure women; pure women are for pure men, and pure men are for pure women. They are innocent of what people say; for them are forgiveness and generous provision.
interpretation: The verse affirms the moral distinction between the corrupt and the virtuous, and declares the virtuous innocent of malicious accusations. In its context, it reassures the falsely slandered that God knows their purity and promises them forgiveness and honor.

translation: O you who believe, do not enter houses other than your own until you have sought permission and greeted their inhabitants. That is better for you, so that you may take heed.
interpretation: This verse teaches that a home is a place of privacy and that entering it requires the occupants’ consent. Seeking permission and offering a greeting makes the visit respectful and protects people from intrusion, reflecting the care and dignity believers should show one another.

translation: If you find no one in them, do not enter until permission is given to you. And if you are told, “Go back,” then go back; that is purer for you. And Allah is fully aware of what you do.
interpretation: The verse teaches that honoring people’s privacy includes accepting their refusal without resentment or pressure. Returning when asked protects dignity and keeps one’s conduct sincere and respectful, even when no one else sees it.

translation: There is no blame upon you for entering houses that are uninhabited and in which you have some use. Allah knows what you make known and what you conceal.
interpretation: The permission concerns places available for legitimate use, not an excuse to disregard others’ privacy. The closing reminder directs people to act with integrity even when their intentions or conduct are hidden from others.

translation: Tell the believing men to lower their gaze and guard their private parts. That is purer for them. Indeed, Allah is fully aware of what they do.
interpretation: The verse teaches that moral purity begins with self-restraint: believers should avoid looking at what is forbidden and protect their sexual conduct. This discipline safeguards dignity and relationships, and Allah’s knowledge of their actions gives the command its lasting seriousness.

translation: And tell the believing women to lower their gaze, guard their chastity, and not display their adornment except what ordinarily appears of it. Let them draw their head coverings over their neck openings, and not display their adornment except to their husbands, their fathers, their husbands’ fathers, their sons, their husbands’ sons, their brothers, their brothers’ sons, their sisters’ sons, their women, those whom their right hands possess, male attendants who have no sexual desire, or children who are not yet aware of women’s private aspects. And let them not stamp their feet so as to reveal what they conceal of their adornment. And turn to God in repentance, all of you believers, so that you may prosper.
