interpretation: The verse presents modesty as an ethic of both conduct and appearance: believers are to restrain their gaze and protect their chastity, while women are instructed to cover themselves without deliberately drawing attention to concealed adornment. It allows ordinary visible adornment and identifies close family and other specified circumstances in which display is permitted. The closing call to repentance places these guidelines within a broader invitation for the whole believing community to seek God’s forgiveness and live in a way that leads to true well-being.

translation: Marry off those among you who are unmarried, and the righteous among your male and female servants. If they are poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty; Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: The verse urges the community and household guardians to make lawful marriage accessible, rather than allowing poverty alone to prevent it. It calls for trust in Allah’s abundant provision while affirming that He knows each person’s circumstances and what is best for them.

translation: Let those who cannot afford marriage remain chaste until Allah enriches them from His bounty. And those among your bondservants who seek a contract of emancipation, make a contract with them if you recognize good in them, and give them from the wealth Allah has granted you. Do not compel your bondwomen to prostitution, if they desire chastity, in pursuit of worldly gain. If anyone compels them, then after they have been compelled, Allah is surely Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: The verse treats chastity and freedom from sexual exploitation as serious moral duties, while encouraging practical means toward marriage and emancipation. Its closing assurance addresses those forced into prostitution: coercion does not make them culpable, and Allah’s mercy is not withheld from them.

translation: And We have certainly sent down to you clear signs, an example drawn from those who came before you, and an admonition for the mindful of God.
interpretation: The verse points to different ways divine guidance reaches people: through unmistakable signs, lessons preserved in the fate of earlier peoples, and moral counsel. Such counsel bears its fullest fruit in those who are mindful of God and willing to take heed.

translation: Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The likeness of His light is that of a niche containing a lamp; the lamp is enclosed in glass, and the glass is like a brilliant star, lit from a blessed olive tree, neither of the east nor of the west, whose oil would almost shine even without being touched by fire. Light upon light. Allah guides to His light whomever He wills, and Allah sets forth parables for people; Allah has knowledge of all things.
interpretation: The parable portrays the clarity and abundance of divine guidance as light shining through a pure and protected source. It is not a description of Allah as a physical light, but an image of how His guidance illuminates the heart and makes truth clear; its radiance is “light upon light,” while its full reality and the way it reaches people are known to Allah.

translation: In houses that Allah has permitted to be raised and in which His name is remembered, He is glorified there morning and evening.
interpretation: These are houses devoted to worship, honored by being maintained and kept pure for Allah’s remembrance. The mention of morning and evening points to worship that is steady and woven into the rhythm of daily life.

translation: Men whom neither trade nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah, from establishing prayer, or from giving zakah; they fear a Day when hearts and eyes will be overturned.
interpretation: Their devotion shows that faith does not require abandoning worldly life; rather, true devotion keeps worldly pursuits from becoming one’s ultimate concern. Awareness of the Hereafter gives their worship and generosity their steady priority.

translation: So that Allah may reward them for the best of what they did and increase them from His bounty. Allah provides for whomever He wills without measure.
interpretation: The verse conveys that Allah’s reward is generous: He honors people for the finest of their deeds and may grant them beyond that from His bounty. His giving is not confined by the limits of human calculation.

translation: As for those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage in a flat desert: the thirsty person thinks it is water, but when he reaches it, he finds nothing. There he finds Allah, who settles his account in full; and Allah is swift in reckoning.
interpretation: The verse portrays the false hope that deeds can offer when they are severed from faith: like a mirage, they may seem to promise rescue, yet cannot provide it when the person most needs it. The encounter with Allah then makes the truth unmistakable, and every person is held fully accountable without delay.

translation: Or [their deeds are] like darknesses in a deep sea, covered by a wave, above which is another wave, above which are clouds—darknesses layered one upon another. When he stretches out his hand, he can hardly see it. And whoever Allah has not granted light has no light.
interpretation: This image portrays a person lost in layers of spiritual darkness: confusion and disbelief so deep that even what is nearest is scarcely discernible. Such darkness cannot be dispelled by human effort alone; without the light of guidance granted by Allah, there is no light to lead the person out.

translation: Have you not seen that all who are in the heavens and the earth glorify Allah, as do the birds with wings outstretched? Each knows its prayer and glorification, and Allah knows all that they do.
interpretation: Worship is not confined to human words or forms: every creature has its own way of honoring its Creator, even when people cannot understand it. The verse invites humility before a world whose devotion is known fully to Allah.

translation: To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and to Allah is the return.
interpretation: No power or possession is independent of Allah; every creature ultimately returns to Him, so life is lived under His authority and with accountability before Him.

translation: Have you not seen how Allah drives the clouds, then brings them together, then makes them into a mass? Then you see rain emerge from within them. And He sends down from the sky—mountains of clouds containing hail—striking with it whomever He wills and turning it away from whomever He wills. The flash of its lightning almost takes away eyesight.
interpretation: The verse directs reflection on the precise order and immense power behind natural forces. Rain and hail are not beyond Allah’s command: the same forces that sustain life may also bring harm. Recognizing this should deepen humility before Him and trust in His wisdom and control.

translation: Allah alternates the night and the day. Surely in that is a lesson for those who possess insight.
interpretation: The regular turning of night into day and day into night points to God’s power and wisdom, inviting thoughtful people to recognize that the world is governed with purpose and care.

translation: Allah created every living creature from water. Some of them move on their bellies, some on two legs, and some on four. Allah creates whatever He wills. Surely Allah has power over all things.
interpretation: The diversity of living creatures—in their forms and ways of moving—points to Allah’s unrestricted power and wisdom: life shares a humble origin, yet He brings forth whatever forms He wills.

translation: We have sent down clear signs, and Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path.
interpretation: The revealed signs make the truth clear, while reaching the straight path ultimately depends on Allah’s guidance; the verse directs people to seek that guidance and follow the truth made evident to them.

translation: They say, “We believe in Allah and the Messenger, and we obey.” Then a group of them turns away after that. Such people are not believers.
interpretation: The verse teaches that faith is not established by words alone: turning away from the Messenger’s guidance after professing belief exposes a lack of sincere submission.

translation: And when they are called to Allah and His Messenger so that he may judge between them, a group of them turns away.
interpretation: Their refusal reveals that their claim to faith is not wholehearted: they accept divine judgment only when it suits them, but turn away when they fear it will go against their interests.

translation: But if the judgment is in their favor, they come to him submissively.
interpretation: The verse exposes the inconsistency of those who accept the Messenger’s judgment only when they expect it to benefit them, revealing that their obedience is driven by self-interest rather than sincere faith.

translation: Is there sickness in their hearts, or have they fallen into doubt, or do they fear that Allah and His Messenger will deal unjustly with them? Rather, they themselves are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse challenges those who turn away from the judgment of Allah and His Messenger: their refusal cannot be blamed on unfairness in that judgment. It stems instead from inner corruption or doubt, and the injustice lies in their own rejection of what is right.

translation: The believers’ only response, when they are called to Allah and His Messenger so that he may judge between them, is to say, “We hear and we obey.” They are the ones who will succeed.
interpretation: True faith is shown by willingly accepting Allah’s guidance and the Messenger’s judgment, rather than resisting them when they conflict with personal preference. This readiness to listen and act is the path to success.

translation: Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, fears Allah, and is mindful of Him—those are the successful.
interpretation: True success comes from bringing obedience together with reverent awareness of Allah: a person honors His commands, fears falling short, and guards against what displeases Him.

translation: They swear by Allah with their strongest oaths that, if you command them, they will surely go forth. Say, “Do not swear. Obedience is what is expected.” Indeed, Allah is fully aware of what you do.
interpretation: The verse teaches that sincere obedience is shown through dependable action, not strengthened by emphatic oaths. Allah knows whether people’s professions of loyalty are genuine.

translation: Say, “Obey Allah and obey the Messenger.” If you turn away, then he is responsible only for what he has been charged with, and you are responsible for what you have been charged with. If you obey him, you will be guided. The Messenger is responsible only for conveying the message clearly.
interpretation: The verse distinguishes the Messenger’s duty from the people’s: he must convey God’s message plainly, while each person is accountable for responding to it. The Messenger’s clear guidance is the path to right guidance, but those who reject it bear the consequences of their own choice.

translation: Allah has promised those among you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will surely grant them succession in the land, as He granted it to those before them; that He will firmly establish for them the religion He has approved for them; and that He will surely replace their fear with security. They worship Me, associating nothing with Me. And whoever disbelieves after that—it is they who are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: The promise of authority, religious stability, and security is bound to sincere faith and righteous conduct, with worship devoted to God alone. These blessings are not grounds for complacency: turning away from faith after receiving them is a grave breach of that trust.

translation: Establish prayer, give zakah, and obey the Messenger so that you may receive mercy.
interpretation: The verse presents divine mercy as something to seek through a life shaped by worship, care for others, and faithful obedience to the Messenger—not as something people can claim while disregarding these responsibilities.

translation: Do not think that those who disbelieve can escape God on earth. Their refuge is the Fire—what a wretched destination.
interpretation: The verse warns against mistaking worldly strength or apparent freedom from consequences for lasting security: no one can thwart God’s judgment, and rejection of the truth ultimately brings accountability.

translation: O you who believe, let those whom your right hands possess and those among you who have not reached puberty ask your permission at three times: before the dawn prayer, when you lay aside your garments at midday, and after the night prayer. These are three times of privacy for you. There is no blame on you or on them at other times, for they move about among you, serving one another. Thus Allah makes His signs clear to you; and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: The verse establishes respect for privacy as part of everyday family life. It singles out times when people are especially likely to be undressed or resting, teaching that even those who live and move freely within a household should seek permission before entering then. Its allowance at other times recognizes ordinary household needs, while its closing words ground these boundaries in God’s knowledge and wisdom.

translation: When the children among you reach puberty, let them seek permission, just as those before them have sought permission. Thus Allah makes His revelations clear to you; Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: Reaching puberty brings a new responsibility: young people should respect the privacy of others by asking permission before entering, just as adults do. The verse presents this etiquette as guidance grounded in Allah’s knowledge and wisdom.

translation: As for elderly women who no longer expect to marry, there is no blame on them if they set aside their outer garments, provided they do not display adornment. But to refrain is better for them. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: The verse grants older women who are no longer seeking marriage a limited ease in their outer dress, while still requiring them not to display adornment. It presents modest restraint as the better course, and reminds that God knows and hears all.

translation: There is no blame upon the blind, no blame upon the lame, and no blame upon the sick, nor upon yourselves for eating from your own homes, or the homes of your fathers, mothers, brothers, sisters, paternal uncles, paternal aunts, maternal uncles, maternal aunts, or those whose keys you possess, or your friends. There is no blame upon you whether you eat together or separately. When you enter homes, greet one another with a greeting from Allah, blessed and good. Thus Allah makes His signs clear to you, so that you may understand.
interpretation: The verse cultivates a community in which ordinary acts of hospitality are not made sources of shame or needless anxiety. It recognizes differing circumstances, encourages trust and ease among people bound by kinship and friendship, and makes the greeting upon entering a home a prayer for peace and blessing—so that social life is marked by care rather than burden.

translation: The believers are only those who believe in Allah and His Messenger and, when they are with him in a matter requiring collective action, do not leave until they have asked his permission. Those who ask you for permission are the ones who believe in Allah and His Messenger. So when they ask your permission to attend to some of their affairs, grant permission to whoever you wish among them, and ask Allah to forgive them. Surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse teaches that faith is reflected in considerate conduct: when a community is gathered for an important shared responsibility, a believer should not leave without permission, since doing so respects the leader and the needs of the group. It also recognizes that people may have genuine personal obligations, entrusting the decision to the Prophet’s judgment while encouraging compassion and prayer for those who depart.

translation: Do not treat the Messenger’s call among you as you treat one another’s calls. Allah knows those of you who slip away secretly. So let those who oppose his command beware lest a trial befall them or a painful punishment strike them.
interpretation: The Messenger’s call carries the authority of his divinely appointed mission, so it must be met with reverence and obedience, not treated as an ordinary request that one may disregard or evade. Those who turn away from his command should fear the spiritual and worldly consequences of doing so.

translation: Indeed, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. He surely knows the state you are in. And on the Day they are returned to Him, He will inform them of what they did. And Allah knows all things.
interpretation: Because all creation belongs to Allah, nothing about people’s outward actions or inner state is hidden from Him. Their return to Him means every deed will be made known and accounted for, so this verse calls people to live with awareness of His knowledge and judgment.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His servant, so that he may be a warner to all worlds.
interpretation: The verse presents the Qur’an as the divine معيار by which truth is distinguished from falsehood, and Muhammad ﷺ as entrusted with conveying its warning beyond any single people or place. Calling God “Blessed” underscores that the revelation and its guidance flow from His abundant goodness.

translation: He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth; He has taken no son and has no partner in dominion. He created everything and determined it with precise measure.
interpretation: The verse presents God’s authority as wholly independent and unmatched: nothing shares in His rule, and nothing exists outside His creative will and measure. It therefore directs the listener to understand the order and limits of creation as signs of divine wisdom, not as powers belonging to a son or partner.

translation: Yet they have taken gods besides Him that create nothing, while they themselves are created; they have no power to bring harm or benefit upon themselves, nor any power over death, life, or resurrection.
interpretation: The verse exposes the contradiction in worshiping beings that are themselves created and powerless: they cannot be true gods or share in the authority that belongs to God alone.

translation: Those who disbelieve say, “This is nothing but a fabrication he has invented, and other people have helped him with it.” They have indeed come with injustice and falsehood.
interpretation: The verse exposes the baselessness of the disbelievers’ claim that the Qur’an was invented with human assistance. Their accusation is a grave injustice and a deliberate falsehood against the Messenger and the revelation he conveyed.

translation: And they say, “Tales of the ancients—he has had them written down, and they are dictated to him morning and evening.”
interpretation: This portrays the opponents’ attempt to dismiss the Qur’an by claiming that the Prophet ﷺ borrowed old stories and had them repeatedly recited to him. Their accusation reframes revelation as human fabrication, but the verse exposes it as an allegation rather than establishing it as fact.

translation: Say, “It was sent down by the One who knows the secrets of the heavens and the earth. Indeed, He is ever Forgiving, Merciful.”
interpretation: The verse grounds the Qur’an’s authority in God’s complete knowledge: its source knows what is hidden throughout creation, far beyond human reach. His forgiveness and mercy also leave the door open for those who turn to Him.

translation: And they say, “What sort of messenger is this? He eats food and walks through the markets. Why was an angel not sent down to him to be a warner alongside him?”
interpretation: Their objection assumes that a true messenger must be unlike ordinary human beings. The verse challenges that assumption: eating and living among people do not undermine a messenger’s divine mission; they allow him to guide people within the realities of their own lives.

translation: “Or why has no treasure been bestowed upon him, or why does he not have a garden from which he eats?” And the wrongdoers said, “You follow none but a bewitched man.”
interpretation: The opponents judge the truth of a messenger by worldly wealth and status, demanding signs that suit their expectations. When he does not meet those demands, they resort to calling him bewitched—an accusation meant to discredit his message rather than engage with it.

translation: انظر كيف يضربون لك الأمثال، فضلّوا فلا يستطيعون سبيلاً.
interpretation: يكشف الله للنبي ﷺ أن معارضيه يختلقون له أوصافاً متناقضة ليصرفوا الناس عن دعوته؛ وقد أضلّهم هذا العناد، فلم يعودوا يهتدون إلى طريق الحق.

translation: Blessed is He who, if He wills, can grant you something better than that: gardens beneath which rivers flow, and make palaces for you.
interpretation: The verse affirms that God’s power and generosity are not limited by what people demand or imagine: He can grant far greater blessings, while their granting rests entirely on His will.

translation: Rather, they have denied the Hour, and We have prepared a blazing Fire for whoever denies the Hour.
interpretation: Denial of the Resurrection is not merely a mistaken belief; it rejects the accountability that gives human choices their ultimate consequence. The verse warns that refusing this reality does not make it disappear, but leaves the denier facing the punishment prepared for that rejection.

translation: When it sees them from a distant place, they will hear its fury and roaring.
interpretation: The verse portrays Hell as if it were alive and already reacting to the condemned, emphasizing the terror of their fate and the severity of the punishment awaiting them.

translation: And when they are thrown into a cramped place within it, bound together, they will cry out there for destruction.
interpretation: Their confinement and bonds portray utter helplessness: faced with punishment they cannot escape, they will long for annihilation as relief.

translation: “Do not call out today for one destruction; call out for many destructions.”
interpretation: The words portray the despair of those facing punishment: a single cry for ruin cannot express the severity of their anguish, so they are told to call for ruin again and again. Yet their cries offer no escape from what they face.

translation: Say, “Is that better, or the Garden of Eternity promised to the mindful of God? It will be their reward and their final abode.”
interpretation: The verse invites a comparison that exposes the fleeting nature of worldly gains beside the lasting reward God has prepared for those who remain mindful of Him.

translation: There they will have whatever they wish, forever. This is a promise from your Lord, one to be sought.
interpretation: The verse portrays the lasting generosity of Paradise: its people will find their desires fulfilled without end. This is a promise God has made, and one believers may earnestly ask Him to grant.

translation: And on the Day He gathers them together with those they worship besides Allah, He will say, “Was it you who led these servants of Mine astray, or did they themselves stray from the path?”
interpretation: The verse depicts a scene of divine judgment in which those worshipped besides Allah are confronted about the people who followed them. The question exposes the followers’ misguidance and makes clear that their choices and responsibility will be brought into the open before Allah.

translation: They will say, “Glory be to You! It was not right for us to take protectors besides You. But You let them and their forefathers enjoy life until they forgot the Reminder and became a people doomed to ruin.”
interpretation: Those invoked besides God will declare themselves innocent of having claimed divine authority or invited people to worship them. The verse points to how prolonged worldly ease can distract people from divine guidance, until heedlessness hardens into ruin.

translation: They have denied what you claim, so you can neither avert the punishment nor help yourselves. Whoever among you does wrong, We will make him taste a great punishment.
interpretation: Those whom the idolaters called upon will disown their claims, leaving them powerless before God’s judgment. The verse warns that no false object of worship can shield anyone from the consequences of wrongdoing.

translation: We did not send before you any messengers except that they ate food and walked in the markets. And We made some of you a trial for others: will you be patient? And your Lord is ever Seeing.
interpretation: The messengers’ ordinary human needs and daily lives do not diminish their divine mission; rather, they show that God guides people through human messengers. Differences in circumstance and status can test how people respond—with patience, humility, and faith—and nothing in those responses is hidden from God.

translation: Those who do not expect to meet Us say, “Why have angels not been sent down to us, or why do we not see our Lord?” They have indeed grown arrogant within themselves and overstepped all bounds.
interpretation: Their demand to see God or have angels sent down is presented as a display of pride, not a sincere search for guidance. By insisting that revelation come on their terms, they have crossed the limits of humility before God.

translation: The day they see the angels, there will be no good news that day for the guilty; and they will say, “A forbidden refuge!”
interpretation: When the guilty encounter the angels at judgment, they will receive no glad tidings. Their cry, “A forbidden refuge,” expresses a desperate attempt to seek protection from what is coming, but no refuge will avail them.

translation: And We shall turn to whatever deeds they have done and make them scattered dust.
interpretation: The verse warns that deeds which lack faith and sincerity toward God will not bring their doers lasting reward in the Hereafter; they will be rendered as insubstantial and dispersed as dust.

translation: The companions of Paradise that Day will have a better abode and a more beautiful place of rest.
interpretation: The verse reassures the believers that the lasting comfort and honor God grants in the Hereafter far surpass any ease or status found in worldly life.

translation: And [warn them of] the Day when the heaven will split open with clouds, and the angels will be sent down in a great descent.
interpretation: The verse portrays the Day of Judgment as a moment when the familiar order of the heavens is overturned and the angels descend by God’s command. This immense scene signals the arrival of divine judgment and the certainty that all people will stand before God.

translation: The true dominion on that Day belongs to the Most Merciful, and it will be a difficult day for the disbelievers.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, every worldly claim to power will fall away, and God’s just authority will be unmistakable; those who rejected Him will face the consequence of that rejection.

translation: And the Day the wrongdoer will bite his hands, saying, “If only I had taken a path with the Messenger!”
interpretation: The verse portrays the anguish of someone who realizes too late that rejecting the Messenger’s guidance led them away from salvation. Their biting their hands expresses profound regret over a choice that cannot now be undone.

translation: “Woe to me! If only I had not taken so-and-so as a close friend.”
interpretation: The speaker’s anguish reflects the way a trusted companion can influence someone toward ruin, leaving them to regret that closeness when its consequences become clear.

translation: “He led me away from the Reminder after it had come to me, and Satan is ever a betrayer of mankind.”
interpretation: The speaker realizes too late that he allowed misleading influence to turn him from God’s guidance. Satan may entice a person toward rejection, but when the consequences arrive, he abandons them; the verse warns against trusting influences that draw one away from the truth.

translation: And the Messenger said, “My Lord, indeed my people have abandoned this Qur’an.”
interpretation: The verse warns that a community may have the Qur’an yet still abandon it by turning away from its guidance and failing to live by it.

translation: Thus We have made for every prophet an enemy from among the criminals; and your Lord is sufficient as a Guide and Helper.
interpretation: The opposition faced by prophets does not mean they have been abandoned. It is part of the struggle against wrongdoing, while God’s guidance and support are enough to sustain them and carry out their mission.

translation: Those who disbelieve say, “Why was the Qur’an not sent down to him all at once?” Thus We revealed it gradually to strengthen your heart, and We recited it in measured, clear stages.
interpretation: The Qur’an’s gradual revelation was a deliberate mercy: its ongoing guidance and reassurance strengthened the Prophet as he faced opposition, while allowing its teachings to be received and understood over time.

translation: They do not bring you any argument or example without Our bringing you the truth and the finest explanation.
interpretation: The verse reassures the Prophet that every challenge raised against his message will be met with truth and clear clarification from God, strengthening him against those who seek to confuse or discredit it.

translation: Those who are gathered on their faces toward Hell—those are worst in station and farthest astray from the way.
interpretation: Being driven to Hell on their faces portrays the utter humiliation and helplessness of those who rejected guidance. Their terrible destination reveals how far they strayed from the path that leads to salvation.

translation: And We certainly gave Moses the Scripture and appointed his brother Aaron as a minister alongside him.
interpretation: The verse shows that carrying out a prophetic mission may require trusted support: Aaron was appointed to strengthen Moses and assist him in fulfilling the responsibility of conveying God’s guidance.

translation: So We said, “Go both of you to the people who denied Our signs.” Then We utterly destroyed them.
interpretation: The verse presents the people’s destruction as the consequence of their persistent denial of God’s signs. The emphatic wording underscores that their end was complete and decisive.

translation: And the people of Noah, when they denied the messengers, We drowned them and made them a sign for mankind; and We have prepared for the wrongdoers a painful punishment.
interpretation: Though Noah was the messenger sent to them, their rejection of him was a rejection of the messengers’ shared call to worship God. Their fate stands as a warning that persistent injustice and denial bring consequences, while God’s punishment for the wrongdoers is not confined to this world.

translation: And [We destroyed] ʿĀd, Thamūd, the people of the Well, and many generations in between.
interpretation: The mention of both well-known peoples and countless others points to a recurring lesson: no community is beyond accountability, and the fate of earlier nations is a warning to those who follow.

translation: To each of them We presented examples, and each We utterly destroyed.
interpretation: God made the lessons clear to every people before them, yet they persisted in rejection; their complete destruction shows the consequence of refusing clear warnings.

translation: They have indeed passed by the town upon which a terrible rain was poured. Have they not seen it? Rather, they do not expect to be raised again.
interpretation: The ruins of the town—understood as the town of Lot—stand as a warning, but merely seeing evidence of past destruction does not awaken people who refuse to reckon with resurrection and accountability.

translation: When they see you, they make you the object of nothing but ridicule, saying, “Is this the one whom Allah has sent as a messenger?”
interpretation: Their derision reflects their arrogance and refusal to recognize the truth: instead of considering the Prophet’s message sincerely, they try to discredit him by mocking the very fact that Allah chose him as a messenger.

translation: He nearly led us away from our gods, had we not remained steadfast to them. And they will know, when they see the punishment, who is farther astray.
interpretation: Their claim that steadfastness kept them from being misled is self-deception: remaining devoted to false gods does not make them rightly guided. When they face the punishment, they will recognize that rejecting the truth—not the Prophet’s call—was the greater error.

translation: Have you considered the one who has taken his own desire as his god? Are you then to be his guardian?
interpretation: The verse describes someone who lets personal desire govern what he accepts and does, placing it above divine guidance. The Prophet is not charged with controlling such a person or bearing responsibility for his choices; his role is to convey the message.

translation: Or do you think that most of them hear or understand? They are only like cattle—rather, they are even further astray from the way.
interpretation: The verse describes people who have been given the capacity to hear and reason but do not use it to recognize guidance. Their heedlessness is worse than that of animals, which simply follow their instincts, because these people turn away despite having the ability to understand and choose the right path.

translation: Have you not seen how your Lord extends the shade? Had He willed, He could have made it still; then We made the sun a guide to it.
interpretation: The changing shade points to the precision of God’s ordering: even an ordinary, shifting feature of the world follows a pattern made discernible through the sun, and could have been otherwise by His will.

translation: Then We draw it back toward Us, little by little.
interpretation: The shadow’s gradual retreat unfolds by God’s command, revealing His measured and continuing control over the changes of the natural world.

translation: And He is the One who made the night a covering for you, sleep a rest, and the day a time of rising.
interpretation: The verse points to the care and wisdom in the rhythm God has established: night offers shelter and rest, while daylight renews people for their activities. These ordinary gifts invite recognition of the One who provides both repose and renewed strength.

translation: He is the One who sends the winds as glad tidings before His mercy, and We send down from the sky purifying water.
interpretation: The verse presents rain as a mercy preceded by signs of hope: the winds announce its coming, and the water itself is made pure and cleansing. It invites reflection on the care and generosity through which God provides life and renewal.

translation: So that We may bring a lifeless land to life through it, and provide drink from it to many of the livestock and people We have created.
interpretation: The rain is presented as a sign of God’s mercy and sustaining care: it revives what seemed barren and provides nourishment for both animals and people.

translation: We have certainly distributed it among them so that they might take heed, but most people insist on nothing but ingratitude.
interpretation: God apportions rain among people in different ways as a sign meant to awaken reflection and gratitude. Yet many turn away from that reminder and respond to His provision with ingratitude.

translation: Had We willed, We could have sent a warner to every town.
interpretation: The verse teaches that God’s choice to send one messenger with a warning for all people is deliberate; the Prophet is entrusted with a universal mission, and those who hear his message are responsible for responding to it.

translation: So do not obey the disbelievers, but strive against them with it in a great striving.
interpretation: The verse calls the Prophet to remain steadfast in his message and to resist opposition through the Qur’an—its guidance, arguments, and recitation—rather than yielding to pressure. It presents patient, principled proclamation as a profound form of striving.

translation: And He is the One who set the two bodies of water flowing: one fresh and sweet, the other salty and bitter; and He placed between them a barrier and an impassable boundary.
interpretation: Their nearness without losing their distinct qualities points to God’s ordering of creation: even where things meet, His measure preserves their appointed limits.

translation: And it is He who created a human being from water, then made him kin by lineage and by marriage. And your Lord is ever powerful.
interpretation: Human life and the bonds that shape human society—through ancestry and marriage—are part of God’s deliberate ordering. Their emergence from a simple beginning points to His power to bring forth complex forms of life and relationship.

translation: They worship besides Allah that which can neither benefit them nor harm them. And the disbeliever is ever an ally against his Lord.
interpretation: The verse condemns turning to powerless objects of worship and portrays disbelief as taking the side of what opposes God, rather than submitting to the One who alone holds power over benefit and harm.

translation: We have sent you only as a bearer of good news and a warner.
interpretation: The verse clarifies that the Prophet’s mission is to convey God’s message: to give hope through the promise of divine mercy and reward, and to warn of the consequences of rejecting guidance. Guidance is presented clearly, without coercion.

translation: Say, “I ask no reward from you for this, except that whoever wishes may take a way to his Lord.”
interpretation: The Prophet seeks no personal payment for conveying the message; what he calls people to is that they freely choose faith and obedience as a path toward God.

translation: And rely upon the Ever-Living, who does not die, and glorify Him with praise. Sufficient is He as the One fully aware of the sins of His servants.
interpretation: Because all created things pass away, true reliance belongs to God alone, whose life is everlasting. Glorifying Him with praise joins trust with worship, while His complete awareness of every servant’s deeds assures that no wrongdoing is hidden from Him.

translation: He is the One who created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them in six days, then established Himself over the Throne—the Most Merciful. So ask about Him one who is well-informed.
interpretation: The verse directs people to recognize the Creator’s supreme authority and mercy, and to seek reliable knowledge about Him from one who truly knows.

translation: When they are told, “Prostrate to the Most Merciful,” they say, “And what is the Most Merciful? Are we to prostrate to what you command us?” And it only increases their aversion.
interpretation: Their question is not a sincere search for understanding but a refusal to humble themselves before God. By dismissing the name “the Most Merciful” and resisting the command, they turn guidance into a reason for even greater rejection.

translation: Blessed is He who placed constellations in the sky, and placed in it a radiant lamp and a luminous moon.
interpretation: The verse directs attention to the ordered beauty of the heavens as a sign of God’s greatness: the constellations, the sun that shines like a lamp, and the moon that lights the night all point to His power and wisdom.

translation: He is the One who made the night and the day succeed one another, for whoever wishes to take heed or to be grateful.
interpretation: The succession of night and day gives people recurring opportunities: if they overlooked a reminder in one, they may reflect in the next, and through the blessings each brings they may grow in gratitude to God.

translation: The servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth humbly, and when ignorant people address them, they respond with words of peace.
interpretation: True devotion to God is reflected in a gentle, unarrogant way of life and in self-control when faced with provocation. Rather than answering foolishness with hostility, believers preserve their dignity and choose a peaceful response.

translation: And those who spend the night before their Lord, prostrating and standing.
interpretation: This describes a devotion rooted in humility and sincerity: even in the quiet of night, they turn to God in worship, seeking closeness to Him rather than recognition from others.

translation: And those who say, “Our Lord, turn away from us the punishment of Hell. Indeed, its punishment is ever-clinging.”
interpretation: Their prayer reflects humility and a constant awareness of the grave, enduring nature of Hell’s punishment, leading them to seek Allah’s protection from it.

translation: Indeed, it is an evil place to settle and reside.
interpretation: The verse portrays Hell as a profoundly dreadful and lasting abode, warning that its inhabitants will find no comfort or refuge there.

translation: And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor miserly, but maintain a balanced course between the two.
interpretation: This teaches that faithful spending is marked by balance: one should use wealth generously and responsibly without wasting it, while also avoiding stinginess and neglect of legitimate needs.

translation: And those who do not call upon any other god alongside Allah, nor take a life that Allah has forbidden except by right, nor commit adultery. Whoever does that will face its penalty.
interpretation: The verse presents these as grave violations of faith and human dignity. “Except by right” refers to a legitimate ground established by divine law, not personal judgment or vengeance; “its penalty” points to the serious consequence awaiting those who commit such acts.

translation: The punishment will be multiplied for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will remain there in disgrace.
interpretation: The verse warns that knowingly persisting in grave wrongdoing brings not only severe punishment but lasting humiliation before God; its force is a call to turn back from such deeds before the final judgment.

translation: Except those who repent, believe, and do righteous deeds: for them, Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds. Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: The verse offers hope to those who have sinned: sincere repentance, renewed faith, and a life of righteous action can transform their past through Allah’s mercy. Their wrongdoing need not define their future, for Allah forgives and rewards those who truly turn back to Him.

translation: And whoever repents and does righteous deeds has truly turned back to Allah in repentance.
interpretation: True repentance is more than regret or words: it is a sincere return to God, shown by a changed course of life and righteous action.

translation: And those who do not bear false witness, and when they pass by idle talk, they pass by with dignity.
interpretation: Their integrity is shown not only in refusing to take part in falsehood, but also in meeting pointless or degrading speech without being drawn into it. They preserve their dignity through restraint rather than answering every provocation.

translation: And those who, when reminded of the signs of their Lord, do not fall upon them deaf and blind.
interpretation: The verse praises those who meet divine guidance with attentive minds and open hearts. They do not merely hear the signs without understanding or turn away from their meaning; they reflect on them and respond with insight.

translation: And those who say, “Our Lord, grant us in our spouses and offspring a joy to our eyes, and make us examples for the mindful of You.”
interpretation: They ask that their family life be a source of deep joy through faith and goodness, and that they themselves become models of righteousness whom others can follow.

translation: Those will be rewarded with the lofty chambers for their patience, and they will be welcomed there with greetings and peace.
interpretation: Their steadfastness in faith—through obedience, resisting wrongdoing, and enduring hardship—earns them an honored place in Paradise, where they are received with dignity and lasting peace.

translation: Abiding therein—excellent as a place of settlement and residence.
interpretation: The phrase portrays Paradise as an enduring, supremely good home: its people remain there, finding lasting rest and a fitting place to dwell.

translation: Say, “What concern would my Lord have for you were it not for your supplication?” Yet you have denied the truth, so the consequence will inevitably come upon you.
interpretation: God has no need of people; their turning to Him in prayer and worship is what gives their lives significance in relation to Him. But the addressees have rejected the truth, and they cannot escape the consequence of that rejection.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Ṭā Sīn Mīm.
interpretation: The basmala begins by invoking Allah’s name and mercy. Ṭā Sīn Mīm are among the Qur’an’s disjointed opening letters; their precise intended meaning is not definitively known, so they are recited as revealed without assigning them a certain interpretation.

translation: These are the verses of the clear Book.
interpretation: Describing the Book as clear signals that what follows is guidance whose message makes the truth plain to those who reflect on it.

translation: Perhaps you will grieve yourself to death because they do not believe.
interpretation: The verse acknowledges the Prophet’s profound concern for those who reject the message, while gently consoling him: he is to convey the truth, but should not let their refusal consume him.

translation: If We willed, We could send down upon them a sign from heaven, before which their necks would remain humbled.
interpretation: God is fully able to compel people into submission through an overwhelming sign, but their faith would then be forced rather than freely chosen. The verse thus underscores that their rejection is not due to any lack of divine power.

translation: Whenever a fresh reminder comes to them from the Most Merciful, they turn away from it.
interpretation: The verse portrays people repeatedly turning aside from divine guidance: each new reminder is an opportunity to reflect and return to God, yet they persist in refusing to heed it.

translation: They have indeed denied the truth, so news of what they used to mock will soon come to them.
interpretation: Their denial and ridicule cannot undo the truth; they will soon face the reality and consequences of what they mocked.

translation: Have they not looked at the earth and seen how many noble pairs We have caused to grow in it?
interpretation: The verse calls people to reflect on the earth’s abundant and varied growth: its beauty and benefit point to God’s power and wisdom, and to His ability to bring life forth again.

translation: Indeed, in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers.
interpretation: The events being described are clear evidence of God’s power and truth, yet many people still refused to believe; seeing a sign does not by itself guarantee faith.

translation: And indeed, your Lord is the Almighty, the Merciful.
interpretation: God’s unmatched power is joined with mercy: He can overcome all opposition, yet His dealings with His servants are marked by compassion.

translation: And when your Lord called Moses, saying, “Go to the wrongdoing people.”
interpretation: The verse portrays Moses’ mission as a direct divine commission, underscoring that confronting injustice is a responsibility entrusted by God, even when the task is difficult.

translation: To the people of Pharaoh: Will they not be mindful of God?
interpretation: The question is a rebuke and a call to turn from wrongdoing: Pharaoh’s people are being urged to recognize their duty to God and live with reverence for Him.

translation: He said, “My Lord, I fear that they will deny me.”
interpretation: Moses’ fear reflects his awareness of the resistance he may face, not hesitation to obey God. It reveals the human vulnerability of a prophet confronting a powerful people and the need for divine reassurance as he undertakes his mission.

translation: My chest feels constricted, and my tongue does not speak freely, so send for Aaron.
interpretation: Moses is asking God to appoint Aaron as his helper, so that Aaron’s eloquence can support him in conveying the message to Pharaoh.

translation: And they hold me guilty of a deed, so I fear they may kill me.
interpretation: Moses is explaining that Pharaoh’s people consider him responsible for the Egyptian’s death, and he fears they will use it as grounds to kill him.

translation: He said, “No! Go, both of you, with Our signs. Indeed, We are with you, listening.”
interpretation: God reassures Moses and Aaron that their fear will not prevent them from carrying out their mission: they are to proceed with His signs, confident that He is present with them and fully attentive to what unfolds.

translation: So go to Pharaoh and say, “Indeed, we are messengers of the Lord of all worlds.”
interpretation: Moses and Aaron are to speak not on their own authority, but as bearers of a message from the Lord whose authority extends over all creation—including Pharaoh.

translation: That you send the Children of Israel with us.
interpretation: This is a demand for the Israelites’ release from Pharaoh’s oppression, conveying that their freedom is part of the divine mission entrusted to Moses and Aaron.

translation: He said, “Did we not bring you up among us as a child, and did you spend among us many years of your life?”
interpretation: Pharaoh appeals to the care and upbringing Moses received in his household to suggest that Moses owes him loyalty, using that past relationship to challenge Moses’ authority and his mission.

translation: “And you committed the deed you committed, and you were among the ungrateful.”
interpretation: Pharaoh invokes Moses’ past deed—the killing of an Egyptian—and portrays him as ungrateful for having been raised in Pharaoh’s household. Here, “ungrateful” reflects Pharaoh’s accusation about Moses’ supposed ingratitude, rather than necessarily referring to disbelief in God.

translation: He said, “I did it then, when I was among those who were unaware.”
interpretation: Moses acknowledges the act but places it in its proper context: it happened before his prophethood, when he did not yet know the right course in that situation. His words describe being unaware, not deliberately rejecting guidance.

translation: So I fled from you when I feared you; then my Lord granted me sound judgment and made me one of the messengers.
interpretation: Moses points out that his earlier flight did not define his standing: God granted him wisdom and prophethood, so his authority comes from God rather than Pharaoh.

translation: “And is this a favor you hold over me—that you enslaved the Children of Israel?”
interpretation: Moses rejects Pharaoh’s claim that raising him in the palace was a favor that should silence him. He points out that Pharaoh’s treatment of him cannot be separated from the oppression Pharaoh inflicted on the Children of Israel.

translation: Pharaoh said, “And what is the Lord of all worlds?”
interpretation: Pharaoh’s question is a challenge: he demands that Moses define the Lord of all creation, as though seeking to reduce the divine reality to something he can question or dismiss.

translation: He said, “He is the Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them, if you are certain.”
interpretation: Moses points beyond Pharaoh’s claims to the true source of all authority: the One who sustains the entire universe. Genuine certainty about this should lead people to acknowledge God’s lordship rather than attribute ultimate power to anyone else.

translation: He said to those around him, “Do you not hear?”
interpretation: Pharaoh appeals to his entourage to ridicule Moses’s words and win their approval, rather than answer the truth of what Moses has said.

translation: He said, “Your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers of old.”
interpretation: Moses points out that the Lord he speaks of is not an abstract or unfamiliar power: He is the one who sustains those listening and their ancestors. This challenges Pharaoh’s claim to ultimate authority by directing them to the Lord who has always held authority over them.

translation: He said, “Indeed, your messenger who was sent to you is surely mad.”
interpretation: Unable to answer Moses’ message directly, Pharaoh calls him mad to discredit him before the people and turn them away from what he has brought.

translation: He said, “The Lord of the east and the west and all that is between them, if you would use your reason.”
interpretation: Moses points to God’s lordship over the whole world—east, west, and everything between—as evidence that no ruler can claim divine authority. His appeal to reason challenges Pharaoh to recognize the truth evident in creation.

translation: He said, “If you take any god other than me, I will surely make you one of the imprisoned.”
interpretation: Pharaoh responds to Moses’ call to worship God alone with a threat, revealing how tyranny uses force to silence the truth when it cannot answer it.

translation: He said, “Even if I bring you something clear?”
interpretation: Moses responds to Pharaoh’s threat by asking whether he would still reject him if he presented unmistakable proof, exposing that Pharaoh’s opposition may persist even in the face of clear evidence.

translation: He said, “Then bring it, if you are truthful.”
interpretation: The speaker challenges the claim by demanding tangible proof, making the truth of the claim the test of whether the promised sign can be produced.

translation: Then he cast down his staff, and behold, it was a manifest serpent.
interpretation: The sudden transformation of Moses’ staff into a clearly visible serpent was a decisive sign of God’s power and support, distinguishing his message from mere illusion.

translation: He drew out his hand, and behold, it was white before the onlookers.
interpretation: The sudden whiteness of Moses’ hand was a miraculous sign, made visible to those present as evidence that his mission was supported by God.

translation: He said to the chiefs around him, “This is indeed a skilled magician.”
interpretation: By calling him a skilled magician, the speaker seeks to discredit Moses’ signs as human trickery and influence those in power to reject his message.

translation: He wants to drive you out of your land by his magic, so what do you advise?
interpretation: Pharaoh presents Moses’ message as a threat to the people’s security, using fear of losing their homeland to rally his advisers against him. The verse exposes how those in power can distort a call to truth into a political danger in order to preserve their authority.

translation: They said, “Keep him and his brother waiting, and send gatherers into the cities.”
interpretation: Pharaoh’s advisers urged him to delay confronting Moses and Aaron while agents gathered people from across the cities—preparing, in the surrounding context, to assemble skilled magicians for a public contest.

translation: They will bring you every masterful sorcerer.
interpretation: The phrase conveys confidence in assembling the most accomplished practitioners of sorcery, setting human skill against the sign Moses will show.

translation: So the magicians were gathered for an appointment on a well-known day.
interpretation: The contest was set for a fixed, publicly known time, so the encounter would take place before people rather than in secret.

translation: And it was said to the people, “Will you gather?”
interpretation: The verse depicts a public summons for people to assemble and witness what was about to take place, making the coming encounter a matter of public attention.

translation: Perhaps we will follow the magicians if they are the victors.
interpretation: The statement reflects an allegiance based on appearances: the people are prepared to side with whoever seems to win, rather than judge the truth independently.

translation: When the magicians came, they said to Pharaoh, “Will we surely have a reward if we are the ones who prevail?”
interpretation: Their question shows that they were seeking Pharaoh’s promised reward before taking part, and that their contest was tied to worldly gain as well as the hope of defeating Moses.

translation: He said, “Yes—and you will indeed be among those brought near.”
interpretation: Pharaoh promises the magicians honor and privileged status if they prevail, using the prospect of royal favor to strengthen their loyalty and encourage them to confront Moses.

translation: Moses said to them, “Throw whatever you are going to throw.”
interpretation: Moses lets them display their magic first, confident that the truth will expose the limits of their illusion.

translation: So they cast down their ropes and staffs, and said, “By Pharaoh’s might, we will surely be the victors.”
interpretation: Their oath reveals that they placed their confidence in Pharaoh’s power and their own craft, declaring victory before the contest had begun. The verse sets their boastful certainty against the truth that would soon be made clear.

translation: So Moses cast down his staff, and behold, it swallowed up what they had fabricated.
interpretation: The sign makes clear that deception cannot withstand the truth: what the magicians had made appear real is undone by God’s power, affirming His support for Moses.

translation: Then the magicians fell down, prostrating.
interpretation: Overcome by the truth they recognized, the magicians surrendered to God in humble prostration.

translation: They said, “We believe in the Lord of all worlds.”
interpretation: Their words express recognition that ultimate authority belongs to God alone, whose lordship extends over all creation.

translation: The Lord of Moses and Aaron.
interpretation: This identifies God as the one who sustains and governs Moses and Aaron, affirming that their mission and authority come from Him.

translation: He said, “You have believed in him before I gave you permission? Surely he is your chief, who taught you magic. You will soon know. I will surely cut off your hands and feet on opposite sides, then crucify you all.”
interpretation: The threat reveals Pharaoh’s attempt to preserve his authority by recasting sincere belief as a plot and using violence to intimidate others. His words expose how power can answer conviction not with evidence, but with accusation and coercion.

translation: They said, “No harm; indeed, we are returning to our Lord.”
interpretation: Their faith has made the ruler’s threat of punishment seem insignificant: whatever happens to them in this life, they are certain they will return to God, whose judgment and reward matter more than worldly suffering.

translation: Indeed, we hope that our Lord will forgive us our sins, since we were the first of the believers.
interpretation: They express sincere hope in God’s forgiveness after turning to faith, trusting that their prompt acceptance of the truth will not make them presumptuous but will deepen their repentance and reliance on His mercy.

translation: And We revealed to Moses: “Set out by night with My servants; indeed, you will be pursued.”
interpretation: The command to leave by night reflects God’s deliberate guidance of Moses and his people at a moment of danger. Though their pursuers would follow, the revelation assures Moses that their escape unfolds under divine direction, not beyond it.

translation: So Pharaoh sent gatherers throughout the cities.
interpretation: The verse portrays Pharaoh using his authority to mobilize people across the land, revealing how urgently he sought to confront Moses and suppress the challenge to his rule.

translation: Indeed, these are but a small band.
interpretation: Pharaoh speaks with contempt, treating the group’s small numbers as proof that they pose no serious threat.

translation: And they are indeed enraging us.
interpretation: Pharaoh portrays their departure as a deliberate provocation, framing it as an affront to his authority and people.

translation: And indeed, we are all on our guard.
interpretation: The speaker portrays the whole group as alert and prepared, using a show of collective vigilance to rally them against what they perceive as a threat.

translation: So We brought them out of gardens and springs.
interpretation: The verse points to how worldly prosperity is not secure: by God’s decree, those who once lived amid abundance were removed from it, showing that wealth and comfort cannot protect a people from the consequences of their actions.

translation: And treasures and a noble station.
interpretation: The phrase points to the wealth and prestige they enjoyed, underscoring that neither riches nor elevated status can protect people from God’s decree.

translation: Thus We made the Children of Israel inherit them.
interpretation: The verse highlights that worldly power and possessions are ultimately subject to God’s will: what a tyrannical people believed secure could be taken from them and passed to those they had oppressed.

translation: So they pursued them at daybreak.
interpretation: The phrase conveys how swiftly the pursuers set out after them, as dawn broke.

translation: When the two groups came into sight of one another, the companions of Moses said, “We are surely going to be overtaken.”
interpretation: Their words express the fear that escape was impossible as Pharaoh’s forces drew near; the verse presents the moment of apparent defeat before Moses’ trust in God is shown.

translation: He said, “No indeed! My Lord is with me; He will guide me.”
interpretation: Moses expresses unwavering trust in God’s support and guidance, even when the danger before him seems inescapable.

translation: Then We revealed to Moses, “Strike the sea with your staff.” So it split, and each part stood like a great towering mountain.
interpretation: The verse portrays deliverance as an act of God’s power: Moses is commanded to act, while the sea’s extraordinary parting makes a way through what seemed impassable.

translation: And We brought the others near.
interpretation: The verse describes God drawing Pharaoh and his pursuing army close to the sea after Moses and his people had crossed, bringing them to the moment of their destruction.

translation: And We saved Moses and all those who were with him.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that deliverance came by God’s protection, encompassing Moses and everyone who stood with him.

translation: Then We drowned the others.
interpretation: The verse portrays the drowning of those who remained in opposition as a decisive consequence of their rejection, while those whom God had saved were spared.

translation: Indeed, in that is a sign, yet most of them would not believe.
interpretation: The sign is clear enough to invite recognition of God’s truth, but many remain unwilling to believe despite the evidence.

translation: And indeed, your Lord is the Almighty, the Merciful.
interpretation: The verse brings together God’s invincible power and boundless mercy: nothing can thwart His will, yet His dealings with creation are marked by compassion.

translation: And recite to them the account of Abraham.
interpretation: The command invites the listeners to reflect on Abraham’s example and the truth of the faith he upheld.

translation: When he said to his father and his people, “What do you worship?”
interpretation: The question invites his father and people to examine the objects of their devotion, opening the way to challenge their worship rather than accept it merely because it is inherited.

translation: They said, “We worship idols and remain devoted to them.”
interpretation: Their reply shows that their worship was sustained by steadfast attachment to the idols, rather than by offering any reason for believing the idols deserved worship.

translation: He said, “Do they hear you when you call upon them?”
interpretation: The question challenges the worshippers to consider whether their idols can even hear their prayers, exposing the emptiness of devotion to beings unable to respond.

translation: Or benefit you or harm you.
interpretation: The phrase challenges the worship of powerless beings: they cannot bring their worshippers benefit or shield them from harm, so they are not worthy of worship.

translation: They said, “Rather, we found our fathers doing the same.”
interpretation: They appeal to inherited practice as though its age made it true, revealing how unquestioned loyalty to tradition can replace honest reflection and sound evidence.

translation: He said, “Have you considered what you have been worshipping?”
interpretation: Abraham challenges his people to examine their worship critically: inherited devotion cannot make an object worthy of worship if it has no true power or divinity.

translation: You and your earliest forefathers.
interpretation: The phrase includes both the people addressed and their ancestors, underscoring that a practice does not become true or worthy of worship merely because it has been inherited across generations.

translation: Indeed, they are enemies to me, except the Lord of all worlds.
interpretation: Abraham declares that the idols his people worship are hostile to him and cannot benefit him; Allah alone, the Lord of all creation, is worthy of his devotion and trust.

translation: He who created me—it is He who guides me.
interpretation: The speaker places complete trust in God: the One who brought him into being is also the One who directs him toward what is right.

translation: And He is the One who feeds me and gives me drink.
interpretation: Abraham recognizes that his sustenance comes from God, expressing his dependence on God’s care and the gratitude owed to Him.

translation: And when I become ill, it is He who heals me.
interpretation: Ibrāhīm acknowledges that healing ultimately comes from God. This expresses trust in Him while recognizing that illness and recovery unfold by His will, often through the means He provides.

translation: And He is the One who causes me to die, then brings me to life.
interpretation: Abraham recognizes that life, death, and resurrection are in God’s hands alone, affirming his complete dependence on Him and trust in His promise of life after death.

translation: And He is the One from whom I hope that He will forgive my sin on the Day of Judgment.
interpretation: The verse expresses humble hope in God’s mercy: even while mindful of his own shortcomings, the believer turns to God for forgiveness and trusts in His compassion on the Day of Judgment.

translation: My Lord, grant me sound judgment and join me with the righteous.
interpretation: This is a prayer for wisdom to discern and follow what is right, and for a place among those whose faith and conduct are pleasing to God.

translation: And grant me a truthful, honorable mention among later generations.
interpretation: He asks God to let his legacy endure as one of truth and goodness, so that those who come after him remember him with sincere praise.

translation: And make me one of the heirs of the Garden of Bliss.
interpretation: This is a prayer for a faithful end and lasting nearness to God: to be granted Paradise is to receive, by His mercy, the enduring reward that no worldly gain can equal.

translation: And forgive my father; indeed, he was among those who went astray.
interpretation: Abraham asks God to forgive his father, acknowledging that he had strayed from the truth. This reflects Abraham’s compassion and hope for his father’s guidance and forgiveness.

translation: And do not disgrace me on the Day they are resurrected.
interpretation: This is Abraham’s plea for God’s mercy on the Day of Judgment: he asks not to be exposed to humiliation before all creation, expressing that true honor and security come from God’s acceptance.

translation: The Day when neither wealth nor children will benefit,
interpretation: On that Day, worldly possessions and family ties cannot secure anyone’s salvation; what matters is the state of one’s heart before God.

translation: Except for one who comes to Allah with a sound heart.
interpretation: A sound heart is one devoted sincerely to Allah, free from disbelief and the inner corruption that turns a person away from Him.

translation: And Paradise will be brought near to the God-conscious.
interpretation: Its being brought near signifies the honor and welcome awaiting those who are mindful of God: they will find their promised reward made accessible to them, not distant or difficult to attain.

translation: And Hellfire will be brought into view for those who went astray.
interpretation: The verse portrays the ultimate consequence of straying as becoming unmistakably visible: those who turned from the truth will face the punishment they had neglected to heed.

translation: And it will be said to them, “Where are those you used to worship?”
interpretation: This question exposes the helplessness of the beings they worshipped: when judgment comes, those whom they relied on besides God cannot answer or help them.

translation: Besides Allah—can they help you or help themselves?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical challenge exposing the powerlessness of those worshipped besides Allah: they can neither rescue their devotees nor defend themselves, so they are unworthy of worship or reliance.

translation: Then they will be hurled into it—both they and those who went astray.
interpretation: The verse portrays the false objects of worship and their misguided followers being cast into Hell together, exposing the helplessness of those worshipped and the ruin of those who followed them.

translation: And all the forces of Iblis.
interpretation: The phrase emphasizes that Iblis’s followers and helpers are treated collectively, with none excluded from accountability.

translation: They will say, while they are arguing therein,
interpretation: Their dispute shows that, in the Hereafter, those who shared in wrongdoing will turn against one another, but their blame and argument will not lessen their punishment.

translation: By God, we were indeed in manifest error.
interpretation: This is a belated confession: they now recognize that treating others as equals to the Lord of all worlds was plainly misguided.

translation: When we equated you with the Lord of all worlds,
interpretation: The speakers confess that they once treated their idols as rivals to God, giving them a share of the worship and devotion due to Him alone.

translation: And none led us astray except the criminals.
interpretation: They recognize that their ruin came from following those who knowingly turned them away from the truth, though this realization comes too late to undo the consequences.

translation: So we have no intercessors.
interpretation: They acknowledge in despair that no one can plead on their behalf before God or spare them from the consequences of their deeds.

translation: Nor any close friend.
interpretation: It portrays the utter helplessness of the Hereafter: even the closest companion cannot rescue a person from the consequences of their deeds.

translation: If only we could return, we would be among the believers.
interpretation: They lament their rejection of faith once its consequences become clear, wishing for another chance to believe—but the wish comes too late.

translation: Indeed, in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers.
interpretation: The verse teaches that clear signs can point toward the truth without forcing people to accept it; recognizing their significance also requires a heart willing to respond.

translation: And indeed, your Lord is the Almighty, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: God’s mercy is never a sign of weakness: He has absolute power, yet deals with His creation in mercy and compassion.

translation: The people of Noah denied the messengers.
interpretation: Although Noah was the messenger sent to them, their rejection of him was a rejection of the messengers as a whole, since they all called people to the same truth.

translation: When their brother Noah said to them, “Will you not be mindful of God?”
interpretation: Noah’s address combines closeness with warning: as one of their own people, he calls them to reverent awareness of God and to turn away from wrongdoing.

translation: Indeed, I am a trustworthy messenger to you.
interpretation: The speaker assures his people that he faithfully conveys what he has been entrusted with, without deceit or alteration.

translation: So be mindful of Allah and obey me.
interpretation: The speaker calls people to honor God through obedience to the messenger who conveys His guidance.

translation: I ask you for no reward for it; my reward is only with the Lord of all worlds.
interpretation: The messenger’s call is offered sincerely, without seeking wealth or personal gain; he entrusts his recompense entirely to God.

translation: So be mindful of Allah and obey me.
interpretation: The speaker calls people to live with reverence for Allah and to follow the guidance he conveys in obedience to Him.

translation: They said, “Shall we believe you when the lowliest people have followed you?”
interpretation: They dismissed the prophet’s message by looking down on those who followed him, assuming that people of humble standing could not be guided to the truth. Their objection reflects pride and social prejudice, not a reasoned response to his message.

translation: He said, “What knowledge do I have of what they used to do?”
interpretation: The verse teaches that a person’s true standing is not determined by outward status or by claims about their past; ultimate judgment belongs to God, who knows what people have done and what lies within them.

translation: Their reckoning is only with my Lord, if you would only understand.
interpretation: The verse teaches that ultimate judgment of people belongs to God alone; people should not claim knowledge of what is hidden in others or take it upon themselves to decide their final standing.

translation: And I am not one to drive away the believers.
interpretation: Faith, not social rank or wealth, determines a person’s worth; a prophet must honor sincere believers rather than reject them to please the powerful.

translation: I am only a clear warner.
interpretation: The speaker defines his role as delivering the warning plainly, without claiming power to compel people or control what they choose to believe.

translation: They said, “If you do not desist, Noah, you will surely be among those who are stoned.”
interpretation: Their threat reveals that, unable to answer Noah’s message, they resorted to intimidation to silence him and deter him from calling them to faith.

translation: He said, “My Lord, indeed my people have denied me.”
interpretation: The verse portrays a messenger turning to God after his people persistently reject his call, entrusting his grievance to the One who knows the truth and can judge with justice.

translation: So decide between me and them decisively, and save me and those of the believers who are with me.
interpretation: The speaker asks God to bring a just and decisive end to the conflict, while protecting him and the believers who stand with him.

translation: So We saved him and those with him in the laden Ark.
interpretation: The verse portrays God’s protection as reaching Noah and his companions through the means He provided, showing that deliverance comes by His care even amid overwhelming danger.

translation: Then, afterward, We drowned those who remained.
interpretation: The phrase portrays the drowning as the final consequence of the events that came before it, marking the end of those who remained.

translation: Indeed, in that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers.
interpretation: The event just described is presented as a clear sign of God’s power and truth, but the presence of such evidence does not compel everyone to believe; many still turn away.

translation: And indeed, your Lord is the Almighty, the Merciful.
interpretation: God’s power is absolute, yet it is joined with mercy: He is able to bring about His judgment, while continuing to show compassion and leave people room to turn back to Him.

translation: ʿĀd denied the messengers.
interpretation: Although ʿĀd rejected the messenger sent to them, the Qur’an describes this as denying the messengers collectively: their message was one in its call to worship God, so rejecting one of them was a rejection of that shared truth.

translation: When their brother Hūd said to them, “Will you not be mindful of Allah?”
interpretation: Calling Hūd their “brother” highlights his closeness to his people and the sincerity of his warning: he urges them to recognize their responsibility before God and turn from heedlessness.

translation: Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger.
interpretation: The messenger assures his people that he faithfully conveys God’s message and can be trusted in his call.

translation: So be mindful of Allah and obey me.
interpretation: The speaker calls people to show reverence for Allah by heeding the guidance entrusted to His messenger and not turning away from it.

translation: I ask you for no reward for it; my reward is only with the Lord of all worlds.
interpretation: The speaker’s message is offered without seeking worldly gain; its worth and recompense are entrusted wholly to God, affirming the sincerity of the call.

translation: Do you build on every elevated place a monument, merely to amuse yourselves?
interpretation: The verse censures using power and resources to erect showy structures for vanity and idle display, rather than for a meaningful purpose. It calls people to reflect on whether their works serve genuine good or merely feed pride.

translation: And you build imposing structures, as though you would live forever.
interpretation: The verse rebukes the arrogance of treating human-made grandeur as lasting security, when no building can make its builders immortal.

translation: And when you seize, you seize like tyrants.
interpretation: The verse condemns using power with arrogant cruelty: strength should not become an excuse for oppression or punishment beyond what is just.

translation: So be mindful of Allah and obey me.
interpretation: The speaker calls people to show reverence for Allah by avoiding disobedience, and to follow the guidance entrusted to him.

translation: And be mindful of the One who has provided you with what you know.
interpretation: The verse calls people to recognize God as the source of the provisions and blessings they depend on, and to let that awareness guide them toward reverence and obedience.

translation: He provided you with livestock and sons.
