translation: When they hear frivolous talk, they turn away from it and say, “We have our deeds, and you have yours. Peace be upon you; we do not seek the company of the ignorant.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that restraint is stronger than answering every provocation: a believer can disengage without hostility, leave others accountable for their choices, and preserve peace without approving of foolish or harmful speech.

translation: Indeed, you cannot guide to faith whom you love; rather, Allah guides whom He wills, and He knows best who are rightly guided.
interpretation: The verse teaches that a person may invite and counsel those dear to them, but cannot bring faith into their hearts. True guidance is granted by Allah, whose knowledge encompasses who is receptive to it.

translation: They say, “If we follow the guidance with you, we will be snatched away from our land.” Have We not established for them a secure sanctuary, to which fruits of every kind are brought as provision from Us? But most of them do not know.
interpretation: Their fear of losing safety should not keep them from accepting guidance: the security and abundant provision they already enjoy are gifts from God, not guarantees that depend on rejecting the truth.

translation: How many a town have We destroyed that grew insolent in its prosperity! Those are their dwellings, scarcely inhabited after them; and We alone were the inheritors.
interpretation: The verse warns that prosperity can become a cause of ruin when people grow arrogant and ungrateful. Their abandoned homes stand as a reminder that worldly power and wealth do not last, while God remains the ultimate owner of all things.

translation: Your Lord would never destroy towns until He had sent a messenger to their principal city, reciting Our signs to its people. And We would destroy towns only when their people were wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse presents divine judgment as grounded in justice: people are not punished before a messenger has brought them guidance and made the truth known. Their destruction follows not mere disbelief or circumstance, but persistent wrongdoing after that warning has reached them.

translation: Whatever you have been given is only an enjoyment and adornment of the life of this world; what is with Allah is better and more enduring. Will you not then reason?
interpretation: The verse calls people to judge their blessings by their lasting worth: worldly pleasures and possessions are temporary, while what Allah has prepared endures. A sound understanding therefore gives greater priority to seeking what is with Allah than to being absorbed in the passing attractions of this life.

translation: Is one to whom We have made a good promise, and who will attain it, like one whom We have allowed to enjoy the pleasures of worldly life, but who on the Day of Resurrection will be among those brought forward?
interpretation: The rhetorical question makes clear that temporary worldly enjoyment cannot compare with the lasting good God has promised. A person’s present prosperity is no proof of ultimate success; what matters is the final outcome before God.

translation: And on the Day He will call them and say, “Where are My partners whom you used to claim?”
interpretation: The question exposes the emptiness of their claims: those they treated as partners with God have no power to answer or help them, and their false belief becomes unmistakable.

translation: Those against whom the decree has come due will say, “Our Lord, these are the ones we led astray. We led them astray just as we ourselves went astray. We disown them before You; they were not worshipping us.”
interpretation: Those who led others into error will admit that their influence drew people into the same misguidance they had chosen for themselves, yet they will disclaim being worthy of worship. The verse exposes the emptiness of following false authorities: on the Day of Judgment, neither the leaders nor the objects of devotion can shield their followers from responsibility before God.

translation: And it will be said, “Call upon those you claimed were partners [with God].” They will call upon them, but they will not answer them, and they will see the punishment. If only they had been rightly guided!
interpretation: This scene exposes the utter helplessness of those they worshipped besides God: when called upon in the Hereafter, they cannot help or even answer. The final words express the condemned people’s regret that they did not follow guidance while they still had the chance.

translation: And [remember] the Day He will call them and say, “What did you answer the messengers?”
interpretation: The question underscores that people will be held accountable for how they responded to God’s messengers: whether they accepted their guidance and acted upon it, or rejected it. No response can be concealed or excused before God.

translation: Then the answers will be unclear to them that Day, and they will not ask one another.
interpretation: When confronted with the truth, they will be unable to find a response or guide one another; their confusion will leave them silent and isolated.

translation: As for whoever repents, believes, and does righteous deeds, it may be that he will be among the successful.
interpretation: The verse holds out hope that past wrongdoing need not define a person: turning back to God, embracing faith, and living righteously are the way toward true success.

translation: And your Lord creates whatever He wills and chooses; they have no choice. Glory be to Allah, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: The verse affirms that creation and the choices made within it belong to God alone. No one can overrule His wisdom or claim authority over whom He chooses, and He is far above the partners people attribute to Him.

translation: And your Lord knows what their hearts conceal and what they make known.
interpretation: Nothing is hidden from God: He knows people’s inward thoughts and intentions as fully as their outward words and deeds.

translation: He is Allah; there is no god except Him. To Him belongs all praise in this world and the Hereafter. His is the judgment, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: The verse teaches that Allah alone is worthy of worship and praise, and that His authority encompasses both worldly life and the Hereafter. Since every person ultimately returns to Him, His judgment is the final and decisive one.

translation: Say, “Have you considered: if Allah were to make the night endless for you until the Day of Resurrection, what god besides Allah could bring you light? Will you not then listen?”
interpretation: The verse invites people to recognize that even the return of daylight is beyond the power of anything they worship besides God. Its question calls for more than hearing the words: it urges a receptive mind to acknowledge its dependence on God and turn from false sources of power.

translation: Say, “Have you considered: if Allah were to make the day everlasting for you until the Day of Resurrection, what god other than Allah could bring you a night in which you could rest? Will you not then see?”
interpretation: The verse draws attention to how human life depends on the ordered alternation of day and night—a provision no one but Allah can grant. Recognizing this dependence should lead people to see that worship and gratitude are due to Him alone.

translation: And out of His mercy He made for you the night and the day, so that you may rest in it and seek of His bounty, and so that you may be grateful.
interpretation: The verse invites people to see the rhythms of rest and activity as a mercy from God, and to let awareness of this provision deepen their gratitude to Him.

translation: And on the Day He calls to them, He will say, “Where are My partners whom you used to claim?”
interpretation: The question is a rebuke that exposes the falsehood of their claims: those they associated with God will be unable to help them or answer in their defense.

translation: And We will bring forth from every community a witness, then say, “Produce your proof.” They will realize that the truth belongs to Allah, and what they used to fabricate will have vanished from them.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, each community will be confronted with a witness to its deeds and beliefs. The demand for proof will expose the baselessness of the false claims they made about Allah, leaving them to recognize that ultimate truth and judgment belong to Him alone.

translation: Indeed, Qarun was one of the people of Moses, but he oppressed them. We had given him such treasures that their keys would burden a company of strong men. His people said to him, “Do not exult; surely God does not love those who exult.”
interpretation: The verse warns that abundant wealth is not a license for arrogance or oppression. What a person possesses is a trust, and taking pride in it while harming others turns blessing into a cause of moral failure.

translation: Seek, through what Allah has given you, the home of the Hereafter, and do not forget your share of this world. Do good, just as Allah has done good to you, and do not seek corruption in the land. Indeed, Allah does not love those who cause corruption.
interpretation: The verse teaches that worldly blessings are entrusted to us: they should be used to seek lasting good without neglecting legitimate needs in this life. Gratitude is shown by extending goodness to others, while pursuing one’s interests must never come at the cost of corruption or harm.

translation: He said, “I have been given it only because of knowledge I possess.” Did he not know that Allah had destroyed before him generations who were greater than him in strength and amassed more? And the guilty will not be asked about their sins.
interpretation: He mistook his wealth for proof of his own merit and knowledge, overlooking that it was a gift from Allah and no protection from accountability. The fate of stronger and richer people before him shows that worldly power cannot avert Allah’s judgment; the guilty need not be questioned to make their guilt known to Him.

translation: Then he went out before his people in all his adornment. Those who desired the life of this world said, “If only we had been given the like of what Qarun has been given! He truly has a great share of good fortune.”
interpretation: The verse shows how worldly glamour can distort people’s sense of what true success is: dazzled by Qarun’s wealth, they mistook material abundance for a sign of great fortune.

translation: Those who had been given knowledge said, “Woe to you! Allah’s reward is better for whoever believes and does righteous deeds, and none will attain it except the patient.”
interpretation: Those grounded in knowledge see beyond dazzling wealth: lasting reward from Allah is better than worldly status, and it is attained through faith and righteous action. Patience is essential—not only to endure hardship, but also to resist the temptation to measure success by what people possess in this life.

translation: So We caused the earth to swallow him and his dwelling. He had no party to help him against God, nor was he able to defend himself.
interpretation: The verse teaches that worldly wealth and influence cannot shield a person from God’s judgment; reliance on power and status is ultimately fragile.

translation: The next morning, those who had wished to be in his place the day before were saying, “How wondrous! Allah grants abundant provision to whomever He wills of His servants, and restricts it. Had Allah not shown us favor, He would have caused the earth to swallow us. How wondrous! The disbelievers do not prosper.”
interpretation: The sudden reversal teaches that wealth is neither proof of divine approval nor a guarantee of security. Seeing the consequence of arrogance, the onlookers recognize that provision lies in God’s hands and that they themselves are saved only by His favor; true success cannot belong to disbelief that rejects this truth.

translation: That is the home of the Hereafter, which We assign to those who seek neither exaltedness on earth nor corruption. And the ultimate outcome belongs to the mindful of God.
interpretation: The verse teaches that lasting success is not won through self-aggrandizement or harmful ambition. It belongs to those who restrain their desire for power and live with awareness of God, trusting that the final measure of success is the outcome God grants.

translation: Whoever comes with a good deed will receive something better than it; and whoever comes with an evil deed—those who did evil deeds will be recompensed only for what they used to do.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the generosity and justice of God: goodness is met with a reward exceeding its measure, while wrongdoing is not punished beyond what it deserves.

translation: Indeed, He who prescribed the Qur’an for you will surely bring you back to a place of return. Say, “My Lord knows best who has come with guidance and who is in clear error.”
interpretation: The verse reassures the Prophet that the One who entrusted him with the Qur’an will not abandon him: He will bring him to his promised return—understood in its context as his return to Mecca, and more broadly as the final return to God. The Prophet is to leave judgment of people’s guidance or error to God, whose knowledge is complete.

translation: You did not expect that the Book would be given to you; it was only by mercy from your Lord. So never be a supporter of the disbelievers.
interpretation: The revelation is presented as an unearned gift of divine mercy, not something the Prophet could have secured by his own effort or expectation. Its source and purpose call him to remain loyal to God’s guidance and never lend support to those who oppose it.

translation: Do not let them turn you away from the signs of Allah after they have been revealed to you. Call people to your Lord, and never be among those who associate partners with Him.
interpretation: Remain steadfast in conveying Allah’s revelation despite opposition, and call people to worship Him alone without associating anything with Him.

translation: Do not call upon any other deity alongside Allah. There is no deity but Him. Everything will perish except His Face. His is the judgment, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: The verse directs people to devote worship and reliance exclusively to God, whose reality and authority endure while all created things pass away. Since all will return to Him, ultimate judgment belongs to Him alone.

translation: In the name of God, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Alif Lām Mīm.
interpretation: The opening invokes God’s mercy and places the recitation under His name. The letters “Alif Lām Mīm” are among the Qur’an’s disjointed opening letters; their ultimate meaning is known to God, and they invite the listener to attend humbly to the revelation that follows.

translation: Do people think they will be left to say, “We believe,” without being tested?
interpretation: Faith is not proved by words alone: trials reveal the sincerity of a person’s belief and call them to remain steadfast when it is put to the test.

translation: We certainly tested those who came before them. Allah will surely make evident those who are truthful and those who are lying.
interpretation: Trials reveal the sincerity of faith: they distinguish those who remain truthful in their commitment from those whose claims prove false. Allah’s knowing is not gained through the test; rather, the test brings what is already known to Him into clear evidence.

translation: Or do those who commit evil deeds think they can escape Us? How badly they judge!
interpretation: Those who persist in wrongdoing deceive themselves if they think they can evade God’s judgment; their deeds cannot place them beyond His reach.

translation: Whoever hopes to meet Allah should know that Allah’s appointed time is surely coming. He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: The verse reassures those who long to meet God that the promised encounter is certain, and calls them to remain steadfast and live in readiness for it. Nothing they say or do is hidden from Him.

translation: Whoever strives, strives only for his own benefit. Indeed, Allah is free of need of all the worlds.
interpretation: A person’s effort in faith and obedience does not add anything to Allah’s greatness or power; its benefit returns to the person, while Allah is utterly independent of all creation.

translation: As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, We will surely erase their misdeeds and reward them according to the best of what they used to do.
interpretation: The verse assures believers that God’s mercy encompasses both forgiveness and reward: He removes the burden of their wrongs and judges their good deeds by their finest measure, not by their shortcomings.

translation: We have enjoined upon the human being kindness to his parents. But if they strive to make you associate with Me something of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them. To Me is your return, and I will inform you of what you used to do.
interpretation: The verse teaches that devotion to God is the highest loyalty: honoring one’s parents remains a profound duty, but it cannot require abandoning faith or affirming what is false. Refusing such a demand does not cancel kindness toward them, and every person will ultimately answer to God for their choices.

translation: As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, We will surely admit them among the righteous.
interpretation: This is a promise from God that sincere faith expressed through good deeds will lead to a place among the righteous, in the honored company of those who obey Him.

translation: Among the people are those who say, “We believe in Allah.” But when they are harmed for Allah’s sake, they treat people’s persecution as though it were Allah’s punishment. Yet if help comes from your Lord, they will surely say, “We were with you.” Is Allah not most knowing of what lies within the hearts of all people?
interpretation: The verse warns against faith that is only professed when it is easy: fear of people’s pressure can expose a heart that has not placed its trust firmly in Allah. It also cautions against claiming solidarity only when success arrives, for Allah knows the sincerity and motives hidden within every heart.

translation: And Allah will certainly make evident those who believe, and He will certainly make evident the hypocrites.
interpretation: Allah’s knowledge is complete and does not arise through discovery; rather, events make people’s true faith or hypocrisy manifest in their actions, so that divine judgment is shown to be just.

translation: Those who disbelieved said to those who believed, “Follow our way, and we will bear your sins.” But they will bear nothing of their sins. Indeed, they are liars.
interpretation: No one can make disobedience safe by promising to take responsibility for another person’s wrongdoing. The verse warns against trusting leaders who use false assurances to draw others away from faith: each person remains accountable before God, and those who mislead others incur responsibility for their own deception as well.

translation: They will surely bear their own burdens, and other burdens along with their burdens; and on the Day of Resurrection they will surely be questioned about what they used to fabricate.
interpretation: Those who deceive or lead others astray are accountable not only for their own wrongdoing but also for the harm caused by their influence, while each person remains responsible for their own choices. Their fabricated claims and excuses will not escape scrutiny before God.

translation: We certainly sent Noah to his people, and he remained among them for a thousand years less fifty years. Then the Flood overtook them while they were wrongdoers.
interpretation: Noah’s long stay among his people conveys the extraordinary patience with which he called them to guidance. Their eventual destruction despite this prolonged warning shows that persistent wrongdoing does not escape divine judgment.

translation: So We saved him and those aboard the ship, and made it a sign for all people.
interpretation: Their rescue stands as a lasting sign of God’s power and mercy, and a warning that those who reject His guidance cannot escape the consequences of their choices.

translation: And [remember] Abraham, when he said to his people, “Worship Allah and be mindful of Him. That is better for you, if you only knew.”
interpretation: Abraham calls his people to recognize that devotion to God and reverence for Him are not burdens but the surest path to their lasting good—a truth that becomes clear when people understand what truly benefits them.

translation: You worship nothing besides Allah but idols, and you fabricate falsehood. Those you worship besides Allah cannot provide you with sustenance. So seek sustenance from Allah, worship Him, and be grateful to Him. To Him you will be returned.
interpretation: The verse challenges the misplaced trust involved in worshipping things that people themselves fashion and falsely invest with divine power. True reliance belongs to Allah, the source of provision; therefore seeking His provision should be joined with worship and gratitude. The reminder of returning to Him gives this devotion moral weight: people are accountable for where they place their trust and how they respond to His gifts.

translation: And if you deny, peoples before you have already denied. The Messenger’s duty is only to deliver the message clearly.
interpretation: The truth of the message does not depend on whether people accept it: earlier peoples also rejected their messengers. The Messenger must make the message clear, while each person is responsible for how they respond.

translation: Have they not seen how Allah originates creation and then brings it back? Surely that is easy for Allah.
interpretation: The renewal of life after death is not beyond the One who first brought creation into being; the world’s beginnings point to the power by which resurrection will occur.

translation: Say, “Travel through the land and observe how He began creation. Then Allah will bring about the next creation. Indeed, Allah has power over all things.”
interpretation: Reflecting on the beginning of creation shows that bringing creation back to life is within Allah’s power; the One who originated it can bring it into being again.

translation: He punishes whom He wills and has mercy on whom He wills, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: The verse calls people to recognize that their ultimate fate rests with God, who alone has authority over punishment and mercy; since everyone will return to Him, they should live mindful of His judgment and hope in His mercy.

translation: You cannot escape God’s power on earth or in heaven, and you have no protector or helper apart from God.
interpretation: The verse calls people to recognize that no place or circumstance lies beyond God’s authority, and that worldly allies cannot ultimately replace His protection. It encourages humility and reliance on God rather than confidence in the illusion of being beyond His reach.

translation: As for those who disbelieve in Allah’s signs and in meeting Him, they have despaired of My mercy, and they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: Rejecting God’s signs and denying that one will meet Him cuts a person off from hope in His mercy. The verse warns that such denial has grave consequences in the Hereafter.

translation: But the only response of his people was to say, “Kill him or burn him.” Yet Allah saved him from the fire. Surely in that are signs for people who believe.
interpretation: The episode shows that human efforts to suppress the truth cannot overcome God’s will. For those who believe, Abraham’s deliverance is a sign of God’s power and of the steadfastness He grants to His messengers.

translation: He said, “You have taken idols besides Allah only as a bond of affection among yourselves in the life of this world. Then, on the Day of Resurrection, you will disown one another and curse one another. Your refuge will be the Fire, and you will have no helpers.”
interpretation: The verse warns that a bond built around worship of what is false may seem to unite people in this life, but it cannot endure before God. When its consequences become clear, that apparent loyalty turns into blame and rejection; no idol or companion can then offer rescue.

translation: So Lot believed him, and he said, “Indeed, I am migrating to my Lord. Surely He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.”
interpretation: Abraham’s migration was an act of trust and obedience: he left his people for the sake of his Lord, confident that Allah’s might and wisdom would guide and protect him.

translation: And We bestowed upon him Isaac and Jacob, and placed prophethood and Scripture among his descendants. We granted him his reward in this world, and in the Hereafter he will surely be among the righteous.
interpretation: Abraham’s faithfulness bore blessings that reached far beyond his own lifetime: God made his family a source of guidance for generations. His worldly blessings were not the measure of his success; his lasting honor lies in God’s approval and his righteous standing in the Hereafter.

translation: And [We sent] Lot, when he said to his people, “Do you commit an outrage such as no one in all the worlds before you has committed?”
interpretation: Lot’s words present his people’s conduct as a grave breach of the moral order, and the claim that none before them had done it underscores the exceptional boldness of their transgression.

translation: “Do you indeed approach men, waylay travelers, and commit abominations in your gatherings?” The only response of his people was to say, “Bring us Allah’s punishment, if you are truthful.”
interpretation: The verse portrays a people whose wrongdoing had become public and habitual, and whose response to moral warning was not reflection or repentance but arrogant defiance. Their demand for punishment exposes how far they had turned from the warning being given to them.

translation: He said, “My Lord, help me against the people who spread corruption.”
interpretation: He appeals to God for support against those whose wrongdoing and corruption have become a threat, recognizing that divine help is needed to confront their harm.

translation: When Our messengers came to Abraham with good news, they said, “We are going to destroy the people of this town; its people have been wrongdoers.”
interpretation: The messengers brought Abraham glad tidings and also disclosed that the people of Lot’s town would be destroyed because of their persistent wrongdoing.

translation: He said, “But Lot is there.” They said, “We know best who is there. We will surely save him and his family, except his wife; she will be among those left behind.”
interpretation: The angels reassure Abraham that Lot and his believing family will be protected from the coming punishment, while Lot’s wife will remain with the people who are doomed because of her rejection.

translation: When Our messengers came to Lot, he was distressed on their account and felt constrained. They said, “Do not fear or grieve. We will save you and your family, except your wife; she is among those who will remain behind.”
interpretation: Lot’s distress reflects his concern for his guests and his awareness of the danger surrounding them. God’s reassurance shows that deliverance comes by His protection, while the exception of Lot’s wife makes clear that kinship alone does not guarantee salvation.

translation: Indeed, We are sending down upon the people of this town a punishment from heaven because they persistently transgressed.
interpretation: The verse teaches that persistent defiance of God’s limits has grave consequences; the punishment is portrayed as a consequence of the people’s continued wrongdoing.

translation: And We have certainly left of it a clear sign for people who reason.
interpretation: The lasting sign is evidence of what befell the people being described, serving as a warning that thoughtful people can recognize and learn from.

translation: And to Midian We sent their brother Shuʿayb. He said, “My people, worship Allah, hope for the Last Day, and do not spread corruption in the land.”
interpretation: Shuʿayb calls his people to let worship of God and awareness of the Day of Judgment guide their conduct. Faith is not detached from how people treat the world around them: hope in the Hereafter should move them away from wrongdoing and corruption.

translation: But they denied him, so the earthquake seized them, and they lay lifeless, fallen in their homes.
interpretation: Their fate shows that when a people persistently reject a messenger’s warning, they may be overtaken suddenly by the consequences of that rejection, despite feeling secure in their homes.

translation: And [We destroyed] ʿĀd and Thamūd, whose fate has become clear to you from their dwellings. Satan made their deeds seem appealing to them and turned them away from the path, though they were discerning.
interpretation: The remains of ʿĀd and Thamūd stand as a warning: they were not incapable of recognizing the truth, but Satan made their wrongdoing appear attractive and led them away from it. Their insight did not benefit them when they chose to follow that deception.

translation: And [We also destroyed] Qarun, Pharaoh, and Haman. Moses came to them with clear proofs, but they grew arrogant in the land; they could not escape [Our judgment].
interpretation: The verse warns that wealth, authority, and influence cannot shield people who arrogantly reject clear guidance. No matter how powerful they seem, they cannot outrun God’s judgment.

translation: Each of them We seized for their sin. Upon some We sent a storm of stones; some were seized by the blast; some We caused the earth to swallow; and some We drowned. God would not wrong them, but they wronged themselves.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that divine punishment is not arbitrary: people bring themselves to ruin through their own wrongdoing, while God’s justice does not impose a wrong upon them.

translation: The example of those who take protectors besides Allah is like that of a spider who takes a house. Surely the frailest of houses is the spider’s house—if only they knew.
interpretation: Those who rely on beings besides Allah for ultimate protection place their trust in something as fragile and inadequate as a spider’s web: it may appear to offer shelter, but cannot truly protect them.

translation: Indeed, Allah knows whatever they call upon besides Him. He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: Those invoked besides Allah are fully known to Him, and none can escape His knowledge or challenge His authority. His might and wisdom affirm that judgment and governance belong to Him alone.

translation: These examples We set forth for people, but none truly understand them except those who know.
interpretation: The verse teaches that grasping the deeper wisdom of divine examples requires knowledge and reflection; their meaning is not fully understood through mere hearing, but through a mind attentive to truth.

translation: Allah created the heavens and the earth in truth. Surely in that is a sign for the believers.
interpretation: The ordered creation of the heavens and the earth points believers to Allah’s wisdom and power, and to the truth that creation is not without purpose.

translation: Recite what has been revealed to you of the Book, and establish prayer. Indeed, prayer restrains from indecency and wrongdoing, and the remembrance of God is greater. And God knows what you do.
interpretation: Prayer is meant to cultivate an enduring awareness of God that turns a person away from indecency and wrongdoing; the remembrance of God is greater because it reaches beyond the prayer itself and guides one’s conduct throughout life. Nothing people do is hidden from Him.

translation: Do not argue with the People of the Book except in the most gracious manner—except with those among them who do wrong. And say, “We believe in what was sent down to us and what was sent down to you. Our God and your God is One, and to Him we submit.”
interpretation: The verse calls for respectful, principled dialogue with the People of the Book, grounded in the shared belief that God is one and that revelation has been sent to both communities. Its exception recognizes that gracious engagement does not require treating wrongdoing as acceptable; the response should remain guided by justice and devotion to God.

translation: Thus We have sent down the Book to you. Those to whom We gave the Scripture believe in it, and among these people are some who believe in it. None rejects Our signs except the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the Qur’an’s truth is recognized by sincere people, including some who received earlier scripture and some among its present audience. Persistently rejecting its signs is portrayed not as a lack of evidence, but as a refusal to accept the truth.

translation: You did not recite any scripture before it, nor did you write one with your right hand; otherwise, those who seek to discredit the truth would have had reason to doubt.
interpretation: The verse points to the Qur’an’s independence from prior scriptural study or authorship by the Prophet: his lack of such a background removes a plausible basis for claiming that he composed it from earlier writings.

translation: Rather, these are clear signs preserved in the hearts of those who have been given knowledge. None reject Our signs except the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The Qur’an’s truth is not dependent on being written in a book; it is preserved and recognized by those granted knowledge. Persistently rejecting its signs is an act of wrongdoing.

translation: They say, “Why have signs not been sent down to him from his Lord?” Say, “The signs are only with Allah, and I am only a clear warner.”
interpretation: The Prophet’s task is to convey a clear warning, not to produce signs on demand; the granting of signs belongs to God and His wisdom.

translation: Is it not enough for them that We have sent down to you the Book, which is recited to them? Surely in that is mercy and a reminder for people who believe.
interpretation: The Qur’an itself is a sufficient sign of the truth of the Prophet’s message: its guidance remains present and recited, offering mercy and renewing the faith of those who are willing to believe.

translation: Say, “Allah is sufficient as a witness between me and you. He knows all that is in the heavens and the earth. Those who believe in falsehood and disbelieve in Allah—it is they who are the losers.”
interpretation: Allah’s all-encompassing knowledge makes Him the ultimate witness to the truth of the message and to how people respond to it. The verse warns that putting trust in falsehood while rejecting Allah leads to real loss, even if that choice appears advantageous for a time.

translation: They urge you to hasten the punishment. Were it not for an appointed term, the punishment would already have come upon them. It will surely come upon them suddenly, while they are unaware.
interpretation: The delay of divine punishment is not a sign that it will never come; it reflects a time set by God. Those who mockingly demand it may therefore be caught off guard, so the verse calls them to take the warning seriously rather than mistake patience for impunity.

translation: They urge you to hasten the punishment, but Hell surely encompasses the disbelievers.
interpretation: The disbelievers’ challenge does not make the promised punishment remote: their rejection has already placed them within the reach of its consequence, even if they do not yet perceive it.

translation: On the Day the punishment envelops them from above them and from beneath their feet, it will be said, “Taste what you used to do.”
interpretation: The verse portrays a punishment from which there is no escape, confronting people with the consequence of their own deeds. The command to “taste” makes clear that what they once did has become a reality they must now experience.

translation: O My servants who believe, My earth is indeed vast, so worship Me alone.
interpretation: Believers are urged not to let a hostile or restrictive environment prevent sincere worship: if their faith cannot be practiced freely where they are, they should seek a place where they can remain devoted to God.

translation: Every soul will taste death; then to Us you will be returned.
interpretation: The verse places human life within a larger horizon: death is not the final end, but the transition to standing before God. Awareness of that return gives moral weight to the choices made in this life.

translation: As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, We will surely settle them in lofty chambers of Paradise, beneath which rivers flow, abiding there forever. How excellent is the reward of those who strive.
interpretation: The verse reassures believers that sincere faith joined with righteous action is not lost: God will honor their striving with a secure, lasting home in Paradise. The promise presents their reward as both a divine gift and a fitting recompense for their perseverance.

translation: Those who are patient and place their trust in their Lord.
interpretation: Their patience is steadfastness through hardship and obedience, while their trust in God means relying on Him with confidence as they face what lies ahead.

translation: How many a creature does not carry its provision! Allah provides for it and for you. He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: The verse reassures people not to let fear of provision undermine their trust in Allah: He knows every creature’s needs and provides for it, and He hears and knows those who turn to Him.

translation: If you ask them, “Who created the heavens and the earth and subjected the sun and the moon?” they will surely say, “Allah.” How, then, are they turned away?
interpretation: The verse highlights the contradiction in acknowledging Allah as the Creator and Sustainer while turning to other objects of worship. Such recognition should lead them to worship Allah alone, so their turning away has no sound basis.

translation: Allah enlarges provision for whom He wills among His servants and restricts it for him. Surely Allah knows all things.
interpretation: The differing measures of provision reflect Allah’s complete knowledge and wisdom, not a measure of a person’s worth or standing with Him.

translation: If you ask them, “Who sent down water from the sky and brought the earth back to life after its death?” they will surely say, “Allah.” Say, “Praise be to Allah.” Yet most of them do not understand.
interpretation: Their acknowledgment that Allah alone brings life to the dead earth should lead them to recognize His power and give Him thanks; their failure to follow that truth to its proper conclusion shows a lack of sound understanding.

translation: This worldly life is nothing but amusement and play, while the home of the Hereafter is truly the real life—if only they knew.
interpretation: The verse teaches that worldly existence, despite its attractions, is fleeting and incomplete when treated as the ultimate purpose. The Hereafter is the enduring reality in which life reaches its full and lasting form, so a person should not let temporary pleasures distract them from preparing for it.

translation: When they embark on a ship, they call upon Allah, devoting their worship sincerely to Him. But when He brings them safely to land, they immediately associate others with Him.
interpretation: The verse exposes a faith that appears only in danger: hardship makes people turn sincerely to God, but once relief comes, they forget the One who saved them. It warns that true devotion should not depend on circumstances; gratitude and worship belong to God in safety as well as in distress.

translation: So that they may deny what We have given them and enjoy themselves; soon they will know.
interpretation: The verse rebukes those who respond to God’s gifts with ingratitude and disbelief, choosing fleeting enjoyment while ignoring the consequences that will eventually become clear to them.

translation: Have they not seen that We made a secure sanctuary, while people are being snatched away all around them? Do they then believe in falsehood and deny Allah’s favor?
interpretation: The verse points to the sanctuary’s security amid the danger surrounding it as a clear favor from Allah. It rebukes those who benefit from that protection yet turn to falsehood and fail to acknowledge the One who granted it.

translation: Who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about Allah or denies the truth when it comes to him? Is there not in Hell a dwelling for the disbelievers?
interpretation: The verse warns that knowingly attributing falsehood to God and rejecting truth after it has become clear are among the gravest forms of wrongdoing, and that such rejection carries a severe consequence in the Hereafter.

translation: As for those who strive for Our sake, We will surely guide them to Our ways. And indeed, God is with those who do good.
interpretation: Those who sincerely exert themselves for God—seeking what is right and resisting what pulls them away from it—are promised that He will open paths of guidance to them and support them in doing good.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Alif, Lam, Mim.
interpretation: The opening invokes Allah by His name and mercy, then begins with letters whose full meaning is known to Him; their placement draws attention to the Qur’an, composed of the same Arabic letters familiar to its hearers, yet beyond their power to imitate.

translation: The Byzantines have been defeated.
interpretation: This announces the Byzantines’ defeat, while the surrounding passage presents their eventual reversal as a sign that worldly fortunes change by God’s decree.

translation: In the nearest land; but after their defeat, they will be victorious.
interpretation: The verse reassures believers that a severe setback need not be final: God can reverse the course of events and bring victory after defeat.

translation: Within a few years. To Allah belongs the command before and after; and on that day the believers will rejoice.
interpretation: The verse teaches that events and changing fortunes unfold by Allah’s decree. The believers’ joy reflects their confidence in His promise and their trust that His support will come at the appointed time.

translation: By Allah’s help. He helps whom He wills, and He is the Almighty, the Merciful.
interpretation: Victory is granted by God’s will, not by human power alone; His might makes it possible, and His mercy guides whom He chooses to support.

translation: Allah’s promise. Allah does not fail His promise, but most people do not know.
interpretation: God’s promise is certain, even when its fulfillment is not yet apparent; people often mistake what they cannot see for what will never come to pass.

translation: They know only the outward aspects of this worldly life, while they are heedless of the Hereafter.
interpretation: The verse warns that people may be skilled in worldly matters yet remain unaware of what matters most: their accountability before God and the life to come.

translation: Have they not reflected within themselves? Allah created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them only in truth and for an appointed term. Yet many people surely deny that they will meet their Lord.
interpretation: The verse calls people to recognize, through reflection, that creation is neither pointless nor everlasting: it has a true purpose and a fixed end. This should lead them to believe that they will return to their Lord for judgment, though many fail to accept that meeting.

translation: Have they not traveled through the land and seen what became of those who came before them? They were mightier than these people, worked the land, and developed it more than these have. Their messengers came to them with clear signs. God would never wrong them; rather, they wronged themselves.
interpretation: The verse warns that worldly strength and prosperity do not shield a people from the consequences of rejecting clear guidance. The earlier nations’ downfall was not an injustice from God, but the result of their own wrongdoing; their history should therefore prompt people to reflect and heed the truth before it is too late.

translation: Then the end of those who did evil was the worst, because they denied the signs of Allah and used to mock them.
interpretation: The verse teaches that persistent wrongdoing leads to ruin when people reject God’s signs and treat them with contempt; their fate follows from their deliberate refusal to heed the truth.

translation: Allah originates creation, then brings it back; then to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: The One who first brought creation into existence is fully able to restore it after death. Your return to Him affirms that life does not end with death and that all people will ultimately stand before their Creator.

translation: And on the Day the Hour is established, the guilty will be overcome with despair.
interpretation: Their despair conveys the collapse of every false hope and excuse when they confront the reality of divine judgment.

translation: They will have no intercessors among those they associated with God, and they will disavow those they associated with Him.
interpretation: The verse portrays the collapse of trust in false gods on the Day of Judgment: those once relied upon cannot intercede, and their worshippers reject their former association when its truth and consequences become clear.

translation: And on the Day the Hour is established, on that Day they will be divided.
interpretation: When the Resurrection begins, people will be separated according to their faith and deeds, each facing the outcome and destination they have earned.

translation: As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, they will be in a garden, rejoicing.
interpretation: Those who unite faith with righteous action will be welcomed into the Garden and enjoy lasting delight there.

translation: But as for those who disbelieved, denied Our signs, and rejected the meeting of the Hereafter, they will be brought into the punishment.
interpretation: The verse presents the Hereafter as a reality people will ultimately face, whether they believed in it or denied it; denial cannot avert accountability.

translation: So glorify Allah when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning.
interpretation: The pairing of evening and morning invites believers to begin and end the day mindful of Allah’s perfection, keeping the changing rhythms of life oriented toward remembrance of Him.

translation: To Him belongs all praise in the heavens and the earth, in the evening and when you are at midday.
interpretation: All praise is God’s alone, in every realm and at every time. Mentioning evening and midday emphasizes that people should remember and praise Him throughout the changing hours of their lives.

translation: He brings the living out of the dead and the dead out of the living, and revives the earth after its death. In the same way, you will be brought forth.
interpretation: The recurring transformation between life and death, and the earth’s renewal after it has become barren, are signs that resurrection is within God’s power. Just as He restores life to the earth, He will bring people back to life.

translation: And among His signs is that He created you from dust; then, behold, you are human beings spreading throughout the earth.
interpretation: Humanity’s emergence from humble earthly matter into living, active beings points to God’s power to bring life into existence and to unfold its vastness from a simple beginning.

translation: And among His signs is that He created for you spouses from among yourselves, so that you may find tranquility with them, and He placed between you affection and mercy. Surely in that are signs for people who reflect.
interpretation: The love and compassion that can grow between spouses are signs of God’s wisdom and care: they make mutual support and a sense of belonging possible. Reflecting on this bond can lead people to recognize that human closeness is not merely a practical arrangement, but a gift meant to be nurtured with kindness and mercy.

translation: And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the diversity of your languages and your colors. Surely in that are signs for all people.
interpretation: The many languages and differences in appearance among human beings, alongside the vastness of the heavens and earth, point to God’s power and wisdom. These signs invite people to recognize the Creator in the richness and variety of creation.

translation: And among His signs is your sleep by night and day, and your seeking of His bounty. Surely in that are signs for people who listen.
interpretation: The alternation of sleep and waking, and the ability to seek a livelihood, point to a wisdom and care beyond human control. Those who listen attentively can recognize in these familiar rhythms signs of God’s sustaining power.

translation: And among His signs is that He shows you lightning, inspiring fear and hope, and sends down water from the sky, bringing the earth to life after its death. Surely in that are signs for people who reason.
interpretation: Lightning stirs fear of danger and hope for life-giving rain, while the land’s renewal after rain makes visible God’s power to restore what has died. Those who reflect can recognize in these signs both His care for creation and the possibility of resurrection.

translation: And among His signs is that the heaven and earth stand firm by His command. Then, when He calls you with a single call from the earth, you will at once emerge.
interpretation: The One who continually sustains the vast order of the heavens and the earth has power to bring people back to life. Resurrection is not a distant or difficult task for Him: His command alone is enough to summon everyone forth.

translation: To Him belongs everyone in the heavens and the earth; all are submissive to Him.
interpretation: Everything that exists is under God’s authority and depends on Him. Their submission may be expressed through conscious worship or through the laws and limits that govern their existence.

translation: He is the One who originates creation and then brings it back again—and that is easier for Him. To Him belongs the highest attribute in the heavens and the earth, and He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: The One who brought creation into existence in the first place is fully able to restore it for resurrection. Calling this “easier” underscores the point in terms people understand; nothing is difficult for God. His perfection is exalted above every comparison, and His power is joined with wisdom.

translation: He sets forth for you an example from your own lives: Do you regard any of those whom your right hands possess as partners in what We have provided for you, so that you are equal in it and fear them as you fear one another? In this way We make the signs clear for people who reason.
interpretation: The example exposes the inconsistency of associating partners with God: people do not accept those under their authority as equal partners in their possessions, yet they attribute partners to God in His authority and worship. The verse calls them to recognize that the Creator is unlike His creatures and has no equal in what belongs to Him.

translation: Rather, those who do wrong follow their desires without knowledge. So who can guide those whom Allah has left astray? They will have no helpers.
interpretation: The verse warns that people who prefer their own desires to knowledge and truth become entrenched in misguidance. When, in response to their rejection, Allah leaves them to that path, no one can guide or rescue them from its consequences.

translation: So set your face steadfastly toward the religion, inclining to the truth—the natural disposition of Allah upon which He created mankind. There is no altering Allah’s creation. That is the upright religion, but most people do not know.
interpretation: The verse calls people to devote themselves wholly to pure monotheism, which accords with the innate disposition God placed within humanity: to recognize and turn toward Him. The upright religion preserves and guides this disposition, even though many people are unaware of it.

translation: Turn to Him in devotion, be mindful of Him, establish prayer, and do not be among the polytheists.
interpretation: The verse calls for a life oriented wholly toward God: continually returning to Him, guarding against disobedience, and expressing devotion through prayer. Such allegiance must remain undivided, free from associating anything with Him.

translation: Among those who divided their religion and became factions, each party rejoicing in what it has.
interpretation: The verse warns against letting religious allegiance fracture into rival factions that treat their own group’s position as sufficient and take pride in it. It calls believers back to sincere devotion to God’s guidance rather than sectarian self-satisfaction.

translation: When hardship touches people, they call upon their Lord, turning back to Him. Then, when He lets them taste mercy from Him, a group of them associate others with their Lord.
interpretation: The verse exposes the inconsistency of those who seek God alone in distress but, once relief comes, return to associating partners with Him. It calls them to remain faithful and grateful in ease as well as in hardship.

translation: So that they may deny what We have granted them. So enjoy yourselves; soon you will know.
interpretation: This is a warning to those who meet God’s blessings with denial: their enjoyment is only temporary, and they will soon face the consequences of their ingratitude.

translation: Or have We sent down to them an authority that speaks in support of what they used to associate with Him?
interpretation: The question challenges those who associate partners with God to produce any divine revelation that authorizes their practice; their beliefs have no revealed authority behind them.

translation: When We let people taste mercy, they rejoice in it; but if hardship befalls them because of what their own hands have done, they immediately despair.
interpretation: The verse points to the instability of people who let their circumstances govern their hearts: they rejoice in blessings yet lose hope when hardship comes. It calls them to recognize that neither ease nor difficulty should sever their trust in God and hope in His mercy.

translation: Have they not seen that Allah gives abundant provision to whom He wills and restricts it? Surely in that are signs for people who believe.
interpretation: The changing measure of people’s provision points to God’s wisdom and sovereignty, rather than serving as a simple measure of anyone’s worth. For those who believe, this is a reason to trust God in both abundance and hardship.

translation: So give the relative his due, and the needy person and the traveler. That is better for those who seek the pleasure of Allah, and they are the successful.
interpretation: The verse teaches that caring for relatives and those in need is part of sincere devotion to Allah: these rights should be fulfilled seeking His pleasure, and true success lies in that devotion.

translation: Whatever you give in usury, seeking to increase it through people’s wealth, does not increase with God. But whatever you give as alms, seeking God’s approval—those are the ones whose reward is multiplied.
interpretation: The verse teaches that worldly gain acquired through usury has no increase in worth with God, whereas giving sincerely for God’s sake brings a lasting, multiplied reward.

translation: Allah is the One who created you, then provided for you, then causes you to die, and then gives you life. Is there any among those you associate with Him who can do any of that? Exalted and far above what they associate with Him is He.
interpretation: The verse calls people to recognize that ultimate authority and worship belong only to the One on whom their entire existence depends. Anything treated as a partner to God is incapable of sharing that power, so associating others with Him has no sound basis.

translation: Corruption has appeared on land and sea because of what people’s hands have earned, so that He may let them taste some of what they have done, in the hope that they will return.
interpretation: The verse presents the harm people bring upon the world as a warning: its consequences may awaken them to turn back to God and change their ways, rather than persist in wrongdoing.

translation: Say, “Travel through the land and observe how those before you met their end. Most of them were idolaters.”
interpretation: The verse urges people to learn from the traces of earlier nations: their downfall is a warning against associating partners with God and turning away from His guidance.

translation: So set your face toward the upright religion before a Day comes from Allah that cannot be turned back. On that Day, people will be divided.
interpretation: The verse urges steadfast commitment to the true faith while there is still time, because the divinely appointed Day of Judgment cannot be postponed or averted, and people will then be separated according to how they responded to God.

translation: Whoever disbelieves bears the consequence of his disbelief, and whoever does righteous deeds prepares good for themselves.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes personal responsibility: faithlessness harms the one who chooses it, while righteous deeds lay the foundation for that person’s own lasting well-being.

translation: So that He may reward, out of His bounty, those who believe and do righteous deeds. Indeed, He does not love the disbelievers.
interpretation: The reward of faith and righteous action is ultimately a gift from God’s generosity, not something people can claim as a right; the verse also warns that persistent disbelief places a person outside His love.

translation: And among His signs is that He sends the winds as bearers of good news, so that He may let you taste of His mercy, that ships may sail by His command, that you may seek of His bounty, and that you may be grateful.
interpretation: The verse invites people to see the natural world not as independent or purposeless, but as part of God’s sustaining care. The benefits people receive through it are gifts that should deepen their awareness of their dependence on Him and lead them to gratitude.

translation: We certainly sent messengers before you to their peoples, and they came to them with clear proofs. Then We took retribution against those who committed crimes; and it was Our due to support the believers.
interpretation: The verse reassures the Prophet and the believers that their struggle follows a pattern seen throughout earlier communities: God’s messengers were sent with clear evidence, wrongdoing ultimately met with divine judgment, and God’s support for the believers is a promise—though its timing and form rest with Him.

translation: Allah is the One who sends the winds, which stir up clouds. He spreads them across the sky as He wills and makes them into fragments, and then you see rain emerge from within them. When He sends it upon whichever of His servants He wills, they rejoice.
interpretation: The verse presents rain as a sign of God’s deliberate care and power: what people depend on for life and welcome with joy is not beyond His governance. It invites trust in His mercy, even when relief comes in ways and at times people cannot control.

translation: Though before it was sent down upon them, they had indeed been despairing.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes how swiftly God’s mercy can transform a state of despair, inviting people not to lose hope when relief seems distant.

translation: So look at the آثار of Allah’s mercy: how He gives life to the earth after its death. Indeed, He is surely the One who gives life to the dead, and He has power over all things.
interpretation: The renewal of barren earth is a visible sign that resurrection is within God’s power; what seems lifeless is not beyond His ability to restore. The verse invites reflection on this sign as reassurance that divine mercy and power encompass both the natural world and human destiny.

translation: But if We sent a wind and they saw their crops turn yellow, they would thereafter persist in disbelief.
interpretation: The verse exposes how quickly people can turn from gratitude to denial when a blessing is damaged: despite having witnessed God’s signs and provision, they may respond to hardship with ingratitude rather than steadfast faith.

translation: Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear, nor can you make the deaf hear the call when they turn away and retreat.
interpretation: The verse teaches that guidance cannot be forced upon those who are inwardly closed to it: just as the dead cannot hear and the deaf who turn away cannot hear a call, a person who persistently rejects the truth cannot be made to accept it.

translation: You cannot guide the blind out of their misguidance. You can make hear only those who believe in Our signs, and so they submit.
interpretation: The verse describes spiritual blindness: a messenger can convey the truth, but cannot make those closed to it accept guidance. Those who believe in God’s signs are receptive to the message and respond with submission to Him.

translation: Allah is the One who created you in weakness, then after weakness gave you strength, then after strength brought weakness and gray hair. He creates whatever He wills, and He is the All-Knowing, the All-Powerful.
interpretation: The changes of human life reveal that strength is temporary and bestowed, not self-sustaining. Recognizing this should humble people and remind them that the One who governs every stage of their lives does so with complete knowledge and power.

translation: And on the Day the Hour is established, the guilty will swear that they had remained no longer than an hour. In this way they used to be turned away from the truth.
interpretation: Their oath reflects how brief their worldly life—and possibly their time in the grave—seems to them when confronted with the Resurrection. Their mistaken sense of time continues the misguidance by which they turned away from the truth in life.

translation: Those who were granted knowledge and faith will say, “You remained, as decreed in Allah’s Book, until the Day of Resurrection. This, then, is the Day of Resurrection—but you did not know.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the certainty of resurrection confronting those who had failed to recognize it: the span appointed by Allah has reached its end, and what they once did not know is now undeniable.

translation: On that Day, the excuses of those who did wrong will not benefit them, nor will they be given the chance to make amends.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that accountability is decisive: once judgment arrives, excuses cannot undo wrongdoing, and the opportunity to seek God’s approval through repentance and correction has passed.

translation: We have certainly set forth for people in this Qur’an every kind of example. Yet if you bring them a sign, those who disbelieve will surely say, “You are nothing but impostors.”
interpretation: The verse portrays people who reject guidance despite the Qur’an’s varied explanations and clear signs: their denial is not for lack of evidence, but leads them to dismiss the messengers with accusations rather than consider the truth.

translation: Thus Allah seals the hearts of those who do not know.
interpretation: The verse teaches that persistent ignorance of the truth can leave a person unable to recognize or accept guidance, as though the heart has become sealed.

translation: So be patient. Surely Allah’s promise is true, and do not let those who lack certainty unsettle you.
interpretation: The verse calls for steadfast trust in Allah’s promise: the doubts or provocations of those who lack conviction should not shake a believer’s resolve.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Alif, Lam, Mim.
interpretation: The opening invokes Allah’s mercy and places the recitation under His name. The meaning of the separate letters “Alif, Lam, Mim” is not established with certainty; one interpretation is that they are a divine sign whose ultimate meaning Allah knows best.

translation: These are the verses of the Wise Book.
interpretation: The verses being referred to are from a revelation whose wisdom is evident in its guidance and judgments, inviting people to reflect on its message and follow it.

translation: A guidance and mercy for those who excel in doing good.
interpretation: Divine guidance and mercy are especially received by those who seek to do what is right with sincerity and excellence.

translation: Those who establish prayer and give zakāh, and who are certain of the Hereafter.
interpretation: Their certainty in the Hereafter gives lasting purpose to their worship and generosity: they live aware that their choices have consequences beyond this life.

translation: Those are upon guidance from their Lord, and it is they who are successful.
interpretation: Their sound direction is a gift from God, and true success lies in remaining guided by Him and attaining the good He promises.

translation: Among people are those who purchase idle talk in order to mislead others from the way of God without knowledge, and who take it in mockery. For them is a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns against using distracting or frivolous speech to turn people away from God’s guidance, especially when doing so in ignorance and treating that guidance with contempt. Its condemnation concerns the purpose and attitude behind such conduct, and it warns that those who mock God’s way face a humiliating punishment.

translation: When Our verses are recited to him, he turns away in arrogance, as though he had not heard them—as though there were deafness in his ears. So give him news of a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse portrays a person whose pride makes him refuse to listen to divine guidance. The image of deafness describes a willful closing of the heart, not an inability to hear; the warning of punishment underscores the seriousness of rejecting truth arrogantly.

translation: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds will have Gardens of Bliss.
interpretation: The verse teaches that sincere faith is meant to shape a person’s actions; the promise of lasting bliss joins inward conviction with goodness lived out.

translation: They will abide therein forever. Allah’s promise is true, and He is the Almighty, the Wise.
interpretation: The verse assures that what God has promised will certainly come to pass: His power makes it sure, and His wisdom governs it with perfect justice.

translation: He created the heavens without pillars that you can see, and set firm mountains in the earth lest it sway with you. He spread throughout it every kind of creature, and We sent down water from the sky and brought forth in it every noble kind of plant.
interpretation: The verse invites reflection on the deliberate order and sustaining care woven into creation: the heavens, the earth, its living creatures, and its flourishing plants all point to a Creator whose power and wisdom uphold life.

translation: This is the creation of Allah; so show me what those besides Him have created. Rather, the wrongdoers are in clear error.
interpretation: The verse challenges those who associate others with Allah to produce evidence that their supposed deities possess any power of creation. It presents worship of anything besides the Creator as a failure to recognize the source of all existence, and therefore as manifest misguidance.

translation: And We certainly granted Luqman wisdom: “Be grateful to God.” Whoever is grateful is grateful for his own benefit; and whoever is ungrateful—surely God is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy.
interpretation: The verse teaches that gratitude is part of true wisdom: it acknowledges that blessings come from God and turns the heart toward Him. Its benefit returns to the grateful person, while ingratitude cannot diminish God in any way, for He needs nothing and is worthy of praise regardless.

translation: And [remember] when Luqman said to his son, as he advised him, “My dear son, do not associate anything with Allah. Indeed, associating others with Allah is a tremendous wrong.”
interpretation: Luqman teaches that the greatest wrong is to give worship or divine status to anything besides Allah, who alone deserves it. This wrong is ultimately against oneself: it misdirects devotion and gratitude away from their rightful source. His tender address shows that this serious warning is offered as loving guidance for his son.

translation: We have enjoined upon the human being kindness to his parents. His mother carried him in weakness upon weakness, and his weaning takes two years. Be grateful to Me and to your parents; to Me is the final return.
interpretation: The verse teaches that gratitude to God is inseparable from recognizing the care and sacrifice of one’s parents, especially a mother’s hardship. Honoring them is a profound duty, while the reminder of returning to God places that duty within the wider accountability of the life to come.

translation: But if they strive to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them; yet accompany them in this world with kindness, and follow the way of those who turn to Me. Then to Me is your return, and I will inform you of what you used to do.
interpretation: The verse teaches that devotion to God sets a boundary that even the strongest family ties cannot override, but that refusing a parent’s demand to compromise faith does not justify mistreating them. Conviction and kindness are to be held together: remain steadfast in belief, deal graciously with parents in worldly life, and take guidance from those who turn sincerely to God, mindful that all will ultimately answer to Him.

translation: “O my son, even if something were the weight of a mustard seed, hidden within a rock, in the heavens, or in the earth, Allah would bring it forth. Surely Allah is Subtle, All-Aware.”
interpretation: Luqman teaches his son that nothing is too small or too concealed to escape Allah’s knowledge: Allah is fully aware of every deed and can bring it to account wherever it may be hidden.

translation: “O my son, establish prayer, enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and be patient with whatever befalls you. Indeed, that is among the matters requiring firm resolve.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that devotion to God should shape one’s conduct toward others, and that acting for what is right may entail hardship. Patience here is steadfast commitment rather than passive surrender: it takes resolve to remain faithful and principled when facing difficulty.

translation: Do not turn your cheek away from people in contempt, nor walk upon the earth arrogantly. Surely God does not love anyone who is conceited and boastful.
interpretation: The verse teaches that humility should shape both how a person treats others and how they carry themselves. Dismissing people with disdain or displaying one’s status through arrogance reflects a pride that is contrary to what God loves.

translation: Be moderate in your pace, and lower your voice. Indeed, the harshest of sounds is the braying of donkeys.
interpretation: This counsel teaches that humility is reflected in ordinary conduct: a person should avoid both ostentation in the way they move and harshness in the way they speak. Measured speech and a composed manner show consideration for others and self-restraint.

translation: Do you not see that God has subjected for you all that is in the heavens and the earth, and has showered you with His blessings, both outward and inward? Yet among people are those who argue about God without knowledge, guidance, or an illuminating Scripture.
interpretation: The verse calls people to recognize that their lives are sustained by blessings they can see and others they may not perceive. In light of this, disputing about God without sound knowledge, true guidance, or revealed teaching reflects heedlessness and misplaced confidence rather than a reasoned search for truth.

translation: When they are told, “Follow what Allah has sent down,” they say, “Rather, we follow what we found our fathers following.” Even if Satan is calling them to the punishment of the Blaze?
interpretation: Blindly following inherited beliefs is no defense when they conflict with Allah’s guidance; the verse warns that such attachment can leave people following Satan toward punishment.

translation: Whoever submits himself to God while doing good has grasped the firmest handhold. To God belongs the final outcome of all affairs.
interpretation: True security lies in wholehearted surrender to God joined with righteous conduct; every matter ultimately rests in His judgment.

translation: Whoever disbelieves, let not his disbelief grieve you. To Us is their return, and We will inform them of what they did. Surely Allah knows what lies within hearts.
interpretation: The verse reassures the Prophet not to be overwhelmed by those who reject faith: their choices and deeds will ultimately be judged by Allah, who knows not only what they do but also the intentions and thoughts hidden within them.

translation: We let them enjoy themselves for a little while, then We drive them to a severe punishment.
interpretation: Their worldly enjoyment is only a brief respite; it does not spare them from the grave punishment they will ultimately be made to face.

translation: If you ask them, “Who created the heavens and the earth?” they will surely say, “Allah.” Say, “All praise belongs to Allah.” But most of them do not know.
interpretation: Their admission that Allah created all things should lead them to worship Him alone and be grateful to Him. Yet many fail to understand the implications of what they themselves acknowledge.

translation: To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. Indeed, Allah is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: Everything exists under Allah’s ownership and authority, while He depends on nothing in creation. His worthiness of praise is complete and does not rely on anyone’s recognition or gratitude.

translation: If every tree on earth were pens, and the sea—with seven more seas replenishing it—were ink, the words of Allah would not run out. Indeed, Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.
interpretation: The verse portrays the boundlessness of Allah’s knowledge, wisdom, and decrees: even an unimaginable abundance of means for recording them could never encompass them.

translation: Your creation and your resurrection are no harder than those of a single soul. Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.
interpretation: God’s creation and resurrection of all people are no more difficult for Him than creating or raising one person; nothing is beyond His power, and He fully hears and sees every person.

translation: Have you not seen that Allah causes the night to enter the day and the day to enter the night, and has subjected the sun and the moon, each running its course until an appointed term, and that Allah is fully aware of what you do?
interpretation: The precise order of the heavens points to Allah’s sovereign power and wisdom; just as nothing in creation lies beyond His control, no human deed is hidden from His knowledge, so people should live with awareness of their accountability to Him.

translation: That is because Allah is the Truth, and what they call upon besides Him is falsehood, and Allah is the Most High, the Great.
interpretation: The signs of order and power in creation point to Allah alone as the ultimate reality and rightful object of worship; anything relied upon as a rival to Him has no independent truth or power. His supremacy and greatness are absolute.

translation: Do you not see that ships sail through the sea by Allah’s grace, so that He may show you some of His signs? Surely in that are signs for everyone who is steadfast and grateful.
interpretation: The ships’ passage through the sea points to Allah’s care and power working through the means He has provided. Those who remain steadfast through hardship and grateful for blessings are especially able to recognize these signs and reflect on their source.

translation: When waves overwhelm them like canopies, they call upon Allah, devoting their worship sincerely to Him. But when He brings them safely to land, some remain faithful and moderate; yet none reject Our signs except one who is utterly treacherous and ungrateful.
interpretation: The verse exposes how hardship can strip away false dependencies and make people turn sincerely to God, while safety reveals whether that sincerity endures. It warns that knowingly betraying the truth and responding to God’s blessings with ingratitude are especially grave forms of denial.

translation: O people, be mindful of your Lord and fear a Day when no parent will avail their child in the least, nor will a child avail their parent in the least. Surely Allah’s promise is true, so do not let the life of this world deceive you, and do not let the Deceiver deceive you about Allah.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, family ties cannot take the place of each person’s own accountability before God. Remembering this should keep people from being lulled by worldly attractions or by false confidence that God’s promise and reckoning can be ignored or put off.

translation: Indeed, Allah has knowledge of the Hour. He sends down the rain and knows what is in the wombs. No soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die. Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing, All-Aware.
interpretation: The verse teaches that knowledge of the unseen belongs fully to Allah: He knows the timing of the Last Hour, the rain He sends, and all that concerns what is in the wombs. People, by contrast, cannot know their own future provision or where they will die. This recognition of human limits calls for humility and trust in Allah, whose knowledge encompasses every detail.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Alif, Lām, Mīm.
interpretation: Alif, Lām, and Mīm are among the Qur’an’s disjoint letters; their precise meaning is known to Allah, and they invite the listener to attend to the revelation that follows.

translation: The revelation of the Book, in which there is no doubt, is from the Lord of all worlds.
interpretation: The verse grounds the Qur’an’s authority in its divine source: its truth does not depend on human opinion or circumstance, but comes from the Lord who sustains all creation.
