translation: Or do they say, “He has fabricated it”? Rather, it is the truth from your Lord, so that you may warn a people to whom no warner came before you, that they may be guided.
interpretation: The verse answers the charge that the Qur’an was invented by affirming its divine origin and showing that the Prophet’s warning is a responsibility entrusted to him. The people’s lack of a prior warner makes this message a means by which they can recognize the truth and choose guidance.

translation: Allah is the One who created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them in six days, then established Himself over the Throne. You have no protector or intercessor besides Him. Will you not then take heed?
interpretation: The verse calls people to recognize that ultimate authority belongs to Allah alone: the One who created and governs all things is the only true source of protection, so no one should place ultimate trust in any other power.

translation: He directs the affair from heaven to earth; then it ascends to Him in a day whose measure is a thousand years by your reckoning.
interpretation: The verse conveys that God’s governance encompasses all creation, while the measure of time as humans experience it does not limit or define the divine order.

translation: That is Allah, the Knower of the unseen and the seen, the Almighty, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: Nothing hidden or manifest is beyond Allah’s knowledge; His absolute might is joined with mercy.

translation: Who perfected everything He created, and began the creation of humankind from clay.
interpretation: The verse invites reflection on the wisdom and care evident throughout creation, while reminding people that their origin is humble and their existence depends entirely on God.

translation: Then He made his offspring from an extract of a humble fluid.
interpretation: The verse points to the humble material origin of human beings, reminding them that their existence and continuation depend entirely on God’s creative power.

translation: Then He fashioned him and breathed into him of His spirit, and gave you hearing, sight, and hearts. Little thanks you give.
interpretation: The verse presents human life and the faculties of understanding as gifts from God. The attribution “of His spirit” signifies an honored spirit created by Him, not a part of God; the closing words call people to respond to these gifts with gratitude.

translation: They say, “When we have vanished into the earth, will we truly be brought forth in a new creation?” Rather, they disbelieve in the meeting with their Lord.
interpretation: Their question treats bodily decay as proof that resurrection cannot happen, but the verse identifies the deeper issue as their denial of standing before their Lord. Their disbelief is not merely uncertainty about how people could be recreated; it is rejection of the accountability that meeting God entails.

translation: Say, “The Angel of Death, who has been appointed over you, will take you in death; then you will be returned to your Lord.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that death is not an escape into nothingness: it occurs under God’s authority, and every person will ultimately return to Him to be judged for how they lived.

translation: If only you could see when the guilty hang their heads before their Lord, saying, “Our Lord, we have seen and heard. Send us back, and we will do righteous deeds; now we are certain.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the remorse of those who denied the truth: when its reality becomes undeniable, they ask for another chance to live righteously. Their certainty comes only after the opportunity to act has passed, underscoring that faith and good deeds must be embraced before the consequences are revealed.

translation: Had We willed, We could have given every soul its guidance; but My decree has come to pass: “I will surely fill Hell with jinn and humankind all together.”
interpretation: The verse affirms that God could have made every soul guided, but He has decreed that earthly life be a test in which people are accountable for how they respond to guidance. His warning of Hell is therefore a solemn declaration of the outcome for those who reject the truth, not a statement that He is unable to guide.

translation: So taste the punishment because you forgot the meeting of this Day of yours. Indeed, We have forsaken you; and taste the everlasting punishment for what you used to do.
interpretation: Their “forgetting” means they disregarded the coming judgment and lived without regard for accountability. God’s “forgetting” is a fitting requital: He leaves them to the punishment they earned, not that anything escapes His knowledge.

translation: Only those believe in Our signs who, when they are reminded of them, fall down in prostration and glorify their Lord with praise, and are not arrogant.
interpretation: True faith softens the heart: when God’s signs remind a person of the truth, they respond with humility, worship, and gratitude rather than pride.

translation: Their sides draw away from their beds as they call upon their Lord in fear and hope, and they give from what We have provided for them.
interpretation: The verse portrays devotion that is sincere and whole: believers willingly leave the comfort of sleep to turn to God, approaching Him with both reverent fear and hopeful trust. Their worship also shapes how they use their blessings, moving them to give generously from what they have received.

translation: No soul knows what joy has been concealed for them as a reward for what they used to do.
interpretation: The verse points to the surpassing, unimaginable nature of the reward God has prepared for the faithful: its delights are beyond what anyone can presently picture, and they are granted in return for their deeds.

translation: Is one who is a believer like one who is defiantly disobedient? They are not equal.
interpretation: Faith and deliberate defiance are not alike in worth or standing before God; a person’s choices shape a path whose spiritual consequences differ.

translation: As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, they will have the Gardens of Refuge as a welcoming abode for what they used to do.
interpretation: The verse presents Paradise as God’s generous welcome for the faithful: their righteous deeds are met with an abiding home of honor and peace.

translation: As for those who defiantly disobeyed, their refuge is the Fire. Whenever they try to come out of it, they will be returned to it, and they will be told, “Taste the punishment of the Fire that you used to deny.”
interpretation: The verse warns that persistent defiance and denial have grave consequences: in the Hereafter, those who rejected the reality of divine judgment will face it directly, with no escape from the punishment they once dismissed.

translation: We will surely make them taste the nearer punishment before the greater punishment, so that they may return.
interpretation: The trials and hardships of this life can serve as a merciful warning, turning people back from wrongdoing before they face the greater punishment of the Hereafter.

translation: And who is more unjust than one who is reminded of the signs of his Lord, then turns away from them? Indeed, We will exact retribution from the criminals.
interpretation: The verse warns that knowingly rejecting God’s guidance after it has been made clear is a grave injustice, and that such rejection does not go unanswered: those who persist in wrongdoing will face divine judgment.

translation: We certainly gave Moses the Scripture, so do not doubt meeting him; and We made it a guidance for the Children of Israel.
interpretation: The verse reassures the Prophet that Moses truly received divine revelation and that he would meet Moses, as he did during the Night Journey. Moses’ Scripture was guidance for his people, affirming the continuity of God’s guidance through His messengers.

translation: And We made from among them leaders who guided by Our command when they were patient and had firm conviction in Our signs.
interpretation: The verse teaches that true spiritual leadership is not simply a position of authority: it is a trust granted to those whose steadfast patience and certainty in God’s signs enable them to guide others in accordance with His direction.

translation: Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ.
interpretation: The verse teaches that disagreements about faith and truth will ultimately be settled by God, whose judgment is complete and just; people should therefore not assume that disputes left unresolved in this life will remain so.

translation: Has it not become clear to them how many generations We destroyed before them, whose dwellings they now walk through? Surely in that are signs. Will they not then listen?
interpretation: The ruins of earlier peoples are a warning: those who reject guidance should take heed from the fate of those who came before them and listen to the message before they meet a similar end.

translation: Have they not seen that We drive water to the barren land, then bring forth by it crops from which their livestock and they themselves eat? Will they not then see?
interpretation: The revival of barren land through water is a sign of God’s power to bring life where there was none. It calls people to recognize His sustaining care and not overlook the possibility of resurrection.

translation: They say, “When will this decisive judgment come, if you are truthful?”
interpretation: They challenge the believers, asking when God’s promised judgment will arrive, as though its delay proves the promise false.

translation: Say, “On the Day of Decision, the faith of those who disbelieved will not benefit them, nor will they be granted respite.”
interpretation: The verse warns that once God’s decisive judgment arrives, turning to faith at that moment cannot undo a life of rejection, and there will be no delay in which to seek another chance.

translation: So turn away from them and wait; indeed, they too are waiting.
interpretation: The Prophet is urged to remain steadfast rather than be disheartened by their rejection: the matter will reach its appointed outcome, and both he and his opponents await what is to come.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. O Prophet, be mindful of Allah and do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites. Surely Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: The command calls the Prophet to remain steadfast in devotion to Allah and not let pressure from opponents or hypocrites divert him from the guidance he has been given. The closing names affirm that Allah fully knows the circumstances and, in His wisdom, guides His Messenger to what is right.

translation: Follow what is revealed to you from your Lord. Indeed, Allah is fully aware of what you all do.
interpretation: The command calls the Prophet to remain guided by revelation rather than human pressure or preference, while reminding the community that Allah knows their deeds and intentions.

translation: And put your trust in Allah; Allah is sufficient as a Trustee.
interpretation: Rely on Allah and entrust your affairs to Him, confident that His care and judgment are sufficient.

translation: Allah has not placed two hearts within any man. Nor has He made your wives whom you declare to be like your mothers into your mothers, nor has He made your adopted sons your own sons. Those are words you utter with your mouths; Allah speaks the truth and guides to the way.
interpretation: The verse teaches that spoken claims do not change the realities Allah has established: declaring a wife forbidden like one’s mother does not make her a mother, and adoption does not create biological lineage. It calls for honesty about family relationships and for following Allah’s guidance rather than treating words as if they could alter the truth.

translation: Call them by the names of their fathers; that is more just in the sight of God. If you do not know their fathers, then they are your brothers in faith and your protégés. You will not be blamed for what you do by mistake, but only for what your hearts deliberately intend. God is ever-forgiving, most merciful.
interpretation: The verse directs believers to preserve a person’s true lineage rather than assign them a false one, while affirming that family-like bonds of faith and care remain meaningful. It distinguishes honest mistakes from deliberate misrepresentation, and closes with reassurance that God forgives and shows mercy.

translation: The Prophet has a greater claim on the believers than they have on themselves, and his wives are their mothers. And in the Book of God, blood relatives have a greater claim on one another than the believers and the emigrants—except that you may show kindness to your allies. This is inscribed in the Book.
interpretation: The verse establishes the Prophet’s authority and the unique respect owed to his household, while making kinship the primary basis for inheritance and legal priority over bonds formed through faith and migration. It nevertheless leaves room to honor those bonds through acts of kindness, in keeping with God’s recorded command.

translation: And when We took from the prophets their covenant—and from you, and from Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus son of Mary—and We took from them a solemn covenant.
interpretation: The solemn covenant signifies the grave responsibility entrusted to the prophets to faithfully convey God’s guidance; the verse’s emphasis on its weight highlights the seriousness of that trust and the unity of their prophetic mission.

translation: So that He may question the truthful about their truthfulness; and He has prepared for the disbelievers a painful punishment.
interpretation: The questioning is a moment of accountability and witness: those who were truthful are called to answer for their faithfulness, while those who rejected the truth face the consequence God has prepared. It is not because God lacks knowledge, but to make the truth of their conduct manifest.

translation: O you who believe, remember God’s favor upon you when forces came against you, and We sent upon them a wind and forces you could not see. God sees all that you do.
interpretation: The verse calls believers to recognize that deliverance in moments of overwhelming danger may come through means beyond their sight or control. Remembering this favor should deepen their trust in God and their gratitude, while the closing reminder that God sees their deeds calls them to remain sincere and steadfast.

translation: When they came at you from above you and from below you, when eyes grew wild and hearts rose to throats, and you entertained all kinds of thoughts about Allah.
interpretation: The verse portrays a moment of overwhelming danger in which fear strained people’s composure and tested their trust in God. Under such pressure, their thoughts about what God would decree were shaken and varied.

translation: There and then the believers were tested and shaken with a severe shaking.
interpretation: The verse portrays the believers’ ordeal as a profound trial that brought their faith under immense pressure and exposed their steadfastness amid fear and hardship.

translation: And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts was sickness said, “Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion.”
interpretation: Their words expose how fear and weak faith had led them to distrust Allah’s promise: faced with hardship, they mistook the trial for proof that the promise was false, rather than recognizing it as a test of their trust.

translation: And when a group of them said, “People of Yathrib, you have no place to stand, so return.” Another group asked the Prophet for permission, saying, “Our homes are exposed,” though they were not exposed. They sought only to flee.
interpretation: The verse exposes how fear led some people to urge others to abandon their post, while others used concern for their homes as a pretext to leave. Their claim was not genuine: the real motive was escape from danger rather than a need to protect their homes.

translation: Had it been entered upon them from every side, and had they been called to renounce their faith, they would have done so, hesitating over it only briefly.
interpretation: The verse exposes the hollowness of their professed loyalty: faced with pressure from every direction, they would quickly have abandoned their commitment to faith.

translation: They had certainly pledged to Allah beforehand that they would not turn their backs; and a covenant with Allah is something for which one will be held to account.
interpretation: A pledge made in God’s name is not an empty promise: it binds the person to act with integrity, especially when fulfilling it becomes difficult. The verse warns that people cannot evade responsibility for commitments they have made before God.

translation: Say, “Flight will never benefit you if you flee from death or being killed; even then, you will enjoy life only briefly.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that fleeing cannot ultimately escape death when its appointed time arrives. At most, flight may postpone hardship for a short while, so people should not mistake it for lasting security.

translation: Say, “Who can protect you from Allah if He intends harm for you, or intends mercy for you?” They will find no protector or helper for themselves besides Allah.
interpretation: No person or power can override Allah’s decree: neither can anyone avert what He wills, nor prevent the mercy He grants. The verse calls people to place their ultimate trust in Him rather than imagining that worldly allies can secure them independently of Him.

translation: Allah already knows those among you who hinder others, and those who say to their brothers, “Come over to us.” They come to the fighting only rarely.
interpretation: The verse warns that no effort to obstruct the believers or draw them away from their duty is hidden from God. Those who urge others to stay with them rather than face hardship reveal their unwillingness to bear the struggle themselves, appearing only occasionally when fighting is required.

translation: They are miserly toward you. When fear comes, you see them looking at you, their eyes rolling like someone overcome by death. But when the fear passes, they lash out at you with sharp tongues, greedy for worldly gains. Such people have not truly believed, so God has rendered their deeds void; that is easy for God.
interpretation: The verse exposes the hollowness of faith that is governed by self-interest: in danger, these people shrink from responsibility, and in safety, they use their words to demand their share of worldly benefits. Their conduct shows that outward affiliation alone cannot give deeds spiritual worth when sincere faith is absent.

translation: They think the confederates have not yet departed. And if the confederates were to come again, they would wish they were out among the Bedouins, asking for news about you. And if they were with you, they would fight only a little.
interpretation: The verse exposes the fear and lack of commitment of those who sought to avoid danger: even while claiming association with the believers, their true concern was personal safety, and they would have offered little support when tested.

translation: Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah you have an excellent example for whoever hopes in Allah and the Last Day and remembers Allah often.
interpretation: The verse calls believers to take the Prophet as their model, following his faithfulness and conduct, especially when doing so requires patience and steadfastness. Such emulation grows from sincere hope in Allah, accountability in the Hereafter, and frequent remembrance of Allah.

translation: When the believers saw the confederate forces, they said, “This is what Allah and His Messenger promised us, and Allah and His Messenger have spoken the truth.” It only increased them in faith and surrender.
interpretation: The believers understood the arrival of the enemy not as a reason to doubt, but as the trial Allah and His Messenger had foretold. Seeing the promise fulfilled strengthened their trust in Allah and their willingness to submit to Him.

translation: Among the believers are men who have been true to the covenant they made with God. Some have fulfilled their pledge, and others are still awaiting their turn; and they have never altered their commitment in any way.
interpretation: The verse presents unwavering faithfulness as the mark of sincere belief: whether a person has already given their life in fulfilling their pledge or remains steadfast while awaiting what lies ahead, they do not compromise the covenant they have made with God.

translation: So that Allah may reward the truthful for their truthfulness, and punish the hypocrites if He wills, or accept their repentance. Indeed, Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse affirms that truthfulness is not merely a claim but a steadfastness Allah rewards, while hypocrisy exposes a person to judgment. Yet punishment is not presented as inevitable: Allah may accept the hypocrites’ repentance, leaving the door open to return and underscoring that His judgment is joined with forgiveness and mercy.

translation: Allah turned back those who disbelieved in their rage, having gained no advantage. Allah spared the believers from fighting. Allah is ever Powerful, Almighty.
interpretation: The verse teaches that the coalition’s strength and hostility could not overcome Allah’s protection of the believers; their plans came to nothing, while Allah’s power and might remain supreme.

translation: And He brought down from their strongholds those among the People of the Scripture who had supported them, and cast terror into their hearts: some you killed, and some you took captive.
interpretation: The verse presents the defeat of those who had allied themselves against the believers as an outcome brought about by God. Their fortified positions did not protect them once fear overtook them, while the believers prevailed over them.

translation: And He made you inherit their land, their homes, their wealth, and a land you had not yet set foot upon. And Allah is capable of all things.
interpretation: The verse teaches that victory and provision come by God’s power: He granted the believers what they had not obtained by their own strength, and His ability extends to blessings and lands still beyond their reach.

translation: O Prophet, say to your wives: “If you desire the life of this world and its adornment, then come, and I will provide for you and release you with a gracious release.”
interpretation: The verse presents the Prophet’s wives with an honest choice: worldly comforts, if that is what they sought, would be met with fair provision and an honorable separation. It emphasizes that such a separation should be handled with generosity and dignity, not resentment or harm.

translation: But if you desire Allah, His Messenger, and the abode of the Hereafter, then Allah has prepared a great reward for those among you who do good.
interpretation: The verse presents devotion to Allah and His Messenger, and prioritizing the Hereafter, as a choice whose worth is shown through righteous conduct; those who meet that choice with excellence are promised a great reward.

translation: O wives of the Prophet, whoever among you commits a manifest wrongdoing, her punishment will be doubled; and that is easy for Allah.
interpretation: The verse teaches that greater honor and closeness to a prophetic household bring greater responsibility: conduct by the Prophet’s wives would carry particular moral influence, so accountability for a grave, evident wrong would be correspondingly weightier.

translation: Whoever among you is devoutly obedient to Allah and His Messenger and does righteous deeds, We will grant her her reward twice over, and We have prepared for her a noble provision.
interpretation: Addressing the Prophet’s wives, the verse teaches that their closeness to the Messenger brings a heightened responsibility to obey Allah and live righteously; in keeping with that responsibility, their reward is multiplied and they are promised an honored provision.

translation: O wives of the Prophet, you are not like other women, if you are mindful of God. So do not be enticing in speech, lest one whose heart is diseased become desirous; rather, speak in an appropriate manner.
interpretation: The verse teaches that the Prophet’s wives, because of their distinguished responsibility, should uphold a particularly careful standard of conduct. Their speech should be dignified and clear—not inviting improper attention—while remaining proper and respectful.

translation: And remain in your homes, and do not display yourselves as women did in the former age of ignorance. Establish prayer, give zakah, and obey Allah and His Messenger. Allah only intends to remove impurity from you, O people of the household, and to purify you completely.
interpretation: The verse presents the honor of the Prophet’s household as bound to dignified conduct, worship, and obedience. Its mention of purification points to Allah’s care in cleansing the household from moral and spiritual defilement; it is an encouragement to live by that guidance, not a release from it.

translation: And remember what is recited in your homes of Allah’s verses and wisdom. Indeed, Allah is ever Subtle, All-Aware.
interpretation: You are called to keep the revelation and wisdom taught in your homes present in your hearts and conduct. Allah’s subtle care and complete knowledge encompass both what is openly taught and what is inwardly intended.

translation: Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women, the believing men and believing women, the devoutly obedient men and devoutly obedient women, the truthful men and truthful women, the patient men and patient women, the humble men and humble women, the charitable men and charitable women, the fasting men and fasting women, the men who guard their chastity and the women who guard theirs, and the men who remember Allah often and the women who remember—Allah has prepared for them forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: The verse makes clear that closeness to God and reward are grounded in faith and righteous character, not gender. By naming men and women alongside one another in every quality, it affirms that both are equally accountable and equally promised God’s forgiveness and great reward when they embody these virtues.

translation: It is not for a believing man or woman, when God and His Messenger have decided a matter, to have any choice in their affair. Whoever disobeys God and His Messenger has surely strayed into manifest error.
interpretation: The verse teaches that faith calls for trustful submission to God’s guidance and the Messenger’s authoritative judgment, rather than treating personal preference as a higher authority. This submission is an expression of devotion, while knowingly rejecting that guidance leads away from the straight path.

translation: And [remember] when you said to the one whom Allah had favored and whom you had favored, “Keep your wife and be mindful of Allah,” while concealing within yourself what Allah was to disclose, and fearing people, though Allah has greater right that you fear Him. Then, when Zayd had no longer any need for her, We married her to you, so that believers would have no difficulty regarding the wives of their adopted sons when those sons have no longer any need for them. And Allah’s command is always carried out.
interpretation: The verse establishes that an adopted son does not have the same legal status as a biological son in matters of marriage. By making the Prophet’s marriage to Zayd’s former wife a public example, Allah removed the stigma and hardship surrounding this distinction. The Prophet’s hesitation reflects his concern about people’s reactions, while the verse teaches that obedience to Allah’s guidance must take precedence over fear of public opinion.

translation: There is no blame upon the Prophet concerning what Allah has ordained for him. This has been Allah’s way with those who came before; and Allah’s command is a decree already determined.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the Prophet is not to be reproached for carrying out what Allah made lawful and ordained for him. His conduct follows the established way of God’s messengers before him, and what God decrees comes about with certainty and according to His wisdom.

translation: Those who convey the messages of Allah and fear Him, and fear no one except Allah. And Allah is sufficient as a Reckoner.
interpretation: Faithful conveyance of God’s message requires sincerity and courage: reverence for God must outweigh fear of people. Since God alone is the ultimate judge and takes full account, the messenger need not distort the truth to win people’s approval or avoid their blame.

translation: Muhammad is not the father of any of your men, but he is the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets. And Allah has full knowledge of all things.
interpretation: The verse distinguishes Muhammad’s prophetic authority from ordinary lineage: his relationship to the community rests on his mission, not on being the biological father of its men. Calling him the Seal of the Prophets affirms that prophethood reaches its completion with him, and God’s knowledge encompasses the wisdom and consequences of this decree.

translation: O you who believe, remember Allah with abundant remembrance.
interpretation: Believers are urged to keep Allah continually in mind, letting remembrance shape their hearts and guide their lives.

translation: And glorify Him morning and evening.
interpretation: Glorify Allah by declaring Him free of every imperfection and remember Him regularly throughout the day; morning and evening point to devotion that continues across all times.

translation: He is the One who bestows blessings upon you, and His angels pray for you, to bring you out of darknesses into the light. And He is ever Merciful to the believers.
interpretation: The verse portrays guidance as an expression of God’s care: He honors and shows mercy to believers, while the angels pray for them, as they are led from the darkness of error and confusion into the light of faith. This assurance grounds their hope in God’s enduring mercy.

translation: Their greeting on the Day they meet Him will be, “Peace”; and He has prepared for them a noble reward.
interpretation: When the believers meet their Lord, they will be welcomed with peace and security, and rewarded with an honor beyond what they could earn or imagine.

translation: O Prophet, We have sent you as a witness, a bearer of glad tidings, and a warner.
interpretation: The Prophet’s mission encompasses both accountability and mercy: he bears witness by conveying God’s message, offers hope to those who respond faithfully, and warns those who turn away of the consequences.

translation: And as one who calls to Allah by His permission, and as a radiant lamp.
interpretation: The verse portrays the Prophet’s mission as divinely authorized guidance: he calls people toward Allah, and his message illuminates the way for those seeking truth.

translation: And give the believers glad tidings that they will have a great bounty from Allah.
interpretation: The believers are promised that Allah’s generosity toward them will be abundant, giving them reason to place their hope and trust in Him.

translation: Do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites. Disregard their hurtful conduct, and place your trust in Allah; Allah is sufficient as the One entrusted with all affairs.
interpretation: The verse calls for steadfastness under pressure: do not compromise what Allah has commanded to appease those who oppose it. Respond to their hurt without letting it divert you from your duty, and rely on Allah to manage what lies beyond your control.

translation: O you who believe, when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them, you have no waiting period to require of them. So provide for them and release them graciously.
interpretation: The verse teaches that a woman divorced before the marriage is consummated is not required to observe a waiting period. The husband is nevertheless instructed to provide for her and end the marriage with kindness and dignity.

translation: O Prophet, We have made lawful for you your wives to whom you have given their bridal dues, and those whom your right hand possesses from what God has granted you, and the daughters of your paternal uncles and aunts, and the daughters of your maternal uncles and aunts who migrated with you; and any believing woman who offers herself to the Prophet, if the Prophet wishes to marry her—this is exclusive to you, apart from the believers. We know what We have prescribed for them concerning their wives and those whom their right hands possess, so that there may be no hardship upon you. And God is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse presents the Prophet’s family arrangements as governed by specific divine rulings, distinct in some respects from those prescribed for other believers. Its closing emphasis is that these provisions are not an unrestricted personal privilege: they belong to the framework of revelation, which sets different responsibilities and permissions while removing hardship. The mention of God’s forgiveness and mercy places those rulings within a broader assurance of divine compassion.

translation: You may defer whichever of them you wish and bring close whichever you wish. And if you desire any of those you had set aside, there is no blame upon you. That is more likely to comfort them, keep them from grieving, and make them content with what you give them all. Allah knows what is in your hearts, and Allah is All-Knowing, Forbearing.
interpretation: The verse grants the Prophet ﷺ discretion in arranging time with his wives, including returning to one whose turn had been deferred, so that they would feel reassured and treated with consideration. Their outward acceptance does not conceal anything from Allah: He knows their hearts and, in His forbearance, does not hasten to punish.

translation: It is not lawful for you to marry women after this, nor to replace your wives with other wives, even if their beauty pleases you—except those whom your right hand possesses. And Allah is ever Watchful over all things.
interpretation: The verse sets a specific limit on the Prophet’s marriages, directing him to remain with his existing wives rather than pursue other marriages or exchange them for others. Its closing reminder that Allah watches all things underscores that this restriction, like all divine commands, is subject to His knowledge and accountability.

translation: O you who believe, do not enter the homes of the Prophet unless you are invited for a meal, and do not wait around for it to be prepared. But when you are invited, then enter; and when you have eaten, disperse, without lingering for conversation. That would indeed trouble the Prophet, but he is too shy to tell you; yet God is not shy of the truth. When you ask his wives for something, ask them from behind a screen. That is purer for your hearts and their hearts. It is not for you to offend the Messenger of God, nor ever to marry his wives after him. That would indeed be grave in God’s sight.
interpretation: The verse teaches that faith includes respecting people’s privacy and not imposing on their time or homes, even when courtesy makes them reluctant to object. Its instruction to speak to the Prophet’s wives from behind a screen establishes a boundary suited to the Prophet’s household and intended to protect the dignity and purity of those involved. The prohibition on marrying his wives after him further underscores the exceptional honor of his household and the seriousness of causing him harm.

translation: Whether you reveal something or conceal it, Allah has always known all things.
interpretation: Nothing is hidden from Allah: He knows both what people make known and what they keep within themselves, so a person’s inner intentions matter just as much as outward actions.

translation: There is no blame upon them regarding their fathers, their sons, their brothers, their brothers’ sons, their sisters’ sons, their women, or those whom their right hands possess. And be mindful of Allah. Indeed, Allah is ever Witness over all things.
interpretation: The verse clarifies that the Prophet’s wives may appear without the same restrictions before these close relatives and specified groups, while reminding them that this allowance remains within a life of God-consciousness. Allah’s witness over everything means that both the permission and the conduct of those who receive it are known to Him.

translation: Indeed, Allah and His angels bless the Prophet. O you who believe, invoke blessings upon him and greet him with peace in full measure.
interpretation: Allah honors the Prophet and the angels pray for his blessing; believers are therefore commanded to honor him by asking Allah to bless him and by greeting him with peace, sincerely and wholeheartedly.

translation: Indeed, those who offend Allah and His Messenger—Allah has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter, and has prepared for them a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: Offending Allah does not diminish Him; rather, it means showing contempt for Him through rejection or defiance, while offending His Messenger includes insulting or mistreating him and opposing his message. The verse warns that such deliberate hostility brings exclusion from divine mercy and disgraceful punishment.

translation: And those who harm believing men and believing women for something they have not done have indeed burdened themselves with slander and manifest sin.
interpretation: The verse warns that unjustly harming believers—by false accusations or other wrongdoing—makes the perpetrator accountable for grave injustice, even when the victims have committed no offense to warrant it.

translation: O Prophet, tell your wives, your daughters, and the women of the believers to draw their outer garments over themselves. That is more likely to make them recognized and not be harmed. And Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: The verse instructs believing women to dress with modesty and dignity in public, drawing their outer garments around themselves. It presents this as a means of being recognized and treated respectfully, in a setting where women could face harassment, while closing with a reminder of God’s forgiveness and mercy.

translation: If the hypocrites, those in whose hearts is sickness, and those who spread alarming rumors in Medina do not desist, We will surely empower you against them; then they will remain your neighbors there only briefly.
interpretation: The verse warns those who undermine the community through hypocrisy, hostility, and rumor-spreading that their conduct will not be tolerated indefinitely. If they persist, the Prophet will be authorized to act against them, and they will lose their place of safety and residence in Medina.

translation: Accursed; wherever they are found, they will be seized and killed utterly.
interpretation: In its context, this is a severe warning concerning those who persist in hostile agitation and corruption: they are under divine condemnation, and the emphatic wording conveys the gravity of the punishment described.

translation: Such has been God’s way with those who came before, and you will never find any change in God’s way.
interpretation: God’s dealings follow an established, consistent pattern: the consequences He decrees are not altered to favor one generation over another.

translation: People ask you about the Hour. Say, “Knowledge of it belongs only to Allah.” And what could make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near.
interpretation: The verse redirects attention from trying to determine the Hour’s timing to recognizing that its knowledge belongs to Allah. Its possible nearness calls people to live prepared for it rather than assume they have time.

translation: Indeed, Allah has cursed the disbelievers and prepared for them a blazing Fire.
interpretation: The verse warns that persistent rejection of faith carries the grave consequence of being excluded from God’s mercy and facing punishment.

translation: They will abide therein forever; they will find no protector or helper.
interpretation: Their state is everlasting, and no one will be able to protect them from it or come to their aid.

translation: On the Day their faces are turned about in the Fire, they will say, “If only we had obeyed Allah and obeyed the Messenger.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the regret of those who recognize too late that rejecting divine guidance brought them to ruin. Their words stress that obedience to Allah and His Messenger was the path they should have followed while they still had the chance.

translation: And they will say, “Our Lord, we obeyed our leaders and our elders, and they led us astray from the way.”
interpretation: The verse warns that blindly following influential people does not remove one’s responsibility before God. A person must discern whether those they follow are guiding them toward truth, rather than surrendering their judgment and later blaming others for their misguidance.

translation: Our Lord, give them double the punishment, and curse them with a mighty curse.
interpretation: Those who were led astray call upon God to intensify the punishment of the leaders who misled them and to banish them utterly from His mercy. Their plea expresses the depth of their regret, though blaming their leaders does not erase their own responsibility for following them.

translation: O you who believe, do not be like those who harmed Moses; Allah cleared him of what they alleged, and he was held in high esteem by Allah.
interpretation: Believers are warned against harming or unjustly accusing God’s messengers. False accusations do not diminish a person’s standing with God; He knows the truth and vindicates whom He wills.

translation: O you who believe, be mindful of Allah and speak words that are upright and true.
interpretation: Faith should shape not only what a person does but how they speak: their words should be truthful, fair, and responsible, helping set matters right rather than misleading or causing harm.

translation: He will set your deeds right for you and forgive your sins. Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has indeed achieved a great triumph.
interpretation: Obedience to Allah and His Messenger brings divine guidance that rectifies one’s actions, along with forgiveness; true success is therefore found in living by their guidance.

translation: Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens, the earth, and the mountains, but they refused to bear it and were afraid of it; yet the human being bore it. Indeed, he has been deeply unjust and ignorant.
interpretation: The Trust is the responsibility to answer to God for one’s choices and fulfill His commands. The verse portrays humanity’s acceptance of this weight as a profound responsibility: people can choose obedience, yet often wrong themselves through injustice and fail to recognize the consequences of what they have undertaken.

translation: So that Allah may punish hypocritical men and women and polytheist men and women, and turn in mercy to believing men and women. And Allah is Ever-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse affirms that Allah’s judgment is just: persistent hypocrisy and associating partners with Him incur punishment, while the believers receive His mercy. Its closing names remind us that the door of repentance and forgiveness remains open, for Allah is abundantly forgiving and merciful.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Praise belongs to Allah, to whom belongs all that is in the heavens and the earth; and to Him belongs all praise in the Hereafter. He is the All-Wise, the All-Aware.
interpretation: Because Allah alone owns all that exists, all praise ultimately belongs to Him in this life and the next. His wisdom governs what He decrees, and His complete awareness encompasses every matter.

translation: He knows what enters the earth and what emerges from it, what descends from the heaven and what ascends into it; and He is the Most Merciful, the All-Forgiving.
interpretation: Nothing is hidden from God—not what is buried or concealed in the earth, nor what comes forth from it, nor any descent or ascent through the heavens. His complete knowledge is accompanied by mercy and forgiveness, so His awareness of every deed is also a source of hope for those who turn to Him.

translation: Those who disbelieve say, “The Hour will never come to us.” Say, “Yes indeed, by my Lord, it will surely come to you—the Knower of the unseen. Not even the weight of an atom in the heavens or the earth escapes Him, nor anything smaller or greater, but it is recorded in a clear Book.”
interpretation: The oath affirms that the Resurrection is certain, while God’s perfect knowledge and clear record of every deed assure that nothing will be overlooked when people are held to account.

translation: So that He may reward those who believe and do righteous deeds. For them is forgiveness and a generous provision.
interpretation: The verse points to God’s purpose in bringing people to account: those who respond with faith and righteous action are met with His forgiveness and a lasting, honorable bounty.

translation: Those who strive against Our signs, seeking to thwart them, will have a punishment of painful torment.
interpretation: The verse warns that those who deliberately oppose God’s signs and try to undermine their truth cannot escape accountability; their defiance leads to severe punishment.

translation: Those who have been given knowledge see that what has been sent down to you from your Lord is the truth, and that it guides to the path of the Almighty, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: True understanding leads people to recognize the revelation as divine truth and to trust its guidance toward God, whose might is absolute and whose praise is deserved.

translation: Those who disbelieve say, “Shall we point you to a man who tells you that, when you have been completely scattered, you will indeed be created anew?”
interpretation: They speak mockingly of the Prophet’s promise of resurrection, treating the return of a body reduced to fragments as impossible, while the verse presents their disbelief as ridicule rather than a reasoned answer to God’s power.

translation: Has he fabricated a lie about Allah, or is he possessed by madness? Rather, those who do not believe in the Hereafter are in punishment and profound misguidance.
interpretation: The verse rejects the accusations made against the Messenger and shows that the real misguidance lies in denying the Hereafter: such denial leads people toward punishment, not toward truth.

translation: Have they not looked at what lies before them and behind them of the heaven and the earth? If We will, We can cause the earth to swallow them, or make fragments of the sky fall upon them. Surely in this is a sign for every servant who turns back to God.
interpretation: The vast heaven and earth surrounding people testify to God’s power and authority. Their security is not something they can take for granted: God could bring it to an end in an instant. The verse calls people to humility and to turn back to Him, recognizing the warning in the world around them.

translation: And We certainly bestowed upon David a favor from Us: “O mountains, echo praises with him, and you too, birds!” And We made iron pliable for him.
interpretation: David’s gifts show that divine power can make both the natural world and human skill serve a sacred purpose: the mountains and birds joined his praise, while pliable iron enabled him to work with strength and ability granted by God.

translation: Make full-length coats of mail, and measure carefully the links in their making. And do righteous deeds; indeed, I see all that you do.
interpretation: David’s skill in making armor is presented as a trust to be practiced with care and precision, alongside a broader duty to act righteously. The reminder that God sees all deeds connects even practical work with moral accountability.

translation: And for Solomon [We subjected] the wind: its morning course was a month’s journey, and its evening course was a month’s journey. And We caused a spring of molten copper to flow for him. And among the jinn were those who worked before him by permission of his Lord. Whoever among them deviated from Our command, We made him taste the punishment of the Blaze.
interpretation: Solomon’s extraordinary power over the wind and the jinn was a gift granted and governed by God, not an independent power of his own. The jinn’s work remained subject to God’s command, and any who disobeyed faced punishment—showing that even remarkable authority and ability operate within divine limits and accountability.

translation: They made for him whatever he wished: sanctuaries, statues, basins as large as reservoirs, and firmly fixed cooking pots. “Work gratefully, O family of David; yet few of My servants are truly grateful.”
interpretation: The verse presents the remarkable works granted to David’s household as blessings that called for active gratitude: serving God through what they did, not merely acknowledging what they had received. Its closing words caution that genuine, sustained gratitude is uncommon.

translation: When We decreed death for him, nothing disclosed his death to them except a creature of the earth eating away at his staff. Then, when he fell, the jinn realized that if they had known the unseen, they would not have remained in humiliating labor.
interpretation: The verse shows that the jinn had no knowledge of the unseen: they continued their labor, unaware that Solomon had died, until his staff gave way. Knowledge of what is hidden belongs to God alone.

translation: There was indeed a sign for the people of Sabaʾ in their homeland: two gardens, one on the right and one on the left. “Eat from your Lord’s provision and give thanks to Him: a good land and a forgiving Lord.”
interpretation: The gardens and fertile homeland were signs of God’s generosity, meant to lead the people to gratitude. The verse presents their well-being as a blessing paired with a call to worship and thankfulness, while “a forgiving Lord” emphasizes that God welcomes those who turn back to Him.

translation: But they turned away, so We sent upon them the flood of al-ʿArim, and replaced their two gardens with two gardens bearing bitter fruit, tamarisk, and a few lote trees.
interpretation: Their turning away from gratitude brought the loss of the abundance they had enjoyed. The replacement gardens—with bitter, scant produce—show how swiftly prosperity can be taken away when people reject the blessings entrusted to them.

translation: That is how We repaid them for their ingratitude. And do We repay anyone but the ungrateful?
interpretation: The verse frames the punishment as a just consequence of persistent ingratitude and rejection of God’s blessings, rather than as arbitrary punishment. Its rhetorical question underscores that such recompense is directed at those who persist in denying and failing to appreciate those blessings.

translation: And We placed between them and the towns We had blessed other towns in plain sight, and We measured out the journey between them: “Travel through them by night and day in safety.”
interpretation: The verse presents an ordered, secure network of settlements and travel as a blessing made readily available. Its underlying emphasis is that such ease and safety are gifts to be recognized with gratitude, not taken for granted.

translation: They said, “Our Lord, make the stages of our journeys farther apart.” They wronged themselves, so We made them a tale told by others and scattered them completely. Surely in this are signs for everyone who is steadfast and grateful.
interpretation: After taking ease and security for granted, they asked for a harder life and rejected the blessings they had been given. Their downfall warns that blessings can be lost when met with ingratitude, while those who remain steadfast through hardship and grateful in ease can recognize the lesson in what happens.

translation: And Iblis’s expectation of them proved true, so they followed him—except for a group of the believers.
interpretation: The verse warns that Satan’s influence succeeds when people give in to temptation, while sincere faith can protect people from following his path.

translation: He had no authority over them, except that We might make evident who believes in the Hereafter and who is in doubt about it. And your Lord is Guardian over all things.
interpretation: God’s allowing Satan to tempt people does not mean Satan can compel them or escape God’s control. The trial makes people’s choices clear in practice: who trusts in the Hereafter and who doubts it. This does not imply that God lacked knowledge beforehand; rather, their choices are brought into actuality, while God remains fully aware and watchful over all things.

translation: Say, “Call upon those you claim [to be gods] besides Allah. They possess not even the weight of an atom in the heavens or on earth; they have no share in either, and He has no supporter among them.”
interpretation: The verse rejects the worship of anything besides Allah: the beings invoked have no independent power or ownership, no share in governing creation, and no role in assisting Allah. Their inability to claim any of these makes worship and supplication due to Allah alone.

translation: Intercession with Him benefits no one except those for whom He grants permission. When the terror is lifted from their hearts, they ask, “What has your Lord said?” They reply, “The truth.” He is the Most High, the Great.
interpretation: The verse affirms that intercession is never an independent power: it has effect only by God’s permission. The angels’ awe at His command, and their confirmation that He has spoken the truth, underscore His absolute authority and the certainty of His revelation.

translation: Say, “Who provides for you from the heavens and the earth?” Say, “Allah.” And indeed, either we or you are surely upon guidance or in clear error.
interpretation: The verse directs people to recognize that provision comes from Allah, then presents the disagreement in a strikingly measured way: one side must be guided and the other plainly mistaken. This invites the listener to weigh the evidence sincerely rather than reject the message out of hostility.

translation: Say, “You will not be questioned about what we have committed, nor will we be questioned about what you do.”
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that each person is accountable for their own deeds: neither group bears responsibility for the other’s actions.

translation: Say, “Our Lord will gather us together, then He will judge between us with truth. He is the Decisive Judge, the All-Knowing.”
interpretation: The verse places the final resolution of disagreement in God’s hands: His judgment uncovers the truth without bias or error, because He knows fully what people conceal and what they intend.

translation: Say, “Show me those whom you have joined with Him as partners.” No indeed! Rather, He is Allah, the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: The verse challenges those who claim that others share in God’s divinity to produce any true basis for that claim. Their supposed partners have no share in His authority; all power and wisdom belong to Allah alone.

translation: We have sent you only to all people, as a bearer of glad tidings and a warner, but most people do not know.
interpretation: The Prophet’s message is universal, addressed to all humanity rather than a particular people. The verse also points to how many fail to recognize the reach and significance of this mission.

translation: And they say, “When will this promise come to pass, if you are truthful?”
interpretation: Their question is a challenge: they demand a date for the promised divine reckoning as a way of expressing doubt, rather than seeking guidance about it.

translation: Say, “You have an appointed day that you can neither delay by an hour nor bring forward.”
interpretation: The appointed day is fixed by God’s decree: neither denial nor impatience can alter when it arrives.

translation: Those who disbelieve say, “We will never believe in this Qur’an, nor in what came before it.” If only you could see when the wrongdoers are made to stand before their Lord, each casting words back at the other: those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant, “Were it not for you, we would have been believers.”
interpretation: The verse warns that rejecting revelation and following arrogant leaders will not absolve anyone of responsibility before God. On that Day, the oppressed will blame those who misled and pressured them, but the exchange exposes the futility of shifting blame after choosing disbelief.

translation: Those who were arrogant will say to those who were oppressed, “Did we turn you away from guidance after it had come to you? Rather, you yourselves were wicked.”
interpretation: Their reply is an attempt to shift blame: the powerful deny having obstructed the truth and accuse their followers instead. The exchange points to the moral responsibility of those who knowingly reject guidance, while showing how people may try to evade their own accountability when confronted with its consequences.

translation: Those who had been oppressed will say to those who were arrogant, “Rather, it was your scheming by night and day, when you urged us to disbelieve in Allah and to set up rivals to Him.” They will conceal their regret when they see the punishment. We will place shackles around the necks of those who disbelieved. Are they repaid for anything but what they used to do?
interpretation: The verse portrays the oppressed rejecting the arrogant leaders’ attempt to evade blame: their persistent scheming and pressure helped lead them into disbelief. Yet the final reckoning holds each person accountable for what they chose and did; regret at seeing the punishment cannot undo those choices.

translation: We did not send a warner to any town without its well-to-do people saying, “We reject what you have been sent with.”
interpretation: The verse highlights how those most invested in their status and comforts often resist a messenger’s call when it challenges the assumptions and privileges on which their power rests.

translation: And they said, “We have more wealth and children, and we will not be punished.”
interpretation: They mistook material abundance for proof that they were favored and beyond accountability. The verse warns that wealth and children do not guarantee safety from divine judgment.

translation: Say, “Indeed, my Lord expands provision for whom He wills and restricts it, but most people do not know.”
interpretation: Abundance or scarcity of worldly provision is not, by itself, a measure of a person’s worth or of God’s favor; its distribution rests on God’s wisdom, which people often cannot fully discern.

translation: Neither your wealth nor your children bring you nearer to Us in rank; rather, those who believe and do righteous deeds will receive a multiplied reward for what they did, and they will be secure in the lofty chambers.
interpretation: True nearness to God is not earned through riches or family status, but through faith expressed in righteous action. God grants such people a multiplied reward and lasting security in the Hereafter.

translation: Those who strive against Our signs, seeking to thwart them, will be brought into the punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns that no one can defeat or evade God’s judgment by opposing His signs; confidence in escaping accountability is misplaced.

translation: Say, “My Lord extends provision to whomever He wills among His servants and restricts it for him. Whatever you spend, He will replace it; and He is the best of providers.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that wealth is entrusted by God, not controlled solely by human effort. Believers should therefore spend generously in good causes without fearing that generosity will diminish what God provides; His replacement may come as renewed provision, blessing, or reward, according to His wisdom.

translation: And [mention] the Day He gathers them all, then says to the angels, “Was it you that these people used to worship?”
interpretation: Allah’s question is not for information; it exposes the falsehood of those who worshipped angels and makes clear that the angels neither called people to worship them nor approved of it.

translation: They will say, “Glory be to You! You are our Protector, not them. Rather, they worshipped the jinn; most of them believed in them.”
interpretation: The angels deny any share in the worship directed toward them and affirm that their true allegiance is to God alone. The verse exposes how the worshippers were, in reality, following the jinn—especially their deceitful promptings—and placing their trust in them.

translation: So today none of you can benefit or harm another. And We will say to those who did wrong: “Taste the punishment of the Fire that you used to deny.”
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, the powers and allies people relied on will be unable to help or harm anyone; those who rejected the coming punishment will face it as a just consequence of their wrongdoing.

translation: When Our clear revelations are recited to them, they say, “This is only a man who wants to turn you away from what your fathers worshipped.” They also say, “This is nothing but a fabricated falsehood.” And when the truth comes to them, those who disbelieve say, “This is nothing but obvious magic.”
interpretation: The verse portrays how people resistant to divine guidance dismiss it with accusations rather than engage with its message: they appeal to inherited custom, call the revelation fabricated, and label its effect as magic. Their claims reveal that their rejection rests on protecting established beliefs, not on honestly weighing the truth.

translation: We had not given them any scriptures to study, nor had We sent to them before you any warner.
interpretation: Their rejection cannot be justified by a scripture they had studied or by an earlier messenger who had warned them; the revelation brought by the Prophet is therefore a clear and unprecedented call to them.

translation: Those before them also denied, though these people have not attained even a tenth of what We had given those earlier peoples. Yet they denied My messengers—so how severe was My rejection of them!
interpretation: The verse warns that the present deniers have far less power and worldly provision than earlier peoples who were nevertheless destroyed for rejecting God’s messengers. Their denial should therefore not make them feel secure: God’s punishment can overtake them just as it overtook those before them.

translation: Say, “I urge you to do just one thing: stand sincerely for God, two by two or alone, then reflect. Your companion is not mad; he is only a warner to you before a severe punishment.”
interpretation: The verse calls people to set aside inherited prejudice and consider the Prophet’s message with clear minds—whether they reflect together or on their own. Honest reflection, it teaches, should lead them to recognize that his warning is not the speech of a madman but a grave call meant for their benefit.

translation: Say, “Whatever payment I have asked of you is yours. My reward is only with Allah, and He is Witness over all things.”
interpretation: The Prophet’s message is not driven by a desire for worldly compensation: any reward sought from the people would be for their benefit, while his own recompense rests with Allah. Allah’s witness over all things affirms the sincerity of his mission and makes clear that nothing is hidden from Him.

translation: Say, “Indeed, my Lord casts forth the truth; He is the Knower of all that is unseen.”
interpretation: God brings the truth with decisive force, overcoming falsehood, and His perfect knowledge of what is hidden confirms that His judgment and revelation rest on complete knowledge.

translation: Say, “The truth has come, and falsehood can neither originate anything nor bring it back.”
interpretation: The verse declares that falsehood has no power to establish or restore what is real: once the truth is made clear, falsehood cannot endure against it.

translation: Say, “If I go astray, I go astray only to my own detriment; and if I am guided, it is through what my Lord reveals to me. Indeed, He is All-Hearing, Near.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that the consequences of error rest on the one who chooses it, while true guidance comes from God’s revelation, not independent human authority. God hears those who seek Him and is near to them.

translation: If only you could see when they are struck with terror: there will be no escape, and they will be seized from a nearby place.
interpretation: The verse depicts the suddenness and certainty of divine judgment: when the deniers are overwhelmed by fear, no refuge or opportunity to escape will remain, and they will be taken wherever they are.

translation: And they will say, “We believe in it.” But how can they reach it from so distant a place?
interpretation: Once the truth becomes undeniable at the moment of reckoning, their profession of faith can no longer benefit them. They are like people trying to grasp something from far beyond their reach: the opportunity to believe and turn back has already passed.

translation: They had disbelieved in it before, and they make conjectures about the unseen from a distant place.
interpretation: Their claims about what lies beyond their knowledge are portrayed as shots made from far away: confident assertions without access to the truth. The verse exposes the distance between their speculation and genuine understanding.

translation: A barrier will be placed between them and what they desire, just as it was placed between their predecessors. Indeed, they were in troubling doubt.
interpretation: When the truth becomes undeniable, they will wish to reach faith and its promised benefit, but the opportunity will have passed. Their fate echoes that of earlier peoples who met the same end after persisting in deeply unsettling doubt.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. All praise belongs to Allah, the Originator of the heavens and the earth, who appoints the angels as messengers with wings—two, three, or four. He adds to creation whatever He wills. Surely Allah has power over all things.
interpretation: The verse directs us to recognize that the order and variety of creation arise from Allah’s unrestricted power. Even the angels, whom He appoints to carry out His commands, have forms and capacities beyond what people can determine or limit; Allah may create as He wills, and nothing lies beyond His power.

translation: Whatever mercy Allah opens for people, none can withhold it; and whatever He withholds, none can release after Him. He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: The verse calls people to place their hope and reliance in Allah: no one can obstruct the mercy He wills to give or independently undo what He withholds. His choices proceed from perfect power and wisdom.

translation: O people, remember Allah’s favor upon you. Is there any creator other than Allah who provides for you from heaven and earth? There is no god but Him. How, then, are you turned away?
interpretation: The verse calls people to recognize that their provision comes from Allah alone, and that this reality should lead them to gratitude and worship of Him alone. Turning to anything else as a source of divine power or devotion has no sound basis.

translation: If they deny you, then messengers before you were also denied; and to Allah all matters return.
interpretation: The verse consoles the Prophet ﷺ: rejection by people does not undermine the truth of his message, for earlier messengers faced the same response. The ultimate outcome and judgment of every affair rest with Allah.

translation: O humanity, indeed Allah’s promise is true. So do not let the life of this world deceive you, and do not let the great deceiver deceive you about Allah.
interpretation: The verse warns against mistaking worldly ease, pleasure, or delay in accountability for lasting security. In particular, do not let Satan or any other deceiver persuade you that you can ignore Allah’s guidance and still rely carelessly on His mercy; trust in Allah should lead to faithfulness and action, not complacency.

translation: Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so treat him as an enemy. He only calls his followers so that they may be among the companions of the Blaze.
interpretation: Believers are urged to remain alert to Satan’s deception and not follow the desires and temptations through which he leads people away from God; treating him as an enemy means resisting his calls and choosing obedience instead.

translation: Those who disbelieve will have a severe punishment, while those who believe and do righteous deeds will have forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: The verse teaches that a person’s response to faith has lasting consequences: rejecting it brings accountability, while sincere belief joined with righteous action is met with God’s forgiveness and generous reward.

translation: Is one whose evil deeds have been made appealing to him, so that he sees them as good, [like one who is rightly guided]? Allah leaves astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. So do not let yourself be consumed with grief over them. Allah knows well what they do.
interpretation: When a person’s wrongdoing is made attractive in their eyes, they may mistake it for virtue and turn away from guidance. The verse consoles the Prophet ﷺ: he should not let sorrow over those who reject the truth consume him, for Allah fully knows their deeds and will judge them with complete knowledge.

translation: Allah is the One who sends the winds, which stir up clouds; then We drive them to a lifeless land and revive the earth by them after its death. Thus will be the Resurrection.
interpretation: The renewal of barren earth through rain is a sign of Allah’s power to bring the dead back to life. Just as He revives the land after it has withered, He will resurrect people after death.

translation: Whoever desires honor, then all honor belongs to Allah. To Him ascends good speech, and righteous deeds raise it. Those who plot evil will have a severe punishment, and the plotting of such people will come to ruin.
interpretation: True honor is found by turning to God, not by schemes for status or power. Good words reach Him when they are upheld by righteous action; deceitful plotting, by contrast, cannot secure lasting honor and ultimately fails.

translation: Allah created you from dust, then from a drop of fluid, then made you pairs. No female conceives or gives birth except with His knowledge. No one whose life is prolonged has it prolonged, nor is anything taken from anyone’s lifespan, except that it is recorded in a Book. Surely that is easy for Allah.
interpretation: Human life, from its beginnings and formation to its length and end, unfolds within Allah’s complete knowledge and decree. What may seem vast and complex to people is effortless for Him, and none of it escapes His record.

translation: The two bodies of water are not alike: one is fresh and sweet, pleasant to drink, and the other is salty and bitter. From each you eat fresh meat and bring forth ornaments to wear. You see ships ploughing through them, so that you may seek of His bounty and perhaps be grateful.
interpretation: The contrast between the waters shows how God brings distinct qualities together within a world ordered for human benefit. Their different properties, yet shared provision and usefulness, invite people to recognize divine wisdom and respond to these gifts with gratitude.

translation: He causes the night to enter into the day and the day to enter into the night, and He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running for an appointed term. That is Allah, your Lord; His is the dominion. Those you call upon besides Him possess not even the thin membrane of a date stone.
interpretation: The ordered turning of the heavens points to one ultimate source of authority. The verse challenges people to direct their trust and worship to the One who sustains the world, rather than to beings that have no power of their own.

translation: If you call upon them, they do not hear your supplication; and even if they heard, they could not answer you. On the Day of Resurrection, they will disavow your associating them with God. None can inform you as the All-Aware can.
interpretation: Those invoked besides God possess neither the ability to hear and answer worshippers nor any power to fulfill their pleas. On the Day of Resurrection, they will repudiate the worship directed to them. The verse thus warns against attributing divine power to anyone besides God, whose knowledge alone is complete and certain.

translation: O mankind, you are in need of Allah, while Allah alone is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: The verse calls people to recognize that their existence and every blessing depend on Allah, whereas He depends on no one. This awareness should lead them to humility and reliance upon Him, while affirming that His perfection and praise are not contingent on anything people do.

translation: If He wills, He can remove you and bring forth a new creation.
interpretation: The verse reminds people that their existence is wholly dependent on God: no one is indispensable to His purpose, and the power to replace one creation with another belongs entirely to Him.

translation: And that is not difficult for Allah.
interpretation: What may seem impossible to human beings is entirely within Allah’s power; nothing can hinder Him from bringing it about.

translation: No bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. And if one weighed down calls upon another to carry some of its burden, nothing of it will be carried—even if that person is a close relative. You can warn only those who fear their Lord though they do not see Him and establish prayer. Whoever purifies himself does so only for his own benefit, and to Allah is the final return.
interpretation: Each person is accountable for their own choices; neither kinship nor anyone else can take away that responsibility. The warning benefits those whose reverence for God shapes their conduct, and the good they pursue through purification ultimately benefits themselves, as all return to God.

translation: The blind and the seeing are not equal.
interpretation: The verse points to the difference between one who cannot recognize the truth and one who sees it clearly: spiritual insight and blindness are not alike.

translation: Nor are the darknesses and the light equal.
interpretation: Falsehood and misguidance, in their many forms, are not equal to the light of truth and guidance.

translation: Nor are the shade and the scorching heat alike.
interpretation: The contrast evokes the difference between the ease and safety of guidance and the distress of misguidance: just as cool shade is not like scorching heat, the two spiritual states are not equal.

translation: The living and the dead are not alike. Indeed, Allah causes whom He wills to hear, and you cannot make those in the graves hear.
interpretation: The verse likens people who are receptive to truth to the living, and those whose hearts are closed to it to the dead. A messenger can convey the truth, but cannot make someone accept it; true receptivity is granted by Allah.

translation: You are only a warner.
interpretation: The address emphasizes that the messenger’s role is to warn people and make the truth clear; guidance and judgment belong to God.

translation: Indeed, We have sent you with the truth as a bearer of glad tidings and a warner; and there has never been a community without a warner having come among it.
interpretation: The verse affirms that God’s guidance has reached every community through a warner, so people are not left without a reminder of the truth. The Prophet’s mission is to convey that truth, offering hope to those who respond and warning those who turn away.

translation: And if they deny you, then those before them also denied. Their messengers came to them with clear proofs, scriptures, and an illuminating Book.
interpretation: The denial you face is not new: earlier messengers were rejected despite bringing clear evidence and divine revelation. The verse thus consoles the Prophet and reminds him that rejection does not diminish the truth of his message.

translation: Then I seized those who disbelieved. How severe, then, was My punishment!
interpretation: God’s punishment of those who rejected the truth shows that His delay is not neglect: when His judgment comes, it is decisive and beyond their power to resist.

translation: Do you not see that Allah sends down water from the sky, and by it We bring forth fruits of varied colors? And among the mountains are white and red streaks, varied in their hues, and intensely black ones.
interpretation: The variety in fruits and mountains points to Allah’s power and wisdom: He creates striking differences within the same kinds of things, inviting people to recognize the Creator through the diversity of what they see.

translation: And among people, moving creatures, and livestock are likewise of differing colors. Only those of His servants who truly know Him stand in awe of Allah. Indeed, Allah is Almighty, All-Forgiving.
interpretation: True knowledge of Allah deepens reverent awareness of Him: the more one recognizes His power and wisdom in the diversity of creation, the more one is moved to obey Him and seek His forgiveness. His might inspires awe, while His forgiveness gives hope.

translation: Indeed, those who recite the Book of Allah, establish prayer, and spend from what We have provided for them, privately and publicly, hope for a trade that will never perish.
interpretation: The verse presents sincere devotion to God as an enduring investment: those who engage with His revelation, worship Him, and give generously trust that their deeds will bring a reward that is not diminished or lost.

translation: So that He may give them their full rewards and increase them from His bounty. Indeed, He is All-Forgiving, Most Appreciative.
interpretation: God will repay them fully for their good deeds and, through His generosity, grant them even more than they earned. He forgives their failings and values their sincere efforts.

translation: What We have revealed to you of the Book is the truth, confirming what came before it. Indeed, God is fully aware of His servants, seeing them clearly.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the Qur’an is true and stands in continuity with the earlier revelations. Its revelation comes from God, whose complete knowledge and vision encompass His servants and their circumstances.
