translation: Then We caused the Book to be inherited by those We chose from among Our servants. Among them are those who wrong themselves, those who take a middle course, and those who are foremost in good deeds by Allah’s permission. That is the great bounty.
interpretation: Being entrusted with revelation is itself a divine favor, though those who receive it respond in different ways. The verse leaves room for the believer who falls short, while honoring those who are steady and those who hasten to goodness; ultimately, their guidance and the ability to do good depend on Allah’s grace.

translation: Gardens of everlasting residence, which they will enter. There they will be adorned with bracelets of gold and pearls, and their garments will be silk.
interpretation: The verse portrays Paradise as a lasting home where its people are honored and given beauty and comfort without end. Its precious adornments and fine garments express the dignity and delight of their reward.

translation: And they will say, “Praise be to Allah, who has removed all sorrow from us. Indeed, our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative.”
interpretation: The people of Paradise recognize that their lasting peace is a gift from God: He has forgiven their failings and, in His generosity, valued and rewarded their sincere efforts.

translation: He has settled us, by His grace, in the abode of everlasting residence; no weariness touches us there, nor any fatigue.
interpretation: The inhabitants of Paradise recognize that their lasting security and freedom from every form of hardship come entirely from God’s grace.

translation: Those who disbelieve will have the Fire of Hell. They will not be sentenced to die, nor will its punishment be lightened for them. Thus do We recompense every persistently ungrateful disbeliever.
interpretation: The verse stresses the unending consequence of rejecting the truth: death will not provide escape, and the punishment will not be eased. This is presented as a just recompense for persistent ingratitude and disbelief.

translation: There they will cry out, “Our Lord, bring us out; we will do righteous deeds, unlike what we used to do.” [They will be told,] “Did We not give you a life long enough for whoever would reflect to take heed, and did not a warner come to you? So taste the punishment; the wrongdoers will have no helper.”
interpretation: Their plea comes only after they have seen the consequence of their choices, when repentance can no longer lead to a new life of action. The rebuke points to the time and warning they were given in the world: the opportunity to reflect and respond was real, so their punishment is not without warning or accountability.

translation: Indeed, Allah knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth. Surely, He knows what is within hearts.
interpretation: Allah’s knowledge encompasses both what is hidden throughout creation and the innermost thoughts and intentions of every person. Nothing is concealed from Him, so people should be sincere in what they hold within as well as in what they show outwardly.

translation: He is the One who made you successors upon the earth. Whoever disbelieves, his disbelief is to his own detriment. The disbelief of those who disbelieve only increases them in their Lord’s displeasure, and their disbelief only increases them in loss.
interpretation: Human beings have been entrusted with life on earth and succeed one another in it, but this position does not exempt anyone from accountability. Disbelief harms those who choose it: it deepens their estrangement from God and leads them further into loss, while God is in no way diminished by their rejection.

translation: Say, “Have you considered your partners whom you call upon besides Allah? Show me what they have created of the earth. Or do they have a share in the heavens? Or have We given them a scripture, so that they stand upon clear evidence from it?” Rather, the wrongdoers promise one another nothing but delusion.
interpretation: The verse challenges the claim that anything worshipped besides Allah deserves divine status: such a claim would need support in creation, a share in governing the heavens, or clear revelation, yet none is offered. What sustains the wrongdoers’ belief is instead mutual deception—reassurances that give false hope without any sound basis.

translation: Indeed, Allah holds the heavens and the earth lest they slip away. And if they were to slip away, none could hold them after Him. Indeed, He is Forbearing, All-Forgiving.
interpretation: The verse teaches that all creation depends at every moment on Allah’s sustaining power; the order of the universe is not self-maintaining. His forbearance and forgiveness also show that the One who upholds creation gives people time to turn back to Him rather than hastening to punish them.

translation: They swore by Allah with their strongest oaths that if a warner came to them, they would be more rightly guided than any other community. But when a warner came to them, it only increased them in aversion.
interpretation: The verse exposes the gap between their confident claim and their response: when the warning they had demanded came, pride and resistance led them to turn away even more. A warning guides those willing to heed it, but can deepen the rejection of those who refuse it.

translation: Out of arrogance in the land and evil plotting. But evil plotting ensnares only those who engage in it. So do they await anything but what befell the peoples of old? You will find no change in God’s way, nor any alteration in God’s way.
interpretation: Those who arrogantly scheme against the truth ultimately bring the consequences upon themselves. God’s established way of holding people accountable does not change, so the fate of earlier rejecters is a warning to those who follow the same path.

translation: Have they not traveled through the land and seen what was the end of those who came before them? They were greater than them in strength. Nothing in the heavens or the earth can escape Allah. He is All-Knowing, All-Powerful.
interpretation: The fate of earlier peoples is a warning that worldly strength cannot protect anyone from accountability before God. Nothing escapes His knowledge or power, so people should not mistake their might or apparent security for immunity from His judgment.

translation: If Allah were to call people to account for what they have earned, He would leave no living creature upon the earth. But He gives them respite until an appointed time; and when their time comes, Allah is indeed All-Seeing of His servants.
interpretation: The verse teaches that the continued life of creation reflects Allah’s forbearance: He does not bring immediate punishment for every wrongdoing, but grants people time until the term He has appointed. This respite is not because their deeds escape His knowledge; He sees His servants fully and judges them with perfect knowledge when that term arrives.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Yā Sīn.
interpretation: The opening invokes Allah’s name and mercy before the recitation. “Yā Sīn” is one of the separated letters at the beginning of certain surahs; its full meaning is known to Allah.

translation: By the Wise Qur’an.
interpretation: The oath highlights the Qur’an’s profound wisdom and truth, drawing attention to the guidance it contains.

translation: Indeed, you are one of the messengers.
interpretation: This affirms that the Prophet’s mission is divinely appointed and places him within the line of messengers sent to guide humanity.

translation: Upon a straight path.
interpretation: It signifies a way of life grounded in divine guidance: clear, upright, and leading toward God’s pleasure.

translation: A revelation from the Almighty, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: The phrase presents the revelation as coming from God, whose absolute power gives it authority and whose mercy makes it guidance for people.

translation: So that you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned, and who are therefore heedless.
interpretation: The verse presents the warning as a means of awakening people who have become heedless, particularly because they had not received a recent warning through their forefathers.

translation: The decree has indeed come to pass against most of them, so they will not believe.
interpretation: Their sustained rejection of the truth has brought them under God’s judgment; they have become so entrenched in disbelief that they will not accept the guidance offered to them.

translation: Indeed, We have placed shackles around their necks, reaching up to their chins, so that their heads are forced up.
interpretation: The image portrays people so entrenched in their rejection of the truth that they cannot humble themselves or turn toward it.

translation: And We placed a barrier before them and a barrier behind them, and veiled them, so they cannot see.
interpretation: The barriers depict how persistent rejection of the truth can close a person off from guidance: they become unable to recognize it, even when it is presented to them.

translation: It is all the same to them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe.
interpretation: The verse describes people so firmly set against faith that a warning, though delivered, will not move them to believe.

translation: You can warn only one who follows the Reminder and fears the Most Merciful though He is unseen. So give him glad tidings of forgiveness and a noble reward.
interpretation: The verse points to a heart that is receptive to guidance: it follows revelation and remains mindful of God even when He is beyond human sight. Such sincere faith is met not merely with warning, but with hope in God’s forgiveness and generous reward.

translation: Indeed, We give life to the dead, and We record what they have sent ahead and the traces they leave behind; and We have accounted for everything in a clear record.
interpretation: The verse teaches that divine accountability encompasses not only a person’s own deeds but also the lasting effects they leave—good or harmful—that continue after them. Nothing is lost or overlooked, and the promise to give life to the dead assures that all will ultimately be brought to account.

translation: And set forth for them the example of the people of the town, when the messengers came to it.
interpretation: The unnamed town is presented as a warning for those hearing the Qur’an: a divine message should be judged by its truth, not dismissed because its messengers are rejected or opposed.

translation: When We sent two messengers to them, they rejected them, so We strengthened them with a third. They said, “Indeed, we have been sent to you.”
interpretation: The messengers’ mission is upheld by divine support: when their message is rejected, they are reinforced, showing that human opposition does not undo the truth of their calling.

translation: They said, “You are only human beings like us. The Most Merciful has sent down nothing; you are only lying.”
interpretation: They reject the messengers by treating their ordinary human nature as proof that they cannot be divinely sent, and they dismiss revelation as a fabrication. The verse exposes how prejudice can be used to shut out a message before it is honestly considered.

translation: They said, “Our Lord knows that we have indeed been sent to you.”
interpretation: By invoking God as witness, the messengers emphasize the certainty and sincerity of their mission, grounding their claim not in human approval but in divine knowledge.

translation: Our duty is only to convey the message clearly.
interpretation: The speaker affirms that their responsibility is to communicate the truth plainly; whether people accept it is not theirs to control.

translation: They said, “We regard you as an ill omen. If you do not desist, we will surely stone you, and a painful punishment will surely come upon you from us.”
interpretation: The people respond to the messengers’ call by blaming them for imagined misfortune and threatening violence, rather than considering their message. The verse exposes how fear and superstition can be used to intimidate those who speak the truth.

translation: They said, “Your ill omen is with you. Is it because you have been reminded? Rather, you are a people who transgress the bounds.”
interpretation: The messengers reject the people’s attempt to blame them for their troubles: the real cause lies in the people’s own conduct. Their hostility arises because they have been reminded of the truth, and their response reveals their excess in wrongdoing.

translation: And a man came running from the farthest part of the city. He said, “O my people, follow the messengers.”
interpretation: His urgent arrival from the distant edge of the city reflects the depth of his conviction: he hastens to support the truth and counsel his people, despite the effort and risk involved.

translation: Follow those who ask no payment from you and are rightly guided.
interpretation: The verse teaches that a person’s call should be judged by its truth and guidance, not by personal gain: sincerity and a life directed toward what is right are signs of trustworthy counsel.

translation: Why should I not worship the One who created me, when to Him you will all be returned?
interpretation: The speaker presents worship of the Creator as the only fitting response to the One who brought him into being, and reminds his audience that their return to God makes this devotion a matter of ultimate consequence.

translation: Should I take gods besides Him? If the Most Merciful wills harm for me, their intercession will not benefit me at all, nor will they rescue me.
interpretation: The verse rejects devotion to beings who have no power independent of God: neither intercession nor rescue can avert what He wills. It directs the heart to rely on God alone, rather than treating other beings as protectors capable of overriding His will.

translation: Indeed, then I would surely be in clear error.
interpretation: The speaker declares that turning away from the One who created him to worship anything else would be unmistakable misguidance.

translation: Indeed, I have believed in your Lord, so listen to me.
interpretation: He openly affirms his faith in their Lord and urges them to take his testimony seriously.

translation: It was said, “Enter Paradise.” He said, “If only my people knew…”
interpretation: The man’s first thought on entering Paradise is for his people: he wishes they knew of God’s forgiveness and the honor he has received, so they might recognize the truth and turn to faith.

translation: For my Lord has forgiven me and made me among the honored.
interpretation: The speaker recognizes that God’s forgiveness and honor are gifts of divine mercy, and longs for others to know the joy and dignity of being brought near to Him.

translation: And after him, We did not send down upon his people any army from heaven, nor were We ever going to send one down.
interpretation: Their destruction required no heavenly army: God’s command alone was sufficient to bring their fate about, showing that His power is not dependent on force or numbers.

translation: It was only one blast, and suddenly they were extinguished.
interpretation: The verse conveys how swiftly and decisively God’s judgment can take effect: a single command was enough to end their power and leave them lifeless.

translation: Alas for the servants! No messenger came to them except that they mocked him.
interpretation: This is an expression of profound lament over people who bring ruin upon themselves by ridiculing the messengers sent to guide them, rather than heeding their warning.

translation: Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them, and that they do not return to them?
interpretation: The verse warns those who deny God’s message by pointing to the peoples who came before them and were destroyed. Their inability to return to worldly life is a reminder that this life is not a chance that can be reclaimed, and that people should heed the warning before facing the same end.

translation: And all of them will surely be gathered and brought before Us.
interpretation: No one escapes the final gathering before God: every person will be present before Him and answerable for their deeds.

translation: A sign for them is the dead earth: We bring it to life and bring forth from it grain, from which they eat.
interpretation: The revival of barren land points to God’s power to restore life after death, while its harvest also shows that human sustenance depends on His care.

translation: And We placed therein gardens of date palms and grapevines, and caused springs to gush forth therein.
interpretation: These abundant, life-sustaining provisions are presented as signs of God’s power and mercy: He brings forth nourishment from the earth and provides the water that sustains it.

translation: So that they may eat of its fruit and of what their hands have made. Will they not then be grateful?
interpretation: The verse calls people to recognize that their food depends ultimately on God’s provision: even what they cultivate or prepare with their own hands rests on the life and growth God grants, so they should respond with gratitude.

translation: Glory be to Him who created all pairs: from what the earth grows, from themselves, and from what they do not know.
interpretation: The verse directs attention to the vastness of God’s creative power: the patterns of pairing and diversity extend beyond what people can observe or understand, reminding them that creation is not limited by the boundaries of human knowledge.

translation: And a sign for them is the night: We strip the day from it, and behold, they are in darkness.
interpretation: The verse invites reflection on the precise, recurring order of creation as a sign of God’s power and wisdom. The transition from light to darkness is not random; it points to the One who governs the world and can bring about life and resurrection.

translation: And the sun runs on its appointed course. That is the determination of the Almighty, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: The sun’s ordered movement is not random; it unfolds according to a precise decree, revealing the power and knowledge of God who governs the universe.

translation: And the moon—we have determined its phases, until it becomes like an old date-palm stalk.
interpretation: The moon’s changing shape follows a precise, appointed course: after appearing full, it wanes to a thin, curved crescent resembling a dry, aged palm stalk. This orderly cycle is a sign of God’s wisdom and power.

translation: It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day; each moves along in its own orbit.
interpretation: The verse points to the precise order governing the heavenly bodies: each follows its appointed course without disrupting the others. Their regularity is a sign of the wisdom and power that sustain the universe.

translation: And a sign for them is that We carried their descendants in the laden ship.
interpretation: Their survival across generations is a sign of God’s power and mercy: He preserved humanity through the ship and continues to sustain their lives.

translation: And We created for them, like it, that which they ride.
interpretation: This points to God’s provision of other means of transport resembling the ship, by which people travel and are carried from place to place.

translation: And if We will, We can drown them; then they will have no one to answer their cry, nor will they be rescued.
interpretation: The verse reminds us that human safety is ultimately dependent on God: the means people rely on for protection cannot save them if He wills otherwise.

translation: Except by mercy from Us, and as provision for a time.
interpretation: Their being spared is a favor granted by God: He allows them to live and benefit for a limited period, until their appointed end.

translation: And when they are told, “Be mindful of what lies before you and what lies behind you, so that you may receive mercy,”
interpretation: The warning calls people to take heed of the consequences of their actions—learning from what has come before and preparing for what lies ahead. By turning from heedlessness and responding to God’s guidance, they may receive His mercy.

translation: Whenever a sign from the signs of their Lord came to them, they turned away from it.
interpretation: The verse portrays persistent rejection: the problem was not an absence of divine signs, but their unwillingness to attend to them and respond with faith.

translation: When they are told, “Spend from what Allah has provided for you,” those who disbelieve say to the believers, “Should we feed those whom Allah would feed if He so willed? You are clearly in error.”
interpretation: The verse exposes the misuse of belief in divine decree as an excuse for refusing to help others. Allah’s provision is not a reason to withhold generosity; rather, it places a responsibility on those who have been given means, while the disbelievers’ accusation reveals their rejection of that responsibility.

translation: And they say, “When will this promise come to pass, if you are truthful?”
interpretation: Their question is a challenge meant to mock the warning and demand immediate proof, rather than a sincere search for guidance.

translation: They await only a single blast, which will seize them while they are disputing.
interpretation: The verse warns that the end will come suddenly, catching people absorbed in their disagreements and worldly affairs before they can prepare or turn back.

translation: Then they will be unable to make a bequest, nor will they return to their families.
interpretation: The suddenness of the appointed event will leave people no time to put their affairs in order or return to their homes; worldly plans and ties cannot delay what has come to pass.

translation: And the Trumpet will be blown, and suddenly they will emerge from their graves, hastening toward their Lord.
interpretation: The verse portrays the resurrection as sudden and unmistakable: those who had died will be raised and brought swiftly before God, where they will face His judgment.

translation: They will say, “Woe to us! Who has raised us from our resting place?” This is what the Most Merciful promised, and the messengers spoke the truth.
interpretation: Their astonishment at being raised from death gives way to recognition: the resurrection they once questioned is the promised reality, confirming the truth of the messengers.

translation: It will be only a single blast, and then all of them will be brought before Us.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes how effortlessly and suddenly God will resurrect everyone: one blast is enough for all people to be gathered before Him, where they will face His judgment.

translation: So today no soul will be wronged in the least, and you will be recompensed only for what you used to do.
interpretation: The verse affirms the perfect justice of the Hereafter: each person’s judgment will correspond to their deeds, without any loss, excess, or injustice.

translation: Indeed, the people of Paradise, on that Day, will be joyfully occupied.
interpretation: Their delight will be so complete that they will be absorbed in the blessings of Paradise, free from the worries and burdens of worldly life.

translation: They and their spouses will be in the shade, reclining on couches.
interpretation: The verse portrays the people of Paradise in lasting comfort and honored companionship, free from hardship and at peace.

translation: There they will have fruit, and they will have whatever they ask for.
interpretation: The verse conveys the complete generosity of Paradise: its people will enjoy its blessings and find their needs and desires graciously fulfilled by God.

translation: “Peace”—a word from a Merciful Lord.
interpretation: In the Hereafter, God Himself bestows peace upon the people of Paradise, assuring them of His mercy, safety, and lasting contentment.

translation: And separate yourselves today, O criminals.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, the guilty are told to stand apart from the righteous, their deeds having marked them out for judgment.

translation: Did I not command you, O children of Adam, not to worship Satan? He is truly a manifest enemy to you.
interpretation: “Worshipping Satan” includes obeying his temptations and choosing disobedience over God’s guidance. The verse recalls humanity’s responsibility to resist him, since his hostility is clear.

translation: And worship Me; this is a straight path.
interpretation: Worshipping God alone is the clear and upright way that leads to His pleasure.

translation: And he had certainly led astray a great multitude of you. Did you not then use reason?
interpretation: This is a rebuke for ignoring the clear signs of Satan’s enmity: so many had already been led astray, yet people failed to reflect and guard themselves against following him.

translation: This is Hell, which you were promised.
interpretation: The verse depicts the promised punishment as now plainly before those who rejected the warning: what they once denied has become an undeniable reality.

translation: Burn in it today for what you used to disbelieve.
interpretation: The verse presents this punishment as the consequence of persistent disbelief: what was denied in worldly life is now encountered as an unavoidable reality.

translation: Today We will seal their mouths; their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will bear witness to what they used to do.
interpretation: The verse portrays a moment when denial can no longer conceal the truth: God silences people’s own claims, while the very bodies through which they acted testify against them. It emphasizes that every deed remains known and that no one can escape accountability by disputing what they did.

translation: If We willed, We could blot out their eyes; then, even if they hurried toward the path, how could they see?
interpretation: The verse warns that sight and the ability to find one’s way depend entirely on God. Those who presume they can reach guidance by their own efforts should recognize that, if God willed, they could be left unable to see even the path before them.

translation: If We willed, We could transform them where they stand, so they would be unable to move forward or return.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that people’s ability to act depends entirely on God’s will: He could alter them in place and leave them unable either to advance or to go back.

translation: And whoever We grant a long life, We gradually reverse in creation. Will they not then understand?
interpretation: A person who lives long may pass from strength and capability into frailty and dependence. This reversal reminds people that human life and strength are not theirs to command, and calls them to reflect on the power of the One who governs their changing condition.

translation: We did not teach him poetry, nor is it fitting for him. It is nothing but a reminder and a clear Qur’an.
interpretation: The Qur’an is not the Prophet’s poetic invention; it is revelation given to him as a clear reminder and guidance for people.

translation: So that he may warn whoever is alive, and so that the decree may be fulfilled against the disbelievers.
interpretation: The warning benefits those whose hearts remain receptive to guidance; those who knowingly reject it leave themselves accountable to God’s just judgment.

translation: Have they not seen that We created for them, by Our own power, livestock that they possess?
interpretation: The verse invites people to recognize that their ability to possess and benefit from livestock is itself a gift from God, who created them and made them available to human beings.

translation: And We have made them manageable for them: some of them they ride, and some of them they eat.
interpretation: The verse points to the ease God has placed in human life through the animals He has made useful. Their benefits are gifts, inviting people to recognize their dependence on God and respond with gratitude and care.

translation: And they have in them benefits and drinks. Will they not then give thanks?
interpretation: These provisions are signs of God’s care: people should recognize that their livelihood comes from Him and respond with gratitude and obedience.

translation: They have taken gods besides Allah, hoping that they might be helped.
interpretation: The verse exposes the futility of seeking protection from beings who have no power to grant it: reliance belongs to Allah alone, not to objects of worship that cannot truly help their worshippers.

translation: They cannot help them, though they are an army present in their service.
interpretation: Those worshipped besides God are powerless to aid their devotees, even though the devotees rally to their cause and serve them. The verse exposes the futility of devotion to beings that cannot even defend those who worship them.

translation: So do not let their words grieve you. Indeed, We know what they conceal and what they disclose.
interpretation: God reassures the Prophet that the opposition’s words need not burden him: nothing they hide or openly express escapes God’s knowledge, and their conduct is therefore in His care.

translation: Has the human being not seen that We created him from a drop, yet he becomes a clear disputant?
interpretation: The verse calls attention to the contrast between humanity’s humble beginning and its later arrogance: the one created from a tiny drop can become openly contentious toward his Creator, even questioning His power to bring the dead back to life.

translation: He sets forth an argument against Us and forgets his own creation. He says, “Who will give life to bones when they have crumbled away?”
interpretation: The verse exposes the flaw in denying resurrection on the basis of bodily decay: the skeptic overlooks that he himself was created in the first place. The One who brought him into being can restore life to him, however completely his bones have crumbled.

translation: Say, “He will give them life—the One who brought them into being the first time. And He knows all creation perfectly.”
interpretation: The One who created life from nothing in the beginning is fully able to restore it after death; His complete knowledge of every creature means that no part of the dead is beyond His power to reassemble.

translation: He is the One who made fire for you from the green tree, so that you kindle fire from it.
interpretation: The verse points to God’s power to bring forth what seems contrary from within its opposite: fire from a fresh, green tree. It therefore challenges the assumption that restoring life after death is impossible for the One whose creative power already encompasses such transformations.

translation: Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the like of them? Yes indeed; He is the All-Creating, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: The One who brought the immense heavens and the earth into existence is certainly able to restore human beings after death. His perfect knowledge encompasses every detail of creation, so no person is beyond His power to recreate.

translation: His command, when He wills a thing, is only to say to it, “Be,” and it is.
interpretation: The verse expresses that God’s will is wholly effective: creation does not depend on effort or delay, but comes into being by His command.

translation: So glorified is He in whose hand is the dominion of all things, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: The verse calls people to recognize Allah’s absolute sovereignty: nothing lies beyond His power or authority. Since all people will return to Him, their lives and choices ultimately stand before His judgment.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. By those who stand in ranks.
interpretation: The verse opens with an oath by beings—understood in traditional interpretation as angels—arrayed in ordered ranks, evoking their disciplined obedience to Allah.

translation: Then, by those who drive away forcefully,
interpretation: This refers to angels who, by God’s command, repel devils from attempting to overhear the heavenly revelation.

translation: And by those who recite the Reminder,
interpretation: The phrase is part of an oath, commonly understood as invoking angels who proclaim and convey God’s revelation, underscoring the divine source and truth of the message that follows.

translation: Indeed, your God is truly One.
interpretation: This is a decisive affirmation of divine unity: all worship, reliance, and ultimate obedience belong to God alone, with no partner or rival.

translation: Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them, and Lord of the points of sunrise.
interpretation: The verse affirms that God alone governs the heavens, the earth, everything between them, and the ordered horizons from which light rises.

translation: Indeed, We have adorned the nearest heaven with the beauty of the stars.
interpretation: The beauty of the stars points to God’s creative power and wisdom, inviting reflection on the order and splendor of creation.

translation: And as protection from every rebellious devil.
interpretation: The verse conveys that the heavens are under God’s protection, beyond the reach of rebellious beings who would seek to intrude upon what is concealed from them.

translation: They cannot listen in on the highest assembly, and they are pelted from every side.
interpretation: The verse depicts rebellious devils as barred from the heavenly assembly and driven away when they try to approach, emphasizing that access to divine knowledge is guarded from them.

translation: Driven away; and for them is an enduring punishment.
interpretation: The phrase portrays the rebellious devils as utterly barred from the heavenly realm, with their expulsion accompanied by lasting punishment.

translation: Except one who snatches a fragment, then a piercing flame pursues him.
interpretation: The verse describes an intruder trying to steal a fragment of heavenly speech and being pursued by a brilliant, penetrating flame. It conveys that access to the unseen is guarded and cannot be seized without divine permission.

translation: So ask them: Are they more difficult to create, or those We have created? Indeed, We created them from sticky clay.
interpretation: The verse challenges those who deny resurrection: if God created humanity from humble, sticky clay in the first place, bringing people back to life is no harder for Him. Their own origin is a sign of His creative power, not a reason to doubt it.

translation: Rather, you marvel, while they ridicule.
interpretation: The verse contrasts the Prophet’s amazement at their denial with their mocking response: instead of taking the truth seriously, they ridicule it.

translation: And when they are reminded, they do not take heed.
interpretation: The phrase describes people who hear a reminder but fail to reflect on it or let it guide their actions.

translation: And when they see a sign, they mock it.
interpretation: Their reaction reveals a dismissive attitude: rather than consider the sign seriously, they turn it into an occasion for ridicule.

translation: And they said, “This is nothing but clear magic.”
interpretation: They dismissed the message as obvious sorcery, using the accusation to reject its truth rather than engage with its call.

translation: When we have died and become dust and bones, will we truly be raised again?
interpretation: The question expresses the deniers’ disbelief in resurrection, as they regard returning to life after the body has become dust and bones as impossible.

translation: Or our forefathers of old, too?
interpretation: The speakers skeptically ask whether their long-deceased ancestors will also be brought back to life.

translation: Say, “Yes indeed—and you will be humbled.”
interpretation: The emphatic reply exposes the certainty of resurrection: those who arrogantly deny God’s power will return utterly subdued before it.

translation: It will be only one blast, and then they will be looking on.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes how effortlessly and suddenly the resurrection will occur: a single command will bring the dead back to life, leaving them alert and witnessing what unfolds.

translation: And they will say, “Woe to us! This is the Day of Judgment.”
interpretation: Their cry expresses the shock and despair of those who had denied resurrection when they recognize that the promised reckoning has truly arrived.

translation: This is the Day of Judgment that you used to deny.
interpretation: The deniers are being confronted with the reality of the Day when God will decisively judge between people, a reality they had rejected in worldly life.

translation: Gather those who did wrong, together with their kindred and whatever they used to worship.
interpretation: The command portrays the judgment as an unmasking of misplaced loyalties: those who committed wrongdoing are brought together with the people and objects bound up in their choices, so that none can evade the consequences of the allegiance they gave.

translation: Those worshipped besides Allah—then lead them to the path of Hellfire.
interpretation: The verse portrays the final judgment: those who turned to others besides Allah will be led to their punishment, while the false objects of worship they relied on cannot save them.

translation: Stop them; indeed, they will be questioned.
interpretation: The verse conveys that no one can evade divine accountability: people will be made to answer for their choices and deeds before proceeding to their final judgment.

translation: “What is the matter with you that you do not help one another?”
interpretation: This is a rebuke to those who once relied on one another: on the Day of Judgment, their alliances will be powerless, and none can defend another from God’s judgment.

translation: Rather, today they are utterly submissive.
interpretation: They will have no power to resist or defend themselves; faced with God’s judgment, they will be completely humbled and resigned.

translation: And they will turn to one another, questioning one another.
interpretation: The verse portrays people facing one another in the Hereafter, as they question each other about what happened and the choices that brought them to that moment.

translation: They will say, “You used to come to us from the right.”
interpretation: They accuse their former leaders of approaching them under the appearance of righteousness and sincerity, using that trust to lead them astray.

translation: They will say, “Rather, you yourselves were not believers.”
interpretation: The reply rejects the attempt to shift blame: the speakers insist that the others’ rejection was their own choice, not something imposed on them.

translation: We had no authority over you; rather, you were a people who transgressed.
interpretation: The speakers deny having forced their listeners to reject the truth: their influence did not remove their responsibility, because they themselves chose to overstep the bounds.

translation: So the word of our Lord has come true against us; indeed, we are tasting the punishment.
interpretation: They acknowledge that God’s warning has been fulfilled and that the punishment they had denied is now inescapable.

translation: So we led you astray, for indeed we ourselves were astray.
interpretation: Those who misled others acknowledge that they did so while themselves following a false path; their own error does not excuse the harm they caused or remove their responsibility for leading others astray.

translation: For indeed, on that Day, they will share in the punishment.
interpretation: Those who joined one another in disbelief and wrongdoing will face its consequence together; their companionship will bring neither comfort nor escape.

translation: Indeed, this is how We deal with the guilty.
interpretation: The verse warns that God’s treatment of those who persist in wrongdoing follows a just and consistent pattern: they are held accountable for their actions.

translation: Indeed, when they were told, “There is no god but Allah,” they would behave arrogantly.
interpretation: Their refusal stemmed from pride: they would not humble themselves before Allah alone or abandon the beliefs and status they cherished. The verse presents arrogance as a barrier that kept them from accepting the truth.

translation: And they would say, “Are we really to abandon our gods for a mad poet?”
interpretation: In their arrogance, they dismiss the Prophet’s call by branding him mad and a poet, treating the truth he brings as an absurd reason to give up their inherited worship.

translation: Rather, he brought the truth and affirmed the messengers.
interpretation: The verse presents the Prophet’s message as the truth, continuous with the revelation given to earlier messengers and confirming their mission.

translation: Indeed, you will surely taste the painful punishment.
interpretation: The emphatic wording conveys that this punishment is certain, serving as a grave warning that no one can dismiss its consequences.

translation: And you will be recompensed only for what you used to do.
interpretation: This affirms that each person’s recompense is grounded in their own deeds: no one is wronged or held accountable for what they did not do.

translation: Except the sincere servants of Allah.
interpretation: The phrase distinguishes those whose worship and devotion are sincerely directed to Allah from those described in the surrounding passage.

translation: Those will have a provision well known.
interpretation: Their sustenance in Paradise is assured and appointed for them, a fitting and abundant provision whose nature and timing are known to them.

translation: Fruits—and they will be honored.
interpretation: In Paradise, their provision comes with dignity and welcome: they are not merely given delights, but are honored by God.

translation: In Gardens of Bliss.
interpretation: It points to the lasting joy and peace of Paradise, where the faithful dwell in nearness to God, free from hardship and loss.

translation: On couches, facing one another.
interpretation: تُصوّر العبارة أُنس أهل الجنة وصفاء مودّتهم؛ فهم في مجلس كريم يتواجهون في صحبةٍ لا يشوبها نفور أو خصام.

translation: A cup from a flowing spring will be passed around among them.
interpretation: The verse evokes the ease and honor of the people of Paradise: their pure drink is brought to them freely, without effort or want.

translation: White, delightful to those who drink.
interpretation: It describes the drink of Paradise as pure and pleasing, offering delight to its drinkers.

translation: There is no harmful effect in it, nor will they be intoxicated by it.
interpretation: The drink of Paradise brings pleasure without the harm or loss of reason associated with worldly intoxicants.

translation: And with them will be companions of modest gaze, with beautiful, wide eyes.
interpretation: The description conveys the purity and dignity of the companionship promised in Paradise: a gaze reserved in devotion, together with radiant beauty.

translation: As though they were well-guarded eggs.
interpretation: The image conveys purity, delicacy, and the unblemished beauty of those being described.

translation: Then they turned to one another, questioning each other.
interpretation: Their turning toward one another suggests that what had been hidden or disputed can no longer be avoided; they must face one another and reckon with their choices.

translation: A speaker among them will say, “I had a companion...”
interpretation: In the scene of the people of Paradise speaking together, one recalls a close companion from worldly life whose disbelief in the resurrection had once challenged his faith. The recollection sets up a contrast between their different outcomes and the truth that was once disputed.

translation: He will say, “Are you really among those who believe?”
interpretation: The speaker reacts with disbelief that his companion believed in resurrection and the Hereafter, which he had considered impossible.

translation: “When we have died and become dust and bones, will we indeed be recompensed?”
interpretation: The question expresses disbelief that resurrection and accountability could follow bodily decay, as though becoming dust and bones made it impossible for God to restore them and call them to account.

translation: He said, “Will you look?”
interpretation: He invites his companions to look toward the Fire, where he will discover the fate of the companion who once tried to lead him astray.

translation: Then he looked down and saw him in the midst of the Hellfire.
interpretation: The scene makes the consequence of denying the Hereafter unmistakable: what had once been dismissed as unlikely is now seen as reality. It warns that worldly confidence cannot shield anyone from the truth when it is finally revealed.

translation: He said, “By Allah, you nearly brought me to ruin.”
interpretation: He recognizes that his companion’s influence had almost led him away from faith and into spiritual ruin, showing how close a person can come to losing the truth through misleading company.

translation: Had it not been for my Lord’s favor, I would surely have been among those brought forth for punishment.
interpretation: The speaker recognizes that his salvation was not his own achievement, but a mercy from God that spared him the fate of those destined for punishment.

translation: Are we, then, not going to die?
interpretation: The question expresses astonishment and gratitude at the prospect of life without end, suggesting that the blessed state they have reached will not be interrupted by death.

translation: We will have no death beyond our first death, and we will not be punished.
interpretation: The speaker expresses certainty that, after the first death, there will be no further death or punishment—an assurance of lasting security in the Hereafter.

translation: Indeed, this is truly the great triumph.
interpretation: The phrase points to a success of lasting worth: attaining God’s pleasure and reward, far surpassing any temporary worldly gain.

translation: For this, let those who strive do their striving.
interpretation: The everlasting reward of Paradise is worthy of every sincere effort; believers should therefore direct their deeds toward earning God’s pleasure and the lasting success of the Hereafter.

translation: Is that a better welcome, or the tree of Zaqqum?
interpretation: The question starkly contrasts the gracious reception awaiting the righteous with the torment prepared for those who reject the truth, urging the listener to recognize the gravity of their choice.

translation: Indeed, We have made it a trial for the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The mention of this punishment tests the wrongdoers: rather than taking the warning seriously, they reject or mock it, exposing the hardness of their hearts.

translation: Indeed, it is a tree that grows in the depths of Hell.
interpretation: Its roots in the heart of Hell make the tree a symbol of the punishment’s utterly dreadful and otherworldly nature.

translation: Its emerging fruit is as though it were the heads of devils.
interpretation: The image conveys the fruit’s terrifying ugliness, making the tree seem deeply repulsive and fearsome.

translation: For they will indeed eat from it and fill their bellies with it.
interpretation: The verse portrays the punishment as inescapable and degrading: those who denied the warning will be forced to consume the very food that brings them torment.

translation: Then, indeed, they will have with it a mixture of scalding water.
interpretation: The verse describes the punishment of the people of Hell: after eating the bitter fruit of the Zaqqum tree, they will be given scalding water mixed with it, adding to their torment.

translation: Then indeed their return will surely be to Hell.
interpretation: The verse warns that worldly indulgence does not alter the final outcome: those being described will inevitably return to the punishment of Hell.

translation: Indeed, they found their fathers astray.
interpretation: Their wrongdoing lay in following their forefathers’ misguided beliefs merely because they had inherited them, rather than seeking the truth for themselves.

translation: So they hurried along in their footsteps.
interpretation: The verse criticizes blindly and eagerly following the ways of one’s forebears, even when those ways are misguided, instead of judging them by the truth.

translation: And indeed, most of the earlier peoples had gone astray before them.
interpretation: The verse warns that widespread rejection of divine guidance is no proof that it is false; many communities before them followed error, so people should take heed rather than be reassured by the crowd.

translation: And We certainly sent among them warners.
interpretation: God sent messengers to those people to caution them against rejecting His guidance and to call them to heed the consequences of their choices.

translation: So observe what was the end of those who had been warned.
interpretation: The verse calls people to reflect on the fate of those who ignored divine warnings, so they may take heed and turn away from the same rejection.

translation: Except the sincere servants of Allah.
interpretation: The phrase highlights the distinction of those who are wholly devoted to Allah: their sincerity in faith and worship sets them apart from those described in the surrounding passage.

translation: And Noah certainly called upon Us, and how excellent We are in answering.
interpretation: The verse presents God’s response to Noah as a sign of His attentive care: sincere supplication is heard, and God answers with wisdom and generosity.

translation: And We saved him and his family from the great distress.
interpretation: God rescued Noah and those who believed with him from the overwhelming hardship of the flood, showing that divine protection can deliver the faithful from even the gravest trial.

translation: And We made his descendants the ones who remained.
interpretation: After the flood, God preserved Noah’s descendants, making them the continuing line of humanity by His will.

translation: And We left for him a good name among later generations.
interpretation: God preserved his honorable legacy, so that people who came after him would remember him with praise.

translation: Peace be upon Noah among all peoples.
interpretation: God honors Noah with enduring peace and praise throughout creation, preserving his noble mention across generations.

translation: Indeed, thus do We reward those who do good.
interpretation: God’s reward for excellence is not arbitrary: He honors those who act with faithfulness and righteousness, as this phrase illustrates.

translation: Indeed, he was among Our believing servants.
interpretation: This describes a person whose faith and devotion made him one of God’s honored servants, affirming that sincere belief is a mark of closeness to Him.

translation: Then We drowned the others.
interpretation: It conveys that those who persisted in opposing God were ultimately overcome, while affirming that deliverance and judgment belong to God.

translation: And indeed, Abraham was among his followers.
interpretation: Abraham belonged to the same community of faith as Noah: he upheld the worship of God alone and continued the prophetic call to submission, even though he came generations later.

translation: When he came to his Lord with a sound heart,
interpretation: Abraham turned to God with sincere devotion, his heart free from idolatry and spiritual corruption.

translation: When he said to his father and his people, “What do you worship?”
interpretation: His question challenges his father and people to examine whether the things they worship truly deserve devotion.

translation: Do you desire false gods besides Allah?
interpretation: The verse challenges those who worship other than Allah, exposing their choice of fabricated gods as a departure from the truth.

translation: So what, then, is your understanding of the Lord of all worlds?
interpretation: Abraham challenges his people to reconsider what they believe about God: the Lord of all creation cannot be equated with powerless idols, and their beliefs about Him should lead them to worship Him alone.

translation: Then he cast a glance at the stars.
interpretation: Abraham looked toward the stars; in context, this glance precedes his saying that he was unwell and serves as part of his way of excusing himself from joining his people.

translation: So he said, “Indeed, I am ill.”
interpretation: Abraham said this to excuse himself from joining his people, creating an opportunity to confront their idol worship after they had left.

translation: So they turned away from him, retreating.
interpretation: Their turning away signifies deliberate rejection: rather than engage with what he had said, they withdrew from him.

translation: Then he turned to their gods and said, “Will you not eat?”
interpretation: Abraham addresses the idols with deliberate irony: though offerings had been placed before them, they could neither eat nor respond. Their helplessness exposes that they are not worthy of worship.

translation: What is wrong with you that you do not speak?
interpretation: The question exposes the helplessness of the idols: they cannot answer or defend themselves, showing that they are unworthy of worship.

translation: Then he turned upon them, striking them with his right hand.
interpretation: Abraham decisively smashed the idols with his right hand, demonstrating that they were powerless to defend themselves.

translation: Then they came toward him, hastening.
interpretation: The phrase conveys the crowd’s urgent, collective rush toward him in response to what had happened.

translation: He said, “Do you worship what you carve?”
interpretation: Abraham challenges his people to recognize the contradiction in worshipping idols they themselves fashioned: what human hands make cannot be divine or worthy of worship.

translation: And Allah created you and what you make.
interpretation: In context, Abraham says that Allah alone is the Creator: He created the idol-makers and the idols they fashioned, so those idols cannot be worthy of worship.

translation: They said, “Build a structure for him, then cast him into the blazing fire.”
interpretation: Their response to Abraham’s call was to use force rather than consider his message, revealing how fear and hostility can drive people to persecute those who challenge their beliefs.

translation: They intended to plot against him, but We made them the lowest.
interpretation: Their plot against Abraham ended in humiliation and defeat, showing that no scheme can prevail when God wills otherwise.

translation: And he said, “Indeed, I am going to my Lord; He will guide me.”
interpretation: This expresses Abraham’s trust as he set out for God’s sake: even when the path ahead was uncertain, he was confident that God would guide him toward what was right.

translation: My Lord, grant me a child from among the righteous.
interpretation: This is a prayer asking God for righteous offspring: not merely a child, but one who would live in faith and goodness.

translation: So We gave him good news of a forbearing boy.
interpretation: The promised son is described as forbearing, pointing to a character marked by patience, restraint, and trust in God—even when faced with hardship.

translation: When he had grown old enough to work alongside him, he said, “My son, I see in a dream that I am sacrificing you, so consider what you think.” He replied, “My father, do as you are commanded. God willing, you will find me among the steadfast.”
interpretation: The verse portrays faith as willing submission to God’s command, joined with trust and tenderness: the father consults his son, and the son meets a profound trial with patience and resolve, while entrusting the outcome to God.

translation: When they had both submitted, and he laid him down upon his forehead,
interpretation: The verse portrays the complete submission of both Abraham and his son to God’s command: their obedience was willing and rooted in trust, even in the face of an immense trial.

translation: And We called to him, “O Abraham!”
interpretation: The divine call marks the moment Abraham’s unwavering obedience has fulfilled the test; in its Qur’anic context, it signals that the sacrifice will not be carried through.

translation: You have indeed fulfilled the vision. Indeed, this is how We reward those who excel in goodness.
interpretation: God affirms that Abraham’s sincere submission fulfilled the test: what mattered was his wholehearted obedience, and God rewards those who act with such excellence.

translation: Indeed, this was surely the clear trial.
interpretation: The trial was unmistakable: Abraham’s willingness to obey God, and his son’s willingness to submit, were brought to their fullest test.

translation: And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice.
interpretation: The verse presents God’s deliverance as an act of mercy: sincere submission is not met with needless loss, but becomes a lasting sign of trust and devotion.

translation: And We left for him a good name among later generations.
interpretation: God preserved his honored remembrance, so later generations would continue to speak of him with praise.

translation: Peace be upon Abraham.
interpretation: God grants Abraham enduring peace and honor, affirming his faithful devotion and the lasting goodness of his example.

translation: Thus do We reward those who do good.
interpretation: God’s reward reflects His justice and generosity: sincere goodness is never overlooked, even when its full recompense is not immediately visible.

translation: Indeed, he was one of Our believing servants.
interpretation: His true distinction lies in his faithful servitude to God, which is the source of his honor.

translation: And We gave him the good news of Isaac, a prophet among the righteous.
interpretation: The glad tidings promised more than a son: Isaac would be honored with prophethood and counted among the righteous, showing that God’s gift included both family joy and spiritual distinction.

translation: And We blessed him and Isaac. Among their descendants are those who do good and those who plainly wrong themselves.
interpretation: God’s blessing upon Abraham and Isaac did not mean that every descendant would follow the same path: their lineage included both people who acted righteously and people who clearly wronged themselves. Righteousness is therefore shown by one’s deeds, not guaranteed by ancestry.

translation: And indeed, We bestowed Our favor upon Moses and Aaron.
interpretation: God’s favor upon Moses and Aaron points to His special support and guidance of them in their mission, affirming that their work was sustained by divine grace.

translation: And We saved them and their people from the tremendous distress.
interpretation: God delivered Moses, Aaron, and their people from the oppression and danger they faced, showing that He can rescue those who rely on Him from even the gravest trials.

translation: And We supported them, so they became the victors.
interpretation: Their victory came through God’s support, showing that those whom He aids can overcome their opponents.

translation: And We gave them both the clear Book.
interpretation: God granted Moses and Aaron the Torah as clear guidance, making the truth plain and distinguishing it from falsehood.

translation: And We guided them both to the straight path.
interpretation: God granted Moses and Aaron clear guidance, enabling them to remain steadfast in obedience and lead others toward what is right.

translation: And We left for them among later generations…
interpretation: God granted Moses and Aaron an enduring place of honor in the remembrance of those who came after them.

translation: Peace be upon Moses and Aaron.
interpretation: This is a divine honor for Moses and Aaron: God grants them peace and lasting praise for their faithful service and devotion.

translation: Indeed, this is how We reward those who do good.
interpretation: God rewards those who excel in faith and righteous action with fitting favor and care.

translation: Indeed, they were among Our believing servants.
interpretation: The verse affirms that both were devoted to God and steadfast in faith, and honors them with the distinction of being counted among His believing servants.

translation: And indeed, Elias was one of the messengers.
interpretation: By affirming Elias’s place among the messengers, the verse presents his mission as part of the continuing divine guidance sent to humanity.

translation: When he said to his people, “Will you not be mindful of God?”
interpretation: The question is a reproachful appeal, urging his people to turn from heedlessness and let reverence for God guide their conduct.

translation: Do you call upon Baal and forsake the best of creators?
interpretation: The verse rebukes those who direct worship to Baal while turning away from God, the one worthy of worship and the source of all creation.

translation: Allah is your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers of old.
interpretation: Allah’s lordship is not a new claim: He is the Creator and Sustainer of both the present generation and those who came before. This calls people to worship Him alone rather than follow inherited practices that set up rivals to Him.

translation: So they denied him; indeed, they will surely be brought [before God].
interpretation: Their rejection will not spare them from accountability: they will be brought before God to face the consequence of their denial.

translation: Except for the sincere servants of Allah.
interpretation: This phrase singles out those devoted purely to Allah: their sincerity distinguishes them from those described before it and marks them as recipients of Allah’s special favor.

translation: And We left for him a good remembrance among later generations.
interpretation: God preserved his honorable mention among those who came after him, so that later generations would remember and praise him.

translation: Peace be upon Ilyas.
interpretation: This is a divine greeting honoring Prophet Ilyas and affirming his noble standing as a faithful servant of God.

translation: Indeed, this is how We reward those who do good.
interpretation: God’s reward for sincere goodness is not arbitrary: He honors those who act with excellence in a manner fitting their devotion, assuring them that their good deeds are never lost.

translation: Indeed, he was one of Our believing servants.
interpretation: The verse honors him by affirming that he belonged to God’s faithful servants: his devotion and belief are recognized and accepted by God.

translation: And indeed, Lot was one of the messengers.
interpretation: This affirms that Lot’s mission was part of the same divinely guided chain of messengers: his call was grounded in revelation, not personal authority.

translation: When We saved him and all his household,
interpretation: The wording emphasizes that God’s deliverance was complete, extending to his household as well as to him.

translation: Except an old woman among those who remained behind.
interpretation: The exception refers to Lot’s wife: she was not among those rescued, but remained with the people who were punished.

translation: Then We destroyed the others.
interpretation: It teaches that divine patience is not approval: those who persist in rejecting the truth ultimately face the consequences of their choices.

translation: And indeed, you pass by them in the morning,
interpretation: The remains of the people who were destroyed are visible along your route, serving as a warning to reflect on the consequences of rejecting God’s messengers.

translation: And at night as well—will you not then use reason?
interpretation: The signs of past peoples’ fate remain before you even at night; reflecting on them should lead you to recognize the truth and heed the warning.

translation: And indeed, Jonah was among the messengers.
interpretation: The verse affirms Jonah’s honored place among those chosen by God to convey His guidance.

translation: When he fled to the fully laden ship,
interpretation: The word “fled” conveys Yunus’s hurried departure from his people; the verse presents it as a moment of urgency, not merely an ordinary voyage.

translation: Then he drew lots and was among those who lost.
interpretation: The lot’s outcome marked a stage in God’s unfolding plan; being counted among the losers here means losing the draw, not being morally blameworthy.

translation: Then the great fish swallowed him, and he was blameworthy.
interpretation: His being described as blameworthy points to his having left his people before receiving permission from God; it does not mean he was beyond God’s mercy, but marks the lapse for which he would turn back in repentance.

translation: Had he not been among those who glorified God…
interpretation: The verse points to the lasting significance of sincere worship: the remembrance and praise Yunus had practiced before his trial became a means of relief in his moment of distress.

translation: He would have remained in its belly until the day they are resurrected.
interpretation: This expresses how completely Jonah’s deliverance depended on God’s mercy: without his devotion and glorification of God, he would have remained there until the Resurrection.

translation: So We cast him onto the open shore while he was ill.
interpretation: The verse suggests that deliverance does not always mean immediate recovery: Jonah was saved, yet still weak, and remained under God’s care as he began to recover.

translation: And We caused a gourd plant to grow over him.
interpretation: God provided Jonah with shelter and care while he was weak, allowing a gourd plant to grow over him as a mercy and protection.

translation: And We sent him to a hundred thousand—or even more.
interpretation: The wording “or even more” emphasizes the great size of the people to whom he was sent: their number was at least a hundred thousand, and may have exceeded that.

translation: So they believed, and We let them enjoy life for a time.
interpretation: When they believed, God granted them a period of well-being until the time He had appointed for them.

translation: So ask them: Are daughters for your Lord, while they have sons?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical challenge to those who attributed daughters to God while claiming sons for themselves. It exposes the inconsistency and arrogance of assigning God what they themselves regarded as less desirable, and rejects the idea that God has offspring at all.

translation: Or did We create the angels as females while they were witnessing?
interpretation: This rhetorical question challenges those who claimed that the angels were female: they could not have witnessed their creation, so they have no grounds for making that claim.

translation: Indeed, it is out of their own fabrication that they surely say…
interpretation: The emphatic wording condemns the claim that follows as something they have invented, rather than something grounded in truth.

translation: “Allah has begotten offspring”—and they are certainly lying.
interpretation: The verse rejects the claim that God has offspring, declaring it a fabricated falsehood and affirming that God is far above having children.

translation: Has He chosen daughters over sons?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rebuke of those who attributed daughters to God while claiming sons for themselves. It exposes the inconsistency and baselessness of that claim; it does not describe an actual choice by God.

translation: What is the matter with you? How do you judge?
interpretation: This is a rebuke of those making a judgment without sound reason: they are called to recognize the inconsistency between their claim and what is truly warranted.

translation: Will you not then take heed?
interpretation: This is a call to reflect on what has been made clear and let its lesson guide you, rather than remain heedless.

translation: Or do you have clear authority?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical challenge asking whether they possess any decisive proof for their claim; the phrase implies that they do not.

translation: Then bring your scripture, if you are truthful.
interpretation: The verse challenges those making the claim to support it with revealed evidence, showing that sincere conviction must be grounded in proof rather than assertion.

translation: They have claimed a kinship between Him and the jinn, though the jinn know full well that they will indeed be brought before Him.
interpretation: The verse rejects attributing family ties to God: the jinn are created beings, not His relatives, and they themselves know they will be summoned to account before Him.

translation: Glory be to Allah, far above what they ascribe to Him.
interpretation: This glorifies Allah as utterly transcendent and perfect, free from every false or deficient attribute people may claim for Him.

translation: Except the sincere servants of Allah.
interpretation: This refers to those devoted wholly to Allah, whose sincere faith and worship set them apart from Satan’s influence.

translation: So indeed, you and whatever you worship…
interpretation: The phrase addresses the idolaters and places them alongside the objects they worship, preparing to affirm that neither they nor their idols can act independently of God’s will.

translation: You cannot lead anyone astray from Him.
interpretation: The passage declares that those who oppose God have no power to mislead people at will; their influence reaches only those already destined for the Fire.

translation: Except whoever is destined to enter the blazing Fire.
interpretation: Misguidance cannot prevail over everyone; it affects only those who are already headed toward the Fire.

translation: There is none of us but has a known station.
interpretation: The angels each have a rank and appointed place in their service to God, carrying out their duties within the order He has set.

translation: And indeed, we are those who stand in ranks.
interpretation: The angels affirm their perfect order and unity in worship and obedience to God, each standing in the place appointed for them.

translation: And indeed, we are surely those who glorify Allah.
interpretation: The speakers are the angels, affirming that they are devoted servants who exalt Allah and have no share in His divinity.

translation: And they would indeed say…
interpretation: The emphatic wording presents this as something they repeatedly said, not a passing remark; the words that follow specify what they said.

translation: If only we had a reminder from the people of old…
interpretation: In context, this is the claim of people who said that an earlier scripture would have made them devoted servants of God. The surrounding verses expose it as an excuse: when the reminder did come to them, they rejected it.

translation: We would indeed have been Allah’s devoted servants.
interpretation: The phrase describes a claim of wholehearted devotion to Allah—serving Him with sincerity rather than associating partners with Him.

translation: So they rejected it; soon they will know.
interpretation: Their rejection will not make the truth disappear; the warning is that they will soon discover the reality and consequences of what they denied.

translation: And Our decree had already gone forth concerning Our servants, the messengers.
interpretation: God’s promise regarding His messengers is firmly established: their mission is upheld by His will, even when they face hardship and opposition.

translation: Indeed, they are the ones who will be granted victory.
interpretation: This affirms God’s promise that His messengers will ultimately receive His support, even if they face hardship or apparent defeat along the way.

translation: And indeed, Our forces will surely be victorious.
interpretation: The verse conveys God’s assurance that those who serve His cause will ultimately prevail through His support, even if their victory is not immediate or outwardly apparent.

translation: So turn away from them for a time.
interpretation: The command is to withdraw from those who reject the message for a while, bearing their opposition patiently and leaving the outcome to God until the appointed time.

translation: And watch them, for they will soon see.
interpretation: The verse assures the Prophet that those who reject the truth will soon witness the reality of what they denied and the consequences of their rejection.

translation: Are they then impatient for Our punishment?
interpretation: The question rebukes those who mockingly demand that punishment come sooner, despite being warned that it will come. Their impatience does not make them safe from it.

translation: But when it descends upon their dwelling, evil will be the morning of those who were warned.
interpretation: The verse conveys the certainty and force of the promised punishment: when it reaches those who dismissed the warning, their dawning will bring ruin rather than safety.

translation: So turn away from them for a time.
interpretation: The command is to bear their rejection patiently and refrain from engaging with them for the present, while awaiting what God will decree; it is a temporary pause, not an end to the Prophet’s mission.

translation: And observe; soon they will see.
interpretation: The phrase warns that what is now hidden from them will soon become evident, and they will witness the outcome of their rejection.

translation: Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of Might, far above what they describe.
interpretation: Allah is utterly transcendent and exalted above every false attribute or claim people ascribe to Him; His perfect might and majesty are beyond their descriptions.

translation: And peace be upon the messengers.
interpretation: This closing benediction honors God’s messengers and affirms their innocence and integrity in conveying His guidance.

translation: And praise belongs to Allah, Lord of all worlds.
interpretation: This is an affirmation that every form of praise and gratitude ultimately belongs to God, who sustains and governs all creation.

translation: In the name of God, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Ṣād. By the Qur’an, rich in reminder.
interpretation: The opening letter Ṣād is among the Qur’an’s disjointed letters, whose ultimate meaning is known to God. The oath by the Qur’an draws attention to its power to awaken hearts and guide people through its reminders.

translation: But those who disbelieve are in pride and opposition.
interpretation: Their refusal is driven by stubborn arrogance: rather than consider the truth sincerely, they persist in defying it and setting themselves against its call.

translation: How many generations before them have We destroyed! Then they cried out, but it was no time to escape.
interpretation: The verse warns that once divine judgment arrives, those who ignored the signs and persisted in wrongdoing can no longer evade its consequences; their cries for help come too late.

translation: They marvel that a warner has come to them from among themselves, and the disbelievers say, “This is a magician, a liar.”
interpretation: Their rejection is rooted in resistance to the message: rather than consider the warning brought by someone they know, they dismiss the messenger with accusations of sorcery and deceit.

translation: “Has he made all the gods into one God? This is truly astonishing!”
interpretation: The verse portrays the opponents’ shock at the call to worship God alone. Their sense of astonishment reflects how deeply their inherited beliefs resisted the idea of exclusive devotion to one God.

translation: The prominent among them went away, saying, “Go on, and remain steadfast in worshipping your gods. This is surely something intended.”
interpretation: The leaders reject the Prophet’s call to worship one God and urge their people to cling to their idols. By calling it “something intended,” they portray the call as a deliberate effort to change their religion and undermine the order they wish to preserve.

translation: “We have never heard of this in the latter religion. This is nothing but an invention.”
interpretation: They dismiss the call to worship one God because it is unfamiliar to them, branding it fabricated rather than considering its truth.

translation: “Has the Reminder been sent down to him, rather than to us?” Rather, they are in doubt about My Reminder; indeed, they have not yet tasted My punishment.
interpretation: Their objection reflects not a reasoned case against the revelation, but doubt and resistance. The warning that they have not yet tasted punishment underscores that their confidence in rejecting it rests on having yet to face its consequences.

translation: Or do they possess the treasuries of mercy of your Lord—the Almighty, the Bestower?
interpretation: The question challenges those who object to whom God grants revelation: they have no claim over His mercy or authority to decide whom He chooses to bestow it upon.

translation: Or do they possess the dominion of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them? Then let them ascend by the means [to heaven].
interpretation: This is a rhetorical challenge to those who reject the Prophet’s message: they possess no authority over God’s dominion, so their objections cannot constrain His will or prevent the revelation He sends.

translation: A host of factions there will be defeated.
interpretation: The opposing factions may appear powerful, but their strength cannot prevail against God’s decree; their defeat is certain.

translation: Before them, the people of Noah, ʿĀd, and Pharaoh, the one of the stakes, denied the truth.
interpretation: The verse warns that worldly power and strength cannot protect a people from the consequences of rejecting God’s message.

translation: And Thamud, the people of Lot, and the inhabitants of the Thicket—those were the confederates.
interpretation: They are called “the confederates” because they represent earlier peoples united in rejecting their messengers. Their mention warns that collective opposition to truth does not protect a people from accountability.

translation: Each of them denied the messengers, so My punishment became due.
interpretation: The verse shows that the peoples who rejected God’s messengers brought judgment upon themselves through their persistent denial; the punishment was a just consequence, not an arbitrary one.

translation: These people await nothing but a single blast, for which there will be no respite.
interpretation: The verse warns that the decisive divine command will arrive suddenly, leaving no interval in which to delay or escape its consequence.

translation: And they say, “Our Lord, hasten for us our share before the Day of Reckoning.”
interpretation: They say this mockingly, challenging the warning of the Hereafter and demanding that their promised share of recompense come immediately.

translation: Be patient over what they say, and remember Our servant David, a man of strength. Indeed, he was always turning back to God.
