interpretation: The verse consoles the Prophet ﷺ to remain steadfast in the face of opposition, taking David as an example: his strength was joined to devoted worship and continual return to God.

translation: Indeed, We subjected the mountains to join him in glorifying Us at evening and at sunrise.
interpretation: God granted David a remarkable sign: the mountains echoed his praise, showing how all creation is under God’s command and joins in glorifying Him.

translation: And the birds, gathered together; all turned back [in praise].
interpretation: The mountains and birds joined David in glorifying God, responding again and again to his praise.

translation: And We strengthened his kingdom and granted him wisdom and decisive judgment.
interpretation: The verse points to the divine support behind just leadership: authority is made firm not by power alone, but by wisdom and the ability to judge disputes clearly and fairly.

translation: And has the account of the disputants come to you, when they climbed over the wall into the prayer chamber?
interpretation: The question draws attention to the remarkable and unexpected arrival of the disputants, setting the scene for a lesson in judging fairly and listening carefully before reaching a decision.

translation: When they entered upon David, he was startled by them. They said, “Do not fear. We are two litigants; one of us has wronged the other. So judge between us with justice, do not overstep, and guide us to the straight and equitable way.”
interpretation: The passage underscores that judgment must be grounded in fairness rather than surprise, fear, or partiality. The request to avoid overstepping and to guide them to the equitable way frames justice not merely as deciding who is right, but as resolving a dispute within the bounds of truth.

translation: “Indeed, this is my brother. He has ninety-nine ewes, and I have only one ewe. Yet he says, ‘Give her to me,’ and he has overpowered me in argument.”
interpretation: The speaker presents a case of stark imbalance: his brother, already possessing far more, is demanding the one ewe he has. The complaint is that wealth and persuasive power are being used to press an unfair claim against someone with little ability to resist.

translation: He said, “He has wronged you by asking for your ewe to add it to his ewes. Indeed, many partners wrong one another, except those who believe and do righteous deeds—and how few they are!” David then realized that We had tested him, so he sought his Lord’s forgiveness, fell down in prostration, and turned to Him in repentance.
interpretation: The passage warns that people in positions of shared interests can let self-interest lead them to wrong others; justice and restraint are rare without faith and righteous conduct. David’s response shows the humility required when one recognizes a divine test: he turns to God in repentance rather than persisting in error.

translation: So We forgave him for that. Indeed, he has nearness to Us and an excellent place of return.
interpretation: God’s forgiveness is accompanied by lasting honor: sincere repentance brings one nearer to Him and toward a blessed final return.

translation: O David, We have appointed you as a steward on earth, so judge between people with justice, and do not follow personal desire lest it lead you away from Allah’s path. Those who stray from Allah’s path will face a severe punishment because they forgot the Day of Reckoning.
interpretation: The verse presents authority as a trust that must be exercised impartially: a person in judgment must resist self-interest and bias, remembering that human decisions are answerable to God. To “forget” the Day of Reckoning is to live and act as though that accountability does not matter.

translation: We did not create the heaven and the earth and all that is between them in vain. That is the assumption of those who disbelieve; so woe to those who disbelieve because of the Fire.
interpretation: The verse teaches that creation has purpose and is governed by wisdom, not futility; denying that purpose obscures the reality of accountability, and the warning of the Fire calls people to take that accountability seriously.

translation: Or should We treat those who believe and do righteous deeds like those who spread corruption on earth? Or should We treat the God-conscious like the wicked?
interpretation: The rhetorical questions affirm that God’s judgment is just: faith and righteousness are not equal to corruption, nor reverence for God to wickedness.

translation: A blessed Book We have sent down to you, so that they may reflect on its verses and people of understanding may take heed.
interpretation: The Qur’an is presented as a source of enduring blessing whose guidance is meant to be pondered deeply, not merely recited. Such reflection should awaken people of sound understanding to remember what is true and live by it.

translation: And We bestowed upon David Solomon. What an excellent servant! Indeed, he was ever turning back to God.
interpretation: Solomon’s distinction lay not merely in the favor and authority granted to him, but in his devoted servitude and continual return to God in repentance and obedience.

translation: When, in the evening, the poised, swift steeds were brought before him,
interpretation: The description highlights the horses’ exceptional training and quality: they stood alert and poised, displaying the grace and strength for which they were prized.

translation: So he said, “Indeed, I have become so fond of these fine things that they have distracted me from the remembrance of my Lord,” until [the sun] disappeared behind the veil.
interpretation: Solomon recognizes that his admiration of the horses absorbed him and drew his attention from remembering God. The verse presents this as a moment of self-reproach when the sun had set.

translation: “Bring them back to me!” Then he began stroking their legs and necks.
interpretation: The verse portrays Solomon turning his attention back to the horses, running his hands over them as an act of care and appreciation.

translation: We certainly tested Solomon and placed a body upon his throne; then he turned back to God.
interpretation: The body on Solomon’s throne was a sign of his trial and of the limits of worldly power. He responded by turning back to God in humility and seeking His favor.

translation: He said, “My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom unlike any that will belong to anyone after me. You alone are the Bestower.”
interpretation: Solomon asks God for forgiveness and for a uniquely great kingdom, recognizing that such authority is a gift bestowed by God alone.

translation: So We subjected the wind to him, flowing at his command gently wherever he wished.
interpretation: The verse presents the wind’s obedience to Solomon as a gift from God: his authority over it was granted by God, and it carried out his wishes with ease.

translation: And the devils—every builder and diver.
interpretation: The verse portrays these powerful beings as placed under Solomon’s command, showing that their formidable abilities operated only by God’s permission.

translation: And others bound together in shackles.
interpretation: This refers to rebellious jinn placed under Solomon’s authority and restrained by God’s command, showing that even powerful unseen beings are subject to God’s will.

translation: “This is Our gift; so bestow or withhold as you wish, without reckoning.”
interpretation: God grants Solomon abundant authority and provision, allowing him to give or withhold freely; the gift is by divine favor, not something he must earn or measure.

translation: And indeed, he has nearness to Us and an excellent place of return.
interpretation: This describes David’s honored standing with God: he was brought near through divine favor and will have a blessed final abode.

translation: And remember Our servant Job, when he called to his Lord: “Indeed, Satan has touched me with hardship and suffering.”
interpretation: Job’s words express humble reliance on God amid prolonged affliction: he names the suffering as a satanic trial, yet turns to his Lord for relief, showing that seeking help from God is not a failure of patience.

translation: Stamp the ground with your foot. Here is cool water for bathing and drinking.
interpretation: God directs Job to strike the ground, whereupon water is provided as a means of relief and healing—both to wash in and to drink.

translation: And We granted him his family and the like of them with them, as a mercy from Us and a reminder for people of understanding.
interpretation: The restoration of Job’s family and the doubling of what he received show that God’s mercy can follow even prolonged hardship. For people of understanding, his story is a reminder to remain patient and trust in God through trials.

translation: “Take in your hand a bundle of stalks, strike with it, and do not break your oath. Indeed, We found him patient. What an excellent servant! He was truly ever-turning to God.”
interpretation: The verse shows God’s mercy in making a gentle way for Job to keep his oath without resorting to a severe blow. His patience through hardship and his constant return to God are praised as marks of exemplary devotion.

translation: And remember Our servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—people of strength and insight.
interpretation: They are praised for their steadfast strength in worship and obedience to God, and for their clear understanding of faith and what pleases Him.

translation: Indeed, We singled them out for a special quality: remembrance of the Hereafter.
interpretation: God endowed them with the distinctive virtue of keeping the Hereafter foremost in their minds, directing their devotion and actions toward it.

translation: And indeed, they are with Us among the chosen and the best.
interpretation: This affirms that those being spoken of were specially honored by God: He chose them for their faith and righteousness and granted them a distinguished rank in His presence.

translation: And remember Ishmael, Elisha, and Dhul-Kifl; each was among the excellent.
interpretation: Their mention honors them as models of devoted righteousness, inviting believers to keep the example of those who remained steadfast in goodness before God.

translation: This is a reminder, and indeed the God-conscious will have an excellent place of return.
interpretation: The accounts and guidance presented here call people to remember God and live with awareness of Him; those who do so may be assured of a gracious and rewarding final home with Him.

translation: Gardens of lasting residence, with their gates opened for them.
interpretation: The open gates signify a welcome without hindrance: their lasting home is prepared for them, and they enter it in honor and security.

translation: Reclining there, they call for abundant fruit and drink.
interpretation: Their reclining and freely calling for what they desire portray the ease and honor of the Garden, where provision is plentiful and their needs are met without hardship.

translation: And with them will be companions of modest, restrained gaze, well-matched in age.
interpretation: The verse portrays the companionship of Paradise as pure and harmonious: companions whose attention is devoted to one another and who are alike in age, suggesting closeness and shared delight.

translation: This is what you were promised for the Day of Reckoning.
interpretation: The words affirm that what God promised will certainly come to pass on the Day of Reckoning, when each person’s deeds are accounted for.

translation: Indeed, this is Our provision; it will never run out.
interpretation: The verse conveys that the provision God grants in Paradise is everlasting and inexhaustible, assuring its recipients that it will never diminish or be taken away.

translation: This is so; and indeed, for the transgressors there is an evil place of return.
interpretation: The verse contrasts the lasting reward granted to the righteous with the fate awaiting those who persist in defiance of God: their final destination is one of misery and punishment.

translation: Hell—they will enter it. What a miserable resting place!
interpretation: The verse portrays Hell as the wretched final abode awaiting those described in its context, emphasizing the severity of their fate.

translation: This, then, let them taste: scalding water and ghassāq—a foul, bitter fluid.
interpretation: The verse portrays the punishment awaiting the wrongdoers through two forms of torment: intensely scorching water and a loathsome, harmful drink. “Ghassāq” is understood by commentators in descriptions such as foul fluid or extreme cold, emphasizing the severity of their punishment.

translation: And other punishments of the same kind, in various forms.
interpretation: The phrase indicates that the punishment includes further torments resembling those already mentioned, in multiple kinds and forms.

translation: “This is a company rushing in with you. No welcome for them; they will burn in the Fire.”
interpretation: The words portray the contemptuous welcome given to another group entering Hell: those already there reject them, though both groups share the same punishment. The exchange underscores how enmity and blame persist even among the condemned.

translation: They will say, “Rather, you are not welcome! You brought this upon us. What a wretched place to settle!”
interpretation: The verse portrays the mutual hostility of those in Hell: each group rejects the other and blames them for leading them to this fate. Their accusations cannot undo what they face, and their words reveal the misery of their final abode.

translation: They will say, “Our Lord, whoever brought this upon us, increase his punishment twofold in the Fire.”
interpretation: Their plea reflects the mutual blame of those in the Fire: they ask that the one who led them into this fate receive an added punishment for having misled others, though blaming their leader does not erase their own responsibility.

translation: And they will say, “Why do we not see men whom we used to count among the wicked?”
interpretation: This depicts the arrogance of those facing punishment giving way to bewilderment: they had judged the believers to be wicked, but now cannot find them among the condemned. Their absence exposes how false and self-serving their judgment had been.

translation: Have we taken them as objects of ridicule, or have our eyes simply failed to see them?
interpretation: The people of the Fire, searching for the believers they once mocked, wonder whether they had ridiculed them or had simply overlooked them. Their bewilderment exposes how mistaken their contempt had been.

translation: Indeed, that is surely true: the disputing of the people of the Fire.
interpretation: The mutual arguing and blame among the people of Hell is a certain reality, showing how their hostility continues even in punishment.

translation: Say, “I am only a warner. There is no deity except Allah, the One, the Subduer.”
interpretation: The verse grounds the Prophet’s role in warning people, while affirming that ultimate authority belongs to Allah alone: He is uniquely one and irresistibly sovereign, so none besides Him deserves worship.

translation: The Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them—the Almighty, the All-Forgiving.
interpretation: God’s absolute power does not exclude mercy: He is beyond being overcome, yet His forgiveness remains open to those who turn to Him.

translation: Say, “It is a momentous announcement.”
interpretation: The announcement is the Qur’anic message of God’s truth and the coming reckoning—grave realities that people turn away from, though they call for reflection and response.

translation: You are turning away from it.
interpretation: The phrase describes a deliberate posture of disregard toward the matter or message being referred to, rather than mere unawareness.

translation: I had no knowledge of the exalted assembly when they were disputing.
interpretation: The verse teaches that the Prophet learned of the unseen dispute among the exalted assembly through revelation, not through personal knowledge or observation.

translation: It is revealed to me only that I am a clear warner.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the Prophet’s warning comes through revelation: his task is to convey God’s message plainly and warn people of its consequences.

translation: When your Lord said to the angels, “I am creating a human being from clay,”
interpretation: The verse presents the creation of the human being as an act initiated by God, who brings life from clay—an earthly, humble material—underscoring both humanity’s dependence on its Creator and the divine purpose behind its creation.

translation: So when I have fashioned him and breathed into him of My spirit, fall down before him in prostration.
interpretation: The phrase “My spirit” expresses the honor God gives to the spirit He created; it does not mean that the spirit is part of God. The command to prostrate honors Adam’s God-given dignity, while the angels’ act is obedience to God, not worship of Adam.

translation: So the angels prostrated, all of them together.
interpretation: The emphatic wording highlights the angels’ complete obedience to God’s command and their honoring of Adam as He had instructed.

translation: Except Iblis: he acted arrogantly and was among the disbelievers.
interpretation: Iblis’s refusal was rooted in arrogance, revealing his disbelief rather than a simple failure to obey.

translation: He said, “O Iblis, what prevented you from prostrating to the one I created with My two hands? Were you arrogant, or did you consider yourself among the exalted?”
interpretation: The question exposes Iblis’s refusal as pride rather than inability: he treated his own status as a reason to withhold obedience. The reference to God creating Adam with His two hands conveys a special honor and distinction bestowed upon him, without implying that God resembles created beings.

translation: He said, “I am better than him: You created me from fire and created him from clay.”
interpretation: His claim of superiority reveals the arrogance that led him to disobey God: he treated the material he was made from as proof of greater worth, though true worth is not established by origin or status.

translation: He said, “Then get out of it, for you are accursed.”
interpretation: Iblis’s defiance has made him unworthy to remain in the honored place he occupied; he is cast out and deprived of divine favor.

translation: And indeed, upon you is My curse until the Day of Judgment.
interpretation: God declares that Iblis is barred from His mercy until the Day of Judgment, a lasting consequence of his rebellion.

translation: He said, “My Lord, grant me respite until the day they are resurrected.”
interpretation: His request reveals that, after choosing defiance, he seeks time to continue his opposition rather than turn back in repentance.

translation: He said, “Then you are among those granted respite.”
interpretation: The reply grants the speaker a delay until an appointed time; it does not mean approval of his defiance or release from its consequences.

translation: Until the day of the appointed time.
interpretation: The phrase emphasizes that the respite granted is limited by a time fixed in God’s decree; it is not an endless escape from accountability.

translation: He said, “By Your might, I will surely lead them all astray.”
interpretation: Satan’s oath expresses his defiant resolve to draw people away from obedience to God, but it does not mean he acts independently of God’s authority.

translation: Except Your servants among them who are devoted to You.
interpretation: Satan concedes that his power to mislead does not reach those whom God has made sincere in their devotion and steadfast in faith.

translation: He said, “The truth—and I speak the truth.”
interpretation: God emphasizes that His declaration is wholly true and certain, free from error or falsehood; in context, it confirms the certainty of His judgment.

translation: I will surely fill Hell with you and all those among them who follow you.
interpretation: This is a decisive warning that Satan’s influence does not remove human responsibility: those who follow his way knowingly share in its consequence, while God’s judgment is certain and just.

translation: Say, “I ask you for no reward for this, nor am I one of those who pretend or make things up.”
interpretation: The Prophet is instructed to make clear that he seeks no worldly gain for conveying the message and that he is not inventing it or claiming what he does not know; he conveys what has been revealed to him.

translation: It is only a reminder to all worlds.
interpretation: The Qur’an is a universal reminder, calling all people to heed divine guidance and turn back to God.

translation: And you will surely know its truth after a time.
interpretation: The verse warns that the truth of the revelation will become unmistakable in due course, when events and their consequences confirm what it foretold.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the Book comes from Allah, whose unmatched power and perfect wisdom establish its divine authority and guide people with truth.

translation: Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, so worship Allah, devoting your religion sincerely to Him.
interpretation: The verse teaches that sincere worship is the proper response to divine guidance: devotion should be directed to Allah alone, free from show or association with anything besides Him.

translation: Surely, sincere devotion belongs to Allah alone. As for those who take protectors besides Him, they say, “We worship them only so that they may bring us nearer to Allah.” Allah will judge between them concerning what they differ about. Allah does not guide one who is a liar and an ungrateful disbeliever.
interpretation: The verse teaches that worship and devotion must be directed sincerely to Allah; claiming that other beings are worshipped merely as a means of nearness does not make that worship acceptable. Allah alone will settle the dispute over this belief, and persistent dishonesty and rejection lead a person away from guidance.

translation: Had God wished to take a child, He could have chosen from among what He creates whatever He willed. Glory be to Him! He is God, the One, the All-Subduing.
interpretation: The verse declares God far above having offspring: nothing could compel Him to do so, and if He willed anything, His choice would be entirely His. His absolute oneness and dominion leave no place for the idea that He has a child or partner.

translation: He created the heavens and the earth in truth. He rolls the night over the day and rolls the day over the night, and He has subjected the sun and the moon; each runs its course until an appointed term. Indeed, He is the Almighty, the All-Forgiving.
interpretation: The ordered alternation of night and day and the courses of the sun and moon point to creation governed by deliberate purpose and irresistible authority. The verse also joins that majesty with mercy: the One who sustains this order is able to forgive those who turn to Him.

translation: He created you from a single soul, then made from it its mate; and He provided for you from livestock eight pairs. He creates you in your mothers’ wombs, stage after stage, within three layers of darkness. That is Allah, your Lord. To Him belongs all sovereignty; there is no god but Him. So how are you turned away?
interpretation: The verse directs people to recognize Allah’s exclusive lordship through the signs of His power and care: human life begins from a single origin and develops through successive stages hidden within the womb, while livestock are provided for their benefit. Since He alone creates and sustains, worship and trust belong to Him alone; turning toward other objects of devotion means turning away from the truth those signs point to.

translation: If you disbelieve, Allah has no need of you; He does not approve of disbelief for His servants. But if you are grateful, He approves it for you. No bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you of what you used to do. Surely He knows what lies within hearts.
interpretation: Allah’s guidance is not for His own benefit: faith and gratitude serve the human being, while rejection cannot diminish Him. Each person is accountable for their own choices, and that accountability reaches beyond outward deeds to the intentions and realities hidden within the heart.

translation: When hardship touches a person, he calls upon his Lord, turning to Him. Then, when He grants him a favor, he forgets what he had called upon Him for before and sets up rivals to Allah, turning others away from His path. Say, “Enjoy your disbelief for a little while; you are surely among the companions of the Fire.”
interpretation: The verse warns against treating devotion to God as something needed only in moments of distress. A person who turns sincerely to God in hardship but becomes heedless and ungrateful when ease returns is not secure in faith; worldly comfort is fleeting, and rejecting God’s guidance carries a lasting consequence.

translation: Is one who devoutly worships during the hours of the night, prostrating and standing, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for his Lord’s mercy [like one who does not]? Say, “Are those who know equal to those who do not know?” Only people of understanding take heed.
interpretation: The verse presents genuine knowledge as something that shapes a person’s life: awareness of God and the Hereafter gives rise to devoted worship, while hope in divine mercy sustains it. Its closing question calls people to recognize that such insight is not equivalent to heedlessness; the truly discerning are those who let what they know guide their conduct.

translation: Say, “O My servants who believe, be mindful of your Lord. Those who do good in this world will have goodness, and God’s earth is vast. The patient will surely be given their reward without measure.”
interpretation: Believers are urged to remain devoted to God and steadfast in doing good, even when their circumstances make that difficult. If faithfulness requires leaving a place or situation that obstructs it, God’s earth is wide; and those who patiently endure for His sake will receive a reward beyond calculation.

translation: Say, “I have been commanded to worship Allah, devoting my worship sincerely to Him.”
interpretation: Worship is to be directed to Allah alone, with no partner, and with sincerity rather than for show or worldly gain.

translation: And I have been commanded to be the first of those who submit to God.
interpretation: The command emphasizes that the Messenger is to lead by example, surrendering himself fully to God’s guidance and obeying it before calling others to do so.

translation: Say, “Indeed, I fear the punishment of a tremendous Day if I were to disobey my Lord.”
interpretation: The verse conveys the seriousness of accountability before God: even the Prophet is commanded to express fear of the punishment that would follow disobedience, emphasizing humility before God and the gravity of the Day of Judgment.

translation: Say, “It is Allah I worship, devoting my religion sincerely to Him.”
interpretation: True worship is directed to Allah alone, with devotion free from seeking the approval of others or associating anything with Him.

translation: So worship whatever you wish besides Him. Say, “Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Truly, that is the manifest loss.”
interpretation: The command to worship whatever one wishes is a warning, not an endorsement: choosing anything besides God leads to the ultimate loss of oneself and one’s family in the Hereafter. The verse calls this loss unmistakable because its consequences are final and cannot be undone.

translation: They will have layers of fire above them and layers beneath them. By this Allah warns His servants: “O My servants, be mindful of Me.”
interpretation: The image of fire surrounding them from every direction makes the warning vivid: no refuge can be found by turning away from God. The direct appeal, “O My servants,” also frames fear of Him as a call to heedful devotion, not merely dread of punishment.

translation: Those who shun false gods, refusing to worship them, and turn back to Allah will have glad tidings. So give good news to My servants.
interpretation: True glad tidings belong to those who reject every rival to Allah and sincerely return to Him; their turning away from false worship is met with the promise of divine favor.

translation: Those who listen to what is said and follow the best of it—those are the ones Allah has guided, and those are people of understanding.
interpretation: This verse praises people who listen thoughtfully rather than accepting every claim uncritically: they discern what is truest and most upright, then act upon it. Their ability to recognize and choose the good is presented as a sign of God’s guidance and sound understanding.

translation: Can one against whom the decree of punishment has become binding be like the one who is guided? Can you rescue those who are in the Fire?
interpretation: The verse consoles the Prophet: he is responsible for conveying the truth, but he cannot force guidance upon those who persistently reject it or rescue them from its consequences; that rests with God.

translation: But those who are mindful of their Lord will have chambers above which are other chambers, built high, with rivers flowing beneath them. This is Allah’s promise; Allah never breaks His promise.
interpretation: The verse portrays the lasting honor and security Allah grants to those who remain mindful of Him. Their elevated chambers signify a reward beyond ordinary imagining, and the closing assurance teaches that this hope rests on Allah’s unfailing promise.

translation: Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky, then channels it into springs in the earth, then brings forth crops of differing colors? They then wither, and you see them turn yellow; then He makes them into dry fragments. Surely in this is a reminder for people of understanding.
interpretation: The changing life of a crop—from growth to decay—invites reflection on how worldly vitality and beauty are temporary, while all change unfolds by Allah’s power. Those who understand are reminded not to be deluded by what fades, but to turn their attention to what endures with Him.

translation: Is one whose heart Allah has opened to Islam, so that he is upon a light from his Lord, [like one whose heart is hardened]? Woe, then, to those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of Allah. They are in manifest error.
interpretation: The verse contrasts God-given openness to faith—which enables a person to see by the guidance of their Lord—with a heart that resists divine remembrance. Its warning is that persistent hardness toward that guidance leaves a person far from the truth.

translation: Allah has sent down the finest discourse: a Book whose verses are consistent and repeated. The skins of those who fear their Lord shiver at it; then their skins and hearts soften at the remembrance of Allah. That is Allah’s guidance, by which He guides whom He wills. And whoever Allah leaves astray will have no guide.
interpretation: The verse portrays true receptivity to revelation as a movement from awe before God’s warning to inward calm and tenderness through His remembrance. This response is itself a gift of divine guidance, not something people can compel for themselves; those deprived of that guidance cannot find another source that will lead them to it.

translation: Is one who shields himself with his face from the worst punishment on the Day of Resurrection [like one who is safe from it]? And it will be said to the wrongdoers, “Taste what you used to earn.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the utter helplessness and humiliation of those facing punishment: they have nothing with which to defend themselves but their own faces. The rebuke links that suffering to the wrong they chose and practiced in this life.

translation: Those before them denied the truth, so the punishment came upon them from a place they did not perceive.
interpretation: The verse warns that people can become so confident in rejecting divine guidance that they fail to recognize the danger gathering around them. Their ruin comes unexpectedly, showing that worldly security does not protect anyone from the consequences of persistent denial.

translation: So Allah made them taste disgrace in the life of this world, and the punishment of the Hereafter is greater—if only they knew.
interpretation: The verse warns that worldly disgrace is only a lesser consequence; the greater punishment lies in the Hereafter. Its closing phrase underscores that truly recognizing this would lead people to take the warning seriously.

translation: We have certainly set forth for people in this Qur’an every kind of example, so that they may take heed.
interpretation: The Qur’an presents varied examples and illustrations to reach people in different ways, helping them reflect, recognize the truth, and let its guidance shape their choices.

translation: An Arabic Qur’an, free from any crookedness, so that they may become mindful of God.
interpretation: Its clear and upright message is free from distortion, offering guidance meant to awaken God-consciousness and turn people away from wrongdoing.

translation: Allah presents the example of a man shared by several quarrelsome partners and a man devoted wholly to one man. Are the two alike? Praise be to Allah—but most of them do not know.
interpretation: The example shows that serving competing masters brings conflict and confusion, while serving one master brings clarity. In the same way, worship belongs to God alone; treating others as partners with Him cannot be equal to sincere devotion to Him.

translation: Indeed, you will die, and they too will die.
interpretation: No one, not even the Prophet or those who oppose him, is exempt from death. The verse places everyone on equal ground before mortality and points to the accountability that follows in the Hereafter.

translation: Then, on the Day of Resurrection, you will dispute before your Lord.
interpretation: Disputes and wrongs that remain unresolved in this life will be brought before God, where every claim will be judged with perfect justice.

translation: Who, then, is more unjust than one who fabricates lies about Allah and rejects the truth when it comes to him? Is there not a dwelling in Hell for the disbelievers?
interpretation: The verse presents deliberate distortion of what is attributed to God, together with refusal to accept truth once it is clear, as a grave form of injustice. Its closing question warns that such rejection has a fitting and lasting consequence.

translation: And the one who brought the truth and those who affirmed it—those are the God-conscious.
interpretation: The verse honors the one who conveys God’s truth and those who sincerely accept it, presenting faithful commitment to that truth as a mark of God-consciousness.

translation: They will have whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the reward of those who excel in doing good.
interpretation: Those who worship God sincerely and act righteously will be honored with a reward beyond measure: they will find their deepest desires fulfilled by their Lord.

translation: So that Allah may forgive them for the worst of what they did and reward them according to the best of what they used to do.
interpretation: The verse points to Allah’s generous mercy: He pardons the believers’ gravest misdeeds and grants them reward in keeping with their finest deeds, rather than treating them only according to their failures.

translation: Is Allah not sufficient for His servant? Yet they frighten you with those besides Him. And whoever Allah leaves to stray, no one can guide him.
interpretation: The verse reassures the Prophet that reliance on Allah is enough, so threats invoking other powers need not shake his trust. It also warns that guidance cannot be forced upon someone who turns away from it and is left to that choice.

translation: Whoever Allah guides, none can lead astray. Is Allah not Almighty, the Possessor of retribution?
interpretation: Allah’s guidance cannot be overturned by any power, and His might assures that those who oppose His truth will ultimately face His just retribution.

translation: If you ask them, “Who created the heavens and the earth?” they will surely say, “Allah.” Say, “Have you considered those you call upon besides Allah? If Allah intends harm for me, can they remove His harm? Or if He intends mercy for me, can they withhold His mercy?” Say, “Allah is sufficient for me; those who trust place their trust in Him.”
interpretation: The verse exposes the inconsistency of acknowledging Allah as Creator while relying on beings that have no power over harm or mercy. True trust belongs to Allah alone, whose will cannot be overridden and whose sufficiency frees the believer from dependence on false objects of worship.

translation: Say, “O my people, act according to your position; I too am acting. You will soon know.”
interpretation: The Prophet is told to answer his opponents with firmness: they may persist in their course, while he remains committed to his mission. The words warn that the truth of their opposing paths will become clear through their eventual outcome.

translation: You will soon know upon whom a punishment that disgraces him will come, and upon whom an abiding punishment will descend.
interpretation: This is a warning that rejection of God’s message has consequences: the truth will become clear when punishment overtakes those who persist in denial, bringing disgrace and lasting suffering.

translation: Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book for all people in truth. Whoever is guided is guided for their own good, and whoever goes astray does so only to their own detriment. You are not their keeper.
interpretation: The verse teaches that divine guidance is offered as truth, but belief cannot be imposed: each person is accountable for how they respond. The Prophet’s duty is to convey the message, not to control people’s choices or bear responsibility for their rejection.

translation: Allah takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that have not died during their sleep. He keeps those for whom He has decreed death and sends the others back until an appointed term. Surely in this are signs for people who reflect.
interpretation: The verse presents sleep and death as moments in which human life lies entirely in God’s hands: the soul’s return from sleep is a sign of His power to restore life, while its being held at death points to the certainty of a final appointed end. Reflecting on this should deepen awareness of human dependence on God and of the reality of resurrection.

translation: Or have they taken intercessors besides Allah? Say, “Even if they possess nothing and understand nothing?”
interpretation: The verse challenges the idea that powerless beings who have no understanding can secure anyone’s intercession. It calls people to recognize that no one should be relied upon as an intercessor apart from Allah’s authority.

translation: Say, “All intercession belongs to Allah alone. To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and to Him you will be returned.”
interpretation: No one possesses independent power to intercede; any intercession is under Allah’s authority. Since all dominion belongs to Him and everyone returns to Him, worship and ultimate reliance are due to Him alone.

translation: When Allah alone is mentioned, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter recoil in aversion; but when those besides Him are mentioned, they rejoice.
interpretation: The verse points to a heart turned away from accountability: it resists the call to worship Allah alone, yet welcomes attention given to other objects of devotion. It presents this reaction as a sign of misplaced allegiance and a refusal to face the Hereafter.

translation: Say, “O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, You will judge between Your servants concerning that over which they used to differ.”
interpretation: The verse places ultimate judgment beyond the limits of human knowledge and authority: Allah knows both what is hidden within people and what is openly done, so disputes are finally resolved by His perfect knowledge and justice.

translation: If those who did wrong possessed everything on earth, and as much again besides, they would offer it to ransom themselves from the terrible punishment on the Day of Resurrection. And there will become apparent to them from God what they had never expected.
interpretation: The verse warns that worldly possessions cannot shield a person from divine judgment: when its reality is revealed, even unimaginable wealth would seem worth surrendering, yet it cannot undo what was earned. The punishment and reckoning will also expose consequences they never anticipated.

translation: The evil consequences of what they had done became clear to them, and what they used to mock encompassed them.
interpretation: The verse portrays the moment when denial can no longer shield people from the truth: the consequences of their choices become undeniable, and the warnings they dismissed as ridiculous become the very reality they face.

translation: When hardship touches a person, he calls upon Us. Then, when We grant him a blessing from Us, he says, “I was given it only because of knowledge I possess.” Rather, it is a trial, but most of them do not know.
interpretation: The verse warns against treating prosperity as proof of one’s own merit or mastery. A blessing tests whether a person will remain grateful and mindful of their dependence on God; claiming it solely as the result of one’s own knowledge reveals a failure to recognize that test.

translation: Those before them said the same, but what they had earned did not benefit them at all.
interpretation: Earlier peoples made the same claim of self-sufficiency, yet their wealth and achievements could not protect them from God’s judgment. The verse warns against trusting worldly success as though it were a safeguard.

translation: So the evil consequences of what they had earned befell them. And those among these who have done wrong will likewise be struck by the evil consequences of what they have earned, and they will not escape.
interpretation: The verse warns that wrongdoing brings consequences that cannot be evaded: just as earlier people faced the results of their deeds, those who do wrong now will also face the consequences of theirs.

translation: Do they not know that Allah expands provision for whom He wills and restricts it? Surely in that are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: Changes in a person’s provision are governed by Allah’s wisdom, not a measure of their worth or His favor. Believers recognize this as a sign of His power and entrust their provision to Him.

translation: Say, “O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of God’s mercy. Indeed, God forgives all sins; He is truly the All-Forgiving, the Most Merciful.”
interpretation: The tender address “My servants” shows that sin does not place a person beyond the reach of God’s care. The verse calls those burdened by wrongdoing to turn back with hope: no sin is too great for sincere repentance and God’s forgiveness, so despair must not become a barrier to returning to Him.

translation: Turn back to your Lord and submit yourselves to Him before the punishment comes upon you; then you will not be helped.
interpretation: The verse presents repentance as a response to God’s mercy that should not be postponed: turning back means abandoning wrongdoing and seeking God, while submission means entrusting oneself to His guidance. Its warning is that once the consequences of rejecting that guidance arrive, the opportunity to seek rescue will have passed.

translation: Follow the best of what has been sent down to you from your Lord before the punishment comes upon you suddenly while you are unaware.
interpretation: The verse urges people to embrace and live by the guidance God has revealed without delay, since postponing repentance and obedience may leave them unprepared when accountability comes unexpectedly.

translation: Lest a soul should say, “Alas for me, for how I neglected my duty toward Allah! Indeed, I was among those who mocked.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the regret of someone who, after the chance to turn back has passed, recognizes that they neglected their obligations toward Allah and treated His guidance with ridicule. It urges people to take that guidance seriously while they still have the opportunity to respond.

translation: Or it may say, “If only Allah had guided me, I would have been among the God-conscious.”
interpretation: This expresses the regret of someone who, when facing the consequences of their choices, blames their failure to be guided rather than acknowledging their own rejection of the guidance made available to them.

translation: Or it may say, when it sees the punishment, “If only I could return, then I would be among those who do good.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the regret of someone who, upon facing punishment, wishes for another chance to return to worldly life and act righteously. It warns that such remorse comes when the opportunity to change has already passed.

translation: Yes indeed, My signs came to you, but you rejected them, acted arrogantly, and were among the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse teaches that a person cannot excuse rejection of guidance by claiming it never reached them: when God’s signs have been made clear, turning away from them out of pride is a deliberate choice for which one is accountable.

translation: On the Day of Resurrection, you will see those who lied about Allah with faces darkened. Is there not in Hell a dwelling for the arrogant?
interpretation: The verse portrays the disgrace awaiting those who knowingly attribute falsehoods to God: their outward appearance will reveal their humiliation, and their arrogance will have led them to a fitting abode in Hell.

translation: And Allah will save those who were mindful of Him through their triumph; no harm will touch them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: The verse assures those who remain conscious of God and avoid wrongdoing that He will deliver them from the consequences of evil and grant them lasting security, so they need not fear what lies ahead or mourn what they have left behind.

translation: Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is the Guardian over all things.
interpretation: Everything owes its existence to Allah and remains under His care and authority. Nothing lies beyond His knowledge or governance, and every affair ultimately depends on Him.

translation: To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth. Those who disbelieve in Allah’s signs—it is they who are the losers.
interpretation: Since all authority and control belong to Allah, His signs are the way to recognize and follow the truth. Rejecting them means turning away from that guidance and suffering the ultimate loss.

translation: Say, “Would you command me to worship anyone other than Allah, O ignorant ones?”
interpretation: The verse expresses a decisive rejection of associating anything with Allah in worship. Calling those who make this demand “ignorant” points to their failure to recognize that worship belongs to Allah alone.

translation: And it has certainly been revealed to you and to those before you: “If you associate others with Allah, your deeds will surely come to nothing, and you will surely be among the losers.”
interpretation: This is a forceful warning about the seriousness of associating partners with Allah: even the greatest deeds cannot benefit a person if they abandon pure worship of Him. Addressing the Prophet ﷺ underscores the universal principle; it does not mean that he committed shirk.

translation: Rather, worship Allah and be among the grateful.
interpretation: Worship belongs to Allah alone, and sincere devotion to Him should be joined with gratitude for His blessings.

translation: They have not measured Allah with the measure due to Him. The whole earth will be in His grasp on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded in His right hand. Glorified and exalted is He above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: The verse rebukes those who fail to recognize Allah’s immense majesty and absolute sovereignty: on the Day of Resurrection, all creation will be wholly subject to His power. Its closing declaration affirms that He is exalted far above the partners and likenesses people attribute to Him.

translation: And the Trumpet will be blown, and all who are in the heavens and the earth will fall unconscious, except those whom Allah wills. Then it will be blown again, and suddenly they will be standing, looking on.
interpretation: The verse portrays the decisive transition from the present creation to resurrection: every created being remains subject to Allah’s command, and life after death begins only when He wills it. The exception is left unspecified, directing attention to the absolute authority of Allah rather than inviting speculation about whom He will spare.

translation: The earth will shine with the light of its Lord; the Record will be set down; the prophets and the witnesses will be brought; and judgment will be passed between them with truth, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, God’s light and justice will be manifest, and every person’s deeds will be accounted for. The prophets and witnesses will testify, and God will judge with perfect fairness, so no one will be deprived of what is due to them or burdened with injustice.

translation: And every soul will be repaid in full for what it did, and He knows best what they do.
interpretation: This assures that God’s judgment is perfectly just: no deed is lost or misjudged, because His knowledge of people’s actions is complete.

translation: Those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups. When they reach it, its gates will be opened, and its keepers will say to them, “Did messengers from among yourselves not come to you, reciting to you the verses of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this Day of yours?” They will say, “Yes indeed; but the decree of punishment has come to pass against the disbelievers.”
interpretation: The keepers’ question makes clear that punishment is not imposed without warning: messengers from among the people had conveyed God’s signs and cautioned them about the Day of Judgment. Their admission confirms that the warning reached them; the consequence follows from their rejection, not from a lack of guidance.

translation: It will be said, “Enter the gates of Hell, abiding there forever. How wretched is the abode of the arrogant!”
interpretation: The verse warns that arrogance—rejecting truth out of pride—leads to lasting ruin; the condemned find no honor or refuge in the end, only a terrible abode.

translation: And those who were mindful of their Lord will be led to Paradise in groups. When they arrive there and its gates are opened, its keepers will say, “Peace be upon you. You have become pure, so enter it to abide forever.”
interpretation: The welcome of the keepers shows that the God-conscious enter Paradise not merely as arrivals, but as people accepted and made pure. Their lasting welcome reflects the honor and security of God’s reward.

translation: And they will say, “Praise belongs to Allah, who has fulfilled His promise to us and made us inherit the land, settling wherever we wish in Paradise. How excellent is the reward of those who strive!”
interpretation: The verse portrays the joy of the people of Paradise as recognition that Allah’s promise has come true. Their welcome and freedom in Paradise are a gift from Him, while their reward is described as excellent because they acted faithfully in this life.

translation: And you will see the angels encircling the Throne, glorifying their Lord with praise. Judgment will be passed between them in truth, and it will be proclaimed, “Praise be to Allah, Lord of all worlds.”
interpretation: The verse presents divine justice as complete and unquestionable: every matter is resolved in truth, and the final recognition of Allah’s praise affirms that all authority and judgment belong to Him.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Ḥā Mīm.
interpretation: The opening invokes Allah’s mercy, then begins with the mysterious letters Ḥā Mīm, whose precise meaning is not known; their presence invites reflection and marks the solemn opening of the revelation.

translation: The sending down of the Book is from Allah, the Almighty, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the revelation comes from God alone: His might guarantees its authority, and His perfect knowledge means its guidance is founded on wisdom and truth.

translation: Forgiver of sin, accepter of repentance, severe in punishment, and possessor of abundant grace. There is no deity but Him; to Him is the final return.
interpretation: The verse presents God’s mercy and justice together: His forgiveness and acceptance of sincere repentance invite people to turn back to Him, while the warning of punishment calls them to take wrongdoing seriously. His abundant grace is the source of hope, and the certainty of returning to Him gives every choice lasting significance.

translation: No one disputes the signs of Allah except those who disbelieve. So do not let their movement through the lands deceive you.
interpretation: The verse warns that the disbelievers’ apparent freedom, prosperity, or influence in the world is not proof that they are right or that they have escaped accountability; outward worldly success should not unsettle a believer’s trust in the truth.

translation: Before them, the people of Noah denied the truth, as did the confederated nations after them. Every community plotted against its messenger to seize him, and they argued with falsehood to defeat the truth. Then I seized them—so how terrible was My punishment!
interpretation: The verse warns that determined opposition to a messenger—whether through threats or deceptive arguments—cannot overcome the truth or escape God’s judgment. Its closing question underscores the severity of the punishment that befell those who persisted in such defiance.

translation: And thus the decree of your Lord has come to pass against those who disbelieved: they are the companions of the Fire.
interpretation: The verse presents their final fate as the fulfillment of God’s just judgment, affirming that persistent disbelief has real and lasting consequences.

translation: Those who bear the Throne and those around it glorify their Lord with praise, believe in Him, and ask forgiveness for those who believe: “Our Lord, You encompass all things in mercy and knowledge, so forgive those who repent and follow Your way, and protect them from the punishment of Hellfire.”
interpretation: The verse shows the honor of believers in that the angels closest to God pray for their forgiveness. Their supplication connects hope in God’s all-encompassing mercy and knowledge with sincere repentance and steadfastly following His way.

translation: Our Lord, admit them into the Gardens of Eden that You have promised them, along with those among their fathers, spouses, and descendants who were righteous. Indeed, You are the Almighty, the Wise.
interpretation: This prayer asks God to grant the believers Paradise and reunite them there with their righteous family members. It entrusts that hope to God, whose power is absolute and whose decisions are perfectly wise.

translation: And protect them from evil deeds. Whoever You protect from evil deeds on that Day, You have indeed shown mercy to; that is the great triumph.
interpretation: The verse presents deliverance from evil and its consequences on the Day of Judgment as a gift of God’s mercy. True success is therefore not merely worldly achievement, but being granted that protection by God.

translation: Those who disbelieved will be called out: “God’s abhorrence of you was greater than your abhorrence of yourselves, when you were called to faith but chose to disbelieve.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the disbelievers’ remorse when they face the consequences of their rejection: they come to loathe themselves, but are told that God’s condemnation of their persistent refusal was even greater. It underscores the gravity of turning away from faith when it was offered to them.

translation: They will say, “Our Lord, You caused us to die twice and gave us life twice. We now acknowledge our sins. Is there any way out?”
interpretation: They recognize that God brought them from a state without life into worldly life, caused them to die, and then restored them to life for the Resurrection. Their confession comes too late: they seek a return from the punishment, but the question is a desperate plea, not a promise that escape will be granted.

translation: That is because when Allah alone was called upon, you disbelieved; but when partners were associated with Him, you believed. So judgment belongs to Allah, the Most High, the Most Great.
interpretation: The verse condemns the reversal of those who reject Allah’s exclusive right to worship yet accept partners alongside Him. Their response reveals that they resist the truth of tawḥīd, while ultimate authority and judgment belong to Allah alone, exalted above all and supreme in greatness.

translation: He is the One who shows you His signs and sends down provision for you from the sky. Yet none takes heed except one who turns back to Him.
interpretation: God’s signs and provision invite people to recognize His care and authority, but this recognition takes root only in a heart willing to turn back to Him in faith and humility.

translation: So call upon Allah, devoting your worship sincerely to Him, even if the disbelievers dislike it.
interpretation: True devotion is directed to God alone, without compromise for the sake of pleasing others; opposition from those who reject faith does not change the believer’s commitment to worship sincerely.

translation: Exalted in rank, the Lord of the Throne, He sends the Spirit by His command to whomever He wills of His servants, to warn of the Day of Meeting.
interpretation: God, supreme in majesty and authority, entrusts revelation to chosen servants so they may warn people of the Day when all will be gathered before Him.

translation: The Day when they will come forth, nothing about them will be hidden from Allah. “To whom belongs all dominion today?” “To Allah, the One, the Irresistible.”
interpretation: The verse presents the Day of Judgment as the moment when every illusion of independent power and every claim to authority is stripped away. The question and its answer affirm that ultimate sovereignty has always belonged to Allah alone, whose authority cannot be resisted.

translation: Today every soul will be recompensed for what it has earned. No injustice will be done today. Indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning.
interpretation: The verse presents the Day of Judgment as a moment of perfect accountability: each person’s deeds are met with a just recompense, without loss or favoritism. Allah’s swift reckoning reflects that nothing escapes His knowledge and that His judgment needs no delay.

translation: Warn them of the approaching Day, when hearts will be in the throats, choked with anguish. The wrongdoers will have no loyal friend and no intercessor whose plea is heeded.
interpretation: The verse portrays the terror of judgment as an inward anguish so overwhelming it is almost physical, while making clear that those who persist in wrongdoing cannot rely on worldly loyalties or influence to secure their rescue.

translation: He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the hearts conceal.
interpretation: Even a fleeting, furtive glance and the intentions kept hidden within a person are fully known to God; no act of inward or outward deception escapes His knowledge.

translation: And Allah judges with truth, while those whom they call upon besides Him judge nothing. Indeed, Allah is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.
interpretation: The verse contrasts Allah’s just and authoritative judgment with the powerlessness of those invoked besides Him. Because Allah hears and sees all things, His judgment is founded on complete knowledge, and He alone deserves to be relied upon.

translation: Have they not traveled through the land and seen what was the end of those who came before them? They were mightier than them and left greater آثار in the land, yet God seized them for their sins, and they had no one to protect them from God.
interpretation: The verse warns that worldly strength and lasting works cannot shield people from the consequences of wrongdoing when they reject God’s guidance.

translation: That was because their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they disbelieved; so Allah seized them. Surely He is Powerful, severe in punishment.
interpretation: The verse teaches that rejecting clear guidance carries consequences: no people can escape God’s judgment, for His power is absolute and His punishment cannot be resisted.

translation: And We certainly sent Moses with Our signs and clear authority.
interpretation: Moses’ mission was supported by unmistakable signs and compelling proof, showing that his call was grounded in divine authority rather than personal claim.

translation: To Pharaoh, Haman, and Qarun; but they said, “A sorcerer, a liar.”
interpretation: Their response shows how those invested in power can dismiss a messenger by attacking his character rather than considering the truth he brings.

translation: When he brought them the truth from Us, they said, “Kill the sons of those who believe with him, and spare their women.” Yet the schemes of the disbelievers lead only to ruin.
interpretation: The verse shows how those threatened by truth may resort to violence against believers and their families to preserve their power. Such oppression cannot ultimately defeat God’s purpose; it only exposes the perpetrators’ misguided reliance on schemes that cannot escape His judgment.

translation: Pharaoh said, “Leave me to kill Moses, and let him call upon his Lord. I fear that he will change your religion or spread corruption in the land.”
interpretation: Pharaoh presents his plan to kill Moses as protection of the people’s religion and public order, though his words expose how he treats a challenge to his authority as a threat to be silenced.

translation: Moses said, “I seek refuge in my Lord and your Lord from every arrogant person who does not believe in the Day of Reckoning.”
interpretation: Moses places his trust in God, the Lord of both himself and his people, seeking protection from the arrogant who deny that they will be held accountable. The verse presents reliance on God as a source of strength in the face of hostility and pride.

translation: A believing man from Pharaoh’s family, who was concealing his faith, said, “Would you kill a man merely for saying, ‘My Lord is Allah,’ when he has brought you clear proofs from your Lord? If he is lying, then the harm of his lie will be upon him; but if he is truthful, then some of what he warns you of will befall you. Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is excessive and a liar.”
interpretation: The believer appeals to reason and justice: uncertainty about Moses’ claim is no grounds for killing him, since the consequences differ sharply depending on whether he is truthful. His measured argument also exposes the danger of letting arrogance and aggression override evidence. The closing warning points to how persistent excess and falsehood can close a person off from divine guidance.

translation: “My people, the kingdom is yours today, and you are dominant in the land. But who will protect us from God’s punishment if it comes upon us?” Pharaoh said, “I show you only what I see, and I guide you only to the way of right guidance.”
interpretation: The speaker warns that worldly power cannot shield anyone from God’s judgment, while Pharaoh presents his own judgment as the sole reliable guide. The contrast exposes the danger of mistaking political authority and self-assurance for truth.

translation: And the one who believed said, “O my people, indeed I fear for you the like of the day of the confederates.”
interpretation: He warns his people that their rejection of the truth could bring upon them a fate like that of earlier peoples who united against their messengers yet were destroyed. The warning urges them to learn from those precedents before it is too late.

translation: Like the fate of the people of Noah, ʿĀd, Thamūd, and those who came after them. And Allah does not will any injustice for His servants.
interpretation: The verse recalls earlier peoples as a warning: their ruin was not an arbitrary act of injustice, but the consequence of their own wrongdoing. Allah does not wrong His servants.

translation: And, O my people, I fear for you the Day of Calling.
interpretation: The speaker warns his people of the Day of Resurrection, when people will call out in distress and seek help, but no one will escape God’s judgment. His words express sincere concern that they turn back before that day arrives.

translation: On the Day you turn your backs and flee, you will have no one to protect you from God. And whoever God leaves to stray has no guide.
interpretation: The verse warns that no escape or worldly protection can avail a person before God; when a person is left without divine guidance, no one else can lead them to the truth.

translation: Joseph had indeed come to you before with clear proofs, yet you continued to doubt what he brought you. Then, when he died, you said, ‘Allah will never send a messenger after him.’ Thus Allah leaves astray whoever is excessive and full of doubt.
interpretation: The verse portrays persistent doubt as more than a lack of evidence: despite clear proofs, people can cling to suspicion until they turn a prophet’s death into an excuse to reject any further guidance. It warns that those who exceed the bounds in denial and remain entrenched in doubt may be left to wander from the truth.

translation: Those who argue about the signs of Allah without any authority that has come to them—their argument is greatly hateful in the sight of Allah and of those who believe. Thus Allah seals every heart that is arrogant and tyrannical.
interpretation: The verse warns that disputing God’s signs without sound evidence is not merely an intellectual error: when driven by arrogance, it hardens the heart until it becomes unreceptive to truth.

translation: Pharaoh said, “O Haman, build for me a lofty tower, so that I may reach the pathways.”
interpretation: Pharaoh’s command reflects his arrogance and refusal to consider the truth: he seeks a grand display of power to make his challenge to Moses seem credible, treating divine reality as though it could be tested or reached by worldly means.

translation: “The ways leading up to the heavens, so that I may look upon the God of Moses—though I truly think he is lying.” Thus Pharaoh’s evil deeds were made alluring to him, and he was turned away from the path. Pharaoh’s scheme led only to ruin.
interpretation: Pharaoh’s claim to seek a way to reach God is a display of arrogant mockery, not a sincere search for truth. By treating revelation with contempt, he becomes further deceived by his own wrongdoing and leads others away from guidance; his schemes are ultimately self-defeating.

translation: And the one who believed said, “O my people, follow me; I will guide you to the way of right guidance.”
interpretation: The believer speaks with concern for his people, urging them to trust his counsel because it leads toward truth and sound judgment. The verse highlights the responsibility to guide others with sincerity and confidence in what is right.

translation: O my people, this worldly life is only a passing enjoyment, while the Hereafter is truly the abode of permanence.
interpretation: The verse calls people to measure their priorities by what endures, rather than letting temporary pleasures distract them from preparing for their ultimate destination.

translation: Whoever does an evil deed will be recompensed only with its equivalent; but whoever does what is right, whether male or female, while being a believer—those will enter Paradise, where they will be provided for without measure.
interpretation: The verse presents God’s justice as measured and His generosity as abundant: wrongdoing is not punished beyond its due, while sincere goodness grounded in faith is rewarded beyond calculation. The promise applies equally to men and women.

translation: And, O my people, why do I call you to salvation while you call me to the Fire?
interpretation: The speaker appeals to his people with sorrow and urgency: he is calling them toward faith and deliverance, while they are urging him toward the path that leads to punishment. The contrast exposes the danger of rejecting sincere counsel and the speaker’s concern for their salvation.

translation: You call me to disbelieve in Allah and associate with Him that of which I have no knowledge, while I call you to the Almighty, the All-Forgiving.
interpretation: The speaker contrasts an invitation founded on baseless claims with a call to worship Allah alone: He is supreme in power, yet open to forgiving those who turn back to Him.

translation: There is no doubt that what you call me to has no right to be invoked, either in this world or in the Hereafter. Our return is to Allah, and the transgressors are the companions of the Fire.
interpretation: The speaker rejects the false gods his people urge him to worship: they have no true claim to worship or power to answer those who call upon them. Since everyone will return to Allah for judgment, those who exceed His bounds by associating partners with Him face the Fire.

translation: You will remember what I say to you, and I entrust my affair to Allah. Surely Allah sees His servants well.
interpretation: The speaker trusts that the truth will become clear in time, even if his people reject it now. By entrusting his affair to Allah, he places himself under the care and judgment of the One who sees every person’s circumstances and deeds.

translation: So Allah protected him from the evil consequences of their plotting, while a terrible punishment engulfed the people of Pharaoh.
interpretation: The verse shows that the believers’ safety rests with Allah: the plot intended to harm the righteous man was turned away from him, while those who persisted in wrongdoing were overtaken by punishment.

translation: They are exposed to the Fire morning and evening; and on the Day the Hour is established, [it will be said], “Admit the people of Pharaoh to the severest punishment.”
interpretation: The verse distinguishes the punishment the people of Pharaoh undergo before the Resurrection from the still more severe punishment that follows when the Hour is established, indicating that punishment begins before the final judgment.

translation: And when they argue in the Fire, the weak will say to those who were arrogant, “We followed you, so can you take away from us any share of the Fire?”
interpretation: The verse portrays the helplessness of those who surrendered their judgment to arrogant leaders: in the Hereafter, following them cannot transfer or lessen the followers’ punishment, and the leaders have no power to rescue them.

translation: Those who were arrogant will say, “Indeed, we are all in it; God has judged between His servants.”
interpretation: The verse shows that worldly arrogance and claims of superiority offer no escape from God’s settled judgment: in the Hereafter, those who exalted themselves stand equally subject to its consequence.

translation: Those in the Fire will say to the keepers of Hell, “Call upon your Lord to lessen the punishment for us for just one day.”
interpretation: Their plea reveals the depth of their despair: they no longer ask for deliverance, only for a brief easing of their suffering. Yet they turn to the keepers rather than directly calling upon God, underscoring how utterly powerless and regretful they have become.

translation: They will say, “Did your messengers not come to you with clear proofs?” They will say, “Yes.” They will say, “Then call [on whom you will].” But the supplication of the disbelievers is only in vain.
interpretation: The verse portrays the disbelievers being confronted with the truth they had once rejected: they acknowledge that clear proofs reached them, yet now no appeal to their false gods or other protectors can rescue them. Their calls are futile because they turned away from the guidance that could have saved them.

translation: Indeed, We will surely support Our messengers and those who believe in the life of this world and on the Day when the witnesses stand forth.
interpretation: God’s support does not mean that believers will never face suffering or defeat; it means that their cause is not abandoned. In this life, God grants His messengers and the faithful whatever vindication and steadfastness He wills, and on the Day of Judgment their truth will be publicly upheld before all witnesses.

translation: On the Day when the wrongdoers’ excuses will not benefit them; theirs will be the curse, and theirs will be the evil abode.
interpretation: The verse warns that, in the Hereafter, wrongdoing cannot be escaped through excuses or self-justification. The wrongdoers will face exclusion from God’s mercy and a grievous final abode.

translation: And We certainly gave Moses the guidance, and We made the Children of Israel inherit the Book.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that divine guidance was entrusted to Moses and then passed on to the Children of Israel through scripture, placing upon them the responsibility to uphold and live by it.

translation: Guidance and a reminder for people of understanding.
interpretation: It is a source of guidance and a reminder for those who use sound judgment and reflect on its message.

translation: So be patient; surely God’s promise is true. Seek forgiveness for your sin, and glorify your Lord with praise in the evening and at dawn.
interpretation: The verse calls for steadfastness rooted in trust that God’s promise will be fulfilled, joined with humility before Him through seeking forgiveness and keeping up His remembrance at the beginning and end of the day.

translation: Indeed, those who dispute Allah’s signs without any authority that has come to them have nothing in their hearts but pride—something they will never attain. So seek refuge in Allah; surely He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.
interpretation: Their baseless disputation springs from pride and a desire for greatness they cannot attain. The verse directs the believer to seek Allah’s protection from such arrogance and opposition, trusting that He hears what people say and sees what they do.

translation: The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of humankind, but most people do not know.
interpretation: The verse calls people to reflect: if God created the vast heavens and earth, bringing human beings back to life is certainly within His power. Many fail to recognize this because they do not consider what creation itself shows about God’s power.

translation: The blind and the seeing are not equal, nor are those who believe and do righteous deeds equal to the evildoer. How little you take heed.
interpretation: Just as physical blindness is not the same as sight, spiritual insight is not the same as heedlessness: faith expressed through righteous deeds cannot be equated with wrongdoing. The verse urges people to recognize this moral distinction and reflect on it.

translation: Indeed, the Hour is surely coming—there is no doubt about it—but most people do not believe.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the Day of Judgment will certainly arrive, even though many people live as if it will not. Its certainty calls people to take accountability before God seriously rather than be misled by disbelief or heedlessness.

translation: Your Lord says, “Call upon Me; I will answer you. Those who are too arrogant to worship Me will enter Hell, humbled.”
interpretation: The verse presents turning to God as an expression of humble worship, not merely a request for particular favors. God’s promise of an answer is an assurance of His attentiveness, while the warning condemns the pride that refuses dependence on Him; the answer need not take the exact form or timing a person expects.

translation: Allah is the One who made the night for you to rest in, and the day bright with sight. Indeed, Allah is gracious to people, but most people are not grateful.
interpretation: The alternation of night and day is a continual mercy: each is made suited to human needs. Recognizing this gift should lead people to gratitude and to acknowledging the One who provides it, yet many overlook that grace.

translation: That is Allah, your Lord, the Creator of all things. There is no deity except Him. How, then, are you turned away?
interpretation: Because all existence depends on Allah as its Creator, directing worship elsewhere is a departure from the truth evident in creation itself.

translation: Thus are turned away those who used to deny the signs of Allah.
interpretation: Persistent denial of God’s signs leads people away from the truth, not because the signs are unclear, but because they refuse to accept them.

translation: Allah is the One who made the earth a dwelling place for you and the sky a canopy, fashioned you and made your forms beautiful, and provided you with good things. That is Allah, your Lord. So blessed is Allah, Lord of all worlds.
interpretation: The verse directs people to recognize that the order and provision sustaining their lives are gifts from their Lord. Its call to glorify Allah follows from this recognition: gratitude and worship belong to the One whose care is evident in both creation and sustenance.

translation: He is the Ever-Living; there is no god but Him. So call upon Him, devoting your worship sincerely to Him. All praise belongs to Allah, Lord of all worlds.
interpretation: Because Allah alone possesses eternal life and is the only true deity, worship and supplication belong to Him alone, offered with sincere devotion; all praise is His as Lord of every world.

translation: Say, “I have been forbidden to worship those you call upon besides Allah, now that clear proofs have come to me from my Lord; and I have been commanded to submit to the Lord of all worlds.”
