interpretation: The verse presents sincere submission to God as the response required by clear guidance: worship must be directed to the Lord of all worlds alone, not to anything invoked besides Him.

translation: He is the One who created you from dust, then from a drop of fluid, then from a clinging clot; then He brings you forth as infants, then lets you reach your full strength, and then become old—though some of you die before that—so that you may reach an appointed term, and perhaps understand.
interpretation: The stages of human life reveal that our existence and development are in God’s hands. The fact that some die before reaching old age also reminds us that life’s course is not ours to control; reflecting on this should awaken humility and help us recognize our dependence on our Creator.

translation: He is the One who gives life and causes death. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, “Be,” and it is.
interpretation: The verse teaches that life, death, and all events unfold under God’s complete authority. His will needs no effort or means beyond His command, and what He decrees cannot be thwarted.

translation: Have you not seen those who dispute about the signs of Allah—how they are turned away?
interpretation: The verse draws attention to the bewildering way people can turn away from the truth even when God’s signs are before them, persisting in argument instead of reflecting on what those signs make clear.

translation: Those who denied the Book and what We sent Our messengers with will soon know.
interpretation: The warning is that those who reject divine revelation will eventually face a moment when its truth and the consequences of their rejection become unmistakable.

translation: When the shackles are around their necks and they are dragged in chains,
interpretation: This depicts the utter helplessness and humiliation of those facing God’s judgment: they are bound and forcibly led, with no power to escape the consequence of their deeds.

translation: In boiling water; then in the Fire they will be set ablaze.
interpretation: The verse uses the image of being kindled in the Fire to convey the severity of the punishment awaiting those addressed, following their exposure to boiling water.

translation: Then it will be said to them, “Where are those you used to associate with Allah?”
interpretation: The question is a rebuke that exposes the false gods’ inability to help their worshippers. It confronts them with the failure of the devotion they placed in partners beside God.

translation: Besides Allah. They will say, “They have vanished from us. Rather, we were not invoking anything before.” Thus does Allah lead the disbelievers astray.
interpretation: When the false gods they relied on prove powerless, the disbelievers disown their former worship. Their denial reveals how completely they had been misled: they placed their trust in what could neither hear nor help them, and so lost sight of the truth that only Allah deserves worship.

translation: That is because you used to rejoice on earth without right and to behave insolently.
interpretation: The verse presents their punishment as the consequence of arrogant, unjust delight in worldly life: instead of receiving their blessings with gratitude and humility, they exulted in wrongdoing and acted as though they were beyond accountability.

translation: Enter the gates of Hell, abiding therein. How evil is the abode of the arrogant.
interpretation: This is a stern warning that arrogance—especially the pride that leads one to reject the truth—ends in a lasting and wretched abode, leaving no room for boasting or self-exaltation.

translation: So be patient. Indeed, Allah’s promise is true. Whether We show you some of what We have promised them, or cause you to die, to Us they will be returned.
interpretation: The verse reassures the Prophet to remain steadfast: the outcome does not depend on whether he witnesses the promised judgment in this life, because all people will ultimately return to God and face His judgment.

translation: We have certainly sent messengers before you. We have told you about some of them, and about others We have not told you. No messenger could bring a sign except by God’s permission. When God’s command comes, judgment is made with truth, and there the falsifiers will lose.
interpretation: The verse teaches that God’s messengers are not free to produce signs whenever people demand them; their mission and the signs given to them are governed by God’s wisdom and permission. The final judgment will establish the truth and expose those who persistently deny it.

translation: Allah is the One who made livestock for you, so that you may ride some of them and eat from some.
interpretation: The verse points to God’s care in making animals useful to human life, and calls people to recognize these everyday benefits as gifts that invite gratitude and humility.

translation: And you have benefits in them, and through them you may reach a destination you desire. And upon them and upon ships you are carried.
interpretation: The verse points to God’s provision in making different means of transport available, enabling people to pursue their purposes across land and sea.

translation: And He shows you His signs. So which of Allah’s signs will you deny?
interpretation: The question is a rebuke that invites honest reflection: when God continually makes His signs known, denying them is not a lack of evidence but a refusal to acknowledge what they point to.

translation: Have they not traveled through the land and seen what became of those who came before them? They were greater in number, mightier in strength, and left more آثار upon the earth; yet all they had earned did not avail them.
interpretation: The verse warns against mistaking worldly power, wealth, or accomplishments for lasting security. Even peoples who seemed stronger and more established could not escape the consequences of their deeds, so their example calls people to humility and accountability before God.

translation: When their messengers came to them with clear proofs, they rejoiced in the knowledge they possessed, and what they used to mock encompassed them.
interpretation: The verse warns that people may become so confident in their own knowledge that they dismiss clear guidance. Their pride and mockery do not protect them; instead, the very consequence they scoffed at ultimately overtakes them.

translation: When they saw Our punishment, they said, “We believe in Allah alone, and we reject what we used to associate with Him.”
interpretation: Their confession came only after punishment had become undeniable. The verse shows that belief forced by the sight of inevitable judgment is not the sincere, freely chosen faith that could have guided them before it was too late.

translation: But their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our punishment. Such is God’s way, already established among His servants; and there the disbelievers were lost.
interpretation: The verse teaches that faith adopted only when punishment becomes undeniable cannot undo a life of rejection. God’s established way is that such last-minute belief does not avert the consequence, and those who persisted in disbelief are left with true loss.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Ḥā Mīm.
interpretation: The opening letters Ḥā Mīm are among the disconnected letters whose precise meaning is known to Allah; their appearance at the start of the sūrah invites reflection on the Qur’an’s divine origin and its composition from the very letters familiar to its hearers.

translation: A revelation from the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse presents this revelation as coming from God, whose mercy encompasses His act of guiding people through His message.

translation: A Book whose verses have been made clear, an Arabic Qur’an for a people who know.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the Qur’an’s message is presented with clarity in the language its first audience understood, so those willing to learn can grasp its guidance and reflect on it.

translation: As a bearer of good news and a warner; yet most of them turn away, so they do not listen.
interpretation: The message offers hope to those who respond to God and warns those who reject it, but many turn away and refuse to heed its guidance.

translation: They say, “Our hearts are wrapped in coverings against what you call us to, our ears are deaf, and between us and you is a barrier. So act as you will; we too are acting.”
interpretation: Their words express a deliberate refusal to receive the Prophet’s message: they portray themselves as closed off from it and insist on keeping their distance, defiantly continuing on their own course.

translation: Say, “I am only a human being like you. It is revealed to me that your God is One God. So remain steadfast in devotion to Him and seek His forgiveness. And woe to those who associate others with Him.”
interpretation: The Prophet’s shared humanity does not lessen the authority of his message: his role is to convey what God reveals. Since God alone is worthy of worship, people are called to direct their lives toward Him, repent of their failings, and reject every form of associating partners with Him.

translation: Those who do not give the purifying alms and who disbelieve in the Hereafter.
interpretation: The verse links withholding the prescribed alms with rejecting the Hereafter: belief in accountability should be reflected in fulfilling one’s duties toward others, not merely affirmed in words.

translation: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds will have a reward that will never be cut off.
interpretation: The verse assures believers that the reward God grants for sincere faith and righteous action is enduring and will not be withheld or diminished.

translation: Say, “Do you truly disbelieve in the One who created the earth in two days, and set up rivals alongside Him? That is the Lord of all worlds.”
interpretation: The verse rebukes those who deny God while associating other powers with Him: the One who brought the earth into being alone is the Lord of all creation, so treating anything as His equal is a contradiction of His sovereignty.

translation: And He placed upon it firmly set mountains, blessed it, and apportioned its provisions therein in four days, equally for all who seek them.
interpretation: The verse portrays the earth’s stability, fertility, and provision as deliberately ordered by God. Its resources are apportioned with wisdom to meet the needs of those who seek them; the four days refer to the stages of this ordering, not necessarily four days in addition to those mentioned earlier.

translation: Then He directed Himself toward the heaven while it was smoke, and said to it and to the earth, “Come, willingly or unwillingly.” They said, “We come willingly.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the heavens and the earth as wholly subject to God’s command as creation is brought into order. The heaven’s being “smoke” points to an unformed state, while the exchange expresses the cosmos’s complete obedience to its Creator.

translation: So He fashioned them into seven heavens in two days, and ordained for each heaven its own order. We adorned the nearest heaven with lamps and made them a protection. That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: The verse portrays the heavens as created with deliberate order: each has its appointed arrangement, while the lights of the nearest heaven serve as adornment and protection, all by the wisdom and power of God.

translation: If they turn away, say, “I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt that struck ʿĀd and Thamūd.”
interpretation: The warning makes clear that turning away from the truth is not harmless: those who persist in rejecting God’s message risk meeting the same kind of devastating punishment that befell earlier peoples.

translation: When the messengers came to them from before them and from behind them, saying, “Worship none but Allah,” they said, “Had our Lord willed, He would have sent down angels. So we disbelieve in what you have been sent with.”
interpretation: The verse portrays a people rejecting the messengers’ call to worship Allah alone by demanding a different kind of messenger—angels—as though their own expectation could determine how God should guide them. Their appeal to God’s power becomes an excuse for refusing the guidance actually brought to them.

translation: As for ʿĀd, they arrogantly behaved in the land without right and said, “Who is stronger than us?” Did they not see that God, who created them, is stronger than they are? Yet they persistently rejected Our signs.
interpretation: Their physical power led them to imagine that no one could overcome them. The verse exposes the folly of that pride: the One who gave them their strength has power far beyond theirs, and their refusal to heed His signs left them without the humility or insight to recognize it.

translation: So We sent against them a furious, bitterly cold wind during ill-fated days, so that We might make them taste the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world. But the punishment of the Hereafter is more disgraceful, and they will have no help.
interpretation: The verse presents the people’s worldly humiliation as a consequence of their defiance, while warning that worldly punishment is not the final measure of accountability. In the Hereafter, their disgrace will be greater, and no one will be able to rescue them.

translation: As for Thamud, We showed them the way, but they preferred blindness to guidance. So the thunderbolt of humiliating punishment seized them because of what they used to do.
interpretation: Their punishment came after guidance had been made clear: they knowingly turned away from it. The verse thus emphasizes that their ruin was the consequence of their own choices and deeds.

translation: And We saved those who believed and were mindful of God.
interpretation: The verse teaches that faith expressed through God-consciousness is a means of divine protection and deliverance.

translation: And [mention] the Day when the enemies of Allah are gathered toward the Fire, where they will be held in ranks.
interpretation: The verse portrays the certainty and order of divine judgment: those who opposed God will be brought together with no power to escape or evade their reckoning.

translation: When they reach it, their hearing, their sight, and their skins will testify against them concerning what they used to do.
interpretation: The verse portrays a judgment in which people cannot deny their deeds: even the faculties through which they acted and perceived become witnesses to how they used them. It warns that a person’s actions are fully known and that accountability cannot be escaped by denial.

translation: They will say to their skins, “Why did you testify against us?” They will reply, “Allah, who gives speech to all things, made us speak. He created you the first time, and to Him you will be returned.”
interpretation: The verse shows that no deed can ultimately be hidden: on the Day of Judgment, even parts of a person’s own body will bear witness by God’s power. His ability to make them speak is also a reminder that the One who created people in the first place can raise them and return them to account.

translation: You did not try to conceal yourselves from your hearing, your eyes, or your skins lest they testify against you. Rather, you thought that Allah did not know much of what you did.
interpretation: The verse exposes the false sense of security that comes from imagining some actions escape God’s knowledge. A person may fail to guard against accountability precisely because they underestimate how completely their deeds are known; no concealment can make them unknown to God.

translation: That was the assumption you held about your Lord that brought you to ruin, and so you became among the losers.
interpretation: The verse warns that mistaking God’s patience or concealment for ignorance or indifference can lead people to persist in wrongdoing until they bring ruin upon themselves. It calls for accountability before God, who knows what people do even when they imagine their actions will remain hidden.

translation: If they endure patiently, the Fire will be their abode; and if they seek to regain favor, they will not be among those whose favor is accepted.
interpretation: Once the judgment has been passed, neither bearing the punishment patiently nor pleading to be reconciled will change their fate; the chance to turn back has passed.

translation: And We assigned to them companions who made attractive to them what lay before them and what lay behind them. So the decree became due against them, as it had against communities before them of jinn and humankind. They were indeed losers.
interpretation: Their corrupt companions made wrongdoing seem appealing and reinforced their delusions about both their past and their future, until they followed the same path of rejection as earlier communities and became deserving of the punishment decreed for them.

translation: Those who disbelieved said, “Do not listen to this Qur’an, and make noise while it is being recited, so that you may prevail.”
interpretation: The verse portrays opposition that seeks to defeat the Qur’an not by answering its message, but by preventing people from hearing and considering it. It warns against using distraction and disruption to suppress truth.

translation: We will surely make those who disbelieve taste a severe punishment, and We will surely recompense them for the worst of what they used to do.
interpretation: The emphatic wording underscores that rejecting faith and persisting in wrongdoing have certain consequences: God’s judgment is just, and people are held accountable for their deeds.

translation: That is the recompense of the enemies of Allah: the Fire. There they will have the home of everlasting abode, as recompense for their having denied Our signs.
interpretation: The verse presents their lasting punishment as a consequence of their persistent denial of God’s signs, emphasizing that rejecting the truth carries enduring accountability.

translation: Those who disbelieved will say, “Our Lord, show us those who led us astray, from among the jinn and humankind, so that we may put them beneath our feet and make them among the lowest.”
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, the disbelievers will bitterly seek to punish those who influenced them toward disbelief, but their anger will not erase their own responsibility for following the misguidance.

translation: Indeed, those who say, “Our Lord is Allah,” and then remain steadfast—the angels descend upon them, saying, “Do not fear or grieve, but rejoice in the Paradise you were promised.”
interpretation: True faith is not merely a declaration; it is remaining faithful to God through one’s choices and conduct. The angels’ reassurance is a promise that those who persevere in this faith will be met with safety and comfort, and with the fulfillment of God’s promise of Paradise.

translation: “We are your guardians in the life of this world and in the Hereafter. There you will have whatever your souls desire, and there you will have whatever you ask for.”
interpretation: The verse offers reassurance that God’s care for the faithful is not limited to worldly life: it accompanies them into the Hereafter, where their deepest hopes are fulfilled without fear or deprivation.

translation: As a welcoming provision from the All-Forgiving, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: The phrase portrays the blessings promised to the believers as generous hospitality from God, flowing from His forgiveness and mercy.

translation: And who is better in speech than one who calls to Allah, does righteous deeds, and says, “Indeed, I am among those who submit to Allah”?
interpretation: The verse teaches that calling others to Allah is most worthy when it is joined with sincere good deeds and an open, humble commitment to submission to Him. The caller’s conduct should bear witness to the message they share.

translation: Good and evil are not equal. Repel evil with what is better, and then the one between whom and you there was enmity will be like a devoted friend.
interpretation: The verse teaches that moral strength lies not in returning hostility in kind, but in answering it with a better response—one guided by patience, fairness, and kindness. Such conduct can soften resentment and open the way for reconciliation, though it does not make wrongdoing itself acceptable.

translation: None are granted this except those who are patient, and none are granted it except one of great good fortune.
interpretation: Responding to harm with what is better requires patient self-restraint; this noble quality is attained by those granted a great share of goodness.

translation: If a prompting from Satan stirs you, seek refuge in God. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: When Satan incites anger, doubt, or wrongdoing, turn to God for protection; He hears your plea and knows what is troubling you.

translation: Among His signs are the night and the day, the sun and the moon. Do not prostrate to the sun or the moon; rather, prostrate to Allah, who created them, if it is He whom you worship.
interpretation: The sun and moon may inspire awe, but their power and beauty are signs of their Creator, not grounds for worship. True devotion is directed to Allah alone, the One who brought them into being.

translation: But if they are arrogant, those who are with your Lord glorify Him night and day, and they never tire.
interpretation: Human refusal does not lessen God’s majesty or the truth of worship: the angels near to Him praise Him without ceasing, showing that devotion to God is not dependent on people’s approval.

translation: Among His signs is that you see the earth lying barren; then, when We send down water upon it, it stirs and swells. Surely the One who brings it to life will bring the dead to life. He is indeed capable of all things.
interpretation: The renewal of barren land after rain is a sign that resurrection is possible: the One who restores life to the earth can restore life to the dead, for nothing is beyond His power.

translation: Indeed, those who distort Our signs are not hidden from Us. Is one who is cast into the Fire better, or one who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection? Do whatever you will; surely He sees all that you do.
interpretation: The verse warns that no attempt to evade or distort God’s revelations escapes His knowledge. Its question contrasts the terrible end of those who reject the truth with the safety of those who meet God faithfully; “Do whatever you will” is a warning, not permission, since every deed is seen and carries its consequence.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieved in the Reminder when it came to them—and indeed, it is a mighty Book.
interpretation: The Qur’an is a powerful and inviolable revelation; rejecting it does not diminish its truth or authority.

translation: Falsehood cannot come to it from before it or from behind it; it is a revelation from the All-Wise, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: The Qur’an is safeguarded from falsehood: nothing can invalidate it, undermine its truth, or corrupt its message. Its origin is the One whose perfect wisdom and praiseworthiness guarantee its truth.

translation: Nothing is said to you except what was said to the messengers before you. Surely your Lord is the possessor of forgiveness and of painful punishment.
interpretation: The Prophet is reassured that the hostility and objections he faces are part of the trials endured by earlier messengers. The verse also holds out two possible outcomes: God’s forgiveness for those who turn back to Him, and painful punishment for those who persist in rejection.

translation: Had We made it a Qur’an in a foreign language, they would have said, “Why have its verses not been made clear? What—a foreign-language scripture and an Arab messenger?” Say, “For those who believe, it is guidance and healing.” But those who do not believe have deafness in their ears, and it is blindness to them. They are being called from a distant place.
interpretation: The objection reveals that the rejecters’ resistance is not really about the Qur’an’s language: had it been in another language, they would have found that objection too. The Qur’an’s guidance and healing are received by those willing to listen, while those who turn away are likened to people too deaf and far off to grasp a call directed to them.

translation: We certainly gave Moses the Scripture, but people differed about it. Had a decree not already gone forth from your Lord, judgment would have been passed between them. They are indeed in deeply troubling doubt about it.
interpretation: The verse points to a recurring response to revelation: people disagree over it, while God allows that disagreement to continue until the time set by His prior decree. Those who remain divided are not acting from settled knowledge, but from uncertainty about the revelation.

translation: Whoever does good, does so for their own benefit; and whoever does evil, does so to their own detriment. Your Lord is never unjust to His servants.
interpretation: A person’s choices ultimately affect their own standing: good deeds bring benefit to the one who performs them, while wrongdoing brings harm upon its doer. God’s judgment is perfectly just, and He wrongs no one.

translation: To Him is referred the knowledge of the Hour. No fruit emerges from its coverings, no female conceives, and no female gives birth except with His knowledge. And on the Day He calls to them, “Where are My partners?” they will say, “We declare to You: none of us bears witness.”
interpretation: The verse affirms that God alone knows every hidden detail, from the coming of the Hour to the smallest events in creation. When those who claimed partners for Him are confronted on the Day of Judgment, they will have no testimony to support those claims.

translation: Those they used to call upon before had failed them, and they realized that they had no escape.
interpretation: When the truth of the Hereafter becomes undeniable, those they relied on besides God cannot help them, and they recognize that there is nowhere to flee from accountability.

translation: Man never tires of praying for good, but when hardship touches him, he becomes utterly despairing and hopeless.
interpretation: The verse points to a human weakness: people may keep seeking blessings, yet let a trial make them lose hope too quickly. It urges a person not to treat present hardship as the end of what is possible, but to remain patient and hopeful in God’s mercy.

translation: If We let him taste mercy from Us after hardship has touched him, he will surely say, “This is mine, and I do not think the Hour will come. And if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely have the best with Him.” We will surely inform those who disbelieved of what they did, and make them taste a severe punishment.
interpretation: The verse exposes the delusion of treating worldly ease as proof of personal entitlement—and even as a guarantee of God’s favor in the Hereafter. True hope in God cannot be founded on prosperity alone; it must be joined to humility and accountability for one’s deeds.

translation: When We bestow favor upon a person, he turns away and withdraws; but when hardship touches him, he pours out lengthy supplication.
interpretation: The verse points to a human weakness: comfort can lead a person to become self-reliant and heedless of God, while hardship makes him urgently turn back in prayer. It warns against remembering God only in distress and calls for gratitude and devotion in times of ease as well.

translation: Say, “Have you considered: if it is from Allah and you disbelieve in it, who could be more astray than one who is in profound opposition?”
interpretation: The verse confronts those who reject the revelation with the possibility that it truly comes from Allah: if so, their rejection places them in the deepest error. Its rhetorical question emphasizes that stubborn opposition to divine truth is not merely a difference of opinion, but a grave departure from guidance.

translation: We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth. Is it not enough that your Lord is witness over all things?
interpretation: The signs of God in the world and in human life progressively make the truth unmistakable. Yet their recognition does not depend solely on what people discover: God’s all-encompassing knowledge and witness is itself sufficient proof of the truth.

translation: Indeed, they are in doubt about meeting their Lord. Indeed, He encompasses all things.
interpretation: Their doubt cannot place them beyond God’s reach: He fully encompasses all things, including their deeds, and they will meet Him for judgment.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Ḥā Mīm.
interpretation: The opening invokes Allah’s mercy before presenting the mysterious letters “Ḥā Mīm,” whose ultimate meaning is known to Allah and which mark the beginning of a Qur’anic chapter.

translation: ʿAyn, Sīn, Qāf.
interpretation: These are among the Qur’an’s disjointed letters; their intended meaning is known to God.

translation: Thus Allah, the Almighty, the Wise, reveals to you and to those who came before you.
interpretation: The revelation given to the Prophet is part of the same divine guidance sent to earlier messengers: it comes from Allah, whose might guarantees its authority and whose wisdom shapes its purpose.

translation: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and He is the Most High, the Most Great.
interpretation: All creation is under God’s ownership and authority; His exaltedness and greatness are beyond comparison with anything He has made.

translation: The heavens are nearly splitting apart above them, while the angels glorify their Lord with praise and seek forgiveness for those on earth. Indeed, Allah is the All-Forgiving, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse evokes the overwhelming majesty of Allah: even the heavens seem on the verge of splitting before Him. At the same time, the angels continually glorify Him and ask His forgiveness for those on earth, reflecting both His greatness and the breadth of His mercy.

translation: As for those who take protectors besides Him, Allah watches over them, and you are not responsible for their affairs.
interpretation: Those who turn to others as protectors apart from God remain under His watch and judgment. The Prophet’s role is to convey the message, not to compel them or answer for their choices.

translation: Thus We have revealed to you an Arabic Qur’an, so that you may warn the Mother of Cities and those around it, and warn of the Day of Gathering, about which there is no doubt: one group will be in Paradise and another in the Blaze.
interpretation: The verse presents the Qur’an’s Arabic revelation as a clear warning first addressed to Mecca and its surrounding people, while its message points beyond them to the certain reckoning of all humanity. The mention of the two final destinies underscores that people’s response to divine guidance has lasting consequences.

translation: Had Allah willed, He could have made them one community. But He admits whom He wills into His mercy, and the wrongdoers will have no protector or helper.
interpretation: Humanity’s differing beliefs are not beyond God’s power to change; rather, He grants His mercy as He wills. Those who persist in wrongdoing cannot rely on any guardian or helper to shield them from its consequences.

translation: Or have they taken protectors besides Him? Allah alone is the Protector; He gives life to the dead, and He has power over all things.
interpretation: The verse challenges the reliance placed on anything besides God: no created being can offer the ultimate protection or authority that belongs to Him. His power to restore the dead to life shows that nothing lies beyond His command.

translation: Whatever you differ about, its judgment belongs to Allah. That is Allah, my Lord; upon Him I rely, and to Him I turn.
interpretation: When people disagree, the final authority for judging between them is Allah, whose guidance provides the measure by which disputes are resolved. The verse expresses trust in His judgment and a continual return to Him for guidance and forgiveness.

translation: Originator of the heavens and the earth, He has made for you spouses from among yourselves, and pairs among the livestock. By this He multiplies you. Nothing is like Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.
interpretation: The order of pairing and multiplication points to God’s creative power, while the verse makes clear that no created likeness can be used to imagine Him. His hearing and sight are real, yet unlike those of His creation.

translation: To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth. He enlarges provision for whom He wills and restricts it. Surely He has knowledge of all things.
interpretation: The verse presents worldly provision as entirely under God’s authority: its abundance or limitation is not beyond His knowledge or control. People should therefore neither mistake wealth for proof of greater worth nor despair when provision is constrained, but trust that God’s giving and withholding occur with full knowledge.

translation: He has prescribed for you of the religion what He enjoined upon Noah, and what We have revealed to you, and what We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses, and Jesus: uphold the religion and do not become divided over it. What you call them to is hard for the polytheists. Allah chooses for Himself whom He wills, and guides to Himself whoever turns back to Him.
interpretation: The verse presents the prophets as united in the essential call to worship God and remain faithful to His guidance. Its command to uphold the religion calls for steadfastness in that shared truth, not division driven by competing loyalties or desires. Though this call may be difficult for those resistant to it, guidance ultimately belongs to God, who guides those who sincerely turn toward Him.

translation: They did not divide among themselves until after knowledge had come to them, out of rivalry with one another. Had it not been for a decree already issued by your Lord, deferred until an appointed time, judgment would have been made between them. Those who inherited the Scripture after them are indeed in troubling doubt about it.
interpretation: Their disagreement arose not because guidance was unavailable, but because rivalry and self-interest prevailed after its truth had become clear. God’s decree allows judgment to be deferred until its appointed time; meanwhile, later heirs of revelation remain unsettled, burdened by doubt about what they have received.

translation: So call to this, and remain steadfast as you have been commanded. Do not follow their desires, but say, “I believe in what Allah has sent down of the Book, and I have been commanded to act justly among you. Allah is our Lord and your Lord. We are accountable for our deeds, and you for yours. There is no dispute between us and you. Allah will gather us together, and to Him is the final return.”
interpretation: The verse calls the Prophet to hold firmly to the divine guidance and to uphold justice without bending the message to suit other people’s desires. It also teaches that disagreements should not lead to injustice or coercion: each person is accountable for their own deeds, and ultimate judgment belongs to Allah, before whom all will return.

translation: Those who dispute about Allah after people have responded to Him—their argument is futile before their Lord. Upon them is wrath, and theirs is a severe punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns against resisting God’s truth after it has been made clear and people have accepted it: such disputation cannot weaken the truth, and those who persist in it are answerable to God.

translation: Allah is the One who sent down the Book in truth, and the balance. And what can make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near.
interpretation: The revelation provides a true standard by which people may distinguish right from wrong and uphold justice. Since the Hour may be near, people should not delay responding to that guidance or preparing to be held accountable.

translation: Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it, while those who believe are apprehensive of it and know that it is the truth. Surely, those who dispute the Hour are in far-reaching error.
interpretation: The verse contrasts two responses to the Day of Judgment: disbelievers challengeingly demand its arrival, whereas believers take its reality seriously, feeling awe at the accountability it brings. To dispute the Hour is to lose one’s way by refusing to recognize a truth that should shape how one lives.

translation: Allah is gracious to His servants; He provides for whom He wills. He is the All-Strong, the Almighty.
interpretation: Allah’s care reaches His servants with subtle gentleness, even in ways they may not immediately perceive. His provision is given according to His wisdom, while His perfect power and authority ensure that nothing can prevent what He wills.

translation: Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter, We increase his harvest for him; and whoever desires the harvest of this world, We grant him some of it, but he will have no share in the Hereafter.
interpretation: The verse presents a person’s ultimate aim as shaping what their efforts yield: those who work seeking God’s reward are granted an increase in the lasting fruit of their deeds, while those whose aim is confined to worldly gain may receive some of what they seek, but that gain does not become a share in the Hereafter.

translation: Or do they have partners who have prescribed for them in religion that which Allah has not permitted? Had it not been for the decree of judgment, the matter between them would already have been decided. Surely the wrongdoers will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse rejects the idea that anyone may invent religious teachings or obligations and attribute them to God without His authorization. The final judgment is deferred until its appointed time, but that delay does not excuse those who do so; they remain accountable for their wrongdoing.

translation: You will see the wrongdoers fearful of what they have earned, and it will surely befall them. But those who believe and do righteous deeds will be in the flowering meadows of the Gardens. They will have whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the great bounty.
interpretation: The verse contrasts the inescapable consequences of wrongdoing with the generous reward God grants to the faithful. It teaches that a person’s deeds matter, while also emphasizing that the joy of the righteous is a gift from their Lord, far beyond mere deliverance from punishment.

translation: That is the good news Allah gives to His servants who believe and do righteous deeds. Say, “I ask you for no reward for it, except affection for my close kin.” Whoever earns a good deed, We will increase its goodness for him. Surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Appreciative.
interpretation: The Prophet’s call is not a means of seeking worldly gain; the affection requested is a bond of kinship and goodwill, not a payment. The verse also teaches that sincere good deeds are met with God’s generosity: He magnifies their reward, forgives shortcomings, and accepts even the smallest good with appreciation.

translation: Or do they say, “He has fabricated a lie against Allah”? If Allah willed, He could seal your heart. But Allah effaces falsehood and establishes the truth by His words. He indeed knows what lies within hearts.
interpretation: The verse answers the accusation that the Prophet invented revelation: Allah’s power over his heart and His decisive removal of falsehood show that revelation is not a fabrication, while His knowledge of what people conceal makes their accusations fully known to Him.

translation: He is the One who accepts repentance from His servants, pardons misdeeds, and knows what you do.
interpretation: God’s mercy is open to those who sincerely turn back to Him: He accepts their repentance and may pardon their wrongs. His complete knowledge of their actions also means that repentance must be genuine; nothing is hidden from Him.

translation: He responds to those who believe and do righteous deeds, and grants them even more of His bounty; but the disbelievers will have a severe punishment.
interpretation: God graciously answers the faithful who act righteously, giving them beyond what they ask or earn. This generosity contrasts with the severe consequence awaiting those who reject faith.

translation: If Allah were to make provision abundant for His servants, they would surely become arrogant and transgress on earth. But He sends it down in the measure He wills. Surely He is All-Aware, All-Seeing of His servants.
interpretation: The verse teaches that wealth and abundance are not always what is best for people: unchecked prosperity can lead them to arrogance and wrongdoing. Allah apportions provision with wisdom, fully knowing what His servants can bear and what is good for them.

translation: And it is He who sends down the rain after they have despaired and spreads His mercy. He is the Protector, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: The verse directs people to recognize that relief can come from God even after hope seems lost. The rain is a sign of His mercy at work, while His care and worthiness of praise remain constant.

translation: And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the creatures He has spread throughout them. And He is able to gather them whenever He wills.
interpretation: The vastness of the heavens and earth and the life spread throughout them point to God’s boundless power. The One who created and sustains these creatures can gather them whenever He wills, including for the final resurrection.

translation: Whatever affliction befalls you is because of what your hands have earned, and He pardons much.
interpretation: The verse invites moral reflection: human actions can bring harmful consequences, yet God’s mercy is greater than what people deserve, for He overlooks many of their wrongs.

translation: You cannot escape [God] on earth, and you have no protector or helper besides Allah.
interpretation: No matter where people go, they cannot evade Allah’s power or judgment; no one apart from Him can ultimately protect or help them.

translation: And among His signs are the ships sailing through the sea, like mountains.
interpretation: The immense ships moving across the sea are a sign of God’s power and wisdom: He has made the waters and the means of navigation serve human life, despite the ships’ great size and the sea’s force.

translation: If He wills, He stills the wind, and they remain motionless upon its surface. Surely in that are signs for everyone who is patient and grateful.
interpretation: The verse points to how entirely human travel and security depend on God’s will: the same winds that carry ships can be stilled, leaving them helpless on the sea. Those who endure hardship with patience and recognize blessings with gratitude are especially able to see this dependence as a sign of God’s power and care.

translation: Or He may cause them to perish for what they have earned, while pardoning much.
interpretation: The phrase teaches that hardship may come as a consequence of people’s deeds, yet God does not punish for every wrong: His forbearance and forgiveness extend far beyond what people deserve.

translation: And those who dispute Our signs will know that they have no escape.
interpretation: Those who stubbornly contest God’s signs will ultimately discover that no refuge can shield them from His judgment.

translation: Whatever you have been given is only a temporary enjoyment of worldly life; what is with Allah is better and more lasting for those who believe and place their trust in their Lord.
interpretation: The verse teaches that worldly blessings, however valuable, are temporary, while what Allah has prepared is lasting. Believers therefore should not make worldly gain their ultimate aim, but trust in their Lord and seek what endures with Him.

translation: And those who avoid grave sins and indecent acts, and when they are angry, they forgive.
interpretation: True faith is shown not only by avoiding serious wrongdoing, but also by mastering anger: rather than letting it turn into harm or lasting resentment, a believer chooses forgiveness.

translation: And those who respond to their Lord, establish prayer, conduct their affairs through consultation among themselves, and spend from what We have provided for them.
interpretation: The verse portrays faith as shaping both personal devotion and communal life: believers turn to God, yet do not let authority become self-will. They seek one another’s counsel and share their provision, recognizing that good judgment and wealth are trusts to be exercised with humility and care.

translation: And those who, when wronged, stand up for themselves.
interpretation: The verse affirms that resisting injustice and seeking one’s rights is legitimate; the oppressed need not submit passively, while their response should remain just and not become a new act of wrongdoing.

translation: The recompense for a wrong is a wrong equal to it. But whoever pardons and makes things right will have their reward with God. He does not love the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse permits a response proportionate to the harm suffered, but presents forgiveness joined with genuine reconciliation as a higher path, rewarded by God. It also warns that retaliation must not become injustice or exceed its proper bounds.

translation: Whoever defends themselves after being wronged—there is no blame upon them.
interpretation: The verse affirms that a wronged person may defend themselves or seek rightful redress without being blameworthy, so long as they do not exceed just limits.

translation: Blame is only upon those who wrong people and transgress in the land without right; for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse places moral responsibility on those who initiate injustice and abuse their power, not on those who respond lawfully to being wronged. It warns that oppression and unjust aggression carry grave accountability before God.

translation: But whoever is patient and forgives—indeed, that is among the matters requiring firm resolve.
interpretation: Forgiving when one has been wronged is not weakness; it takes steadfastness and deliberate strength to restrain retaliation and choose pardon.

translation: And whoever Allah leaves to stray will have no protector after Him. And you will see the wrongdoers, when they see the punishment, saying, “Is there any way to return?”
interpretation: The verse warns that no one can protect a person from the consequences of being left to their chosen misguidance. When the wrongdoers finally witness the punishment, they will desperately wish to return to earthly life and act differently, but that opportunity will have passed.

translation: And you will see them exposed to it, humbled by disgrace, looking furtively from the corner of their eyes. Those who believed will say, “Indeed, the losers are those who lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection.” Surely, the wrongdoers will be in lasting punishment.
interpretation: The verse portrays the final abasement of those who did wrong: their fearful, furtive gaze stands in stark contrast to the certainty of the believers’ judgment. Their loss is profound—not merely punishment, but the ruin of their own souls and the bonds they hoped to preserve—and their wrongdoing leads to punishment without end.

translation: They had no protectors to help them apart from Allah. And whoever Allah leaves astray has no way forward.
interpretation: No ally can secure someone against Allah’s judgment or replace the guidance He grants; when a person is left without that guidance, no path to salvation remains.

translation: Respond to your Lord before a Day comes from Allah that cannot be turned back. On that Day you will have no refuge, nor any way to deny your deeds.
interpretation: The verse urges people to answer God’s call while they still have the chance to repent and obey. When the Day of Judgment arrives, it cannot be delayed or escaped, and no one will be able to disavow what they have done.

translation: But if they turn away, We have not sent you as a guardian over them. Your duty is only to convey the message. When We let a person taste mercy from Us, they rejoice in it; but when hardship befalls them because of what their own hands have done, the human being is indeed ungrateful.
interpretation: The verse reassures the Messenger that he is responsible for conveying God’s message, not for forcing people to accept it. It also points to a human failing: people may rejoice in blessings yet respond to hardship—especially hardship brought about by their own actions—with ingratitude rather than reflection and repentance.

translation: To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He creates whatever He wills. He grants daughters to whom He wills, and He grants sons to whom He wills.
interpretation: The verse teaches that children are gifts entrusted by God, not outcomes people can command. Their being daughters or sons lies within His wisdom, so neither should be treated as a measure of a parent’s worth or as grounds for preferring one child over another.

translation: Or He gives them both males and females, and makes whom He wills barren. Indeed, He is All-Knowing, All-Powerful.
interpretation: The verse teaches that having children, and the form that family life takes, lies within God’s knowledge and power; no one’s circumstances fall outside His wisdom or control.

translation: It is not for any human that God should speak to him except by revelation, or from behind a veil, or by sending a messenger who, by His permission, conveys what He wills. Indeed, He is Most High, All-Wise.
interpretation: The verse teaches that God’s communication with human beings occurs only in ways He chooses, without resembling ordinary human speech or compromising His transcendence. Each way is under His authority and wisdom.

translation: And thus We revealed to you a spirit by Our command. You did not know what the Book was or what faith was, but We made it a light by which We guide whom We will among Our servants. And indeed, you guide to a straight path.
interpretation: The revelation is described as a life-giving light: knowledge of the Book and the way of faith comes through God’s gift, not through the Prophet’s prior knowledge. By conveying this revelation, the Prophet guides people to the straight path by God’s permission.

translation: The path of Allah, to whom belongs all that is in the heavens and the earth. Surely, to Allah all matters return.
interpretation: Allah’s path is the way of true guidance because everything belongs to Him and every affair ultimately returns to Him. This calls people to follow His guidance and entrust their affairs to Him, knowing that He alone has final authority.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Ḥā Mīm.
interpretation: The opening calls upon Allah through His mercy, then begins with the mysterious letters Ḥā Mīm. Their precise meaning is known to Allah; their presence also draws attention to the Qur’an’s use of familiar Arabic letters in a revelation whose full depth is beyond human knowledge.

translation: By the clear Book.
interpretation: This oath draws attention to the Qur’an as a clear, illuminating revelation that makes the truth and guidance plain.

translation: Indeed, We have made it an Arabic Qur’an so that you may understand.
interpretation: The Qur’an was revealed in the language its first audience understood, making its guidance clear and accessible to them and inviting them to reflect on its message.

translation: And indeed, it is in the Mother of the Book with Us—exalted and full of wisdom.
interpretation: The Qur’an has its source with God in the heavenly Mother of the Book; its lofty standing and perfect wisdom are therefore beyond doubt.

translation: Shall We then turn the Reminder away from you, disregarding you, because you are a people who transgress?
interpretation: The rhetorical question rebukes the assumption that persistent wrongdoing would cause God to withhold His reminder. Rather, the warning continues as a mercy and a call to return, even when people repeatedly exceed the bounds.

translation: And how many a prophet We sent among the peoples of old!
interpretation: The verse points to the abundance of divine guidance throughout history, reminding its audience that revelation is not new and that earlier peoples were also given prophets. It invites reflection on how people respond to that guidance.

translation: Whenever a prophet came to them, they mocked him.
interpretation: The verse highlights a recurring pattern of arrogance: instead of considering the prophets’ message, these people treated them with scorn, revealing their resistance to guidance.

translation: So We destroyed those who were mightier than them, and the example of the peoples of old has already passed.
interpretation: The verse warns that worldly strength cannot protect those who persist in rejecting God: peoples greater in power have already faced destruction, and their fate stands as a lesson for those who follow.

translation: And if you ask them, “Who created the heavens and the earth?” they will surely say, “The Almighty, the All-Knowing created them.”
interpretation: Their own acknowledgment that God alone created the heavens and the earth exposes the inconsistency of associating others with Him in worship: the One who possesses absolute power and knowledge is the only one worthy of worship.

translation: He is the One who made the earth a resting place for you and made paths through it, so that you may find your way.
interpretation: The verse draws attention to the earth as a place made suitable for human life, with routes that let people travel through it. These provisions invite people to recognize the wisdom and care behind creation.

translation: And He is the One who sent down water from the sky in due measure, then We revived with it a dead land. In the same way, you will be brought forth.
interpretation: The revival of lifeless land through rain is a sign that God can likewise resurrect people after death; the measured provision of water also reflects His wisdom and control.

translation: And He is the One who created all kinds in pairs, and made for you ships and livestock to ride.
interpretation: The verse directs people to see the order of creation and the means of travel as gifts made available by God. Their usefulness is not merely a human achievement; it invites recognition of the Creator’s generosity and gratitude for what has been placed at their service.

translation: So that you may settle upon their backs, then remember your Lord’s blessing when you have settled upon them, and say, “Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us; we could never have brought it under our control ourselves.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that when people benefit from transport and other means placed at their disposal, they should recognize that such power is not theirs alone. They are called to respond with humility and gratitude, acknowledging God as the one who made these means usable for them.

translation: And indeed, to our Lord we will surely return.
interpretation: This is a declaration that every journey—and ultimately all of life—ends in returning to God, where people will answer for how they lived.

translation: And they assign to Him a portion of His servants. Indeed, man is clearly ungrateful.
interpretation: The verse condemns attributing offspring or divine kinship to God: it falsely makes some of His created servants a part of Him, despite His absolute independence and oneness. Such a claim is a grave expression of ingratitude and denial of the truth.

translation: Or has He taken daughters from among what He creates, while favoring you with sons?
interpretation: This rhetorical question exposes the contradiction in claiming that God has offspring—especially daughters—while regarding sons as preferable for oneself. It rejects such human judgments about God, who is exalted above having any offspring.

translation: When one of them is given the news of what he has assigned to the Most Merciful as a likeness, his face darkens, and he is filled with suppressed anguish.
interpretation: The verse exposes the contradiction of those who attributed daughters to God while regarding the birth of a daughter to themselves as shameful. Their reaction reveals both their contempt for what they claimed about God and the injustice of their own values; God is far above the attributes they ascribe to Him.

translation: Or one who is brought up amid adornment and is not clear in a dispute?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical challenge to those who assigned daughters to God while regarding them as inferior. The verse exposes the inconsistency of projecting their own judgments and social assumptions onto God: no offspring, male or female, can be attributed to Him.

translation: They have made the angels, who are servants of the Most Merciful, females. Did they witness their creation? Their testimony will be recorded, and they will be questioned.
interpretation: The verse challenges the claim that angels are female: those who make this assertion have no knowledge or firsthand witness of the angels’ creation. It warns that speaking about the unseen without evidence is accountable before God.

translation: And they say, “If the Most Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped them.” They have no knowledge of this; they do nothing but make conjectures.
interpretation: They use God’s will to excuse their worship of others, but they have no knowledge that God approves of it. The verse rejects this as mere speculation: divine power does not make their choice a justified act or excuse them from responsibility.

translation: Or have We given them a Book before it, to which they are holding fast?
interpretation: The question challenges those making this claim to produce a genuine scriptural authority for it: no earlier revelation has been given to them that they can rightly invoke as its basis.

translation: Rather, they say, “We found our forefathers following a way, and we are guided by their footsteps.”
interpretation: The verse challenges the assumption that an inherited tradition must be true simply because one’s ancestors followed it. Guidance requires sound grounds, not merely imitation of those who came before.

translation: Thus, We never sent a warner before you to any town without its affluent people saying, “We found our forefathers following a way, and we are following in their footsteps.”
interpretation: The verse exposes how people—especially those comfortable with the established order—may reject a divine warning by appealing to inherited customs rather than examining whether they are true. Following one’s forebears is not, by itself, proof that a belief is right.

translation: He said, “Even if I bring you guidance better than what you found your fathers following?” They replied, “We reject what you have been sent with.”
interpretation: The verse exposes the stubbornness of those who treat inherited custom as more authoritative than truth: even when offered clearer and better guidance, they refuse it simply because it challenges what they received from their forefathers.

translation: So We took retribution upon them. See, then, what was the end of those who denied.
interpretation: The verse calls the listener to reflect on the fate of those who persistently reject God’s truth: their power cannot shield them from divine justice, and their downfall serves as a warning to those who follow their path.

translation: And when Abraham said to his father and his people, “I am truly free of what you worship,”
interpretation: Abraham declares that he rejects the idols and false objects of worship his people have adopted, making clear that his devotion belongs to God alone.

translation: Except for the One who created me; He will surely guide me.
interpretation: The speaker turns away from all that is worshipped besides God and entrusts himself to his Creator, confident that the One who brought him into being will guide him to what is true.

translation: And he made it an enduring word among his descendants, so that they might return.
interpretation: Abraham’s declaration of devotion to the one Creator was kept alive among his descendants as a lasting reminder, calling those who turned away to return to worshipping God alone.

translation: Rather, I allowed these people and their forefathers to enjoy life until the truth came to them, along with a clear messenger.
interpretation: Their long enjoyment of worldly life was a respite, not approval of their beliefs. When the truth arrived through a clear messenger, they could no longer rely on their forefathers’ ways as an excuse for turning away.

translation: When the truth came to them, they said, “This is magic, and we reject it.”
interpretation: Their response shows a refusal to consider the truth on its merits: they dismiss it as magic and openly reject it rather than engage with its message.

translation: And they say, “Why was this Qur’an not sent down to a great man from one of the two cities?”
interpretation: They object to the Prophet’s message because he does not belong to the worldly elite they consider worthy of leadership. The verse exposes their mistaken assumption that revelation is granted according to social rank; the choice of a messenger belongs to God, not to human status or prestige.

translation: Is it they who distribute the mercy of your Lord? We have apportioned among them their livelihood in the life of this world, and raised some of them above others in rank, so that some may employ others in service. Yet the mercy of your Lord is better than what they accumulate.
interpretation: No one can judge or allocate God’s mercy by human standards of wealth and status. Differences in worldly provision serve practical purposes in human life; they are not proof that one person is more worthy before God than another. What God grants of His mercy is far more valuable than any material wealth people gather.

translation: Were it not that people might become one community [in disbelief], We would have made for those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful silver roofs for their houses, and stairways by which they could ascend.
interpretation: The verse teaches that abundant worldly wealth is not proof of God’s favor or of a person’s worth. God withholds such lavishness because it could tempt people to unite in disbelief; material splendor is therefore of little consequence compared with faith.

translation: And for their houses [We would have provided] doors and couches upon which they recline.
interpretation: Doors and couches represent the comforts and luxuries of worldly life; possessing them is not, by itself, a sign of lasting honor or nearness to God.

translation: And (We would have given them) gold ornaments. Yet all of that is only the enjoyment of worldly life, while the Hereafter with your Lord is for the God-conscious.
interpretation: Material abundance and splendor are not signs of lasting honor or divine favor; they are temporary. What truly matters is God-consciousness, whose reward endures in the Hereafter.

translation: Whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We assign to him a devil, who becomes his companion.
interpretation: Turning away from remembrance of God leaves a person open to a persistent satanic influence that accompanies and draws them further from guidance.

translation: Indeed, they surely turn them away from the path, while they think they are rightly guided.
interpretation: The verse warns that a person can be led away from God’s guidance while remaining convinced they are on the right course. Such confidence does not make a mistaken path true; it can instead deepen the misguidance by preventing recognition of it.

translation: Until, when he comes to Us, he says, “If only there were between me and you the distance between the two easts! What a wretched companion!”
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, the one misled by his devilish companion will recognize the harm that companion caused and wish they had been separated by the greatest possible distance. But that regret will come too late.

translation: And it will not benefit you today, because you did wrong, that you share in the punishment.
interpretation: Sharing the punishment with others cannot ease it or undo the consequences of wrongdoing; each person remains accountable for their own choices.

translation: Can you then make the deaf hear, or guide the blind and those who are in clear error?
interpretation: The verse teaches that a messenger can convey the truth, but cannot make people accept it when they have closed themselves off from guidance. “Deaf” and “blind” describe spiritual unwillingness to hear and recognize the truth, not physical disability.

translation: If We take you away, then surely We will exact retribution from them.
interpretation: The Prophet’s departure would not shield his opponents from accountability: God’s justice does not depend on the Prophet remaining among them, and their rejection will be answered in due course.

translation: Or We may show you what We have promised them; surely We have full power over them.
interpretation: God reassures the Prophet that the promised outcome will certainly come to pass: He may witness it himself, but whether or not he does, those addressed cannot escape God’s power.

translation: So hold firmly to what has been revealed to you; indeed, you are on a straight path.
interpretation: Remain steadfast in the revelation and let it guide your choices, for it is the sure path to truth and God’s approval.

translation: Indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people, and you will be questioned.
interpretation: The Qur’an is both an honor and a reminder for the Prophet and his people; they will be held accountable for how they receive and respond to its guidance.

translation: Ask those of Our messengers whom We sent before you: “Did We appoint gods besides the Most Merciful to be worshipped?”
interpretation: The verse underscores that the message entrusted to all prophets was the worship of God alone. Their teachings offer no basis for worshipping any deity alongside the Most Merciful.

translation: And indeed, We sent Moses with Our signs to Pharaoh and his chiefs, and he said, “I am truly a messenger of the Lord of all worlds.”
interpretation: Moses’ message derives its authority from God, not from worldly power. By declaring himself the messenger of the Lord of all worlds, he challenges Pharaoh’s claim to ultimate authority and calls him and his court to answer to a sovereignty beyond their own.

translation: But when he came to them with Our signs, they immediately laughed at them.
interpretation: Their laughter reflects their dismissive arrogance: instead of considering the signs and the truth they pointed to, they treated them with ridicule.

translation: We showed them no sign except that it was greater than its counterpart, and We seized them with punishment so that they might return.
interpretation: Each sign surpassed the one before it in force and clarity, yet they remained heedless. The punishments were meant as warnings to turn them back from their defiance and toward God.

translation: And they said, “O sorcerer, call upon your Lord for us by virtue of the covenant He has made with you. We will surely be guided.”
interpretation: In their distress, they appeal to Moses to pray for the punishment to be lifted, promising to follow guidance if their plea is answered. Their words acknowledge the standing they believe he has with God, yet the promise proves insincere when relief comes.

translation: But when We removed the punishment from them, they immediately broke their promise.
interpretation: The verse shows that a promise made under the pressure of hardship may prove insincere when relief comes; genuine faithfulness is shown by keeping one’s word even after the danger has passed.

translation: Pharaoh called out among his people, saying, “My people, does the kingdom of Egypt not belong to me, and do these rivers not flow beneath me? Do you not see?”
interpretation: Pharaoh appeals to his visible wealth and authority as though they proved his right to rule and made him worthy of obedience. The verse exposes the arrogance of measuring truth and status by worldly power, which can dazzle people without establishing genuine merit.

translation: “Or am I better than this man, who is contemptible and can scarcely express himself clearly?”
interpretation: Pharaoh arrogantly tries to discredit Moses by mocking his social standing and speech, using worldly status as a substitute for engaging with the truth of his message.

translation: Why, then, have gold bracelets not been bestowed upon him, or why have angels not come with him in attendance?
interpretation: Pharaoh derides Moses by demanding signs of worldly prestige and a grand heavenly entourage, as though true authority must appear in the forms that impress rulers and crowds. The verse exposes how arrogance can dismiss a messenger’s truth by setting up false standards of status and spectacle.

translation: So he made light of his people, and they obeyed him. Indeed, they were a defiantly disobedient people.
interpretation: Pharaoh exploited his people’s weak judgment and willingness to turn from what was right, making them easy to manipulate. Their obedience was not a sign of truth in his claims, but a consequence of their own corruption.

translation: When they provoked Our displeasure, We exacted retribution from them and drowned them all.
interpretation: The verse teaches that their persistent defiance and wrongdoing brought a decisive divine punishment; their drowning is presented as a warning about the consequences of rejecting guidance.

translation: So We made them a precedent and an example for those who came after.
interpretation: Their fate stands as a warning to later peoples: rejecting God’s truth and persisting in injustice can bring a consequence others should learn from.

translation: When the son of Mary was cited as an example, your people immediately raised an outcry over it.
interpretation: Their uproar shows how they used the example of Jesus to dispute and deflect, rather than calmly consider the point being made.

translation: And they said, “Are our gods better, or is he?” They put this to you only to argue; indeed, they are a contentious people.
interpretation: Their comparison was not a sincere search for truth but a debating tactic meant to challenge the Prophet’s message. The verse portrays their argument as polemical rather than grounded in a genuine desire to understand.

translation: He was only a servant whom We had favored and made an example for the Children of Israel.
interpretation: The verse presents Jesus as a human servant honored by God, not as divine, and as a sign through whom the Children of Israel could recognize God’s power and guidance.

translation: And if We willed, We could make angels from among you to succeed one another on earth.
interpretation: The verse affirms that God could replace humanity with angels who would inhabit and succeed one another on earth; the existence and succession of human beings are therefore matters of divine will, not necessity.

translation: And indeed, he is a sign of the Hour, so do not doubt it, and follow Me; this is a straight path.
interpretation: Jesus’ miraculous life and his return before the Hour are signs that it is approaching. The verse calls people not to doubt the coming Resurrection, but to follow God’s guidance on the straight path.

translation: And let not Satan turn you away; indeed, he is a clear enemy to you.
interpretation: Do not let Satan’s promptings divert you from the truth and obedience to God; his enmity toward you is unmistakable.

translation: And when Jesus came with clear proofs, he said, “I have come to you with wisdom and to make clear to you some of the matters about which you differ. So be mindful of Allah and obey me.”
interpretation: Jesus’ message joins divine wisdom with clarification: he was sent to resolve disagreements by guiding people back to what God had revealed. His call to be mindful of God and obey him therefore asks his people to receive that guidance in humility and faithfulness.

translation: Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is the straight path.
interpretation: The verse teaches that recognizing Allah as the Lord of all calls for worship directed to Him alone; this exclusive devotion is the straight way to follow.

translation: Then the factions differed among themselves. So woe to those who do wrong, because of the punishment of a painful day.
interpretation: The verse warns that those who distort the truth about Jesus and persist in wrongdoing will face a severe punishment on the Day of Judgment.

translation: Are they waiting for anything but the Hour to come upon them suddenly while they are unaware?
interpretation: The verse warns against postponing repentance and preparation: the Hour is certain, but its arrival is unknown, so people should not let heedlessness leave them unprepared.

translation: Close friends on that Day will be enemies to one another, except the righteous.
interpretation: The verse teaches that companionship built on wrongdoing or worldly gain will collapse on the Day of Judgment, while friendship grounded in reverence for God and obedience to Him will endure.

translation: O My servants, no fear will there be upon you today, nor will you grieve.
interpretation: God reassures His devoted servants that, by His mercy, they will be safe from the terror of that Day and free from sorrow.

translation: Those who believed in Our signs and were submissive to God.
interpretation: True faith is joined with sincere submission to God: belief in His signs should shape a person’s life through obedience and devotion.

translation: Enter Paradise, you and your spouses, rejoicing.
interpretation: The verse portrays the believers’ welcome into Paradise as a shared joy: they enter with their spouses, honored and made glad in a state of lasting delight.

translation: They will be served with plates of gold and cups; there they will have whatever their souls desire and whatever delights their eyes, and they will remain there forever.
interpretation: The verse portrays Paradise as a place of complete and lasting fulfillment: its comforts are a sign of the honor God grants its inhabitants, and their joy will never be diminished by loss or ending.

translation: And that is the Paradise you have been made to inherit because of what you used to do.
interpretation: The language of inheritance conveys that Paradise is bestowed as a lasting home, while the mention of deeds affirms that a person’s choices matter; their deeds are a means of receiving this reward, not a claim independent of God’s mercy.

translation: Therein you have abundant fruit, from which you eat.
interpretation: The verse presents the fruits of these gardens as a generous provision from God: plentiful and made available for people’s nourishment and enjoyment.

translation: Indeed, the guilty will remain forever in the punishment of Hell.
interpretation: The verse presents the fate of those who persist in wrongdoing as a grave and enduring consequence, underscoring the seriousness of moral accountability before God.

translation: It will not be eased for them, and they will be therein in despair.
interpretation: Their punishment will never let up, leaving them utterly hopeless and unable to find relief.

translation: We did not wrong them, but they themselves were the wrongdoers.
interpretation: Their suffering was not caused by any injustice from God; it came from their own wrongdoing and choices.

translation: And they will call, “O Mālik, let your Lord put an end to us.” He will say, “Indeed, you will remain.”
interpretation: The people of Hell, overwhelmed by their punishment, ask its keeper to plead for their death as a release. His reply makes clear that they will not escape through death: they will remain in that state of punishment.

translation: We have indeed brought you the truth, but most of you are averse to the truth.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that rejection does not arise from the truth being absent or unclear; rather, many resist accepting it. It warns that aversion can prevent people from responding to guidance even when it has been brought to them.

translation: Or have they devised a scheme? Then We too are carrying out Our decree.
interpretation: This warns that any scheme devised against God’s truth cannot escape His power: He will decisively bring about what He wills and thwart their plans.

translation: Or do they think that We do not hear their secrets and private conversations? Indeed, Our messengers are with them, recording.
interpretation: The verse warns that no hidden scheme or whispered conversation escapes God’s knowledge. The recording angels accompany people and preserve their deeds, so they should not imagine their private words are beyond accountability.

translation: Say, “If the Most Compassionate had a son, I would be the first of the worshippers.”
interpretation: This is a rhetorical conditional that rejects the claim that God has a son: the Prophet would be first to acknowledge and worship such a son if that were true, but the premise is false. God is exalted above having offspring.

translation: Glory be to the Lord of the heavens and the earth, the Lord of the Throne, far above what they describe.
interpretation: The verse declares God utterly exalted above every false attribute or claim people ascribe to Him; His lordship over all creation and the Throne affirms His incomparable sovereignty and majesty.

translation: So leave them to indulge in idle talk and play until they meet the Day they have been promised.
interpretation: Their heedlessness is not escape from accountability: they are being granted time, but their distractions will end when the promised Day arrives.

translation: And He is the God in heaven and the God on earth; and He is the All-Wise, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: His divinity is not confined to any place or realm: He alone is worthy of worship throughout all creation. His perfect wisdom governs all things, and His knowledge encompasses them completely.

translation: Blessed is the One to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them. With Him is knowledge of the Hour, and to Him you will be returned.
