interpretation: The verse invites reflection on the earth as a divinely provided home, made accessible and suited to sustain the lives of its many inhabitants.

translation: In it are fruits and palm trees with sheathed spathes.
interpretation: The palm’s protective coverings point to the hidden stages through which nourishment is prepared, inviting reflection on the care and order woven into creation.

translation: And grain with husks, and fragrant plants.
interpretation: The verse points to the varied provision God brings forth from the earth: nourishing grain and plants whose fragrance and beauty delight people.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you both deny?
interpretation: Addressed to both humankind and jinn, this question challenges them to recognize their Lord’s blessings and not respond to them with denial or ingratitude.

translation: He created الإنسان from dry clay like pottery.
interpretation: The verse points to Allah’s power to bring human life into being from humble, lifeless material, just as He formed the clay into a finished creation.

translation: And He created the jinn from a flame of fire.
interpretation: The verse points to the jinn’s distinct created nature: they were made from a fiery flame, unlike humankind, whose origin is described elsewhere as clay. Their unseen nature and different origin remain within God’s creative power.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you two deny?
interpretation: The repeated question calls both humankind and jinn to recognize that their Lord’s countless blessings leave no honest ground for denial or ingratitude.

translation: Lord of the two easts and Lord of the two wests.
interpretation: The two easts and two wests refer to the sun’s differing points of rising and setting through the year, whose orderly variation displays God’s sovereignty over the cosmos.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you two deny?
interpretation: Addressing both humankind and jinn, this recurring question challenges them to recognize their Lord’s countless blessings and to respond with gratitude rather than denial.

translation: He let the two bodies of water flow, and they meet.
interpretation: The verse points to God’s power in bringing vast waters together and governing their meeting according to His order.

translation: Between them is a barrier; they do not overstep.
interpretation: The verse points to the divinely ordained order in creation: even where distinct waters meet, their boundary and balance remain under God’s command, revealing His wisdom and power.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you two deny?
interpretation: Addressing both humankind and jinn, this refrain calls them to recognize that every blessing is a sign of their Lord’s generosity, and that denying or overlooking those blessings is a failure of gratitude.

translation: From both of them emerge pearls and coral.
interpretation: The verse draws attention to the seas as a source of precious gifts, inviting reflection on the Creator’s power to bring beauty and value from the waters.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you both deny?
interpretation: Addressing humankind and jinn, this question calls them to recognize and affirm the blessings of their Lord rather than deny them.

translation: And to Him belong the ships sailing through the sea, towering like mountains.
interpretation: The verse invites reflection on how even humanity’s great works depend on the order and forces Allah has placed in creation; their grandeur points to His sovereignty and favor.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you both deny?
interpretation: Addressing both humankind and jinn, this refrain challenges them to recognize that none of their Lord’s countless blessings and signs can rightly be denied, and calls them to gratitude.

translation: Everyone upon it will perish.
interpretation: The verse teaches that worldly existence is temporary: no created being or worldly condition endures forever. It invites humility and a focus on what has lasting value rather than attachment to what must pass away.

translation: And the Face of your Lord, Possessor of Majesty and Honor, will remain.
interpretation: The verse affirms that God alone is everlasting: all created things pass away, while He remains, exalted in majesty and perfect in honor, without being likened to His creation.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you both deny?
interpretation: The repeated question calls humans and jinn to recognize the abundance of God’s blessings and not respond to them with denial or ingratitude.

translation: Everyone in the heavens and the earth asks of Him; every day He is bringing about a matter.
interpretation: All creation depends on God and turns to Him for its needs. His care and governance are continually at work, as He gives, withholds, raises, lowers, forgives, and decrees according to His wisdom.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you both deny?
interpretation: Addressing humans and jinn, this repeated question calls them to recognize their Lord’s countless blessings and answer them with gratitude rather than denial.

translation: We will attend to you, O two weighty beings.
interpretation: This is a solemn warning to humankind and jinn that they will face God’s judgment; “attend to you” means that their reckoning will come, not that God is occupied with other matters.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you both deny?
interpretation: Addressing both humankind and jinn, this repeated question confronts them with the impossibility of denying God’s countless signs and gifts, and calls them to recognize His generosity with gratitude and faith.

translation: O company of jinn and humans, if you are able to pass beyond the bounds of the heavens and the earth, then pass. You will not pass beyond them except by authority.
interpretation: The verse challenges jinn and humans to escape the reach of God’s dominion: no creature can cross the limits He has set unless He grants the power or authority to do so.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you both deny?
interpretation: Addressing humans and jinn, this question challenges them to recognize that none of their Lord’s countless blessings can truly be denied, and calls them to respond with gratitude.

translation: A flame of fire and molten copper will be sent against you, and you will not be able to defend yourselves.
interpretation: The verse warns that no creature can escape God’s authority by its own power; when His judgment comes, neither human strength nor any other means can protect against it.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you both deny?
interpretation: Addressing both humankind and jinn, this recurring question calls them to recognize their Lord’s blessings and signs rather than deny them.

translation: When the sky is split open and becomes rose-red, like molten oil.
interpretation: The striking image conveys the collapse of the familiar cosmic order at the Resurrection: even the vast heavens will be transformed, reminding humanity that worldly stability is not permanent before God’s power.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you both deny?
interpretation: Addressing humankind and jinn, this recurring question challenges them to recognize the blessings and signs of their Lord rather than deny them, and to respond with gratitude.

translation: That Day, no human or jinn will be asked about their sin.
interpretation: Their guilt will be evident, so they will not be questioned to discover what they did; any questioning elsewhere is for rebuke or judgment, not to gain information.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you both deny?
interpretation: Addressing humankind and jinn, this verse challenges them to recognize their Lord’s countless blessings and signs rather than deny them.

translation: The guilty will be recognized by their marks, then seized by their forelocks and feet.
interpretation: The verse portrays the criminals’ guilt as impossible to conceal: their condition will be exposed, and they will be utterly powerless before divine judgment. The image emphasizes the humiliation and helplessness that follow a life of wrongdoing.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you both deny?
interpretation: Addressing humankind and jinn, this repeated question calls them to recognize their Lord’s blessings and respond with gratitude rather than denial.

translation: This is Hell, which the criminals used to deny.
interpretation: The verse confronts those who rejected the warning with the reality they denied, emphasizing that denial cannot make the promised reckoning disappear.

translation: They will go back and forth between it and water boiling at its fiercest.
interpretation: Their punishment is intensified by being driven between two forms of extreme heat, with no relief or escape.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you both deny?
interpretation: Addressing humans and jinn, this recurring question calls them to recognize that their Lord’s blessings and signs leave no reasonable ground for denial, and to respond with gratitude and obedience.

translation: But for whoever fears standing before his Lord, there are two gardens.
interpretation: True reverence for God shapes a person’s choices, restraining them from wrongdoing and guiding them toward obedience; the promise of two gardens is a special reward for such God-consciousness.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you both deny?
interpretation: This recurring question addresses both humankind and jinn, urging them to recognize their Lord’s blessings with gratitude rather than deny them.

translation: Both are full of luxuriant branches.
interpretation: The gardens are depicted as flourishing and abundant, their spreading branches suggesting rich shade and the generous beauty of their provision.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you both deny?
interpretation: Addressing humans and jinn, this question calls them to recognize their Lord’s blessings and signs rather than deny them, and to respond with gratitude.

translation: In them are two springs flowing.
interpretation: Their continuous flow evokes the ease and abundance of Paradise: its blessings are ever-present, without effort or scarcity.

translation: So which of the favors of your Lord will you both deny?
interpretation: Addressed to humankind and jinn, this recurring question challenges them to recognize their Lord’s countless blessings and respond with gratitude rather than denial.

translation: In both of them are two kinds of every fruit.
interpretation: The gardens contain abundant variety: every kind of fruit is provided in two forms or varieties, suggesting the completeness and richness of their delights.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you both deny?
interpretation: This recurring question calls both humankind and jinn to recognize their Lord’s blessings and signs, and to respond with gratitude rather than denial.

translation: Reclining on couches lined with brocade, with the fruit of the two gardens hanging within reach.
interpretation: The verse portrays the gardens’ comfort and abundance: their furnishings are richly appointed, and their fruit is so near that it can be gathered with ease.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you two deny?
interpretation: Addressed to both humans and jinn, this question calls them to recognize that their Lord’s countless blessings cannot rightly be denied, and to respond with gratitude and faith.

translation: In them are women who restrain their gaze, whom neither human nor jinn has touched before them.
interpretation: The verse depicts the companions of Paradise as honored by complete purity and devoted modesty, untouched by anyone before their destined partners.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you two deny?
interpretation: Addressing humankind and jinn, the verse calls them to recognize the signs and blessings surrounding them and to respond with gratitude rather than denial.

translation: As though they were rubies and coral.
interpretation: The comparison conveys their radiant beauty and purity: like precious stones, they are vivid, luminous, and exquisitely lovely.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you two deny?
interpretation: Addressing humankind and jinn, this recurring question challenges them to recognize that their Lord’s blessings are beyond denial and calls them to respond with gratitude and obedience.

translation: Is the reward for excellence anything but excellence?
interpretation: The verse assures that those who act with excellence toward God and His creation will be met with fitting goodness from God, whose generous reward surpasses what their deeds alone could earn.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you two deny?
interpretation: This recurring question addresses both humankind and jinn, urging them to recognize their Lord’s countless favors and signs rather than deny them.

translation: And besides those two are two other gardens.
interpretation: The verse points to further gardens distinct from the ones previously mentioned, understood by many commentators as a lower rank—while still part of the abundant reward God has prepared in Paradise.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you both deny?
interpretation: Addressing humankind and jinn, this refrain challenges them to recognize the countless blessings and signs of their Lord and to respond with gratitude rather than denial.

translation: They are both deep green.
interpretation: The phrase evokes gardens so lush and flourishing that their greenery appears deep and intense.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you both deny?
interpretation: Addressing both humanity and jinn, this recurring question urges them to recognize their Lord’s blessings and respond with gratitude rather than denial.

translation: In them are two springs, gushing forth.
interpretation: The springs’ vigorous flow evokes abundant, lively refreshment—a sign of the ease and delight prepared in Paradise.

translation: So which of your Lord’s blessings will you both deny?
interpretation: Addressing humankind and jinn, the verse challenges them to recognize their Lord’s abundant favors and respond with gratitude rather than denial.

translation: In both of them are fruit, date palms, and pomegranates.
interpretation: The verse portrays the gardens as abundant in nourishment and delight, singling out date palms and pomegranates as especially valued gifts within their varied produce.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you two deny?
interpretation: Addressing humankind and jinn, this refrain challenges them to recognize their Lord’s blessings and asks how they could deny any of them.

translation: In them are women of excellent character and beautiful appearance.
interpretation: The verse portrays the companions of Paradise as united in inner goodness and outward beauty, expressing the completeness of its blessings.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you two deny?
interpretation: Addressing humans and jinn, this refrain challenges them to recognize their Lord’s blessings and respond with gratitude rather than deny them.

translation: Fair companions, secluded in pavilions.
interpretation: The verse evokes the honor, privacy, and purity of the companions promised in Paradise; their seclusion suggests protected dignity, not captivity.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you both deny?
interpretation: Addressed to humankind and jinn, this question calls them to recognize their Lord’s blessings and respond with gratitude rather than denial.

translation: No human or jinn had touched them before their companions.
interpretation: The verse portrays the women of Paradise as untouched before their spouses, emphasizing their purity and the honor of their companionship.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you two deny?
interpretation: Addressing humankind and jinn, this recurring question challenges them to recognize that the signs and blessings of their Lord leave no sound basis for denial, and calls them to gratitude.

translation: Reclining on green cushions and beautiful carpets.
interpretation: The verse evokes the serenity and splendor of Paradise, where the believers enjoy dignified rest amid beauty and comfort.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you both deny?
interpretation: The verse challenges humans and jinn to recognize that God’s countless gifts and signs leave no honest grounds for denial, and calls them to respond with gratitude and faith.

translation: Blessed is the name of your Lord, the Possessor of Majesty and Honor.
interpretation: God’s name is exalted and abundant in blessing; His perfect majesty inspires reverence, while His generosity makes Him worthy of praise and devotion.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. When the Inevitable Event takes place,
interpretation: The verse opens by invoking Allah’s mercy, then declares that the Day of Resurrection will certainly come to pass; no one can prevent or deny it.

translation: There will be no denying its occurrence.
interpretation: When the Resurrection takes place, its reality will be unmistakable, and no one will be able to deny that it has occurred.

translation: Bringing some low and raising others high.
interpretation: The Day of Judgment will overturn worldly status: those who were arrogant and powerful may be brought low, while the faithful who were overlooked may be raised in honor.

translation: When the earth is shaken with a violent shaking,
interpretation: This depicts the upheaval of the Day of Judgment, when the familiar stability of the world gives way to the reality of resurrection and accountability.

translation: And the mountains are crushed to dust.
interpretation: The mountains’ collapse conveys that, on the Day of Resurrection, even what seems most solid and enduring will yield completely to God’s command.

translation: Then they become scattered dust.
interpretation: The image conveys how what seems most solid and enduring can be utterly dissolved by divine power, awakening the listener to the upheaval of the Last Day.

translation: And you will be divided into three groups.
interpretation: On the Day of Resurrection, people will be separated into three distinct groups according to their standing before God and their ultimate fate.

translation: Then the companions of the right—what are the companions of the right!
interpretation: The rhetorical question magnifies their honor and blessedness, drawing attention to the lofty reward and secure standing granted to them by God.

translation: And the companions of the left—what are the companions of the left?
interpretation: The repeated question is an expression of awe and warning: it underscores the grievous plight awaiting those who are counted among the people of the left.

translation: And the foremost are the foremost.
interpretation: This phrase honors those who hasten to faith and obedience, striving to draw near to God; their precedence reflects the exceptional rank they will receive.

translation: Those are the ones brought near [to God].
interpretation: They are honored with nearness to God through their faith and devotion—a nearness of rank and favor, not physical distance.

translation: In gardens of bliss.
interpretation: This phrase evokes the lasting joy and peace of Paradise, where the faithful are welcomed into a life of complete contentment and nearness to God.

translation: A multitude from the earlier generations.
interpretation: It indicates that many of those brought near to God were from the peoples of earlier times.

translation: And a few from the later generations.
interpretation: It indicates that only a small number from later generations attain this distinguished spiritual rank; closeness to God is not guaranteed by belonging to any particular era.

translation: Upon intricately woven couches.
interpretation: The phrase evokes the honor and refined comfort prepared for the people of Paradise, with couches crafted in an exquisite, interlaced design.

translation: Reclining upon them, facing one another.
interpretation: Their posture conveys ease and mutual companionship: they enjoy the Garden together, free from discomfort or estrangement.

translation: Immortal youths will circulate among them.
interpretation: The verse evokes the honor and ease of the people of Paradise: they are attended by youthful servants whose freshness does not fade, a sign of comfort and blessing without decline.

translation: With cups, pitchers, and a goblet filled from a flowing spring,
interpretation: The verse evokes the honor and ease of Paradise: its people are served pure drink in vessels of abundance, without toil or deprivation.

translation: They will suffer no headache from it, nor will they become intoxicated.
interpretation: The drink of Paradise brings pleasure without the pain, impairment, or loss of reason associated with worldly drink.

translation: And fruit of whatever they choose,
interpretation: The verse evokes the abundance and ease of Paradise: its people may choose the fruits they desire, with every pleasure freely available to them.

translation: And the flesh of birds that they desire.
interpretation: The verse portrays the provision of Paradise as abundant and perfectly suited to its inhabitants’ wishes, a sign of God’s generous honor toward them.

translation: And [with them are] companions of striking, beautiful eyes.
interpretation: The phrase portrays the companionship of Paradise through imagery of purity and beauty, describing companions whose eyes are especially lovely and striking.

translation: Like pearls carefully kept away.
interpretation: Their beauty and purity are likened to precious pearls preserved from blemish and harm.

translation: As recompense for what they used to do.
interpretation: It expresses that what people receive is a just recompense for their deeds.

translation: They will hear no idle talk or sinful speech therein.
interpretation: The verse portrays the inhabitants of Paradise as surrounded by complete peace and dignity: their conversations are free from words that are empty, harmful, or morally blameworthy.

translation: Except for the words, “Peace, peace.”
interpretation: The verse portrays Paradise as free from hurtful or futile speech, where people exchange only words of peace and goodwill.

translation: And the companions of the right—what are the companions of the right?
interpretation: This rhetorical question magnifies the honor and blessed rank of the companions of the right, whose place in the Hereafter is one of great felicity.

translation: Among thornless lote trees,
interpretation: The verse evokes the gentle abundance of Paradise: even its lote trees are free of thorns, offering beauty and delight without the discomfort found in worldly life.

translation: And banana trees laden with fruit, one cluster upon another.
interpretation: The verse evokes the abundance and ease of the gardens of Paradise: their fruit is plentiful and beautifully clustered, ready to be enjoyed.

translation: And in extended shade,
interpretation: The phrase evokes the lasting comfort and shelter of Paradise: shade that is spacious and uninterrupted, unlike shade that shifts or fades in the worldly life.

translation: And flowing, abundant water.
interpretation: The phrase evokes water readily and continually available, conveying the ease and enduring comfort of the Garden.

translation: And abundant fruit,
interpretation: This describes the plentiful fruit of Paradise, a lasting blessing given in abundance to its people.

translation: Neither are they ever cut off, nor are they withheld.
interpretation: The phrase portrays the enduring abundance of Paradise: its blessings do not run out, and no one is denied access to them.

translation: And couches raised high,
interpretation: The raised couches evoke the honor and comfort prepared for the people of Paradise, where they are received with dignity and ease.

translation: Indeed, We have brought them into being in a new creation.
interpretation: The verse points to God’s power to transform them into a renewed and perfected state suited to the life of Paradise.

translation: And We made them virgins,
interpretation: In the context of the verses describing the people of Paradise, this means that God grants them companions in a state of complete purity and renewed freshness, free from the imperfections and burdens of earthly life.

translation: Loving and of equal age.
interpretation: The phrase portrays the women of Paradise as affectionate toward their companions and well matched in age, evoking a relationship marked by closeness and harmony.

translation: For the companions of the right.
interpretation: It refers to the people honored with their record of deeds in their right hand, signifying divine acceptance and a blessed end.

translation: A great multitude from the earlier generations.
interpretation: The phrase describes a substantial number of people from those who came before, emphasizing their abundance among the group being discussed.

translation: And a multitude from later generations.
interpretation: In context, this indicates that the people of the right hand will include many from later generations, just as they include many from earlier ones.

translation: And the companions of the left—what are the companions of the left?
interpretation: The rhetorical question magnifies their grievous fate, preparing the listener for the severity of what awaits them.

translation: In scorching wind and scalding water.
interpretation: The pairing of burning air and boiling water portrays punishment as inescapable: even the surroundings offer no relief.

translation: And a shade of black smoke,
interpretation: This is a shade that offers no relief or comfort; it is part of the punishment awaiting those condemned to the Fire.

translation: Neither cool nor pleasant.
interpretation: This shade offers no relief or comfort; it is oppressive rather than soothing.

translation: Indeed, before that, they lived in luxury.
interpretation: Their former prosperity had left them heedless and self-indulgent, so they failed to heed the truth and give thanks for what they had been given.

translation: And they persisted in the great sin.
interpretation: They continued obstinately in associating partners with God, rather than turning back from this grave wrongdoing.

translation: They used to say, “When we have died and become dust and bones, will we really be raised again?”
interpretation: Their words express a dismissive denial of resurrection: they regarded the body’s return to dust and bones as proof that being brought back to life was impossible, overlooking God’s power to recreate them.

translation: And our forefathers of old too?
interpretation: The phrase continues a skeptical question about resurrection, extending it to their long-deceased ancestors: could they, too, be brought back to life?

translation: Say, “Indeed, the former and the latter…”
interpretation: The phrase encompasses people across every age, with none beyond God’s knowledge or judgment.

translation: They will surely be gathered at the appointed time of a known day.
interpretation: The phrase emphasizes that the gathering for judgment is certain and will occur at a time fixed by God, even if its exact moment is unknown to people.

translation: Then indeed you, O misguided deniers, ...
interpretation: The direct address rebukes those who have turned away from the truth and rejected the message, underscoring the certainty of what follows for them.

translation: You will surely eat from a tree of Zaqqum.
interpretation: The emphatic wording presents this as a certain consequence, portraying Zaqqum as a stark and dreadful form of sustenance.

translation: Then you will fill your bellies with it.
interpretation: This describes the people of Hell being made to eat from the Tree of Zaqqūm until their bellies are full, emphasizing the severity and humiliation of their punishment.

translation: Then, on top of it, you will drink scalding water.
interpretation: The verse depicts the punishment as one torment compounding another: after eating the bitter fruit of the tree of Zaqqum, the condemned are given boiling water to drink, with no relief between the two.

translation: Then you will drink as thirst-stricken camels drink.
interpretation: The image conveys an unbearable, unquenchable thirst: they gulp down drink with the desperate urgency of camels afflicted by extreme thirst, yet find no relief.

translation: This is their welcome on the Day of Judgment.
interpretation: “Welcome” refers to what has been prepared for them as their reception: a fitting punishment for their rejection, not an honor. The verse emphasizes that their recompense is appointed for the Day of Judgment.

translation: We created you, so why do you not believe?
interpretation: Your own creation is a sign of God’s power, giving you reason to believe that He can bring you back to life after death.

translation: Have you considered the semen you emit?
interpretation: The verse calls people to recognize that they do not create or control the beginnings of human life; its origin and unfolding point to God’s power.

translation: Is it you who create it, or are We the Creator?
interpretation: The verse directs people to recognize that human beings do not originate life by their own power: despite their role in its causes, its creation ultimately belongs to God.

translation: We have decreed death among you, and We cannot be thwarted.
interpretation: Death comes by God’s decree, not by chance or human control; no one can escape or prevent what He has ordained.

translation: So that We may replace you with others like you and bring you into being in a form you do not know.
interpretation: God’s power to create is not limited to the form in which people now exist: He can replace them with others and recreate them in a state beyond their knowledge, so resurrection is no more beyond His power than their first creation.

translation: You already know of the first creation, so why do you not take heed?
interpretation: Since you know that God brought you into existence in the first place, you have reason to recognize that He can bring you back to life after death. The verse calls you to reflect on this and not dismiss the resurrection.

translation: Have you considered what you sow?
interpretation: The verse invites people to recognize that although they prepare and sow the seed, its growth into a crop is not within their power alone; it depends on God’s sustaining and creative power.

translation: Is it you who make it grow, or are We the One who makes it grow?
interpretation: Though people sow and tend the seed, its growth is beyond their control. The verse directs attention to God as the source of the life and conditions that make cultivation fruitful, inviting humility rather than pride in human effort.

translation: If We willed, We could turn it into dry, shattered debris, and you would be left lamenting.
interpretation: The verse calls people to recognize that the harvest they rely on is not theirs to control: its continued growth is a blessing sustained by God. This awareness should humble them and lead them to gratitude rather than taking their provisions for granted.

translation: We are truly burdened with loss.
interpretation: They say this in despair, believing that their ruined harvest has left them financially ruined.

translation: Rather, we are deprived.
interpretation: They recognize that they have been deprived of the harvest they expected, showing that human effort alone cannot secure provision; its fulfillment remains in God’s hands.

translation: Have you considered the water you drink?
interpretation: The verse invites reflection on how a necessity as simple as drinking water depends on provision beyond human control, cultivating gratitude and humility before God.

translation: Is it you who send it down from the clouds, or are We the Ones who send it down?
interpretation: The verse directs people to recognize that rain is not within human control: however much people may understand or influence their surroundings, the power to send life-giving water from the clouds belongs to God alone.

translation: If We willed, We could make it bitter and undrinkable; so why are you not grateful?
interpretation: The verse calls people to recognize that the drinkable water they rely on is not something they can take for granted. Its goodness is a gift of God, and awareness of how easily it could be otherwise should lead to sincere gratitude.

translation: Have you considered the fire that you kindle?
interpretation: The verse invites people to recognize that, although they kindle and use fire, its existence and power ultimately depend on God’s creation.

translation: Is it you who brought forth its tree, or are We the ones who bring it forth?
interpretation: The verse invites people to recognize that the source of the tree—and of the means it provides—lies beyond human power, pointing to God as the Creator who brings life and provision into being.

translation: We made it a reminder and a provision for those who travel through the wilderness.
interpretation: The fire you kindle is both a practical gift, especially for travelers, and a reminder of God’s power—prompting reflection on His ability to bring about resurrection.

translation: So glorify the name of your Lord, the Most Great.
interpretation: Exalt your Lord by remembering Him with reverence, affirming that He is far above every imperfection and alone possesses supreme greatness.

translation: No indeed! I swear by the positions of the stars.
interpretation: The oath directs attention to the stars’ precisely appointed places, inviting awe at the order and wisdom woven into creation.

translation: And indeed, it is a tremendous oath, if you only knew.
interpretation: The oath is described as immense because what it invokes—the stars and their appointed positions—is a sign of the vastness and precision of God’s creation, whose full significance exceeds human understanding.

translation: Indeed, it is a noble Qur’an.
interpretation: The Qur’an is exalted and honored, and its divine origin and guidance make it worthy of reverence.

translation: In a well-guarded book.
interpretation: The phrase describes the Qur’an as preserved in a protected, concealed record, underscoring its sanctity.

translation: None touch it except the purified.
interpretation: The verse points to the Qur’an’s exalted and protected nature: it is attended by purified beings, underscoring the purity and honor of its divine source.

translation: A revelation from the Lord of all worlds.
interpretation: The words affirm that this revelation comes from God, the sovereign and sustainer of all creation, rather than from any human source.

translation: Is it this discourse that you treat lightly?
interpretation: The verse rebukes those who respond to the Qur’an with indifference or evasive compromise, instead of giving due weight to its truth and guidance.

translation: And you make your share of provision that you deny.
interpretation: You respond to the provision God gives you with denial and ingratitude, attributing the blessing to other than Him instead of recognizing His favor.

translation: So why, when it reaches the throat…
interpretation: The verse evokes the moment of death, when the soul reaches the throat, confronting people with how powerless they are to prevent it.

translation: while you are then looking on,
interpretation: You witness the moment helplessly, unable to prevent what is unfolding.

translation: And We are nearer to him than you, but you do not see.
interpretation: God’s nearness here is not physical distance; it expresses His complete knowledge and authority over the dying person, while those present cannot perceive the unseen reality unfolding around them.

translation: Then why, if you are not to be brought to account,
interpretation: The verse challenges those who deny divine judgment: if you are truly beyond God’s reckoning and power, why can you not restore the soul when it reaches the throat? Their inability exposes the weakness of that claim.

translation: Bring it back, if you are truthful.
interpretation: The challenge concerns the departing soul: people are unable to return it to the body, exposing the limits of human power and the truth of God’s sovereignty over life and death.

translation: Then, if he is one of those brought near [to Allah]…
interpretation: The verse begins a conditional statement about a person granted closeness to Allah, signaling a special standing whose outcome is completed in the following verse.

translation: Then [there is] comfort, fragrant provision, and a Garden of bliss.
interpretation: The verse conveys the gracious welcome awaiting the faithful: God grants relief and serenity, along with blessings that are pure and delightful, as they enter a state of lasting joy in His care.

translation: But if he is one of the companions of the right…
interpretation: This refers to a person granted a blessed and honored standing in the Hereafter; being among the companions of the right signifies God’s favor and salvation.

translation: Then peace be upon you, from the people of the right.
interpretation: The person who belongs to the people of the right is welcomed with peace and reassurance, signifying safety and honor in the Hereafter.

translation: But if he is one of the deniers, the astray,
interpretation: The phrase identifies the person who rejects the truth and departs from guidance; in its surrounding passage, it introduces a warning of a grievous fate in the Hereafter.

translation: Then his welcome will be scalding water.
interpretation: The word “welcome” evokes the provision offered to a guest, but here it marks a bitter reversal: the denier’s reception is itself a form of punishment.

translation: And burning in the blazing Fire.
interpretation: The phrase portrays the punishment awaiting those who reject the truth: they are made to suffer the fire of Hell.

translation: Indeed, this is the very truth of certainty.
interpretation: What has been revealed is not conjecture or mere warning, but a reality established with absolute certainty and grounded in God’s truth.

translation: So glorify the name of your Lord, the Magnificent.
interpretation: Honor and exalt your Lord, declaring Him far above every imperfection and acknowledging His supreme greatness.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Allah; He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: All creation, by its existence and ordered nature, bears witness to Allah’s perfection and freedom from every flaw. His absolute power is joined with wisdom, so nothing in His decree is beyond purpose or knowledge.

translation: To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He gives life and causes death, and He has power over all things.
interpretation: The verse directs people to recognize that no force or circumstance lies beyond God’s authority. Because life, death, and all creation are under His control, trust and ultimate reliance belong to Him alone.

translation: He is the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden, and He has knowledge of all things.
interpretation: God’s names here affirm that nothing precedes Him or outlasts Him, and that nothing is beyond His reach: His signs make His presence evident, while His essence remains beyond full human perception. His knowledge encompasses both what is outwardly visible and what is concealed.

translation: He is the One who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then established Himself over the Throne. He knows what enters the earth and what emerges from it, what descends from the sky and what ascends into it. He is with you wherever you may be, and Allah sees all that you do.
interpretation: The verse teaches that God’s sovereignty and knowledge encompass all creation, while His being “with” people signifies His all-encompassing awareness and oversight, not bodily presence in a place. Nothing is hidden from Him, so human actions are always within His knowledge and sight.

translation: To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and to Allah all affairs return.
interpretation: The verse teaches that all authority is ultimately God’s, while human power is limited and temporary. Every matter will finally be resolved by Him, so people should place their trust in Him and remain mindful that their choices are answerable to Him.

translation: He causes the night to pass into the day and causes the day to pass into the night, and He knows fully what is within people’s hearts.
interpretation: The seamless turning of night into day and day into night points to God’s complete command over creation. The same Lord who governs what is outwardly visible also knows every hidden thought and intention within a person.

translation: Believe in Allah and His Messenger, and spend from what He has entrusted to you. Those among you who believe and spend will have a great reward.
interpretation: The verse presents wealth as a trust rather than an absolute possession: what people hold has been placed in their care for a time. Giving from it for good is therefore a way of putting faith into practice, with the assurance of a great reward from Allah.

translation: And what is the matter with you that you do not believe in Allah, while the Messenger is calling you to believe in your Lord, when He has already taken your covenant—if you are truly believers?
interpretation: The verse reproaches those who withhold faith despite the Messenger’s clear invitation, reminding them that their bond with God already obliges them to believe and respond sincerely to His call.

translation: He is the One who sends down clear signs upon His servant to bring you out of darkness into light. Indeed, Allah is Most Kind and Most Merciful to you.
interpretation: The revelation is presented as an act of divine care: its clear guidance enables people to leave spiritual confusion and turn toward faith and truth. Allah’s kindness and mercy are shown in giving them this guidance.

translation: And what is the matter with you that you do not spend in the way of Allah, when the inheritance of the heavens and the earth belongs to Allah? Those among you who spent and fought before the Victory are not equal to those who spent and fought afterward. They are greater in rank, though Allah has promised the best reward to each. And Allah is fully aware of what you do.
interpretation: The verse urges believers to give generously for Allah’s cause, reminding them that all wealth ultimately belongs to Him. It honors those who sacrificed before the Victory with a higher rank because their faith and commitment were tested under greater hardship, while affirming that those who served afterward are also promised the best reward. Allah knows the sincerity and deeds of every person.

translation: Who is it that will lend Allah a goodly loan, so that He may multiply it for him, and he will have a generous reward?
interpretation: The verse invites people to give sincerely for God’s sake, portraying such generosity as a loan that God will repay many times over. The image emphasizes both the lasting value of giving and the promise of generous reward from God.

translation: On the Day you see believing men and believing women, their light proceeding before them and to their right: “Good news for you today: gardens beneath which rivers flow, where you will remain forever. That is the supreme triumph.”
interpretation: Their light is a sign of the faith and righteous deeds by which God guides and honors them on the Day of Judgment. Their lasting nearness to God’s mercy is the true triumph, surpassing every worldly success.

translation: On the Day when the hypocrite men and women will say to those who believed, “Wait for us, so that we may take some of your light,” it will be said, “Go back behind you and seek light.” Then a wall will be placed between them, with a gate: within it is mercy, and outside it, facing them, is punishment.
interpretation: The verse portrays the ultimate separation between sincere faith and hypocrisy: the light that guides and saves cannot be borrowed at the last moment merely by standing near the believers. The wall makes visible the different outcomes of inward realities—mercy for those within and punishment for those left outside.

translation: They will call to them, “Were we not with you?” They will reply, “Yes, but you led yourselves into temptation, waited, doubted, and were deluded by wishful thinking until Allah’s command came. And the Deceiver deceived you about Allah.”
interpretation: The verse shows that mere outward association with the believers will not save those who inwardly undermined their faith. Their own choices—giving in to temptation, delaying commitment, nurturing doubt, and relying on false hopes—left them vulnerable to deception about Allah and His promises.

translation: So today no ransom will be accepted from you, nor from those who disbelieved. Your abode is the Fire; it is your fitting companion—and what an evil destination!
interpretation: Once judgment has come, neither wealth nor any substitute can undo the consequences of disbelief. The Fire is called their fitting companion because, by their choices, they have made it their deserved abode.

translation: Has the time not come for those who believe for their hearts to become humble at the remembrance of Allah and at the truth that has been sent down, and not to be like those who were given the Scripture before, then time passed over them and their hearts hardened? Many of them are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: The verse calls believers to let remembrance of Allah and revelation continually soften and guide their hearts. It warns that prolonged neglect can dull a community’s spiritual responsiveness, as happened among many who received scripture before them.

translation: Know that Allah gives life to the earth after its death. We have made the signs clear to you so that you may understand.
interpretation: The earth’s renewal after it lies barren is a sign of Allah’s power to bring the dead back to life, and a reminder that hearts, too, can be revived by faith and guidance.

translation: Indeed, the men and women who give charity and lend Allah a goodly loan—it will be multiplied for them, and they will have a noble reward.
interpretation: The verse teaches that sincere generosity, whether through charity or other acts of giving for God’s sake, is never lost: God greatly multiplies its reward and grants the giver an honorable recompense.

translation: Those who believe in God and His messengers are the people of truth; and the witnesses are with their Lord. They have their reward and their light. But those who disbelieve and deny Our signs are the companions of the Fire.
interpretation: True faith is not merely a claim: it makes a person steadfast in truth and receptive to God’s guidance. The verse points to the lasting dignity and illumination God grants to those who bear witness to the truth, while warning that denying it shuts a person off from that guidance.

translation: Know that the life of this world is only play, amusement, adornment, boasting among yourselves, and competition in increasing wealth and children. It is like rain whose growth delights the tillers; then it dries, and you see it turn yellow, then become broken fragments. In the Hereafter there is severe punishment, and forgiveness from God and His pleasure. The life of this world is nothing but a deceptive enjoyment.
interpretation: The verse warns against treating worldly success and pleasure as lasting ends. Like crops that flourish briefly and then decay, wealth, status, and other attractions pass away; what ultimately matters is whether one’s life is directed toward God, whose punishment and forgiveness belong to the lasting reality of the Hereafter.

translation: Race toward forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden as vast as the heavens and the earth, prepared for those who believe in Allah and His messengers. That is Allah’s bounty, which He grants to whom He wills; Allah is the possessor of immense bounty.
interpretation: The verse urges believers to hasten toward repentance and righteous deeds, while reminding them that entry into Paradise is ultimately a gift of Allah’s boundless generosity, not something they can claim as their own achievement.

translation: No calamity befalls the earth or yourselves except that it is recorded in a Book before We bring it into being. Surely that is easy for Allah.
interpretation: The verse teaches that nothing that happens lies beyond Allah’s prior knowledge and decree. Knowing this can steady a person through hardship: events are not outside His wisdom or control, even when their purpose is not yet clear.

translation: So that you may not grieve over what has passed you by, nor exult over what He has given you. And Allah does not love anyone who is arrogant and boastful.
interpretation: The verse teaches a steady, humble response to life’s losses and blessings: do not let what you miss consume you, or what you receive make you conceited, since both are within Allah’s knowledge and decree.

translation: Those who are miserly and urge people to be miserly. Whoever turns away—Allah is indeed the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: The verse warns against not only withholding what one ought to give, but also encouraging others to do the same. Turning away from generosity does not diminish Allah in any way; He is entirely free of need and worthy of praise, while people themselves bear the consequences of their choices.

translation: We sent Our messengers with clear proofs, and sent down with them the Book and the balance, so that people may uphold justice. And We sent down iron, in which there is great might and benefits for people, so that God may make known who supports Him and His messengers, unseen. Surely God is Strong, Almighty.
interpretation: Revelation establishes the moral measure by which justice is to be upheld, while iron points to the material power and practical means that can protect it. The verse thus presents justice as a responsibility requiring both sound guidance and human effort. Supporting God and His messengers means standing for that cause even when its ultimate outcome is unseen; this is a test for people, not a need of God, whose strength is absolute.

translation: Indeed, We sent Noah and Abraham, and placed prophethood and the Scripture among their descendants. Among them are those who are guided, but many of them are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: The verse teaches that receiving the honor of prophethood and scripture within one’s lineage does not guarantee that every descendant will follow guidance. Each person remains accountable for how they respond: some accept the truth, while many turn away in disobedience.

translation: Then We sent Our messengers, one after another, following in their footsteps, and We sent Jesus, son of Mary, and gave him the Gospel. We placed compassion and mercy in the hearts of those who followed him. As for monasticism, they instituted it themselves; We had not prescribed it for them, but they did so seeking God’s pleasure. Yet they did not observe it as it should have been observed. So We granted those among them who believed their reward, while many of them were defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: The verse distinguishes sincere devotion from religious practices people impose upon themselves: monasticism was not prescribed by God, though its founders adopted it in pursuit of His approval. The real test was whether they remained faithful to that sincere aim; those who believed were rewarded, while many failed to uphold it. Thus, devotion is not measured by self-imposed hardship, but by fidelity to God and sincere obedience.

translation: O you who believe, be mindful of Allah and believe in His Messenger. He will grant you a double share of His mercy, provide you with a light by which you may walk, and forgive you. And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse calls believers to make their faith sincere and active through reverence for Allah and trust in His Messenger. The promised double share of mercy points to abundant divine favor, while the light signifies guidance that helps a person discern the right path and live by it; forgiveness reminds us that this guidance and reward come from Allah’s mercy.

translation: So that the People of the Scripture may know that they have no power over any of God’s bounty, and that bounty is in God’s hand: He grants it to whomever He wills. God is Possessor of immense bounty.
interpretation: God’s favor is not something any people can claim, control, or restrict. Its source and authority belong entirely to God, who grants it as He wills.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Allah has indeed heard the words of the woman who pleads with you about her husband and appeals to Allah. Allah hears the exchange between you both. Surely Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.
interpretation: The verse reassures the woman that her plea and private conversation are fully known to Allah. Her appeal is not overlooked: Allah hears her distress and sees the circumstances behind it, affirming that no one’s grievance is beyond His knowledge or care.

translation: Those among you who declare their wives forbidden to them by likening them to their mothers—those women are not their mothers. Their mothers are only the women who gave birth to them. Surely they utter something reprehensible and false; yet God is Pardoning, All-Forgiving.
interpretation: The verse rejects the practice of treating a wife as a mother through a spoken declaration: words cannot change the truth of a relationship, and such a claim is a grave falsehood. God’s closing assurance of pardon and forgiveness leaves the door open to those who turn back from this wrongdoing.

translation: As for those who declare their wives forbidden to them as their mothers’ backs, then wish to go back on what they have said, they must free a slave before the two of them touch one another. By this you are admonished; and Allah is fully aware of what you do.
interpretation: The verse treats declaring one’s wife forbidden through this kind of pronouncement as a grave matter, not a casual utterance. If a husband wishes to resume marital relations, he must first make the prescribed expiation, underscoring both the weight of his words and his accountability before God.

translation: Whoever cannot find [a slave to free] must fast for two consecutive months before the spouses touch one another. Whoever is unable to do that must feed sixty needy people. This is so that you may believe in Allah and His Messenger. These are Allah’s limits, and for those who reject them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: The prescribed expiation is meant to be carried out before the spouses resume marital relations, with a graduated alternative for whoever cannot fulfill the preceding requirement. The passage thus makes obedience to Allah’s limits part of sincere faith in Him and His Messenger, and warns against treating those limits lightly.

translation: Indeed, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger have been brought low, just as those before them were brought low. We have sent down clear signs, and for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: The verse presents the humiliation of earlier opponents as a warning: resisting clear divine guidance does not grant lasting power or dignity. Once the signs have been made plain, those who persist in rejection face a punishment that reflects the disgrace of their defiance.

translation: On the Day Allah raises them all, He will inform them of what they did. Allah has kept account of it, though they have forgotten it; and Allah is witness over all things.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that no deed is lost or hidden from Allah: even what people themselves have forgotten remains fully known and recorded, so they will face a just reckoning.

translation: Have you not seen that Allah knows whatever is in the heavens and the earth? There is no private conversation among three except that He is their fourth, nor among five except that He is their sixth; nor fewer nor more than that, wherever they may be, without His being with them. Then, on the Day of Resurrection, He will inform them of what they did. Indeed, Allah has knowledge of all things.
interpretation: Allah’s being “with” people means that nothing in their private counsel is beyond His knowledge—not that He is physically present among them. The verse therefore calls people to remember that even what they conceal is known to God and will be accounted for.

translation: Have you not seen those who were forbidden to hold secret conversations, yet return to what they were forbidden and confer in sin, hostility, and disobedience to the Messenger? When they come to you, they greet you with words Allah has not used to greet you, and say to themselves, “Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?” Hell is enough for them: they will enter it. What a miserable destination!
interpretation: The verse warns that the absence of immediate punishment is not proof that wrongdoing is harmless or accepted. Those who use secret counsel to foster hostility, insult the Messenger, and then take the delay of divine punishment as a reason for mockery are deceiving themselves: accountability may be deferred, but it is not removed.

translation: O you who believe, when you speak privately, do not speak privately about sin, aggression, or disobedience to the Messenger. Rather, speak privately about righteousness and mindfulness of God. And be mindful of God, to whom you will be gathered.
interpretation: Private counsel is not ethically neutral: secrecy should not become a means of plotting harm or undermining what is right. Believers should use it to support good and deepen their sense of responsibility, remembering that every hidden conversation remains answerable before God.

translation: Secret conversations are only from Satan, to grieve those who believe; yet they cannot harm them in any way except by Allah’s permission. So let the believers put their trust in Allah.
interpretation: The verse warns against private plotting or hushed talk used to unsettle believers. Such talk has no independent power to harm them; believers should therefore resist fear and place their trust in Allah.

translation: O you who believe, when you are told, “Make room in gatherings,” then make room; Allah will make room for you. And when you are told, “Rise,” then rise. Allah will raise in rank those of you who believe and those who have been granted knowledge. Allah is fully aware of what you do.
interpretation: The verse teaches that humility and consideration for others are signs of sincere faith, while knowledge joined with faith brings a person greater honor in Allah’s sight. Such rank is not merely a matter of social standing; Allah knows the sincerity and deeds behind it.

translation: O you who believe, when you wish to speak privately with the Messenger, offer charity before your private conversation. That is better for you and purer. But if you cannot afford it, then surely God is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: The instruction cultivates sincerity and reverence in seeking the Messenger’s private attention, discouraging needless demands while making clear that inability to give is met with God’s mercy, not blame.

translation: Were you apprehensive about giving charity before your private consultation? Since you did not do so, and God has turned toward you in mercy, establish prayer, give zakat, and obey God and His Messenger. God is fully aware of what you do.
interpretation: The requirement to give charity before a private consultation was lifted after the believers did not carry it out; the verse directs them back to their enduring duties and reminds them that God knows the sincerity behind their actions.

translation: Have you not seen those who ally themselves with a people upon whom Allah has brought His anger? They belong neither to you nor to them, and they knowingly swear false oaths.
interpretation: The verse rebukes people who shift their loyalties for worldly advantage, aligning themselves with those opposed to divine guidance while denying where they truly stand and knowingly using false oaths to conceal it.

translation: Allah has prepared a severe punishment for them. Indeed, evil was what they used to do.
interpretation: Their punishment is presented as the just consequence of their persistent wrongdoing, not as something imposed without cause.

translation: They have made their oaths a shield, and thereby turned people away from the way of Allah. So they will have a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: Their oaths serve not as truthful testimony but as cover for wrongdoing, protecting them from scrutiny while they obstruct others from Allah’s way. The punishment is humiliating because it strips away that false appearance and exposes their disgrace.

translation: Neither their wealth nor their children will avail them at all against Allah. They are the people of the Fire, abiding therein forever.
interpretation: The verse teaches that worldly possessions and family ties cannot shield a person from Allah’s judgment; lasting security comes not from these things but from faith and obedience to Him.

translation: On the Day Allah raises them all, they will swear to Him just as they swear to you, thinking that they are upon something. Surely, they are indeed the liars.
interpretation: Their repeated false oaths have so distorted their judgment that they imagine deception can still protect them before Allah. The verse warns that the self-deception they use among people will not make their claims true or conceal their reality from Him.

translation: Satan gained mastery over them and caused them to forget the remembrance of God. They are Satan’s party. Surely, Satan’s party are the losers.
interpretation: The verse warns that when people yield to Satan’s influence, heedlessness of God can take hold of their lives and shape their loyalties. Their loss is ultimately spiritual: they abandon the guidance that leads to lasting success.

translation: Indeed, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger will be among the most humiliated.
interpretation: The verse teaches that defying Allah and His Messenger cannot lead to lasting honor; such opposition ultimately brings humiliation before Allah, regardless of a person’s worldly standing.

translation: Allah has decreed: “I will surely prevail—I and My messengers.” Indeed, Allah is Strong, Almighty.
interpretation: This is a divine assurance that God’s purpose, conveyed through His messengers, will ultimately overcome opposition. Their mission rests on God’s power and might, even when its victory is not immediately apparent.

translation: You will not find people who believe in Allah and the Last Day showing affection to those who oppose Allah and His Messenger—even if they are their fathers, sons, brothers, or clan. Allah has inscribed faith in their hearts and strengthened them with a spirit from Him. He will admit them into Gardens beneath which rivers flow, where they will remain forever. Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. They are Allah’s party. Indeed, Allah’s party are the successful.
interpretation: The verse teaches that faith demands moral loyalty to God above every tie of kinship when those ties are set against Him; it is not a call to mistreat relatives, but to refuse complicity in opposition to what is right. Such fidelity is not merely human resolve: God roots faith in the heart and sustains the believer, making divine approval—not worldly allegiance—the measure of true success.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Allah; and He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: The verse invites us to recognize that all creation, whether or not its glorification is perceptible to us, is subject to Allah’s authority and reflects His wisdom. His might is never separate from wise purpose.

translation: He is the One who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Book from their homes at the first banishment. You did not think they would leave, and they thought their fortresses would protect them from God. But God came upon them from where they had not expected, and cast terror into their hearts; they destroyed their homes with their own hands and the hands of the believers. So take heed, people of insight.
interpretation: The verse teaches that worldly strength and security cannot shield anyone from God’s decree. Those who trusted in their fortresses were overcome through means they had not anticipated, and their own actions became part of their undoing. People of insight are therefore urged to reflect on the limits of human power and place their trust in God rather than in apparent protections.

translation: Had Allah not decreed their exile, He would have punished them in this world; and in the Hereafter they will have the punishment of the Fire.
interpretation: Their exile was the worldly consequence decreed for them, but it does not replace the reckoning of the Hereafter, where they face the punishment of the Fire.

translation: That is because they opposed Allah and His Messenger. Whoever opposes Allah—indeed, Allah is severe in punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns that deliberately setting oneself against God’s guidance and the Messenger’s mission is a grave matter, carrying consequences that cannot be evaded.

translation: Whatever palm trees you cut down, or left standing on their roots, it was by God’s permission, so that He might disgrace the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: The verse teaches that the believers’ actions in this confrontation—including cutting down some palm trees and leaving others—occurred with God’s authorization, and served His purpose of exposing and humiliating those who defied Him.

translation: Whatever Allah granted His Messenger from them, you drove neither horses nor camels to obtain it. Rather, Allah gives His messengers authority over whomever He wills, and Allah has power over all things.
interpretation: The verse teaches that this gain came not through the Muslims’ military effort but through Allah’s granting of victory. Its allocation was therefore entrusted to the Messenger, underscoring that such outcomes and their disposition are governed by divine wisdom, not merely by the usual rules of battlefield spoils.

translation: Whatever Allah granted His Messenger from the people of the towns belongs to Allah, the Messenger, close relatives, orphans, the needy, and the traveler, so that it does not remain circulating only among the wealthy among you. Whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it. Be mindful of Allah; surely Allah is severe in punishment.
interpretation: The verse establishes that wealth acquired in this way is entrusted for the common good, not reserved for the powerful; its distribution is meant to prevent riches from concentrating among the wealthy. It also makes obedience to the Messenger’s commands and prohibitions part of that trust, binding believers to act justly and remain conscious of accountability before Allah.

translation: It is for the poor emigrants who were driven from their homes and possessions, seeking bounty from Allah and His approval, and supporting Allah and His Messenger. They are the truthful ones.
interpretation: Their sincerity is shown by the cost of their faith: they left behind their homes and wealth, seeking Allah’s favor and remaining steadfast in supporting His Messenger. The verse honors that sacrifice and affirms their truthfulness.

translation: And those who had settled in the home and embraced faith before them love those who emigrated to them. They feel no resentment in their hearts over what the emigrants have been given, and they give them preference over themselves, even when they are in need. Whoever is protected from the greed of their own soul—those are the successful.
interpretation: True faith is shown not only through belief, but through a heart free of envy and possessiveness. The verse presents selfless generosity, even in hardship, as a sign of inner spiritual victory: a person who overcomes the urge to hoard and puts others’ needs before their own attains success.

translation: And those who came after them say, “Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and place no rancor in our hearts toward those who believe. Our Lord, You are truly Most Kind, Most Merciful.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that faith binds believers across generations: those who come later should pray for themselves and for those who believed before them, while asking God to keep their hearts free of resentment toward fellow believers. Such humility and concern for the community reflect trust in God’s tenderness and mercy.

translation: Have you not seen those who hypocrite, saying to their brothers who disbelieved among the People of the Book, “If you are expelled, we will surely leave with you, and we will never obey anyone against you; and if you are fought, we will surely help you”? Allah bears witness that they are truly liars.
interpretation: The verse exposes the hypocrites’ promises of loyalty as deception: they offer support to their allies, but their words cannot be trusted, for Allah knows they will not fulfill them.

translation: If they are expelled, they will not leave with them; and if they are fought, they will not come to their aid. And even if they do come to their aid, they will surely turn their backs; then they will not be helped.
interpretation: The verse exposes the hollow promises of those who pledge support to God’s enemies: when the moment of danger comes, they will abandon them, and neither group will find help or protection.

translation: You inspire greater fear in their hearts than Allah does. That is because they are a people who do not understand.
interpretation: Their fear of people outweighs their awe of Allah because they fail to grasp His power and the consequences of opposing Him.

translation: They will not fight you all together except in fortified towns or from behind walls. Their hostility toward one another is fierce. You think they are united, but their hearts are divided. That is because they are a people who do not reason.
interpretation: Their apparent unity is only outward: fear and mutual distrust keep them behind defenses, while their inner divisions prevent them from acting as one. The verse presents this disunity as a consequence of failing to understand their situation rightly.

translation: Like those shortly before them: they tasted the evil consequences of their deeds, and for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: Their fate is a warning: those who defy God and persist in wrongdoing may face the consequences of their actions in this life, while a painful punishment awaits them in the Hereafter.

translation: Like Satan, when he says to a person, “Disbelieve,” then, when that person disbelieves, he says, “I am free of you. Indeed, I fear Allah, Lord of all worlds.”
interpretation: The verse warns that a tempter may urge someone toward wrongdoing and then abandon them when its consequences arrive. The one who follows such a call cannot excuse their choice by blaming the instigator; each person remains accountable before God.

translation: So the end of them both was that they would be in the Fire, remaining there forever. That is the recompense of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse warns that neither leading someone into wrongdoing nor following that call excuses a person from accountability: those who choose injustice face its consequence, even if one later disowns the other.

translation: O you who believe, be mindful of Allah, and let every soul consider what it has sent ahead for tomorrow. Be mindful of Allah; indeed, Allah is fully aware of what you do.
interpretation: The verse calls believers to examine their deeds honestly and prepare for the Hereafter, as though it were tomorrow. Its repeated command to be mindful of Allah underscores that no deed is hidden from Him, so this self-accounting should guide how one acts.

translation: And do not be like those who forgot Allah, so He made them forget themselves. Those are the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: Forgetting Allah means neglecting His guidance and one’s duties toward Him. As a consequence, they lose sight of what truly benefits their own souls and fail to prepare for their ultimate return to Him; this heedlessness is a mark of disobedience.

translation: The companions of the Fire and the companions of Paradise are not equal. The companions of Paradise are the successful ones.
interpretation: True success is measured by one’s ultimate standing before God, not by worldly status or gain; the verse calls people to recognize the lasting consequence of their choices.

translation: Had We sent down this Qur’an upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled and split apart from fear of Allah. Such examples We set forth for people so that they may reflect.
interpretation: The image invites people to consider the profound weight of the Qur’an’s message: even a mountain is portrayed as yielding before it. Human beings, with the capacity to understand and respond, should therefore let its guidance soften their hearts and prompt serious reflection.

translation: He is Allah; there is no deity except Him, the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed. He is the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse directs the heart to rely on Allah alone: nothing hidden from creation is hidden from Him, and nothing openly seen lies beyond His knowledge. His complete knowledge is joined with compassion and mercy, so turning to Him means seeking guidance and care from the One who knows every circumstance.

translation: He is Allah—there is no deity except Him—the Sovereign, the Holy, the Source of Peace, the Giver of Security, the Guardian, the Almighty, the Compeller, the Supremely Great. Glory be to Allah, far above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: These names teach that every kind of sovereignty, holiness, protection, and might belongs ultimately to Allah alone. Nothing shares His authority or resembles His perfection, so assigning partners to Him diminishes the truth of who He is.

translation: He is Allah, the Creator, the Originator, the Fashioner. To Him belong the most beautiful names. Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Him, and He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: The verse invites us to recognize that the perfection and variety of creation are signs of Allah’s unmatched power and wisdom. Because all things depend on Him and bear witness to His glory, worship and praise belong to Him alone.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. O you who believe, do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies, showing them affection, when they have rejected the truth that has come to you and have driven out the Messenger and you because you believe in Allah, your Lord. If you have gone forth striving in My way and seeking My pleasure, how can you secretly show them affection? I know what you conceal and what you make known. Whoever among you does this has strayed from the straight path.
interpretation: The verse warns believers against giving loyalty or covert support to those actively opposing the faith and persecuting its followers. A claim to strive for God’s cause is inconsistent with secretly assisting such opposition; sincere allegiance to God must shape both outward actions and private intentions, which God knows completely.

translation: If they get the better of you, they will be your enemies, and they will reach out against you with their hands and their tongues in harm, wishing that you would disbelieve.
interpretation: The verse warns that people who harbor hostility toward the believers may seek to harm them both through actions and words, and may hope to turn them away from faith; it cautions against trusting such hostility merely because it is not always openly expressed.

translation: Your relatives and your children will never benefit you. On the Day of Resurrection, He will judge between you, and Allah sees all that you do.
interpretation: Family ties cannot save anyone from accountability before Allah. What ultimately matters is one’s faith and deeds, all of which Allah sees; on the Day of Resurrection, He will distinguish and judge between people with perfect justice.

translation: There is indeed an excellent example for you in Abraham and those with him, when they said to their people, “We disown you and whatever you worship besides Allah. We reject you, and between us and you there has arisen enmity and hatred forever, until you believe in Allah alone”—except for Abraham’s words to his father, “I will surely ask forgiveness for you, though I have no power to do anything for you before Allah.” They said, “Our Lord, in You we place our trust; to You we turn in repentance, and to You is the final return.”
interpretation: The example is one of unwavering devotion to Allah: faith requires refusing to endorse the worship of anything besides Him, even when that brings estrangement from one’s community. Abraham’s promise to seek forgiveness for his father is expressly excepted, so it is not a model for maintaining allegiance to those who oppose faith; the believers instead entrust their affairs to Allah, turn back to Him, and remember that all return to Him.

translation: Our Lord, do not make us a trial for those who disbelieve, and forgive us, our Lord. You are indeed the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: They ask God not to let the disbelievers’ treatment or eventual fate become a means of misleading them—such as their taking victory over the believers as proof that their beliefs are true—and they seek forgiveness, trusting in God’s power and wisdom.

translation: There is certainly an excellent example for you in them—for whoever hopes in Allah and the Last Day. And whoever turns away, then surely Allah is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: The conduct of Abraham and those who believed with him is held up as a model of steadfast faith: their loyalty to Allah took precedence over allegiance to those who opposed Him. Those who hope for Allah’s approval and the Hereafter should follow that example; anyone who turns away does not diminish Allah in any way, for He is utterly self-sufficient and worthy of all praise.

translation: Perhaps Allah will bring about affection between you and those among them with whom you have been hostile. Allah is All-Powerful, and Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.
