interpretation: The verse offers hope that hostility can give way to affection by Allah’s will. No enmity is beyond His power to transform, and His forgiveness and mercy leave room for people to turn from conflict toward reconciliation.

translation: Allah does not forbid you from treating with kindness and justice those who have not fought you on account of religion or driven you from your homes. Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly.
interpretation: This teaches that religious difference alone is no reason to withhold kindness or fairness. When people do not persecute or forcibly displace you, you should treat them with goodness and justice; such conduct is beloved to God.

translation: Allah only forbids you from taking as allies those who fought you because of your faith, drove you from your homes, or helped drive you out. Whoever takes them as allies—those are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse makes allegiance to hostile oppressors the issue: loyalty that supports those attacking believers and dispossessing them is a grave injustice. Its restriction to such aggressors also distinguishes them from people who do not fight or expel the believers.

translation: O you who believe, when believing women come to you as emigrants, examine them. God knows best their faith. If you find them to be believers, do not send them back to the disbelievers: they are not lawful for them, nor are the disbelievers lawful for them. Give their former husbands what they had spent. There is no blame on you if you marry them after giving them their bridal gifts. Do not retain the marriage bonds of disbelieving women; ask for what you spent, and let them ask for what they spent. That is God’s judgment; He judges between you. God is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: The verse addresses a specific situation in which women were leaving hostile communities and seeking refuge among the believers. Its rulings guard their freedom to follow their faith while requiring fairness toward the spouses left behind through repayment of marital expenses. The instruction to examine the women calls for care in discerning their circumstances, while the reminder that God knows their faith best warns against claiming certainty about what lies within their hearts. The closing attributes the judgment to God’s knowledge and wisdom, framing these measures as justice in a difficult communal and family conflict.

translation: And if any of your wives have gone over to the disbelievers, and then you gain spoils, give those whose wives have gone away the equivalent of what they had spent. And be mindful of Allah, in whom you believe.
interpretation: The verse establishes a measure of fairness for believers whose wives had departed to the opposing community: if the community later obtained resources from them, it was to compensate those husbands for what they had spent. The instruction to be mindful of Allah grounds this obligation in faith and calls for justice even amid conflict.

translation: O Prophet, when believing women come to you pledging that they will associate nothing with Allah, steal nothing, commit no adultery, kill none of their children, bring forth no slander they have fabricated between their hands and feet, and disobey you in nothing that is right, then accept their pledge and ask Allah to forgive them. Surely Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: The pledge binds faith to integrity in both private and public life: it rejects idolatry, theft, sexual wrongdoing, harm to children, and fabricated accusations—including false claims about a child’s parentage. The command to obey the Prophet is expressly limited to what is right, showing that obedience is not a license for wrongdoing. His acceptance of their pledge and prayer for their forgiveness also reflect the door to repentance and divine mercy.

translation: O you who believe, do not take as allies a people upon whom Allah has brought His anger. They have despaired of the Hereafter, just as the disbelievers have despaired of those in the graves.
interpretation: The verse warns believers against aligning themselves with those who reject the Hereafter and have incurred Allah’s anger. Their despair reflects a denial that the dead will be raised, like the disbelievers’ despair concerning those in the graves.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Allah; and He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: All creation bears witness to Allah’s perfection and freedom from every flaw, each in the way He has ordained. His might is absolute, and His wise ordering of creation ensures that nothing is beyond His power or purpose.

translation: O you who believe, why do you say what you do not do?
interpretation: Faith calls for integrity: a believer’s words should be matched by sincere effort and action. The verse warns against making promises or claiming virtues without striving to live by them.

translation: How hateful it is in the sight of Allah that you say what you do not do.
interpretation: The verse warns that claiming virtues or commitments without living by them is a grave failure of sincerity; faithfulness requires one’s actions to accord with one’s words.

translation: Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in ranks, as though they were a firmly bonded structure.
interpretation: The verse portrays steadfast unity and disciplined solidarity among those striving in God’s cause: like a tightly joined structure, they support one another and stand together with resolve.

translation: And [remember] when Moses said to his people, “O my people, why do you hurt me, though you know that I am Allah’s Messenger to you?” Then, when they turned away, Allah caused their hearts to turn away. And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.
interpretation: The verse warns that knowingly resisting a messenger and persisting in wrongdoing can harden a person’s heart: when people choose to turn from guidance, Allah leaves them to the misguidance they have chosen, and they are not granted guidance while they persist in disobedience.

translation: And [remember] when Jesus, son of Mary, said, “O Children of Israel, I am indeed God’s messenger to you, confirming what came before me of the Torah and giving good news of a messenger who will come after me, whose name is Ahmad.” But when he came to them with clear proofs, they said, “This is unmistakable magic.”
interpretation: The verse presents divine guidance as a continuous message: Jesus affirms the revelation given before him and points toward a messenger yet to come. It also warns that clear evidence does not always overcome unwillingness to accept the truth; people may dismiss what challenges them rather than consider it honestly.

translation: Who is more unjust than one who invents lies about Allah while being called to Islam? Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: The verse condemns the grave injustice of attributing falsehood to God even as one is invited to submit to Him. Persisting in such wrongdoing closes a person off from guidance; it is not a fault in the guidance itself, but a consequence of rejecting it.

translation: They wish to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah will perfect His light, even though the disbelievers dislike it.
interpretation: The verse teaches that people may try to undermine God’s guidance through their words, but their opposition cannot prevent Him from bringing His light to completion.

translation: He is the One who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, so that He may make it prevail over every religion, even though the polytheists dislike it.
interpretation: God sent the Messenger with guidance and the true way of worship, and He will make its truth and message manifest despite the opposition of those who reject it.

translation: O you who believe, shall I guide you to a trade that will save you from a painful punishment?
interpretation: The verse presents faith and obedience to God as a priceless “trade”: unlike worldly bargains, it leads to lasting salvation. Its inviting question calls believers to recognize the value of this path and respond to it wholeheartedly.

translation: Believe in Allah and His Messenger, and strive in the way of Allah with your wealth and your lives. That is better for you, if you only knew.
interpretation: The verse presents sincere faith as something expressed through committed action and sacrifice in God’s cause. It teaches that devotion involving both one’s resources and one’s personal effort is ultimately better for the believer, even when its value is not immediately apparent.

translation: He will forgive you your sins and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow, and to goodly dwellings in gardens of everlasting residence. That is the supreme triumph.
interpretation: The verse presents true success as God’s forgiveness and lasting nearness to Him: not merely escaping punishment, but being granted a secure and joyful home that endures.

translation: And another [favor] that you love: help from Allah and a near victory. And give glad tidings to the believers.
interpretation: The verse reassures believers that their faithfulness will be met with Allah’s support and a victory soon to come, giving them reason to remain steadfast and hopeful.

translation: O you who believe, be helpers of Allah, as Jesus son of Mary said to the disciples, “Who will be my helpers in the cause of Allah?” The disciples said, “We are helpers of Allah.” Then a group of the Children of Israel believed and a group disbelieved. So We strengthened those who believed against their enemy, and they became dominant.
interpretation: To be a helper of Allah is to uphold His religion and truth—not because Allah needs help, but by answering the call to faith with loyal action, as the disciples did. The verse encourages believers to remain steadfast when opposed, trusting that Allah can strengthen those who stand for the truth and grant them the upper hand.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah—the Sovereign, the Most Holy, the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: All creation declares Allah’s perfection, whether through conscious praise or by its very existence and order. His sovereignty is absolute, His holiness free of every imperfection, His power unconquerable, and His wisdom evident in all that He decrees and creates.

translation: He is the One who sent among the unlettered people a messenger from among themselves, reciting to them His revelations, purifying them, and teaching them the Book and wisdom, though before that they had indeed been in clear misguidance.
interpretation: The verse presents prophethood as a gift that transforms people from within their own community. The messenger’s mission is more than conveying words: revelation cultivates moral and spiritual purity, while teaching gives people guidance and wisdom to live by. Their former misguidance underscores how profoundly divine guidance can change a society.

translation: And [He has sent him to] others among them who have not yet joined them. And He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: The Prophet’s mission extends beyond those who lived in his time to later generations who would follow them, showing that divine guidance is not confined to one era. Allah brings this about through His power and perfect wisdom.

translation: That is Allah’s favor; He grants it to whom He wills. And Allah is the Possessor of immense favor.
interpretation: The verse teaches that divine favor is bestowed by Allah according to His wisdom, not something people can claim as their own entitlement. His generosity is vast, so believers should receive His gifts with gratitude and humility.

translation: The example of those who were entrusted with the Torah but then did not uphold it is like that of a donkey carrying books. How awful is the example of people who deny God’s signs. God does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: The verse warns that possessing sacred knowledge is not enough: if people fail to understand and live by what they have been entrusted with, their knowledge benefits them no more than books benefit an animal carrying them. It condemns rejecting God’s signs and neglecting the responsibility that comes with guidance.

translation: Say, “O you who are Jews, if you claim that you are God’s allies to the exclusion of other people, then wish for death, if you are truthful.”
interpretation: The verse challenges the claim of exclusive nearness to God: if they were truly certain of their favored standing with Him, they would not fear meeting Him through death. Their reluctance would reveal that the claim was not sincere.

translation: But they will never wish for it because of what their hands have sent ahead; and Allah knows the wrongdoers.
interpretation: Their refusal to wish for death reveals that they know their deeds leave them no confidence in meeting God. “What their hands have sent ahead” means the wrongdoing they have committed, and God’s knowledge of it exposes the truth of their claims.

translation: Say, “The death from which you flee will surely meet you. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do.”
interpretation: The verse challenges the illusion that avoiding thoughts of death can free a person from accountability. Since every deed is known to God, awareness of death should lead one to live responsibly rather than evade the consequences of one’s choices.

translation: O you who believe, when the call to prayer is made on Friday, hasten to the remembrance of God and leave off trade. That is better for you, if only you knew.
interpretation: The verse teaches believers to give God’s remembrance priority when the Friday prayer is called, setting aside worldly transactions so they can attend with due attention. This obedience is for their own good, even when its wisdom may not be immediately apparent.

translation: When the prayer has been concluded, disperse through the land, seek the bounty of Allah, and remember Allah often so that you may succeed.
interpretation: The verse teaches that devotion to Allah should shape both worship and everyday life: after prayer, one may pursue lawful provision, while keeping Allah in frequent remembrance. Success lies in joining worldly effort with spiritual mindfulness.

translation: When they see a trade or some amusement, they rush toward it and leave you standing. Say, “What is with Allah is better than amusement and trade, and Allah is the best of providers.”
interpretation: The verse warns against letting immediate worldly attractions distract from worship and guidance. Its deeper reassurance is that honoring what Allah commands does not diminish one’s provision: true and lasting good comes from Him, so devotion should take precedence over passing gain or entertainment.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. When the hypocrites come to you, they say, “We testify that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah.” Allah knows that you are indeed His Messenger, and Allah bears witness that the hypocrites are surely lying.
interpretation: Their words about the Prophet’s messengership are true, but their claim to believe is false: they utter the testimony while concealing disbelief. The verse therefore exposes the gap between a truthful statement and a dishonest heart.

translation: They have made their oaths a shield, and so they turn people away from the path of Allah. Truly evil is what they have been doing.
interpretation: The verse warns that invoking God or making solemn promises can become a disguise for insincerity when used to protect wrongdoing and obstruct others from guidance. Such conduct corrupts the trust that oaths are meant to uphold and is condemned by God.

translation: That is because they believed, then disbelieved, so their hearts were sealed; therefore they do not understand.
interpretation: Their initial profession of faith followed by rejection hardened their hearts, leaving them unable to recognize or grasp the truth.

translation: When you see them, their appearance impresses you; and if they speak, you listen to what they say. They are like propped-up pieces of timber. They think every shout is directed against them. They are the enemy, so beware of them. May Allah destroy them! How are they turned away?
interpretation: The verse warns against being deceived by an impressive exterior or persuasive speech: these people appear substantial, yet are inwardly empty and driven by suspicion and fear. Their outward appeal does not make their hostility any less real, so vigilance is required.

translation: And when it is said to them, “Come, the Messenger of Allah will ask forgiveness for you,” they turn their heads aside, and you see them turning away in arrogance.
interpretation: Their refusal to seek the Messenger’s prayer for forgiveness reveals a pride that prevents them from acknowledging their wrongdoing and turning sincerely toward God.

translation: It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; Allah will never forgive them. Indeed, Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.
interpretation: This refers to those who persist in hypocrisy and deliberate defiance: the Prophet’s plea for forgiveness cannot benefit them while they remain committed to rejecting the truth. Their refusal to turn back from disobedience is why they are left without divine guidance.

translation: They are the ones who say, “Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse.” Yet to Allah belong the treasures of the heavens and the earth, but the hypocrites do not understand.
interpretation: The verse exposes the hypocrites’ attempt to weaken the believers by cutting off their support. They wrongly believe that controlling people’s resources gives them control over the community, failing to recognize that all provision ultimately belongs to Allah.

translation: They say, “If we return to Medina, the more honored will surely drive out the more humble.” Yet all honor belongs to Allah, His Messenger, and the believers, but the hypocrites do not know.
interpretation: The hypocrites mistake worldly influence for true honor and presume they can force the believers out. The verse teaches that lasting dignity and authority belong to Allah and are granted to His Messenger and the believers, while the hypocrites’ boast reveals their ignorance of where true honor lies.

translation: O you who believe, do not let your wealth or your children distract you from the remembrance of Allah. Whoever does so—those are the losers.
interpretation: The verse warns that even cherished responsibilities and blessings can become a spiritual trial if they take precedence over devotion to God. Its warning of loss points to the deeper harm of allowing worldly attachments to draw a person away from the source of faith and guidance.

translation: And spend from what We have provided you before death comes to one of you, and he says, “My Lord, if only You would grant me a brief delay, so that I might give charity and be among the righteous.”
interpretation: The verse warns against postponing generosity and righteous action until a moment of regret. What a person has is entrusted by God, and the opportunity to use it well lasts only until death; therefore, sincere obedience must begin while there is still time.

translation: And Allah will never delay a soul once its appointed time has come. And Allah is fully aware of what you do.
interpretation: The verse warns against assuming that one can postpone turning toward God indefinitely: every life has a fixed term, and no one can extend it once it arrives. Since God knows all that people do, they should use the time they have to act faithfully and sincerely.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. All that is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Allah. To Him belongs all dominion and all praise, and He has power over all things.
interpretation: The whole of creation, whether or not its praise is audible to us, declares Allah’s perfection. Since everything belongs to Him and depends on His power, He alone is ultimately worthy of worship and praise.

translation: He is the One who created you; yet among you are those who disbelieve and those who believe. And Allah sees all that you do.
interpretation: The verse reminds people that although all are created by Allah, they differ in how they respond to faith. Their choices and deeds are fully known to Him, so each person remains accountable for how they live.

translation: He created the heavens and the earth in truth, fashioned you and made your forms beautiful; and to Him is the final return.
interpretation: Creation is purposeful, not without meaning: the beauty and form granted to human beings are signs of divine wisdom, while the return to God reminds them that their lives are accountable to Him.

translation: He knows what is in the heavens and the earth, and He knows what you conceal and what you make known. And Allah knows what is within hearts.
interpretation: Nothing is hidden from God—not private words or actions, nor the intentions and thoughts behind them. This invites a person to be sincere, knowing that God’s judgment encompasses both outward deeds and what lies within the heart.

translation: Has the account of those who disbelieved before you not reached you? They tasted the evil consequences of their deeds, and a painful punishment awaits them.
interpretation: The verse warns that rejecting faith has consequences both in this life and the next. The fate of earlier disbelieving peoples is presented as a lesson: their suffering should prompt people to heed the warning rather than repeat their denial.

translation: That was because their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they said, “Are human beings to guide us?” So they disbelieved and turned away. And Allah had no need of them; Allah is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy.
interpretation: They rejected the messengers not for lack of clear evidence, but because they objected to being guided by people like themselves. Their refusal harmed only themselves: Allah needs nothing from them, while He alone deserves praise.

translation: Those who disbelieve claim that they will never be resurrected. Say, “Yes indeed, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected, then you will surely be told what you did. And that is easy for Allah.”
interpretation: The verse answers denial of the Resurrection with a solemn oath: every person will be raised and confronted with the truth of their deeds. Bringing creation back to life and holding it to account is no difficulty for Allah.

translation: So believe in Allah, His Messenger, and the Light that We have sent down. And Allah is fully aware of what you do.
interpretation: The “Light” refers to the revelation that guides people out of spiritual darkness. The verse calls for sincere faith in Allah, His Messenger, and that guidance, reminding people that their actions are known to Allah.

translation: On the Day He gathers you for the Day of Gathering—that is the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain. Whoever believes in Allah and does righteous deeds, He will erase their misdeeds and admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, to remain there forever. That is the great triumph.
interpretation: The final gathering will make clear what truly counted as gain or loss: worldly appearances will give way to the lasting outcome of each person’s choices. Allah’s promise is that sincere faith joined with righteous action brings forgiveness for sins and an eternal home of reward.

translation: As for those who disbelieve and deny Our signs, they are the companions of the Fire, remaining there forever. What a wretched destination.
interpretation: The verse warns that rejecting God’s signs is not a harmless refusal: it leads to lasting separation from His mercy. Calling the Fire a “wretched destination” underscores the gravity of that outcome and urges people to heed the signs before reaching it.

translation: No calamity befalls except by Allah’s permission. Whoever believes in Allah, He guides their heart. And Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: Faith enables a person facing hardship to find steadiness and guidance in the heart, trusting that what occurs is within Allah’s knowledge and decree.

translation: Obey Allah and obey the Messenger. But if you turn away, Our Messenger is responsible only for conveying the message clearly.
interpretation: The verse makes clear that the Messenger’s duty is to deliver Allah’s message plainly; people remain responsible for whether they heed it, and turning away does not lessen that responsibility.

translation: Allah—there is no deity except Him. So let the believers place their trust in Allah.
interpretation: Because Allah alone is worthy of worship and possesses ultimate power, believers should entrust their affairs to Him, relying on Him while seeking His help rather than depending ultimately on anything else.

translation: O you who believe, indeed, among your spouses and your children are enemies to you, so be wary of them. But if you pardon, overlook, and forgive, then surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: The warning concerns family members who may, through their demands or pressure, turn a believer away from faith and duty; it is not a judgment that spouses or children are inherently hostile. Believers should guard their commitments while meeting family tensions with pardon and mercy.

translation: Your wealth and your children are only a trial, and with Allah is a great reward.
interpretation: This verse cautions that love of wealth and family can test whether a person remains faithful and obedient to God. These blessings should be cherished without letting attachment to them distract from what is right; the lasting reward is with God.

translation: So be mindful of Allah as much as you are able, listen and obey, and spend; that is better for yourselves. Whoever is protected from the stinginess of their own soul—those are the successful.
interpretation: The verse teaches that devotion is measured by sincere effort within one’s capacity, and that faith should lead to obedient responsiveness and generosity. True success comes when a person is freed from the self’s grasping impulses and gives for the sake of what is right.

translation: If you lend Allah a good loan, He will multiply it for you and forgive you. And Allah is Appreciative, Forbearing.
interpretation: Giving sincerely for Allah’s sake is described as a loan—not because Allah needs anything, but to honor the giver and assure them of a return far beyond what they give. Allah rewards such generosity and may forgive sins, while His being Appreciative means no sincere good deed is overlooked, and His being Forbearing means He does not hasten to punish.

translation: Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: God’s knowledge encompasses all that is hidden and all that is manifest. His power is absolute, and His judgments and actions are governed by perfect wisdom.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them at the beginning of their waiting period, and keep count of the waiting period. Be mindful of Allah, your Lord. Do not turn them out of their homes, nor should they leave, unless they commit a manifest immorality. These are the limits set by Allah. Whoever transgresses Allah’s limits has wronged himself. You do not know; perhaps Allah will bring about something new after that.
interpretation: The verse teaches that divorce must be carried out with care and within the boundaries Allah has set, rather than in a way that makes reconciliation impossible or causes needless harm. Keeping the woman in her home during the waiting period preserves her security and leaves room for circumstances—and hearts—to change. Its warning is that people should not assume they know what the future holds, but act with restraint and reverence for God’s limits.

translation: When they have nearly reached the end of their waiting period, either retain them honorably or part from them honorably. And call two just people from among you to witness, and uphold the testimony for Allah. This is an admonition for whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day. Whoever is mindful of Allah, He will make a way out for them.
interpretation: The verse teaches that divorce must be handled with fairness and reverence for God: a spouse must not be retained to cause harm, nor dismissed unjustly, and witnesses help protect everyone’s rights. Its closing promise encourages mindfulness of God’s limits even in painful circumstances, assuring that He can open a way through hardship.

translation: And He provides for him from where he does not expect. Whoever puts his trust in Allah, He is sufficient for him. Surely Allah brings His purpose to completion; Allah has set a measure for everything.
interpretation: The verse teaches that a believer may entrust their affairs to Allah even when the outcome or means of provision is unseen. Such trust rests on the assurance that Allah’s will is carried out, and that events unfold according to the measure He has appointed.

translation: As for those of your women who no longer menstruate—if you are uncertain—their waiting period is three months, and likewise for those who have not menstruated. As for pregnant women, their term ends when they deliver their burden. Whoever is mindful of God, He makes ease for them in their affairs.
interpretation: The verse presents divine guidance as attentive to differing circumstances, while grounding the observance of its rulings in mindfulness of God. Its closing assurance teaches that such mindfulness brings God-given ease amid the matters a person must navigate.

translation: That is Allah’s command, which He has sent down to you. Whoever is mindful of Allah, He will erase his misdeeds and greatly increase his reward.
interpretation: The verse teaches that reverent awareness of Allah is shown by taking His revealed guidance seriously. When a person strives to live by it, Allah, in His mercy, removes the burden of their wrongs and grants them a reward greater than their deeds alone could earn.

translation: House them where you live, according to your means, and do not harm them in order to make life difficult for them. If they are pregnant, provide for them until they give birth. If they nurse the child for you, give them their due payment, and consult one another in a fair manner. But if you cannot agree, then another woman may nurse the child.
interpretation: The verse frames separation not as permission to punish or pressure a former spouse, but as a situation in which justice and the child’s welfare must still govern. Its call to fair consultation recognizes both parents’ responsibilities while leaving room for a practical alternative when agreement cannot be reached.

translation: Let the one who has ample means spend according to his means, and let the one whose provision is restricted spend from what Allah has given him. Allah does not burden any soul beyond what He has given it. Allah will bring ease after hardship.
interpretation: In the context of family support, this verse teaches that financial duties must be fulfilled fairly according to a person’s actual means—not by imposing an impossible burden or withholding what one can reasonably provide. Its reassurance that hardship will be followed by ease encourages patience and trust in Allah while people meet their responsibilities as best they can.

translation: How many a town defied the command of its Lord and His messengers! So We called it to a severe account and punished it with a terrible punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns that communities that arrogantly reject God’s guidance are not beyond accountability: their worldly power or apparent security cannot shield them from the consequences of persistent defiance.

translation: So it tasted the evil consequence of its conduct, and the outcome of its affair was loss.
interpretation: The verse warns that turning away from God’s guidance brings consequences that may culminate in complete loss; no community is beyond accountability for its choices.

translation: Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment. So be mindful of Allah, O people of understanding who have believed. Allah has sent down to you a Reminder.
interpretation: The warning is meant to awaken believers to the seriousness of rejecting God’s guidance. Those granted understanding should respond to the Reminder Allah has sent by remaining mindful of Him and following its guidance, rather than assuming that faith alone makes heedfulness unnecessary.

translation: A Messenger reciting to you the clear verses of Allah, so that he may bring those who believe and do righteous deeds out of darkness into light. Whoever believes in Allah and does righteous deeds, He will admit into gardens beneath which rivers flow, to remain there forever. Allah has indeed provided him with an excellent provision.
interpretation: The Messenger’s recitation is a means by which divine guidance frees people from the many forms of spiritual darkness and leads them toward faith and righteous living. The promise of lasting Paradise shows that this guidance culminates in a reward bestowed by Allah’s generosity.

translation: Allah is the One who created seven heavens, and of the earth their like. His command descends among them, so that you may know that Allah has power over all things and that Allah encompasses all things in knowledge.
interpretation: The ordered creation of the heavens and earth, and the command that governs them, is a sign calling people to recognize that nothing lies beyond Allah’s power or outside His knowledge.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. O Prophet, why do you forbid yourself what Allah has made lawful for you, seeking to please your wives? Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse gently teaches that one should not treat something Allah has made lawful as forbidden merely to satisfy others. Its closing names Allah’s forgiveness and mercy, underscoring that this admonition is given with compassion.

translation: Allah has prescribed for you a way to release yourselves from your oaths. Allah is your Protector, and He is the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.
interpretation: The verse teaches that an oath need not become an unbreakable burden: God has provided a lawful means of release, including its prescribed expiation. His knowledge and wisdom guide this provision, and His protection assures believers that His rulings are made for their good.

translation: And when the Prophet confided a matter to one of his wives, and she disclosed it, Allah made it known to him. He made known part of it and passed over part. When he told her of it, she asked, “Who informed you of this?” He said, “The All-Knowing, the All-Aware informed me.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that no private conversation is hidden from Allah, who disclosed what had been confided to the Prophet. It also shows the Prophet’s restraint: he addressed what needed to be addressed without exposing everything that had been revealed to him.

translation: If you two turn to Allah in repentance, then your hearts have indeed inclined [from what is right]. But if you support one another against him, then Allah is his Protector, and Gabriel and the righteous among the believers; and after that, the angels are his supporters.
interpretation: The verse addresses two of the Prophet’s wives, urging them to repent and set right what had gone astray in their conduct. It warns that any united opposition to the Prophet cannot prevail against him, for Allah is his protector, with Gabriel, the righteous believers, and the angels supporting him.

translation: It may be that, if he divorces you, his Lord will give him in your place wives better than you: women who submit to God, believe, are devoutly obedient, repent, worship, fast, and are previously married or virgins.
interpretation: The verse warns that no one’s position is guaranteed by closeness to the Prophet; what matters is sincere faith and obedience to God. It presents repentance, worship, and devotion as the qualities by which a person is truly better.

translation: O you who believe, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is people and stones, over which are angels, stern and powerful, who do not disobey Allah in what He commands them and do whatever they are commanded.
interpretation: Belief entails responsibility for one’s own conduct and for guiding one’s family toward what pleases Allah. This protection is sought through obedience, avoiding wrongdoing, and teaching and encouraging one another toward faith and good deeds. The description of the angels emphasizes that the punishment is carried out with complete obedience to Allah’s command.

translation: O you who disbelieved, make no excuses today. You are only being recompensed for what you used to do.
interpretation: The verse portrays the certainty of accountability in the Hereafter: once judgment has come, excuses cannot undo the consequences of one’s choices and deeds.

translation: O you who believe, turn to God in sincere repentance. It may be that your Lord will erase your misdeeds and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow, on the Day when God will not disgrace the Prophet and those who believed with him. Their light will shine before them and on their right, and they will say, “Our Lord, perfect our light for us and forgive us. Surely You have power over all things.”
interpretation: Sincere repentance is a wholehearted return to God, not merely regretful words: it entails leaving wrongdoing and seeking to live faithfully. The verse joins this effort with hope in God’s mercy, while its image of believers asking for their light to be completed shows that even on the Day of Judgment they depend on God for guidance, forgiveness, and salvation.

translation: O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be firm with them. Their refuge is Hell—what a wretched destination.
interpretation: The verse calls the Prophet to confront rejection and hypocrisy with resolve, using the appropriate means for each, and warns that those who persist in them face divine judgment. It is a charge to the Prophet, not a license for individuals to act on their own.

translation: Allah sets forth an example for those who disbelieve: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot. They were married to two of Our righteous servants, but they betrayed them, and they could not protect them from Allah in any way. It was said, “Enter the Fire with those who enter.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that neither family ties nor closeness to a righteous person can substitute for faith and obedience to God. The betrayal described is understood as betrayal of their husbands’ religious cause, not sexual infidelity.

translation: And Allah presents as an example for those who believe the wife of Pharaoh, when she said, “My Lord, build for me near You a house in Paradise, save me from Pharaoh and his deeds, and save me from the wrongdoing people.”
interpretation: Her prayer shows that true faith is not determined by one’s surroundings or worldly position. Though she lived in Pharaoh’s household, she sought closeness to God above its power and comforts, asking to be freed from tyranny and from complicity in evil.

translation: And Mary, daughter of ʿImrān, who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into her of Our spirit; she affirmed the words of her Lord and His scriptures, and was among the devoutly obedient.
interpretation: Mary is presented as an example of steadfast faith and devotion: she guarded her chastity and trusted God through an extraordinary divine decree, affirming His revelation and remaining obedient to Him.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Blessed is He in whose hand is all dominion, and He has power over all things.
interpretation: The verse teaches that God’s authority is absolute and that nothing lies beyond His power. Recognizing this calls a person to trust in Him and to approach life with humility, knowing that all affairs ultimately rest with Him.

translation: He is the One who created death and life to test which of you is best in deeds. He is the Almighty, the All-Forgiving.
interpretation: Life and death mark out a purposeful trial in which deeds are weighed by their goodness, not merely their number. God’s might makes the trial and its judgment just, while His forgiveness leaves room for those who turn back to Him.

translation: He is the One who created seven heavens in layers. You will see no imperfection in the creation of the Most Merciful. Look again: do you see any flaw?
interpretation: The verse invites us to reflect carefully on the heavens: repeated scrutiny reveals no defect or disorder in their creation, directing the heart to recognize the wisdom and perfection of the Most Merciful.

translation: Then turn your gaze back again and again; your gaze will return to you humbled and weary.
interpretation: No matter how persistently you search for a flaw in the heavens, your effort will end in humble recognition that you cannot find one.

translation: We have indeed adorned the nearest heaven with lamps, made them missiles against the devils, and prepared for them the punishment of the Blaze.
interpretation: The verse presents the heavens as a display of divine beauty and power, while affirming that rebellious devils remain subject to God’s authority and will face His punishment.

translation: For those who disbelieve in their Lord is the punishment of Hell—how wretched a destination!
interpretation: The verse presents disbelief as a choice with lasting consequences, warning that turning away from one’s Lord leads to an ultimately ruinous end.

translation: When they are thrown into it, they hear it roaring as it boils.
interpretation: The vivid sound and motion portray Hell as terrifying and overwhelming, warning that rejecting the truth has consequences too dreadful to take lightly.

translation: It almost bursts with rage. Whenever a group is cast into it, its keepers ask them, “Did no warner come to you?”
interpretation: The verse portrays Hell as so terrifying that it seems ready to split apart in fury, while its keepers’ question confronts its inhabitants with the fact that they had been warned. It emphasizes the seriousness of rejecting guidance and the accountability that follows.

translation: They will say, “Yes, a warner did come to us, but we rejected him and said, ‘Allah has sent down nothing; you are only in great error.’”
interpretation: The verse portrays the people acknowledging too late that they had received a warning. Their admission exposes how they rejected the messenger and turned their own accusation of error against him; their punishment follows from knowingly refusing the warning, not from never having been given one.

translation: And they will say, “If only we had listened or reasoned, we would not be among the companions of the Blaze.”
interpretation: The verse portrays a regret that comes too late: deliverance required more than merely hearing words—it required taking guidance seriously and reflecting on its truth before consequences became unavoidable.

translation: So they will confess their sin. Away with the inhabitants of the Blaze!
interpretation: Their confession comes only after the truth has become undeniable, when it can no longer avert the consequence; “away with” conveys their being cast far from mercy.

translation: Indeed, those who fear their Lord though unseen will have forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: True reverence is shown in private, when no one else is watching. Those who remain mindful of God in unseen moments are promised His forgiveness and a reward beyond measure.

translation: Whether you conceal your words or speak them openly, He surely knows what is within the hearts.
interpretation: No thought or intention is hidden from God, even when a person’s words are kept private; this calls for sincerity before Him, rather than relying on outward silence to conceal what is within.

translation: Does He who created not know, while He is the Most Subtle, the All-Aware?
interpretation: The verse teaches that the One who brought every being into existence cannot be unaware of any part of its reality. His knowledge reaches what is hidden as well as what is apparent, and His subtle wisdom encompasses every detail.

translation: He is the One who made the earth manageable for you, so travel through its regions and eat of His provision; and to Him you will be resurrected.
interpretation: The verse invites people to make responsible use of the opportunities and resources available to them, while recognizing that their efforts do not make them independent of God. Its closing reminder places worldly striving within the larger reality of returning to God, where human choices will matter.

translation: Do you feel secure that the One above the heavens will not cause the earth to swallow you, as it suddenly convulses?
interpretation: The verse challenges people’s complacency: the ground they take for granted is not beyond God’s power to overturn. It calls them to humility and to recognize their dependence on Him.

translation: Or do you feel secure that the One who is in heaven will not send upon you a storm of stones? Then you will know how true My warning is.
interpretation: The verse warns against mistaking a reprieve for safety from God’s power. It calls people to take the warning seriously before a punishment arrives and leaves no room for denial.

translation: Those before them also denied, so how severe was My retribution!
interpretation: The verse warns that persistent denial does not escape God’s judgment: the fate of earlier peoples stands as a stark reminder of the severity of His punishment.

translation: Have they not looked at the birds above them, spreading their wings and folding them? None holds them aloft except the Most Compassionate. Indeed, He sees all things.
interpretation: The birds’ flight is a sign that creation is sustained by God’s care and governed with perfect knowledge; what appears effortless in nature depends on His sustaining power.

translation: Or who is there that could be an army for you, helping you apart from the Most Merciful? The disbelievers are only in delusion.
interpretation: The verse challenges those who place their trust in powers or protectors apart from God: none can independently shield them from His will. Believing otherwise is a false sense of security.

translation: Or who is it that could provide for you if He withheld His provision? Yet they persist in arrogance and aversion.
interpretation: The verse challenges people to recognize that no one can replace God as the source of provision; their continued defiance despite this dependence reflects a stubborn refusal to turn toward Him.

translation: Is one who walks with his face cast down better guided, or one who walks upright on a straight path?
interpretation: The verse portrays the confusion of someone turned away from divine guidance: like a person stumbling face-first, they cannot see where they are going. By contrast, the one guided by God can move upright with clarity and direction. The question is rhetorical, affirming that true guidance lies in following the straight path.

translation: Say, “He is the One who brought you into being and gave you hearing, sight, and hearts. Little gratitude you show.”
interpretation: The verse calls people to recognize that their ability to hear, see, and understand is a gift from God, and to use these faculties with gratitude rather than heedlessness.

translation: Say, “He is the One who spread you throughout the earth, and to Him you will be gathered.”
interpretation: Humanity’s dispersal across the earth is part of God’s creation, not a departure from His care. The promise of being gathered to Him means earthly life is not the final end: every person will return to God, where their deeds will be brought to account.

translation: And they say, “When will this promise come to pass, if you are truthful?”
interpretation: They challenge the messengers with a demand for the promised reckoning to arrive, using its delay as a taunt rather than a sincere search for guidance.

translation: Say, “Knowledge is only with Allah, and I am only a clear warner.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that ultimate knowledge of what is hidden belongs to Allah alone. The Messenger’s role is to convey the warning plainly, not to claim knowledge that Allah has kept to Himself.

translation: Then, when they see it drawing near, the faces of those who disbelieved will be stricken with distress, and it will be said, “This is what you used to call for.”
interpretation: The verse depicts the moment when the punishment they denied becomes unmistakably near: their confidence gives way to anguish, and their former demands to see it brought about are answered with a reminder that it is now before them.

translation: Say, “Have you considered: if Allah causes me and those with me to perish, or has mercy on us, who will protect the disbelievers from a painful punishment?”
interpretation: The verse challenges the disbelievers to recognize that the Prophet’s fate does not determine their own: whether he and the believers perish or are spared, no one can shield those who reject the truth from Allah’s punishment.

translation: Say, “He is the Most Compassionate. We believe in Him, and in Him we place our trust. You will soon know who is in clear error.”
interpretation: The verse affirms that true security rests in faith in the Most Compassionate and reliance upon Him, even when that faith is challenged. The warning leaves the final judgment to what time will make evident: who was truly guided and who had gone plainly astray.

translation: Say, “Have you considered: if your water were to sink deep into the earth, who could bring you flowing water?”
interpretation: The verse calls people to recognize how completely their lives depend on blessings they cannot secure for themselves. Even something as essential as accessible water is ultimately beyond human control, so its availability should awaken humility, gratitude, and trust in God.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Nūn. By the pen and what they write.
interpretation: The oath by the pen and its written words honors knowledge and the preservation of truth. The opening letter “Nūn” is among the Qur’an’s disjointed letters, whose precise meaning is known to Allah.

translation: By the grace of your Lord, you are not mad.
interpretation: The verse rejects the accusation of madness and grounds the Prophet’s dignity and soundness in God’s favor, reassuring him not to be shaken by his opponents’ insults.

translation: And indeed, you will have a reward that never ends.
interpretation: Your reward with God is lasting and undiminished; it will neither be cut off nor held back.

translation: And indeed, you are of outstanding character.
interpretation: God affirms that the Prophet embodies an exalted and exemplary moral character, making his conduct a model of virtue.

translation: Then you will see, and they will see.
interpretation: The truth will soon become unmistakable: the Prophet’s opponents will come to recognize that he is not afflicted with madness, and that their accusations are false.

translation: Which of you is truly afflicted with madness?
interpretation: The phrase challenges the deniers who accused the Prophet of madness: the truth will become clear, revealing whether he or his opponents are the ones astray.

translation: Indeed, your Lord knows best who has strayed from His way, and He knows best those who are rightly guided.
interpretation: The verse teaches that ultimate judgment of people’s guidance belongs to God, whose knowledge is complete; people should therefore approach claims about others’ faith with humility.

translation: So do not obey those who deny the truth.
interpretation: The verse calls the Prophet to remain steadfast in his message and not let the demands or pressure of those who reject the truth turn him away from it.

translation: They wish that you would compromise, so they would compromise too.
interpretation: The verse warns against diluting the truth to win approval: their willingness to meet the Prophet halfway depends on his first compromising his message, rather than on sincere acceptance.

translation: And do not obey every contemptible, habitual swearer.
interpretation: The verse warns against letting persistent oath-taking and low character lend someone authority; trust should rest on integrity, not emphatic claims.

translation: A slanderer, going about spreading malicious gossip.
interpretation: The phrase condemns someone who habitually harms others by fault-finding and carrying rumors between people, sowing distrust and discord.

translation: A withholder of good, a transgressor, and a sinner.
interpretation: This describes someone whose character combines withholding goodness from others with violating moral limits and persisting in wrongdoing.

translation: 粗暴无礼；除此之外，他还是个卑劣之徒。
interpretation: 这里描绘的是一个人品性恶劣到极点：他不仅粗暴强横，还以卑劣而声名狼藉的行径为人所知。

translation: Because he has wealth and sons,
interpretation: His wealth and sons are not grounds for accepting his judgment or overlooking his wrongdoing; worldly status does not make a person worthy of obedience when he rejects God’s signs.

translation: When Our verses are recited to him, he says, “Tales of the ancients.”
interpretation: The verse portrays someone who, rather than considering the revelation sincerely, dismisses it as mere ancient stories. His response reflects a refusal to recognize its truth and guidance.

translation: We will brand him upon the snout.
interpretation: This is a threat that the arrogant rejecter will be marked with a visible sign of disgrace, exposing his humiliation before others.

translation: Indeed, We have tested them as We tested the owners of the garden, when they vowed to harvest it in the morning.
interpretation: The verse warns that worldly prosperity is a test, not a guarantee of security: when people rely on their own plans and forget their dependence on God, their apparent control can be swiftly undone.

translation: And they made no exception.
interpretation: They spoke with certainty about carrying out their plan without acknowledging that it depended on God’s will, revealing their presumption and heedlessness.

translation: Then a visitation from your Lord swept over it while they were asleep.
interpretation: The garden was struck by a calamity decreed by God during the night, beyond its owners’ awareness or control—a reminder that human plans cannot shield anyone from God’s will.

translation: Then it became like a field that had been completely reaped.
interpretation: The image conveys utter devastation: what had once been flourishing was left bare and lifeless, as though its growth had been cut away.

translation: So they called to one another in the morning.
interpretation: Their gathering at dawn shows how deliberately and eagerly they set out to carry through their plan.

translation: “Set out early to your field, if you intend to harvest it.”
interpretation: The command reflects the owners’ plan to gather the crop before anyone else could reach it, revealing their intention to withhold its benefit from those in need.

translation: So they set out, whispering to one another.
interpretation: Their hushed words show them deliberately concealing their plan, hoping the needy would not learn of it.

translation: “Let no needy person enter it among you today.”
interpretation: This expresses a deliberate intention to exclude the poor, showing how greed can lead people to deny others their rightful share of their blessings.

translation: And they set out early, determined and confident in their ability.
interpretation: They went intending to keep the needy from receiving any of the garden’s produce, certain that they could carry out their plan; their confidence reflects deliberate resolve, not awareness that God could thwart them.

translation: When they saw it, they said, “We have surely lost our way.”
interpretation: Their bewilderment shows how completely the garden’s ruin upended their expectations, reminding us that people do not truly control the blessings they take for granted.

translation: Rather, we have been deprived.
interpretation: They recognize that they have been denied the harvest they expected, a consequence of their intention to keep it from those in need.

translation: The most moderate of them said, “Did I not tell you, ‘Why do you not glorify Allah?’”
interpretation: The most clear-sighted brother reminds them that they should have glorified Allah by acknowledging His authority and repenting of their intention to deny the needy their share. Their failure to do so showed that they had acted as though their plan were independent of God’s will.

translation: They said, “Glory be to our Lord! We were indeed wrongdoers.”
interpretation: Their words express sincere remorse: they recognize that their own wrongdoing, not injustice from God, brought about their loss, and they turn to God with reverence.

translation: Then they turned to one another, blaming each other.
interpretation: Their mutual reproach reflects their recognition that they had all shared responsibility for their wrongful plan.

translation: They will say, “Woe to us! We were indeed transgressors.”
interpretation: Their words show a moment of painful recognition: they now admit that their own excesses and wrongdoing brought them to this loss, after having failed to acknowledge it earlier.

translation: Perhaps our Lord will give us something better than it in its place. Indeed, we turn to our Lord with hope.
interpretation: After recognizing their wrongdoing, they place their hope in God’s mercy and provision. Their words express repentance and trust that what God grants may be better than what they lost.

translation: Such is the punishment; and the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew.
interpretation: The worldly punishment is only a foretaste and warning; the consequence in the Hereafter is far greater, and recognizing this would lead people to heed the warning and turn away from wrongdoing.

translation: Indeed, for the God-conscious are Gardens of Bliss with their Lord.
interpretation: The verse teaches that lasting felicity is a divine reward for those who remain mindful of God and live in obedience to Him.

translation: Shall We then treat the Muslims like the criminals?
interpretation: This rhetorical question rejects the idea that those who submit to God and those who persist in wrongdoing could be treated alike. It affirms that God’s judgment is just and that their different choices will have different outcomes.

translation: What is the matter with you? How do you judge?
interpretation: This is a rebuke of people who reach unjust conclusions without sound grounds, calling them to reconsider how they judge.

translation: Or do you have a scripture in which you study,
interpretation: This is a rhetorical challenge to those who presume they are entitled to what they claim: do they possess any revealed scripture that supports their assumptions? The question exposes the absence of divine authority for their position.

translation: Surely you will have therein whatever you choose?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical challenge to those claiming they may choose whatever outcome they wish: what authority entitles them to such a privilege? The verse exposes that claim as baseless, not as a promise that they will receive whatever they desire.

translation: Or do you have binding oaths from Us, lasting until the Day of Resurrection, that you will have whatever you decree?
interpretation: The verse challenges those who presume they are assured of whatever they desire: they have no covenant from God guaranteeing such a claim. Their confidence has no divine promise behind it.

translation: Ask them which of them is responsible for guaranteeing that.
interpretation: The verse challenges those making the claim to identify someone who can truly guarantee it, exposing that their assertion has no credible authority behind it.

translation: Or do they have partners [with God]? Then let them bring their partners, if they are truthful.
interpretation: The verse challenges those who claim that others share in God’s authority or can support them: if that claim is true, let them produce those they rely on as proof.

translation: On the Day when the severity is laid bare, they will be called to prostrate, but they will be unable.
interpretation: The verse portrays the overwhelming distress of the Day of Judgment. Those who refused to humble themselves before God in worldly life will then be summoned to prostrate, but their defiance will have left them unable to do so.

translation: Their eyes will be humbled, and humiliation will overwhelm them. Yet they used to be called to prostrate while they were well and able.
interpretation: Their humiliation in the Hereafter is the consequence of having rejected the call to worship when they still had the ability to respond. What they once refused freely will no longer be within their power.

translation: So leave Me with whoever denies this discourse; We will gradually lead them on from where they do not know.
interpretation: The verse warns that those who reject God’s revelation may be given time and apparent ease, but this should not be mistaken for approval: they are being drawn gradually toward the consequences of their choices, beyond their awareness.

translation: And I will grant them respite; indeed, My plan is firm.
interpretation: Their delay in punishment is not a sign of approval or weakness: God gives them time, while His decisive plan remains beyond their ability to evade.

translation: Or do you ask them for a payment, so that they are weighed down by debt?
interpretation: The verse challenges the claim that people reject the message because its cost burdens them: the Messenger seeks no payment from them, so their refusal cannot be blamed on financial hardship.

translation: Or do they possess knowledge of the unseen, so that they write it down?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical challenge: they have no access to the unseen that would justify their claims or give them certainty about what is to come.

translation: So be patient with your Lord’s judgment, and do not be like the companion of the fish when he called out, distressed and full of anguish.
interpretation: The verse urges steadfast patience in carrying out God’s command, especially under hardship, and cautions against letting distress lead to the kind of impatience associated with Jonah before his trial had run its course.

translation: Had it not been for a favor from his Lord that reached him, he would have been cast onto the barren shore, blameworthy.
interpretation: God’s mercy rescued Jonah and accepted his repentance; without that favor, he would have been left exposed and condemned for his mistake.

translation: Then his Lord chose him and made him one of the righteous.
interpretation: God’s acceptance of Jonah after his repentance shows that a sincere return to Him can restore a person to favor and guide them toward righteousness.

translation: Those who disbelieve almost make you stumble with their eyes when they hear the Reminder, and they say, “He is surely mad.”
interpretation: The verse depicts the disbelievers’ fierce hostility toward the Prophet: as they hear the Qur’an, they glare at him with such intensity that it is described as nearly making him stumble, then dismiss his message by calling him mad. Their accusation reflects their rejection, not the truth of his message.

translation: And it is nothing but a reminder for all worlds.
interpretation: The Qur’an is a universal reminder, calling people everywhere to recognize God’s guidance and live with awareness of their accountability to Him.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. The Inevitable Reality.
interpretation: The opening names the Day of Judgment as an inescapable reality, urging the listener to take its certainty seriously.

translation: What is the Inevitable Reality?
interpretation: “Al-Ḥāqqah” is a name for the Resurrection: the certain reality whose truth will become unmistakable, and before which every denial is overturned.

translation: And what can make you know what the Inevitable Reality is?
interpretation: The question underscores the tremendous gravity of the Inevitable Reality, showing that its full magnitude surpasses ordinary human understanding.

translation: Thamūd and ʿĀd denied the Striking Calamity.
interpretation: The verse warns that the Day of Resurrection and Judgment—the overwhelming event that strikes people with terror—is certain, and recalls the fate of earlier peoples who denied it.

translation: As for Thamud, they were destroyed by the overpowering blast.
interpretation: The word “overpowering” conveys that no strength or resistance could protect them from the consequence that came upon them; their destruction was decisive and beyond their control.

translation: As for ʿĀd, they were destroyed by a furious, violent wind.
interpretation: The verse presents the destruction of ʿĀd as a sign of God’s power: a force of nature, beyond human control, became the means by which their defiance ended. The wind’s intensity underscores that no worldly strength can protect a people from divine judgment.

translation: He unleashed it upon them for seven nights and eight days in succession, and you would see the people lying fallen, as though they were hollow trunks of palm trees.
interpretation: The unbroken duration and image of hollow, toppled palm trunks convey the overwhelming force of the punishment and the complete destruction it brought upon the people.

translation: So do you see any remnant of them?
interpretation: This rhetorical question emphasizes the complete destruction of the people addressed: no trace or survivor of them remained.

translation: And Pharaoh, those before him, and the overturned cities came with wrongdoing.
interpretation: The verse points to a recurring pattern: powerful peoples and communities were not spared when they persisted in grave disobedience and rejected the truth. Their fate is a warning that worldly power cannot protect anyone from accountability before God.

translation: But they disobeyed the messenger of their Lord, so He seized them with a mighty, overwhelming seizure.
interpretation: Their rejection of their Lord’s messenger brought upon them a punishment of extraordinary severity, showing the grave consequence of knowingly defying divine guidance.

translation: Indeed, when the water overflowed, We carried you aboard the vessel.
interpretation: The verse recalls God’s deliverance of Noah and those with him in the Ark, addressing later generations as heirs of those who were saved. It invites recognition of divine protection and gratitude for it.

translation: So that We might make it a reminder for you, and that an attentive ear might retain it.
interpretation: The sign is meant not merely to be heard, but to be held in a receptive heart, where its lesson can guide a person toward faith and heedfulness.

translation: When the Trumpet is blown with a single blast,
interpretation: The verse conveys the suddenness and certainty of the great upheaval: by a single command, the created order will be set in motion toward the Resurrection.

translation: And the earth and the mountains are lifted up and crushed with a single crushing.
interpretation: The verse portrays the final upheaval as the undoing of everything people regard as firm and enduring. The earth and mountains themselves cannot withstand God’s command, underscoring the absolute power of the Creator and the certainty that worldly stability will give way to the Hereafter.

translation: Then, on that Day, the Inevitable Event will take place.
interpretation: The verse portrays the Resurrection as a certain and decisive reality: when its appointed Day arrives, no one will be able to avert it.

translation: And the heaven will be split apart; on that Day it will be frail.
interpretation: The verse portrays the collapse of the heavens’ apparent stability, showing that even the greatest parts of creation are subject to God’s command and will not remain unchanged when the Hour comes.

translation: And the angels will be at its edges, and that Day eight will bear the Throne of your Lord above them.
interpretation: The verse portrays the overwhelming order and majesty of the Day of Resurrection: the angels stand at the edges of the transformed heaven, while appointed bearers carry out their task by God’s command. This does not imply that God depends on them; rather, it underscores His absolute sovereignty.

translation: That Day you will be brought forth, and nothing about you will remain hidden.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, every person will stand fully exposed before God: no deed, intention, or hidden matter can be concealed from His knowledge.

translation: As for the one who is given his record in his right hand, he will say, “Here, read my record!”
interpretation: His invitation to others to read his record expresses joyful confidence: he knows that God’s judgment has vindicated him, and he has nothing to hide.

translation: Indeed, I was certain that I would face my reckoning.
interpretation: The speaker’s certainty of being held accountable reflects a faith that shaped how he lived: he understood that his deeds would not go unnoticed and prepared to answer for them.

translation: Then he will be in a life of contentment.
interpretation: The phrase describes the enduring bliss of the Hereafter: a life so pleasing that its blessings bring complete satisfaction and leave no room for distress.

translation: In a lofty garden.
interpretation: The phrase portrays the Garden as exalted in rank and honor, a place of lasting bliss prepared for the people of Paradise.

translation: Its fruit clusters will be within easy reach.
interpretation: The blessings of Paradise are made readily accessible, requiring no effort to obtain.

translation: Eat and drink with enjoyment for what you sent ahead in days gone by.
interpretation: The verse portrays the people of Paradise being welcomed to its blessings as a reward for the good deeds they performed during their earthly lives.

translation: But as for the one who is given his record in his left hand, he will say, “If only I had not been given my record!”
interpretation: Receiving the record in the left hand signifies utter disgrace and a reckoning whose outcome is now unavoidable. The words express the profound, belated regret of someone who sees the consequences of their deeds but can no longer change them.

translation: And I did not know what my reckoning would be.
interpretation: He is overwhelmed by the terrifying reality of the reckoning, realizing that he had never understood what awaited him.

translation: If only it had been the end!
interpretation: The speaker, overwhelmed by regret and punishment, wishes that death had brought a final end rather than being followed by resurrection and accountability.

translation: My wealth has not benefited me.
interpretation: The verse underscores that worldly possessions cannot shield a person from the consequences of rejecting God; wealth has no lasting value when it cannot help one in the Hereafter.

translation: My authority has perished from me!
interpretation: The speaker laments that the power and influence he once relied on have vanished and can no longer help him before God.

translation: Seize him and shackle him.
interpretation: The command portrays the severe and inescapable punishment awaiting the condemned, underscoring the gravity of his deeds and the certainty of divine justice.

translation: Then burn him in the blazing Fire.
interpretation: The command expresses the certainty and severity of punishment for one who has rejected the truth and persisted in wrongdoing.

translation: Then put him through a chain seventy cubits long.
interpretation: The verse depicts the condemned person being subjected to utter humiliation and confinement, with the immense chain conveying the severity of the punishment and the impossibility of escape.

translation: Indeed, he did not believe in Allah, the Magnificent.
interpretation: The verse points to a settled refusal to acknowledge Allah’s supreme greatness and authority. Such disbelief is not merely an abstract opinion; it means turning away from the accountability that follows from recognizing Him.

translation: And does not urge the feeding of the needy.
interpretation: The verse portrays indifference to the needy as a moral failure: a person’s concern for the vulnerable should be evident not only in their own generosity, but also in encouraging others to help.

translation: So today he has no close friend here.
interpretation: In the Hereafter, no loyal companion is there to comfort or defend him; his earthly ties cannot shield him from the consequence of his deeds.

translation: And no food except from ghislīn.
interpretation: Ghislīn is understood as the foul discharge of the people of Hell. The verse depicts the sustenance of the condemned as utterly degrading and unlike nourishing food.

translation: None will eat it except the sinners.
interpretation: The verse conveys that this food is a fitting punishment for those who persisted in wrongdoing, emphasizing the grave consequences of their choices.

translation: No! I swear by what you see.
interpretation: The verse draws attention to the visible world as a witness to the force and truth of the assertion that follows.

translation: And what you do not see.
interpretation: It points to realities beyond human perception, reminding us that what lies outside our sight is no less real or significant.

translation: Indeed, it is the word of a noble messenger.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the Qur’an is conveyed by an honored messenger, rather than being fabricated or composed by him.

translation: And it is not the word of a poet—little indeed is what you believe.
interpretation: The revelation is not human poetry but divine truth; the people’s scant belief reflects their failure to recognize its source and heed its message.

translation: Nor is it the speech of a soothsayer. Little do you take heed.
interpretation: The verse rejects the claim that the revelation is fortune-telling, and reproaches those who give little thought to its truth.

translation: A revelation from the Lord of all worlds.
interpretation: The Qur’an is presented as coming from God, the Lord and sustainer of all creation, rather than being the invention of a human being.

translation: And if he had invented some sayings and attributed them to Us…
interpretation: The verse begins a grave hypothetical warning: revelation is not the Prophet’s own invention, and falsely attributing words to God would bring severe consequences. In its Qur’anic context, it affirms that the message is faithfully conveyed, not fabricated.

translation: We would have seized him by the right hand.
interpretation: This is a forceful expression of Allah’s power: had the Messenger fabricated anything in His name, Allah would have swiftly and decisively restrained him and punished him.

translation: Then We would have severed his aorta.
interpretation: In context, this is a conditional warning: were the Messenger to fabricate words and attribute them to God, God would punish him decisively. It underscores that the message is not his invention and that no one could shield a person from such judgment.

translation: So none of you could have shielded him from it.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that no human being, however influential, could avert God’s judgment or protect someone from it if God decreed otherwise.

translation: And indeed, it is a reminder for the God-conscious.
interpretation: The revelation serves as a lasting admonition for those mindful of God, helping them recognize the truth and live by it.

translation: And indeed, We know that among you are those who deny.
interpretation: God knows that some among the people addressed reject the truth, even if their denial is concealed from others.

translation: And indeed, it is a source of regret for the disbelievers.
interpretation: The Qur’an becomes a profound regret for those who reject it when they realize the truth they turned away from.

translation: And indeed, it is the truth of certainty.
interpretation: It declares that what has been spoken of is utterly certain—not a matter of doubt or conjecture—and calls the listener to receive it as established truth.

translation: So glorify the name of your Lord, the Magnificent.
interpretation: The verse calls you to honor and exalt God, recognizing His supreme greatness and directing your worship and remembrance to Him alone.

translation: In the name of God, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. A petitioner asked for a punishment that is sure to befall.
interpretation: The verse portrays someone demanding the promised punishment, perhaps in defiance or disbelief. Its wording emphasizes that the punishment is not an empty threat: it will inevitably come by God’s decree.

translation: For the disbelievers, there is no one to avert it.
interpretation: The punishment decreed for those who reject God cannot be warded off by any power.

translation: From Allah, the Lord of the ascending pathways.
interpretation: The phrase portrays Allah as possessing the exalted ranks and pathways through which the angels ascend, emphasizing His supreme majesty and authority.

translation: The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him on a day whose measure is fifty thousand years.
interpretation: This describes the immense scale of the Day of Judgment: the angels, and the Spirit—understood as Gabriel—ascend to God, and that day’s measure is fifty thousand years, conveying its overwhelming length and gravity.

translation: So be patient with gracious patience.
interpretation: Remain steadfast without resentment or despair, entrusting the outcome to God and meeting hardship with dignity.

translation: Indeed, they see it as far off.
interpretation: Those who deny the promised Day of Judgment regard it as distant and unlikely, though it is certain to come.

translation: And We see it as near.
interpretation: What people regard as far off—the promised Day of Judgment—is near in God’s knowledge and certain to come, so it should not be treated as remote or doubtful.

translation: On the Day when the sky will be like molten metal,
interpretation: The verse evokes the immense upheaval of the Day of Judgment: even the sky will lose its familiar order and appear terrifyingly altered.

translation: And the mountains will be like carded wool.
