interpretation: The image conveys the upheaval of the Day of Judgment: even mountains, symbols of solidity and permanence, will lose their firmness and become light and scattered, showing that the familiar order of the world will be transformed.

translation: And no close friend will ask about a close friend.
interpretation: The terror of the Day of Judgment will be so overwhelming that even the closest companions will be absorbed in their own fate, unable to turn to one another.

translation: They will see one another; the guilty person will wish to ransom himself from the punishment of that Day by giving up his children.
interpretation: The verse portrays the Day of Judgment as so terrifying that even the closest family bonds cannot offer comfort: the guilty person would sacrifice what is dearest to him to escape, yet no ransom can shield him from God’s judgment.

translation: And his wife and his brother,
interpretation: The phrase portrays the overwhelming terror of the Day of Resurrection: even one’s closest family will be left behind as each person is consumed by concern for their own fate.

translation: And his clan that shelters him,
interpretation: Even the kin who usually protect and support a person will be no refuge to him on that Day; the terror will make each person concerned only with himself.

translation: And everyone on earth, all of them, hoping thereby to save himself.
interpretation: It portrays the desperate wish to ransom oneself from the coming punishment by offering up everyone on earth; yet no such exchange can bring deliverance.

translation: No! Indeed, it is the Blaze.
interpretation: The verse sharply rejects the boastful person’s expectation of receiving more worldly favor: his end is instead the fiercely burning Fire, called *Lazā*.

translation: It strips away the scalp.
interpretation: The phrase portrays the fire’s torment as intensely destructive, emphasizing the utter exposure and helplessness of those subjected to it.

translation: It calls whoever turned away and turned his back.
interpretation: The verse portrays the Fire as drawing toward itself those who rejected the truth and persisted in turning away from God.

translation: and amassed wealth, then hoarded it.
interpretation: The verse censures the impulse to treat wealth as something to stockpile and keep for oneself, rather than using it responsibly and fulfilling the rights others have upon it.

translation: Indeed, the human being was created prone to anxiety.
interpretation: The verse describes a human tendency to become unsettled and impatient when faced with hardship or uncertainty.

translation: When adversity touches him, he becomes impatient.
interpretation: The verse portrays a person’s tendency to lose patience when hardship comes, revealing how readily distress can overwhelm him.

translation: And when good comes to him, he is withholding.
interpretation: The verse points to a tendency to cling to one’s blessings and withhold them from others, rather than responding to them with generosity.

translation: Except those who pray,
interpretation: This marks the worshippers as an exception to the human tendency toward panic and selfishness: their prayer grounds them in devotion and steadiness.

translation: Those who are constant in their prayer,
interpretation: They maintain their prayers consistently, giving worship a steady place in their lives rather than turning to it only occasionally.

translation: And those who have in their wealth a known, appointed share,
interpretation: Their wealth is not treated as theirs alone: they acknowledge a defined right within it for those in need, giving it as a duty rather than merely as an occasional act of generosity.

translation: For the one who asks and the deprived.
interpretation: It points to a rightful share in the wealth of those who have means for people in need—both those who ask openly and those whose hardship remains unseen because they do not ask.

translation: And those who affirm the Day of Recompense,
interpretation: They are certain that they will stand before God and be held accountable for their deeds, so they live with awareness of the Hereafter.

translation: And those who are apprehensive of the punishment of their Lord,
interpretation: Their awareness of standing accountable before God keeps them humble and vigilant. They do not presume that their deeds make them secure; instead, they strive to obey Him while seeking His mercy.

translation: Indeed, the punishment of their Lord is not something from which one can feel secure.
interpretation: The verse teaches that a person should not presume immunity from God’s judgment, but remain humble and mindful of accountability, seeking God’s mercy.

translation: And those who guard their private parts,
interpretation: They protect their chastity by refraining from sexual conduct outside the bounds God has permitted.

translation: Except with their spouses or those whom their right hands possess; then they are not blameworthy.
interpretation: The passage identifies the relationships it regards as lawful within its original social and legal context, distinguishing them from sexual conduct outside those bounds.

translation: So whoever seeks beyond that, those are the transgressors.
interpretation: The verse identifies the lawful relationships mentioned in its context as the boundary for sexual relations; seeking fulfillment beyond that boundary is disobedience to God’s limits.

translation: And those who faithfully honor their trusts and their commitments.
interpretation: Faithfulness is shown by safeguarding what others entrust to you and keeping your promises; both are responsibilities before God and people.

translation: And those who uphold their testimonies,
interpretation: They are faithful and steadfast in bearing witness to the truth, neither concealing it nor altering it for personal gain.

translation: And those who are steadfast in guarding their prayers.
interpretation: They treat prayer as a lasting commitment, preserving its times and proper observance rather than neglecting it or allowing worldly concerns to displace it.

translation: Those are honored in gardens.
interpretation: Their honor in Paradise is a lasting dignity bestowed by God, beyond the fleeting status people may seek in worldly life.

translation: So what is the matter with those who disbelieve, hurrying toward you?
interpretation: The verse challenges the disbelievers’ intent, hurried approach to the Prophet, drawing attention to their attitude toward him and his message.

translation: From the right and from the left, in separate groups.
interpretation: They are gathered around the Prophet in scattered clusters on either side, rather than coming together as one united group.

translation: Does every one of them expect to enter a Garden of Bliss?
interpretation: The question challenges the presumption that merely wishing for Paradise guarantees its reward: a person’s hope must be grounded in faith and a life responsive to God’s guidance.

translation: No indeed! We created them from what they know.
interpretation: The verse rebukes those who presume they are beyond accountability or guaranteed honor: they know they were created from humble beginnings, so they have no grounds for pride or for denying God’s power to resurrect and judge them.

translation: So I swear by the Lord of the easts and the wests: We are surely able.
interpretation: The oath invokes God’s sovereignty over every place where the sun rises and sets, affirming that His power is limitless. Nothing can prevent Him from bringing about what He wills, including resurrection and replacing one people with another.

translation: [We are able] to replace them with better than them, and none can outstrip Us.
interpretation: God is not dependent on any people: if they persist in rejecting Him, He can bring others who are better in faith and obedience, and no one can thwart His will.

translation: So leave them to indulge and play until they meet the Day they have been promised.
interpretation: The verse warns that those who turn away from the truth may be left to pursue their distractions for a time, but this respite does not mean they will escape accountability when the promised Day arrives.

translation: The Day they emerge from their graves in haste, as though rushing toward a set-up marker.
interpretation: The image conveys the urgency and inevitability of the Resurrection: people will hurry toward the gathering with no power to delay or turn aside, like competitors racing toward a fixed goal.

translation: Their eyes will be downcast, and humiliation will overwhelm them. That is the Day they were promised.
interpretation: The verse warns that the promised reckoning will make denial impossible: those who disregarded the warning will stand exposed and powerless before its truth.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Indeed, We sent Noah to his people, saying, “Warn your people before a painful punishment comes upon them.”
interpretation: Noah’s warning shows that divine admonition is an act of mercy: his people were given the chance to turn back before the consequences of rejecting guidance arrived.

translation: He said, “O my people, I am indeed a clear warner to you.”
interpretation: The warning is presented as an act of sincere care: the speaker makes his message plain so his people can recognize the danger and respond knowingly.

translation: Worship Allah, be mindful of Him, and obey me.
interpretation: The verse calls people to devote worship to Allah alone and let reverence for Him guide their conduct. Noah’s call to obey him is obedience to his role as Allah’s messenger, not worship of Noah.

translation: He will forgive you some of your sins and grant you respite until an appointed time. When God’s appointed time comes, it cannot be delayed—if only you knew.
interpretation: The verse presents the messenger’s call as an opportunity to turn back to God: repentance brings forgiveness and a period of respite, but that respite has a limit. Once God’s appointed time arrives, no one can postpone it.

translation: He said, “My Lord, I have indeed called my people night and day.”
interpretation: Noah’s words express his steadfast patience and devotion in calling his people to guidance, continuing his efforts at every opportunity.

translation: But my calling them only increased their flight.
interpretation: Noah explains that despite his persistent efforts to call his people to God, their stubborn resistance made them recoil even further from the truth.

translation: Whenever I called them so that You might forgive them, they put their fingers in their ears, covered themselves with their garments, persisted in rejection, and grew exceedingly arrogant.
interpretation: Their response shows a deliberate refusal to hear the call to faith: they tried to shut out its message, persisted in rejecting it, and let arrogance prevent them from turning back and seeking God’s forgiveness.

translation: Then indeed I called them openly.
interpretation: Noah explains that when private appeals did not bring his people to faith, he also proclaimed his message publicly, continuing to call them to God without concealment.

translation: Then I proclaimed to them openly and spoke to them privately.
interpretation: Noah explains that he used every suitable way to reach his people, addressing them both publicly and in private, in earnest effort to guide them toward God.

translation: So I said, “Seek forgiveness from your Lord; indeed, He is ever-forgiving.”
interpretation: The verse conveys an invitation to turn back to God with hope: His forgiveness is abundant and enduring, so a person should not despair of seeking it.

translation: He will send abundant rain upon you.
interpretation: In Noah’s appeal, this is a promise that turning back to God and seeking His forgiveness can bring His mercy and provision, represented here by plentiful rain.

translation: And He will provide you with wealth and children, and make gardens for you and rivers.
interpretation: The verse presents material provision and flourishing as blessings God may grant in response to sincere turning back to Him, while pointing beyond the gifts themselves to His care and generosity.

translation: What is the matter with you that you do not hold Allah in due reverence?
interpretation: The verse rebukes people for failing to honor Allah with the awe and reverence due to His greatness, which should lead them to submit to Him and obey Him.

translation: And He has created you in stages.
interpretation: The verse draws attention to the gradual stages of human creation as a sign of God’s power and wisdom, inviting people to reflect on their dependence on Him.

translation: Have you not considered how Allah created seven heavens in layers?
interpretation: The verse calls people to reflect on the heavens’ ordered, layered structure as a sign of Allah’s power and wisdom, and to recognize that such creation is not without purpose.

translation: And He made the moon among them a light, and made the sun a lamp.
interpretation: The verse draws attention to the ordered heavens through the distinct roles of the moon and sun: the moon is described as a light, while the sun is likened to a lamp. Their presence and benefit point to the wisdom and power of the Creator.

translation: And Allah has caused you to grow from the earth, as a growth.
interpretation: The verse likens human development to the growth of a plant, emphasizing that life and its gradual unfolding come from Allah’s creative power.

translation: Then He will return you to it and bring you forth again.
interpretation: God returns people to the earth after death, then brings them out of it at the Resurrection.

translation: And Allah has made the earth for you an expanse.
interpretation: The verse points to the earth as a provision made fit for human life, offering a place to dwell and move about by God’s care.

translation: So that you may travel through its broad paths.
interpretation: The verse points to Allah’s provision of accessible routes across the earth, making travel through its wide passes and varied terrain possible.

translation: Noah said, “My Lord, they have disobeyed me and followed those whose wealth and children have increased them in nothing but loss.”
interpretation: Noah’s lament shows that worldly abundance is no measure of true success: when people rely on wealth and status while rejecting guidance, those very blessings can deepen their ruin rather than benefit them.

translation: And they devised a mighty plot.
interpretation: The verse describes the people’s deliberate and far-reaching schemes to oppose Noah’s message and turn others away from it.

translation: And they said, “Never abandon your gods; never abandon Wadd, Suwāʿ, Yaghūth, Yaʿūq, or Nasr.”
interpretation: The verse portrays how the people’s leaders reinforced idolatry by urging them to remain attached to their gods. The named figures were idols revered among Noah’s people, and invoking them by name reflects how deeply inherited worship had become entrenched.

translation: They have led many astray, so do not increase the wrongdoers except in further misguidance.
interpretation: Noah is speaking of those who persisted in wrongdoing and led others away from faith. His plea reflects that, having rejected guidance despite clear warning, they be left to deepen in the error they have chosen.

translation: Because of their sins, they were drowned, then made to enter a Fire, and they found no helpers for themselves besides God.
interpretation: The verse presents the people’s drowning as a consequence of their wrongdoing and rejection, followed by punishment in the Fire. No one they relied upon could protect them from God’s judgment.

translation: And Noah said, “My Lord, leave not upon the earth a single inhabitant among the disbelievers.”
interpretation: After enduring his people’s persistent rejection, Noah asks God to bring their wrongdoing to an end. His plea reflects the gravity of their defiance and the certainty that, if left unchecked, it would continue to corrupt those who came after them.

translation: Indeed, if You leave them, they will lead Your servants astray, and they will beget none but wicked, utterly disbelieving offspring.
interpretation: Noah is expressing his judgment, based on the people’s persistent rejection, that their influence would further obstruct faith and that their defiance had become entrenched across generations. This is a statement about those he is addressing, not a general claim that children inherit their parents’ disbelief.

translation: My Lord, forgive me, my parents, whoever enters my house as a believer, and the believing men and women. And grant the wrongdoers nothing but destruction.
interpretation: This is a prayer asking God for mercy for oneself and one’s family, for believers who come into one’s home, and for all believing men and women. It also asks that those who persist in wrongdoing meet the ruin their actions bring upon them.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Say: “It has been revealed to me that a group of jinn listened, and they said, ‘We have heard a wondrous Qur’an.’”
interpretation: The verse shows that the Qur’an’s compelling nature is not confined to human listeners: even the jinn recognized its wonder, affirming that its message carries a distinctive power and truth.

translation: It guides to the right way, so we have believed in it, and we will never associate anyone with our Lord.
interpretation: The speakers recognize the Qur’an’s guidance and respond with sincere faith, affirming that devotion belongs to God alone.

translation: And exalted is the majesty of our Lord; He has taken neither wife nor child.
interpretation: God’s greatness is utterly beyond human needs and relationships; attributing a spouse or offspring to Him wrongly applies creaturely qualities to the Creator.

translation: And that our foolish one used to utter outrageous things about Allah.
interpretation: The jinn acknowledge that the foolish among them had falsely attributed to Allah claims far beyond the truth, recognizing that such speech was an offense against His majesty.

translation: And we had thought that humans and jinn would never speak a lie about God.
interpretation: The jinn acknowledge that they had wrongly assumed no human or jinn would attribute falsehood to God; they now recognize that such claims had indeed been made.

translation: And indeed, some men among humankind used to seek refuge with some men among the jinn, and they only increased them in distress.
interpretation: The verse warns against seeking supernatural protection from the jinn: such appeals do not bring security, but deepen fear and encourage arrogance and wrongdoing. True refuge belongs with God.

translation: And they thought, just as you thought, that Allah would never resurrect anyone.
interpretation: The verse identifies denial of resurrection as a mistaken assumption shared by both groups, affirming that no one’s belief can prevent Allah from raising the dead.

translation: And we sought to reach the heaven, but found it filled with stern guards and flaming projectiles.
interpretation: The jinn describe how they could no longer approach the heaven to listen for its news: it was guarded against them by powerful sentinels and flaming missiles. This points to the protection of heavenly revelation from their interference.

translation: And we used to sit there in places to listen; but whoever tries to listen now will find a flame waiting for him.
interpretation: The jinn describe a change in the protection of the heavens: the unseen is no longer open to their attempts at eavesdropping. The waiting flame signifies that divine revelation is guarded and cannot be reached by those who try to intercept it.

translation: And we do not know whether evil is intended for those on earth, or whether their Lord intends guidance for them.
interpretation: The speaker acknowledges that the unseen outcome for humanity is beyond their knowledge, while affirming that true guidance comes by their Lord’s will.

translation: “Among us are the righteous, and among us are otherwise; we have followed divergent ways.”
interpretation: The jinn acknowledge that moral and spiritual character differs among them: they are not a single, uniform community, but individuals who have taken distinct paths and are accountable for the path they choose.

translation: And we thought that we could never escape Allah on earth, nor could we escape Him by fleeing.
interpretation: No creature can evade Allah’s power or judgment: neither hiding anywhere on earth nor fleeing can place anyone beyond His reach.

translation: “And when we heard the guidance, we believed in it. Whoever believes in his Lord need not fear having his reward diminished or being wronged.”
interpretation: The verse conveys that faith in God rests on trust in His perfect justice: He will neither withhold any rightful reward nor impose injustice on those who believe in Him.

translation: “Among us are those who submit to God, and among us are those who are unjust. Whoever submits to God has sought the right guidance.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that a person’s standing is determined by their response to God: sincere submission is a deliberate seeking of guidance, while turning away from what is right is injustice.

translation: As for the unjust, they will be fuel for Hell.
interpretation: Those who turn away from justice and persist in wrongdoing will face the consequence of their choices, becoming fuel for the Fire.

translation: And [it was revealed] that if they had remained steadfast upon the way, We would have given them abundant water.
interpretation: Steadfastness upon God’s guidance would have opened the way to abundant provision; that abundance, as the following verse indicates, would itself be a test of whether they remained grateful and obedient.

translation: So that We may test them with it. Whoever turns away from the remembrance of his Lord, He will lead him into an increasingly arduous punishment.
interpretation: Abundant provision is not merely a comfort; it is a test of whether people remain mindful and obedient to God. Turning away from that remembrance brings a punishment that grows in severity and is difficult to endure.

translation: And the mosques belong to Allah, so do not call upon anyone alongside Allah.
interpretation: Worship and supplication are to be directed to Allah alone; no person or being should be treated as a partner in that devotion.

translation: And when the servant of Allah stood up calling upon Him, they almost crowded around him in dense throngs.
interpretation: The jinn, hearing the Prophet worship and recite to his Lord, gathered so closely around him that they nearly formed a compact crowd—an image of their intense attention and amazement.

translation: Say, “I call upon my Lord alone, and I associate no one with Him.”
interpretation: The verse affirms that worship and devotion belong to God alone, rejecting any partner or intermediary treated as divine alongside Him.

translation: Say, “I have no power to bring you harm or guide you.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that the Messenger does not control people’s fate or possess independent power to guide them; his role is to convey God’s message, while ultimate power belongs to God.

translation: Say, “Indeed, no one can protect me from Allah, and I will find no refuge apart from Him.”
interpretation: The verse affirms that no power can shield anyone from Allah’s will; true refuge is found only by turning to Him.

translation: My duty is only to convey what comes from Allah and His messages. Whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger will have the Fire of Hell, abiding therein forever.
interpretation: The verse presents the Messenger’s role as conveying Allah’s revelation and warns that knowingly turning away from Allah’s guidance and the Messenger’s command carries the gravest consequence: lasting punishment in Hell.

translation: Until, when they see what they have been promised, they will know who is weaker in support and fewer in number.
interpretation: Those who dismiss the warning will discover, when its promised outcome becomes real, that worldly confidence and numbers cannot protect them; the boast of strength will be exposed as empty.

translation: Say, “I do not know whether what you are promised is near, or whether my Lord will set a term for it.”
interpretation: The timing of what God has promised is not for the Prophet to determine; it rests with God alone. The verse therefore directs people away from speculation about when it will occur and toward trust in God’s wisdom and readiness for what He has decreed.

translation: Knower of the unseen, He reveals His unseen to no one,
interpretation: God alone possesses complete knowledge of the unseen; no one can access it independently of Him.

translation: Except for a messenger whom He has chosen, He appoints guardians before him and behind him.
interpretation: God safeguards the revelation entrusted to His chosen messenger, surrounding him with guardians so that it is faithfully conveyed and protected.

translation: So that He may make known that they have conveyed the messages of their Lord; He encompasses all that is with them and has counted everything precisely.
interpretation: God’s protection of the revelation ensures that His messengers faithfully convey it, making their delivery clear and complete. This does not mean that God learns something He did not know before: His knowledge already encompasses the messengers and all they receive and convey, and nothing escapes His exact reckoning.

translation: In the name of God, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. O you who are wrapped in your mantle,
interpretation: The address is directed to the Prophet while he is wrapped in his cloak. Its intimate, gentle tone prepares him for the weighty spiritual calling that follows.

translation: Stand in prayer during the night, except for a little of it.
interpretation: The verse calls the Prophet to make the greater part of the night a time of worship and intimate devotion to God, while allowing a portion for rest.

translation: Half of it, or a little less.
interpretation: In the context of the surrounding verses, this sets a measured portion of the night for prayer, allowing a little less than half as a disciplined but merciful practice.

translation: Or add to it, and recite the Qur’an in a measured, deliberate manner.
interpretation: The verse calls for reciting the Qur’an calmly and clearly, giving its words their due and allowing time to reflect on their meaning rather than rushing through them.

translation: Indeed, We shall bestow upon you a weighty word.
interpretation: The Qur’an is described as weighty because receiving and carrying it entails a profound responsibility: its truth bears deeply on the heart, and faithfully conveying and living by it calls for steadfastness.

translation: Indeed, the hours of the night are more effective in bringing the heart and tongue into accord, and more conducive to upright speech.
interpretation: The quiet of the night helps a person attend more fully to prayer and recitation, so the heart can be more present and the words more deliberate and sincere.

translation: Indeed, you have prolonged activity during the day.
interpretation: Because the day is occupied with many demands and movements, the night offers a quieter time for sustained devotion and reflection.

translation: And remember the name of your Lord, and devote yourself to Him with complete devotion.
interpretation: True devotion begins with keeping God present in the heart and grows through turning to Him sincerely and wholeheartedly, without allowing worldly distractions to divide one’s commitment.

translation: [He is] the Lord of the East and the West; there is no god but Him, so take Him as your guardian and disposer of affairs.
interpretation: Because God alone governs all creation and is worthy of worship, place your trust in Him alone and entrust your affairs to His care.

translation: And be patient with what they say, and leave them with gracious avoidance.
interpretation: Remain steadfast in the face of hurtful words, and distance yourself without spite or retaliation, preserving dignity and entrusting the matter to God.

translation: Leave Me to deal with the deniers, those who enjoy ease, and give them a little respite.
interpretation: The verse reassures the Prophet that he need not take the deniers’ fate into his own hands: their worldly comfort and temporary reprieve do not place them beyond God’s judgment.

translation: Indeed, with Us are shackles and a blazing fire.
interpretation: This is a grave warning that persistent rejection of God’s guidance has consequences beyond worldly power or escape: no one can evade His judgment, and those who defy Him will face a punishment they cannot overcome.

translation: And food that chokes, and a painful punishment.
interpretation: This depicts the torment awaiting those who reject the truth: even their food will bring no relief, but will itself become a source of suffering, compounded by painful punishment.

translation: On the Day when the earth and the mountains will quake, and the mountains will become heaps of shifting sand.
interpretation: The verse depicts the overwhelming upheaval of the Day of Judgment: even the mountains, symbols of solidity, will lose their stability and crumble, showing that nothing in the created world can withstand that moment.

translation: Indeed, We have sent to you a Messenger as a witness over you, just as We sent a Messenger to Pharaoh.
interpretation: The comparison warns that rejecting a messenger is not without consequence: just as Pharaoh was answerable for how he responded to his messenger, those addressed by the Prophet will be answerable for their response to him.

translation: But Pharaoh disobeyed the Messenger, so We seized him with a severe punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns that rejecting a messenger’s clear call is not a matter without consequence: worldly power cannot shield someone from divine judgment.

translation: How, then, will you protect yourselves if you disbelieve in a Day that will turn children’s hair gray?
interpretation: The verse warns that the Day of Judgment will be so terrifying that even children will appear gray-haired from its horrors. It urges people not to reject faith, but to seek protection through belief and obedience to God.

translation: The sky will be split apart because of it; His promise is sure to be fulfilled.
interpretation: The image of the sky splitting conveys the overwhelming force of the promised Day of Judgment: even the greatest parts of creation will be shaken, and nothing can prevent God’s decree from coming to pass.

translation: Indeed, this is a reminder; so whoever wills may take a path to his Lord.
interpretation: The verse presents the reminder as guidance toward God, while calling each person to choose to follow that path rather than merely hear it.

translation: Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand in prayer for nearly two-thirds of the night, or half of it, or a third of it, along with a group of those who are with you. Allah determines the measure of the night and the day. He knows that you cannot keep an exact count, so He has turned to you in mercy. Recite, then, whatever is easy for you of the Qur’an. He knows that some of you will be ill, others will travel through the land seeking Allah’s bounty, and others will fight in Allah’s cause. So recite whatever is easy of it. Establish prayer, give the prescribed charity, and offer Allah a goodly loan. Whatever good you send ahead for yourselves, you will find it with Allah—better and greater in reward. And seek Allah’s forgiveness; indeed, Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse teaches that worship is meant to draw a person toward God, not become an unbearable burden. Allah knows the limits imposed by illness, work, travel, and struggle, and therefore makes room for people to worship according to their capacity. What matters is sincere, sustained devotion: reciting what one can, fulfilling prayer and charity, and doing good with trust that none of it is lost with Allah. The call to seek forgiveness keeps that effort humble, grounded in reliance on His mercy rather than confidence in one’s own deeds.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. O you who are wrapped in your mantle!
interpretation: Allah addresses the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in his covered state, gently calling him to awaken and prepare to carry out the mission entrusted to him.

translation: Arise and warn.
interpretation: This command calls the Prophet to take up his mission with resolve, warning people to turn from wrongdoing and heed God’s guidance.

translation: And magnify your Lord.
interpretation: Declare your Lord’s greatness and honor Him above all else, directing your worship and reverence to Him alone.

translation: And purify your garments.
interpretation: The command calls for outward cleanliness as part of the Prophet’s preparation for his mission, reflecting the purity and dignity with which he should meet people and worship God.

translation: And shun all defilement.
interpretation: The verse commands the Prophet to keep himself entirely apart from idolatry and every form of spiritual impurity.

translation: And do not give expecting more in return.
interpretation: Give generously without using your gifts to place others in your debt or to seek greater repayment.

translation: And for your Lord, be patient.
interpretation: Remain steadfast through hardship, seeking your Lord’s pleasure and relying on Him.

translation: When the Trumpet is sounded,
interpretation: The sounding of the Trumpet marks the onset of the Resurrection, when worldly life gives way to the final reckoning.

translation: That Day will be a difficult day.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the severity and dread of the Day of Judgment, when people will face the consequences of their deeds.

translation: For the disbelievers, it will not be easy.
interpretation: The phrase emphasizes the severity of that Day for those who reject faith: they will find no ease or relief from its trials.

translation: Leave Me to deal with the one I created alone.
interpretation: God tells the Prophet to leave this person’s affair to Him: the person was created without worldly wealth or support, and will answer to God for his choices.

translation: And I granted him abundant wealth,
interpretation: His ample wealth is presented as a favor bestowed by God, and therefore a test of whether he would respond with gratitude and humility.

translation: And sons present with him,
interpretation: His sons were nearby and readily at hand, providing him with companionship, support, and standing among his people.

translation: And I made things easy for him, granting him ample comfort and means.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes how extensively worldly advantages were laid out for him—ease, resources, and opportunity—making his later arrogance all the more blameworthy rather than excusable.

translation: Then he hopes that I will give him more.
interpretation: The verse exposes the presumption that blessings are an entitlement: even after receiving much, a person may greedily expect more while remaining ungrateful to the One who bestowed them.

translation: No! Indeed, he has been stubbornly opposed to Our signs.
interpretation: The verse portrays a deliberate, persistent resistance to God’s revelations—not confusion or lack of evidence, but a refusal to accept their truth despite their clarity.

translation: I will burden him with a steep ascent.
interpretation: The image of an arduous climb conveys an unrelenting, crushing ordeal: he will face hardship and punishment from which he cannot easily escape.

translation: Indeed, he thought and deliberated.
interpretation: The verse portrays a deliberate attempt to devise a misleading judgment about the Qur’an, rather than a sincere search for the truth.

translation: So may he be ruined! How cleverly he schemed!
interpretation: The verse is a severe rebuke of someone who deliberately weighed how to discredit the Qur’an: his calculated plotting is condemned as arrogant and false.

translation: Then may he perish—how he plotted!
interpretation: This is a forceful condemnation of someone who deliberately schemed to devise an accusation against the revelation; the wording underscores both the care he took in plotting and the blameworthiness of his intent.

translation: Then he looked.
interpretation: After deliberating over what to say about the Qur’an, he scrutinized it in search of a basis for rejecting it.

translation: Then he frowned and scowled.
interpretation: The verse portrays a man’s hostile reaction after weighing the Qur’an: instead of responding with openness, he lets displeasure show on his face, revealing the resistance of someone intent on rejecting its message.

translation: Then he turned away and grew arrogant.
interpretation: He rejected the truth after recognizing it, letting pride keep him from accepting guidance.

translation: Then he said, “This is nothing but magic passed down.”
interpretation: He dismisses the Qur’an as merely inherited or transmitted magic, alleging that it comes from human sources rather than divine revelation.

translation: This is nothing but the speech of a human being.
interpretation: The phrase voices the claim of those who rejected the Qur’an, dismissing it as human speech rather than revelation; in its context, it exposes their refusal to recognize its divine source.

translation: I will cast him into Saqar.
interpretation: Saqar is a name for Hell; the verse conveys the certainty and severity of the punishment awaiting the one being addressed.

translation: And what will make you know what Saqar is?
interpretation: This rhetorical question emphasizes that Saqar’s severity is beyond ordinary human understanding, preparing the listener to grasp the gravity of the warning that follows.

translation: It spares nothing and leaves nothing.
interpretation: The phrase conveys the relentless severity of Saqar: nothing can escape its punishment or remain untouched by it.

translation: Scorching human skin.
interpretation: The phrase depicts a fire whose punishment is so intense that it chars and alters the skin, conveying the severity of the warning.

translation: Over it are nineteen.
interpretation: The verse refers to nineteen appointed guardians over Hell, emphasizing that its affairs are governed by God’s command, not by human strength or control.

translation: We have appointed none but angels as the keepers of the Fire, and We have made their number only a trial for those who disbelieve: so that those given the Scripture may become certain, the believers may grow in faith, and neither those given the Scripture nor the believers may doubt; and so that those whose hearts are diseased and the disbelievers may say, “What does God mean by this example?” Thus God lets whoever He wills go astray and guides whoever He wills. None knows the forces of your Lord except Him. This is only a reminder to humankind.
interpretation: The mention of the angels and their number is a test that exposes how people respond to revelation: sincere believers take it as a reason to deepen their trust, while those resistant to faith turn it into an occasion for mockery and doubt. The verse cautions that the unseen realities of God’s power cannot be measured by human knowledge, and that this passage is meant to awaken people to the truth rather than satisfy idle speculation.

translation: No indeed! By the moon,
interpretation: The verse begins with a forceful denial and an oath by the moon, drawing attention to its ordered cycles as a sign of divine power and underscoring the seriousness of what follows.

translation: And by the night when it turns away,
interpretation: The night’s retreat points to the certainty of change: darkness does not endure, and the signs of God’s power and judgment will become clear in their appointed time.

translation: And by the morning when it grows bright,
interpretation: The dawn’s emergence from darkness serves as an image of clarity and certainty, underscoring the truth of the warning that follows.

translation: Indeed, it is one of the greatest (signs).
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the immense gravity of what has just been described, presenting it as a profound warning meant to awaken people to the consequences of rejecting the truth.

translation: A warning to humanity.
interpretation: It describes the Qur’an as a serious warning for all people, urging them to heed its guidance and turn away from what leads to ruin.

translation: For whoever among you wishes to advance or fall behind.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that each person chooses whether to hasten toward faith and obedience or hold back from them, and is accountable for that choice.

translation: Every soul is held in pledge for what it has earned.
interpretation: Each person is answerable for their deeds and remains bound to their consequences until God judges them.

translation: Except the people of the right.
interpretation: This refers to those whom God has granted salvation: they are not held accountable in the way of those who rejected Him, but are honored for their faith and obedience.

translation: In gardens, they will ask one another.
interpretation: The verse portrays the people of Paradise in peace and fellowship, freely conversing with one another in a place of lasting joy.

translation: About the criminals.
interpretation: The phrase refers to those guilty of wrongdoing; its precise meaning depends on the surrounding verse.

translation: What brought you into Saqar?
interpretation: The question directs attention to the choices and failures that led to punishment, urging reflection on their consequences.

translation: They will say, “We were not among those who prayed.”
interpretation: Their answer reveals that neglecting prayer was a sign of their turning away from worship and their relationship with God.

translation: And we did not used to feed the poor.
interpretation: Their words reveal that neglecting the needy was a sign of a deeper spiritual failure: they had abandoned compassion and the moral duties that faith requires.

translation: And we used to engage in vain talk with those who engaged in it.
interpretation: The phrase points to willingly joining others in falsehood and heedless talk, showing that following a crowd does not excuse a person from responsibility for what they take part in.

translation: And we used to deny the Day of Judgment.
interpretation: Their denial of the Day of Judgment reflects a refusal to face ultimate accountability, allowing them to live without regard for the consequences of their choices.

translation: Until death came to us.
interpretation: “The certainty” refers to death, whose arrival makes the reality of the Hereafter undeniable; the phrase describes people persisting in heedlessness until their opportunity to turn back has ended.

translation: So the intercession of intercessors will not benefit them.
interpretation: The verse warns that those who persist in rejecting faith and accountability cannot rely on anyone’s intercession to escape the consequences of their choices.

translation: So what is the matter with them that they turn away from the Reminder?
interpretation: The verse rebukes those who refuse the Qur’an’s admonition: their turning away is not for lack of guidance, but a deliberate refusal to heed it.

translation: As though they were startled wild donkeys,
interpretation: The image portrays people recoiling from the reminder in sudden, instinctive fear, like wild animals bolting from danger rather than calmly considering what they hear.

translation: Fleeing from a lion.
interpretation: The image conveys the intensity of their aversion to the reminder: they recoil from it as wild creatures flee from a predator.

translation: Rather, each one of them wants to be given scriptures laid open.
interpretation: Their demand for separate, visible scriptures reflects an unwillingness to accept the Qur’an as it has been revealed; they want revelation on their own terms.

translation: No indeed; rather, they do not fear the Hereafter.
interpretation: Their rejection of the reminder stems from lacking fear of the Hereafter and accountability before God.

translation: No indeed; it is a reminder.
interpretation: The Qur’an is a reminder that calls people to reflect and take heed; its guidance is available to whoever is willing to turn toward it.

translation: So whoever wills may remember it.
interpretation: The reminder is available to all, but its benefit comes to those who willingly turn their attention to it and take heed.

translation: And they will not take heed unless Allah wills. He is worthy of being mindful of, and worthy of granting forgiveness.
interpretation: The verse teaches that genuine receptiveness to guidance depends on Allah’s enabling, while affirming that He alone is fully deserving of reverence and uniquely able to grant forgiveness.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. No! I swear by the Day of Resurrection.
interpretation: The opening “No!” rejects the denial of resurrection, while the oath gives solemn emphasis to its certainty and the reality of the final reckoning.

translation: And I swear by the self-reproaching soul,
interpretation: The self-reproaching soul is the conscience that calls a person to account for wrongdoing and regrets falling short; its presence points to an inner awareness of moral responsibility.

translation: Does man think that We will never assemble his bones?
interpretation: The verse challenges the assumption that death makes resurrection impossible: even the body’s scattered bones are fully within God’s power to restore.

translation: Yes indeed, We are able to restore even his fingertips.
interpretation: The verse affirms that resurrection is no difficulty for God: His power extends to restoring a person in the finest detail, so the human body’s disintegration cannot make its return impossible.

translation: But man desires to persist in sin for the rest of his life.
interpretation: The verse points to a person’s wish to keep wrongdoing open before him, avoiding accountability by imagining he can repent or face its consequences later.

translation: He asks, “When is the Day of Resurrection?”
interpretation: The question is posed in a spirit of denial and mockery, as though demanding its date could undermine the certainty of the Resurrection. The verse points to the person’s disregard for the reality of accountability, not a sincere search for knowledge.

translation: So when sight is dazzled,
interpretation: At the onset of the Resurrection, terror and astonishment overwhelm people’s vision as they witness the reality of the Day of Judgment.

translation: And the moon is darkened.
interpretation: The verse evokes the upheaval of the Day of Resurrection, when even the moon’s familiar light is extinguished, reminding people that the world’s apparent stability will come to an end.

translation: And the sun and the moon are brought together.
interpretation: The verse portrays the upheaval of the Day of Judgment, when even the sun and moon no longer follow their familiar order, showing that the world as people know it has come to an end.

translation: That Day, the human being will say, “Where can I flee?”
interpretation: When confronted with the terrors of the Resurrection, a person will desperately seek somewhere to escape, but there will be no refuge from standing before God.

translation: No! There will be no refuge.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, no place will offer escape from God’s judgment; no one can evade accountability.

translation: To your Lord, on that Day, is the final abode.
interpretation: On the Day of Resurrection, every person’s ultimate return and reckoning will be with Allah; none can escape His judgment.

translation: On that Day, the human being will be informed of what he sent ahead and what he left behind.
interpretation: He will be made fully aware of his deeds and of the lasting effects of his choices, with nothing concealed or forgotten.

translation: Indeed, a person is a witness against himself.
interpretation: A person has an inward awareness of their own deeds and intentions, even when they try to conceal or excuse them.

translation: Even if he offers his excuses.
interpretation: A person knows the truth about their own deeds, and making excuses cannot conceal it from God—or from their own conscience.

translation: Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it.
interpretation: The verse reassures the Prophet not to hurry in repeating the revelation out of concern that he might forget it; he can listen calmly, trusting that God will preserve it for him.

translation: Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation.
interpretation: God assures the Prophet that He will preserve the revelation in his heart and enable him to recite it correctly.

translation: So when We have recited it, follow its recitation.
interpretation: God reassures the Prophet that once the revelation has been recited to him, he should follow it attentively and trust that its words will be preserved and made clear.

translation: Then, indeed, its clarification is incumbent upon Us.
interpretation: God assures the Prophet that He will make the revelation clear to him, guiding him to understand its meaning and message.

translation: No indeed! Rather, you love the immediate life.
interpretation: This is a rebuke of those who give precedence to worldly pleasures because they are near and tangible, while neglecting the lasting life to come.

translation: And you forsake the Hereafter.
interpretation: It reproaches those who turn away from the lasting life to come, giving their attention instead to worldly life.

translation: Some faces on that Day will be radiant.
interpretation: The verse depicts the faces of the blessed as shining with joy and hope on the Day of Resurrection.

translation: Gazing at their Lord.
interpretation: It describes the supreme honor granted to the righteous in the Hereafter: beholding their Lord, a vision that brings them joy and nearness beyond any worldly reward.

translation: And faces on that Day will be gloomy.
interpretation: Their gloom reflects the distress and humiliation of those who recognize that they are facing the consequences of their choices.

translation: They expect that a crushing calamity will befall them.
interpretation: The phrase portrays faces filled with dread, anticipating an ordeal so devastating that it breaks and overwhelms those who face it.

translation: No! When it reaches the collarbones,
interpretation: The verse evokes the moment of death, when the soul reaches the throat and a person’s worldly confidence and sense of control can no longer help them.

translation: And it is said, “Who can cure him?”
interpretation: As death draws near, those present ask whether anyone can provide healing, conveying their desperate search for help when the dying person’s final hour has come.

translation: And he realizes that it is the moment of parting.
interpretation: As death approaches, the person recognizes that he is leaving worldly life and all its attachments behind, crossing into what comes after.

translation: And one leg is entwined with the other.
interpretation: This depicts the severity of death’s agony, when a person’s strength fails and the legs draw together. It also evokes the passage from worldly life into the Hereafter, as the trials of one life give way to those of the next.

translation: On that Day, the journey will be toward your Lord.
interpretation: At life’s end, every person is brought inevitably before God; no one can turn aside from that final return.

translation: So he neither believed nor prayed.
interpretation: The verse portrays a person who turns away from the truth inwardly and fails to worship God outwardly.

translation: But he denied and turned away.
interpretation: It describes a deliberate rejection of the truth followed by turning away from its guidance and obligations.

translation: Then he went back to his people, strutting arrogantly.
interpretation: His swagger reflects the pride of someone who, having turned away from the truth, feels no remorse and behaves as though he has nothing to fear.

translation: Woe to you—indeed, woe!
interpretation: This is a stern warning to the one who rejects the truth: ruin and punishment are drawing near.

translation: Then woe to you—woe indeed!
interpretation: This is an emphatic threat: the person addressed is warned that ruin and punishment are drawing near, with the repetition intensifying the warning.

translation: Does man think that he will be left without purpose?
interpretation: The verse challenges the assumption that human life has no ultimate purpose or accountability: people are not abandoned, but will be brought back to God and answer for how they lived.

translation: Was he not a drop of semen emitted?
interpretation: The verse calls people to reflect on their humble beginning, showing that the One who brought them into existence from such a small origin is able to create them again.

translation: Then he became a clinging clot, and He created him and fashioned him in due proportion.
interpretation: The verse points to the human being’s ordered development as a sign of God’s power and wisdom, affirming that the One who fashioned him from such a humble beginning is able to bring him back to life.

translation: Then He made from it the two kinds: male and female.
interpretation: This points to God’s power to bring the diversity of human life from a single origin.

translation: Is He not able to give life to the dead?
interpretation: This rhetorical question affirms that the One who created human beings in the first place is fully able to resurrect them after death.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Has there ever come upon man a stretch of time when he was nothing worth mentioning?
interpretation: The verse invites people to reflect on their humble beginning: there was a time when they had no existence or renown. This calls for humility and recognition that human life and significance come from Allah.

translation: Indeed, We created the human being from a mingled drop, testing him, and made him hearing and seeing.
interpretation: The verse presents human life as both a gift and a moral trial: God gives a person the senses and awareness needed to recognize guidance and choose how to respond.

translation: Indeed, We guided him to the way, whether he is grateful or ungrateful.
interpretation: God has made the path clear, but guidance does not compel a person’s response; gratitude or rejection reflects the choice for which each person is accountable.

translation: Indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers chains, shackles, and a blazing fire.
interpretation: The verse warns that persistently rejecting God carries grave consequences. Its vivid imagery emphasizes the severity of the punishment and urges people to take accountability and choose faith and obedience.

translation: Indeed, the righteous will drink from a cup whose mixture is camphor.
interpretation: The verse portrays the reward awaiting the righteous in Paradise as pure and refreshing, with camphor evoking coolness and fragrance; it conveys the honor and delight God has prepared for them.

translation: A spring from which God’s servants drink, making it gush forth abundantly.
interpretation: The verse portrays the spring of Paradise as placed at the disposal of God’s faithful servants: they drink from it and cause its water to flow freely wherever they wish.

translation: They fulfill their vows and fear a Day whose hardship will spread far and wide.
interpretation: The verse portrays devotion as steadfastness in what one has pledged to God, sustained by a serious awareness of accountability. Their fear of the Day of Judgment is not despair, but a source of sincerity and perseverance in doing what is right.

translation: And they give food, despite their love for it, to the needy, the orphan, and the captive.
interpretation: Their generosity is sincere because they share food that they themselves value, seeking God’s pleasure rather than repayment or praise. The mention of the captive highlights compassion even toward someone who may be outside their own community.

translation: “We feed you only for the sake of Allah; we desire from you neither reward nor thanks.”
interpretation: True generosity is offered sincerely for Allah’s pleasure, without seeking repayment, praise, or even gratitude from those who receive it.

translation: Indeed, we fear from our Lord a day that is grim and intensely distressing.
interpretation: The speakers are mindful of the Day of Judgment and its severity; their fear of standing before God guides them to act sincerely and seek His approval.

translation: So Allah will protect them from the evil of that Day and grant them radiance and joy.
interpretation: The verse conveys that God’s care transforms the believers’ fear of the Day of Judgment into safety and gladness, with their inner happiness reflected in their faces.

translation: And He rewarded them for their patience with a Garden and silk.
interpretation: The verse teaches that steadfastness in faith and righteousness through hardship is met by God with generous honor and lasting comfort in Paradise.

translation: Reclining there upon couches, they will experience neither the heat of the sun nor bitter cold.
interpretation: The verse portrays Paradise as a place of complete comfort, free from the harsh extremes of temperature and the discomfort they bring.

translation: Its shade will be close over them, and its fruits will be made easy to reach.
interpretation: The verse evokes a reward marked by effortless comfort: in Paradise, blessings are not distant or difficult to obtain, but graciously brought within reach.

translation: Vessels of silver and cups like crystal are passed around among them.
interpretation: The refined, luminous serving vessels evoke the honor and exquisite delight of the people of Paradise, whose pleasures surpass the ordinary limits of worldly life.

translation: Crystal-clear vessels of silver, fashioned to exact measure.
interpretation: The vessels unite the clarity of crystal with the preciousness of silver, and their exact measure suggests a delight perfectly prepared for those who receive it.

translation: And they will be given to drink there from a cup blended with ginger.
interpretation: The mention of ginger evokes a distinctive, pleasing flavor: the drink is portrayed as a refined delight prepared for them in Paradise, where familiar pleasures are perfected beyond ordinary experience.

translation: A spring therein called Salsabil.
interpretation: Salsabil is the name of a spring in Paradise, evoking a drink that flows easily and is pleasing to drink.

translation: And there will circulate among them ever-youthful attendants; when you see them, you would think them scattered pearls.
interpretation: Their enduring youth and pearl-like radiance convey the purity, beauty, and gracious honor of the people of Paradise.

translation: And when you look there, you will see bliss and a great kingdom.
interpretation: The verse portrays the people of Paradise as granted a dignity and abundance beyond worldly measure: their joy is not fleeting, and their ‘great kingdom’ signifies the immense honor and freedom bestowed upon them by God.

translation: Upon them will be garments of fine green silk and brocade, and they will be adorned with bracelets of silver; and their Lord will give them a pure drink.
interpretation: The verse portrays the people of Paradise as honored with beauty and comfort, culminating in a drink given by their Lord. Its purity suggests a delight wholly free from harm or impurity, and the direct attribution to God emphasizes the intimacy and generosity of their reward.

translation: Indeed, this is your reward, and your striving has been appreciated.
interpretation: The verse conveys that God not only rewards sincere devotion but also acknowledges the effort behind it; no good deed is overlooked or treated as insignificant.

translation: Indeed, We have sent down the Qur’an to you in a gradual, deliberate revelation.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the Qur’an’s revelation comes from God with purpose and care, unfolding in a way that guides and strengthens the Prophet as he carries his mission.

translation: So be patient with your Lord’s decree, and do not obey any sinner or ingrate among them.
interpretation: Remain steadfast in carrying out God’s command, even when facing opposition, and do not let those who persist in wrongdoing or reject gratitude turn you from what is right.

translation: And remember the name of your Lord morning and evening.
interpretation: The verse calls for steady remembrance of God throughout the day, so that devotion is not confined to a single moment but shapes one’s heart and conduct from morning to evening.

translation: And during part of the night, prostrate before Him and glorify Him throughout the long night.
interpretation: The verse calls for sincere, sustained worship beyond the daylight hours, when quiet and solitude can help the heart turn more fully toward God.

translation: Indeed, these people love the life of this world and leave behind them a momentous day.
interpretation: The verse warns that attachment to immediate worldly pleasures can make people neglect the Day of Judgment, whose weight and consequences they will ultimately face.

translation: We created them and firmly fashioned their constitution; and, whenever We will, We can replace them with others like them, completely.
interpretation: Human beings owe their existence and strength to God, so they should not mistake their present security for independence. He can bring others in their place just as readily as He created them.

translation: Indeed, this is a reminder; so whoever wills may take a way to their Lord.
interpretation: The verse presents revelation as guidance that awakens people to their purpose and opens a path toward God. A person is called to choose that path through faith and obedience, rather than remain heedless.

translation: And you do not will unless Allah wills. Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: Human beings make choices, but their ability to will and act exists within Allah’s encompassing will. His knowledge and wisdom govern what He permits, without making human responsibility meaningless.

translation: He admits whom He wills into His mercy; and for the wrongdoers He has prepared a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse presents divine mercy and justice together: entry into God’s mercy is by His will, while those who persist in wrongdoing face the punishment prepared for them.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. By those sent forth in succession,
interpretation: The verse swears by the winds sent out one after another by God. Their ordered movement points to God’s power and prepares the listener for the solemn truth affirmed in the verses that follow.

translation: Then, by those that blow fiercely,
interpretation: The verse is commonly understood as an oath by powerful winds, whose force and movement display the Creator’s command and might.

translation: By those that spread widely,
interpretation: This is an oath by the angels who carry and disseminate God’s commands, affirming that the revelation they convey comes by His will and authority.

translation: Then by those that make a clear distinction,
interpretation: This oath refers to the angels who distinguish truth from falsehood by conveying God’s revelation and guidance.

translation: Then by those who convey a reminder,
interpretation: This refers to the angels who convey Allah’s revelation to the prophets, establishing that the reminder comes from God.

translation: As an excuse or a warning.
interpretation: The reminder is delivered to leave people with no valid excuse and to warn them of the consequences of rejecting it.

translation: Indeed, what you are promised is certain to come to pass.
interpretation: The emphatic wording calls the listener to treat God’s promise as an assured reality, not a distant possibility, and to live with accountability in view.

translation: Then, when the stars are blotted out,
interpretation: This portrays the Day of Judgment as a moment when the familiar order of the heavens is undone, leaving no created sign untouched by God’s command.

translation: And when the sky is split open,
interpretation: The splitting of the sky evokes the collapse of the familiar cosmic order at the Resurrection, revealing that the world’s stability is temporary and that all creation stands under God’s power and judgment.

translation: And when the mountains are blown away,
interpretation: This depicts the upheaval of the Day of Judgment, when even the mighty mountains lose their firmness and are scattered, showing that the familiar order of the world will be completely transformed.

translation: And when the messengers are gathered at their appointed time,
interpretation: This refers to the Day of Judgment, when God will assemble the messengers at the appointed time to bear witness concerning the peoples to whom they were sent.

translation: For what day was it appointed?
interpretation: The question emphasizes the gravity of the appointed time: the messengers’ gathering is set for the Day of Decision, when all people will be judged.

translation: For the Day of Decision.
interpretation: It refers to the appointed Day when God judges creation and distinguishes truth from falsehood.

translation: And what can make you know what the Day of Judgment is?
interpretation: This question magnifies the gravity of the Day when God decisively distinguishes truth from falsehood and judges every person with perfect justice—its reality is beyond ordinary human comprehension.

translation: Woe, on that Day, to those who deny the truth.
interpretation: This is a grave warning that those who persistently reject God’s truth will face severe consequences on the Day of Judgment.

translation: Have We not destroyed the former peoples?
interpretation: The rhetorical question warns those who reject God’s messengers to learn from earlier peoples: no community is beyond God’s judgment when it persists in defiance.

translation: Then We caused the others to follow them.
interpretation: The phrase points to successive generations meeting the same fate: those who came later followed the earlier rejecters in turning away from the messengers and facing God’s judgment.

translation: Thus do We deal with the criminals.
interpretation: The phrase points to a consistent divine way of requital: wrongdoing does not escape its consequences, and those who persist in it are dealt with justly.

translation: Woe, that Day, to those who deny the truth.
interpretation: This is a grave warning that those who persist in rejecting God’s truth will face ruin and regret on the Day of Judgment.

translation: Did We not create you from a humble fluid?
interpretation: The verse invites human beings to recognize the humility of their origin and, from that, to acknowledge the Creator’s power and their dependence on Him.

translation: Then We placed it in a secure resting place.
interpretation: The verse points to the protected place in the womb where human life develops, inviting reflection on Allah’s care and wisdom in creation.

translation: To a known, appointed measure.
interpretation: It points to a fixed and precisely determined limit, showing that what is described unfolds according to an order set by God.

translation: So We determined it—and excellent are We in determining.
interpretation: God’s determining is precise and purposeful: nothing in His creation is left to chance, and His power to ordain its measure and course is perfect.

translation: Woe, on that Day, to those who denied the truth.
interpretation: The repeated warning stresses that rejecting divine truth is not without consequence: on the Day of Judgment, denial will meet a grave and inescapable reckoning.

translation: Have We not made the earth a receptacle?
interpretation: The earth is made to gather and contain its inhabitants: the living dwell upon it, while the dead are laid within it. This points to the Creator’s power and care in providing a place for every stage of human life.

translation: The living and the dead.
interpretation: The phrase points to the earth as a dwelling that holds people during life and receives them after death.

translation: And We placed therein towering mountains, and gave you sweet, refreshing water to drink.
interpretation: The verse points to God’s care in providing both stability in the earth and life-sustaining water, inviting people to recognize these blessings as signs of His power and generosity.

translation: Woe, on that Day, to those who deny the truth.
interpretation: The verse warns that rejecting divine truth is not a harmless choice: it carries grave consequences when each person is held accountable before God.

translation: Proceed to that which you used to deny.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, those who rejected the promised punishment are told to face the reality they had denied. The command underscores that their denial has not made the warning any less true.

translation: Proceed to a shade with three branches.
interpretation: The verse describes a grim, deceptive “shade”: not a refuge from heat, but a spreading mass of smoke that offers no comfort or protection.

translation: Neither providing shade nor protecting from the flames.
interpretation: What appears to be shelter offers no true refuge: it cannot shield those facing punishment from the fire.

translation: Indeed, it throws sparks as huge as castles.
interpretation: The image likens the fire’s sparks to towering castles, conveying the terrifying scale and force of its blaze—something far beyond the small sparks people ordinarily know.

translation: As though they were yellow camels.
interpretation: The comparison evokes sparks that are immense and striking in color, making the scene vivid and fearsome.

translation: Woe, on that Day, to those who deny the truth.
interpretation: The verse warns that those who knowingly reject God’s truth will face grave consequences on the Day of Judgment.

translation: This is a Day on which they will not speak.
interpretation: The verse portrays the terror and helplessness of the Day of Judgment: those being judged will be unable to speak in their own defense at this moment, as all authority belongs to God.

translation: Nor will they be given permission to offer excuses.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, those being condemned will have no opportunity to plead their case; the truth of their deeds will be clear, and excuses will avail them nothing.

translation: Woe, on that Day, to those who deny the truth.
interpretation: This is a grave warning that denying God’s truth and the coming judgment is not without consequence; the Day of reckoning will expose that denial and bring its deserved outcome.

translation: This is the Day of Decision; We have gathered you and the peoples of old.
interpretation: The verse underscores that no generation escapes accountability: those addressed and the peoples who came before them are brought together before God for judgment.

translation: So if you have a plan, then carry it out against Me.
interpretation: This is a rhetorical challenge that exposes the deniers’ inability to escape God’s judgment: no scheme of theirs can thwart His power.

translation: Woe, on that Day, to those who deny.
interpretation: This is a warning that those who persistently reject God’s truth will face a grave reckoning on the Day of Judgment.

translation: Indeed, the God-conscious will be amid shades and springs.
interpretation: The verse assures those who are mindful of God that they will find lasting comfort and security in the Hereafter, surrounded by shade and flowing springs as a gift of divine mercy.

translation: And fruits of whatever they desire.
interpretation: This portrays the abundance and ease of the people of Paradise: they will find the fruits they long for, without hardship or deprivation.

translation: Eat and drink with enjoyment for what you used to do.
interpretation: This is a welcome to the people of Paradise: they are invited to enjoy its blessings as a gracious reward for their righteous deeds.

translation: Indeed, this is how We reward those who do good.
interpretation: God’s way is to repay sincere goodness with a fitting reward, so doing what is right is never lost with Him.

translation: Woe, that Day, to those who deny the truth.
interpretation: This is a stern warning that denying God’s message is not a matter without consequence; the Day of Judgment will bring the deniers face to face with the truth they rejected.

translation: Eat and enjoy yourselves for a little while; indeed, you are guilty of wrongdoing.
interpretation: This is a rebuke and a warning, not an endorsement of wrongdoing: those who persist in sin may enjoy worldly pleasures briefly, but that enjoyment is fleeting and does not spare them from accountability.

translation: Woe, that Day, to the deniers.
interpretation: This is a grave warning that those who reject the truth will face judgment and loss on the Day of Resurrection.

translation: And when it is said to them, “Bow down,” they do not bow.
interpretation: Their refusal to bow reflects a proud rejection of worship and submission to God, even when they are called to do so.

translation: Woe, that Day, to those who deny.
interpretation: The verse warns that those who reject the truth will face severe loss when they are held accountable before God.

translation: Then what message after it will they believe in?
interpretation: The verse challenges those who reject the Qur’an: if they will not believe in this clear revelation, no further message is likely to persuade them.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. About what are they asking one another?
interpretation: This opening question draws attention to the people’s dispute over a momentous matter—the great news that the following verse identifies—and signals its importance.

translation: About the momentous news,
interpretation: It refers to the Resurrection—the great event people disputed and questioned, though it is certain to come.

translation: That about which they disagree.
interpretation: It refers to a matter whose truth is disputed among people; their differing views do not, by themselves, change its reality.

translation: No indeed! They will soon know.
interpretation: This is a forceful warning to those who dismiss the truth: their denial will not prevent the reality from becoming unmistakably clear to them.

translation: Then, no indeed—they will come to know.
interpretation: This is a stern warning that those disputing the resurrection will discover its reality with certainty, but only when the truth can no longer be denied.

translation: Have We not made the earth a resting place?
interpretation: The verse invites reflection on the earth as a place made stable and habitable, prepared to support human life.

translation: And the mountains as pegs.
interpretation: The mountains are likened to pegs, suggesting that they are firmly set in the earth and serve as part of its ordered stability.

translation: And We created you in pairs.
interpretation: This points to God’s wisdom in creating human beings as male and female, with a natural complementarity that makes companionship and the continuation of human life possible.

translation: And We made your sleep a means of rest.
interpretation: Sleep is a mercy from God: it brings relief from the strain of wakefulness and renews a person’s strength.

translation: And We made the night a covering.
interpretation: The night is likened to a garment that envelops and conceals, offering creation a time of quiet and repose.

translation: And We made the day for livelihood.
interpretation: The day is presented as a provision from God: its light and activity give people the opportunity to work, seek sustenance, and attend to their needs.

translation: And We built above you seven mighty heavens.
interpretation: The seven heavens are portrayed as firmly established and powerful, inviting reflection on the Creator’s majesty and the order of creation.

translation: And We made a blazing lamp.
interpretation: This refers to the sun, whose intense light and heat are among the signs of God’s power and provision.

translation: And We sent down from the rain-bearing clouds abundant, pouring water.
interpretation: The verse points to God’s power and mercy in sending down rain in abundance, a provision through which the earth and its creatures are sustained.

translation: So that We may bring forth by it grain and vegetation.
interpretation: The rain is presented as a means through which God brings forth the provisions that sustain life, inviting reflection on His power to nurture the earth and its creatures.

translation: And luxuriant, densely intertwined gardens.
interpretation: The phrase evokes abundant growth, with foliage and branches woven together, portraying the gardens as richly flourishing.

translation: Indeed, the Day of Decision is an appointed time.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the final judgment will arrive at the time God has decreed; it is certain, not subject to human control or postponement.

translation: The Day the Trumpet is blown, and you will come forth in multitudes.
interpretation: The verse depicts the resurrection as a moment when all people are raised and gathered together, arriving in great numbers to face God’s judgment.

translation: And the heaven will be opened, becoming gateways.
interpretation: The verse depicts the heavens transformed at the Resurrection, as the familiar order of the cosmos gives way to the reality of divine judgment.

translation: And the mountains are set in motion, becoming a mirage.
interpretation: The verse portrays the upheaval of the Day of Resurrection: even the mountains, symbols of firmness, will lose their apparent solidity and disappear from sight. It warns against mistaking the permanence of the present world for something lasting.

translation: Indeed, Hell is lying in wait.
interpretation: Hell is portrayed as an unavoidable reckoning, ready to receive those who persist in rejecting God’s guidance; no one can evade the justice that awaits them.

translation: A destination for the transgressors.
interpretation: Those who persist in rebellion against God are warned that they will ultimately return to an abode of punishment.

translation: Remaining therein for ages.
interpretation: The phrase conveys an extended, successive duration of punishment, emphasizing how long they remain in that place.

translation: They will taste no coolness there, nor any drink.
