interpretation: The verse portrays a state of unrelieved torment: they will find neither the comfort of coolness nor anything to quench their thirst.

translation: Except scalding water and foul, festering fluid.
interpretation: The verse portrays the drink of the condemned as torment rather than relief: one burns with heat, while the other is repulsive and harmful.

translation: A fitting recompense.
interpretation: Their recompense will correspond to what they earned, justly matching their deeds.

translation: Indeed, they did not expect an accounting.
interpretation: Their disregard for the reckoning reflects a life lived without expecting to answer to God, leaving them heedless of the consequences of their choices.

translation: And they utterly denied Our signs.
interpretation: Their rejection was not a passing doubt; they persistently treated God’s clear signs as false, refusing to heed the truth they conveyed.

translation: And We have recorded everything in a book.
interpretation: Nothing escapes God’s complete knowledge or precise record; every matter is preserved and accounted for.

translation: So taste [the punishment]; We will increase you in nothing but torment.
interpretation: The verse conveys the finality of punishment for those who persisted in rejecting the truth: there is no relief or improvement ahead, only an increase in suffering. Its stark wording serves as a warning to turn back before that outcome is reached.

translation: Indeed, for the God-conscious there is triumph.
interpretation: The verse assures those who remain mindful of God that their steadfastness will lead to lasting success and deliverance.

translation: Gardens and grapevines
interpretation: The phrase evokes abundant, flourishing provision as a sign of the delights prepared for the righteous.

translation: And full-bosomed maidens, well-matched in age.
interpretation: The verse portrays the companions of Paradise as possessing youthful beauty and being alike in age, evoking harmony and fitting companionship in the life to come.

translation: And a cup filled to the brim,
interpretation: The cup’s fullness evokes an abundant, generous provision in Paradise, with no shortage or deprivation.

translation: They will hear therein neither idle talk nor falsehood.
interpretation: The verse portrays Paradise as a place of perfect peace, where speech is free from anything futile, hurtful, or untrue.

translation: A reward from your Lord—a generous gift, fully sufficient.
interpretation: The reward is bestowed by God as a complete and abundant gift, enough to satisfy its recipients fully.

translation: The Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them—the Most Merciful. They will have no power to address Him.
interpretation: All creation is under God’s dominion and mercy, yet no one can speak before Him on their own authority; any address to Him depends entirely on His permission.

translation: The Day the Spirit and the angels stand in rows; none will speak except one whom the Most Merciful permits and who speaks rightly.
interpretation: The verse conveys that all authority on the Day of Judgment belongs to God: even the greatest of His creatures cannot speak or intercede independently. Any speech must be permitted by Him and truthful, underscoring the humility and accountability of every being before Him.

translation: That is the Day of Truth; so whoever wills may take a way back to his Lord.
interpretation: The Day of Judgment is an undeniable reality, and a person can prepare for it by choosing faith and obedience as a path back to God.

translation: Indeed, We have warned you of a punishment near at hand: the Day when each person will see what his hands have sent ahead, and the disbeliever will say, “Would that I were dust!”
interpretation: The verse conveys the urgency of moral accountability: what people do in this life will become unmistakably clear, leaving no room to undo it. The disbeliever’s wish to be dust expresses the depth of regret at facing that truth, and warns the living not to postpone turning toward what is right.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. By those who pull out forcefully.
interpretation: This is an oath by the angels who wrench the souls of the wicked from their bodies with great force.

translation: By those who draw forth gently,
interpretation: The verse is understood as an oath by the angels who gently draw the souls of the faithful from their bodies, pointing to the solemn passage from earthly life toward what follows.

translation: And by those who glide swiftly, moving with ease.
interpretation: This oath points to the angels as they swiftly carry out the commands entrusted to them, their effortless movement reflecting the precision and obedience with which God’s order is fulfilled.

translation: Then those who race ahead, outstripping all others.
interpretation: This refers to the angels hastening to carry out God’s commands, in complete obedience and without delay.

translation: And by those who direct affairs,
interpretation: This refers to angels who carry out the affairs entrusted to them by God, acting only by His command and permission.

translation: On the Day when the first blast shakes everything.
interpretation: It refers to the first blast of the Trumpet, whose tremendous shaking marks the onset of the Resurrection and the collapse of the world as people know it.

translation: The second blast will follow it.
interpretation: It describes the second blast of the Trumpet following the first, marking the next stage in the events of resurrection.

translation: Hearts on that Day will be trembling.
interpretation: The verse portrays the profound fear that will seize people as they face the Resurrection and its reckoning, a dread felt deep within the heart.

translation: Their eyes will be downcast.
interpretation: Their lowered gaze reflects the fear and humiliation of those confronted with the overwhelming reality of the Hereafter.

translation: They say, “Will we really be returned to our former state?”
interpretation: Their question expresses disbelief in resurrection: they find it inconceivable that, after death and decay, they could be restored to the life they knew before.

translation: “When we have become decayed bones?”
interpretation: The words voice the deniers’ incredulity at being brought back to life after their bodies have decayed, as though such a return were beyond God’s power.

translation: They say, “That, then, would be a losing return.”
interpretation: The deniers sarcastically dismiss the prospect of being raised from the dead, treating resurrection as an absurd and ruinous outcome rather than a truth for which they will be held accountable.

translation: It will be but one blast.
interpretation: The phrase emphasizes that resurrection is effortless for God: a single divine command is sufficient to bring it about.

translation: Then suddenly they will be upon the surface of the earth.
interpretation: The verse conveys the suddenness of resurrection: those who thought they had vanished will be brought back to life and present on the open earth, with no escape from standing before God.

translation: Has the story of Moses come to you?
interpretation: This rhetorical question draws attention to Moses’ account and invites reflection on the signs of God and the guidance conveyed through His messengers.

translation: When his Lord called him in the sacred valley of Ṭuwā,
interpretation: The verse recalls God’s direct call to Moses in a sanctified place, showing that his prophetic mission began through God’s choosing and command.

translation: Go to Pharaoh; indeed, he has transgressed.
interpretation: Moses is being sent to confront Pharaoh because his power has led him beyond all bounds. The verse frames this mission as a call to challenge tyranny and summon its ruler back to obedience to God.

translation: Then say, “Would you be willing to purify yourself?”
interpretation: The question is a gentle invitation to Pharaoh to cleanse himself of disbelief and arrogance by turning to faith and obedience to God.

translation: And I will guide you to your Lord, so that you may fear Him.
interpretation: The promise of guidance is meant to lead to reverent awareness of God—an awareness that humbles a person and turns them toward obedience.

translation: Then he showed him the greatest sign.
interpretation: The sign was a manifest proof of God’s power, given to Moses to call Pharaoh to recognize the truth.

translation: So he denied and disobeyed.
interpretation: The verse portrays a deliberate rejection of the truth and refusal to obey God’s command.

translation: Then he turned away, striving.
interpretation: Pharaoh turned away from the truth and energetically set about opposing Moses, revealing that his rejection was deliberate and active.

translation: Then he gathered [his people] and called out.
interpretation: The phrase portrays Pharaoh turning his power outward: he assembled the people and addressed them publicly, setting the stage for his arrogant claim to supreme authority.

translation: So he said, “I am your highest lord.”
interpretation: He arrogantly claimed ultimate authority over his people, presenting himself as supreme and denying any authority above him.

translation: So Allah seized him with an exemplary punishment in this life and the Hereafter.
interpretation: Pharaoh’s fate stands as a warning that no ruler can escape God’s justice, and that wrongdoing carries consequences both in this world and in the next.

translation: Indeed, in that is a lesson for whoever fears Allah.
interpretation: A heart mindful of Allah can discern guidance in the signs and events around it, letting them deepen its reverence and steer it away from wrongdoing.

translation: Are you more difficult to create, or the heaven? He built it.
interpretation: The verse challenges human pride by directing attention to the immense heaven: the One who brought it into being is not powerless to create human beings again.

translation: He raised its height and fashioned it perfectly.
interpretation: The verse points to God’s power and wisdom: the heavens are not a disorderly expanse, but a creation raised and made with harmony and proportion.

translation: And He made its night dark and brought forth its daylight.
interpretation: The verse points to God’s power in setting the balance of night and day, bringing darkness and light into creation by His command.

translation: And after that, He spread out the earth.
interpretation: The verse describes God making the earth expansive and prepared for life and habitation, bringing its surface into a form suited to its creatures.

translation: He brought forth from it its water and its pasture.
interpretation: The verse points to God’s power and care in making the earth yield the water and vegetation on which life depends.

translation: And the mountains—He set them firmly in place.
interpretation: The verse points to God’s power and wisdom in establishing the earth’s features, presenting the mountains as part of the ordered world prepared for life.

translation: As provision for you and your livestock.
interpretation: This phrase points to God’s provision for human beings and their animals, making the means of life a benefit shared by both.

translation: Then, when the greatest calamity comes,
interpretation: “The greatest calamity” refers to the Day of Resurrection, whose overwhelming reality will eclipse every worldly concern and bring people face to face with the consequences of their deeds.

translation: On the Day when a person will remember what they strove for,
interpretation: The verse points to the moment when a person fully recognizes the meaning and consequences of their choices. What may have seemed distant or forgotten in worldly life will become unmistakable, calling each person to face their deeds with honesty.

translation: And Hellfire will be brought into view for all to see.
interpretation: Its reality and the fate awaiting its people will be made unmistakably clear; nothing will remain hidden from those who witness it.

translation: As for the one who transgressed…
interpretation: This refers to someone who exceeds the limits set by God, acting arrogantly and without regard for accountability.

translation: And prefers the life of this world.
interpretation: This describes choosing the fleeting pleasures and interests of worldly life over what is lasting with God.

translation: Then indeed, Hell is the abode.
interpretation: This warns that Hell is the ultimate dwelling place of the person described in the preceding verse.

translation: As for whoever feared standing before his Lord and restrained the soul from its desires,
interpretation: This describes a person whose awareness of answering to God leads them to resist desires that would draw them into wrongdoing, choosing obedience and accountability over immediate gratification.

translation: For indeed, Paradise is the abode.
interpretation: Paradise is presented as the lasting home and refuge—the final place of security and reward for those whom God admits into it.

translation: They ask you about the Hour: “When will it arrive?”
interpretation: The question concerns the exact time of the Final Hour, whose timing is beyond human knowledge and is not for the Prophet to determine.

translation: What have you to do with mentioning it?
interpretation: The question turns attention away from demanding the Hour’s timing: its knowledge belongs to God, and the Prophet’s role is to warn people about it, not to disclose when it will occur.

translation: To your Lord is its final end.
interpretation: The ultimate knowledge and determination of the Hour belong to God alone; human beings are not given authority over its timing.

translation: You are only a warner to whoever fears it.
interpretation: The Prophet’s role is to warn people of the Hour; those mindful of its coming are the ones most likely to heed the warning.

translation: On the Day they see it, it will be as though they had remained only for an evening or its morning.
interpretation: When they witness the Resurrection, the life they spent in this world will seem to them astonishingly brief—no more than part of a day—because the reality before them will make their former years feel fleeting.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. He frowned and turned away.
interpretation: The verse conveys a gentle divine correction: a sincere seeker of guidance should not be overlooked in favor of people of worldly status. A person’s spiritual worth is not measured by their influence or rank.

translation: When the blind man came to him
interpretation: The phrase refers to the blind man’s arrival, which prompted the moment of divine correction described in the surrounding verses. It highlights that a person’s sincere desire for guidance matters more than status or outward appearance.

translation: And what could make you know? Perhaps he would be purified.
interpretation: The verse teaches that a person who sincerely seeks guidance may be brought nearer to spiritual purity, even when their worth or potential is not immediately apparent.

translation: Or be reminded, and the reminder benefit him.
interpretation: The verse points to the value of sincere receptivity: a reminder can guide and benefit someone who is willing to take heed.

translation: As for the one who considers himself self-sufficient,
interpretation: The verse points to the danger of imagined self-sufficiency: when someone believes they have no need of God or guidance, that pride can make them unreceptive to the truth.

translation: Yet you give him your attention.
interpretation: The verse gently corrects giving special attention to someone because of his standing or perceived influence, reminding that sincere seekers deserve care regardless of their social status.

translation: And you are not responsible if he does not purify himself.
interpretation: The verse teaches that a caller to faith is responsible for conveying guidance, not for compelling someone to accept it or become spiritually purified.

translation: And as for the one who came to you, striving…
interpretation: It refers to someone who came earnestly seeking guidance, showing that sincere eagerness to learn deserves attentive care.

translation: while he is fearful
interpretation: His fear of God reflects a sincere, humble heart, making him attentive to guidance.

translation: Then you are distracted from him.
interpretation: The verse gently corrects the turning of attention away from a sincere seeker of guidance in favor of people who regard themselves as self-sufficient. Their status should not outweigh a person’s genuine desire to learn and be guided.

translation: No indeed, it is a reminder.
interpretation: The revelation is a reminder that calls people to reflect and take heed; its guidance is available to whoever sincerely seeks it.

translation: So whoever wills may take heed of it.
interpretation: The reminder is offered openly, but its guidance is embraced by those who choose to turn their attention to it.

translation: In honored pages,
interpretation: The revelation is portrayed as possessing a sacred dignity: it is preserved and held in honor, not treated as ordinary human speech.

translation: Exalted and purified.
interpretation: The phrase describes honored, elevated pages kept pure from falsehood and defilement, reflecting the sacred dignity of the revelation they contain.

translation: In the hands of scribes,
interpretation: The passage portrays the revelation as entrusted to noble scribes, emphasizing its honored and carefully preserved transmission.

translation: Noble and righteous.
interpretation: The phrase describes the bearers of revelation as honored and wholly obedient to God, distinguished by their purity and uprightness.

translation: May man be destroyed! How ungrateful he is!
interpretation: This is a stern rebuke of human beings who deny their Creator and fail to recognize the blessings and signs placed before them.

translation: From what thing did He create him?
interpretation: This rhetorical question calls the human being to reflect on the humble origin of his creation and recognize that his existence is entirely dependent on God.

translation: From a drop of fluid He created him, then proportioned him.
interpretation: The verse points to God’s power and wisdom: He brings a human being from a humble beginning and gives him a measured form and constitution.

translation: Then He made the way easy for him.
interpretation: God made the passage from the womb into the world easy for the human being, despite his helplessness.

translation: Then He causes him to die and provides him with a burial.
interpretation: The verse points to God’s care over human life even at its end: death and the dignity of burial are part of His ordering of human existence.

translation: Then, when He wills, He will raise him again.
interpretation: The verse affirms that resurrection is wholly subject to God’s will: just as He brought the human being into existence, He will restore him to life at the appointed time.

translation: No indeed! He has not yet fulfilled what He commanded him.
interpretation: This is a rebuke to the human being: despite God’s gifts and care, he has not fully carried out the duties of faith and obedience entrusted to him.

translation: So let the human being consider his food.
interpretation: The verse invites people to reflect on the origin and provision of what sustains them, recognizing in it a sign of divine care and a reason for gratitude.

translation: Indeed, We pour down water abundantly.
interpretation: The verse draws attention to rain as a deliberate act of divine provision, sustaining life and inviting reflection on the care by which the earth is made fruitful.

translation: Then We split the earth open, splitting it apart.
interpretation: The verse points to God’s power in bringing life forth from the soil: the earth opens so that plants may emerge, providing sustenance by His command.

translation: So We caused grain to grow in it.
interpretation: The growth of grain points to God’s power to bring nourishment from the earth and sustain life through its provision.

translation: And grapes, and fresh herbage.
interpretation: The verse points to Allah’s provision of grapes for people and tender fodder for livestock, showing how sustenance is made available for both.

translation: And olives and date palms,
interpretation: The mention of these familiar crops draws attention to the care and provision through which God sustains human life.

translation: And luxuriant, densely grown gardens.
interpretation: The phrase evokes abundant, flourishing provision and invites reflection on the generosity behind the natural world.

translation: And fruit and herbage.
interpretation: The verse points to the care woven into creation: the earth’s growth provides nourishment for people and grazing for animals, sustaining life through varied forms of provision.

translation: As provision for you and your livestock.
interpretation: The phrase points to these blessings as sustenance made available for human life and for the animals people depend on.

translation: Then, when the Deafening Blast comes…
interpretation: The phrase refers to the overwhelming blast of the Day of Resurrection, whose terror is so immense that it deafens and shakes all who hear it.

translation: On that Day, a person will flee from his brother.
interpretation: The verse depicts the overwhelming terror of the Day of Resurrection: each person will be so consumed by their own reckoning that even the closest family ties cannot draw their attention away or offer reassurance.

translation: And his mother and his father,
interpretation: The mention of a person’s closest family underscores the overwhelming terror of the Day of Judgment: each person will be so absorbed in their own fate that even those dearest to them will not occupy their attention.

translation: And his wife and his sons,
interpretation: The phrase conveys the sinner’s desperation on the Day of Judgment: he would wish to give up even his closest loved ones as a ransom to escape the punishment.

translation: That Day, each person among them will have a concern that preoccupies him completely.
interpretation: The verse conveys the intensity of the Day of Judgment: each person will be so absorbed in facing their own reckoning and its consequences that they will have no attention to spare for anyone else.

translation: Faces on that Day will be radiant.
interpretation: Their radiance signifies the joy and reassurance of those who meet their Lord with faith and are pleased with the outcome of their deeds.

translation: Laughing, rejoicing.
interpretation: The phrase conveys a joy so evident that it shines through in their faces, reflecting the reassurance and delight of those granted a favorable outcome in the Hereafter.

translation: And faces that Day will be covered with dust,
interpretation: The dust signifies humiliation and distress on the Day of Judgment, when some faces will bear the outward signs of their sorrow and disgrace.

translation: A gloom will overwhelm them.
interpretation: The phrase portrays a darkness and abasement that envelops their faces, expressing their distress and disgrace.

translation: Those are the disbelievers, the wicked.
interpretation: The phrase describes those who reject faith and persist in wrongdoing, joining denial of God with corrupt conduct.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. When the sun is folded up,
interpretation: The verse evokes the collapse of the familiar order of creation: even the sun, seemingly constant and powerful, is subject to God’s command. Its transformation signals the certainty of the Resurrection and reminds people that worldly stability is not everlasting.

translation: And when the stars are dimmed and scattered,
interpretation: The verse evokes the collapse of the familiar cosmic order, reminding people that the universe is not permanent or independent: its Creator can overturn it, and humanity must face the final judgment.

translation: And when the mountains are set in motion,
interpretation: The verse evokes the collapse of what seems most permanent: at the Resurrection, even the mountains will lose their stability, showing that the familiar order of the world will be transformed.

translation: And when pregnant she-camels are left unattended,
interpretation: Even the most prized possessions will be abandoned when the terror of the Resurrection overwhelms people.

translation: And when the wild animals are gathered together,
interpretation: The verse evokes the upheaval of the Last Day: even creatures that ordinarily live apart will be brought together, showing that no part of creation lies beyond God’s power to resurrect and assemble.

translation: And when the seas are set ablaze,
interpretation: The verse evokes the upheaval of the Last Day, when even the vast seas are transformed by God’s command, signaling that the world’s familiar order is coming to an end.

translation: And when the souls are joined with their bodies,
interpretation: This describes the resurrection, when every soul is reunited with its body and brought forward for judgment. The pairing marks the restoration of each person for accountability before God.

translation: And when the girl buried alive is asked,
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, the girl killed by burial will be asked—not because she bears any blame, but to make her killers’ injustice plain and expose the horror of what they did.

translation: For what sin was she killed?
interpretation: The question exposes the injustice of killing an innocent girl: she had committed no sin that could justify her death. By giving the victim a voice, the verse confronts her killers with their crime and its accountability before God.

translation: And when the records are spread open,
interpretation: This portrays the Day of Judgment, when people’s records of deeds are opened and made visible, leaving nothing hidden from God’s judgment.

translation: And when the sky is stripped away,
interpretation: The verse evokes the collapse of the familiar cosmic order on the Day of Resurrection: the sky, once a sheltering canopy, is removed, leaving creation exposed to the reality of divine judgment.

translation: And when Hellfire is set ablaze,
interpretation: The image conveys the terrifying reality of divine judgment: the consequences of human choices will become fully manifest, leaving no room to dismiss accountability.

translation: And when Paradise is brought near,
interpretation: Its being brought near signifies that, on the Day of Judgment, Paradise will be made ready and accessible to its people, marking the fulfillment of God’s promise and their honor.

translation: Then every soul will know what it has brought forth.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, each person will recognize the deeds they brought with them and face their true significance.

translation: So I swear by the stars that recede and disappear.
interpretation: The verse draws attention to the hidden, ordered movements of the heavens as a sign of God’s power and a solemn affirmation of what follows.

translation: Those that move along their courses and disappear from sight.
interpretation: The phrase points to celestial bodies whose movement follows a precise order and whose appearance and disappearance invite reflection on the Creator’s power and wisdom.

translation: By the night as it draws to a close,
interpretation: The verse calls attention to the night’s turning point, when darkness begins to recede and dawn approaches, inviting reflection on the order and change woven into creation.

translation: By the dawn as it breathes forth.
interpretation: The dawn is portrayed as coming to life: light gradually spreads after darkness, a sign of God’s power to bring renewal and transformation.

translation: Indeed, it is the word of a noble messenger.
interpretation: The Qur’an is being affirmed as revelation conveyed by a noble, trustworthy messenger—not something invented by a poet or soothsayer.

translation: Possessing great strength, and held in an honored station with the Lord of the Throne.
interpretation: The verse portrays Gabriel as powerful and honored in nearness to God, affirming the trustworthiness and dignity of the messenger who conveys revelation.

translation: Obeyed there, and trustworthy.
interpretation: The verse describes Gabriel as honored and obeyed among the angels, and utterly faithful in conveying God’s revelation.

translation: And your companion is not mad.
interpretation: The verse rejects the accusation of madness against the Prophet, affirming that his message is not the product of delusion but should be received with seriousness and discernment.

translation: And he certainly saw him on the clear horizon.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the Prophet ﷺ saw Gabriel plainly in his true form, assuring that the revelation came through a real encounter and was not imagined.

translation: And he is not withholding knowledge of the unseen.
interpretation: The Prophet does not keep back any of the revelation entrusted to him; he conveys what God reveals faithfully and completely.

translation: And it is not the word of an accursed devil.
interpretation: The verse rejects the claim that the Qur’an comes from satanic influence: its source is not an outcast devil, but divine revelation.

translation: So where are you going?
interpretation: This is a searching rebuke to those who turn away from the Qur’an: when the truth has been made clear, what path could they choose that leads them away from it?

translation: It is only a reminder to all the worlds.
interpretation: The Qur’an is a reminder and guidance offered to all people, calling them to reflect and turn toward what is right.

translation: For whoever among you wishes to follow the straight path.
interpretation: The guidance is open to anyone who sincerely chooses uprightness and seeks to follow it.

translation: And you do not will unless Allah wills—the Lord of all worlds.
interpretation: Human choice is real, yet it is never independent of God: every capacity and opportunity to choose exists within His encompassing will and sustaining authority.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. When the sky is split open,
interpretation: The image portrays the familiar order of the universe giving way at the Resurrection, reminding us that even the heavens are subject to Allah’s command and that worldly life will not endure forever.

translation: And when the stars are scattered,
interpretation: The verse evokes the collapse of the ordered cosmos at the onset of the Resurrection, when even the heavens’ familiar lights no longer remain in their appointed places.

translation: And when the seas are made to burst forth,
interpretation: This describes the upheaval of the Day of Resurrection, when the seas will overflow and their boundaries will be undone, as the familiar order of creation is transformed.

translation: And when the graves are turned inside out,
interpretation: The image portrays the Day of Resurrection, when the dead emerge from their resting places and what was hidden is brought into the open before God.

translation: A soul will know what it sent ahead and what it left behind.
interpretation: When the truth is unveiled, each person will recognize both the deeds they performed and the lasting effects their actions set in motion, with nothing hidden or forgotten.

translation: O human being, what has deceived you about your Generous Lord?
interpretation: This is a searching rebuke: what has made you careless of your duty to God, despite His generosity toward you? It calls you to recognize that His kindness should inspire gratitude and obedience, not complacency.

translation: Who created you, fashioned you, and proportioned you,
interpretation: The verse draws attention to the care and wisdom in God’s creation of each person: human form and faculties are deliberately shaped in fitting balance, not brought about by chance.

translation: In whatever form He willed, He fashioned you.
interpretation: Your form is not accidental: God shaped you as He willed, showing His power and wisdom in the way He creates.

translation: No indeed! Rather, you deny the Judgment.
interpretation: The verse rebukes those who assume that God’s generosity means they will not be held accountable. It identifies denial of the final reckoning as the source of their heedlessness and disregard for their deeds.

translation: And indeed, over you are guardians.
interpretation: This verse teaches that human actions are not lost or forgotten: appointed watchers preserve them, reminding people that their lives unfold under divine knowledge and that they are accountable for what they do.

translation: Noble scribes.
interpretation: This describes the angels entrusted with recording human deeds as honorable and trustworthy, affirming that people’s actions are faithfully witnessed and preserved.

translation: They know what you do.
interpretation: The verse points to the watchful recording angels: no deed is hidden from them, reminding people that their actions are accountable.

translation: Indeed, the righteous are surely in bliss.
interpretation: The verse assures those who live righteously that their goodness leads to lasting felicity with God, beyond the hardships of worldly life.

translation: And indeed, the wicked will surely be in Hellfire.
interpretation: The verse warns that persistent wrongdoing and defiance of God have a grave consequence, urging people to turn from sin before they are held accountable.

translation: They will burn in it on the Day of Recompense.
interpretation: The verse portrays the punishment as a certain consequence that will confront them when they are judged.

translation: And they will not be absent from it.
interpretation: The evildoers will not be able to evade the Fire or escape its punishment; they will remain subject to it.

translation: And what will make you know what the Day of Judgment is?
interpretation: The question emphasizes that the Day of Judgment is so momentous that its full reality and gravity cannot be grasped by ordinary human understanding.

translation: Then what will make you know what the Day of Judgment is?
interpretation: The question emphasizes that the reality and gravity of that Day exceed what people can fully grasp from ordinary experience.

translation: The Day when no soul can do anything for another; and that Day, all authority belongs to Allah.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, no one can independently protect or benefit another. All judgment and authority rest with Allah alone.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Woe to those who give short measure.
interpretation: This is a stern warning that cheating people and withholding what they are owed is a grave breach of trust for which one is accountable before God.

translation: Those who, when they take measure from people, take it in full,
interpretation: This exposes the injustice of insisting on complete fairness when receiving while failing to show the same fairness toward others—a warning that integrity must be mutual, not self-serving.

translation: But when they measure or weigh for others, they give less than is due.
interpretation: The verse condemns dishonest dealings and the double standard of demanding full measure for oneself while withholding what is owed to others.

translation: Do they not think that they will be resurrected?
interpretation: The question challenges heedlessness: a person who truly expects to stand before God again would take accountability seriously and would not treat others unjustly.

translation: For a tremendous day.
interpretation: It points to a day of immense consequence, understood as the Day of Judgment, when people will face the outcome of their deeds.

translation: The Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of all worlds.
interpretation: This evokes the awe of the Day of Judgment, when every person will stand before God with no authority or refuge apart from Him, underscoring the certainty of divine accountability.

translation: No indeed! The record of the wicked is surely in Sijjin.
interpretation: Sijjin signifies the woefully confined register or abode assigned to the wicked: their deeds are preserved there, and its very name conveys the humiliation and restriction awaiting them.

translation: And what can make you know what Sijjīn is?
interpretation: The question emphasizes the grave and fearsome reality of Sijjīn, whose full nature is beyond ordinary human knowledge.

translation: A written record.
interpretation: It refers to a definite, carefully preserved record whose contents are fixed and cannot be denied or altered.

translation: Woe, on that Day, to those who deny.
interpretation: This is a grave warning that those who knowingly reject God’s truth will face the consequences of their denial on the Day of Judgment.

translation: Those who deny the Day of Judgment.
interpretation: Their denial rejects the reality that people will be held accountable for their deeds, leaving them to live as though no final judgment awaits them.

translation: And none denies it except every transgressor, steeped in sin.
interpretation: The verse portrays denial of the Hereafter as bound up with a life of transgression: someone who repeatedly crosses moral limits may reject accountability because accepting it would challenge the way they choose to live.

translation: When Our verses are recited to him, he says, “Tales of the people of old.”
interpretation: The verse portrays someone who dismisses divine revelation as mere ancient fiction rather than engaging with its truth—a response that reflects arrogance and rejection.

translation: No indeed! Rather, what they used to earn has covered their hearts with a stain.
interpretation: The verse portrays wrongdoing as a gradual spiritual corrosion: deeds can cloud the heart until it becomes resistant to recognizing the truth.

translation: No indeed! Surely they, on that Day, will be veiled from their Lord.
interpretation: Their rejection of the truth will leave them deprived of the honor and nearness granted to the people of faith; this is a grave punishment and a sign of their estrangement from God.

translation: Then indeed they will surely burn in the Hellfire.
interpretation: The verse stresses the certainty of the punishment awaiting those destined for the Fire: their end is not merely a warning, but a consequence they will inevitably face.

translation: Then it will be said, “This is what you used to deny.”
interpretation: Those who rejected the truth will be confronted with the reality they denied, and their denial will no longer shield them from its consequences.

translation: No indeed! The record of the righteous is surely in ʿIlliyyūn.
interpretation: The verse portrays the deeds and standing of the righteous as preserved in a lofty, honored register, affirming that their worth is known and safeguarded by God.

translation: And what will make you know what ʿIlliyyūn is?
interpretation: The question magnifies ʿIlliyyūn as something exalted beyond ordinary understanding; in context, it refers to the lofty, preserved record of the righteous.

translation: A written record.
interpretation: It refers to a clearly inscribed and preserved record, indicating that what is recorded is firmly established and not lost.

translation: Witnessed by those brought near (to Allah).
interpretation: The record of the righteous is held in a place of honor, and the angels brought near to Allah bear witness to it—an indication of its distinction and the honor bestowed upon those whose deeds it records.

translation: Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss.
interpretation: Those who are devoted to goodness and obedience to God will attain lasting joy and well-being.

translation: Reclining on couches, they will be looking on.
interpretation: The believers are portrayed in the honor and security of Paradise, looking on as the truth of what they were promised becomes clear.

translation: You will recognize in their faces the radiance of bliss.
interpretation: تبدو على وجوه أهل النعيم في الجنة آثارُ ما أكرمهم الله به من راحةٍ وسرور؛ إشراقةٌ تكشف عن سكينةٍ ورضًا عميقين.

translation: They will be given to drink from sealed nectar.
interpretation: The sealed nectar signifies a pure and honored reward, preserved from any impurity and reserved for those granted it in the Hereafter.

translation: Its seal is musk; so let those who strive compete for this.
interpretation: The verse presents the reward of the righteous as pure and precious, urging people to direct their striving toward God’s favor and the lasting blessings of the Hereafter.

translation: And its mixture is from Tasnīm.
interpretation: The drink of the righteous is blended with water from Tasnīm, a lofty spring in Paradise, signifying the honor and nearness to God bestowed upon them.

translation: A spring from which those brought near drink.
interpretation: The verse portrays those brought near to God as honored with direct access to a pure, blessed drink, expressing their special standing and intimacy with Him.

translation: Indeed, those who committed sins used to laugh at those who believed.
interpretation: The verse condemns the arrogance of those who mocked believers, treating their faith as a reason for ridicule. Their laughter reflects a false sense of superiority, one that does not determine whose way is truly worthy.

translation: And when they passed by them, they would wink at one another.
interpretation: The verse portrays the mockery of the believers by their persecutors: as they passed them, they exchanged knowing gestures of ridicule, treating the believers with contempt.

translation: And when they returned to their people, they returned amused and enjoying themselves.
interpretation: Their carefree amusement reflects their arrogance: they treated their mockery of the believers as entertainment, heedless of the reckoning that awaited them.

translation: And when they saw them, they would say, “Indeed, these are surely misguided.”
interpretation: The verse exposes the arrogance of those who judged the believers as misguided merely because their faith and conduct differed from their own. Their confident accusation reflects their own distorted understanding, not the believers’ true standing.

translation: They were not appointed as guardians over them.
interpretation: Those who mocked the believers had no authority or divine commission to oversee them or judge their faith.

translation: So today those who believed laugh at the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse portrays the reversal of worldly mockery: those who were ridiculed for their faith are vindicated in the Hereafter, while those who mocked them face the consequence of their rejection.

translation: Reclining on couches, they will look on.
interpretation: The believers will enjoy honor and tranquility in Paradise, observing the fulfillment of God’s promise and the humiliation of those who rejected faith.

translation: Have the disbelievers been repaid for what they used to do?
interpretation: الاستفهام للتقرير؛ أي إن الله جازى الكافرين جزاءً عادلاً على أعمالهم، ومن ذلك تكذيبهم واستهزاؤهم بالمؤمنين، فظهر عدل الله وانقلبت الحال عليهم.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. When the sky is split open,
interpretation: The splitting of the sky portrays the collapse of the familiar cosmic order at the Resurrection, showing that even the greatest structures of creation remain subject to Allah’s command. It signals the arrival of the final reckoning.

translation: And it has obeyed its Lord, as it was bound to do.
interpretation: The verse portrays creation as submitting completely to God’s command: when He decrees its transformation, it responds without resistance, fulfilling what is rightfully required of it.

translation: And when the earth is spread out,
interpretation: The verse evokes the upheaval of the Last Day, when the earth is transformed and laid open, leaving nothing hidden from God’s judgment.

translation: And casts out what is within it and becomes empty.
interpretation: The earth is depicted as surrendering everything hidden within it at the Resurrection, leaving nothing concealed as it submits to God’s command.

translation: And it has listened to its Lord, as it must.
interpretation: The earth submits completely to God’s command when the Resurrection comes; its obedience is certain and fitting, for all creation is subject to its Lord.

translation: O human being, you are striving toward your Lord with a striving, and you will meet Him.
interpretation: Every person’s life is a journey of effort that inevitably leads to standing before God. The verse invites us to consider how we direct that effort, knowing that we will meet our Lord and be answerable for how we lived.

translation: As for the one who is given his record in his right hand…
interpretation: Receiving the record in the right hand signifies God’s favor and a hopeful outcome in the judgment, reflecting a life whose deeds can be faced with confidence.

translation: Then he will be called to account with an easy reckoning.
interpretation: This points to God’s merciful treatment of the believer: the reckoning will be made easy, without a harsh or burdensome account.

translation: And he will return to his people rejoicing.
interpretation: It portrays the joy and reassurance of the believer who, having received his record in his right hand, returns to his loved ones in Paradise, confident in the good outcome of his reckoning.

translation: But as for the one who is given his record behind his back…
interpretation: Being handed his record from behind portrays the utter humiliation and disgrace of someone who cannot face the record of his deeds.

translation: Then he will call out for destruction.
interpretation: Overwhelmed by the punishment awaiting him, he will cry out for his own ruin, wishing to escape what he must face.

translation: And he will burn in a blazing Fire.
interpretation: It portrays the severe punishment awaiting him in the blazing Fire.

translation: Indeed, he used to be joyful among his family.
interpretation: His ease among his family reflects a carefree confidence rooted in worldly life, with no thought of the accountability awaiting him.

translation: Indeed, he thought he would never return.
interpretation: He lived as though he would never be brought back to God for reckoning, and so gave no thought to the consequences of his actions.

translation: Yes indeed, his Lord has always seen him.
interpretation: God’s complete awareness of a person and all they do means that no deed is hidden from Him, and each person will be held accountable.

translation: Nay, I swear by the twilight.
interpretation: The twilight’s gradual fading is a sign of the ordered changes God brings about, directing attention to His power and to the certainty of what He has promised.

translation: By the night and what it gathers in.
interpretation: The verse draws attention to the night as it gathers and conceals what lies within it, inviting reflection on the order and power of the One who governs its coming.

translation: And by the moon when it becomes full,
interpretation: The moon’s completion in its appointed phases points to the wisdom and power of the One who governs the heavens.

translation: You will surely pass from one stage to another.
interpretation: Human beings are carried through successive states of existence, each beyond their control, until they meet God; the verse therefore calls them to recognize that life is a journey with an inevitable reckoning.

translation: So what is the matter with them that they do not believe?
interpretation: The question rebukes those who reject faith, inviting them to recognize that nothing justifies their refusal to believe in God and His message.

translation: And when the Qur’an is recited to them, they do not prostrate.
interpretation: Their refusal to prostrate reflects a deeper unwillingness to humble themselves before God and respond with submission when His words are recited.

translation: But those who disbelieve deny the truth.
interpretation: The verse portrays disbelief as a refusal to accept the truth, even when it has been made clear.

translation: And Allah knows best what they conceal within themselves.
interpretation: Nothing they harbor in their hearts—whether denial, hostility, or intention—is hidden from Allah; He knows it fully and will judge them with perfect knowledge.

translation: So give them the news of a painful punishment.
interpretation: The phrase uses the language of glad tidings ironically: what is normally welcomed as good news is, in this context, a warning of a grave and certain consequence. Its stark wording underscores the seriousness of the warning.

translation: Except those who believe and do righteous deeds—they will have a reward that never ends.
interpretation: Faith joined with righteous action leads to a lasting reward from God, one that is neither cut off nor diminished.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. By the sky with its constellations.
interpretation: The oath directs attention to the grandeur and ordered beauty of the heavens as a sign of Allah’s wisdom and power.

translation: And by the Promised Day,
interpretation: The phrase refers to the Day of Resurrection, whose coming is certain and on which every person will answer for their deeds.

translation: And by the witness and that which is witnessed,
interpretation: Allah swears by every witness and every witnessed event, drawing attention to how human actions are observed and will be brought to account.

translation: Cursed were the people of the trench.
interpretation: The verse pronounces divine condemnation on those who persecuted believers, affirming that cruelty and oppression do not escape God’s judgment.

translation: The fire, abundant in fuel.
interpretation: The phrase emphasizes a fiercely burning fire, its plentiful fuel underscoring the intensity of the torment.

translation: When they sat around it,
interpretation: Their sitting around the fire portrays the persecutors’ deliberate cruelty: they calmly watched the believers suffer rather than showing them mercy.

translation: And they themselves bear witness to what they do to the believers.
interpretation: Their presence as witnesses underscores that the persecution was deliberate and carried out openly; they watched the believers suffer rather than acting in ignorance, making them answerable for their cruelty.

translation: They resented them for no reason other than that they believed in Allah, the Almighty, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: The verse exposes the injustice of the persecutors: the believers’ only “offense” was their faith in God, whose might and praiseworthiness stand in contrast to the cruelty of those who oppressed them.

translation: To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is witness over all things.
interpretation: God’s sovereignty is complete, and nothing escapes His witness. This calls people to trust in His authority and remember that every deed is known to Him and will be judged with perfect justice.

translation: Indeed, those who persecuted believing men and believing women, then did not repent, will have the punishment of Hell and the punishment of the burning Fire.
interpretation: The verse warns that persecuting people for their faith is a grave injustice, while also making clear that repentance remains open: the punishment described is for those who persist in that wrongdoing without repenting.

translation: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds will have gardens beneath which rivers flow. That is the great triumph.
interpretation: The verse presents lasting nearness to God and the joy of Paradise as the ultimate success: faith is made real through righteous conduct, and its reward surpasses the temporary gains people pursue in this world.

translation: Indeed, your Lord’s grasp is severe.
interpretation: This is a warning that when God holds people accountable for wrongdoing, His judgment is decisive and cannot be resisted; it calls people to take His warning seriously and turn from injustice.

translation: Indeed, He is the One who originates and restores.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the power by which God first brings creation into being is fully His to exercise again, so resurrection is no more beyond His power than creation itself.

translation: And He is the All-Forgiving, the Loving.
interpretation: God’s forgiveness is vast, and His love is enduring: He welcomes those who turn to Him with mercy and draws His servants near through His care.

translation: The Possessor of the Throne, the All-Glorious.
interpretation: God alone possesses supreme sovereignty, and His majesty and glory are boundless.

translation: Doer of whatever He wills.
interpretation: God’s will is absolute and unrestricted; nothing can prevent Him from bringing about what He chooses.

translation: Has the account of the armies reached you?
interpretation: The rhetorical question prepares the listener to reflect on the fate of powerful forces that opposed God’s messengers: worldly strength cannot shield anyone from divine judgment, while the warning also reassures the Prophet that his opponents will not prevail indefinitely.

translation: Pharaoh and Thamud.
interpretation: The pairing evokes two past peoples known for rejecting God’s messengers, serving as a warning that power and strength cannot protect those who persist in defiance.

translation: Rather, those who disbelieve remain in denial.
interpretation: Their rejection is not due to a lack of evidence; they persist in refusing the truth despite the signs and warnings before them.

translation: And Allah encompasses them from every side.
interpretation: Their plans cannot escape Allah’s knowledge or power; however secure they may feel, they remain wholly within His authority.

translation: Rather, it is a glorious Qur’an.
interpretation: The Qur’an is exalted and worthy of honor; it is divine revelation, not something fabricated or diminished by those who reject it.

translation: In a Preserved Tablet.
interpretation: The Qur’an is kept in a divinely guarded record, secure from corruption and beyond human alteration.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. By the heaven and the night-comer.
interpretation: The oath draws attention to the vastness of the heavens and to the celestial light that appears in the night, inviting reflection on the signs of Allah’s power and wisdom.

translation: And what can make you know what the night visitor is?
interpretation: The question heightens the awe and mystery of the “night visitor,” preparing the listener for a revelation of its significance.

translation: The piercing star.
interpretation: The phrase evokes a star whose brilliant light pierces the darkness, presenting the night sky as a sign of the precision and power of its Creator.

translation: There is no soul but that it has a guardian over it.
interpretation: Every person is under God’s watch, with a guardian appointed to preserve and record their deeds; this points to the accountability of every soul before Him.

translation: So let man consider from what he was created.
interpretation: The verse invites a person to reflect on their humble beginning, recognizing that their existence is not self-made and that the One who brought them into being has power over them.

translation: He was created from a gushing fluid.
interpretation: The verse calls attention to the human being’s humble origin, reminding us that our existence depends on the Creator’s power, not on our own strength or status.

translation: It emerges from between the backbone and the ribs.
interpretation: In context, this refers to the gushing fluid from which a human is created, emphasizing the human being’s humble beginning and God’s power to bring life from it.

translation: Indeed, He is surely able to bring him back.
interpretation: The One who brought the human being into existence is fully able to restore him to life after death for the final judgment.

translation: On the Day when hidden thoughts and deeds are brought to light.
interpretation: The verse points to a day when a person’s inward reality—intentions and truths concealed from others—will be exposed before God, so that judgment rests on what was truly within, not merely on outward appearances.

translation: Then he will have no strength and no helper.
interpretation: When a person stands exposed before God, neither personal power nor anyone else can protect or rescue him; worldly supports will be of no avail.

translation: By the sky that repeatedly returns [the rain].
interpretation: The sky’s recurring return of rain reflects a purposeful order that continually renews life, directing attention to the certainty of what God has promised.

translation: And by the earth that splits open,
interpretation: The earth’s cracking open for plants to emerge points to its power of renewal and to the provision that God brings forth from the ground.

translation: Indeed, it is a decisive word.
interpretation: The Qur’an speaks with final authority: its truth is not idle talk, but a clear criterion by which truth is distinguished from falsehood.

translation: And it is not a thing of jest.
interpretation: The Qur’an is a grave and truthful revelation, not idle speech to be treated lightly; its message and warnings call for serious reflection.

translation: Indeed, they are devising a scheme.
interpretation: Those who oppose the truth are plotting against it, but their schemes remain within God’s knowledge and cannot escape His power.

translation: And I, too, devise a plan.
interpretation: God declares that the schemes of those who oppose the truth will not escape His power: He may allow them time, but His judgment ultimately turns their plotting against them.

translation: So give the disbelievers respite; leave them for a little while.
interpretation: The verse tells the Prophet not to be distressed by the disbelievers’ rejection or to hasten their punishment. Their time is granted only briefly, and their eventual accountability rests with God.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High.
interpretation: The command calls for honoring Allah by declaring Him exalted above every imperfection, and by worshipping Him with reverence befitting His supreme majesty.

translation: Who created and proportioned.
interpretation: The phrase points to creation as purposeful and ordered: God gave each thing a form and measure suited to its nature.

translation: And who determined [all things], then guided [them].
interpretation: God has assigned each created thing its measure and purpose, and guides it toward the course suited to it.

translation: And who brought forth the pasture,
interpretation: The verse points to Allah’s power and care: He brings vegetation out of the earth and provides nourishment for His creatures.

translation: Then He made it dark, withered stubble.
interpretation: The verse portrays how God turns flourishing vegetation into dry, dark remnants, reminding us that worldly growth and beauty are temporary and remain subject to His power.

translation: We shall make you recite, and you will not forget.
interpretation: God assures the Prophet that He will enable him to receive and retain the revelation, preserving it in his memory by divine care.

translation: Except what Allah wills. Surely He knows what is spoken openly and what is hidden.
interpretation: The exception affirms that all remembrance and retention remain subject to Allah’s will, not human control. His knowledge encompasses both what is expressed aloud and what remains concealed within.

translation: And We will ease you toward what is easy.
interpretation: Allah promises to guide and support the Prophet, making his mission and the path of obedience manageable for him.

translation: So remind, if the reminder is of benefit.
interpretation: The verse calls the Prophet to convey sincere counsel, whose benefit is received by those willing to reflect; it does not mean that the message should be withheld from others.

translation: He will be reminded who fears [Allah].
interpretation: Admonition finds a receptive heart in the one whose reverence for Allah makes him willing to reflect and be guided.

translation: And the most wretched will shun it.
interpretation: The one most lost in misery turns away from the reminder, refusing to heed the guidance offered to him.

translation: He who will enter the Great Fire.
interpretation: The phrase portrays the grave fate of one who is cast into Hell, whose punishment is described as immense and overwhelming.

translation: Then he will neither die therein nor live.
interpretation: This describes an existence of unrelieved torment: death does not come to end the suffering, and life brings no comfort or true well-being.

translation: Successful indeed is the one who purifies himself.
interpretation: True success comes through cleansing the heart of disbelief and wrongdoing and cultivating faith and obedience to God.

translation: And remembers the name of his Lord and prays.
interpretation: True devotion is expressed by keeping God in one’s heart and turning to Him in prayer.

translation: But you prefer the life of this world.
interpretation: This rebuke points to the tendency to choose immediate worldly pleasures over what is lasting in the Hereafter, even when that choice draws one away from what truly benefits them.

translation: And the Hereafter is better and more lasting.
interpretation: This teaches that lasting success lies beyond worldly life, so a person should not sacrifice what endures for what soon passes away.

translation: Indeed, this is in the earlier scriptures,
interpretation: The guidance just mentioned is part of the enduring message of revelation, taught in earlier scriptures as well; the Qur’an thus affirms the continuity of God’s message across prophets.

translation: The scriptures of Abraham and Moses.
interpretation: This points to the continuity of divine guidance: the truth taught in the Qur’an is part of the same revelation entrusted to earlier prophets.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Has the account of the Overwhelming Event come to you?
interpretation: The question draws the listener’s attention to the Day of Resurrection, called “the Overwhelming” because its immense terrors will encompass all who face it.

translation: Some faces on that Day will be humbled.
interpretation: The verse portrays the abasement of those who face the Hereafter in disgrace, with their outward condition reflecting the humiliation they have brought upon themselves.

translation: Toiling, exhausted.
interpretation: It describes people who will be worn out by labor and hardship in the Hereafter, with no relief from their exhaustion.

translation: They will burn in a scorching fire.
interpretation: The verse warns that worldly striving cannot avert the ultimate consequence of turning away from God; its image of an intensely burning fire conveys the severity of that reckoning.

translation: They will be made to drink from a boiling spring.
interpretation: The boiling spring portrays drinking itself as a source of torment, intensifying the severity of their punishment.

translation: They will have no food except a thorny, bitter plant.
interpretation: The verse portrays the people of Hell as deprived even of sustaining food: what is given to them is a source of misery, offering neither nourishment nor relief.

translation: It neither nourishes nor relieves hunger.
interpretation: The phrase emphasizes the utter deprivation of this food: although it is consumed, it gives no strength or comfort, underscoring the helplessness and punishment of those who must endure it.

translation: Some faces that Day will be radiant and joyful.
interpretation: The verse portrays the people of Paradise: their faces will show the comfort, delight, and honor they enjoy.

translation: Pleased with their efforts.
interpretation: The blessed will be content with the good they did, seeing that their striving has led to a lasting reward.

translation: In a lofty Garden,
interpretation: Its elevation conveys not only a high and beautiful dwelling, but also the honor and blessedness granted to its inhabitants.

translation: You will hear no vain or offensive speech therein.
interpretation: The verse portrays Paradise as a place of complete peace, free from empty, hurtful, or troubling words; its speech is pure and pleasant.

translation: In it is a flowing spring.
interpretation: The flowing spring evokes the ease and abundance of Paradise: its refreshment is ever-present, needing no effort to obtain.

translation: In it are couches raised high.
interpretation: The elevated couches suggest the honor, comfort, and splendid welcome prepared for the people of Paradise.

translation: And cups set in place,
interpretation: The cups are prepared and readily available, suggesting the ease and generous hospitality of the people of Paradise.

translation: And cushions arranged in rows.
interpretation: The orderly cushions evoke a scene of ease and gracious welcome, suggesting the comfort and dignity prepared for the people of Paradise.

translation: And carpets spread out.
interpretation: The carpets are laid out throughout the dwellings of Paradise, suggesting comfort and ease prepared for its inhabitants.

translation: Do they not look at the camels—how they were created?
interpretation: The verse calls people to recognize divine wisdom and power through careful reflection on the camel’s remarkable design and its suitability to the conditions in which it lives.

translation: And the sky—how it was raised?
interpretation: The verse directs the heart to contemplate the sky’s immense height and order as a sign of God’s power and wisdom, inviting recognition of the One who raised it.

translation: And at the mountains—how they were set up!
interpretation: The verse draws attention to the mountains’ imposing form and firm placement as a sign of deliberate design, inviting reflection on the power and wisdom of their Creator.

translation: And at the earth—how it has been spread out?
interpretation: The verse invites reflection on how God has made the earth accessible and suitable for life, presenting its broad, ordered expanse as a sign of divine power and care.

translation: So remind; you are only a reminder.
interpretation: The verse directs the Prophet to convey the truth faithfully and remind people of God, while leaving their response to them rather than claiming power to compel belief.

translation: You are not one who has power to compel them.
interpretation: The Prophet’s task is to convey the message, not to force people to accept it; their response is not under his control.

translation: Except for whoever turns away and disbelieves,
interpretation: It refers to those who deliberately reject the reminder and refuse to believe; their response is left to God, who will hold them accountable.

translation: Then Allah will punish him with the greatest punishment.
interpretation: It refers to the ultimate punishment of the Hereafter, emphasizing the gravity of knowingly turning away from the truth.

translation: Indeed, to Us is their return.
interpretation: Everyone will ultimately return to God, where their deeds and ultimate fate are determined.

translation: Then, indeed, their reckoning is upon Us.
interpretation: The verse affirms that ultimate judgment belongs to God alone: every person’s deeds will be fully accounted for, and no one can escape His just decision.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. By the dawn.
interpretation: The oath by dawn calls attention to Allah’s power and wisdom, as the darkness gives way to light and a new day begins.

translation: And by the ten nights.
interpretation: The verse is an oath by ten especially blessed nights, commonly understood as the first ten nights of Dhul-Hijjah, calling attention to their sacredness and the value of worship during them.

translation: By the even and the odd,
interpretation: The pairing and singularity found throughout creation point to its deliberate order and to the oneness of its Creator.

translation: And by the night as it passes away,
interpretation: The departing night points to the constant turning of time: darkness gives way to dawn, and every passing moment brings people closer to the consequences of their deeds.

translation: Is there not in that an oath for one endowed with understanding?
interpretation: The rhetorical question emphasizes that the preceding oaths are weighty evidence for anyone of sound judgment, calling them to reflect and recognize their significance.

translation: Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with ʿĀd?
interpretation: The verse calls the listener to reflect on the fate of ʿĀd: no people’s strength or power can protect them when they persist in defiance of God.

translation: Iram, the city of lofty pillars.
interpretation: The phrase evokes the imposing architecture and worldly power associated with the people of ʿĀd, whose might was not lasting.

translation: The like of which had never been created in the lands.
interpretation: The phrase portrays Iram as unmatched in its time, while reminding us that worldly greatness is no guarantee of lasting security or divine favor.

translation: And [consider] Thamud, who hewed out the rocks in the valley?
interpretation: The verse points to Thamud’s remarkable ability to carve dwellings from solid rock, yet their impressive strength and skill could not protect them from the consequences of rejecting God. It warns against trusting in worldly power while disregarding divine guidance.

translation: And Pharaoh, the man of the stakes,
interpretation: “The man of the stakes” portrays Pharaoh as a tyrant who used stakes as instruments of torture, binding people to them to punish and terrorize them. The epithet underscores the cruelty by which he enforced his rule.

translation: Those who transgressed throughout the lands,
interpretation: Their wrongdoing was not confined to themselves: they abused their power across the lands, showing that widespread authority does not place anyone beyond accountability before God.

translation: So they spread much corruption therein.
interpretation: The phrase portrays wrongdoing that became widespread, damaging the moral and social order of the place.

translation: So your Lord poured upon them a scourge of punishment.
interpretation: The image of a scourge conveys punishment that strikes with force and severity: God’s judgment came upon them as the consequence of their wrongdoing.

translation: Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful.
interpretation: God is fully aware of every deed and holds people accountable in due time; no wrongdoing escapes His justice.

translation: As for the human being, when his Lord tests him by honoring him and granting him blessings, he says, “My Lord has honored me.”
interpretation: The verse cautions against taking comfort, wealth, or blessing as proof of one’s superior standing with God. Such ease is itself a test, and a person should respond with humility and gratitude rather than assume it guarantees divine favor.

translation: But when He tests him by restricting his provision, he says, “My Lord has humiliated me.”
interpretation: The verse corrects the assumption that material hardship means God has rejected or dishonored someone. A person’s provision is part of a test, not a reliable measure of their worth or standing with God.

translation: No indeed! Rather, you do not honor the orphan.
interpretation: The verse rebukes those who mistake worldly prosperity for divine favor: the real failing is neglecting the dignity and care owed to the orphan.

translation: And you do not encourage one another to feed the needy.
interpretation: The verse condemns a society in which people fail not only to care for the needy themselves but also to encourage one another to do so, stressing that concern for the vulnerable is a shared responsibility.

translation: And you devour inheritance greedily and indiscriminately.
interpretation: The verse condemns a greed that disregards justice and the rights of others, treating wealth as something to seize rather than distribute with due regard for those entitled to it.

translation: And you love wealth with an intense love.
interpretation: The verse warns that excessive attachment to wealth can take hold of a person’s heart, leading them to put possessions before the responsibilities and values God has entrusted to them.

translation: No indeed! When the earth is pounded and pounded again,
interpretation: The verse evokes the final upheaval in which the earth is utterly leveled, exposing how fragile worldly security is and preparing for the reckoning that follows.

translation: And your Lord comes, and the angels, rank upon rank.
interpretation: The verse portrays the Day of Judgment, when God’s decisive judgment is made manifest and the angels stand in ordered ranks; it affirms God’s coming in a manner befitting Him, without describing how.

translation: And Hell will be brought forth on that Day. On that Day, the human being will remember—but how could remembrance then benefit him?
interpretation: When the reality of the Hereafter becomes undeniable, a person will recognize the truth and recall what they did and neglected. But that recognition comes after the time for choosing and acting has passed, so it cannot undo the consequences; the verse warns against postponing repentance and heedfulness until the Day of Judgment.

translation: He will say, “If only I had sent something ahead for my life!”
interpretation: He will realize that the lasting life is the Hereafter, and regret not having used his time in this world to prepare for it—when the chance to act has passed.

translation: So on that Day, none will punish as He punishes.
interpretation: The verse warns that God’s judgment will be utterly decisive: no punishment people know can compare with the punishment He decrees for those who persist in rejecting the truth.

translation: And none can bind as He binds.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that no restraint or punishment can equal the severity of God’s judgment on that Day.

translation: O tranquil soul,
interpretation: This addresses a soul made serene by trust in God—one whose faith has brought it to rest in His care.

translation: Return to your Lord, content and pleasing to Him.
interpretation: It is an invitation to the tranquil soul to return to God, at peace with His decree and welcomed by Him because He is pleased with it.

translation: So enter among My servants,
interpretation: The address invites the soul at peace to draw near to God by joining His devoted servants, finding belonging and honor in their company.

translation: And enter My Paradise.
interpretation: The phrase portrays the faithful soul’s final welcome into lasting bliss, with “My Paradise” expressing the honor and closeness of being received by God.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. I swear by this city.
interpretation: The oath honors the sacred city of Mecca and draws attention to its significance; the opening “I swear” introduces a solemn declaration about what follows.

translation: And you, [O Muhammad], are permitted in this city.
interpretation: The verse refers to Mecca’s sacred status and the special permission given to the Prophet to fight there at its conquest, although fighting was ordinarily forbidden in the city. This permission was exceptional and brief.

translation: And by the parent and what they beget,
interpretation: The oath points to humanity’s shared origin and generations, reminding people that every life belongs to a lineage and that human beings are accountable for how they live.

translation: We have certainly created the human being in hardship.
interpretation: Human life is marked by effort, struggle, and trials; this calls for patience and perseverance rather than expecting a life free of difficulty.

translation: Does he think that no one has power over him?
interpretation: The verse challenges the illusion that a person is beyond accountability, reminding him that no one can escape God’s power.

translation: He says, “I have spent heaps of wealth.”
interpretation: The verse portrays someone boasting about how much wealth he has spent, as though the size of his expenditure proves his greatness. It exposes the emptiness of pride in wealth: spending much does not by itself make a person righteous or place him beyond God’s judgment.

translation: Does he think that no one has seen him?
interpretation: The verse warns against imagining that one’s actions are unseen or beyond accountability: nothing a person does is hidden from God.

translation: Have We not given him two eyes?
interpretation: The verse draws attention to sight as a gift from God, inviting a person to recognize divine generosity and use this faculty responsibly.

translation: And a tongue and two lips.
interpretation: These faculties are presented as deliberate gifts from God, enabling people to speak, express themselves, and communicate—gifts that carry responsibility in how they are used.

translation: And We guided him to the two paths.
interpretation: God has made clear to every person the way of good and the way of evil, granting the discernment to choose between them.

translation: Yet he has not undertaken the steep ascent.
interpretation: The “steep ascent” signifies the demanding path of righteousness: choosing compassion and selfless good even when it costs effort. The verse reproaches a person who has not chosen that path despite being able to do so.

translation: And what will make you know what the steep pass is?
interpretation: The question draws attention to the immense difficulty and significance of the moral challenge about to be described.

translation: Freeing a person from bondage.
interpretation: The phrase refers to emancipating an enslaved person. It presents liberation from bondage as a demanding act of righteousness that restores a person’s freedom and dignity.

translation: Or feeding [someone] on a day of severe hunger,
interpretation: This points to the virtue of giving food when need is most urgent—during famine or hardship—when generosity is especially demanding and its benefit most keenly felt.

translation: An orphan who is near of kin.
interpretation: The phrase highlights the special responsibility to care for an orphan who is also a relative: kinship makes an already vulnerable person’s claim on one’s compassion especially close.

translation: Or a destitute person lying in the dust.
interpretation: The phrase portrays someone in extreme poverty, so deprived that they have no shelter or means of comfort.

translation: Then he is among those who believe, urge one another to patience, and urge one another to compassion.
